# Native Android → KMP Parity Audit

> **Strict gap analysis** comparing the original Native Android app (`native-app/`, the source of truth) against the new Kotlin Multiplatform app. **This is an audit only — no code was changed.** Every divergence from the native app is treated as a potential regression.

**Method:** the app was split into **42 sections**; one **Opus 4.8** agent audited each section by reading both implementations, then a second **Opus 4.8** agent independently re-checked (confirmed/refuted) every Critical and High finding. **148 agents total** (42 section auditors + 106 adversarial verifiers).

## At a glance

- **Total findings:** 681
- 🔴 **Critical:** 13  ·  🟠 **High:** 98  ·  🟡 **Medium:** 202  ·  ⚪ **Low:** 368
- **Adversarial verification of Critical/High:** 93 confirmed, 17 partially correct, 1 refuted (likely false positives, flagged inline).
- **Sections audited:** 42

**Severity rubric:** 🔴 Critical = core flow broken/missing or crash · 🟠 High = feature/state/interaction missing or clearly wrong · 🟡 Medium = noticeable UI/behaviour divergence · ⚪ Low = subtle/cosmetic.

## 3. Detailed findings by section

### Home Feed  `home-feed`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 26 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡7 ⚪16)

> Native Home (MVVM, MangaViewModel + HomeViewModel + HomeRoute + HomeScreen) renders a Scaffold with a custom 24sp-bold top bar, a source-tab strip, an 8dp spacer, then either a list (popular HorizontalUncontainedCarousel + MangaHomeItem rows with chapter chips + bookmark toggle) or grid (SearchItems poster cards), with native ads interleaved every 5 items, pull-to-refresh, infinite scroll, per-source siteState gating, and a 403/Cloudflare recovery path (Handle403Error + a Lekmanga site-status snackbar). KMP (MVI: HomeViewModel/HomeState + :ui HomeScreen + HomeReworkScreenRoute) faithfully reproduces most of the structure and most dp/typography values, and the leaf components are well-documented ports. However there are real regressions: ads are entirely absent, the carousel uses a LazyRow approximation instead of the M3 carousel (different fling/scale behavior), the default view flips to GRID (native defaults to list), the help affordance was downgraded from an in-app video dialog to opening an MP4 URL in WebView, the 403/Cloudflare recovery + Lekmanga status snackbar are gone, the error message no longer interpolates the source's failure text, the open-in-webview icon and behavior changed, the per-source brand tab icons and the source badge on cards are missing, the "new source" badge is hard-disabled, and several smaller spacing/typography/identity divergences exist. Core browsing works but with multiple monetization, resilience, and visual-fidelity gaps.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Home Feed</summary>

**🟠 [High] Home feed — native ad interleaving — Native interleaves a native ad every 5 feed items (both grid and list); KMP renders no ads at all** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:147-158 builds mergedState via interleaveAdsCustom(interval=5, items=...); grid renders ListEntryWithAd.Ad → NativeAdListItem (HomeScreen.kt:323-330), list likewise (HomeScreen.kt:422-429)
- **KMP:** No — HomeScreen.kt HomeGrid (lines 363-386) / HomeList (404-442) render only HomeFeedGridCard / HomeFeedRow from state.feed; no ad type, no interleave; grep for interleaveAds/NativeAdListItem in ui/presentation/domain/data returns nothing
- **Explanation:** Monetization is a core product behavior: every 5th card in the native Home feed is a native ad (interval=5). The KMP rework has no ad-mob integration in any layer, so the entire ad revenue surface on Home is gone and the visual cadence of the feed (ad break every 5 items) is absent.
- **Suggested fix:** Reintroduce an ad-interleave concept in the rework. Either model a sealed feed-entry type (Item vs Ad) in HomeState and add a Compose ad slot in :ui (platform-expect for the ad SDK), or interleave at the route-adapter level in :composeApp where the legacy ad_mob types are reachable, mirroring interleaveAdsCustom(interval=5).
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — confirmed exactly as claimed. native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/home/ui/screens/HomeScreen.kt:147-158 builds mergedState = interleaveAdsCustom(interval = 5, items = mangaItemsState.data) producing State<List<ListEntryWithAd<MangaItem>>>. Grid branch (lines 313-332): `is ListEntryWithAd.Ad -> NativeAdListItem(position = index, ...)` at 323-330. List branch (lines 405-431): same NativeAdListItem at 422-429. Supporting infra present: ad_mob/util/ListEntryWithAd.kt:6-8 (sealed Item/Ad), ad_mob/util/ads_lists/interleaveAds7.kt (interleaveAdsCustom/interleaveAds), ad_mob/native_ads/NativeAdListItem.kt, plus full ad_mob package (NativeAdQueue, AdCoordinator, RewardedAdManager). Wired into the live screen via native-app/.../navigation/routes/HomeRoute.kt. KMP — feed ad-interleaving confirmed absent. ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/home/HomeScreen.kt HomeGrid (363-386) renders only HomeFeedGridCard from state.feed; HomeList (388-442) renders only HomeFeedRow. No ad branch, no ListEntryWithAd, no NativeAdListItem. state.feed is List<HomeFeedItem>; HomeFeedItem (domain/.../model/home/HomeFeedItem.kt:22) is a plain data class with no ad variant. grep for interleaveAds/NativeAdListItem/ListEntryWithAd/feedAd/loadNative/NativeAd returns ZERO matches across :ui, :presentation, :domain, :data, :platform, :composeApp, :app. CORRECTION to the claim's explanation: "no ad-mob integration in any layer" is inaccurate. :platform DOES have a real AdMob facade — platform/.../ads/AdProvider.kt (interface, lines 19-25) with Android actual platform/.../ads/AndroidAdProvider.kt wrapping com.google.android.gms.ads (interstitial+rewarded+banner), platform/.../consent/ConsentFlowClient.kt (UMP), and app/.../MyApp.kt:133 calls MobileAds.initialize(...). HOWEVER that facade exposes ONLY loadInterstitial/showInterstitial/loadRewarded/showRewarded/loadBanner — there is NO native-ad API and it is not consumed by Home (consumers outside :platform are only :shared DI modules + MyApp.kt). So the specific audited feature — native-ad interleaving every 5th Home feed item — is genuinely 100% absent in KMP.

**🟠 [High] Home default layout (grid vs list) — Native defaults to LIST view; KMP defaults to GRID view** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:110 `var isGridView by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` (false = list with carousel + MangaHomeItem rows)
- **KMP:** Yes but inverted — HomeState.kt:46 `val isGridView: Boolean = true`
- **Explanation:** On first launch the native app shows the rich list layout: the popular carousel at top followed by detailed rows (cover + title + 3 chapter chips + bookmark). KMP defaults to the grid of poster cards, which omits the carousel and the per-row chapter chips and save button entirely until the user toggles. This is a noticeable change to the default Home experience and hides the popular carousel by default.
- **Suggested fix:** Change HomeState.isGridView default to false to match native's initial list view. Also consider persisting the user's last choice (native does not persist it, so matching false is sufficient for parity).
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). Native (source of truth): /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/home/ui/screens/HomeScreen.kt:110 `var isGridView by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` — default false = LIST. It is a plain `remember` (no DataStore/prefs restore anywhere in the home package), so first launch is always list. In list mode (HomeScreen.kt:353-452) a LazyColumn renders MangaCarousel at top (lines 385-399) then MangaHomeItem rows; MangaHomeItem.kt:142-198 shows cover + title + up to 3 chapter chips (`item.chapters?.take(3)`) + a bookmark IconButton (save/saved). In grid mode (HomeScreen.kt:280-352) it renders a LazyVerticalGrid of SearchItems poster cards only — no carousel, no chapter chips, no save button. KMP: /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/home/HomeState.kt:45 `val isGridView: Boolean = true` — default true = GRID (claim cited line 46; actual is line 45, content exact). HomeViewModel.kt:57 `initialState = HomeState()` uses that default unchanged; the only writer is the user toggle at HomeViewModel.kt:72 (`OnToggleGridView -> copy(isGridView = !it.isGridView)`); no persisted-pref override. UI: /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/home/HomeScreen.kt:341 `state.isGridView -> HomeGrid(...)` else :342 `HomeList(...)`. HomeGrid (347-386) renders only HomeFeedGridCard, which (HomeFeedGridCard.kt:42-93) is a pure poster card (cover + bottom title band) with NO chapter chips and NO save button. HomeList (388-442) renders FeaturedCarousel (411) plus HomeFeedRow rows carrying onChapterClick + onSaveToggle. Conclusion: defaults are genuinely inverted (native false/list vs KMP true/grid), and the KMP grid default omits the popular carousel, per-row chapter chips, and the save button until the user toggles — exactly as claimed. Only nit: KMP line is 45, not 46.

**🟠 [High] 403 / Cloudflare recovery (Handle403Error) — Native auto-recovers from a 403 on the feed by re-fetching after a delay; KMP has no equivalent** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeRoute.kt:135-147 wraps the feed state in Handle403Error(state, api, baseUrl, onDismiss = { delay(1000); mangaViewModel.getMangaHome() }) when siteState == WORKING
- **KMP:** No — HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt and HomeViewModel have no 403-specific handling; a Network.Http(403) surfaces only as a transient ShowError snackbar and the static error pane (with an Open-in-WebView action)
- **Explanation:** Sources behind Cloudflare frequently return 403 until a WebView token refresh occurs. Native detected this and (via Handle403Error and the WebView dialog flow) refreshed and re-fetched automatically. The KMP rework only offers a manual Open-in-WebView action in the error pane and a toast; the automatic detect-refresh-retry loop is gone, so protected sources are more likely to stay broken without explicit user action.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the 403 recovery: when feedError is AppError.Network.Http(403), prompt/trigger the WebView token refresh and auto re-fetch the feed (the legacy Handle403Error + onDismiss getMangaHome() loop). At minimum make the Open-in-WebView action navigate to the active source's manga URL and re-fetch on return.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth) — claim confirmed: HomeRoute.kt:135-147 gates `Handle403Error(state=mangaItemsState, currentApi.API, currentBaseUrl, onDismiss={ coroutineScope.launch{ delay(1000); mangaViewModel.getMangaHome() } })` on `siteState==SourceState.WORKING` (exactly the cited signature/lines). Handle403Error.kt:32-48: LaunchedEffect auto-opens WebViewDialog ("please solve the bot check" Cloudflare dialog) when `state is State.Error && state.code==403`, then on dismiss runs onDismiss (the delayed re-fetch) — automatic detect→WebView-refresh→re-fetch loop. State.kt:14 `data class Error(val code: Int?,...)`; State.kt:37 classifies 403. MangaViewModel.kt:191 `fun getMangaHome()` is the real re-fetch target. Native ALSO has a second 403 path: HomeRoute.kt:118-128 shows a snackbar with an Open-WebView action. KMP — Home-feed gap is REAL: HomeViewModel.kt routes EVERY failure (initial feed :218, pagination :164, featured :231) to HomeEffect.ShowError(error) with NO statusCode branch; HomeEffect.kt declares only ShowError + NavigateToWebView (no SolveCloudflareChallenge). HomeScreen.kt:184 surfaces ShowError as a snackbar; HomeScreen.kt:326-334 is a static error pane with manual Retry/Open-in-WebView/Help. HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:156-158 wires onOpenWebView as plain manual nav with no auto-retry-on-return. So Home has no automatic 403 detect-refresh-retry. CLAIM FRAMING CORRECTIONS (why PartiallyCorrect): (1) The 403 code is NOT lost in KMP — AppError.kt:90 `data class Http(val statusCode: Int,...)` preserves it. (2) The auto-recovery pattern the claim says is "gone" actually EXISTS in the KMP rework, just not in Home: DetailsViewModel.kt:413-414 (+ CHALLENGE_STATUSES={403,429,503,520-524} at :160) and ReaderViewModel.kt:540-546 (+ :629) both emit SolveCloudflareChallenge, and route adapters auto-retry on WebView return (ChapterImagesByLegacyArgsReworkScreenRoute.kt:158-159). The infrastructure is present and trivially reusable; it simply isn't wired into the Home slice.

**🟡 [Medium] Error state — failed-to-load message — Native error message interpolates the source's actual failure text; KMP shows a static 'Failed to load' with no detail** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:297-300 & 370-373 `stringResource(R.string.failed_to_load, mangaItemsState.message)`; string is `Failed to load : %1$s` (strings.xml:222)
- **KMP:** No — HomeScreen.kt:327 `stringResource(Res.string.home_failed_to_load)`; string is just `Failed to load` (strings.xml:366), the AppError detail is dropped
- **Explanation:** Native surfaced the underlying error (HTTP code / parse message) inline in the error pane, which helped users and support distinguish a 403/Cloudflare block from a parse error. The KMP error pane is a generic static line; the typed AppError is only used for the transient snackbar (ShowError), not the persistent error pane.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a parameterized string (Failed to load: %1$s) and pass a human-readable AppError summary into YamiErrorState, mirroring native's interpolation. Reuse rememberHomeErrorMessages to map state.feedError to a string for the pane.

**🟡 [Medium] Lekmanga site-status 403 snackbar — Native runs a per-source HTTP health check (Lekmanga) and shows an actionable snackbar on 403; KMP omits this entirely** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeViewModel.kt:83-126 getSiteStatus(api) HEADs `${url}manga/` for Lekmanga; HomeRoute.kt:118-128 shows a snackbar with action `libaray_open_the_web_button` that navigates to Screen.WebView for Lekmanga on 403
- **KMP:** No — no getSiteStatus equivalent in HomeViewModel/ObserveSiteStateUseCase; observeSiteState only maps the stored Room SourceState, it does not perform a live HTTP probe
- **Explanation:** Native proactively probed the Lekmanga source and, on 403, nudged the user into the WebView to clear the block via an action snackbar. The KMP rework has no live probe and no such prompt, so a Lekmanga block presents only as a failed feed with a generic toast.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a per-source health-probe use case (or fold into the 403 recovery) that performs the lightweight HEAD/GET native did and emits an effect to show an actionable 'open in WebView' snackbar for the affected source.

**🟡 [Medium] Help affordance (HelpVideoDialog) — Native opens an in-app video Dialog (streamed MP4 with loading spinner + close button + lifecycle-safe cleanup); KMP opens the raw MP4 URL in the WebView** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — HelpVideoDialog.kt renders a Dialog with an Android VideoView playing https://yamimanga.me/video/help_video.mp4, a CircularProgressIndicator while loading, a top-end Close IconButton, and ANR-safe async cleanup; reachable from ErrorScreen onHelp (HomeScreen.kt:303,376)
- **KMP:** Partial/Downgraded — HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:162-170 onHelp navigates to Screen.WebView(url = 'https://yamimanga.me/video/help_video.mp4', api = '') i.e. loads a bare .mp4 URL in the in-app browser
- **Explanation:** The polished in-app help video dialog (overlay, spinner, close affordance, controlled playback) is replaced by handing a .mp4 URL to a WebView, which on many platforms triggers a download or a plain video tag rather than the framed dialog experience. This is a UX regression for the help flow. (Note: this is a documented KMP substitution because Android VideoView is not portable.)
- **Suggested fix:** Implement a cross-platform help-video player (expect/actual media player, or an embedded HTML5 player page) presented as a modal dialog matching the native framing, instead of navigating to a raw .mp4 URL.

**🟡 [Medium] Popular carousel (MangaCarousel vs FeaturedCarousel) — Native uses M3 HorizontalUncontainedCarousel with mask/scale per CarouselItemDrawInfo + single-advance fling; KMP uses a plain LazyRow with a coarse 1f/0.9f scale on the first-visible item** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaCarousel.kt:46-95: HorizontalUncontainedCarousel(itemWidth=150.dp, itemSpacing=16.dp, contentPadding=horizontal 12.dp, height 220.dp), per-item scale = info.size/info.maxSize animated with spring(DampingRatioMediumBouncy), singleAdvanceFlingBehavior
- **KMP:** Partial — FeaturedCarousel.kt:66-95: LazyRow + rememberSnapFlingBehavior; scale animates between 1f (firstVisibleItemIndex == index) and 0.9f only; same 220.dp/150.dp/16.dp/12.dp envelope
- **Explanation:** The native carousel continuously scales/masks items based on their viewport position (the signature M3 'uncontained' parallax), and snaps one item per fling. The KMP approximation snaps via SnapFlingBehavior and applies a binary 1f/0.9f scale tied to firstVisibleItemIndex, so only one card is 'big' and the smooth per-position scaling/edge-masking is lost. Documented as a deliberate cross-platform substitution (GAP-HOME-06) but it is a visible motion/visual divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** If acceptable cross-target, use HorizontalUncontainedCarousel (CMP supports M3 carousel on most targets) to restore the mask+scale; otherwise compute each item's scale from its layoutInfo offset relative to viewport center (not just firstVisibleItemIndex) for a continuous parallax closer to native.

**🟡 [Medium] Source-tab brand icons — Native renders each source's brand icon (repo.ICON, fallback team_x) in the tab; KMP renders a generic Inbox glyph for every tab** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — SourcesTabs.kt:104-111 `painterResource(if repo.ICON != 0 else R.drawable.team_x)` tinted Color.Unspecified when selected (full-color brand logo), 18.dp
- **KMP:** No — HomeScreen.kt:244-255 iconForTab renders YamiIcons.Empty (Icons.Outlined.Inbox) for every tab at 18.dp; SourceTab.iconKey is populated (= api) but never resolved to a drawable
- **Explanation:** Native tabs are visually distinguishable by their source brand logos (MangaDex, Team-X, etc.). In KMP every tab shows the same generic inbox icon, so the only differentiator is the text label. This is a clear branding/visual-recognition regression. Documented as GAP-HOME-04 (the :composeApp RepoIconResolver was not threaded through).
- **Suggested fix:** Thread the :composeApp RepoIconResolver (or a multiplatform icon registry keyed on SourceTab.iconKey/api) through the iconForTab slot in HomeReworkScreenRoute so each tab shows its real source icon with the native tint behavior (Unspecified/full-color when selected).

**🟡 [Medium] 'New source' badge on edit-tabs button — Native shows an animated 'New' badge over the edit-tabs button when there are new sources; KMP hard-codes the badge off** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — SourcesTabs.kt:144-148 renders AnimatedNew over the edit IconButton when isNewSource; isNewSource is driven by repoSettingsViewModel.newSources (HomeRoute.kt:89)
- **KMP:** No — HomeScreen.kt:236 passes `showNewBadge = false` literally; SourceTabsRow supports showNewBadge but it is never set true, and there is no newSources observation in HomeViewModel/HomeState
- **Explanation:** The native app draws attention to newly available sources with an animated badge over the edit button, nudging users to open the sources manager. KMP never shows it (hard-disabled), so the discovery affordance for new sources is lost on Home.
- **Suggested fix:** Observe a 'new sources available' flag (the rework Sources VM equivalent of newSources) into HomeState and pass showNewBadge = that flag; clear it when navigating to Sources, matching native's setNewSources(false) on edit click.

**🟡 [Medium] Pagination scroll-position preservation — Native replaces the feed with the full accumulated list (source returns prior+new), preserving identity; KMP appends new items and distinctBy feedKey, which is a different merge contract** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaViewModel.kt:225-245 getMoreManga passes the current list to fetchMoreManga(page, currentItems) and posts State.Success(result) (the source returns the FULL combined list); no client-side de-dup
- **KMP:** Partial/Different — HomeFeedRepositoryImpl keeps `accumulated` and passes it to fetchMoreManga(page, snapshot) BUT fetchMore returns only that call's result; HomeViewModel.onEndReached (HomeViewModel.kt:142-159) then does `(it.feed + more).distinctBy(feedKey)` and ends pagination if nothing new was added
- **Explanation:** The merge contract changed. Native trusted the source to return the entire accumulated list and replaced state wholesale. KMP appends `more` to the existing feed then de-dups, and treats an all-duplicate page as end-of-pagination (hasMorePages = merged.size > old). For sources whose fetchMoreManga returns the FULL list (as native assumed), KMP's `feed + more` will momentarily double the list before distinctBy collapses it, and the hasMorePages heuristic could prematurely stop pagination if a source legitimately returns a page that fully overlaps the previous accumulation. This is a behavioral risk introduced by the migration.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm per-source fetchMoreManga return semantics (full-list vs delta). If sources return the full accumulated list (native's assumption), have fetchMore/onEndReached REPLACE rather than append+distinct; if they return deltas, keep append+distinct. Make the contract explicit and consistent with the legacy source behavior to avoid premature pagination stop.

**⚪ [Low] Open-in-WebView top-bar action — Native uses a globe (Web) icon for open-in-browser; KMP uses an OpenInNew arrow icon, and the URL resolution differs** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:244-246 Icon(Icons.Default.Web) contentDescription 'Options'; HomeRoute.kt:164-177 resolves the live base URL via getCurrentBaseUrl()/getCurrentApi() then navigates Screen.WebView(url, api)
- **KMP:** Partial — HomeScreen.kt:211-215 uses YamiIcons.OpenInWebView (Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.OpenInNew); HomeViewModel.onOpenWebView emits NavigateToWebView(url = "", api) with a BLANK url, relying on the WebView route to resolve url from api
- **Explanation:** The icon glyph changed (globe → open-in-new arrow) and the content description changed from 'Options' to a localized 'open in webview' string. Functionally, native passes the resolved source base URL while KMP passes an empty url and depends on the WebView route to backfill it from api; if that resolution path differs this could open the wrong/blank page, but the icon itself is a low-severity cosmetic divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Switch YamiIcons.OpenInWebView to a globe (Icons.Filled.Public/Web) to match native, and verify the WebView route reliably resolves the source landing URL from a blank url+api (or resolve the base URL in the data/route layer before emitting the effect, as native did).

**⚪ [Low] Site-status screen (maintenance/stopped/adult) rendering — Native SimpleStatusScreen is a fully specified layout (120dp circular icon card, 48dp icon, headlineMedium bold title, titleLarge subtitle, bodyLarge message with exact spacers); KMP delegates to a generic YamiSiteStatusView** _(Component)_

Unless YamiSiteStatusView replicates those exact values, the status screens will look subtly different (icon-card size, spacing, message opacity).

**⚪ [Low] List-mode card shadow tint — Native MangaHomeItem outer card uses a custom ambient/spot shadow tinted onSurface@0.9; KMP uses only M3 cardElevation default shadow** _(Color)_

KMP rows only have the default M3 elevation shadow, so rows appear flatter. The elevation value matches; only the shadow color/intensity diverges. Documented as a known cross-platform limitation.

- **KMP:** No explicit shape — HomeFeedRow.kt:77-90 Card has no `shape =` argument, so it falls back to CardDefaults shape (RoundedCornerShape 12.dp)

**⚪ [Low] List-mode chapter chips layout — Native stacks up to 3 chapter chips vertically in a weight-4 column; KMP wraps them horizontally in a FlowRow** _(UI/Layout)_

- **KMP:** No — HomeFeedRow.kt:114-125 chapter chips are a FlowRow (weight 1f) with xs spacing, so they flow horizontally and wrap
- **Explanation:** Native chapter chips read as a vertical mini-list (chapter per line), while KMP lays them out as horizontally-flowing pills. With 3 short chapter numbers this changes the row's vertical rhythm and the visual emphasis on recent chapters. Documented as an intentional FlowRow choice but it diverges from the native stacked look.

**⚪ [Low] Save/bookmark toggle affordance — Native list row uses custom ic_bookmark / ic_bookmark_bold drawables; KMP uses Material Bookmark / outlined BookmarkBorder** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaHomeItem.kt:192-196 painterResource(if isSaved R.drawable.ic_bookmark_bold else R.drawable.ic_bookmark) inside an IconButton, with a CircularProgressIndicator (inversePrimary) while saving
- **KMP:** Partial — HomeFeedRow.kt:140-151 YamiIconButton with YamiIcons.Bookmark (Icons.Filled.Bookmark) / YamiIcons.BookmarkOutline (Icons.Outlined.BookmarkBorder), tinted primary when saved / onSurfaceVariant when not; saving spinner is primary 20dp
- **Explanation:** The bookmark semantics are preserved (filled when saved, outline when not) but the glyphs are the generic Material bookmark vs native's custom-drawn bookmark, and the saving spinner color differs (native inversePrimary vs KMP primary). Subtle visual divergence on the save control. (Note: the alternate native MangaHomeCard used a red heart, but the component wired into Home is MangaHomeItem with bookmark drawables, so the KMP bookmark choice is correct.)
- **Suggested fix:** Port the ic_bookmark / ic_bookmark_bold vector drawables into :ui resources and use them for exact glyph parity; align the saving spinner color to inversePrimary as native did.

**⚪ [Low] First-page de-duplication — KMP de-dups the first feed page by feedKey; native does not de-dup at all** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** No — MangaViewModel.startHomeFetch posts source State verbatim (MangaViewModel.kt:173-175), no distinctBy; native LazyColumn keys are by index (itemsIndexed), so duplicates don't crash
- **KMP:** Yes — HomeViewModel.kt:201 `items.distinctBy(HomeFeedItem::feedKey)`; required because :ui keys LazyGrid/LazyColumn by feedKey() (HomeScreen.kt:374,424) which would crash on duplicate keys
- **Explanation:** KMP introduces feedKey-based de-duplication that native lacked. This is generally an improvement (and necessary because KMP uses stable keys while native used positional index keys), but it means a source that legitimately returns the same title twice (e.g. two language editions sharing api\|language\|url\|title) will show ONE row in KMP vs TWO in native. Edge-case behavioral divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable as-is (stable keys are safer), but verify the feedKey (api\|language\|url\|title) is unique enough that no legitimately-distinct entries collapse; if duplicates with identical url but different chapters are expected, include a finer discriminator.

**⚪ [Low] Tab-switch scroll reset — Native resets BOTH list and grid scroll on tab change via a shared persisted state and a previousTabIndex guard; KMP resets via LaunchedEffect on activeTabIndex per-list-instance** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:111-120 LaunchedEffect(activeTabIndex) scrolls both listState and gridState to 0 only when previousTabIndex != activeTabIndex; states are hoisted/shared across recompositions
- **KMP:** Partial — HomeList/HomeGrid each rememberLazyListState/rememberLazyGridState locally and LaunchedEffect(state.activeTabIndex){ scrollToItem(0) } (HomeScreen.kt:357,398); the list/grid states are NOT hoisted, so toggling grid<->list loses scroll position
- **Explanation:** Native hoists listState and gridState from the route (HomeRoute passes them in) so they survive grid/list toggles and tab switches with a single previousTabIndex guard. KMP creates the lazy states inside HomeList/HomeGrid, so they are recreated when toggling between grid and list (scroll resets to top on every toggle) — a minor behavioral divergence. Both reset on tab switch as intended.
- **Suggested fix:** Hoist the LazyListState/LazyGridState to HomeScreenContent (or remember them keyed only by view-mode) so the scroll position is preserved across grid/list toggles, matching native's hoisted states.

**⚪ [Low] Refresh spinner indicator styling — Native PullRefreshIndicator uses explicit colors (background = inverseSurface, content = background); KMP PullToRefreshBox uses default indicator styling** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:455-461 PullRefreshIndicator(backgroundColor = inverseSurface, contentColor = background)
- **KMP:** No — HomeScreen.kt:222-228 PullToRefreshBox with no custom indicator/colors (default M3 PullToRefresh indicator)
- **Explanation:** Native's pull-to-refresh spinner has a deliberately inverted color scheme (inverseSurface circle, background-colored arrow). KMP uses the default M3 PullToRefresh indicator colors, so the refresh affordance looks different (default surface/primary). Also note native uses the older Material PullRefresh while KMP uses Material3 PullToRefreshBox (different default visuals/animation).
- **Suggested fix:** Provide a custom indicator to PullToRefreshBox with containerColor = inverseSurface and the arrow/content color = background to match native, or accept the M3 default as the design-system standard.

**⚪ [Low] Empty-state handling — KMP shows a dedicated 'No manga found' empty state when the feed is empty; native shows no empty state (just an empty list / bare carousel)** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — HomeScreen.kt list/grid State.Success simply renders an empty LazyColumn/LazyVerticalGrid when data is empty; no empty-state composable
- **KMP:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:339-340 YamiEmptyState(title = home_empty 'No manga found') when feed is empty (with a special-case to still show the carousel in list mode)
- **Explanation:** KMP adds an empty-state message that native never had. This is generally an improvement (GAP-HOME-16) but is a behavioral divergence: where native showed a blank feed (and, in list mode, the popular carousel alone), KMP shows an explicit 'No manga found' message. The list-mode carry-through of the carousel is handled, but grid mode with empty feed shows only the empty state (native showed blank grid).
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable improvement; ensure it does not suppress the carousel in list mode (already handled) and confirm product wants the explicit empty message vs native's silent-empty behavior.

**⚪ [Low] Source badge on feed item (api + language) — Native MangaHomeCard variant rendered a per-source colored badge (api - language) over the cover; the wired MangaHomeItem and KMP HomeFeedRow do not** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Partial — MangaHomeCard.kt:155-178 draws a colored TopStart badge `${api} - ${language}` over the cover (showSource), using per-api COLORS and AutoSubtitleText; however the component actually wired into Home is MangaHomeItem (no badge)
- **KMP:** No — HomeFeedRow.kt has no source badge; HomeFeedItem carries api/language but they are not surfaced on the card
- **Explanation:** There is an alternate native card (MangaHomeCard) with a source-colored badge that is NOT the one wired into Home (MangaHomeItem is). So this is not a strict Home regression, but worth flagging: if product ever expected the source badge on Home rows, neither the wired native screen nor KMP shows it. Listed for completeness; the wired native Home has no badge, so KMP matches the wired native behavior here.
- **Suggested fix:** No action required for parity with the wired native Home. If a source badge is desired, port MangaHomeCard's badge (per-source COLORS + 'api - language' label) into HomeFeedRow.

**⚪ [Low] Grid card cover scaling — Both use ContentScale.FillBounds on a 250dp poster with a 50dp black@0.3 scrim band and white 10sp bold title — parity is high here** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaSearchItems.kt SearchItems: 250dp Box, FillBounds AsyncImage, bottom 50dp Black@0.3 band, white 10sp bold 2-line centered title, card RoundedCornerShape(8.dp) elevation 2.dp
- **KMP:** Yes — HomeFeedGridCard.kt:50-92: 250dp Box, FillBounds YamiCoverImage, bottom 50dp Black@0.3 band, white 10sp bold 2-line centered title, card RoundedCornerShape(8.dp) elevation 2.dp
- **Explanation:** The grid poster card is a faithful port (GAP-HOME-10): identical 250dp height, FillBounds, 50dp 0.3-alpha scrim, white 10sp bold centered title, 8dp corners, 2dp elevation. One minor difference: native LazyVerticalGrid had no horizontal/vertical arrangement spacing (only contentPadding 8dp), while KMP adds Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.sm) between cells (HomeScreen.kt:368-369), so KMP cells have slightly more inter-item gap.

**⚪ [Low] Search overlay reachability from Home — Both flip an isSearching flag and swap Home<->Search in the same backstack entry; parity is high** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeRoute HomeScreenContainer:288-316 shows SearchScreen when isSearchVisible with a BackHandler to closeSearch; toggled via MangaViewModel.isSearching
- **KMP:** Yes — HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:93-116 shows SearchScreen when homeState.isSearching, onClose flips OnToggleSearch; HomeViewModel toggles isSearching
- **Explanation:** The search overlay-swap behavior is preserved. One gap: native installs a system BackHandler that closes search on back press (HomeRoute:289-294); the KMP route adapter KDoc explicitly defers the system-back-while-searching intercept, so on KMP a back press while searching may pop the Home destination instead of closing the search overlay.

### Search  `search`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 27 (🔴0 🟠4 🟡9 ⚪14)

> Native search is a HomeRoute overlay (toggled on MangaViewModel.isSearching) hosting a SearchAppBar + a two-segment ChipsRow (Search / Multi Search) over a 2-page HorizontalPager: page 0 is a single-source LazyVerticalGrid (MangaSearchItems, with a BannerAdView and a rich ErrorScreen offering Retry/Open-in-browser/Help), page 1 is a per-source LazyColumn of horizontal card rows (MultiRepoResults). A Settings-gear action opens a SearchBottomSheet with a collapsible Genres chip section (single-select, fires search immediately and blanks the query) and an Order-By dropdown (fires immediately, carries the selected genre). Single search is driven by MangaViewModel.startSearch and multi by HomeViewModel.fetchAllSearchResults. KMP reproduces the structure faithfully in a clean MVI slice (SearchViewModel/State/Intent/Effect + ui SearchScreen/SearchFilterSheet) and even matches several exact metrics (Adaptive 160dp grid, 250dp card with Black@0.3 band 10sp bold title, 140x200 multi card Black@0.6 top-start label, 24dp section gap, transparent labelLarge field), but diverges in behavior and chrome: filters only apply via a deferred Apply button (no live filtering), the filter icon is Tune not Settings, the single-result error path is retry-only (no open-in-browser/help), there are no banner ads anywhere, system-back while searching is not intercepted (will pop Home), the sort/genre routing is mutually-exclusive (genre overrides sort, unlike native's combined SORT), the sort dropdown displays a default it never commits, genre filtering keeps the query instead of clearing it, and several strings/labels (Filter & Sort, Order By, Apply Filters, Multi Search casing) and chip colors/icon differ. No search-history or query-suggestions feature exists on either side. Headline regressions: missing system-back handling, lost open-in-browser/help error recovery, deferred-only filter apply, and the sort/genre + sort-default commit logic bugs.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Search</summary>

**🟠 [High] Search filter sheet — genre selection behavior — Native applies a genre immediately on chip tap; KMP defers all genre changes to the Apply button** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchBottomSheet.kt:130 onClick = { onGenreClicked(genre) } wired to MangaViewModel.onGenreClicked (MangaViewModel.kt:101) which calls startSearch(SearchType.GENRES(...)) right away, no Apply needed
- **KMP:** Partial — SearchFilterSheet.kt:114 onClick only mutates local draftGenre; the search runs only when the Apply Button (SearchFilterSheet.kt:164) dispatches OnApplyFilters
- **Explanation:** In native, tapping a genre chip fires a new GENRES search instantly (the sheet stays open and results update live behind it). In KMP nothing happens until the user taps Apply, which also dismisses the sheet (SearchScreen.kt:218-221 sets showFilters=false). This changes the entire filter UX: native = live filtering while browsing chips, KMP = batch commit + close. Also the sort dropdown in native fires immediately on selection (SearchBottomSheet.kt:187 onSortSelected -> onSortClick -> startSearch) whereas KMP only stages draftSort.
- **Suggested fix:** Match the native immediate-apply behavior: dispatch the genre/sort intent on chip/dropdown selection (not only on Apply), and keep the sheet open so results update live behind it. If a draft+Apply model is intentionally desired, document it as a deliberate UX change.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (immediate search on tap; sheet stays open): SearchBottomSheet.kt:130 genre chip onClick = { onGenreClicked(genre) } -> SearchScreen.kt:208 passes it straight through -> MangaViewModel.kt:101-113 onGenreClicked() launches and immediately calls startSearch(SearchType.GENRES(...)), no Apply needed. Sort: SearchBottomSheet.kt:187-188 onClick -> onSortSelected(option, selectedGenre) -> SearchScreen.kt:202-205 onSortClick(...) -> MangaViewModel.kt:91-99 immediately startSearch(SearchType.SORT(...)). The Apply Button (SearchBottomSheet.kt:197-205) is wired onClick = onDismiss ONLY (SearchScreen.kt:197 onDismiss = { ShowSetting = false }) — it just closes the sheet and runs no search; genre tap never calls onDismiss, so the sheet stays open while results update live. KMP (deferred to Apply, which also closes the sheet): SearchFilterSheet.kt:114 genre chip onClick = { draftGenre = if (selected) null else genre } mutates local draft only; SearchFilterSheet.kt:154 sort onClick = { draftSort = option } mutates local draft only. The ONLY outward emission is SearchFilterSheet.kt:165 Apply Button onClick = { onApply(draftSort, listOfNotNull(draftGenre)) }. In the host, SearchScreen.kt:218-221 onApply dispatches SearchIntent.OnApplyFilters(...) AND sets showFilters = false (dismisses sheet). SearchViewModel.kt:42-60 + 77-81: only OnApplyFilters (plus OnQueryChange, OnModeTabChange) reaches runSearch; there is no genre/sort intent, confirmed by SearchIntent.kt:12-34 (no per-chip/per-sort intent exists). So nothing runs until Apply. Net: native = live filtering, sheet persists across chip/sort taps; KMP = batch commit + close on Apply. Minor secondary nuance: native genre tap always re-fires a GENRES search (no toggle), KMP draft toggles/clears on re-tap (SearchFilterSheet.kt:114) — does not affect the timing claim.

**🟠 [High] Search filter sheet — genre clears the query — Native genre filter forces query="" (genre-only browse); KMP keeps the current query and joins genres into the search** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaViewModel.onGenreClicked (MangaViewModel.kt:101-113) calls startSearch(SearchType.GENRES(genres = type, query = "")) — the text query is discarded
- **KMP:** No — SearchViewModel.runSingleSearch (SearchViewModel.kt:101-117) builds SearchMode.GENRES while passing state.value.query unchanged; searchTypeOf (HomeMappers.kt:143) puts that query into SearchType.GENRES(query = query, ...)
- **Explanation:** Native treats a genre tap as 'browse this genre' and intentionally blanks the text query, so the source's genre-listing endpoint is hit with no text term. KMP keeps whatever the user typed, so the GENRES SearchType carries a non-empty query. Depending on the per-source fetchSearchDataF implementation this yields different (possibly empty/incorrect) results versus native, a real behavioral regression in the genre-filter path.
- **Suggested fix:** When applying a genre filter, clear the query before running the GENRES search (or pass query="" into searchTypeOf for the GENRES branch) to mirror MangaViewModel.onGenreClicked.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): MangaViewModel.onGenreClicked (native-app/.../presentation/common/viewmodel/MangaViewModel.kt:101-113) calls startSearch(SearchType.GENRES(genres = type, query = "")) — query is hard-forced to "" and the live searchQuery is never read. This is wired as an IMMEDIATE per-chip action: SearchBottomSheet.kt:130 `onClick = { onGenreClicked(genre) }` passes the single tapped genre string; SearchScreen.kt:208 binds `onGenreClicked = onGenreClicked`; HomeRoute.kt:224 binds it to mangaViewModel::onGenreClicked. Native's sort path is separate (onSortClick, MangaViewModel.kt:91-99) and DOES pass the query — so genre-tap = blank-query genre browse is deliberate. KMP: SearchViewModel.runSingleSearch (presentation/.../search/SearchViewModel.kt:101-118) passes `query = query` (the live state.value.query, threaded from onApplyFilters at SearchViewModel.kt:77-81 → runSearch → runSingleSearch) unchanged; genres come from state.value.selectedGenres; mode resolves to SearchMode.GENRES when genres non-empty (line 105-109). searchTypeOf (data/.../mapper/HomeMappers.kt:143-146) maps SearchMode.GENRES → SearchType.GENRES(query = query, genres = genres.joinToString(",")) — query preserved, never blanked. SearchRepositoryImpl.searchSource (data/.../repository/SearchRepositoryImpl.kt:75-79) dispatches that SearchType onto repo.fetchSearchDataF, same source method native uses. Source impact (severity basis): several sources interpolate query into the GENRES URL — MangaworldItRepository.kt:69 `archive?keyword=${searchType.query}&genre=${searchType.genres}`, ManhwawebEsRepository.kt:111 `buscar=${searchType.query}...generes=...`. Native sends keyword empty; KMP sends the user's text, yielding a different (text+genre intersection) result set. Additional nuance (makes regression at least as bad as claimed): KMP runSearch (SearchViewModel.kt:88-94) early-returns and clears results when query.isBlank(), so a genre-only browse with no text cannot fire at all in KMP — native's "blank-query genre browse" is structurally impossible in KMP. Also the UX differs: native fires on chip tap; KMP defers to the Apply button (SearchFilterSheet.kt:114,165). SearchType definitions are structurally identical in both apps (shared/.../SearchType.kt vs native-app/.../SearchType.kt), so the difference is purely in what query value is supplied.

**🟠 [High] Search single-result error state — actions — Native error screen offers Retry + Open in Browser + Help; KMP single-result error offers only Retry** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchScreen.kt:145-156 renders ErrorScreen with onRetry, onOpenInBrowser, onHelp; ErrorScreen.kt:85-102 shows three IconAboveTextButtons (Retry / Open in browser / Help)
- **KMP:** No — SearchScreen.kt:362-366 SingleResults uses YamiErrorState(message, retryLabel, onRetry) — the retry-only overload. The 5-arg YamiErrorState with onOpenInWebView/onHelp exists (YamiStateViews.kt:183-192) but is NOT used here
- **Explanation:** On a single-source search failure native gives the user two recovery affordances beyond retry: 'Open in browser' (to bypass Cloudflare/anti-bot via WebView) and 'Help' (help video). KMP drops both — the only option is Retry. The 'Open in browser' path is the primary way native users get past 403/Cloudflare blocks, so losing it materially degrades error recovery. The webview/help wiring is also absent from the route adapter (HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:93-116 passes no such callbacks to SearchScreen).
- **Suggested fix:** Use the richer YamiErrorState overload (openInWebView + help) for SingleResults, wire onOpenInWebView to Screen.WebView(activeSource baseUrl) and onHelp to the help video, and thread those callbacks through SearchScreen from the route adapter.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/.../home/ui/screens/search/SearchScreen.kt:145-156 — on State.Error for page 0 (single-source Search tab) renders ErrorScreen(message, onRetry={onSearchChange(localQuery)}, onOpenInBrowser={onOpenInWebView()}, onHelp={onHelp()}). native-app/.../common/screens/ErrorScreen.kt:79-103 renders a Row of THREE IconAboveTextButtons: Retry (Refresh), Open-in-browser (WebAsset, R.string.action_open_in_browser), Help (HelpOutline). The SearchScreen call site (native-app/.../navigation/routes/HomeRoute.kt:295-316) passes onOpenInWebView + onHelp; onOpenInWebView (HomeRoute.kt:164-178) navigates to Screen.WebView(getCurrentBaseUrl(), getCurrentApi()) — the in-app browser path used to bypass source/Cloudflare blocks (fully functional). KMP: ui/.../search/SearchScreen.kt:352-389, SingleResults UiState.Error branch (lines 362-366) calls YamiErrorState(message, retryLabel=stringResource(retry), onRetry) — the retry-ONLY 4-arg overload defined at ui/.../components/YamiStateViews.kt:130-167. The 5+-arg multi-action YamiErrorState (Retry + Open-in-WebView + Help) EXISTS at YamiStateViews.kt:182-239 but is NOT called by SingleResults. The route adapter composeApp/.../navigation/routes/HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:93-116 invokes SearchScreen with only viewModel/onNavigateToDetails/onClose/coverModel — no webview/help callbacks; and the KMP SearchScreen signature (SearchScreen.kt:114-121) has no such params at all. (HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:156-170 wires onOpenWebView/onHelp for the Home grid, confirming the capability is intentionally absent from the search overlay.) So KMP single-result search error offers only Retry; native offers Retry + Open-in-Browser + Help. Two recovery affordances are dropped, including the functional Cloudflare/403 WebView bypass. MINOR CORRECTION (does not change verdict): the native onHelp lambda on the SEARCH wiring path is an empty stub (HomeRoute.kt:179-181: /* show help dialog, etc. */), so the native Help button on the search error screen renders but is a no-op on this exact route (it IS wired on the Home grid path via showHelpDialog/HelpVideoDialog, HomeScreen.kt:303,376,465-467). The genuinely lost-and-functional affordance on the search path is Open-in-Browser. Claim severity High is appropriate: Open-in-Browser is the primary native path past 403/Cloudflare blocks and is absent from the KMP single-result error.

**🟠 [High] Search overlay — system back handling — Native intercepts system Back while searching to close the overlay; KMP defers the back intercept (only the top-bar Close works)** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeRoute.kt:288-294 BackHandler(enabled = isSearchVisible) { closeSearch() }
- **KMP:** No — HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:27-29 KDoc explicitly states 'The system-back-while-searching intercept is deferred ... the Search top-bar close button ... is the canonical way to leave'; no BackHandler is registered
- **Explanation:** In native, pressing the device/system Back button while the search overlay is open returns to Home. In KMP there is no back intercept, so system Back on the search overlay will pop the Home destination off the nav backstack (leaving the app/Home tab) instead of just closing the search overlay. This is a real navigation regression and a likely user-confusing behavior.
- **Suggested fix:** Register a BackHandler (or PredictiveBackHandler) gated on homeState.isSearching that dispatches HomeIntent.OnToggleSearch, matching the native BackHandler.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/navigation/routes/HomeRoute.kt:288-294 — inside `if (isSearchVisible) {` (L288) it registers `BackHandler(enabled = isSearchVisible) { closeSearch() }` (L289-294) before rendering SearchScreen. `closeSearch()` is defined in /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/common/viewmodel/MangaViewModel.kt:145-146 as `isSearching.value = !isSearching.value`, which flips the overlay off WITHIN the same backstack entry (the overlay is an isSearching content swap, not a nav destination). So device/system Back while searching dismisses the overlay and returns to Home content. Claim's cited L288-294 is accurate. KMP (new app): The claimed file is actually under /composeApp, not /ui (minor path inaccuracy in the claim). /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:27-30 KDoc verbatim: \"The system-back-while-searching intercept is deferred (same gap the legacy route documented); the Search top-bar close button (`SearchEffect.Close` ...) is the canonical way to leave the overlay.\" The composable body (L78-174) registers NO BackHandler; the search branch (L93-116) renders SearchScreen with only `onClose = { homeViewModel.submit(HomeIntent.OnToggleSearch) }`. KMP SearchScreen (/Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/search/SearchScreen.kt) has NO `androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler` import and no back intercept — its only exit path is `onClose` (L118/128/142/156 `SearchEffect.Close -> onClose()`), i.e. the top-bar Close button. No commonMain BackHandler exists anywhere: /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/App.kt:110-114 and 179-183 document that BackHandler calls from upstream Home/Library blocks were intentionally dropped (\"there's no commonMain BackHandler shim yet ... TODO Phase 10.x: add a commonMain BackHandler expect/actual\") and \"Recursive Grep for `BackHandler` across `:composeApp/commonMain` matches ZERO live references file-wide.\" The BackHandler grep hits in ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt, MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute.kt, etc. are all KDoc prose documenting the ABSENCE of BackHandler, not live calls — verified by reading the matched lines (e.g. \"**No `BackHandler`**: matches sibling rework adapters deliberately\"). The behavioral regression is real: native closes the search overlay on system Back; KMP does not (system Back is left to default Compose Navigation, which acts on the Home backstack entry rather than dismissing the overlay). Minor caveat on the claim's explanation: the exact outcome (\"pop the Home destination off the nav backstack\") depends on whether Home is the current start/back-stack state (start destination is Welcome or Library per App.kt:161-163, with Home a bottom-nav tab), so system Back may pop toward Library or exit rather than precisely \"leaving the Home tab\" — but the substance (overlay is NOT dismissed by system Back) is correct.

**🟡 [Medium] Search results grid + multi-repo — banner ads — Native shows a BannerAdView above both the single-search grid and the multi-repo list; KMP shows no ads** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaSearchItems.kt:51 BannerAdView() above the LazyVerticalGrid; MultiRepoResults.kt:56 BannerAdView() above the LazyColumn. SearchScreen.kt imports interleaveAds/ListEntryWithAd (lines 37-39)
- **KMP:** No — neither SingleResults (SearchScreen.kt:352-389) nor MultiRepoResults (SearchScreen.kt:397-426) renders any ad; grep finds zero BannerAdView usage anywhere under ui/
- **Explanation:** Native monetizes the search surfaces with a fixed banner ad above each results list. KMP renders no banner at all, removing a revenue surface and changing layout (results start ~banner-height higher). This is a deliberate-looking omission but is a parity gap against the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the cross-platform banner ad slot above the single-search grid and the multi-repo list (or confirm ads are intentionally deferred for the KMP build).

**🟡 [Medium] Search filter sheet — collapsible Genres section — Native genres section has a tappable collapsible header (expand/collapse chevron); KMP renders genres flat with no collapse** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchBottomSheet.kt:112-147 SectionHeader(title=Genres, expanded, onHeaderClick) with KeyboardArrowUp/Down icon (SectionHeader at lines 212-235) wrapping an AnimatedVisibility FlowRow
- **KMP:** No — SearchFilterSheet.kt:102-124 renders a plain Genres Text label + FlowRow, no header row, no expand/collapse, no chevron icon
- **Explanation:** Native lets the user collapse the (potentially long) genre chip list via a header with an up/down arrow; the genre area is also internally scrollable (heightIn max 300.dp + verticalScroll, SearchBottomSheet.kt:120-123). KMP drops the collapse control and the per-section scroll cap, instead scrolling the whole sheet column (SearchFilterSheet.kt:85). Behavior + affordance regression on sources with many genres.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a collapsible Genres section header with an expand/collapse chevron (and consider the heightIn(max=300dp)+verticalScroll cap) to match SearchBottomSheet.

**🟡 [Medium] Search filter sheet — section titles / labels — Sheet title, sort label, and Apply button text all differ from native strings** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — 'Filter & Sort' (filter_sort_title, strings.xml:230), 'Genres' (genres:231), 'Order By' (order_by:232), 'Apply Filters' (apply_filters:234)
- **KMP:** No (different) — 'Filters' (search_filter_sheet_title, strings.xml:377), 'Genres' (search_genres:378), 'Sort' (search_sort:379), 'Apply' (search_apply_filters:381)
- **Explanation:** The filter sheet copy diverges: native title 'Filter & Sort' vs KMP 'Filters'; native sort label 'Order By' vs KMP 'Sort'; native button 'Apply Filters' vs KMP 'Apply'. These are user-visible string regressions versus the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the KMP strings to native: 'Filter & Sort', 'Order By', 'Apply Filters' (and verify Arabic translations exist for each).

**🟡 [Medium] Search filter sheet — no-filters fallback — Native shows a full-screen 200dp centered 'filters not ready' message AND hides the Apply button; KMP shows a short inline text but STILL renders the Apply button** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchBottomSheet.kt:89-103 when both sortTypes & genres empty: a 200dp Box centered Text(search_filters_not_ready) then return@ModalBottomSheet (no Apply button)
- **KMP:** Partial — SearchFilterSheet.kt:95-100 shows a small bodyMedium Text(search_no_filters) but falls through to render the Apply Button (SearchFilterSheet.kt:164) anyway
- **Explanation:** When the active source exposes no sort types and no genres, native shows a prominent centered 'filters not ready' panel and removes the Apply button entirely (nothing to apply). KMP shows a small left-aligned line and still shows an Apply button that, when tapped, re-runs a NORMAL search and closes the sheet. Different layout + a meaningless Apply affordance. Also the message wording differs (search_filters_not_ready vs search_no_filters: 'This source has no filters.').
- **Suggested fix:** In the no-filters case render a centered message and suppress the Apply button (early return), matching SearchBottomSheet; align the wording.

**🟡 [Medium] Search mode selector — chip styling (icon/colors/border) — Native mode chips use the Done icon with custom primary container/label colors and an explicit border; KMP chips use the Check icon with default FilterChip colors and no custom border** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — ChipsRow/ChipItemRow (ChipsRow.kt:50-82): leadingIcon Icons.Default.Done tinted onPrimary, selectedContainerColor=primary, selectedLabelColor=onPrimary, custom filterChipBorder (primary when selected), defaultMinSize(minHeight=32.dp), padding(horizontal=4.dp)
- **KMP:** Partial — SearchModeChip (SearchScreen.kt:261-273): FilterChip with leadingIcon YamiIcons.Check, NO custom colors (M3 defaults), NO custom border, RoundedCornerShape(16.dp); row uses spacing.sm(8dp) gap + md/sm padding
- **Explanation:** Native selected mode chip is a solid primary-colored chip (primary container, onPrimary label, Done check tinted onPrimary, primary border). KMP uses default FilterChip selected styling (tonal secondaryContainer-ish) with a plain Check icon and no border override. Selected-chip color, icon glyph (Done vs Check), border, and per-chip min-height/padding all diverge — a clearly different look for the Search / Multi Search selector.
- **Suggested fix:** Port ChipItemRow's colors (selectedContainerColor=primary, selectedLabelColor=onPrimary), the primary border, the Done icon tint, and defaultMinSize(32.dp)+horizontal 4.dp padding to SearchModeChip.

**🟡 [Medium] Search top bar — close button clears query — Native close button clears the query (onQueryChange("")) in addition to toggling search off; KMP close just emits Close** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchAppBar.kt:51-55 navigationIcon onClick = { onToggleSearch(); onQueryChange("") } — closing search resets the query state
- **KMP:** No — SearchScreen.kt:291-297 the Close navigation YamiIconButton onClick = onClose -> dispatches SearchIntent.OnClose -> SearchEffect.Close (SearchViewModel.kt:58), which does NOT clear state.query
- **Explanation:** In native, closing the search overlay also wipes the query, so re-opening starts blank. In KMP the SearchViewModel is a separate koin VM whose state persists; OnClose never resets query/results, so re-opening search shows the previous query and results. Whether the VM is recreated on next open depends on koin scoping (koinViewModel at HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:84) — if retained, this is a stale-state regression.
- **Suggested fix:** On OnClose, reset query/single/multi/selected filters in the VM (or scope the SearchViewModel so it's recreated per overlay open) to mirror the native clear-on-close.

**🟡 [Medium] Search results grid — single-result card source-aware image request — Native builds a per-source ImageRequest (with source headers) via buildImageRequest(context,url,api); KMP passes only a plain cover URL string** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaSearchItems.SearchItems (MangaSearchItems.kt:101-106) AsyncImage(model = buildImageRequest(context, manga.imageUrl, manga.api), imageLoader = getImageLoader()) — request carries source-specific headers/loader
- **KMP:** Partial — HomeFeedGridCard resolves coverUrl = coverModel?.invoke(item) as? String ?: item.coverUrl (HomeFeedGridCard.kt:50) and HomeReworkScreenRoute sets coverModel = { it.coverUrl } (HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:91) — a bare URL string; per-source auth headers are said to attach at the Coil ImageLoader level
- **Explanation:** Native attaches per-source request configuration (headers/referer needed by many manga sources to avoid hotlink/Cloudflare blocks) on a per-image ImageRequest built from the manga's api. KMP only passes a plain URL and relies on a global ImageLoader to inject headers (HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:88-91 KDoc). For sources that need per-source/per-host headers, covers may fail to load in KMP where they loaded in native. Same concern applies to the multi-repo MultiRepoCard (SearchScreen.kt:489) and is the more relevant data-layer parity risk.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify the global Coil ImageLoader attaches the correct per-source/per-host headers for every source; if not, thread a per-source request model through coverModel so search covers load identically to native.

**🟡 [Medium] Search filter sheet — sort dropdown default selection — Native pre-selects the first sort type as the displayed value; KMP shows draftSort ?: first(), but applying without touching the dropdown commits null** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchScreen.kt:193 selectedSort defaults to sortTypes.first() (or 'No Sort Types'); the dropdown always shows a concrete value and onSortSelected fires immediately
- **KMP:** Partial — SearchFilterSheet.kt:136 displays draftSort ?: filters.sortTypes.first() but draftSort stays null until the user opens the dropdown and picks (SearchFilterSheet.kt:154); Apply commits draftSort which may be null even though a value is displayed
- **Explanation:** Native always has a concrete selected sort (first type) and fires the sort search as soon as the sheet logic runs / a value is chosen. In KMP the dropdown DISPLAYS the first sort type but the underlying draftSort is null until explicitly chosen; tapping Apply then sends sort=null with SearchMode resolved as NORMAL (since selectedSort==null, SearchViewModel.kt:105-108), so the user sees 'Latest' selected yet gets a plain search. This display/commit mismatch is a real logic bug.
- **Suggested fix:** Initialize draftSort to filters.sortTypes.firstOrNull() so the displayed value and the committed value agree, matching native's first-type default.

**🟡 [Medium] Search filter sheet — applying sort also carries the selected genre — Native onSortClick passes both the sort type AND the currently selected genre into SearchType.SORT; KMP applies sort and genre but routes mode by precedence so a genre present forces GENRES (ignoring sort)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchBottomSheet.kt:187-188 onSortSelected(option, selectedGenre) -> MangaViewModel.onSortClick(type, query, genres) -> startSearch(SearchType.SORT(query, sortType=type, genres)) — sort + genre combined
- **KMP:** No (different) — SearchViewModel.runSingleSearch (SearchViewModel.kt:105-109): if genres non-empty -> SearchMode.GENRES (sort dropped); else if sort != null -> SORT; the two are mutually exclusive by precedence
- **Explanation:** Native's SORT search carries the chosen genre alongside the sort type (SearchType.SORT has a genres field). KMP's runSingleSearch picks GENRES whenever any genre is selected, which never produces a SORT request that also includes the genre — so selecting both a sort and a genre behaves differently than native (native = sort+genre combined; KMP = genre-only, sort ignored). Functional regression for sources whose SORT endpoint accepts a genre.
- **Suggested fix:** When both a sort and a genre are selected, dispatch SearchMode.SORT with both sort and genres populated (matching SearchType.SORT(query, sortType, genres)) rather than letting genre presence override into GENRES.

**⚪ [Low] Search filter sheet — genre is single-select — Both are single-select, but KMP carries genres as a List that gets joined with commas; native carries exactly one genre string** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — selectedGenre is a single String (SearchBottomSheet.kt:61); SearchType.GENRES(genres: String) is one value
- **KMP:** Partial — SearchFilterSheet emits listOfNotNull(draftGenre) (SearchFilterSheet.kt:165) (0 or 1), but HomeMappers.searchTypeOf joins with genres.joinToString(",") (HomeMappers.kt:141,145)
- **Explanation:** KMP preserves single-select at the UI (draftGenre is a single nullable), so functionally it matches native today. The comma-join is harmless for a 0/1-element list but is a latent shape mismatch: if the contract ever passes >1 genre, native's single-genre source endpoints would receive a comma string they never expect. Documenting as a low-risk divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Keep genre strictly single in the domain contract (pass the single genre string, not a joined list) to match the source SearchType.GENRES shape, or assert the list size is <=1.

**⚪ [Low] Search top bar — filter action icon — Native filter/settings action uses the Settings (gear) icon; KMP uses the Tune (sliders) icon** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchScreen.kt:108 Icon(Icons.Default.Settings, contentDescription = R.string.title_settings) opens the filter sheet
- **KMP:** No (different icon) — SearchScreen.kt:344 YamiIconButton(icon = YamiIcons.Tune, contentDescription = Res.string.search_filters)
- **Explanation:** The action that opens the filter/sort sheet is rendered with a gear (Settings) icon in native and a Tune (sliders) icon in KMP. Different glyph and different content description ('Settings' vs 'Filters'). Visual + a11y label divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Use the gear (Settings) icon and a matching content description for the filter action, or confirm Tune is an intentional improvement.

**⚪ [Low] Multi-repo results — error rendering — Native shows raw 'Error: <message>' per source; KMP shows a mapped/localized AppError message** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MultiRepoResults.kt:110-113 Text(text = "Error: ${state.message}", color = error)
- **KMP:** No (different) — SearchScreen.kt:450-454 RepoSection error branch shows rememberSearchErrorMessages()(state.error) (a localized bucket string), no 'Error:' prefix
- **Explanation:** Per-source failure text differs: native prints the literal repo error message with an 'Error: ' prefix; KMP prints a generic localized category string (network/storage/etc.). KMP is arguably nicer but it is a content divergence — the exact failure text native showed is gone.
- **Suggested fix:** If preserving native behavior, surface the underlying message; otherwise document the localized bucket strings as an intentional improvement.

**⚪ [Low] Multi-repo results — empty state — KMP renders a 'No results found' empty state when the multi map is empty; native renders nothing (just the banner + empty list)** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — MultiRepoResults.kt:59-77 iterates the map with no empty-state branch; an empty map simply shows the BannerAdView and an empty LazyColumn
- **KMP:** Yes — SearchScreen.kt:403-406 if (results.isEmpty()) YamiEmptyState(title = search_empty)
- **Explanation:** On the Multi Search tab before any query (empty map), native shows just the (empty) list under the banner, while KMP shows a centered 'No results found' empty state. This is a new state KMP introduced; minor but visible divergence in the idle multi-tab.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide whether the idle multi tab should show an empty state; native showed none. Consider distinguishing idle (no query yet) from genuinely-empty results.

**⚪ [Low] Search single-result empty state — KMP shows a 'No results found' empty state for an empty success list; native shows an empty grid (only the banner)** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — MangaSearchItems.kt:54-72 renders the LazyVerticalGrid unconditionally; an empty list yields an empty grid with the banner, no message
- **KMP:** Yes — SearchScreen.kt:368-369 if (state.data.isEmpty()) YamiEmptyState(title = search_empty)
- **Explanation:** For a single-source search returning zero results, native shows an empty grid (no explicit 'no results' messaging), whereas KMP shows a centered empty state. Note the initial idle state in KMP is UiState.Success(emptyList()) (SearchState.kt:36), so on first open KMP immediately shows 'No results found' before the user types anything — native shows a blank grid in that idle case.
- **Suggested fix:** Differentiate the pristine/idle state (no query entered) from an actual zero-result search; native showed no message on idle. Avoid showing 'No results found' before the first query.

**⚪ [Low] Search mode selector — Multi Search label casing — Native label is 'Multi Search'; KMP label is 'Multi search'** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — strings.xml:754 <string name="multi_search">Multi Search</string>
- **KMP:** No (different) — strings.xml:375 <string name="search_tab_multi">Multi search</string>
- **Explanation:** The multi-search tab/chip label differs only in capitalization ('Multi Search' vs 'Multi search'). Subtle but a literal string mismatch against the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Change search_tab_multi to 'Multi Search' to match native casing.

**⚪ [Low] Multi-repo fan-out — stale query cancellation — Native never cancels a previous multi-repo fan-out; KMP cancels prior single+multi jobs on every new query/mode change** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** No cancellation — HomeViewModel.fetchAllSearchResults (HomeViewModel.kt:55-77) launches without storing/cancelling a prior job; a new multi search races against the old one
- **KMP:** Yes — SearchViewModel.runSearch (SearchViewModel.kt:88-99) calls singleSearchJob?.cancel() and multiSearchJob?.cancel() before each search
- **Explanation:** KMP intentionally improves on native by cancelling the previous fan-out (documented locked-decision in SearchViewModel KDoc). This is a behavioral divergence from the source of truth (native could show late results from an abandoned query). Flagging as a deliberate improvement rather than a bug, but it IS a behavior change to be aware of.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed if the cancel-previous behavior is intended; document it as an intentional correctness improvement over native.

**⚪ [Low] Search query — submit vs live search semantics — Both are submit-driven, but native keeps separate VMs (single via MangaViewModel, multi via HomeViewModel) and ties the active page to which search fires; KMP routes both through one SearchViewModel keyed on state.mode** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchScreen.kt:95-98: onSearch fires onMultiSearch(localQuery) if page==1 and onSearchChange(localQuery) if page==0; only the visible tab's search runs on submit
- **KMP:** Partial — SearchTopBar onSearch dispatches OnQueryChange (SearchScreen.kt:177); SearchViewModel.onQueryChange runs runSearch(query, state.value.mode) (SearchViewModel.kt:67-69), so only the current mode searches — equivalent, but the clear-X also runs an empty search (SearchScreen.kt:315-318) which native's clear-X did not do
- **Explanation:** Functionally the submit-fires-current-tab behavior matches. One subtle divergence: KMP's clear-X (trailing icon) calls onSearch("") which runs an empty search and (per runSearch) resets results to empty (SearchViewModel.kt:91-93). Native's clear-X (SearchAppBar.kt:81) only calls onQueryChange("") which updates the text field but does NOT trigger startSearch — native leaves the previous results on screen until the user submits. Minor results-clearing divergence on clear.
- **Suggested fix:** If strict parity is desired, make the clear-X only reset the text field without re-running a search; otherwise document the clear-also-clears-results behavior.

**⚪ [Low] Single-result card title band — exact padding — Title text padding inside the 50dp bottom band differs slightly** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaSearchItems.kt:136 the title Text has padding(vertical = 1.dp, horizontal = 4.dp) and is .align(Center) over a separate Black@0.3 box
- **KMP:** Partial — HomeFeedGridCard.kt:84-86 title Text has padding(horizontal = 4.dp) only (no vertical 1.dp) inside a contentAlignment=Center band
- **Explanation:** Both use a 250dp box, FillBounds cover, 50dp Black@0.3 bottom band, white 10sp bold 2-line centered title — a faithful port. The only nit: native adds vertical = 1.dp padding on the title text; KMP omits it. Negligible visually but a literal divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Add vertical = 1.dp to the title text padding in HomeFeedGridCard to match MangaSearchItems exactly (or accept as immaterial).

**⚪ [Low] Multi-repo card — title band padding — Top-start title label vertical padding differs (native 4dp vs KMP 2dp)** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — MultiRepoResults.kt:178 the title label Box uses padding(horizontal = 6.dp, vertical = 4.dp)
- **KMP:** No (different) — SearchScreen.kt:514 MultiRepoCard label Box uses padding(horizontal = 6.dp, vertical = 2.dp)
- **Explanation:** The multi-repo card's translucent (Black@0.6, rounded bottomEnd 4) top-start title label uses vertical = 4.dp in native but vertical = 2.dp in KMP. The card size (140x200), shape (rounded 8), elevation (4dp), Crop scale, white bodySmall 1-line ellipsis all match. Only the label vertical padding is off by 2dp.
- **Suggested fix:** Change the MultiRepoCard label vertical padding to 4.dp to match MultiRepoResults.

**⚪ [Low] Multi-repo section list — LazyRow content padding — Native multi-repo LazyRow has horizontal contentPadding of 4dp and 12dp item spacing; KMP has no contentPadding and 8dp item spacing** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — MultiRepoResults.kt:116-118 LazyRow(horizontalArrangement = spacedBy(12.dp), contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 4.dp))
- **KMP:** No (different) — SearchScreen.kt:463 LazyRow(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.sm /*8dp*/)) with no contentPadding
- **Explanation:** Within each multi-repo source section, native spaces cards 12.dp apart with a 4.dp horizontal content padding; KMP spaces them 8.dp apart with no content padding. The first/last card edge inset and inter-card gap both differ slightly.
- **Suggested fix:** Set the multi-repo LazyRow item spacing to 12.dp and add contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 4.dp) to match MultiRepoResults.

**⚪ [Low] Multi-repo section header — typography weight — KMP adds FontWeight.Bold to the source-name header; native uses titleLarge primary without an explicit bold override** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — MultiRepoResults.kt:93-98 Text(apiName, style = titleLarge, color = primary) — no fontWeight override (uses titleLarge's default weight)
- **KMP:** No (different) — SearchScreen.kt:437-443 Text(api, style = titleLarge, fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold, color = primary)
- **Explanation:** The per-source section header is titleLarge + primary on both sides, but KMP forces FontWeight.Bold on top of titleLarge while native relies on the titleLarge default weight. Depending on the type scale this makes the KMP header heavier than native.
- **Suggested fix:** Remove the explicit FontWeight.Bold (or confirm the desired weight) so the multi-repo section header matches native's titleLarge default.

**⚪ [Low] Search top bar — query field height — Native search field is a fixed 56.dp tall with end padding 8.dp; KMP field has no fixed height and uses vertical xs(4dp) padding** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — SearchAppBar.kt:109-113 OutlinedTextField modifier .fillMaxWidth().height(56.dp).padding(end = 8.dp)
- **KMP:** No (different) — SearchScreen.kt:337-339 OutlinedTextField modifier .fillMaxWidth().padding(vertical = spacing.xs /*4dp*/) — no height constraint, no end padding
- **Explanation:** Native pins the in-app-bar search field to 56.dp with an 8.dp trailing inset; KMP lets the field size itself and adds 4.dp vertical padding instead. The field's vertical footprint and trailing spacing in the top bar differ. Both use transparent borders/containers + labelLarge text style (matched).
- **Suggested fix:** Constrain the KMP search field to height(56.dp) and add padding(end = 8.dp) to match SearchAppBar's metrics.

**⚪ [Low] Search single-result grid — content padding — Native grid uses asymmetric content padding (h=8dp, v=4dp) with per-card 8dp padding; KMP uses uniform 8dp content padding plus 8dp grid arrangement spacing** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaSearchItems.kt:55-56 LazyVerticalGrid(columns=Adaptive(160dp), contentPadding=PaddingValues(horizontal=8dp, vertical=4dp)); each SearchItems Card has .padding(8.dp) (MangaSearchItems.kt:90) and no grid arrangement spacing
- **KMP:** No (different) — SearchScreen.kt:373-376 LazyVerticalGrid(columns=Adaptive(160dp), contentPadding=PaddingValues(spacing.sm /*8dp all sides*/), horizontalArrangement=spacedBy(8dp), verticalArrangement=spacedBy(8dp)); cards have no individual padding
- **Explanation:** Columns match (Adaptive 160dp). But native achieves spacing via per-card 8dp padding + (8h/4v) content padding (no arrangement spacing), while KMP uses 8dp arrangement spacing + uniform 8dp content padding and no per-card padding. Net inter-card gap (native ~16dp from two adjacent 8dp paddings vs KMP 8dp) and outer vertical inset (native 4dp vs KMP 8dp) differ — visibly looser/tighter grid.
- **Suggested fix:** Reproduce native's spacing exactly: drop arrangement spacing and instead use 8dp per-card padding with contentPadding(horizontal=8dp, vertical=4dp), or recompute the arrangement to net the same gaps.

### Library  `library`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 27 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡10 ⚪14)

> Native renders the Library as a grid of MangaCards where the title + 4 detail-icon counts are OVERLAID on the cover behind a bottom gradient scrim, with affinity/delete buttons stacked top-end on the cover, a source badge top-start, a custom VerticalGridFastScroller, a continuous "items per row" slider (auto/0..8), a toggleable full-width SearchAppBar, an Inbox empty-state with the tab name, an animated Lottie download preloader, and a 3-tab bottom sheet (Filter chips / Sort chips+switch / Display slider+5 switches). The KMP rework keeps the same MVI-driven feature surface (filter/sort/category/display toggles/per-card actions) but diverges heavily in presentation: the card title and metrics are rendered in a Row/captions BELOW the cover (not overlaid), the items-per-row slider was replaced by a 3-value GridDensity enum, search is an always-visible inline OutlinedTextField (no toggle), the empty state is plain text with no icon/library-name, the download indicator is a static count badge instead of the Lottie animation, the fast-scroller is gone, and several extra per-card captions (last-read / added / progress) were added that native never showed. KMP also adds a multi-select selection mode and per-card delete confirmation dialog that native does not have. Filter-chip order (BOOKMARKED/COMPLETED) and category-tab order (LIKED/WATCHING_NOW) are swapped vs native, and the STARTED filter predicate is computed differently. The headline divergences are the card layout (overlay vs below), the slider→density feature reduction, the search UX, and the empty-state. Numerous spacing/typography/iconography details also differ.
