**🟠 [High] Library card layout (title + metrics) — Title and detail counts overlaid on cover vs rendered below cover** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes - MangaCard.kt:286-331: title + IconWithCount row are inside a Column aligned BottomStart, drawn over the cover behind a Brush.verticalGradient(Transparent -> Black 0.8f) scrim, padding 8.dp; title is white Bold 14sp on the cover.
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryScreen.kt:972-1042: the title is in a Row BELOW the cover (Modifier.padding(top=spacing.xs)), bodyMedium/onSurface, not overlaid. A separate LibraryCardDetailBadges (LibraryScreen.kt:1218-1260) IS overlaid bottom-start, but the title is not.
- **Explanation:** Native's card is a single full-bleed cover with the title text overlaid on a gradient scrim at the bottom (poster-style). KMP splits this: cover on top, then a separate text Row beneath for the title + extra captions. The visual identity of the card is materially different - native is an image-dominant poster; KMP is an image+caption list-card. The card's overall height/shape and information density differ.
- **Suggested fix:** Render the manga title (white, Bold, 14sp, maxLines 2, ellipsis) overlaid on the cover's bottom gradient scrim inside the BoxWithConstraints, matching MangaCard.kt:297-307, instead of in a Row below the cover.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth) - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/library/ui/screens/MangaCard.kt: Card (L118) -> BoxWithConstraints fillMaxSize (L128); AsyncImage with Modifier.matchParentSize() fills the cover (L146-158). Title+metrics are overlaid: Column .align(Alignment.BottomStart).fillMaxWidth().background(Brush.verticalGradient(listOf(Color.Transparent, Color.Black.copy(alpha=0.8f)))).padding(8.dp) (L286-296). Inside it, title AutoSubtitleText color=Color.White, fontWeight=FontWeight.Bold, fontSize=14.sp (L297-307), and the IconWithCount metric row (List/RemoveRedEye/Download/BookmarkAdd) gated on showDetails (L309-330). So title + metrics are both drawn over the cover behind the gradient scrim. Claim's native description (MangaCard.kt:286-331) is VERBATIM correct. KMP - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt: LibraryCard (L867) -> Card (L876) -> Column(padding=spacing.sm) (L894). First child is BoxWithConstraints (L915) holding LibraryCardCover (L918), LibrarySourceBadge top-start (L924-932), LibraryCardDetailBadges overlaid .align(Alignment.BottomStart) on the cover (L937-948), and LibraryCardActionRow (L949-970). The cover Box CLOSES at L971. Then at L972 a Row with Modifier.padding(top=spacing.xs) holds the title Text style=bodyMedium, fontWeight=Medium, no explicit color (inherits onSurface) (L976-983) plus unread/download/bookmark count badges. grep confirms item.manga.title is rendered exactly once (L977) and the other hit (L887) is only a pointerInput key - so the title is NOT overlaid on the cover; it sits below in the Column. Claim's KMP description (LibraryScreen.kt:972-1042 title below; LibraryCardDetailBadges 1218-1260 overlaid bottom-start) is also CORRECT. So the core structural claim is REAL: native = full-bleed poster with title overlaid on a gradient scrim; KMP = cover-on-top + title/caption Row beneath. NUANCE that softens the claim's framing: KMP's 4 on-cover metric badges (LibraryCardDetailBadges, L1218-1260) WERE intentionally moved back ONTO the cover bottom-start (white tint, over the scrim) to match native (see GAP-LIB-18 comment L933-936), and the cover is pinned to native's 1f/1.5f aspect ratio (L1168). So the on-cover metrics already MATCH native; the genuine residual difference is the TITLE placement (overlaid white-bold-14sp vs below-cover bodyMedium-onSurface) plus extra below-cover caption rows (last-read/added/progress, L1066-1140). The claim's 'image-dominant poster vs image+caption list-card / information density differ' framing overstates it since the metric strip is no longer split off.

**🟠 [High] Display options: items-per-row slider vs grid density — Continuous items-per-row slider (auto/0..8) replaced by 3-value density enum** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes - DisplayOptionsSection.kt:35-60 + LibraryViewModel.kt:65,358-363: a Slider valueRange 0f..8f, steps 7, where 0 = 'Auto' (GridCells.Adaptive(screenWidthDp/itemsPerRow)) and 1..8 = GridCells.Fixed(n). Label shows 'Auto' or 'N item(s)'.
- **KMP:** No - LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:154-167 + GridDensity.kt: a 3-option list COMPACT(96dp)/COMFORTABLE(120dp)/SPACIOUS(160dp) all via GridCells.Adaptive. There is no slider, no explicit column-count control, and no 'Auto' option.
- **Explanation:** Native lets the user pick an exact number of columns (1-8) or Auto. KMP removed this and offers only 3 coarse adaptive densities. A user who set 4 columns in native has no equivalent control in KMP, and the persisted library_items_per_row value is ignored. This is a real feature reduction in the display controls.
- **Suggested fix:** Replace the GridDensity OptionRows with a Slider (0..8, 0=Auto) writing items-per-row, and drive LazyVerticalGrid columns with GridCells.Fixed(n) for n>0 / GridCells.Adaptive for n==0, mirroring LibraryItems.kt:184-201.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) = continuous items-per-row Slider + Auto: - DisplayOptionsSection.kt:41-46 — `Slider(value = count.toFloat(), onValueChange = { onCountChange(it.toInt()) }, valueRange = 0f..8f, steps = 7)`. count comment at :25 "0 means 'auto'". Label at :47-57 shows R.string.auto_text when count==0 else "N item(s)" via items_count_format. (NOTE: code comment at :45 mislabels steps=7 as "5 positions" — actually 0..8 = 9 discrete stops; cosmetic, the 0..8 range is what governs.) - LibraryViewModel.kt:65 `val itemsPerRow: Int = 2`; :123 `KEY_ITEMS_PER_ROW = "library_items_per_row"`; :159 persisted read `itemsPerRow = prefs.getInt(KEY_ITEMS_PER_ROW, 0)` (effective default = Auto); :358-362 `onItemsPerRowChange(count)` persists via prefs.putInt + updates state. - LibraryScreen.kt:266-269 wires `DisplayOptionsSection(count = itemsPerRow, onCountChange = viewModel::onItemsPerRowChange, ...)`. - LibraryItems.kt:184-201 grid honors it: `minSizeDp = if (itemsPerRow > 0) (screenWidthDp / itemsPerRow).dp else 140.dp`; `columns = if (itemsPerRow > 0) GridCells.Fixed(itemsPerRow) else GridCells.Adaptive(minSizeDp)` (applied to both VerticalGridFastScroller and inner LazyVerticalGrid). So 0=Adaptive(Auto), 1..8=Fixed(N) exactly as claimed. KMP = 3-value density enum, Adaptive-only, no slider/column control, items_per_row not honored: - domain/.../library/GridDensity.kt:73-77 — enum has exactly COMPACT, COMFORTABLE, SPACIOUS (3 values). - ui/.../library/LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:154-167 — `GridDensity.entries.forEach { option -> OptionRow(label = gridDensityLabel(option), selected = option == density, onClick = { onIntent(LibraryIntent.OnGridDensityChange(option)) }) }`. A selectable list, no Slider. - ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt:655-658 `GridDensity.minSize()`: COMPACT->96.dp, COMFORTABLE->120.dp, SPACIOUS->160.dp; :845 grid uses `columns = GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = gridDensity.minSize())` only. - Tree-wide grep across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/platform/composeApp/app for `itemsPerRow\|library_items_per_row\|GridCells.Fixed\|columnCount` returns ZERO matches (exit 1). The only `Slider` imports/usages in KMP are in reader/ReaderScreen.kt (page scrubber), not library. So there is no explicit column-count control, no 'Auto', and the persisted library_items_per_row value has no consumer in KMP. Side note (does not affect verdict): GridDensity.kt KDoc at :654/:908 references "five GridDensity choices" — the KDoc is itself stale; the enum has 3. This only reinforces that KMP offers 3 coarse densities.

**🟠 [High] Search bar — Toggleable full-width SearchAppBar vs always-visible inline OutlinedTextField** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:94,118-135 + SearchAppBar.kt: a Search IconButton in the top bar toggles showSearchBar; when on, the whole top bar is REPLACED by SearchAppBar (Close nav icon, leading Search icon, trailing clear-X when non-blank, ImeAction.Search, transparent borders, 56.dp height). BackHandler exits search.
- **KMP:** No (different) - LibraryScreen.kt:498-506: an OutlinedTextField is permanently rendered below the top bar (no toggle, no Search icon, no Close/clear icons, no IME Search action, no BackHandler). The native Search IconButton is absent.
- **Explanation:** The entire search UX differs. Native hides search behind a toggle that takes over the app bar with dedicated affordances (close, clear, IME search, back-to-exit). KMP shows a permanent text field that occupies vertical space at all times and lacks the clear button, leading icon, and search-submit action. The search-entry interaction (tap magnifier) is missing.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a Search IconButton to the top bar that toggles a full-width search field replacing the title row (Close + clear-X + leading Search icon + ImeAction.Search), and a BackHandler/back-gesture to exit, matching SearchAppBar.kt.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — toggleable SearchAppBar that takes over the whole top bar: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/library/ui/screens/LibraryScreen.kt:94 `var showSearchBar by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }`. - LibraryScreen.kt:106-112 `BackHandler(enabled = showSearchBar) { showSearchBar = false; viewModel.onSearchChanged("") }` — system back exits search. - LibraryScreen.kt:117-182 the Scaffold `topBar` lambda: `if (showSearchBar) { SearchAppBar(...) } else { TopAppBarCom(...) }` — the entire top bar is REPLACED, not augmented. - LibraryScreen.kt:140-142 a Search `IconButton(onClick = { showSearchBar = true }) { Icon(Icons.Default.Search, ...) }` in the normal top bar toggles search on. - SearchAppBar.kt confirms every claimed affordance: nav icon = Close (`:51-61`, Icons.Default.Close, calls onToggleSearch + clears query), leading `Icons.Default.Search` icon (`:73-78`), trailing clear-X only when `query.isNotBlank()` (`:79-88`), `imeAction = ImeAction.Search` (`:90-92`) with `KeyboardActions(onSearch = ...)` (`:93-98`), all-transparent borders/containers (`:100-108`), and `.height(56.dp)` (`:111`). KMP (NEW app) — permanent inline OutlinedTextField, no toggle: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt:498-506 — inside `LibraryTopBar`'s non-selection branch, an `OutlinedTextField(value = state.searchQuery, onValueChange = { onIntent(LibraryIntent.OnSearchQueryChange(it)) }, placeholder = {...}, singleLine = true, modifier = fillMaxWidth().padding(...))` is rendered UNCONDITIONALLY below the TopAppBar (only gated by `!state.isInSelectionMode`, not by any search toggle). - This field has NO leadingIcon, NO trailingIcon/clear button, NO keyboardOptions (no ImeAction.Search), NO keyboardActions. - The top bar `actions` (LibraryScreen.kt:479-496) contain only a Tune/options button, a download badge, and a MoreVert overflow — NO Search IconButton. - A full-file grep for BackHandler / showSearchBar / SearchAppBar / ImeAction / Search icon in ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt returns none of them; the only hits are the always-rendered OutlinedTextField (498,500) and `state.isSearching` used solely to pick the empty-state message text (283, 821-827). The `SearchAppBar` token appears only in the unrelated ui/.../search/SearchScreen.kt, not in Library. All five distinguishing elements the claim names (toggle entry via magnifier, app-bar takeover, Close nav, leading Search icon, trailing clear-X, IME Search action, BackHandler-to-exit) are present in native and absent in KMP; KMP shows a permanent borderless-less plain text field occupying vertical space. The claim's file:line citations match exactly.

**🟡 [Medium] Library card extra captions (last-read / added / progress) — KMP shows below-card text captions native never renders** _(Component)_

- **Native:** No - native MangaCard shows ONLY the title overlay + a single Row of 4 IconWithCount metrics (total/read/downloaded/bookmarked) on the cover. There is no 'Last read', 'Added', or 'N / M chapters' text caption anywhere on the card.
- **KMP:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:1065-1140 renders 'Last read X ago' (library_card_last_read), 'Added X ago' (library_card_added), and 'N / M chapters' (library_card_chapters_progress) text captions below the card, all gated on display.showDetails.
- **Explanation:** The KMP card adds three relative-time/progress text rows that do not exist in the native source of truth. Native conveys read/total/downloaded/bookmarked purely as icon+count badges on the cover. These extra rows change the card's footprint and information layout and are a fabricated feature not present in the original.
- **Suggested fix:** Remove the last-read/added/progress text captions (or hide them) to match native, which represents these via the on-cover IconWithCount badge row only.

**🟡 [Medium] Empty library state — Icon + named message vs plain text only** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes - EmptyLibraryPlaceholder.kt:26-50: centered Outlined.Inbox icon (72.dp, onBackground @0.7f alpha) + Spacer 16.dp + titleLarge Bold centered text 'Your <tabName> is empty' where tabName is Library/Watching Now/Likes.
- **KMP:** No (different) - LibraryScreen.kt:820-832 EmptyLibraryMessage renders only a single bodyLarge onSurfaceVariant Text: 'no_results_found' when searching else 'library_empty'. No icon, no Inbox, no tab/library name, smaller text style, no Bold.
- **Explanation:** Native's empty state is a prominent illustrated placeholder (large Inbox icon + bold title naming the current tab). KMP shows a small one-line caption with no icon and no contextual tab name. The empty state reads very differently and loses the visual prominence and the per-tab message.
- **Suggested fix:** Render an Outlined.Inbox icon (72.dp, onBackground @0.7f) above a titleLarge Bold centered message that includes the active category name (Library/Likes/Watching Now), matching EmptyLibraryPlaceholder.kt; keep a distinct 'no results' message only for the search case.

**🟡 [Medium] Top bar download indicator — Animated Lottie preloader vs static count badge** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:143-150 + AnimatedPreloader.kt: when isDownloading, an IconButton shows a looping Lottie animation (R.raw.download_anim) with dynamic bg/icon colors (background / primary). Binary presence (no count).
- **KMP:** No (different) - LibraryScreen.kt:723-737 DownloadProgressBadge shows a static YamiCountBadge (Download icon + numeric count) tinted primary, only when count>0. No animation.
- **Explanation:** Native surfaces active downloads with an eye-catching animated Lottie spinner. KMP replaces it with a static icon+count badge. While the count is arguably richer data, the animated motion cue that signals 'work in progress' is lost, and the visual treatment differs from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Render an animated download indicator (Lottie or an indeterminate CircularProgressIndicator) when downloads are active to match the native motion cue; optionally retain the count overlay.

**🟡 [Medium] Grid fast-scroller — Custom draggable fast-scroll thumb present in native, absent in KMP** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryItems.kt:188-197: the LazyVerticalGrid is wrapped in VerticalGridFastScroller with a primary-colored draggable thumb, Arrangement.spacedBy(8.dp), contentPadding 8.dp.
- **KMP:** No - LibraryScreen.kt:844-863 LibraryGrid is a bare LazyVerticalGrid with no fast-scroller wrapper. Large libraries can only be scrolled normally.
- **Explanation:** Native provides a fast-scroll thumb for quickly traversing large libraries. KMP omits it entirely, so navigating a long library is slower. This is a missing interaction/component.
- **Suggested fix:** Wrap the grid in an equivalent fast-scroller (draggable thumb tinted primary) or add a scrollbar overlay to restore quick traversal of large libraries.

**🟡 [Medium] Per-card action buttons placement & styling — Buttons aligned TopEnd below the source badge vs CenterEnd; tint/shape differences** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes - MangaCard.kt:199-282: watch-later/like/delete buttons are in a Column aligned to the TOP-END (just under the source badge), each a Box of size cardWidth*0.22f (4..40dp) with a circular RoundedCornerShape(50) background (surface @0.8f for watch/like, errorContainer @0.8f for delete). Like tint Color.Red, watch tint primary, delete tint White. Spacer between = cardWidth*0.01f (1..3dp).
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryScreen.kt:949-970,1286-1331: buttons are a Column aligned CenterEnd (Alignment.CenterEnd), rendered as plain YamiIconButtons (no circular translucent background Box). Delete tint = onErrorContainer (not White on an errorContainer circle); spacing = spacing.xs (fixed) not the adaptive cardWidth*0.01f.
- **Explanation:** Native anchors the action column to the top-right corner directly under the source badge, and each button sits on a translucent circular chip (surface/errorContainer at 80% alpha) for contrast against the cover. KMP centers the column vertically and drops the circular background chips, changing both position and the contrast treatment. The delete button color treatment also differs (native: white glyph on red-ish circle; KMP: onErrorContainer glyph, no circle).
- **Suggested fix:** Align the action Column to TopEnd, wrap each icon in a circular (RoundedCornerShape(50)) translucent background (surface @0.8f, errorContainer @0.8f for delete), use the native tints (primary / Color.Red / White), and use the adaptive spacer (cardWidth*0.01f coerced 1..3dp).

**🟡 [Medium] Multi-select / selection mode — KMP added long-press multi-select + bulk delete; native has none** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** No - native LibraryScreen/MangaCard have no long-press handler, no selection set, no selection top bar, no bulk delete. MangaCard.kt:124 only has clickable { onMangaClick(...) }.
- **KMP:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:464-475,887-891 + LibraryViewModel.kt:316-351: long-press enters selection mode (isInSelectionMode), the top bar swaps to a 'N selected' bar with Delete/Cancel, and OnDeleteSelected triggers a bulk-delete confirmation + BulkRemoveFromLibraryUseCase.
- **Explanation:** KMP introduced an entire multi-select selection mode with bulk delete that does not exist in the native source of truth. While useful, it is a fabricated feature relative to native, and it changes the long-press gesture semantics (native long-press does nothing). Per the audit's source-of-truth rule, this is a divergence to document.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm whether multi-select is an intended enhancement; if strict parity is required, gate or remove it. If kept, note it as an additive deviation from native.

**🟡 [Medium] Category tabs ordering — Tab order swapped: native NAN/Watching Now/Likes vs KMP NAN/Likes/Watching Now** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryViewModel.kt:88-89 enum FilterTabs { NAN, WATCHING_NOW, LIKED } and LibraryItems.kt:90,112-129 iterates entries in that order, so tabs render All, Watching Now, Likes.
- **KMP:** No (reordered) - LibraryCategory.kt enum { NAN, LIKED, WATCHING_NOW } and LibraryScreen.kt:685-697 CategoryTabs iterates entries in that order, so tabs render All, Likes, Watching Now.
- **Explanation:** The second and third category tabs are swapped relative to native. A user's muscle memory (and any persisted selected-index, given native persisted nothing but KMP derives index from enum order) maps to the wrong tab. This is a concrete ordering regression.
- **Suggested fix:** Reorder LibraryCategory entries to NAN, WATCHING_NOW, LIKED (or reorder the tab rendering) to match the native FilterTabs order.

**🟡 [Medium] Sort options sheet layout — Native: header + direction Switch + 'Sort by' + FilterChip row; KMP: plain selectable rows + a divider toggle row** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - SortOptionsSection.kt:44-104: a titleLarge 'Sort Options' header, a 'Sort Direction' row with a SwapVert icon + Ascending/Descending label + a Switch, then a titleMedium 'Sort by' label and a FlowRow of FilterChips (RoundedCornerShape(16dp)) for each sort type.
- **KMP:** No (different) - LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:118-153: sort types are plain full-width OptionRows (label + check icon), and the direction control is a single clickable Row with a label + an ascending/descending arrow Icon (no Switch, no SwapVert icon, no 'Sort Options'/'Sort by' headers, no chips).
- **Explanation:** The Sort tab is structurally different. Native uses a labeled section with a toggle Switch for direction and chip-style sort selection. KMP uses a list of rows with checkmarks and an arrow-icon tap row for direction. The headers ('Sort Options', 'Sort by'), the SwapVert icon, the Ascending/Descending text + Switch, and the chip presentation are all absent in KMP.
- **Suggested fix:** Rebuild the Sort tab with the 'Sort Options' titleLarge header, a SwapVert + Ascending/Descending + Switch direction row, a 'Sort by' titleMedium label, and FilterChips for the sort options, matching SortOptionsSection.kt.

**🟡 [Medium] Filter options sheet presentation — Native filter = FlowRow of FilterChips with check leading-icon; KMP = vertical selectable rows** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - FilterChipsRow.kt:28-91: filter options are a FlowRow of FilterChips, RoundedCornerShape(16dp), with a Done leading icon + onPrimary tint when selected, primary border when selected, defaultMinSize minHeight 32dp.
- **KMP:** No (different) - LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:111-117,204-235: filter options are vertical full-width OptionRows (label + trailing primary Check icon when selected), not chips.
- **Explanation:** Native presents filters as a wrapping row of pill-shaped chips (compact, multi-per-line). KMP presents them as a vertical list of full-width rows. The visual layout and density of the Filter tab are substantially different.
- **Suggested fix:** Render filter options as a FlowRow of FilterChips (RoundedCornerShape(16dp), Done leading icon when selected, primary border/onPrimary label when selected), matching FilterChipsRow.kt, instead of vertical rows.

**🟡 [Medium] Display options sheet content — Native has items-per-row slider + 5 SwitchItems separated by Dividers; KMP has density rows + 5 Switch rows + a density header** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - DisplayOptionsSection.kt + LibraryScreen.kt:266-312: a 'Items per row:' SemiBold label + Slider + an 'Auto'/'N item(s)' caption, then 5 SwitchItem rows (Show Items Details, Show Items Source, Show Items Count, Show Buttons, Show Tabs) each preceded by a Divider/HorizontalDivider.
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:154-194: a 'Density' titleSmall header + 3 density OptionRows, a single HorizontalDivider, then the same 5 ToggleRows. The slider + 'Items per row'/'Auto' caption are gone; per-switch dividers are gone; an extra 'Density' header/section is added.
- **Explanation:** Beyond the slider->density change already noted, the Display tab structure differs: native interleaves a Divider before each switch and leads with the items-per-row slider; KMP leads with a density section + single divider and a different switch grouping. The five toggle labels themselves match (reused show_* strings), but the surrounding layout/dividers differ.
- **Suggested fix:** Restore the items-per-row slider + Auto/N caption at the top of the Display tab and place a Divider before each SwitchItem, matching DisplayOptionsSection.kt; drop the added 'Density' section if the slider is restored.

**⚪ [Low] Per-card delete confirmation — Native deletes directly (no confirm); KMP added a confirmation dialog** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** No confirmation - MangaCard.kt:259-279 + LibraryScreen.kt:64,217: the delete icon calls onToggleDelete(manga.id) which goes straight to removeManga; there is NO per-card AlertDialog. (The KDocs in KMP claiming a 'legacy route-level delete-confirmation AlertDialog' do not match this native MangaCard source.)
- **KMP:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:311-316,963-968 + LibraryViewModel.kt:278-284,608-615: the delete icon dispatches OnSingleDeleteRequest which stages pendingSingleDelete and shows SingleDeleteDialog (library_single_delete_title/message) before removal.
- **Explanation:** KMP added a confirmation gate that native does not have for the per-card delete. This is arguably a safety improvement, but it is a behavioral divergence from the source of truth (extra tap required, extra dialog). The KMP KDoc justification cites a legacy route file as precedent, but the actual native MangaCard deletes without confirmation.
- **Suggested fix:** Either remove the per-card confirmation dialog to match native's direct-delete behavior, or confirm with product that the added safety gate is intended; if kept, document it as an intentional deviation rather than 'parity'.

**⚪ [Low] Filter chip ordering — Filter order swapped: native ...STARTED/BOOKMARKED/COMPLETED vs KMP ...STARTED/COMPLETED/BOOKMARKED** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryViewModel.kt:74 enum FilterType { ALL, DOWNLOADED, UNREAD, STARTED, BOOKMARKED, COMPLETED } and FilterChipsRow renders entries in that order.
- **KMP:** No (reordered) - LibraryFilter.kt { ALL, DOWNLOADED, UNREAD, STARTED, COMPLETED, BOOKMARKED } and LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:111 renders entries in that order, so Completed and Bookmarked are swapped vs native.
- **Explanation:** The last two filter chips (Bookmarked, Completed) appear in the opposite order to native. Minor but a visible ordering divergence in the Filter tab of the options sheet.
- **Suggested fix:** Reorder LibraryFilter entries to ALL, DOWNLOADED, UNREAD, STARTED, BOOKMARKED, COMPLETED to match native FilterType order.

**⚪ [Low] STARTED filter predicate — Native: readCount>0; KMP: unreadCount<totalChapters** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryViewModel.kt:198 FilterType.STARTED -> item.readCount > 0 (manga with at least one read chapter).
- **KMP:** Partial/different - LibraryViewModel.kt:660 LibraryFilter.STARTED -> categorized.filter { it.unreadCount < it.totalChapters }. With readCount = totalChapters - unreadCount, native's readCount>0 is equivalent to unreadCount<totalChapters in the common case, BUT the edge case of a manga with totalChapters==0 differs: native readCount>0 = false; KMP unreadCount(0)<totalChapters(0) = false (same here). However if denormalized unreadCount can exceed totalChapters transiently or counts drift, the two formulas can disagree.
- **Explanation:** The two predicates are algebraically equivalent only if readCount == totalChapters - unreadCount exactly. KMP computes 'started' from unreadCount/totalChapters rather than a direct read count, which can diverge if the denormalized aggregates are momentarily inconsistent (e.g. during a chapter-list refresh) or if a manga is fully read (native: readCount>0 true; KMP: unreadCount<total also true) - mostly aligned but derived from a different source field.
- **Suggested fix:** If LibraryManga exposes a read count, use readCount > 0 directly to match native exactly; otherwise document that STARTED is derived as unreadCount < totalChapters and verify the aggregates are always consistent.

**⚪ [Low] Items-count header label — Native uses an Android plurals resource; KMP uses a single format string** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryItems.kt:154-167 uses pluralStringResource(R.plurals.items_count, n, n) -> '1 item' / 'N items' with proper one/other plural selection; gated on showCount; styled labelSmall 12sp Medium onSurfaceVariant, placed in the same Row as 'Last updated' (SpaceBetween).
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryScreen.kt:527-528,546-557 LibraryItemCountCaption uses stringResource(Res.string.library_items_count, count) - a single format string, not a plural resource, and is rendered on its OWN full-width row BELOW the last-updated row (not in the same SpaceBetween Row).
- **Explanation:** Native pluralizes the count ('1 item' vs '2 items') via a plurals resource and places it on the same row as the last-updated label (right-aligned). KMP uses a non-plural format string and a separate full-width row. For languages with complex plural rules this loses correct pluralization, and the layout (separate row vs inline-right) differs.
- **Suggested fix:** Use a plural-aware resource for the item count and render it right-aligned in the same Row as the last-updated label (SpaceBetween), matching LibraryItems.kt:135-168.

**⚪ [Low] Last-updated row layout & typography — Native row is italic+styled and shares a SpaceBetween Row with the count; KMP is a separate non-italic row** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryItems.kt:142-153: 'Last updated: X' is labelSmall copied to fontSize 12sp, FontWeight.Medium, FontStyle.Italic, onSurfaceVariant, in a Row(padding horizontal 16.dp vertical 8.dp, SpaceBetween) with the count on the right.
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryScreen.kt:766-781 LastUpdatedRow renders labelSmall onSurfaceVariant (NO italic, NO explicit 12sp/Medium override) full-width, padding horizontal spacing.lg vertical spacing.xs, on its own row.
- **Explanation:** Native styles the last-updated text as italic Medium 12sp and lays it out inline (left) opposite the count (right). KMP drops the italic style and the explicit weight/size, and splits the count onto a different row. Subtle typographic and layout divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply FontStyle.Italic + FontWeight.Medium + 12sp to the last-updated text and combine it with the item-count in a single SpaceBetween Row, matching the native header.

**⚪ [Low] showCount flag semantics — Native showCount gates ONLY the header item-count; KMP historically conflated it with per-card badges (now re-gated to showDetails)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryItems.kt:154 'Show Items Count' (showCount) gates only the header 'N items' label. Per-card detail badges are gated solely by showDetails (MangaCard.kt:309).
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryScreen.kt:527,1001,1016,1033: showCount now gates only the header LibraryItemCountCaption, and per-card badges are gated on showDetails. The KMP code comments (GAP-LIB-21) acknowledge an earlier conflation that was corrected; current behavior is aligned but the per-card 'downloaded check / downloaded count / bookmark count' badges below the title are KMP additions (see separate finding).
- **Explanation:** Current showCount/showDetails gating is aligned with native after the GAP-LIB-21 correction, so this is largely informational. The residual divergence is that KMP renders additional per-card count badges in the below-title Row (download-check, downloaded count, bookmark count) gated on showDetails that native does not render in that location (native shows those only as the 4-icon on-cover row).
- **Suggested fix:** Verify showCount gates only the header count (it does) and remove the duplicate below-title download/bookmark count badges that native does not show, keeping only the on-cover IconWithCount row.

**⚪ [Low] Search behavior on submit — Native clears the query when a non-blank search is submitted; KMP keeps the query and filters live** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:126-132: onSearch lambda does `if (it.isNotBlank()) viewModel.onSearchChanged("")` - submitting the keyboard Search action RESETS the query to empty (filtering is otherwise live as you type).
- **KMP:** No (different) - LibraryScreen.kt:498-506: there is no IME Search action handler at all; typing filters live via OnSearchQueryChange and the query persists. There is no submit-clears-query behavior.
- **Explanation:** Native has a quirky behavior where pressing the keyboard search action clears the field (live filtering means the action is mostly redundant). KMP simply has no submit action. This is a minor behavioral divergence; arguably KMP's is more sensible, but it differs from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide intended behavior; if matching native, add an ImeAction.Search that clears the query on submit. Otherwise document the intentional change.

**⚪ [Low] Card cover scrim gradient values — Native scrim is Transparent->Black 0.8f full-height vertical; KMP scrim is 0.55->Black 0.45f** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes - MangaCard.kt:291-293: Brush.verticalGradient(listOf(Color.Transparent, Color.Black.copy(alpha = 0.8f))) applied to the bottom info Column (the gradient spans that Column's height).
- **KMP:** Partial - YamiCoverImage.kt (scrim branch): Brush.verticalGradient(0.55f to Transparent, 1f to Black @0.45f) over the full cover. Different alpha (0.45 vs 0.8) and different stop distribution.
- **Explanation:** The bottom gradient scrim used to darken the cover for overlay legibility is lighter in KMP (max alpha 0.45 starting at 55% height) than native (alpha 0.8). Combined with the fact that KMP doesn't overlay the title on the scrim, the cover bottom reads noticeably lighter than native.
- **Suggested fix:** Match the native scrim alpha (~0.8 at the bottom) when overlaying the title/badges, or tune YamiCoverImage's library scrim to approximate Transparent->Black@0.8f.

**⚪ [Low] Card container color / placeholder — Native card has no tinted container (image fills it); KMP card uses surfaceVariant/primaryContainer container + outline placeholder tint** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes - MangaCard.kt:118-127: Card with elevation 2.dp, RoundedCornerShape(8dp), no explicit container color (cover fills it); placeholder = onSurface @0.12f, error = error @0.24f.
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryScreen.kt:876-884: Card containerColor = primaryContainer when selected else surfaceVariant, elevation 3.dp; cover placeholder tint = primary(selected)/outline, background placeholderTint @0.15f.
- **Explanation:** Native cards have elevation 2.dp and let the cover image fill the whole card with neutral placeholders. KMP uses elevation 3.dp, a surfaceVariant container (primaryContainer when selected, since selection mode exists), and an outline/primary placeholder tint. Because KMP renders the title below the cover, the surfaceVariant container shows as a visible card background panel that native does not have.
- **Suggested fix:** Use elevation 2.dp and neutral placeholders; once the title overlay is moved onto the cover, the container color becomes the cover itself, removing the visible panel and matching native.

**⚪ [Low] Top bar title typography — Native title is titleLarge @24sp Bold on background; KMP uses default TopAppBar title style** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes - TopAppBarCom.kt:18-41: title rendered titleLarge copied to fontSize 24sp, FontWeight.Bold, color onBackground, maxLines 1 ellipsis, container = background.
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryScreen.kt:477-478: TopAppBar(title = { Text(stringResource(title_library)) }) with default Material3 TopAppBar title typography (titleLarge ~22sp, not forced Bold/24sp) and default surface container (the Column wraps it in colorScheme.surface).
- **Explanation:** Native forces a 24sp Bold title on a background-colored bar. KMP uses the Material3 default TopAppBar title (≈22sp, Regular) on a surface-colored bar. The header reads less bold/smaller than native.
- **Suggested fix:** Set the top bar title Text to fontSize 24sp, FontWeight.Bold (titleLarge override) and align the bar container color with native (background), matching TopAppBarCom.kt.

**⚪ [Low] Refresh trigger surface (pull-to-refresh + overflow Refresh) — Native has pull-to-refresh AND an overflow Refresh item, both passing the visible items list; KMP has both but Refresh ignores items** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:166-169,185-189: overflow 'Refresh' calls onRefresh(uiState.items) and pull-to-refresh calls onRefreshClick(uiState.items); both pass the current visible list to the refresh handler.
- **KMP:** Partial - LibraryScreen.kt:272-277,582-587 + LibraryViewModel.kt:251: both pull-to-refresh and the overflow Refresh dispatch OnRefresh which just calls refreshLibrary() with no list argument (enqueues the background LibraryRefresh worker).
- **Explanation:** Both apps expose pull-to-refresh and an overflow Refresh action (parity on entry points). The difference is that native's refresh handlers receive the visible items list (the refresh logic operates over the currently displayed set), whereas KMP's refresh is argument-less and delegates entirely to the background worker. Whether this changes what actually gets refreshed depends on the handler implementations, but the contract differs.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm the KMP RefreshLibraryUseCase refreshes the same scope native does (the visible/whole library); if native refreshes only the visible filtered set, pass that scope through to the use case.

**⚪ [Low] Open Random Manga action — Both present; selection source differs (native passes full items, KMP picks from visible filtered items)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:171-178: overflow 'Open Random Manga' calls onOpenRandomClick(uiState.items).
- **KMP:** Yes - LibraryScreen.kt:588-594 + LibraryViewModel.kt:362-365: overflow 'Random' dispatches OnOpenRandom which picks state.items.randomOrNull() (the post-filter/search visible list) and navigates to details.
- **Explanation:** Both have the Open Random Manga overflow action (good parity). KMP picks from the currently-visible (filtered/searched) items; native passes uiState.items (also the filtered list) to its handler, so behavior is likely aligned. Label differs slightly (native 'Open Random Manga' via dropdown_button_open_random_manga vs KMP 'Random' via library_random). Minor label divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the menu label with native's 'Open Random Manga' string if exact wording parity is required; confirm the random pick scope matches native.

**⚪ [Low] Source badge contrast color source — Brand-color map duplicated in :ui; behavior matches but maintenance/divergence risk** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes - MangaCard.kt:110-113 uses api.COLORS (from :shared sources_repositry) + isDark() to pick White/Black text on an 80%-alpha brand Card badge, 8sp Bold, padding h6/v2.
- **KMP:** Yes - LibrarySourceBrand.kt:18-71 duplicates the COLORS map and isDark() verbatim into :ui; LibrarySourceBadge (LibraryScreen.kt:1181-1205) renders the same 8sp Bold, h6/v2-padded, RoundedCornerShape(4dp), 80%-alpha brand Card. Visually matches native.
- **Explanation:** The source badge itself is faithfully reproduced (same hex map, same isDark luminance test, same 8sp Bold styling and padding). The only concern is the brand-color map is now duplicated in :ui rather than shared, so a new source added to :shared COLORS would not appear branded in the KMP library badge (falls through to black) until the :ui copy is updated. Functionally parity is high today.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a code comment / test linking LibrarySourceBrand.libraryBrandColor to the :shared COLORS map so new sources are kept in sync, or expose the map through :presentation to avoid duplication drift.

**⚪ [Low] DownloadProgressDialog usage — Native ships a DownloadProgressDialog in library components; no equivalent dialog wired in the KMP library screen** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Partial - DownloadProgressDialog.kt exists (AlertDialog with LinearProgressIndicator, downloaded/total text, percent, Stop/Continue buttons) in the library components package, intended for the download indicator tap flow.
- **KMP:** No - the KMP library DownloadProgressBadge merely navigates to the Downloads screen on tap (LibraryScreen.kt:488-491,724-736); there is no in-library progress dialog with Stop/Continue.
- **Explanation:** Native has a DownloadProgressDialog component co-located with the library feature (showing progress + Stop/Continue) that ties into the download indicator. KMP routes the download badge tap to a separate Downloads screen and has no equivalent in-library progress dialog. Depending on whether native actually shows this dialog from the library top-bar, this may be a missing in-context affordance.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm whether native opens DownloadProgressDialog from the library download indicator; if so, provide an equivalent progress dialog (or accept the navigate-to-Downloads approach as the intended replacement).

### Library Details (in-library manga)  `library-details`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 19 (🔴0 🟠4 🟡10 ⚪5)

> The native app has a dedicated in-library detail screen, `LibraryMangaScreen` (LibraryMangaScreen.kt) backed by `LibraryDetailsViewModel`, reached via the distinct route `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails(mangaId: Long)`. It is a rich, library-specific surface: parallax blurred header cover, Resume FAB that jumps to the first unread chapter, pull-to-refresh, a filter/sort bottom sheet (FilterType ALL/DOWNLOADED/UNREAD/READED/BOOKMARKED + SortType ID/NUMBER/DATE/LAST_READ_DATE with asc/desc), per-chapter download/read/bookmark/cancel affordances, a NEW badge, total-downloaded-size banner, per-chapter file size, a banner ad, an in-context multi-select action row (download/bookmark/mark-down-read/delete/mark-all-read/close), and a top-bar overflow with delete-all-downloads + refresh + share. In KMP this whole screen was deliberately folded into the single unified `DetailsScreen` (ui/details/DetailsScreen.kt) backed by `DetailsViewModel`; the native `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails` route was retired (App.kt §103/§177) and the Library tab now navigates to the shared `Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api)` URL-only entry. The unified screen restores many features (offline saved-details overlay, in-library gating, bookmark heart, download-all, per-chapter read/download/cancel, multi-select, adult gate, cover blur, expandable description, genre overflow), but a large set of library-specific affordances are missing or diverge: no Resume FAB, no pull-to-refresh, no filter/sort sheet, no NEW badge (the domain Chapter model has no `isNew`), no total-size banner, no per-chapter file size, no per-chapter bookmark toggle in the row, no LAST_READ_DATE sort, a reduced multi-select action set, raw ISO chapter dates instead of relative strings, and a different chapter label format. These are documented below as individual findings.

**🟠 [High] Resume FAB — Resume/continue floating action button is absent in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — AnimatedCircleExtendedFab in LibraryMangaScreen.kt:225-235 with Icons.Default.PlayArrow, text "Resume ${firstUnread.number}" or "You finished this manga"; firstUnread computed at :144-152 honoring sort direction; tapping opens the first unread chapter; FAB expands/collapses on scroll (:153-175).
- **KMP:** No — grep of ui/details shows no floatingActionButton/PlayArrow/firstUnread/ExtendedFab; Scaffold (DetailsScreen.kt:322) has no floatingActionButton parameter.
- **Explanation:** The Resume FAB is a core reading-continuation affordance on the in-library detail screen — it is the fastest path back into reading and computes the first-unread chapter respecting the current sort order. KMP offers no equivalent; the user must scroll the chapter list to find where they left off.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an extended FAB to DetailsScreen that computes the first unread chapter from details.chapters (respecting list order) and dispatches OnChapterClick; mirror the native expand-on-scroll-up / collapse-on-scroll-down behavior and the "You finished this manga" empty state.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). - **KMP:** No — grep of ui/details and presentation/details finds no FilterType/SortType/sortAscending/FilterChips/SortOptions/toggleSort/FilterList. DetailsState has no filter/sort fields; chapters render in fetched order de-duped by url (DetailsScreen.kt:572).
- **Explanation:** Filtering (e.g. show only unread/downloaded/bookmarked) and sorting (by number/date/last-read, asc or desc) are major chapter-management features of the native library detail screen. None exist in KMP — the chapter list is fixed in source order with no way to filter or change sort, a significant regression for large libraries.
- **Suggested fix:** Add filter/sort state to DetailsState and a bottom sheet (reuse the library filter sheet components) plus an inline sort toggle; implement the five filters and four sorts with asc/desc in the VM reducer over details.chapters.

**🟠 [High] NEW chapter badge — NEW badge on freshly-discovered chapters is missing in KMP** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryChapterItem.kt:621-640 renders a red Card badge (Color.Red bg, white bold labelSmall text, RoundedCornerShape 4.dp, top-end) with R.string.new_chapter ("NEW") when chapter.isNew. isNew is set true on refresh for newly inserted chapters (LibraryDetailsViewModel.refreshChapters :287) and cleared on open (setIsNewChapter).
- **KMP:** No — domain Chapter model (Chapter.kt:62-83) has no isNew field; ui/details has no isNew/new_chapter rendering.
- **Explanation:** The NEW badge is how the user spots chapters added since their last visit. The KMP domain Chapter model dropped the isNew concept entirely, so there is no data to render it and no UI for it. This is a data-model regression, not just a UI omission.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an isNew flag to the domain Chapter / saved-chapter mapping, set it when refresh inserts new chapters and clear it on open, and render a NEW badge on the chapter row matching the native red badge styling.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — the NEW badge is a complete, working feature: - /native-app/.../library_details/ui/screens/LibraryChapterItem.kt:621-640 renders the badge exactly as claimed: `if (chapter.isNew)` (:622) -> Card aligned TopEnd, RoundedCornerShape(4.dp), CardDefaults.cardColors(containerColor = Color.Red), Text(stringResource(R.string.new_chapter)) padded 6/2.dp, labelSmall, FontWeight.Bold, Color.White. - R.string.new_chapter = "NEW" at /native-app/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:633 (localized across all locales). - isNew origin: /native-app/.../data/local/entity/SavedChapterEntity.kt:37 `val isNew: Boolean = false`; set true on refresh for newly-inserted chapters at /native-app/.../library_details/ui/viewmodel/LibraryDetailsViewModel.kt:286 (SavedChapterEntity(... isNew = true) for chapters whose url is not already local, :277-288). Cleared via /native-app/.../data/local/dao/ChapterDao.kt:73 `UPDATE saved_chapters SET isNew = 0 WHERE id = :chapterId`. KMP — confirmed missing in the domain model and UI, though persistence still carries it: - domain/.../domain/model/Chapter.kt:62-83 data class Chapter has fields number,name,url,date,isDownloaded,isBookmarked,isRead — NO isNew field (claim cited :62-83 correctly). - Both entity/legacy -> domain mappers drop isNew: data/.../mapper/MangaDetailsMappers.kt:76-83 (LegacyChapterItem.toDomain) and :91-99 (SavedChapterEntity.toDomainChapter, which DOES copy isRead but NOT isNew) — so even the persisted flag never reaches domain. - presentation/src has ZERO isNew references (grep empty). ui/.../details/DetailsScreen.kt (the only KMP details screen) has no isNew / new_chapter / Color.Red / NEW badge rendering (grep empty). - The only KMP isNew UI is unrelated WhatsNew feature chips (ui/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewScreen.kt:605, domain WhatsNewFeature.isNew) — not chapters. - Note (refines the claim, does not refute it): the KMP PERSISTENCE layer still fully supports isNew — shared/.../data/local/entity/SavedChapterEntity.kt:45 `val isNew: Boolean = false`, shared/.../data/local/Migrations.kt:142 adds the column, shared/.../data/local/dao/ChapterDao.kt:107 clears it, and app/.../work/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:246 sets isNew=true on refresh. So the data is written to Room but severed at the domain-mapper boundary, confirming the "data-model regression" characterization: the field is dropped going entity->domain->presentation->UI.

**🟠 [High] Per-chapter bookmark toggle — Chapter rows have no bookmark toggle in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Explanation:** Native lets the user bookmark individual chapters directly from the row (and filter by BOOKMARKED). The Chapter model carries isBookmarked, but KMP exposes no UI or intent to toggle it from the row, so a key per-chapter action is missing.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an OnToggleChapterBookmark intent + VM handler and a bookmark IconButton in ChapterRow (filled when isBookmarked) gated on in-library, matching the native BookmarkRemove/BookmarkBorder toggle.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). **🟡 [Medium] In-library detail screen / route — Dedicated LibraryMangaDetails route and screen folded into the generic Details screen** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — Screen.LibraryMangaDetails(mangaId: Long) (NavGraphV2.kt:102-104, composable at 469-495) renders the dedicated LibraryMangaScreen via LibraryMangaRoute.kt; library entries pass a Room mangaId.
- **KMP:** Partial — route retired (App.kt:103-104,177). Library tab now navigates to Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api) → unified DetailsScreen (App.kt:478-502, DetailsScreen.kt DetailsScreenByUrl).
- **Explanation:** Native treated in-library manga as a first-class distinct screen identified by Room mangaId, loading the saved entity directly (LibraryDetailsViewModel.loadMangaDetails(mangaId)). KMP uses one URL-keyed screen for both browse and in-library cases; the in-library affordances are conditionally shown based on state.isInLibrary. This is an intentional architecture change but it changes identity semantics (mangaId vs api+url) and means the library detail experience is now a subset of a generic screen rather than a tailored one.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm the unified screen reaches full parity with the library-specific affordances (see other findings); if a mangaId-keyed deep entry is still needed, add an OnEnterById intent so library navigation can resolve the saved manga directly instead of re-fetching by URL.

**🟡 [Medium] Pull-to-refresh — Pull-to-refresh gesture missing in KMP details** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — rememberPullRefreshState + Modifier.pullRefresh + PullRefreshIndicator in LibraryMangaScreen.kt:243-247,261-265,461-467 (backgroundColor inverseSurface, contentColor background); onRefresh = refreshChapters() in LibraryDetailsViewModel.refreshChapters() (:246-302) which re-fetches and inserts new chapters.
- **KMP:** No — no pullRefresh/PullToRefresh in ui/details. Refresh is only available via the top-bar refresh IconButton dispatching OnRetry (DetailsScreen.kt:504-509, 335).
- **Explanation:** Native lets the user pull down anywhere on the list to refresh chapters with a visible spinner overlay. KMP only exposes refresh through a top-bar button. The refresh also behaves differently: native inserts newly-discovered chapters into the library DB (marking them isNew), whereas KMP OnRetry just re-runs the fetch and overlays saved state.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a pull-to-refresh container around the chapter LazyColumn wired to OnRetry (or a dedicated OnRefresh intent), with a refreshing indicator bound to state.isLoading; ensure refresh inserts/flags newly published chapters as in native refreshChapters().

**🟡 [Medium] Total downloaded size banner — Total-downloaded-size header banner is absent in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — TotalSizeDisplay (TotalSizeDisplay.kt) renders a pill (primaryContainer @0.3f alpha, RoundedCornerShape 12.dp, Storage icon 20.dp primary tint) with downloaded_header string "%1$s • %2$d downloaded" when totalSize non-empty and downloadedCount>0; placed in LibraryHeaderSection.kt:64-68.
- **KMP:** No — grep of ui/details finds no TotalSize/getFormattedMangaSize/FileSizeUtils/Storage usage; the header (DetailsHeader, DetailsScreen.kt:629-755) has no size banner.
- **Explanation:** Native shows the total on-disk size of downloaded chapters and the downloaded count as a header pill, giving the user storage awareness for a saved manga. KMP has no on-disk size computation in the details surface and no banner.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a downloaded-size summary to the header shown when the manga is in-library and has downloaded chapters; compute total size on a background dispatcher and render a pill matching the native Storage-icon styling and downloaded_header string.

**🟡 [Medium] Multi-select action row — KMP selection bar offers fewer bulk actions than native** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — ChapterSelectionActionsRow.kt:71-96 offers: Download all, Bookmark all, Mark-down-read (ic_done_down_arrow, only when exactly 1 selected), Delete (only when all selected are downloaded), Mark all read, Close. Shows selected count.
- **KMP:** Partial — ChapterSelectionBar (DetailsScreen.kt:1173-1216) offers only Mark read, Download, Close + selected count. No bulk bookmark, no delete-downloaded, no mark-down-read.
- **Explanation:** The KMP multi-select bar is a strict subset. Missing: bulk bookmark (onBookmarkAll), delete downloaded chapters (onDeleteAll, conditional on all-downloaded), and mark-all-chapters-below-as-read (onMarkAllDownRead, single-selection). KDoc in DetailsScreen.kt:1170 acknowledges bookmark/delete/mark-down-read were deferred.
- **Suggested fix:** Add bulk bookmark, delete-downloaded (conditional), and mark-down-read actions to ChapterSelectionBar and corresponding intents/VM handlers to match the native ChapterSelectionActionsRow.

**🟡 [Medium] Chapter date formatting — KMP shows raw ISO date; native shows relative/localized date** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryChapterItem.kt:418-419 uses chapter.date?.toRelativeString(context) → Date.toRelativeString (Date.kt:13-17): "Today" / "Yesterday" / "MMM d, yyyy".
- **KMP:** Partial — ChapterRow renders date.toString() (DetailsScreen.kt:1100-1104), i.e. ISO yyyy-MM-dd, with no Today/Yesterday/localized month formatting.
- **Explanation:** Native presents human-friendly relative dates (Today/Yesterday) and a localized "MMM d, yyyy" format; KMP shows the locale-neutral ISO string. This is a noticeable UX and localization regression on every chapter row.
- **Suggested fix:** Format chapter dates with a Today/Yesterday/localized fallback (the header already has lastChapterDateLabel logic for Today/Yesterday/N days ago — reuse a shared relative-date helper for rows).

**🟡 [Medium] LAST_READ_DATE sort / lastReadDate field — Last-read-date sort and the underlying field are absent in KMP** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — SortType.LAST_READ_DATE sorts by chapter.lastReadDate (LibraryDetailsViewModel.kt:117,146-154).
- **KMP:** No — domain Chapter model (Chapter.kt) has no lastReadDate; no sort exists at all (see filter/sort finding).
- **Explanation:** Beyond the missing sort sheet, the KMP Chapter model lacks the lastReadDate timestamp that native uses to sort by reading recency, so even if sorting were added this option could not be reproduced without a data-model change.
- **Suggested fix:** If parity with the last-read sort is required, add a lastReadDate field to the domain/saved-chapter model and populate it on chapter open, then expose the sort option.

**🟡 [Medium] Header cover & parallax — Header layout and parallax behavior differ** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryMangaScreen.kt:253-259 paints a full-width blurred ImageWithGradientOverlay backdrop (headerHeightDp=250.dp, blur=14.dp) with a scroll-driven parallaxOffset (:131-141), and a centered 200x250dp rounded cover (CoverImage, InfoCompose.kt:34-49) above a centered title (20.sp bold) and "api language - status" info line.
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsHeader (DetailsScreen.kt:629-755) uses a Row with a 96dp-wide aspect-0.7 cover beside a left-aligned title/status/source column; backdrop is a blur(24.dp) AsyncImage with a verticalGradient scrim (DetailsHeaderBackdrop :766-794) but NO scroll parallax; title is titleLarge SemiBold left-aligned (not centered 20.sp bold).
- **Explanation:** The header is structurally redesigned: native centers a large 200x250 cover with a centered title over a 250dp parallax-scrolling blurred backdrop (14.dp blur); KMP uses a compact 96dp side-by-side cover with a static 24.dp-blur backdrop and left-aligned text. Different layout, blur radius, cover size, alignment, and the loss of the parallax scroll effect.
- **Suggested fix:** If visual parity matters, restore the centered large cover + centered title and the scroll-driven parallax backdrop with the native 14.dp blur and 250dp band; otherwise document the redesign as intentional.

**🟡 [Medium] Top-bar overflow menu (delete-all-downloaded, refresh, share, cancel-all) — Native overflow/cancel-all actions reorganized in KMP** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaTopAppBar.kt:49-98: a Stop icon to cancel all downloads (shown only while isDownloadingAll, error tint), a FilterList icon, and a MoreVert overflow with Delete all downloaded chapters / Refresh / Share items.
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsTopBar (DetailsScreen.kt:457-511) has bookmark heart, Downloads (navigates to Downloads screen), Open-in-WebView, and Refresh icons. No overflow menu, no delete-all-downloaded action, no cancel-all-downloads Stop button, no Share, no FilterList.
- **Explanation:** The native top bar exposes delete-all-downloaded-chapters and a cancel-all-downloads control (while downloading) plus refresh and a (no-op) share. KMP replaces this with direct icons and drops delete-all-downloaded, cancel-all-downloads, filter, and share. The native Share item was a no-op stub, but delete-all and cancel-all are real and missing.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a top-bar overflow (or actions) with delete-all-downloaded-chapters and a cancel-all-downloads affordance (visible while a bulk download runs), plus the filter entry point; treat share per product decision.

**🟡 [Medium] Download-all entry point & gating — Download-all is a header dropdown with custom-download in native vs a single header button in KMP** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — ActionsRow.kt:61-68 "Download all" ActionButton opens DownloadMenu (DownloadMenu.kt) with "Download all" and "Custom download / Download selected (N) / Cancel selection" items; also a Bookmark/Remove button, a Schedule (last-chapter relative date) button, and Open-in-browser button — four ActionButtons in a SpaceEvenly row.
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsHeader shows a single OutlinedButton "Download all" only when isInLibrary (DetailsScreen.kt:740-751) and an inert Schedule AssistChip; bookmark + open-in-browser moved to the top bar; there is no "custom download" menu. Custom/selected download is only reachable via long-press multi-select.
- **Explanation:** Native groups bookmark/last-update/download-all/open-in-browser as a 4-button header action row and exposes a download dropdown offering both "download all" and "custom download" (multi-select). KMP splits these: bookmark/webview to the top bar, download-all to a single header button, and custom download only via long-press. The discoverable "Custom download" menu entry is gone.
- **Suggested fix:** Consider adding a download menu (download all / custom select) to the header download button to restore the discoverable custom-download path, and review the header action-row layout for parity.

**🟡 [Medium] Back behavior in selection mode — Back press exits selection mode in native; KMP relies on a Clear button** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — BackHandler in LibraryMangaScreen.kt:178-184: if showChaptersCheckBox is active, back clears selection mode instead of navigating away.
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsScreen has no platform BackHandler intercept for selection mode; selection is cleared via the ChapterSelectionBar Close button (OnSelectionClear) or by toggling all off. System back would pop the screen even while chapters are selected.
- **Explanation:** Native intercepts the back gesture to first dismiss multi-select mode, a standard selection-mode UX. KMP's unified screen does not, so pressing back while in selection mode navigates away rather than exiting selection, losing the user's selection context unexpectedly.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a back interceptor (BackHandler / predictive-back) on the details screen that dispatches OnSelectionClear when state.isInChapterSelectionMode, falling through to navigate-back otherwise.

**⚪ [Low] Per-chapter file size — Downloaded chapter rows do not show file size in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryChapterItem.kt:343-351,434-461 computes FileSizeUtils.getFormattedChapterSize off-main and renders it after the date with a • separator, primary color, Medium weight, 12.sp AutoSubtitleText.
- **KMP:** No — ChapterRow (DetailsScreen.kt:1046-1165) shows only the chapter label and raw date; no per-chapter size.
- **Explanation:** Native displays each downloaded chapter's size next to its date. KMP omits this entirely, reducing per-chapter storage visibility.
- **Suggested fix:** When a chapter is downloaded and in-library, compute and display its formatted file size in the row subtitle (after the date with a bullet separator), matching native typography.

**⚪ [Low] Multi-select mark-read semantics — KMP bulk action only marks read; native toggles read** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — selection "mark all read" calls onMarkAllRead → viewModel.toggleChaptersRead(ids) (LibraryMangaRoute.kt:230-232, ViewModel.toggleChaptersRead :313-317), which flips read state.
- **KMP:** Partial — OnMarkSelectedRead calls markChaptersRead(selected) (DetailsViewModel.kt:572-577) via MarkChaptersReadUseCase — marks read only, never un-reads.
- **Explanation:** Native's bulk action is a toggle (read ↔ unread) per the toggleChaptersRead name, whereas KMP's bulk action only sets read. For a selection of already-read chapters, native would unmark them; KMP leaves them read. Subtle behavioral divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide intended semantics; if matching native, use a toggle-based bulk use case or compute the target state from the selection; otherwise document the deliberate change.

**⚪ [Low] Chapter label format — Chapter row title text differs between native and KMP** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryChapterItem.kt:404-409 shows chapter.number.ifBlank { chapter.name } (bold) — number only, name only as fallback, no prefix.
- **KMP:** Partial — chapterDisplayLabel (DetailsScreen.kt:1231-1238) shows "Ch. {number}" or "Ch. {number} — {name}" (details_chapter_label_number="Ch. %1$s", details_chapter_label_named="%1$s — %2$s").
- **Explanation:** Native renders just the raw chapter number (or name if number blank). KMP prefixes "Ch." and appends the name when present. For sources whose number field already contains text like "Volume 3 Ch. 7", KMP would render "Ch. Volume 3 Ch. 7", duplicating the prefix. Visual/text divergence on every row.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native by rendering number-only (name as fallback) or guard the "Ch." prefix so it isn't doubled for sources whose number already includes textual labeling.

**⚪ [Low] Banner ad in header — Header banner ad is absent in KMP** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryHeaderSection.kt:71 renders BannerAdView() in the header.
- **KMP:** No — DetailsHeader (DetailsScreen.kt:629-755) has no banner ad; AdMob ads are not part of the rework details surface.
- **Explanation:** Native shows a banner ad in the library detail header (and the route preloads/show rewarded ads on download via AdViewModel). KMP details has no ad surface. This is a monetization-behavior divergence; may be intentional but is a parity gap.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm whether ads are intended on the rework details screen; if so, add the banner ad slot and rewarded-ad-on-download hooks present in the native LibraryMangaRoute.

**⚪ [Low] Site-status / 403 pre-check — Native proactively probes site status and prompts WebView on 403; KMP only reacts on fetch failure** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryDetailsViewModel.getSiteStatus (:196-239) issues an OkHttp request to manga.url with the source's defaultHeaders on open and exposes imageStatus; LibraryMangaRoute.kt:86-98 raises a WebView dialog when the status is 403, and initializeSite() (:180-193) calls repo.initSite().
- **KMP:** Partial — there is no proactive site-status probe; KMP only routes to the WebView when the details fetch itself returns a challenge status (DetailsViewModel.runFetch onFailure → SolveCloudflareChallenge, CHALLENGE_STATUSES 403/429/503/520-524, DetailsViewModel.kt:160,404-418).
- **Explanation:** Native performs an independent HEAD/GET probe of the manga URL on screen entry to detect Cloudflare/anti-bot blocks and surface a WebView dialog even before/independent of the chapter fetch, and explicitly initializes the source site. KMP folds anti-bot handling into the single details fetch path. KMP's approach actually covers more status codes, but it drops the separate proactive probe and the explicit initSite call.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify the unified fetch path adequately initializes the source (headers/cookies) for in-library opens; if the proactive probe added value (e.g. for offline/blocked detection before fetch), consider an equivalent pre-check.

### Manga Details  `manga-details`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 28 (🔴1 🟠4 🟡11 ⚪12)

> The native details screen (DetailsContent + HeaderSection + ChapterItem + MangaDetailsScreen) is a centered hero layout: a 200x250dp cover above a centered Bold-20sp title and a single 'api language - status' metadata line, a banner ad, a grouped genres+description section with custom bordered chips, a 4-button equal-weight header action row (bookmark/last-chapter/download-all/open-in-browser), and a chapter list of shadowed cards showing the raw chapter number and a localized relative date. The KMP DetailsScreen redesigns this into a horizontal header (96dp side cover + left-aligned titleLarge title, with author/status/source/rating split across lines), moves bookmark/downloads/webview/refresh into the top app bar, drops the banner ad, replaces custom chips with Material AssistChips, adds a chapters-count header, re-formats chapter labels as 'Ch. N — name' with raw ISO dates, and adds per-chapter read-toggle + multi-select features absent in native. The two most serious divergences are behavioral/compliance regressions: the adult-content gate is inverted (native hard-blocks all adult content via a 3-step MStep dialog flow that always back-navigates, while KMP's single dialog lets the user Continue and view it), and the remove-from-library destructive-action confirmation (with its 'downloads will be deleted' warning) is gone. Other notable losses are the Firebase 'manga_open' analytics event, the Help affordance on the error state, the inline 403 WebViewDialog + 1s auto-retry, and two missing Arabic translations. The MVI data plumbing is solid and several additions (multi-select, broadened Cloudflare status set, offline saved-details overlay) exceed native, but visual and behavioral parity with the source of truth is only partial.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Manga Details</summary>

**🔴 [Critical] Adult-content gate (multi-step MStep monetization-block dialogs) — Native runs a 3-state gate (AdultWarning → MStep1 → MStep2) that blocks adult content entirely and forces back-navigation; KMP shows ONE dialog whose Continue reveals the content** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — DialogState enum {AdultWarning, MStep1, MStep2, None} (DialogState.kt:3); MangaDetailsScreen.kt:74-128 chains AdultConfirmationDialog → MConfirmationDialog(imgs1, showContinue=true) → MConfirmationDialog(imgs2, showContinue=false), and EVERY path ultimately calls onBackClick() — content is never shown
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsScreen.kt:418-429 a single AdultConfirmationDialog; Continue sets adultConfirmed=true and reveals the body (DetailsScreen.kt:420-423)
- **Explanation:** Native's adult gate is a hard content-block: it shows AdultConfirmationDialog (header 'Content unavailable', a 120dp red ic_pluss18 icon, a Play-policy apology message), then two MConfirmationDialog meme-image steps, and in ALL branches calls onBackClick() — the user is NEVER allowed to view adult content (Google Play policy compliance). KMP instead shows one dialog titled 'Adult content' with a 48dp Warning icon and a 'Continue only if you are over 18' message whose Continue button reveals the content (unblurs cover, shows chapters). This inverts the product/legal behavior: KMP now displays content native explicitly blocks. Also the icon (ic_pluss18 120dp red vs Material Warning 48dp), title text, and message text all differ.
- **Suggested fix:** Restore the native hard-block semantics: the adult gate must NOT permit viewing the content (all paths back-navigate), and port the multi-step MStep dialog flow + the ic_pluss18 asset, header 'Content unavailable', and the Play-policy message. This is a compliance-sensitive divergence.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). NATIVE (source of truth) — hard content-block, content never shown for adult manga: - DialogState.kt:3 — `enum class DialogState { AdultWarning, MStep1, MStep2, None }` (confirmed verbatim). - MangaDetailsScreen.kt:63 — adult manga initializes `dialogState = DialogState.AdultWarning` when `isPlus18(genres, api)` is true (else None). isPlus18 (MangaDerailsViewModel.kt:60-69) = any genre in the source's blackListGenres. - MangaDetailsScreen.kt:74-128 — `when (dialogState)` chains AdultWarning→MStep1→MStep2; EVERY terminal lambda calls onBackClick(): AdultWarning onDismiss=onBackClick (82); MStep1 onDismiss=onBackClick (96); MStep2 onConfirm=onBackClick (105) AND onDismiss=onBackClick (110). DialogState.None (DetailsContent, the only path that shows content) is reachable ONLY if isPlus18 is false at init — no dialog branch transitions into None. So adult content is never displayed. - AdultConfirmationDialog.kt: confirmButton (76-77) AND dismissButton (88-90) BOTH call onDismiss() — the dialog's onConfirm param (wired to →MStep1 in MangaDetailsScreen.kt:79) is dead code, so the first dialog ALWAYS back-navigates and MStep1/MStep2 are effectively unreachable. Icon: ic_pluss18, .size(120.dp), tint Color.Red.copy(0.65F) (54-60). Header "Content unavailable" (strings.xml:137); message is the Google-Play-policy apology "We're sorry — this content can't be shown. Due to Google Play policy..." (strings.xml:138). - MConfirmationDialog.kt:35,48-57 — random meme image (Plus18memes.imgs1/imgs2), .size(240.dp); Continue button only if showContinue (63). KMP (:ui) — single dialog, Continue REVEALS the content: - DetailsScreen.kt:284 `var adultConfirmed`; :288 `val shouldBlurCover = state.isAdult && !adultConfirmed`. - DetailsScreen.kt:418-428 — one AdultConfirmationDialog; onContinue (420-423) sets adultDialogVisible=false AND adultConfirmed=true → shouldBlurCover becomes false → DetailsBody (380-400) cover unblurs and chapters stay visible. onGoBack fires DetailsIntent.OnBackClick. - DetailsScreen.kt:1297-1342 — single dialog with NO MStep flow (KDoc 1286-1289 states the legacy MStep flow was dropped; KDoc 1293-1295 states no ic_pluss18). Icon = Icons.Filled.Warning, .size(48.dp), tint error.copy(0.8f) (1309-1315). Title "Adult content" (strings.xml:246); message "This title is flagged as adult content by the source. Continue only if you are over 18." (strings.xml:245); confirm "Continue" (1333), dismiss "Go back" (1338). Net: native NEVER shows adult content (Play-policy block, all paths back-navigate); KMP shows it on Continue. Icon (120dp red ic_pluss18 vs 48dp Material Warning), title ("Content unavailable" vs "Adult content"), and message (Play-policy apology vs over-18 notice) all differ as claimed.

**🟠 [High] Header action row (bookmark / last-chapter / download-all / open-in-browser) — Native renders a 4-button horizontal ActionButton row inside the header; KMP scatters these into the top bar and a single in-header button** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — HeaderSection.kt:109-146 renders a Row(SpaceEvenly) of 4 ActionButton: Bookmark/Remove, last-chapter Schedule, Download-all, Open-in-browser (Language icon)
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsScreen.kt:476-509 puts bookmark, downloads, open-in-webview, refresh as top-bar IconButtons; the Schedule label becomes a disabled AssistChip (723-734) and Download-all an OutlinedButton (740-751), both in the header column, not a row
- **Explanation:** Native presents a prominent equal-weight 4-action row under the cover (each ActionButton is icon 24.dp + AutoSubtitleText 10sp, weight(1f), SpaceEvenly). KMP removes this row entirely: bookmark/open-in-webview/downloads move to the top app bar as icon-only buttons (losing their text labels), the last-chapter date becomes a disabled chip, and download-all becomes a left-aligned OutlinedButton only shown when in-library. The action affordances, their layout, labels, and discoverability differ substantially.
- **Suggested fix:** Reconstruct the equal-weight header ActionButton row (bookmark, last-chapter schedule, download-all, open-in-browser) beneath the cover/metadata to match native placement and labeled-icon styling, rather than relocating them to the top bar.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — confirmed exactly as claimed: - HeaderSection.kt:109-146 renders `Row(horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceEvenly, modifier = fillMaxWidth())` containing 4 ActionButton, each `Modifier.weight(1f)`:   1) line 110-116 Bookmark/Remove (BookmarkBorder vs BookmarkRemove, action_bookmark/action_remove)   2) line 120-131 last-chapter Schedule icon with relative-date label (Today/Yesterday/N days/No-chapter-yet via daysSince(), onClick = {})   3) line 132-138 Download-all (Icons.Default.Download, action_download_all; if not saved → onRequestAddBookmark(true))   4) line 139-145 Open-in-browser (Icons.Default.Language, action_open_in_browser → onOpenInWebView) - ActionButton.kt:30-81 confirms each is a Column (CenterHorizontally): Icon Modifier.size(24.dp) at line 62-67 + AutoSubtitleText fontSize=10sp/maxSize=10sp/minSize=4sp at line 70-78. Matches "icon 24.dp + AutoSubtitleText 10sp, weight(1f), SpaceEvenly" exactly. - HeaderSection is genuinely used: DetailsContent.kt:141 calls it inside the chapter LazyColumn header item. The native top bar (DetailsContent.kt:101-111, TopAppBarCom) carries ONLY the title + a back IconButton — it has NO bookmark/download/open-in-browser icons. So in native these actions live ONLY in the in-header row. KMP — confirmed exactly as claimed (DetailsScreen.kt at /Users/.../ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/details/DetailsScreen.kt): - DetailsTopBar actions block lines 472-510 puts FOUR icon-only YamiIconButtons in the top app bar: bookmark (476-485, FavoriteFilled/FavoriteOutline), Download (489-493), OpenInWebView (497-501), and Refresh (504-509). These are icon-only (contentDescription only, no visible text label) — labels are lost vs native. - A code comment at line 486-488 explicitly states: "top-bar placement (no HeaderSection action-row equivalent in rework yet)", and line 716-718 comment says the schedule action became a chip. - The last-chapter Schedule action is a DISABLED AssistChip in the header Column: lines 723-734 (`onClick = {}, enabled = false`, Schedule leading icon, lastChapterDateLabel). - Download-all is an OutlinedButton in the header Column, shown ONLY `if (isInLibrary)`: lines 740-751 (np_details_download_all, Download icon + text), left-aligned within the Column at DetailsHeader (629-755), not in a SpaceEvenly row. - There is NO equal-weight 4-button SpaceEvenly ActionButton row anywhere in the KMP Details screen. The structural/layout/label/discoverability differences are real and correctly characterized.

**🟠 [High] Header layout: cover + title arrangement — Native centers a large 200x250dp cover above centered title/metadata; KMP places a small 96dp cover beside a left-aligned title column** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — HeaderSection.kt:62-102: Column(CenterHorizontally), AsyncImage size(200.dp,250.dp) clip RoundedCornerShape(8.dp), then centered Bold 20sp title, then centered bodyMedium metadata
- **KMP:** No (different) — DetailsScreen.kt:643-755: Box backdrop + Row with DetailsCover width 96.dp aspectRatio(0.7f) clip RoundedCornerShape(6.dp) on the LEFT and a left-aligned Column(weight 1f) with titleLarge SemiBold title

KMP: horizontal layout, cover 96dp wide aspectRatio 0.7 (≈96x137dp, 6dp corners) on the left, title left-aligned titleLarge SemiBold maxLines=2. Cover size, corner radius, alignment, title style/weight/size and overall composition all diverge.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native: centered Column header with a 200x250dp / 8dp-corner cover and a centered Bold 20sp title; or explicitly accept the redesign and document it.
