**🟠 [High] Chapter download button (not-in-library) — Native shows a tappable Download icon on every chapter row that prompts add-to-library when not saved; KMP shows only a static downloaded dot (or nothing) when not in library** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — ChapterItem.kt:87-94 IconButton always present; onClick = if(isSaved) onDownloadClick() else onRequestAddBookmark(); icon DownloadDone/Download tinted primary/onSurface .7
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsScreen.kt:1108-1162: trailing actions (read-toggle + download/cancel/done) render ONLY when isInLibrary; not-in-library rows show just an 8dp primary dot if downloaded, else nothing (no download affordance, no add-to-library prompt)
- **Explanation:** Native lets the user tap a per-chapter download button even before saving: it routes to the add-to-library prompt (onRequestAddBookmark). KMP hides all per-chapter download/read affordances unless the manga is already in the library, replacing them with a passive 8dp dot. A not-in-library user loses the per-chapter download entry point entirely.
- **Suggested fix:** Show a per-chapter download IconButton for not-in-library rows that dispatches the add-to-library confirm flow (matching native onRequestAddBookmark), instead of only a static dot.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): /native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/details/ui/screens/ChapterItem.kt:87-94 — IconButton is unconditionally present on EVERY chapter row: `IconButton(onClick = { if (isSaved) onDownloadClick() else onRequestAddBookmark() })`, with Icon = `if (chapter.isDownloaded) Icons.Default.DownloadDone else Icons.Default.Download`, tint primary when downloaded else onSurface.copy(alpha=0.7f). Call site DetailsContent.kt:164-173 renders ChapterItem for every `manga.chapters` item regardless of isSaved, passing `onRequestAddBookmark = { showAddBookmarkAlert.value = true }`. DetailsContent.kt:86-98 shows that alert is ConfirmDialogClean(title=add_library_title, confirmText=confirm_add_to_library, onConfirm -> onMangaBookmark(manga)) — i.e. an add-to-library prompt. So a not-in-library user tapping the per-chapter download icon is routed to the add-to-library dialog exactly as claimed. KMP: /ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/details/DetailsScreen.kt — ChapterRow (def at 1046, sole chapter-row composable, called once at line 611). Trailing actions block is gated by `if (isInLibrary)` at line 1108: read-toggle YamiIconButton (1110-1123) and the download/cancel/done `when` (1125-1151) render ONLY when in library. The `else if (chapter.isDownloaded)` branch (1152-1162) renders just an 8.dp primary-tinted Box (the "downloaded dot"); if not downloaded, nothing is rendered. There is NO download IconButton and NO add-to-library prompt on not-in-library rows. The doc comment at lines 1041-1042 confirms the intent: "Trailing actions are only shown when [isInLibrary] ... for a not-in-library manga the row keeps its prior tap-to-read + downloaded-dot shape." Conclusion: claim is exact on every point — native always-present tappable Download icon routing to add-to-library when unsaved vs KMP hiding all per-chapter download/read affordances unless isInLibrary, leaving only a passive 8dp dot. Line numbers cited (ChapterItem.kt:87-94, DetailsScreen.kt:1108-1162) match precisely.

**🟠 [High] Remove-from-library confirmation dialog — Native shows a confirm dialog before removing from library; KMP removes immediately with no confirmation** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** Yes — DetailsContent.kt:74-84 ConfirmDialogClean(remove_bookmark_title 'Remove Bookmark', remove_bookmark_message 'Are you sure... All downloaded chapters will be deleted.') gates removal (showBookmarkAlert)
- **KMP:** No — DetailsScreen.kt:349-351 isInLibrary tap dispatches OnToggleInLibrary directly with no confirm; only the ADD direction shows a dialog (DetailsScreen.kt:431-439)
- **Explanation:** Native asks the user to confirm before removing a manga from the library, warning that all downloaded chapters will be deleted (remove_bookmark_message). KMP removes immediately on tap (the remove direction is unconfirmed by design per the VM KDoc). A user can accidentally delete a library entry and its downloads with a single tap, losing the destructive-action warning native provided. (Note: native's showBookmarkAlert remove dialog appears defined but the header onClick path calls onMangaBookmark directly for the remove case at HeaderSection.kt:114 — still, the remove dialog and its warning string exist in native and are entirely absent in KMP.)
- **Suggested fix:** Add a remove-from-library confirmation dialog (with the 'all downloaded chapters will be deleted' warning) before dispatching OnToggleInLibrary on the in-library tap path.
- **Verification:** Refuted (corrected severity: NotABug). The claim's headline ("Native shows a confirm dialog before removing from library; KMP removes immediately") is contradicted by the native code itself for the manga-details screen under audit. NATIVE (manga-details screen): The remove button calls removal DIRECTLY with no confirmation. HeaderSection.kt:114 — `onClick = { if (isSaved) onMangaBookmark(manga) else onRequestAddBookmark(true) }`. When isSaved (the remove direction) the button invokes onMangaBookmark(manga) immediately. The remove-confirm dialog at DetailsContent.kt:74-84 (ConfirmDialogClean with remove_bookmark_title/remove_bookmark_message, strings.xml:179-180) is gated on `showBookmarkAlert.value`, but in the entire details feature that flag is only declared (DetailsContent.kt:57), read (74), and reset to false (79, 82) — it is NEVER set to true. grep across native-app/.../features/details/ confirms no `showBookmarkAlert.value = true` anywhere. So on the details screen the remove dialog is dead/unreachable UI; removal is unconfirmed. (The reachable remove dialog lives in a DIFFERENT feature, library_details/LibraryMangaScreen.kt:185-198 / onRequestBookmark at :288 — out of scope for the manga-details audit.) Native's add direction does prompt (showAddBookmarkAlert, DetailsContent.kt:86-98) via onRequestAddBookmark. KMP (manga-details screen): Identical behavior. DetailsScreen.kt:349-353 — `if (state.isInLibrary) { onIntent(OnToggleInLibrary) } else { showAddBookmarkAlert = true }`: remove tap toggles immediately, add tap shows AddBookmarkConfirmDialog (DetailsScreen.kt:431-439). DetailsViewModel.kt:490-501 onToggleInLibrary() calls toggleInLibrary(manga) with no confirmation in either direction; the only gate is the isTogglingBookmark double-tap race guard. Conclusion: On the audited manga-details screen BOTH apps remove from library immediately on tap with no confirmation, and BOTH show a confirm dialog only for the ADD direction — full behavioral parity. The claim's premise of a native-only destructive-action confirmation is false; the claim itself concedes this in its parenthetical (HeaderSection.kt:114 calls onMangaBookmark directly). The only real difference is the mere existence of unused remove_bookmark_* strings + an unreachable dialog composable in native's details code, which produces no user-visible behavior — not a functional/validation gap.

**🟡 [Medium] Header backdrop (blurred cover + gradient + parallax) — Native uses a 250dp ImageWithGradientOverlay backdrop with parallax scroll; KMP uses a matchParentSize blurred backdrop with no parallax and a different blur/gradient** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — DetailsContent.kt:118-123 ImageWithGradientOverlay(headerHeightDp=250.dp, blur=14.dp, parallaxOffset) where parallax = scrollOffset/2 (DetailsContent.kt:73); gradient background.copy(0.4f)→background (ImageWithGradientOverlay.kt:23-24)
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsScreenBackdrop matchParentSize blur(24.dp), gradient surface.copy(0.45f)→surface (DetailsScreen.kt:767-794); NO parallax scroll effect, height tracks header Row not a fixed 250dp band
- **Explanation:** Native blur radius is 14.dp over a fixed 250dp band with a parallax translationY = -scrollOffset/2 as the list scrolls. KMP blur is 24.dp, no parallax, the band height is whatever the header Row measures (not a fixed 250dp). Gradient start alpha 0.4f (native) vs 0.45f (KMP). The parallax motion is entirely missing.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the parallax translationY tied to list scroll offset, use a fixed 250dp backdrop band, and align blur (14.dp) and gradient start alpha (0.4f) to native.

**🟡 [Medium] Banner advertisement in header — Native shows a BannerAdView between metadata and description; KMP has none** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — HeaderSection.kt:104 BannerAdView() between the source/status line and the genres/description section
- **KMP:** No — grep for BannerAdView/AdView/admob in :ui and :presentation returns zero hits
- **Explanation:** The native details header embeds an AdMob banner ad (HeaderSection.kt:104, with Spacer(8.dp) above and below). The KMP details screen renders no ad anywhere. This is a monetization-surface regression on a core screen.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the banner-ad surface into the KMP details header (or expose an expect/actual ad slot) to restore the monetization placement; if intentionally dropped, document the product decision.

**🟡 [Medium] Chapter row label format — Native shows raw chapter.number (or name); KMP prefixes 'Ch. ' and joins name with an em-dash** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — ChapterItem.kt:76-77 Text(chapter.number.ifBlank { chapter.name }) FontWeight.Bold — raw number string, no prefix
- **KMP:** Yes — DetailsScreen.kt:1231-1238 chapterDisplayLabel uses details_chapter_label_number 'Ch. %s' and details_chapter_label_named '%s — %s'; row Text is bodyLarge FontWeight.Medium (DetailsScreen.kt:1083-1097)
- **Explanation:** Native renders the bare source number string (e.g. '12') in Bold; if number is blank it falls back to the chapter name. KMP wraps the number as 'Ch. 12' and, when a name exists, renders 'Ch. 12 — Name', with weight Medium (not Bold). The visible chapter label text, weight, and composition all differ from native.
- **Suggested fix:** Render the raw chapter.number with name fallback in Bold to match native, or document the 'Ch. N — name' template as an intended change.

**🟡 [Medium] Chapter row date format — Native shows a localized relative date (Today/Yesterday/'MMM d, yyyy'); KMP shows the raw ISO LocalDate.toString()** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **KMP:** Yes — DetailsScreen.kt:1098-1105 Text(date.toString()) — kotlinx.datetime LocalDate.toString() = ISO 'yyyy-MM-dd'
- **Explanation:** Native formats each chapter's date relatively and localized: 'Today', 'Yesterday', or 'MMM d, yyyy' (e.g. 'Jun 1, 2026'). KMP renders the unformatted ISO date '2026-06-01'. This is a visible per-row formatting regression and is not localized.
- **Suggested fix:** Format chapter.date with a relative/localized helper (Today/Yesterday/medium-date) mirroring Date.toRelativeString, instead of LocalDate.toString().

**🟡 [Medium] Genre chips styling — Native uses bordered Box chips (1dp onBackground .5 alpha, 6dp corners); KMP uses Material AssistChip** _(Component)_

**🟡 [Medium] 403 / Cloudflare challenge handling (inline WebViewDialog + auto-retry) — Native shows an inline WebViewDialog overlay on 403 then auto-retries after 1s; KMP navigates away to a full WebView screen** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaDetailsRoute.kt:57-67 Handle403Error wraps the screen, pops a WebViewDialog on State.Error code==403 (Handle403Error.kt:32-48), then on dismiss delay(1000) + onRetry()
- **KMP:** Partial — DetailsViewModel.kt:413-414 emits SolveCloudflareChallenge for statuses {403,429,503,520-524}; DetailsScreen.kt:317 routes to onSolveCloudflareChallenge → onOpenInWebView (a full screen navigation, not an inline dialog)
- **Explanation:** Native handles a 403 inline: it overlays a WebViewDialog (modal, stays on the details screen) and auto-retries the fetch 1 second after dismissal (max 1 dismissal). KMP navigates to a separate full WebView screen and relies on resume-time re-dispatch of OnRetry. The interaction model (inline modal dialog vs full-screen nav) and the 1s auto-retry timing differ; KMP does broaden the status set (429/503/520-524), which native did not.
- **Suggested fix:** Either restore an inline WebView dialog overlay with the 1s post-dismiss auto-retry, or document the full-screen-WebView model as an intentional redesign; verify the resume auto-retry actually fires.

KMP breaks this into up to four separate left-aligned lines (author, status as labelLarge primary, 'api · language' joined with a middle dot, and a '★ rating' line). KMP adds author and rating (native HeaderSection rendered neither author nor rating in this area), uses different separators ('·' vs '-'), different styles, and left alignment.

### Reader — Core / Paging  `reader-core`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 17 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡5 ⚪9)

> The native reader (source of truth) is a multi-chapter continuous feed: ReaderViewModel accumulates every loaded chapter's pages into one growing List<ReaderItem> (allReaderItems) that also contains inline NextChapterOverlay / ErrorOverlay sentinel items, and a single pager/LazyColumn spans ALL loaded chapters so the user reads seamlessly across chapter boundaries with automatic next-chapter loading at the end. It supports six reading modes via four distinct composables, per-page OOM/compression handling (99 MB threshold, BitmapPainter compression), custom per-mode reader icons, a download-percentage loading placeholder, a Card-based SeekBar with prev/next chapter step buttons, a top app bar + bottom action bar overlay, immersive system-bar hiding, and a banner ad below the reader. The KMP reader (ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt, presentation/reader/*) renders only the CURRENT chapter's pages (state.pages), clearing them on every chapter swap, so there is no cross-chapter continuous scroll and no append-based multi-chapter feed. It reaches good parity on chrome (top bar, HUD, scrubber, reading-mode dialog, immersive mode, share, bookmark, 403→WebView), and correctly maps the six modes to three layout composables, but it diverges materially on the core rendering pipeline: no continuous multi-chapter feed, no auto-load-next-chapter on scroll-to-end, no inline NextChapter/Error overlay sentinels in the page list, no OOM/large-image compression path, generic Material reading-mode icons instead of the custom drawables, and a plain spinner instead of the determinate download-% placeholder for the webtoon mode. Several of these are explicitly documented as deferred in the KMP KDocs.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Reader — Core / Paging</summary>

**🟠 [High] Reader chapter feed / continuous reading across chapters — Native is a multi-chapter continuous feed; KMP renders one chapter at a time** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderViewModel.kt loadChapter() appends each chapter's pages into one growing _allReaderItems list (line 228 `_allReaderItems.update { old -> old + itemsForThisChapter }`); goToNextChapter (473-489) loads the next chapter and APPENDS it without clearing, and the pager/LazyColumn spans every loaded chapter. setCurrentChapterIndex is derived from which item is visible (ReaderScreen.kt 268-300).
- **KMP:** No — ReaderViewModel.kt onEnter (374-392) sets `pages = emptyList()` on every chapter establish/change and runFetch replaces state.pages with the single current chapter's list (502-513). ReaderState.pages holds only the active chapter. onNextChapter (422-438) calls onEnter which clears pages entirely.
- **Explanation:** In native, after finishing chapter N the user keeps scrolling/swiping straight into chapter N+1's pages within the same list — a seamless binge-reading experience with both chapters resident. In KMP, advancing to the next chapter wipes the current pages and refetches, so there is a hard stop + reload at every chapter boundary and no overlap. This is a core reading-flow regression. The KMP ReaderState KDoc explicitly defers the 'multi-chapter feed' (lines 51-61).
- **Suggested fix:** Introduce a feed accumulator in the VM (a FetchChapterFeedUseCase or in-VM accumulation) that appends newly fetched chapters to state.pages instead of replacing, keying pages by (chapterUrl,index), and derive currentChapterIndex from the visible page's owning chapter — mirroring native allReaderItems.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). VERIFIED in both apps; every cited line checks out. NATIVE (source of truth) — multi-chapter continuous feed: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/reader/ui/viewmodel/ReaderViewModel.kt   - L63-64: single growing list `_allReaderItems`.   - L228: `_allReaderItems.update { oldList -> oldList + itemsForThisChapter }` — each loaded chapter is APPENDED, never replacing prior chapters (streaming path appends identically at L391/L394-414).   - L473-489 goToNextChapter: loads next chapter via `loadChapter(nextIdx,...)` and APPENDS; it does NOT clear `_allReaderItems`. (Only goToChapter L491-512 clears the list — used for explicit jumps, not for seamless next.)   - Each chapter's items carry `chapterIndex` (L204) and a NextChapterOverlay/ErrorOverlay marker (L207-224) so chapters are stitched into one timeline. - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/reader/ui/screens/ReaderScreen.kt   - L183-186: `pagerState = rememberPagerState(pageCount = { allReaderItems.size })` — the SINGLE pager spans EVERY loaded chapter's pages.   - L257-266: swiping to `allReaderItems.lastIndex` auto-calls goToNextChapter (append, no clear) — seamless binge scroll.   - L268-300: setCurrentChapterIndex is DERIVED from the visible item's `chapterIndex` (`snapshotFlow{pagerState.currentPage}`/`listState.firstVisibleItemIndex` → item.chapterIndex), exactly as claimed.   - All reading-mode composables (Vertical/Horizontal/WebToon/ContinuousVertical, L372-525) receive the whole `allReaderItems` list. KMP — one chapter at a time: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderViewModel.kt   - onEnter (L353-405): L379 sets `pages = emptyList()` on every chapter establish/change; L390 also resets pageProgress.   - runFetch (L491-554): L502-513 REPLACES `state.pages` with the single current chapter's list (`prev.copy(pages = pages, ...)`) — not append.   - onNextChapter (L422-438): L437 calls `onEnter(manga, current.chapters[nextIdx])`, which wipes `pages` and refetches → hard stop + reload at each boundary. (Note: the VM's stale KDoc at L40-41 claims it "owns ONE: ... single chapter" but its own audit postscript L134-148 flags that as STALE-SUPERSEDED; regardless, the LIVE code confirms single-chapter page rendering.) - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderState.kt   - `pages: List<Page>` (L146) holds only the active chapter; L51-61 "Deferred state fields" explicitly defers the multi-chapter feed ("needs a richer FetchChapterFeedUseCase that aggregates a sliding window of chapters"). L102-109 audit note distinguishes shipped multi-chapter NAVIGATION from the still-deferred multi-chapter page rendering. - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt   - L546-568 ReaderPageLayout / L1041-1345 layouts (ReaderVerticalList/HorizontalPager/VerticalPager) render ONLY `state.pages` (one chapter). pageCount/items are `pages.size`/`pages` (L1186-1187, L1239, L1308).   - L585-595 NextChapterOverlay appears only on the last page and on tap dispatches OnNextChapter → onEnter → clears+refetches (confirming the hard boundary, not an overlapping feed). Net: native keeps chapter N AND N+1 resident in one continuous pager/LazyColumn; KMP wipes chapter N's pages and refetches N+1 at every boundary. Difference is REAL and characterized correctly.

**🟠 [High] Auto-load next chapter on scroll/swipe to end — Native auto-loads the next chapter when the user reaches the end; KMP only marks-read and shows a tappable card** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebToonReadingMode.kt (95-106) and ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt (82-93) watch listState.isScrolledToTheEnd() and call onLoadNextChapter(); ReaderScreen.kt (257-266) watches pagerState.currentPage == lastIndex and calls goToNextChapter automatically.
- **KMP:** No — ReaderScreen.kt computes onLastPage (585) only to SHOW a NextChapterOverlay banner; no scroll-end watcher loads the next chapter. The VM's onPageChanged (448-477) on reaching pages.lastIndex only fires markChapterRead — it never triggers onNextChapter. The KDoc claims 'the reader auto-advances on the last page already (the VM's existing behaviour)' (line 1523) but no such code exists.
- **Explanation:** Native readers flow into the next chapter hands-free at the end of the current one (both paged and continuous modes). KMP requires an explicit tap on the NextChapterOverlay card or the top-bar Next button; there is no automatic advance, contradicting the in-file comment. This is a noticeable interaction regression for continuous reading.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a scroll-end / last-page watcher (snapshotFlow over listState.isScrolledToTheEnd() for the list modes and pagerState.currentPage == lastIndex for pagers) that dispatches OnNextChapter once per end-reach, guarded by an 'alreadyLoading' latch as native does.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) auto-loads next chapter at end in all reader modes: - /native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/reader/ui/reading_modes/WebToonReadingMode.kt L95-106: LaunchedEffect(listState){ snapshotFlow{ listState.isScrolledToTheEnd() }.collect{ reachedEnd -> if(reachedEnd && !alreadyLoading){ alreadyLoading=true; onLoadNextChapter() } ... } } — fires once per scroll-to-end. - ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt L82-93: identical pattern calling loadingNextChapter(). - isScrolledToTheEnd.kt L6-10: returns last visible item index == totalItemsCount-1 (true end detection). - ReaderScreen.kt L257-266: LaunchedEffect(pagerState.currentPage){ if(pagerState.currentPage == allReaderItems.lastIndex){ readerViewModel.goToNextChapter(...) } } — paged-mode hands-free advance, no tap. KMP has NO scroll-end/last-page auto-load (matches claim): - /ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt L585: onLastPage is computed only to render the TAPPABLE NextChapterOverlay (L586-595, onGoToNext={ onIntent(ReaderIntent.OnNextChapter) }). - The three layout composables install ONLY page-tracking snapshotFlows, no auto-load: ReaderVerticalList L1127-1131, ReaderHorizontalPager L1241-1245, ReaderVerticalPager L1310-1314 each `snapshotFlow{ firstVisibleItemIndex / currentPage }.distinctUntilChanged().collect(onPageChanged)`. - /presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderViewModel.kt onPageChanged L448-477: on reaching pages.lastIndex (L474) it ONLY does `viewModelScope.launch { markChapterRead(chapterUrl) }` (L475); it never calls onNextChapter(). The sole onNextChapter() path is explicit ReaderIntent.OnNextChapter (handle() L313 -> onNextChapter() L422), dispatched only by the top-bar Next button (L484) and the overlay card tap (L592). - grep across :ui/:presentation/:domain/:data finds no isScrolledToTheEnd / onLoadNextChapter / loadingNextChapter / reachedEnd reader logic. - The KDoc claim at KMP ReaderScreen.kt L1522-1523 ('the reader auto-advances on the last page already (the VM's existing behaviour)') is contradicted by the VM code above — no auto-advance exists; the comment is false. (Minor: claim's line refs are slightly imprecise — KDoc is at L1522-1523 not 1523, and the layout snapshotFlows are at ~L1127/1241/1310 — but the symbol/behavior identification is correct.)

**🟠 [High] Large-image OOM handling & bitmap compression — Native compresses/handles images over 99 MB and shows an OOM fallback; KMP has neither** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — every reading-mode image item checks `img.size <= 99L*1024*1024` (PagerImageItem.kt 101-133, WebToonReadingMode.kt 249-282, ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt 256-288) and routes oversized images to a CompressedImageHandler that calls ReaderViewModel.startImageCompression / compressImageToSizeOptimized (ViewModel 580-698, scaling to screen width). drawFallbackOnOOM.kt draws a broken-image icon + 'tap to open in WebView' fallback text on a draw exception.
- **KMP:** No — ReaderPageItem (1347-1507) renders via SubcomposeAsyncImage with loading/error slots only; there is no size threshold check, no compression, and no OOM draw-fallback. ReaderState KDoc lines 58-61 explicitly note compression was componentpruned/deferred ('needs a cross-platform bitmap-compression pipeline').
- **Explanation:** Native protects against decoding very large manga pages (long webtoon strips) by compressing them and shows a graceful OOM fallback that lets the user open the chapter in a WebView. KMP will attempt to decode at full size with only maxBitmapSize(Undefined) — for huge strips this risks OOM crashes or blank pages with no recovery affordance. Crash/regression risk on memory-constrained devices.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the 99 MB threshold + downscale-to-screen-width compression path (or rely on a per-request bitmap-size cap that bounds memory), and add an OOM draw-fallback modifier equivalent to drawFallbackOnOOM that offers Open-in-WebView when decode fails.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) implements all three pieces of the claim: - 99 MB threshold + compression routing in every reading mode:   * PagerImageItem.kt:101 `val maxBytes = 99L * 1024 * 1024`; :105 `if (img.size <= maxBytes)` else PagerCompressedImageHandler (:119-133) -> onStartImageCompression (:171).   * WebToonReadingMode.kt:249 `99L * 1024 * 1024`; :250 size check; else CompressedImageHandler (:269-279).   * ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:256 `99L * 1024 * 1024`; :260 size check; else ContinuousVerticalCompressedImageHandler (:276-287). - ReaderViewModel.kt:580-643 startImageCompression(...) launches a job calling compressImageToSizeOptimized; :669-698 scales bitmap to screen width (:680 widthScale=screenWidthPx/bitmap.width, :697 bitmap.scale(finalWidth,finalHeight)). - drawFallbackOnOOM.kt:87-142 wraps `runCatching { drawContent() }.onFailure { ... }`; on failure draws DarkGray bg (:93), broken-image icon (:96-99), and tappable "image too large / open in WebView" text (:103-140). Applied at PagerImageItem.kt:113-117, WebToonReadingMode.kt:260-264, ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:267-271. KMP confirms absence of all three: - ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt ReaderPageItem (fn at :1348, body :1356-1507) renders via SubcomposeAsyncImage (:1417) with only loading (:1422-1447) and error (:1448-1505) slots. The only bitmap-size handling is `.maxBitmapSize(Size(Dimension.Undefined, Dimension.Undefined))` (:1381) — no img.size threshold, no compression routing, no runCatching{drawContent()} OOM draw-fallback. The error slot's Open-in-WebView (:1499) fires only on a Coil load error, not on OOM-during-draw. - presentation/.../reader/ReaderState.kt:58-61 KDoc: "Per-page bitmap compression (was the legacy compressionStates shim, now componentpruned ...) — needs a cross-platform bitmap-compression pipeline." (claim cited 58-61; exact match.) - presentation/.../reader/ReaderViewModel.kt has no compressionStates / startImageCompression / 99MB threshold (only KDoc mentions of the pruned shim at :39). - The string image_too_large_tap_here_to_open_the_chapter_in_webview exists only as orphaned XML resources in composeApp (values/strings.xml:349 et al.) and is referenced by ZERO KMP code (grep across ui/composeApp/presentation kotlin returned nothing). Minor citation nit: claim says ReaderPageItem 1347-1507; function signature is at 1348. Immaterial. KMP KDoc 58-61 and native 99MB line refs are all accurate.

**🟡 [Medium] Reading-mode picker dialog icons — Native shows a distinct custom drawable per reading mode; KMP shows only a generic Check on the staged item** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReadingMode.kt assigns each mode a custom drawable (ic_reader_continuous_vertical_24dp, ic_reader_rtl_24dp, ic_reader_ltr, ic_reader_vertical_24dp, ic_reader_webtoon_24dp). ReadingModeChips.kt ChipItem (68-73) renders painterResource(mode.iconRes) at 20.dp tinted onPrimary/primary alongside the label.
- **KMP:** No — ReadingScreen.kt ReadingModeDialog (826-843) renders each FilterChip with label only; leadingIcon is YamiIcons.Check ONLY when the chip is staged-selected (831-840). There is no per-mode glyph. readingModeLabel (875-882) resolves text only; the domain ReadingMode enum carries no icon (by design).
- **Explanation:** Native users recognise reading modes by their distinctive direction/orientation glyphs (RTL arrow, webtoon strip, vertical, etc.). KMP loses all of these — every chip looks identical except for text and a checkmark, reducing scannability and visual parity of the picker.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a `when(mode)` icon lookup in :ui (co-located with readingModeLabel) mapping each ReadingMode to an appropriate vector/imported drawable, and render it as the chip leadingIcon (keeping the Check only as the selection affordance, or overlaying as native does).

**🟡 [Medium] Inline NextChapter / Error sentinel items in the page stream — Native injects NextChapterOverlay and ErrorOverlay as real items in the scrollable feed; KMP renders a single overlay banner aligned to the bottom** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderViewModel.loadChapter appends a ReaderItem.NextChapterOverlay (or ErrorOverlay 'No Next Chapter') after each chapter's images (208-224); the reading-mode composables render NextChapterCard (full-screen, fillMaxSize, surface @95% alpha, clickable) and errorCard as ordinary list/pager items between chapters. ErrorOverlay also carries errorCode (e.g. 403) used to auto-open WebView (ReaderScreen 197-205).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP has a single NextChapterOverlay composable (1528-1588) but it is drawn as a bottom-aligned banner over the page area (align BottomCenter, alpha 0.95) only when onLastPage, not as an in-stream item; per-chapter error sentinels do not exist (errors go through state.error / ReaderErrorPane for the whole screen, plus per-page SubcomposeAsyncImage error slot).
- **Explanation:** Because native carries chapter-boundary cards inside the feed, the user scrolls THROUGH a 'You are in X / Going to Y' card between chapters and through per-chapter error cards mid-feed. KMP collapses this into one bottom banner on the last page of the (single) current chapter, so the mid-feed boundary affordance and per-chapter inline error cards are absent. Combined with the single-chapter feed, the inter-chapter visual rhythm differs.
- **Suggested fix:** Once a multi-chapter feed lands, model NextChapter/Error sentinels as list items (e.g. a sealed ReaderFeedItem) rendered inline between chapters, mirroring native's NextChapterCard/errorCard placement and the 403 errorCode auto-WebView trigger.

**🟡 [Medium] Page seekbar / scrubber layout — Native uses three rounded Cards (prev-card, slider-card with N…total labels, next-card); KMP uses a flat Row of two icon buttons + bare Slider** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — SeekBarContainer.kt: Row with three Cards (RoundedCornerShape(50), background @0.8 alpha). Left/right cards hold IconButtons (ic_previous / ic_next custom drawables) for chapter step; center card holds current-page number (progress+1) bodySmall, a Slider (weight 9), and total-page number bodySmall. Cards give a pill background; valueRange 0f..total-1, steps total-1.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderPageScrubber (949-995): a plain Row with NavigateBefore icon button (page-1), a bare Material Slider (no surrounding Card/pill, no inline page-number labels), and NavigateNext icon button (page+1). No rounded-card pill backgrounds; no '1' / total numeric labels flanking the slider; uses Material AutoMirrored Navigate icons rather than custom ic_previous/ic_next.
- **Explanation:** Native's scrubber is a polished 3-pill control with visible current/total page numbers beside the slider and the buttons step CHAPTERS (prev/next chapter), whereas KMP's buttons step a single PAGE and there are no numeric labels or pill backgrounds. Both the visual treatment and the button semantics differ (chapter-step vs page-step), and the inline page counters are missing (the count only appears in the separate HUD/top-bar).
- **Suggested fix:** Wrap the scrubber controls in rounded Surface/Card pills at 0.8 alpha, add current/total page number Texts flanking the Slider (bodySmall onBackground), and decide whether the flanking buttons should step chapters (native) or pages (current KMP) — native steps chapters via onPrevious/onNext.

**🟡 [Medium] Reader top app bar content & styling — Native top bar shows manga title (titleLarge) + chapter number subtitle (bodySmall) over a translucent background with a menu (dots) button; KMP shows a single title line with chapter/page count labels and many action icons** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — ControlOverlay.kt TopAppBar (105-156): a custom 56.dp Row with background @0.8 alpha, back IconButton (ic_back_), a Column with manga name (titleLarge, maxLines 1 ellipsis) + 2.dp spacer + chapter number (bodySmall, onBackground @0.75 alpha), and a trailing 'dots' menu IconButton (currently a no-op onMenu).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderTopBar (637-777) uses Material3 TopAppBar with a single title (chapterDisplayTitle, titleMedium, ellipsis) — NOT manga name + chapter subtitle. Actions row packs Prev-chapter, an 'N / total' chapter label, Next-chapter, an 'X / Y' page label, Bookmark, Share, and an Overflow(MoreVert) button that opens the reading-mode dialog.
- **Explanation:** Native's title area is two-line (manga name primary, chapter number secondary) on a translucent custom bar; KMP shows only the chapter title (manga name is not displayed in the bar) and instead surfaces chapter/page counters and several actions inline. The information shown (manga name vs chapter), the typography (titleLarge vs titleMedium), and the translucent-background treatment differ. Native's overflow 'dots' is a placeholder no-op, whereas KMP's overflow opens the reading-mode dialog (native opens that dialog from the BOTTOM action bar settings icon instead).
- **Suggested fix:** Show manga title as the primary line and chapter number as a secondary subtitle (titleLarge + bodySmall) to match native; consider a translucent bar background. Reconcile where the reading-mode picker is triggered (native: bottom settings icon; KMP: top overflow).

**🟡 [Medium] Bottom action bar (settings / bookmark / share) — Native has a dedicated bottom action bar with Settings/Bookmark/Share; KMP folds these into the top bar and has no bottom action bar** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — ControlOverlay.kt BottomActionBar (158-196): a 56.dp Row at 0.8 alpha holding three weight(1f) IconButtons — Settings (ic_reader_setting, opens ReadingModeDialog), Bookmark (Icons.Filled.Bookmark / Outlined.BookmarkBorder), Share (ic_panal_shera). It sits below the SeekBarContainer in the bottom overlay Column.
- **KMP:** No — there is no bottom action bar. ReaderScreen's bottom chrome (607-630) contains only the page-indicator HUD pill and the page scrubber. Settings(reading-mode), Bookmark, and Share were all moved into the top bar actions (738-764).
- **Explanation:** Native splits chrome into a top app bar (title + back + dots) and a bottom action bar (settings/bookmark/share) above the seekbar. KMP has no bottom action bar at all and relocates those three actions to the top bar. The control layout and the bottom-of-screen reachability of bookmark/share/settings differ from native.
- **Suggested fix:** If strict layout parity is desired, add a bottom action bar row (settings → reading-mode dialog, bookmark, share) above the scrubber at 0.8 alpha with weighted icon buttons, matching native ControlOverlay.BottomActionBar, instead of (or in addition to) the top-bar actions.

**⚪ [Low] Webtoon/continuous loading placeholder (download %) — Native shows a determinate ring with download percent + byte size; KMP shows a plain or determinate spinner without size text** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebToonReadingMode.kt LoadingImagePlaceholder (357-414) renders a CircularProgressIndicator with progressState.percent/100, an overlaid percent Text (labelMedium), and a separate size Text (bodySmall, alpha 0.6) via ProgressManager/formattedPercent/formattedSize.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderPageItem loading slot (1422-1447) shows a determinate ring when PageDownloadProgress.InProgress.fraction is non-null, otherwise an indeterminate spinner. There is NO percent text and NO byte-size text; ContinuousVerticalReadingMode native actually used a plain spinner so continuous mode matches, but webtoon mode loses the percent/size readout.
- **Explanation:** Native's webtoon loading placeholder gives rich feedback (e.g. '47%' + '1.2 MB / 2.6 MB') while large strips download. KMP shows only a ring with no numbers, so users get less feedback during slow page loads. The KMP ReaderScreen KDoc even notes this as a known difference (lines 157-160).
- **Suggested fix:** Render the fraction as a percent label overlaid on the determinate ring and add a byte-size sub-label when the platform progress (PageDownloadProgress.InProgress) carries downloaded/total bytes, matching native LoadingImagePlaceholder.

**⚪ [Low] NextChapterCard layout & typography — Native shows a 4-line full-screen card (you-are-in / current / going-to / next) with titleLarge primary+secondary; KMP shows a compact bottom banner with titleMedium and a single accent color** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — NextChapterCard.kt: full-screen Box (fillMaxSize + heightIn(screenHig)), 24.dp padding, surface @0.95 alpha; texts: 'you_are_in' (bodyMedium onSurface), current chapter quoted in titleLarge primary, 'going_to' (bodyMedium onSurface), next chapter quoted in titleLarge secondary (note: native uses TWO different accent colors — primary for current, secondary for next).
- **KMP:** Partial — NextChapterOverlay (1528-1588): bottom banner (fillMaxWidth + padding spacing.md, RoundedCornerShape, tonalElevation 6.dp); 'you_are_in' labelMedium onSurfaceVariant, current titleMedium onSurface, 'going_to' labelMedium onSurfaceVariant, next titleMedium PRIMARY (single accent — no secondary color), terminal 'no next chapter' bodyMedium onSurfaceVariant.
- **Explanation:** Beyond placement (banner vs full-screen, separate finding), the typography scale differs (titleLarge vs titleMedium; bodyMedium vs labelMedium for the connective text) and native uses primary for the current chapter and secondary for the next, while KMP uses onSurface + primary. Cosmetic divergence in the chapter-transition card.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the text styles (titleLarge for chapter labels, bodyMedium for connective lines) and use distinct accent colors (primary for current, secondary for next) to match native NextChapterCard.

**⚪ [Low] Reading-mode dialog footer buttons & icons — Native footer uses an OutlinedButton (Revert) + filled Button (Apply, onBackground bg, Check + label in background color); chips use FilterChip with primary selected container; KMP uses default Material button/chip colors** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReadingModeDialog.kt: Surface tonalElevation 8.dp, surfaceContainerHigh, RoundedCornerShape(16). Header 'Reading mode' headlineSmall Bold. Footer Revert = OutlinedButton with 1.dp onBackground border, RoundedCornerShape(8), bold onBackground text; Apply = Button with containerColor onBackground, RoundedCornerShape(8), Check icon (18.dp, tint background) + bold label in background color. Chips: FilterChip selectedContainerColor primary, RoundedCornerShape(18), height 40.dp.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReadingModeDialog (797-863): Surface RoundedCornerShape(spacing.lg), color surface, tonalElevation 8.dp; title np_reader_mode_dialog_title titleLarge (not headlineSmall Bold). Footer Revert = OutlinedButton (default colors), Apply = Button (default primary colors) with a Check icon + label. Chips: default FilterChip colors, fillMaxWidth, no explicit 40.dp height or RoundedCornerShape(18).
- **Explanation:** Both implement a staged-selection Apply/Revert dialog (good behavioral parity), but the visual treatment differs: native uses bespoke onBackground/background button colors, explicit 8/16/18 dp corner radii, headlineSmall Bold header, and fixed 40.dp chip height; KMP uses default Material colors and theme spacing tokens, with titleLarge header. Subtle cosmetic divergence in the picker.
- **Suggested fix:** If pixel parity matters, align corner radii (16 dialog / 18 chips / 8 buttons), use headlineSmall Bold for the header, and match the onBackground/background filled-Apply button styling; otherwise document as an intentional theme-token modernization.

**⚪ [Low] DEFAULT reading mode resolution — Both treat DEFAULT as paged-vertical, but neither resolves a per-source preferred mode — KMP explicitly defers it** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Partial — isPaged.kt marks DEFAULT as paged; ReaderScreen.kt maps DEFAULT and VERTICAL to the same VerticalReadingMode (VerticalPager). Native also does not resolve a per-source default in this code path (DEFAULT == VERTICAL).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt ReaderPageLayout (1077-1087) maps DEFAULT and VERTICAL both to ReaderVerticalPager; the KDoc (1073-1076) explicitly flags per-source DEFAULT resolution as deferred (§66).
- **Explanation:** This is actually a parity MATCH at the code level — both treat DEFAULT as vertical paging. Noted only to confirm no regression here and to record that the documented 'per-source preferred mode' is not implemented on either side, so it is not a KMP-specific gap.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed for parity; if per-source default is eventually wanted, implement it on both — but it is currently equivalent.

**⚪ [Low] Pager image content scale (paged modes) — Native paged modes load the image via SubcomposeAsyncImage with default (no explicit Fit) while KMP forces ContentScale.Fit** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — PagerImageItem.kt (107-118) uses SubcomposeAsyncImage with no explicit contentScale on the success path (Coil default = Fit), but the compressed-painter branch (50-62) uses ContentScale.Fit explicitly; horizontal/vertical pagers fill the page via .fillMaxSize().
- **KMP:** Yes — ReaderHorizontalPager/ReaderVerticalPager pass contentScale = ContentScale.Fit to ReaderPageItem (1278, 1342); list modes use the default FillWidth (1355).
- **Explanation:** Effectively equivalent for paged modes (both Fit) and for list modes (both FillWidth/wrapContentHeight semantics). Recorded to confirm the per-mode content-scale split is preserved and no scaling regression was introduced.
- **Suggested fix:** No change needed; content-scale per mode matches native (Fit for pagers, FillWidth for vertical list).

**⚪ [Low] Zoom / pinch gesture implementation — Native uses engawapg zoomableWithScroll on pagers/lists and telephoto ZoomableAsyncImage in one helper; KMP uses engawapg zoomable() on pagers/list** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — HorizontalReadingMode/VerticalReadingMode/WebToon/ContinuousVertical apply Modifier.zoomableWithScroll(rememberZoomState(), onTap=...) (e.g. HorizontalReadingMode.kt 46-50). A separate ZoomableImage.kt uses me.saket.telephoto ZoomableAsyncImage, though it is not referenced by the active reading-mode composables.
- **KMP:** Yes — ReaderHorizontalPager/ReaderVerticalPager/ReaderVerticalListBody apply Modifier.zoomable(rememberZoomState()) (1174, 1262-1264, 1327-1329). Tap is handled separately by detectTapGestures on the outer Box (514-516) rather than via zoomable's onTap.
- **Explanation:** Both provide pinch-to-zoom via the engawapg library. Native combines tap + zoom in zoomableWithScroll(onTap=...); KMP separates the chrome-toggle tap onto an outer Box detectTapGestures and uses plain zoomable(). Functionally close; minor risk that KMP's outer-box tap and the zoomable double-tap-to-zoom could interact differently than native's integrated onTap, but no concrete defect observed.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify on-device that single-tap chrome-toggle and double-tap zoom coexist; if conflicts arise, consider routing tap through zoomable's onTap like native zoomableWithScroll.

**⚪ [Low] First-chapter loading indicator — Native shows a centered spinner overlay only while the FIRST chapter (startIndex) loads; KMP shows a centered spinner whenever isInitialLoading (no pages yet)** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderScreen.kt derives isFirstChapterLoading = isCurrentChapLoading && currentChapterIndex == startIndex (309-311) and shows a full-size centered CircularProgressIndicator(primary) (623-632); subsequent chapters show in-mode loading (LoadingScreen / per-card spinners).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt shows CircularProgressIndicator centered when state.isInitialLoading (523-525), i.e. isLoading && pages.isEmpty(). Because KMP clears pages on every chapter swap, this centered spinner appears on EVERY chapter transition, not just the first.
- **Explanation:** Native distinguishes the initial load (big centered spinner) from later chapter loads (in-feed spinners) because later chapters append to an existing feed. In KMP, since pages are cleared on each chapter change, the full-screen initial-loading spinner re-appears at every chapter boundary, which is a louder loading state than native shows for non-first chapters. This is a downstream symptom of the single-chapter-feed design.
- **Suggested fix:** Once the multi-chapter feed is in place, only show the full-screen spinner for the very first fetch (no prior pages) and use in-feed placeholders for subsequent chapters, mirroring native's isFirstChapterLoading gate.

**⚪ [Low] Banner ad below reader — Native renders a BannerAdView under the reader content; KMP has none in the reader-core screen** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderScreen.kt (617) places BannerAdView() in the outer Column directly beneath the reader Box, so an ad strip is always visible at the bottom of the reader.
- **KMP:** No — the KMP ReaderScreen Scaffold content contains only the page layout, overlays, HUD and scrubber; there is no banner ad composable.
- **Explanation:** Native reserves space for and shows a banner ad at the bottom of the reader. KMP omits it. This affects layout (native reader content height is reduced by the ad strip) and monetization parity. May be intentional for the rework, but it is a divergence from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** If ads are part of the product, add the banner ad slot beneath the reader content (or document the omission as intentional for the KMP migration).

**⚪ [Low] ProManga / Prochan streaming page accumulation — Both handle streaming sources, but native interleaves new pages before the inline overlay while accumulating; KMP replaces the whole list per emission** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderViewModel.loadChapterStreaming (277-468) tracks added URLs, inserts only NEW images, and places them BEFORE the NextChapter/Error overlay item in the existing list, with completion detection when allUrls.size == trackedUrls.size.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderViewModel.runFetch (491-554) treats every Success as the latest cumulative snapshot and replaces state.pages wholesale (502-513); startObservingProgress restarts all per-page observers on each emission (582-596). FetchChapterPagesUseCase just forwards the repo flow.
- **Explanation:** Both ultimately render the growing page set for streaming sources. Native does incremental insertion preserving overlay position and uses URL-set tracking; KMP relies on monotonic cumulative emissions and replaces the list (with url-keyed LazyColumn items to keep composables stable). Behaviorally similar for the user, but KMP's full-list replacement plus observer restart per emission is more churny and could cause minor scroll/recompose differences for streaming sources. No concrete defect, but worth noting given native is the reference.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm streaming sources render smoothly with url-keyed items; if scroll jumps or observer churn appear on Prochan, switch to incremental append + targeted observer add rather than restart-all per emission.

</details>

### Reader — Controls & Settings  `reader-controls`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 20 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡7 ⚪11)

> Native renders reader chrome as a custom-built overlay: a scrimmed top Row (custom drawables for back/menu/share/settings, manga-name title + chapter-number subtitle stacked) animated in/out, plus a bottom Column containing a SeekBarContainer (prev/next-chapter rounded cards flanking a page-number Slider in its own rounded card) and a separate BottomActionBar (settings/bookmark/share spread evenly with weight). KMP relocates everything into a Material3 TopAppBar (back nav icon + prev-chapter chevron + "N / M" chapter label + next-chapter chevron + "X / Y" page label + bookmark + share + overflow), and a bottom AnimatedVisibility Column with a rounded HUD pill ("3 / 27") above a ReaderPageScrubber (prev-page button + Slider + next-page button). Both share the tap-to-toggle + auto-hide-after-3s behavior and a staged Apply/Revert reading-mode dialog. Headline divergences: the entire top-bar layout shape and icon set differ (custom branded drawables vs generic Material icons); native's chapter Prev/Next live in the bottom seekbar while KMP's live in the top bar; native shows a BannerAdView under the reader (absent in KMP); KMP adds page-count/chapter-count labels and a HUD pill that native lacks; the reading-mode chips drop the per-mode icons; several string labels diverge; and native's full-screen NextChapterCard becomes a bottom banner. The KMP version is functionally rich (it even fixes native's chapter-nav icon/label inversion and adds Cloudflare auto-recovery) but visually and structurally is a redesign, not a port.

**🟠 [High] Reader top bar title — Native shows a two-line title (manga name titleLarge + chapter number bodySmall subtitle); KMP shows a single-line chapter title in titleMedium** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — ControlOverlay.kt:133-146: Text(title=mangaName, style=titleLarge, color=onBackground, maxLines=1, Ellipsis) then 2.dp Spacer then Text(number=chapterNumber, style=bodySmall, color=onBackground.copy(alpha=0.75f)).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:662-668 single Text(title = chapterDisplayTitle(chapter), style=titleMedium, maxLines=1, Ellipsis). The displayed string is chapter.name/number (ReaderScreen.kt:1612-1614), NOT the manga name; no second subtitle line.
- **Explanation:** Native dedicates the title to the MANGA NAME (currentChapter.mangaName) with the chapter number as a smaller 75%-alpha subtitle underneath. KMP shows only the chapter title (chapter.name, falling back to number, falling back to literal 'Chapter') and never shows the manga name at all. A reader in KMP cannot see which manga they are in from the top bar, and the typography scale (titleLarge vs titleMedium) and the subtitle line are both lost.
- **Suggested fix:** Render the manga title as the primary TopAppBar title (titleLarge equivalent) and add a secondary subtitle line with the chapter number (bodySmall, onSurface at ~0.75 alpha), mirroring ControlOverlay TopAppBar's Column.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — two-line title confirmed. ControlOverlay.kt:60-65 the reader's TopAppBar is called with `title = currentChapter.mangaName` and `number = currentChapter.chapterNumber`. The private TopAppBar (ControlOverlay.kt:105-156) renders a Column with TWO Text lines: line 133-139 `Text(text=title, style=titleLarge, color=onBackground, maxLines=1, overflow=Ellipsis)`, then line 140 `Spacer(height=2.dp)`, then line 141-146 `Text(text=number, style=bodySmall, color=onBackground.copy(alpha=0.75f), maxLines=1)`. So the MANGA NAME is the titleLarge top line and the chapter number is the 75%-alpha bodySmall subtitle. The native model ReaderChapters.kt:14,21 has both `chapterNumber: String` and `mangaName: String`. KMP — single-line chapter title confirmed. ReaderScreen.kt:469-470 calls `ReaderTopBar(title = chapterDisplayTitle(state.chapter ?: chapter), ...)`. ReaderTopBar (ReaderScreen.kt:637-668) renders exactly ONE Text in the title slot: lines 663-668 `Text(text=title, maxLines=1, overflow=Ellipsis, style=MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium)`. No second/subtitle line exists. The displayed string comes from chapterDisplayTitle (ReaderScreen.kt:1612-1614): `chapter.name.ifBlank { chapter.number.ifBlank { stringResource(Res.string.reader_chapter_fallback) } }`. The fallback string resolves to the literal "Chapter" (strings.xml:313 `<string name="reader_chapter_fallback">Chapter</string>`). Crucially, the KMP domain Chapter model (Chapter.kt:62-82) has `number` and `name` but NO mangaName field at all — so the manga name genuinely cannot be shown from the KMP reader top bar. Net: native = two-line (manga name titleLarge + chapter number bodySmall@75% subtitle); KMP = single-line chapter name/number/"Chapter" in titleMedium, no manga name, no subtitle. Every cited line number, style token, color alpha, and fallback chain matches the claim exactly.

**🟠 [High] Banner advertisement — Native shows a BannerAdView below the reader content; KMP has none** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderScreen.kt:617 BannerAdView() is placed in the outer Column directly under the reader Box (so the reader content has weight(1F) and the ad occupies the residual height at the bottom).
- **KMP:** No — neither ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt nor the route adapter ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt renders any banner/AdMob view (grep for banner/adview/admob returns only the NextChapterOverlay KDoc 'banner' wording).
- **Explanation:** The native reader reserves bottom screen space for an AdMob banner that is part of the app's monetization. The KMP reader is full-bleed with no ad slot. This is a missing monetization surface and also changes the available vertical space for the page image.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the cross-platform banner ad slot to the reader route (below the page area) if monetization parity is required, mirroring the BannerAdView placement; if ads are intentionally dropped in KMP, confirm with product.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/.../reader/ui/screens/ReaderScreen.kt:617 places BannerAdView() in the outer Column (opened L356), directly under the reader Box which carries .weight(1F) (L363) — so the reader content gets the weighted height and the ad occupies the residual bottom strip, exactly as claimed. The only 'banner' tokens in the file are the NextChapterOverlay KDoc at L1512 ('Rendered as a banner pinned to the bottom of the page area') and L1522 ('A bottom banner ...'), describing the next-chapter transition card, not an ad — precisely matching the claim. composeApp/.../navigation/routes/ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt (entire file) only renders ReaderScreen(...) Net: no banner ad anywhere in KMP, and the reader has no ad slot. **🟡 [Medium] Reader top bar — Top bar is a custom scrimmed Row in native vs a Material3 TopAppBar in KMP** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — ControlOverlay.kt:106-156 TopAppBar() is a hand-built Row with .height(56.dp), .background(colorScheme.background.copy(alpha=0.8f)), .padding(horizontal=8.dp); back IconButton, weighted Column title, menu IconButton.

The visual result differs: native shows the page faintly through the bar, KMP shows a solid bar. Height, padding, and color token also differ (native fixed 56.dp Row with explicit 8.dp horizontal padding vs M3 default 64.dp content height and 4.dp action spacing).
- **Suggested fix:** If exact parity is desired, replace the M3 TopAppBar with a Row matching native (height 56.dp, background colorScheme.background at alpha 0.8f, horizontal padding 8.dp) or apply TopAppBarColors with a translucent containerColor; otherwise document the intentional M3 redesign.

**🟡 [Medium] Reader top bar icons — Native uses custom branded drawables (ic_back_, dots, ic_reader_setting, ic_panal_shera); KMP uses generic Material icons** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — ControlOverlay.kt:122 R.drawable.ic_back_, :150 R.drawable.dots (menu), :176 R.drawable.ic_reader_setting (settings), :191 R.drawable.ic_panal_shera (share); SeekBarContainer.kt:57 ic_previous, :121 ic_next.

- **Explanation:** Every reader-chrome glyph in native is a bespoke drawable (custom back arrow, three-dots, settings gear, share 'panal_shera', custom previous/next). KMP substitutes stock Material icons. The settings gear in particular (ic_reader_setting) becomes a generic overflow MoreVert in KMP, changing the affordance's meaning from 'reader settings' to 'more options'.
- **Suggested fix:** Bundle the native reader drawables (ic_back_, ic_reader_setting, ic_panal_shera, ic_previous, ic_next, dots) as composeResources and map YamiIcons entries to them for visual brand parity, or accept the Material redesign and document it.

**🟡 [Medium] Chapter previous/next navigation placement — Native puts Prev/Next-CHAPTER buttons in the bottom seekbar flanking the page slider; KMP puts them in the top bar** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — SeekBarContainer.kt:44-63 (prev-chapter rounded Card+IconButton, ic_previous) and :108-130 (next-chapter rounded Card+IconButton, ic_next), one on each side of the page Slider; wired to onNext/onPrevious chapter in ControlOverlay.kt:83-89.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:688-713 PrevChapter/NextChapter YamiIconButtons sit in the TopAppBar actions row, with a '${idx+1} / $chaptersCount' label between them. The bottom scrubber's prev/next buttons are page-level, not chapter-level (ReaderScreen.kt:970-993).
- **Explanation:** The chapter-navigation affordance moved from the bottom-center seekbar (thumb-reachable, beside the page slider) to the top bar. Functionally both exist, but the location, grouping (native groups them with the page slider in rounded cards), and ergonomics differ. KMP's bottom scrubber instead has previous-PAGE/next-PAGE step buttons, which native does not have at all.
- **Suggested fix:** If matching native layout, move chapter Prev/Next into the bottom control row as rounded cards flanking the page slider; otherwise document the top-bar relocation as an intentional UX change.

**🟡 [Medium] Page seekbar / scrubber layout — Native page slider sits inside a rounded translucent Card with start/end page-number labels; KMP slider is a bare Slider with step buttons and no inline numeric labels** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — SeekBarContainer.kt:66-106: Slider inside a RoundedCornerShape(50) Card (background alpha 0.8f), with Text(progress+1) on the left (weight 1f) and Text(total) on the right (weight 1f), Slider weight 9f, bodySmall labels in onBackground.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:963-994 ReaderPageScrubber is a plain Row: NavigateBefore button + Slider(weight 1f) + NavigateNext button, no surrounding Card, no inline current/total numeric labels. The numeric readout instead lives in a separate HUD pill above and in the top bar.
- **Explanation:** Native's seekbar shows the current page number and total page count as text on either side of the slider, all wrapped in a rounded 80%-alpha card for legibility over the image. KMP drops the inline labels (relying on the separate HUD pill / top-bar label) and the rounded card container, and adds discrete page-step buttons native lacks. The visual container and inline numbering are a noticeable divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Wrap the scrubber Slider in a rounded translucent Surface/Card and add current/total page Text labels flanking it (bodySmall) to match SeekBarContainer; or keep the HUD-pill approach and document it.

**🟡 [Medium] Bottom action bar (settings/bookmark/share) — Native has a dedicated bottom BottomActionBar Row with Settings/Bookmark/Share spread by weight; KMP folds these into the top bar** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — ControlOverlay.kt:158-196 BottomActionBar: a 56.dp-tall Row (background alpha 0.8f, horizontal padding 16.dp) with three weight(1f) IconButtons: settings (opens reading-mode dialog), bookmark (Filled.Bookmark/Outlined.BookmarkBorder), share.
- **KMP:** No — there is no bottom action bar. Bookmark (ReaderScreen.kt:738-742), Share (749-756) and the reading-mode dialog trigger (760-764) are all in the TopAppBar actions. The bottom of the screen has only the HUD pill + page scrubber.
- **Explanation:** Native splits chrome into two horizontal bars at the bottom (seekbar row + action row); the action row holds the three primary actions evenly distributed with weight(1f). KMP eliminates this entire bottom bar and moves its actions to the top. Bookmark filled/outline state parity is preserved, but the spatial layout (bottom, evenly-weighted, 56.dp tall, translucent) is gone.
- **Suggested fix:** Either reintroduce a bottom action bar with weighted Settings/Bookmark/Share IconButtons matching ControlOverlay.BottomActionBar, or document the consolidation into the top bar as an intentional redesign.

**🟡 [Medium] Reading-mode chips icons — Native chips show a per-mode icon (ltr/rtl/vertical/webtoon drawables) beside the label; KMP chips show only a leading Check on the selected mode and no per-mode icon** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReadingModeChips.kt:67-81 each FilterChip label is a Row of Icon(painterResource(mode.iconRes), size 20.dp, tinted) + 8.dp Spacer + Text(mode.titleRes). Icons come from ReadingMode.kt (ic_reader_ltr, ic_reader_rtl_24dp, ic_reader_vertical_24dp, ic_reader_webtoon_24dp, ic_reader_continuous_vertical_24dp).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:826-843 FilterChip has label = Text(readingModeLabel(mode)) only; leadingIcon is a Check glyph ONLY when selected (831-840). No mode-distinguishing icon is ever shown.
- **Explanation:** Native distinguishes each reading-mode option with its own glyph (a left-to-right arrow, a right-to-left arrow, a vertical arrow, a webtoon strip icon, etc.) so users recognize modes visually. KMP shows only text plus a generic check on the selected chip, losing the per-mode iconography entirely.
- **Suggested fix:** Add per-mode leadingIcon vectors to the KMP reading-mode FilterChips (map each ReadingMode to its icon), matching native ReadingModeChips; keep the selected-state styling.

**🟡 [Medium] Next-chapter transition card — Native NextChapterCard is a full-screen centered overlay; KMP NextChapterOverlay is a small bottom banner Surface** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — NextChapterCard.kt:31-78: Box.fillMaxSize().heightIn(screenHig).background(surface @0.95f).clickable; centered Column with 'You are in' (bodyMedium onSurface), chapter number (titleLarge primary), 'Going to' (bodyMedium onSurface), next number (titleLarge secondary). Shown as a full reader-area page when swiping past last page.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:1526-1588 NextChapterOverlay is a bottom-aligned fillMaxWidth Surface (padding spacing.md, RoundedCornerShape, surface @0.95f, tonalElevation 6.dp) with labelMedium/titleMedium text; current in onSurface, next in primary. Pinned to BottomCenter, layered over the last page rather than replacing it.
- **Explanation:** Native presents the chapter transition as a full-screen card that you tap to advance (occupying the whole reader area, centered, chapter numbers in titleLarge with primary/secondary color split). KMP shows a compact bottom banner overlaid on the last page (titleMedium, primary for next, no secondary color). Both convey the same info and tap-to-advance, but the size, position, typography scale, and color roles differ substantially.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide on parity: either render the next-chapter affordance as a full-screen centered card (titleLarge, primary current / secondary next) as native does, or keep the bottom-banner redesign and document it. At minimum align the next-chapter color to native's secondary token if matching.

**⚪ [Low] Reading-mode dialog selected-chip styling — Native selected chip uses primary container + onPrimary label and a custom 18.dp shape with explicit border colors; KMP uses default M3 FilterChip selection styling** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReadingModeChips.kt:55-99 FilterChipDefaults.filterChipColors with selectedContainerColor=primary, selectedLabelColor=onPrimary, containerColor=inverseOnSurface.copy(0.3f); RoundedCornerShape(18.dp); explicit filterChipBorder with primary/onSurface 0.12 alpha; fixed height 40.dp; padding(horizontal=12, vertical=6).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:827-842 default FilterChip (no custom colors, no custom shape, no fixed 40.dp height, no explicit border, fillMaxWidth only). Selection conveyed by the M3 default selected container + the leading Check icon.
- **Explanation:** The chip color tokens, corner radius (18.dp vs M3 default 8.dp), fixed 40.dp height, 12/6 dp padding, and custom border colors are all bespoke in native. KMP relies on stock FilterChip styling, so selected/unselected colors and chip geometry differ visibly.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply FilterChipColors (selectedContainerColor=primary, selectedLabelColor=onPrimary, containerColor=inverseOnSurface@0.3), RoundedCornerShape(18.dp), fixed height 40.dp, and the matching border to the KMP chips.

**⚪ [Low] Reading-mode dialog header — Native dialog header is 'Reading mode' in headlineSmall + FontWeight.Bold with 24/16 dp padding; KMP uses titleLarge with default weight and lg padding** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReadingModeDialog.kt:67-74 Text('Reading mode', fontWeight=Bold, style=headlineSmall, color=onSurface, padding horizontal=24.dp vertical=16.dp). Surface color = surfaceContainerHigh, tonalElevation 8.dp, RoundedCornerShape(16.dp), fillMaxWidth(1f).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:816-819 Text(np_reader_mode_dialog_title, style=titleLarge) with no bold; Surface color=surface (not surfaceContainerHigh), RoundedCornerShape(spacing.lg), tonalElevation 8.dp, content padded by spacing.lg.
- **Explanation:** Header typography (headlineSmall+Bold vs titleLarge regular), surface tonal color (surfaceContainerHigh vs surface), corner radius (literal 16.dp vs spacing.lg token), and explicit 24/16 padding all differ. Minor but visible cosmetic divergence in the settings sheet.
- **Suggested fix:** Set the KMP dialog header to headlineSmall + Bold with 24/16 dp padding, switch the Surface to surfaceContainerHigh, and pin the corner radius to 16.dp to match the native dialog.

**⚪ [Low] Reading-mode dialog Apply/Revert buttons — Native Apply button uses onBackground container with a Check icon + bold label; Revert is an OutlinedButton with a 1.dp onBackground border + bold; KMP uses default M3 Button/OutlinedButton styling** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReadingModeDialog.kt:104-147: Revert OutlinedButton (RoundedCornerShape(8.dp), border 1.dp onBackground, bold onBackground label) + 12.dp Spacer + Apply Button (containerColor=onBackground, Check icon size 18.dp tinted background, bold background-colored label).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:849-858: OutlinedButton(onClick=onDismiss){Text(revert)} and Button(onClick){Icon(Check)+Text(apply)} both with default M3 colors/shapes; no bold, no 8.dp corner override, no onBackground container override.
- **Explanation:** Native deliberately inverts the Apply button to onBackground container with background-colored content for high contrast, bolds both labels, and uses 8.dp corners and a 1.dp border on Revert. KMP uses default primary-filled Button + default OutlinedButton. The Apply button color and label weight differ noticeably.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native: Revert OutlinedButton with 1.dp onBackground border + bold label, Apply Button with onBackground container and background-colored Check icon + bold label, both RoundedCornerShape(8.dp).

**⚪ [Low] Reading-mode option labels (localization) — Reading-mode label strings differ in wording/casing between native and KMP** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — strings.xml:214-218: reading_mode_right_to_left='Right-to-Left', reading_mode_left_to_right='Left-to-Right', reading_mode_continuous_vertical='Continuous Vertical' (hyphenated, title-cased).
- **KMP:** Partial — ui strings.xml:161-165: reading_mode_rtl='Right to left', reading_mode_ltr='Left to right', reading_mode_continuous='Continuous vertical' (unhyphenated, sentence-cased). reading_mode_default/vertical/webtoon match.
- **Explanation:** The KMP reader uses different string keys (reading_mode_rtl/ltr/continuous) with different values: native is 'Right-to-Left'/'Left-to-Right'/'Continuous Vertical' (hyphen + title case), KMP is 'Right to left'/'Left to right'/'Continuous vertical' (spaces + sentence case). User-visible label text differs for three of six modes.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the KMP reading_mode_rtl/ltr/continuous string values to native's exact wording ('Right-to-Left', 'Left-to-Right', 'Continuous Vertical') or vice versa for cross-app consistency.

**⚪ [Low] Reading-mode dialog Apply/Revert string keys — Native uses but_apply/but_revert string keys; KMP uses np_reader_mode_apply/np_reader_mode_revert (same English text 'Apply'/'Revert')** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReadingModeDialog.kt:117 stringResource(R.string.but_revert), :143 R.string.but_apply; strings.xml:219-220 'Revert'/'Apply'.
- **KMP:** Yes — ReaderScreen.kt:850 np_reader_mode_revert, :857 np_reader_mode_apply; strings_np_details_reader.xml:35-36 'Apply'/'Revert'. Values match in English.
- **Explanation:** Functionally identical English labels but sourced from divergent string keys. This is a maintenance/translation-parity concern (the Arabic translations live under different keys, risking drift) rather than a visible bug today.
- **Suggested fix:** Reuse a single shared key set for Apply/Revert across the app, or ensure the Arabic (and other locale) translations of np_reader_mode_apply/revert exactly match the legacy but_apply/but_revert values.

**⚪ [Low] Page-count / chapter-count labels in top bar — KMP adds 'N / M' chapter label and 'X / Y' page label in the top bar that native does not have** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** No — ControlOverlay top bar shows only title + chapter-number subtitle; there is no 'chapter N of M' or 'page X of Y' numeric label in the bar. Page numbers appear only inside the bottom SeekBarContainer.
- **KMP:** Yes — ReaderScreen.kt:702-707 Text('${currentChapterIndex+1} / $chaptersCount', labelMedium) between the chevrons, and :727-732 Text('${currentPageIndex+1} / $pagesCount', labelMedium) after them.
- **Explanation:** KMP introduces two new numeric labels in the top bar (chapter position and page position). These are additions beyond the native source of truth. Not a regression in capability, but it is a divergence from native's chrome and can crowd the action row on narrow screens (back + prev + label + next + label + bookmark + share + overflow is many slots).
- **Suggested fix:** If strict native parity is the goal, remove the top-bar numeric labels (native shows page count only in the bottom seekbar); otherwise keep but verify the action row does not overflow on small screens / RTL.

**⚪ [Low] Page-indicator HUD pill — KMP renders a bottom-center rounded HUD pill ('3 / 27'); native has no such pill** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** No — native shows the current/total page only as the two Text labels inside SeekBarContainer's slider card; there is no separate floating HUD pill above the seekbar.

**⚪ [Low] Per-page image error pane (Open in WebView) — Both show Retry + Open-in-WebView, but native uses BorderedPrimaryButton with custom geometry; KMP uses default M3 Buttons** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — ImageLoadError (referenced in legacy) / ReaderScreen.kt:730-765 BorderedPrimaryButton: height 38.dp, contentPadding vertical 8 / horizontal 28, RoundedCornerShape(16.dp), primary background, onPrimary content, elevation 4.dp.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:1492-1502 two default M3 Buttons in a Row (Retry via painter.restart(), Open-in-browser via onOpenInWebView). No 16.dp corner / 38.dp height / 28.dp horizontal padding / elevation overrides.
- **Explanation:** Functional parity is achieved (retry + open-in-webview side by side), and KMP even routes Open-in-WebView through a proper MVI effect plus auto-403 Cloudflare recovery. But the button geometry/typography (native's BorderedPrimaryButton: fixed 38.dp height, 16.dp corners, 28.dp horizontal padding, 4.dp elevation) is not reproduced; KMP uses stock Buttons.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply the BorderedPrimaryButton geometry (height 38.dp, RoundedCornerShape 16.dp, contentPadding 8/28, elevation 4.dp) to the KMP error-pane buttons if pixel parity is required.

**⚪ [Low] Overflow / dots menu — Native top-bar dots button is a dead no-op; KMP overflow button opens the reading-mode dialog** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes (dead) — ControlOverlay.kt:64 onMenu = { /* ... */ } and :148-154 the dots IconButton calls onMenu, which does nothing. The settings action is instead the separate bottom-bar gear (ic_reader_setting) which opens ReadingModeDialog.
- **KMP:** Yes (functional) — ReaderScreen.kt:760-764 the Overflow (MoreVert) button sets menuExpanded=true, opening the ReadingModeDialog (767-776).
- **Explanation:** In native the three-dots button does nothing (placeholder), while the reading-mode dialog is opened from the bottom-bar settings gear. KMP collapses these: there is no bottom gear; the overflow icon itself opens the reading-mode dialog. So the entry point to reader settings moved from a dedicated gear in the bottom bar to the overflow icon in the top bar. KMP arguably improves on native (no dead button), but the affordance location/icon diverges from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** If matching native UX, provide a dedicated settings (gear) entry point rather than overloading the overflow icon; or document that the dead native dots button was intentionally repurposed.

**⚪ [Low] Chrome show/hide animation timing — Native uses explicit tween(250) enter / tween(200) exit for the chrome slide+fade; KMP uses default AnimatedVisibility timing** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — ControlOverlay.kt:57-58 enter=fadeIn(tween(250))+slideInVertically(tween(250)){-it}, exit=fadeOut(tween(200))+slideOutVertically(tween(200)){it} for both top and bottom bars.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:466-467 (top) and 610-611 (bottom) enter=fadeIn()+slideInVertically{ -it/it }, exit=fadeOut()+slideOutVertically{...} with NO explicit duration (uses Compose default ~ spec).
- **Explanation:** Native specifies a 250ms enter / 200ms exit tween for the chrome transition; KMP omits the tween spec and inherits the AnimatedVisibility defaults (different easing/duration). The chrome appears/disappears at a slightly different speed and easing than native.
- **Suggested fix:** Pass enter = fadeIn(tween(250)) + slideInVertically(tween(250)) and exit = fadeOut(tween(200)) + slideOutVertically(tween(200)) to the KMP AnimatedVisibility wrappers to match native timing.

**⚪ [Low] First-chapter loading indicator — Native overlays a centered primary-colored CircularProgressIndicator only for the first chapter load; KMP shows a centered default indicator whenever initial-loading with no pages** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderScreen.kt:623-632: if (isFirstChapterLoading) a full-screen Box(padding 16.dp, center) with CircularProgressIndicator(color=primary). Gated specifically on currentChapterIndex == startIndex (only the very first chapter).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:522-525 when state.isInitialLoading -> CircularProgressIndicator aligned Center (default color, no 16.dp box padding). isInitialLoading = isLoading && pages.isEmpty() (ReaderState.kt:240), i.e. any first-fetch with no prior pages.
- **Explanation:** Both show a centered spinner during the initial load. Differences: native tints it with colorScheme.primary and wraps in a 16.dp-padded full-screen Box gated to the start chapter; KMP uses the default indeterminate color and the generic isInitialLoading flag. Minor cosmetic (tint) divergence plus subtly different gating semantics.
- **Suggested fix:** Tint the KMP initial-loading CircularProgressIndicator with colorScheme.primary to match native; gating semantics are acceptably equivalent.

### Reader — Gestures & Zoom  `reader-gestures-zoom`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 10 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡3 ⚪4)

> Both apps use the same gesture library (net.engawapg.lib:zoomable 2.8.0) and both leave the Compose pagers/lists on default page-transition behavior (no custom fling, page spacing, or per-page animations). Pinch-zoom + pan + double-tap-to-2.5x + one-finger-zoom are therefore behaviorally preserved in KMP because both sides rely on the engawapg defaults. The headline divergences are: (1) native applies the scroll-aware zoomableWithScroll(enableNestedScroll=true) to its LazyColumn modes while KMP applies plain zoomable(enableNestedScroll=false), changing how pinch-pan coordinates with list scrolling in webtoon/continuous modes; (2) tap-to-toggle-chrome is wired three times in native (outer clickable + per-mode onTap + telephoto onClick) vs a single outer detectTapGestures in KMP — and KMP's inner zoomable receives no onTap so taps rely entirely on the outer detector; (3) edge-of-chapter behavior diverges sharply — native silently AUTO-advances to the next chapter when the user swipes to the last page (paged modes) or scrolls to the list end (webtoon/continuous), whereas KMP performs no auto-advance and instead surfaces a tappable NextChapterOverlay; (4) native's CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL uses ContentScale.Fit while KMP renders it FillWidth like webtoon; (5) the native per-image telephoto ZoomableImage is orphaned (declared, not invoked) and KMP omits telephoto entirely. KMP also adds gestures/affordances native lacks (a page scrubber Slider, prev/next-page step buttons, auto-hide chrome after 3s — which native also has). Overall the core gesture set is close, but scroll-coordination and auto-advance behavior differ enough to be user-noticeable.
