<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Reader — Gestures & Zoom</summary>

**🟠 [High] Reader pinch-zoom in webtoon / continuous-vertical (LazyColumn) modes — Native uses scroll-aware zoomableWithScroll (enableNestedScroll=true); KMP uses plain zoomable (enableNestedScroll=false)** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebToonReadingMode.kt:134 and ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:125 apply Modifier.zoomableWithScroll(rememberZoomState(), onTap={...}) to the LazyColumn. zoomableWithScroll sets enableNestedScroll=true (engawapg Zoomable.kt:160), designed for lazy lists so pinch-pan coordinates with list scrolling and propagates at the content edge.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderVerticalListBody (ReaderScreen.kt:1174) applies Modifier.zoomable(rememberZoomState()) to the LazyColumn. zoomable sets enableNestedScroll=false (engawapg Zoomable.kt:81), the variant intended for non-scrollable content.
- **Explanation:** The engawapg library exposes two distinct modifiers: zoomable (enableNestedScroll=false) for fixed content, and zoomableWithScroll (enableNestedScroll=true) explicitly 'designed to be applied to lazy composable functions such as LazyColumn'. Native deliberately chose zoomableWithScroll for its two LazyColumn-backed modes so that when the user is zoomed in and pans past the content edge, the pan hands off to the list's own vertical scroll (nested-scroll integration). KMP applies the non-scroll zoomable to the LazyColumn, so once zoomed-in the pan is captured by the zoom layer without nested-scroll coordination with the LazyColumn, producing different pan/scroll hand-off behavior at edges and while zoomed. The KDoc at ReaderScreen.kt:1168-1173 even claims it mirrors legacy WebToonReadingMode.kt but uses the wrong overload (zoomable vs zoomableWithScroll).
- **Suggested fix:** For the WEBTOON / CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL LazyColumn (ReaderVerticalListBody), switch Modifier.zoomable(...) to Modifier.zoomableWithScroll(rememberZoomState(), ...) (it is @ExperimentalZoomableApi) to restore native's enableNestedScroll=true scroll-coordinated pinch-pan. Keep plain zoomable for the pagers (matching native HorizontalReadingMode/VerticalReadingMode which also use zoomableWithScroll on the Pager but pagers are not nested-scroll lists).
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth) uses zoomableWithScroll on its two LazyColumn modes: native-app/.../reading_modes/WebToonReadingMode.kt:134 `.zoomableWithScroll(rememberZoomState(), onTap = { onTap() })` (import line 62, @OptIn(ExperimentalZoomableApi) line 109); native-app/.../reading_modes/ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:125 `.zoomableWithScroll(rememberZoomState(), onTap = {...})` (import line 51, @OptIn line 96). Both are applied to the fillMaxSize LazyColumn. KMP uses the plain zoomable overload: ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt:1174 `.zoomable(rememberZoomState())` inside ReaderVerticalListBody (declared line 1156), applied to the LazyColumn. Import is `net.engawapg.lib.zoomable.zoomable` (line 82) — there is NO zoomableWithScroll import and no local shadow. The KDoc at ReaderScreen.kt:1168-1173 explicitly says it mirrors legacy WebToonReadingMode.kt line 134, yet uses the non-scroll overload. LIBRARY semantics verified from extracted engawapg sources (net.engawapg.lib:zoomable:2.8.0 — IDENTICAL version in both apps: native-app/app/build.gradle.kts:209 and gradle/libs.versions.toml:60 zoomable=2.8.0). Zoomable.kt:60-82 shows Modifier.zoomable passes enableNestedScroll=false (literal at line 81). Zoomable.kt:138-161 shows Modifier.zoomableWithScroll passes enableNestedScroll=true (literal at line 160); its KDoc (lines 116-118) states it 'can be applied to lazy composable functions such as LazyColumn and LazyRow.' Zoomable.kt:262-282 (ZoomableNode.init) shows enableNestedScroll is the sole differentiator: when true it delegates a nestedScrollModifierNode whose onPostScroll calls zoomState.applyPan(available,...), bridging unconsumed LazyColumn scroll into the zoom pan. Every other node (pointer-input gesture node line 284, measure/scale layer line 393) is identical between the two overloads. So the difference is genuinely functional, not cosmetic: native hands leftover edge scroll into pan; KMP does not.

**🟠 [High] Edge-of-chapter: auto-advance on swipe to last page (paged modes) — Native silently auto-loads the next chapter when the pager reaches the last page; KMP does not auto-advance and only shows a tappable overlay** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderScreen.kt:257-266: LaunchedEffect(pagerState.currentPage){ if(pagerState.currentPage == allReaderItems.lastIndex) readerViewModel.goToNextChapter(...) }. Swiping to the final page triggers automatic next-chapter load with no tap.
- **KMP:** No — ReaderViewModel.onPageChanged (ReaderViewModel.kt:448-477) on reaching pages.lastIndex only marks the chapter read (markChapterRead); it never calls onNextChapter. Advancing requires an explicit OnNextChapter intent (NextChapterOverlay tap at ReaderScreen.kt:588-594 or the top-bar Next button).
- **Explanation:** This is a core reading-flow divergence. In native, simply swiping to the end of a chapter seamlessly continues into the next chapter (infinite-scroll-style paged reading). In KMP the reader stops at the last page and the user must tap the NextChapterOverlay banner or the top-bar Next chevron. The KMP NextChapterOverlay KDoc (ReaderScreen.kt:573-579) even claims 'the reader auto-advances on the last page already (the VM's existing behaviour)', but no such auto-advance exists in onPageChanged — the claim is stale and the behavior is missing. Users migrating will perceive the reader as 'stuck' at chapter ends.
- **Suggested fix:** In ReaderViewModel.onPageChanged, when clamped == pages.lastIndex AND state.canGoNext, dispatch the same next-chapter load native performs (call onNextChapter() or equivalent), matching ReaderScreen.kt:257-266. Alternatively gate it behind a setting, but default should match native's silent auto-advance. Update/remove the inaccurate KDoc claiming auto-advance already exists.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — silent auto-advance EXISTS. native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/reader/ui/screens/ReaderScreen.kt:256-266: `LaunchedEffect(pagerState.currentPage) { if (pagerState.currentPage == allReaderItems.lastIndex) { readerViewModel.goToNextChapter(chaptersList, mangaApi, screenWidthPx, context) } }`. The target it calls genuinely loads the next chapter: native ReaderViewModel.kt:473-489 `goToNextChapter` guards `if (curr >= chaptersList.lastIndex) return` then `loadChapter(nextIdx, ...)` and sets `_currentChapterIndex.value = nextIdx` — so swiping to the absolute last page seamlessly continues into the next chapter with no tap. KMP — auto-advance is ABSENT. presentation/.../reader/ReaderViewModel.kt:448-477 `onPageChanged`: at line 474 `if (clamped == current.pages.lastIndex)` it only fires `viewModelScope.launch { markChapterRead(chapterUrl) }` (line 475); it never calls onNextChapter. ReaderViewModel.kt:305-313 shows `onNextChapter()` is dispatched ONLY by `ReaderIntent.OnNextChapter` (line 313), an explicit intent. The pager layouts ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt:1241-1245 (horizontal) and 1310-1313 (vertical) collect `snapshotFlow { pagerState.currentPage }.distinctUntilChanged().collect(onPageChanged)` only — no LaunchedEffect anywhere auto-advances at lastIndex. Reaching the last page (ui ReaderScreen.kt:585 `val onLastPage = state.hasPages && state.currentPageIndex >= state.pages.lastIndex`) only renders the tappable NextChapterOverlay (586-595) whose onGoToNext dispatches OnNextChapter (592); the top-bar Next button (484) is the only other path. STALE KDoc confirmed as flagged: ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt:1522-1524 NextChapterOverlay KDoc states 'the reader auto-advances on the last page already (the VM's existing behaviour)', and ReaderScreen.kt:578-579 says it 'supplements the existing top-bar Next button + silent auto-advance' — both reference an auto-advance that does not exist in onPageChanged. The claim is correct; its line citations are off by a few (overlay block is 585-595 not 588-594; the stale KDoc sentence is at 1522-1524 and 578-579 not 573-579) but every substantive assertion is accurate.

**🟠 [High] Edge-of-chapter: auto-load on scroll-to-end (webtoon / continuous-vertical) — Native auto-loads the next chapter when the LazyColumn scrolls to its end; KMP has no scroll-end auto-load** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebToonReadingMode.kt:96-106 and ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:83-93: snapshotFlow{ listState.isScrolledToTheEnd() }.collect{ if(reachedEnd && !alreadyLoading) onLoadNextChapter() }. Reaching the bottom of the stitched list automatically fetches the next chapter (debounced via alreadyLoading).
- **KMP:** No — ReaderVerticalList / ReaderVerticalListBody (ReaderScreen.kt:1107-1205) install only snapshotFlow{ listState.firstVisibleItemIndex } for OnPageChanged. A grep for isScrolledToTheEnd / reachedEnd / layoutInfo / onLoadNext across the KMP reader returns nothing.
- **Explanation:** In native webtoon/continuous modes the next chapter is fetched automatically when the user scrolls to the end, giving continuous reading. KMP's vertical-list modes never observe scroll-to-end, so scrolling to the bottom does nothing beyond showing the tappable NextChapterOverlay banner; the next chapter never loads on its own. This is the LazyColumn-mode counterpart of the paged-mode auto-advance gap above and is equally user-visible (continuous reading flow is broken at chapter boundaries).
- **Suggested fix:** Add a snapshotFlow over listState.layoutInfo (lastVisibleItemIndex >= total-1, or a reusable isScrolledToTheEnd) in ReaderVerticalList that dispatches OnNextChapter once per end-reach (with an alreadyLoading debounce mirroring native), so scrolling to the end auto-loads the next chapter.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — auto-loads next chapter on scroll-to-end, exactly as claimed: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/reader/ui/reading_modes/WebToonReadingMode.kt:95-106 — `var alreadyLoading...; LaunchedEffect(listState){ snapshotFlow{ listState.isScrolledToTheEnd() }.collect{ reachedEnd -> if(reachedEnd && !alreadyLoading){ alreadyLoading=true; onLoadNextChapter() } else if(!reachedEnd && alreadyLoading){ alreadyLoading=false } } }`. - .../reading_modes/ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:82-93 — identical pattern calling loadingNextChapter(). - Helper .../presentation/common/componants/isScrolledToTheEnd.kt:6-10 returns true when last visible item index == totalItemsCount-1 (true bottom-of-list). Native NextChapterCard onGoToNext is a no-op in ContinuousVertical (line 161-163: "Parent's effect watching scroll-end will load next chapter"), confirming the scroll-end effect is the load trigger. KMP — no scroll-end auto-load, confirmed: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt: ReaderVerticalList (L1107-1153) installs ONLY `snapshotFlow{ listState.firstVisibleItemIndex }.distinctUntilChanged().collect(onPageChanged)` (L1127-1131) + a scrubber scrollToItem effect (L1139-1144). ReaderVerticalListBody (L1155-1205) just renders ReaderPageItem in a LazyColumn. No isScrolledToTheEnd / layoutInfo.visibleItemsInfo / onLoadNext anywhere in the vertical-list path. - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderViewModel.kt onPageChanged (L448-477): reaching pages.lastIndex (L474) fires ONLY markChapterRead — it does NOT load/advance the next chapter. - onNextChapter() (L422-438) is reachable ONLY via ReaderIntent.OnNextChapter (handle() L313), dispatched only by explicit user taps: top-bar Next button (ReaderScreen.kt:484, 711) and NextChapterOverlay banner tap (ReaderScreen.kt:592). The overlay (L1528-1545) is a tappable banner, not an auto-loader. - The in-tree KDoc at ReaderScreen.kt:1523 ("the reader auto-advances on the last page already") is contradicted by the actual VM code; the composeApp copy of isScrolledToTheEnd.kt is referenced only in KDoc, not wired into any active reader. Net: scrolling to the bottom of the KMP webtoon/continuous-vertical LazyColumn shows only the tappable NextChapterOverlay; the next chapter never loads on its own — matching the claim.

**🟡 [Medium] Reader pinch-zoom in paged modes (LTR / RTL horizontal, vertical paged) — Native applies zoomableWithScroll to the HorizontalPager/VerticalPager; KMP applies plain zoomable** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — HorizontalReadingMode.kt:47 and VerticalReadingMode.kt:39 wrap the Pager in Modifier.zoomableWithScroll(rememberZoomState(), onTap={onTap()}).fillMaxSize().
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderHorizontalPager (ReaderScreen.kt:1262-1264) and ReaderVerticalPager (ReaderScreen.kt:1327-1329) use Modifier.zoomable(rememberZoomState()).fillMaxSize(), with no onTap and the non-scroll overload.
- **Explanation:** Native uses the enableNestedScroll=true overload even on the pagers, so zoom-pan past the page edge can coordinate with the pager's own swipe. KMP uses enableNestedScroll=false. For pagers the practical difference is smaller than for the LazyColumn (each page fills the viewport), but it still changes how a pan gesture at the edge of a zoomed page interacts with page-turn swipes, and it diverges from the source of truth's exact modifier choice.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native by using zoomableWithScroll on the pagers too, or document/justify the intentional switch to zoomable. At minimum keep the choice consistent with the LazyColumn fix above.

**🟡 [Medium] Tap-to-toggle reader chrome (single tap anywhere) — Native toggles controls via three redundant tap paths; KMP relies on a single outer detectTapGestures and passes no onTap into the zoomable layer** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — (a) outer Box .clickable{ showControls = !showControls } (ReaderScreen.kt:364-367); (b) each reading mode passes onTap into zoomableWithScroll(..., onTap={ showControls=!showControls }) (e.g. HorizontalReadingMode.kt:48, VerticalReadingMode.kt:41); (c) the orphaned telephoto ZoomableImage onClick (ZoomableImage.kt:68).
- **KMP:** Partial — single BoxWithConstraints.pointerInput { detectTapGestures(onTap = { onIntent(ReaderIntent.OnUiToggle) }) } at ReaderScreen.kt:514-516. The inner zoomable() is called with NO onTap (ReaderScreen.kt:1174, 1263, 1328).
- **Explanation:** Native wires the tap both at the outer Box and inside the gesture modifier, so a tap is caught regardless of whether the zoomable layer consumed the pointer. KMP relies solely on the outer detectTapGestures while the inner zoomable consumes pointer events for its own gesture detector. The engawapg zoomable installs a pointerInput gesture detector; depending on event consumption a clean single tap that the zoomable's own tap detector handles (it has an onTap param defaulting to null) may not propagate to the outer Box detector. This creates a risk that some single taps over a loaded page fail to toggle chrome — a behavior native guards against by ALSO passing onTap into the gesture modifier. The KDoc (ReaderScreen.kt:509-513) assumes taps coexist, but the safer parity move is to also feed onTap into zoomable.
- **Suggested fix:** Pass onTap = { onIntent(ReaderIntent.OnUiToggle) } into each zoomable/zoomableWithScroll call (as native does) so chrome-toggle is captured at the gesture layer as well as the outer Box, eliminating any dependence on tap-event propagation through the gesture detector.

**🟡 [Medium] CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL image scaling — Native CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL renders page images with ContentScale.Fit (default); KMP renders the merged vertical-list mode with ContentScale.FillWidth** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:262-273 draws the Image with no contentScale argument (Compose default = ContentScale.Fit) and .fillMaxWidth().wrapContentHeight(). WebToon by contrast uses ContentScale.FillWidth (WebToonReadingMode.kt:204,256).
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderVerticalList feeds ReaderPageItem with its default contentScale = ContentScale.FillWidth (ReaderScreen.kt:1355); both WEBTOON and CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL collapse into this single layout, so CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL uses FillWidth.
- **Explanation:** Native distinguishes the two LazyColumn modes' image fit: WebToon = FillWidth (strip fills width, height follows), Continuous-Vertical = Fit (image fits within its slot, may not fill width). KMP merged the two modes into one ReaderVerticalList with FillWidth for both, so CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL images that are wider than tall (or that native would letterbox) now stretch to full width. For typical portrait manga pages the visual result is similar, but for non-portrait pages the rendering diverges from native.
- **Suggested fix:** Either split the vertical-list path so CONTINUOUS_VERTICAL passes contentScale = ContentScale.Fit (matching native's default) while WEBTOON keeps FillWidth, or parameterize ReaderVerticalList with the contentScale derived from readingMode.

**⚪ [Low] Per-image telephoto zoom component — Native declares a telephoto-based ZoomableImage (per-image pinch-zoom with onClick) but it is orphaned; KMP omits telephoto entirely** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Partial — ZoomableImage.kt:62-71 wraps me.saket.telephoto.zoomable.coil3.ZoomableAsyncImage with onClick→onTap; build.gradle.kts:208 depends on telephoto. However a grep shows ZoomableImage() is only referenced in a comment (ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:120) and never actually invoked, so it is dead code in native.
- **KMP:** No — telephoto is declared in libs.versions.toml:61,192 but not referenced anywhere in :ui or :presentation; KMP uses only engawapg zoomable at the pager/list level.
- **Explanation:** Native ships telephoto and a ZoomableImage composable but never wires it into the live reader (the actual zoom comes from engawapg zoomableWithScroll at the container level). KMP correctly does not port this dead component. This is effectively parity-neutral (no live native behavior is lost), but worth recording: anyone comparing the dependency lists or expecting per-image telephoto zoom will find it absent, and the KMP libs.versions.toml carries an unused telephoto alias.
- **Suggested fix:** No functional change needed for parity. Optionally remove the unused telephoto alias from KMP libs.versions.toml to avoid implying a feature that isn't wired, and confirm with the team that native's ZoomableImage is intentionally dead before relying on container-level zoom only.

**⚪ [Low] Page navigation scrubber / step buttons — KMP adds a bottom Slider scrubber + prev/next-page step buttons; native uses a SeekBarContainer in its ControlOverlay** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Partial — native page jump is handled inside ControlOverlay via onPageChange + SeekBarContainer (referenced from ReaderScreen.kt:536-546); jumping uses pagerState.scrollToPage / scrollTarget for lists.
- **KMP:** Yes — ReaderPageScrubber (ReaderScreen.kt:949-995) is a Material3 Slider flanked by NavigateBefore/NavigateNext step buttons, each dispatching OnPageChanged; layouts close the loop via LaunchedEffect(currentPageIndex){ scrollToItem/scrollToPage }.
- **Explanation:** Both apps provide a page-seek affordance, but the visual component differs: native uses a custom 3-card SeekBarContainer inside its ControlOverlay (and the KDoc at ReaderScreen.kt:957-962 notes the legacy SeekBarContainer had a famous left/right label inversion), while KMP uses a standard Slider plus discrete step IconButtons. Functionally comparable (both jump pages via the same index mechanism), but the control's appearance and exact layout are not a 1:1 match. This is an improvement/cosmetic divergence rather than a regression.
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable as a modernized equivalent. If strict visual parity is required, compare against SeekBarContainer.kt layout (3-card row) and align spacing/iconography; otherwise document the intentional Slider-based replacement.

**⚪ [Low] Page transitions / pager animation configuration — No divergence — both rely on default Compose pager snap/fling with no custom transitions** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — native HorizontalPager/VerticalPager are created with only state + reverseLayout; no pageSpacing, beyondBoundsPageCount, flingBehavior, snapPosition, or graphicsLayer page-offset animation (grep returns none).
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP ReaderHorizontalPager/ReaderVerticalPager likewise set only state, reverseLayout, modifier, key; no custom transition params (grep returns none).
- **Explanation:** Both implementations use the stock Compose pager behavior for page transitions (default snap-and-fling, no parallax/scale/alpha page animations, no inter-page spacing). There is genuine parity here; recorded explicitly because the audit scope calls out 'page transitions/animations' and a reader could otherwise assume a gap exists.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed — parity confirmed.

**⚪ [Low] Double-tap zoom & one-finger (drag) zoom — No divergence — both inherit the engawapg defaults (double-tap toggles 1.0x↔2.5x, one-finger-zoom enabled)** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — native never overrides onDoubleTap or enableOneFingerZoom (grep returns none), so zoomableWithScroll uses the library default onDoubleTap = toggleScale(2.5f, position) and enableOneFingerZoom=true (engawapg Zoomable.kt:142-147).
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP likewise never overrides onDoubleTap or enableOneFingerZoom, so zoomable uses the identical defaults (engawapg Zoomable.kt:63,66-68).
- **Explanation:** Because both sides use engawapg 2.8.0 and neither customizes the double-tap or one-finger-zoom parameters, double-tap-to-2.5x-zoom and double-tap-then-drag one-finger zoom behave identically. Recorded to document that these specific gestures are NOT a regression, despite native using zoomableWithScroll and KMP using zoomable (the two overloads share the same defaults for these params).
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed — parity confirmed for double-tap and one-finger zoom.

</details>

### Downloads & Offline  `downloads-offline`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 16 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡3 ⚪11)

> Both apps implement the same Downloads screen: a 3-tab (Active/Failed/Completed) Scaffold over a queue persisted in the Room `chapter_downloads` table, with per-row cancel/retry/delete, an in-flight progress card, and a WorkManager-backed download engine (DownloadWorkerV2 + ChapterDownloadService) on Android. The KMP migration is a faithful port of the Android engine into `:shared/androidMain` and a clean MVI rework of the UI (`:ui/downloads/DownloadsScreen` + `:presentation/downloads/DownloadsViewModel` + `:domain` use cases + `:data` strangler-fig repos delegating to the legacy `:shared` DownloadRepository). Headline divergences: (1) the native screen uses paged per-tab Room queries (`observeDownloadsByStatePaged`) while KMP loads the entire downloads table into one in-memory list and partitions in the VM — losing paging entirely; (2) the native Active tab queries only RUNNING+QUEUED so COMPRESSING rows are invisible in native, whereas KMP shows COMPRESSING in Active — a real behavior divergence; (3) iOS/Desktop (`CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl`) deliberately skip CBZ archiving and download per-page files, so the CBZ-format download path and `useCbzFormat` setting are Android-only in KMP; (4) numerous small UI deltas (title em-dash vs hyphen, AutoSubtitleText autosizing vs fixed Text, IconButton vs the screen's own KDoc claim of TextButton, non-localized "unknown" fallback, added empty/loading states, progress bar height). The core download/queue/cancel/retry/delete/offline-read flow has parity on Android.

**🟠 [High] Downloads list — paging — Native uses Paging3 per-tab Room queries; KMP loads entire downloads table into one in-memory list** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — DownloadsScreenRoute.kt:23-39 builds three `Flow<PagingData<ChapterDownloadEntity>>` via `getDownloadsByState(...)`; DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:88-110 wraps a `Pager(PagingConfig(pageSize=50, prefetchDistance=15, initialLoadSize=50))` over `dao.observeDownloadsByStatePaged(states)`; the screen uses `collectAsLazyPagingItems()` and renders an append `CircularProgressIndicator` / error row (DownloadsScreen.kt:119,177-202).
- **KMP:** No — ObserveDownloadsUseCase returns `Flow<List<DownloadedChapter>>` (ObserveDownloadsUseCase.kt:96) over `dao.observeAllDownloads()` (ORDER BY id DESC, no LIMIT); DownloadsViewModel.kt:165-181 holds the full list in `DownloadsState.all` and `.filter`s into 3 buckets. No paging, no append spinner.
- **Explanation:** The native DAO explicitly deprecated the non-paged `observeAllDownloads` query with `@Deprecated("Use observeAllDownloadsPaged instead to avoid CursorWindow overflow")`. KMP regresses to exactly the deprecated path: it loads the whole `chapter_downloads` table (every queued, failed AND completed row across the user's entire download history) into memory on every Room re-emit, and re-filters into 3 buckets on every progress tick. For a heavy user with hundreds/thousands of completed chapters this risks SQLite CursorWindow overflow and heavy recomposition/allocation churn during active downloads — the exact failure the native code was redesigned to avoid. The KMP route KDoc (DownloadsScreenRoute.kt:121-125) acknowledges this as a deferred Phase 10.x item.
- **Suggested fix:** Restore per-tab paging in the KMP read path: add a paged DAO query (KMP Room supports `androidx.paging` on Android; or use `paging-compose-common` once available) and have the VM expose three `Flow<PagingData<DownloadedChapter>>` buckets instead of materializing the full list, mirroring native's `observeDownloadsByStatePaged`.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) uses Paging3 per-tab Room queries: native-app/.../navigation/routes/DownloadsScreenRoute.kt:23-39 builds three Flow<PagingData<ChapterDownloadEntity>> via downloadViewModeltestv2.getDownloadsByState(listOf(RUNNING,QUEUED) / FAILED / SUCCESS). native-app/.../download/ui/test2/DownloadViewModelv2.kt:58-59 -> getDownloadsByState(states) = repository.observeDownloadsByStatePaged(states). native-app/.../download/domain/clean/DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:88-110 wraps Pager(PagingConfig(pageSize=50, prefetchDistance=15, initialLoadSize=50, enablePlaceholders=false)) over dao.observeAllDownloadsPaged()/observeDownloadsByStatePaged(states). native-app/.../data/local/dao/ChapterDownloadDao.kt:121-129 declares observeAllDownloadsPaged()/observeDownloadsByStatePaged(states): PagingSource<Int,ChapterDownloadEntity>; the non-paged observeAllDownloads() at :96-98 carries @Deprecated("Use observeAllDownloadsPaged instead to avoid CursorWindow overflow") over SELECT * FROM chapter_downloads ORDER BY id DESC. native-app/.../download/ui/screens/DownloadsScreen.kt:119,135 call collectAsLazyPagingItems(); :177-202 and :233-258 render an append CircularProgressIndicator on LoadState.Loading and an error Text on LoadState.Error. KMP loads the entire table into one in-memory list, no paging: domain/.../usecase/downloads/ObserveDownloadsUseCase.kt:96 operator fun invoke(): Flow<List<DownloadedChapter>> = repository.observeAll(). data/.../repository/DownloadsRepositoryImpl.kt:116-117 observeAll() = legacy.observeAllDownloads().map { it.toDomain() }. shared/.../data/local/dao/ChapterDownloadDao.kt:168-169 @Query("SELECT * FROM chapter_downloads ORDER BY id DESC") fun observeAllDownloads(): Flow<List<ChapterDownloadEntity>> (no LIMIT, no paging); DAO comment lines 162-167 note the @Deprecated annotation was removed in Phase 6 and the two paginated PagingSource methods were dropped because Room LimitOffsetPagingSource is Android-only, deferring Pager{} to Phase 10. presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsViewModel.kt:163-184 init{} subscribes to observeDownloads().onEach, stores the full list in DownloadsState.all and .filter into active/failed/completed buckets on every emission. presentation/.../downloads/DownloadsState.kt:69-72 holds all + 3 bucket plain List<DownloadedChapter>. ui/.../downloads/DownloadsScreen.kt renders state.active/.failed/.completed via LazyColumn + items(items=...) at line 288, with only a single state.isLoading-gated centered CircularProgressIndicator (line 230) and per-bucket empty states; grep for LazyPagingItems/PagingData/loadState/Pager/PagingConfig across data+presentation+domain+ui returned zero download matches, confirming no append spinner/error row. composeApp/.../navigation/routes/DownloadsScreenRoute.kt:121-125 KDoc ("No paging delta vs the legacy... Phase 10.x lifts both consumers to paging-compose-common") acknowledges the deferral as the claim cites.

**🟠 [High] CBZ archiving on iOS/Desktop — iOS/Desktop download path skips CBZ archive creation entirely; downloads always stored as per-page files** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — ChapterDownloadService.kt reads `dataStoreHelper.useCbzFormatFlow.first()` and, when enabled, calls `optimizedCbzManager.createCbzParallel(...)` to pack pages into a `.cbz` (lines 196-218, 353-369), with OOM fallback to loose files.
- **KMP:** Partial — Android KMP keeps the full CBZ path (shared/androidMain ChapterDownloadService.kt is a 1:1 port). But the iOS/Desktop `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl` explicitly skips CBZ: its KDoc states "Skips CBZ archive creation" and `processJob` writes per-page `image_<i>.<ext>` files only (CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:56-60, 230-262). `useCbzFormat` is never consulted on non-Android.
- **Explanation:** On the source-of-truth (Android) downloads can be stored as space-saving CBZ archives governed by `useCbzFormat`. On the new KMP iOS/Desktop targets that capability is absent — downloads are always loose page files regardless of the user's CBZ preference. This is a platform-specific feature regression: a user toggling CBZ format on iOS/Desktop sees no effect, and storage behavior differs from Android. The KMP code documents this as a deliberate gap (no native ZIP writer on iOS; Desktop CbzWriter re-encodes lossy PNG).
- **Suggested fix:** Either wire the existing platform `CbzWriter` (AndroidCbzWriter/DesktopCbzWriter/IosCbzWriter under :platform/cbz) into `CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl` so the CBZ branch honors `useCbzFormat`, or surface a clear platform-capability note and disable the CBZ toggle on iOS/Desktop. At minimum verify the offline reader handles both archive and loose-file layouts identically across platforms.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). CLAIM IS REAL AND CORRECTLY CHARACTERIZED for the live-download path. NATIVE (source of truth) — /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/download/domain/ChapterDownloadService.kt: - Reads the CBZ preference live during download: `val useCbz = dataStoreHelper.useCbzFormatFlow.first()` at line 156 (streaming path) and line 340 (batch path). - When enabled, packs pages into a .cbz: `optimizedCbzManager.createCbzParallel(paths, chapter.mangaId, chapter.id, ...)` at lines 203 (streaming) and 359 (batch), with OOM fallback to loose files at lines 230-236 / 377-382. KMP ANDROID — /Users/.../shared/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/features/download/domain/ChapterDownloadService.kt: - 1:1 port (class KDoc line 51: "Behaviour is otherwise identical to upstream"). Bound PlatformModule.desktop.kt:114. It is reachable on iOS/Desktop: wired via CompressExistingDownloadsUseCase (composeApp SettingsReworkModule.kt:143), SettingsViewModel.handleCompressExistingDownloads (line 205), and a "Compress Existing" button + AUTO_CONVERT_TO_CBZ toggle in ui/.../SettingsScreen.kt:516-518. **🟡 [Medium] Active tab — COMPRESSING state visibility — COMPRESSING rows appear in KMP's Active tab but are invisible in native (native Active = RUNNING+QUEUED only)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Partial — DownloadsScreenRoute.kt:23-27 queries the Active tab with `listOf(DownloadingState.RUNNING, DownloadingState.QUEUED)` only. COMPRESSING is not in any tab's state filter (Failed=FAILED, Completed=SUCCESS), so a chapter in COMPRESSING state is not shown in any tab while compressing.
- **KMP:** Yes — DownloadsViewModel.kt:166-170 puts `DownloadState.COMPRESSING` into the `active` bucket alongside RUNNING and QUEUED, so a compressing chapter renders in the Active tab as a `DownloadCard` whose status label is "Compressing" (DownloadsScreen.kt:514, statusLabel).
- **Explanation:** This is a genuine behavioral divergence in which rows surface during the brief CBZ-compression phase. Native deliberately omits COMPRESSING from the Active query, so the row momentarily vanishes from all tabs until it transitions to SUCCESS. KMP shows it in Active (arguably better UX), but it does not match the source of truth, and the KMP DownloadCard for a COMPRESSING row also renders a Cancel IconButton (DownloadCardActions.kt:361-376) that native never exposes for a compressing chapter.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide the canonical behavior: to match native, change the KMP `active` filter to RUNNING+QUEUED only and route COMPRESSING into completed (or hide it). If the KMP improvement is intentional, document it and confirm the Cancel action on a COMPRESSING row behaves sanely (queue-prune `onCancel` mid-compression).

**🟡 [Medium] CBZ settings UI (toggle + convert-existing) — Download/CBZ settings section (CBZ toggle, auto-convert, convert-existing button) and the CbzConversionDialog** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Partial — both `DownloadSettingsSection.kt` and the conversion section are fully commented out in native, but `CbzConversionDialog.kt` is live (a complete dialog with converting/success/error/stopped states, progress %, current-chapter info, Stop button) and the engine reads `useCbzFormat`/`autoConvertToCbz` from DataStore. CbzMigrationWorker is also present to repack existing loose downloads into CBZ.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP ports `CbzMigrationWorker` (app/.../work/CbzMigrationWorker.kt) and CbzManager, but I located no KMP equivalent of `CbzConversionDialog` nor a Downloads/CBZ settings section in `:ui`. The migration worker is described as "not auto-scheduled" with no found enqueue trigger.
- **Explanation:** Native ships a live, polished CBZ conversion progress dialog and an on-disk migration worker reachable from a storage-cleanup flow. In KMP the worker class exists but I could not find a UI entry point that enqueues it nor a CbzConversionDialog port, so the user-facing 'convert existing downloads to CBZ' experience appears absent in KMP. Note the native settings section itself was already commented out, so the live surface in native is the dialog + worker, not a settings switch.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm whether a storage-cleanup/settings entry enqueues `CbzMigrationWorker` in KMP; if not, port the conversion entry point and a CbzConversionDialog-equivalent (progress %, current chapter, Stop) so the conversion experience matches native. If intentionally dropped, document the decision.

**🟡 [Medium] FAILED row — error message fallback — Native falls back to localized R.string.unknown ("Unknown"/Arabic); KMP falls back to a hardcoded non-localized lowercase "unknown"** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — DownloadsScreen.kt:322-329: `val msg = item.errorMsg ?: stringResource(R.string.unknown)` then `stringResource(R.string.download_failed, msg)` → "Failed: Unknown" (localized, capitalized).
- **KMP:** Partial — DownloadsScreen.kt:516-519 (statusLabel): `val msg = item.errorMsg?.takeIf { it.isNotBlank() } ?: "unknown"` then `stringResource(Res.string.download_failed_reason, msg)` → "Failed: unknown" with a hardcoded English lowercase literal that is NOT pulled from resources.
- **Explanation:** The KMP fallback string 'unknown' is hardcoded in code, lowercase, and not localized — so in Arabic the failed-reason becomes 'فشل: unknown' instead of native's fully-localized 'فشل: غير معروف' (whatever R.string.unknown maps to). This is a localization regression for the failed-download empty-reason case.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an `unknown` string resource to :ui composeResources (with Arabic) and use `stringResource(Res.string.unknown)` for the fallback, matching native's localized R.string.unknown.

**⚪ [Low] Download row — title text rendering — Native uses AutoSubtitleText (auto-shrinking font) with a hyphen + trailing space; KMP uses a fixed-size Text with an em-dash** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — DownloadsScreen.kt:297-304 renders `AutoSubtitleText(text = "Ch ${item.number} - ${item.mangaTitle} ", fontSize=16.sp, maxSize=16.sp, maxLines=1, fontWeight=Bold)`; the running card uses `minSize=8.sp` (line 423) so the title auto-shrinks to fit. Separator is a hyphen `-` with a hardcoded trailing space.
- **KMP:** Partial — DownloadsScreen.kt:329-335 renders a plain `Text(stringResource(Res.string.download_chapter_title, number, mangaTitle), style=titleMedium, fontWeight=Bold, maxLines=1, overflow=Ellipsis)`. The string is `"Ch %1$s — %2$s"` (em-dash `—`, no trailing space; strings.xml). No auto-shrink — long titles ellipsize instead.
- **Explanation:** Two differences: (1) native auto-sizes the title down to 8.sp to keep it on one line; KMP uses fixed titleMedium and ellipsizes, so long chapter/manga titles truncate where native would shrink-to-fit. (2) The visible separator differs: native shows 'Ch 12 - Title ' (hyphen, trailing space), KMP shows 'Ch 12 — Title' (em-dash). Both are cosmetic but visibly different. Also 'titleMedium' (≈16sp) is theme-token-driven vs native's literal 16.sp.
- **Suggested fix:** Use the same separator (hyphen vs em-dash) as native and, if exact parity is required, replace the KMP Text with an auto-sizing text composable (BasicText with autoSize, or a Yami equivalent) matching native's maxSize 16.sp / minSize 8.sp behavior on the running card.

**⚪ [Low] Download row — action affordances (cancel/delete icons) — Cancel and delete render as IconButtons in KMP; the KMP screen's own KDoc and the route KDoc claim they are TextButtons** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — Active QUEUED/COMPRESSING and Completed/Failed rows: non-running cancel is a TextButton "Cancel" in red (DownloadsScreen.kt:341-343); running progress shows a TextButton showing "${progress}%" (lines 344-348); the running card cancel is `Icons.Default.Cancel` IconButton (lines 428-434); delete is `Icons.Default.Delete` IconButton (366-374); SUCCESS shows an inert `Icons.Outlined.Done` (356-364).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP renders QUEUED/COMPRESSING cancel as `Icons.Filled.Cancel` IconButton (DownloadsScreen.kt:368-374), Retry as TextButton (386-388), Delete as `YamiIcons.Delete` IconButton (389-395), SUCCESS inert `Icons.Outlined.Done` + Delete IconButton (407-418), running cancel as `Icons.Filled.Cancel` IconButton (498-504). The file-level KDoc (lines 110-117) AND DownloadsReworkScreenRoute KDoc (lines 77-82) both assert these are labelled TextButtons — that documentation is stale/wrong vs the code.
- **Explanation:** Functional parity is good (the KMP icons largely match native: Cancel=Icons.Default.Cancel, Delete, Outlined.Done). The notable divergence vs native is on the non-running QUEUED row: native uses a red TextButton labelled "Cancel" (text), KMP uses a red Cancel icon button. Native's RUNNING row shows the percentage as a TextButton; KMP shows the percentage as a plain label next to the title in the running card. These are minor visual deltas, plus a documentation bug where the KDoc contradicts the actual IconButton implementation.
- **Suggested fix:** Pick one affordance style to match native (native non-running cancel = text "Cancel"). Update the stale KDoc in DownloadsScreen.kt (lines 110-117) and DownloadsReworkScreenRoute.kt that incorrectly says actions are TextButtons, to avoid future-audit confusion.

**⚪ [Low] Empty state — KMP renders an illustrated centered YamiEmptyState per empty bucket; native renders nothing (empty LazyColumn)** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — native ActiveDownloadsTabPaged / CompletedDownloadsTabPaged (DownloadsScreen.kt:147-260) render an empty `LazyColumn` when there are no items; there is no empty-state placeholder. The only non-list UI is the paging append spinner/error.
- **KMP:** Yes — DownloadBucketList (DownloadsScreen.kt:280-283) shows `YamiEmptyState(title = emptyLabel)` (centered icon + text) for each empty bucket, with distinct strings: no_active_downloads / no_failed_downloads / no_completed_downloads.
- **Explanation:** KMP adds an empty-state placeholder that native lacks. This is an improvement but a divergence from the source of truth — native shows a blank area. The three empty strings are KMP-new (no native counterparts).
- **Suggested fix:** If strict parity is desired, gate or remove the empty-state to match native's blank list; otherwise document this as an intentional UX enhancement. Ensure the new empty strings are localized (Arabic values were found, so this is fine).

**⚪ [Low] Loading state — KMP shows a full-screen centered spinner while isLoading; native has no initial loading state (only paging append spinner)** _(State)_

- **Native:** Partial — native has no `isLoading` screen state. The only spinner is the Paging append-loading `CircularProgressIndicator` shown at the bottom of the list while a page loads (DownloadsScreen.kt:177-189).
- **KMP:** Yes — DownloadsScreenContent (DownloadsScreen.kt:230-233) renders a full-area `YamiLoadingState()` while `state.isLoading == true` (default true until the first Room emission), then the tabs. There is no append-loading spinner because there's no paging.
- **Explanation:** Because KMP dropped paging, it substitutes a one-shot full-screen spinner covering the gap between subscription and first Room emission, and drops native's per-page append spinner/error row. Different loading affordance, tied to the paging-removal finding. The full-screen spinner also hides the TabRow until first emission, which native never does.
- **Suggested fix:** Tied to restoring paging; if paging is restored, reintroduce the append spinner/error row and avoid hiding the TabRow behind a full-screen spinner. Otherwise keep but verify the spinner doesn't flash on fast Room emits.

**⚪ [Low] Running download card — progress bar height & placement — Progress bar height and the % position differ between native and KMP running cards** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — RunningDownloadItemCard (DownloadsScreen.kt:439-457): a 24.dp Box containing a `LinearProgressIndicator` of `height(8.dp)` aligned CenterStart, with the percentage Text (12.sp, onSurface) overlaid centered ON TOP of the bar. Outer card padding 6.dp/12.dp; inner padding 12.dp.
- **KMP:** Partial — RunningDownloadCard (DownloadsScreen.kt:485-489): `LinearProgressIndicator` of `height(6.dp)` placed BELOW the title row; the percentage Text (labelMedium, onSurfaceVariant) is in the title Row to the right of the title, not overlaid on the bar. Outer padding 6.dp/12.dp matches; inner padding uses `spacing.md` token (≈16.dp) vs native literal 12.dp.
- **Explanation:** Native overlays the % centered on an 8.dp-tall bar inside a 24.dp box; KMP puts a thinner 6.dp bar below the title and moves the % next to the title (labelMedium / onSurfaceVariant tint vs native 12.sp / onSurface). Also inner padding differs (spacing.md token vs literal 12.dp). These are visible layout/typography deltas on the most-watched (in-progress) card.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native: use 8.dp bar height, overlay the percentage centered on the bar inside a 24.dp box, use 12.sp/onSurface for the % text, and align inner padding to 12.dp (or confirm spacing.md == 12.dp).

**⚪ [Low] Running card cancel semantics (Android) — Cancelling one running chapter cancels the entire WorkManager unique work then re-enqueues — a global interruption** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — DownloadRepositoryImpl.cancelARunningChapter (lines 117-122): `workManager.cancelUniqueWork(WORK_NAME)`, delete that chapter's files, mark it failed, then `enqueueRequest()` to resume the rest of the queue.
- **KMP:** Yes — identical on Android (shared/androidMain DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt:92-97). On iOS/Desktop the CoroutineDownloadRepositoryImpl.cancelARunningChapter (lines 156-170) cancels ONLY the active job for that chapterId (finer-grained), deletes files, marks failed, and wakes the queue.
- **Explanation:** Android KMP preserves native's coarse behavior exactly (cancel whole worker + re-enqueue, which momentarily stops any other in-flight chapter). The KMP iOS/Desktop impl is actually finer-grained (per-job cancel) — a behavioral divergence between platforms, but both are reasonable. Worth flagging only because the cross-platform cancel granularity is not identical to the Android source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix required for parity with native on Android. Optionally document that iOS/Desktop cancel is per-job (does not interrupt sibling downloads) so QA expectations are aligned across platforms.

**⚪ [Low] Notification cancel intent delivery (Android) — Native targets the cancel receiver with an explicit Intent(context, DownloadCancelReceiver::class); KMP uses an implicit action Intent with setPackage** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes — DownloadWorkerV2.kt:227-237 builds `Intent(context, DownloadCancelReceiver::class.java).apply { action = ACTION_CANCEL; putExtra(EXTRA_WORK_ID, ...) }` (explicit component) for the notification cancel-all and cancel-chapter actions.
- **KMP:** Partial — shared/androidMain DownloadWorkerV2.kt:316-319, 355-360 builds `Intent(ACTION_CANCEL).apply { setPackage(context.packageName); putExtra(...) }` (implicit action, package-scoped) and relies on the receiver declared in app/AndroidManifest.xml:82-86 (DownloadCancelReceiver with the two action intent-filters).
- **Explanation:** Both reach the same DownloadCancelReceiver, but via different mechanisms — native explicit component reference vs KMP implicit-action + manifest intent-filter + setPackage. Functionally equivalent on modern Android (setPackage makes it explicit-enough), but the implicit-action form is more fragile to manifest mistakes and OS implicit-broadcast restrictions. Verified the KMP manifest declares the receiver, so it should work; flagged as an implementation divergence to validate at runtime.
- **Suggested fix:** Prefer the native explicit-component Intent (`Intent(context, DownloadCancelReceiver::class.java)`) in the KMP worker to remove any dependence on implicit-broadcast routing, matching the source of truth and reducing OEM-specific risk.

**⚪ [Low] Download worker — initial delay — No initial delay in current native/KMP enqueue (both dropped the old 5s delay)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Partial — the live native repo (DownloadRepositoryImpl.enqueueRequest, lines 63-67) enqueues a `OneTimeWorkRequest<DownloadWorkerV2>` with a CONNECTED constraint and NO initial delay. The old commented-out DownloadViewModel.kt:265 had `setInitialDelay(5, SECONDS)` but that ViewModel is dead.
- **KMP:** Yes — shared/androidMain DownloadRepositoryImpl.enqueueRequest (lines 64-71) is identical: CONNECTED constraint, ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP, WORK_NAME="mangaDownloadv2", no initial delay.
- **Explanation:** Parity confirmed — both the live native repo and KMP Android repo enqueue with the same unique-work name, KEEP policy, and CONNECTED network constraint, no delay. The 5s delay only existed in the dead/commented native DownloadViewModel. No regression; documented for completeness.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed — this is parity.

**⚪ [Low] Snackbar error feedback on mutation failure — KMP surfaces mutation failures via a snackbar; native silently swallows them** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — the native DownloadViewModelv2 fires mutations (deleteDownload/cancel/retry) as fire-and-forget `viewModelScope.launch(IO){...}` with no result handling or error UI (DownloadViewModelv2.kt:83-111).
- **KMP:** Yes — DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl wraps each mutation in `runCatching` (lines 127-160); DownloadsViewModel.emitOnFailure (lines 224-231) emits `DownloadsEffect.ShowError(message)` which the screen shows in a SnackbarHost (DownloadsScreen.kt:180-186, 222).
- **Explanation:** KMP adds an error-feedback path that native lacks (a strict improvement). Divergence from source of truth but not a regression. The retry path can now surface 'download row not found' on a race that native would silently no-op (DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl.kt:141-149).
- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed; this is an intentional improvement. Just ensure the error messages shown are localized/user-friendly (the throwable.message fallback chain may surface raw technical text).

**⚪ [Low] Top app bar — Native uses a shared TopAppBarCom wrapper; KMP uses raw Material3 TopAppBar** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — DownloadsScreen.kt:85-96 uses `TopAppBarCom(title = stringResource(R.string.downloads), navigationIcon = { IconButton{ Icon(Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack, tint=onBackground) } })`.
- **KMP:** Partial — DownloadsScreen.kt:209-220 uses Material3 `TopAppBar(title={Text(downloads)}, navigationIcon={ IconButton{ Icon(YamiIcons.Back, tint=onBackground) } })`. Back icon is `YamiIcons.Back` (mapped to an AutoMirrored back arrow) rather than directly Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack.
- **Explanation:** Both show a 'Downloads' title and a back arrow tinted onBackground. The wrapper differs (TopAppBarCom likely applies app-specific container color/elevation/typography) vs a plain Material3 TopAppBar, which could yield subtly different bar background/elevation/title style. Back icon parity depends on YamiIcons.Back resolving to the same AutoMirrored arrow. Low risk but a structural divergence worth a visual check against TopAppBarCom's styling.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm the KMP TopAppBar container color, elevation and title typography match what TopAppBarCom applies in native (verify YamiIcons.Back == Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack); align if they differ.

**⚪ [Low] BackHandler — Native registers an explicit Compose BackHandler that routes to onBack; KMP relies on default nav back** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — DownloadsScreen.kt:74 `BackHandler { onBack() }` intercepts the system back gesture/button and routes it through the same onBack as the toolbar arrow.
- **KMP:** No — KMP DownloadsScreenContent has no BackHandler; system back is handled by the nav host's default pop (the screen only wires onBack to the top-bar arrow, DownloadsScreen.kt:212).
- **Explanation:** Native explicitly intercepts back to run its onBack (safePopBackStack equivalent). KMP omits the BackHandler and depends on NavController default back behavior. In practice both pop the back stack, but native guarantees the same code path for hardware-back and toolbar-back; KMP's hardware back bypasses the screen's onBack callback. Minor, and likely equivalent given safePopBackStack on the route, but it is a structural divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** If exact parity is desired, add a BackHandler in the KMP screen that calls onBack so hardware back and the toolbar arrow share one path; otherwise verify nav-default back matches native's behavior.

### History  `history`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 15 (🔴0 🟠0 🟡4 ⚪11)

"manga deleted from library" Toast; the KMP screen has neither the conditional library route nor any existence guard and always navigates to MangaDetails / the reader. KMP also ADDS a centered empty state and a loading spinner that native never renders. Smaller divergences: Arabic title translation differs (السجل vs native التاريخ), Arabic month abbreviations for the >6-day header were never shipped, and per-row ellipsis/overflow handling differs slightly.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for History</summary>

**🟡 [Medium] History — cover (manga) tap navigation — Native routes cover-tap conditionally to LibraryMangaDetails vs MangaDetails by mangaId; KMP always routes to MangaDetails** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — NavGraphV2.kt:321-352: onHistoryImgClick checks `if (it.mangaId != 0L)` then `isMangaExists(it.mangaId)` → navigate Screen.LibraryMangaDetails(mangaId) else show Toast; else branch navigates Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api).
- **KMP:** No (partial) — HistoryReworkScreenRoute.kt:83-90 / HistoryScreenRoute.kt:175-181 always call safeNavigate(Screen.MangaDetails(mangaUrl, api)); HistoryViewModel.kt:130-135 OnMangaClick unconditionally emits NavigateToDetails(api, mangaUrl). Screen.LibraryMangaDetails was retired in KMP (App.kt:104).
- **Explanation:** Native distinguishes library manga (mangaId != 0) from network manga and opens the in-library details screen for the former, falling back to the network details screen otherwise. KMP collapses both into the network MangaDetails route. In practice KMP-written history rows always carry mangaId = 0L (HistoryRepositoryImpl.record sets mangaId = 0L, see :92-104), so the divergence is mostly latent for rows created by the KMP reader, but legacy/existing rows with non-zero mangaId would route differently than native intends.
- **Suggested fix:** In the History route adapter (or via a new HistoryEffect), branch on entry.mangaId: when non-zero navigate to the in-library details destination (the KMP equivalent of LibraryMangaDetails), otherwise to MangaDetails — matching native's mangaId-based routing.

**🟡 [Medium] History — 'manga deleted from library' guard — Native guards both cover-tap and chapter-tap with isMangaExists(...) and shows a Toast if the manga was removed; KMP has no guard** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — NavGraphV2.kt:323-337 (cover) and :356-385 (chapter): coroutineScope.launch { if (sharedChaptersVm.isMangaExists(mangaId)) navigate else Toast.makeText(context, "THis Manga Is Deleted from the Libarary", LENGTH_SHORT) }.
- **KMP:** No — grep for isMangaExists across composeApp/presentation/ui/domain/data returns zero matches. HistoryViewModel.kt:130-136 emits navigation effects directly with no existence check; route adapters navigate unconditionally.
- **Explanation:** Native protects against tapping a history entry whose underlying library manga was deleted by checking existence and surfacing a user-facing Toast instead of navigating into a broken/empty details or reader screen. KMP removed this safety check entirely, so tapping a stale history row navigates regardless, potentially landing on an empty or error screen with no explanation.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an existence check before emitting the navigation effect (e.g. a domain use case mirroring sharedChaptersVm.isMangaExists) and surface a transient message effect when the manga no longer exists, matching native; or document deliberately dropping it if the KMP details/reader handle the missing-manga case gracefully.

**🟡 [Medium] History — top bar clear-all / per-row delete affordance — Native uses material icons (DeleteForever for clear-all, Outlined.Delete per row); KMP uses labelled TextButtons ("Clear all" / "Delete")** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — HistoryScreen.kt:55-61 IconButton{ Icon(Icons.Default.DeleteForever, tint = error) }; HistoryItem.kt:114-120 IconButton{ Icon(Icons.Outlined.Delete, tint = onBackground) }.
- **KMP:** No (substituted) — HistoryScreen.kt:192-197 TextButton{ Text(stringResource(clear_all), color = error) }; :323-325 TextButton{ Text(stringResource(delete), color = onBackground) }. KDoc lines 95-99 acknowledge History was not in the icon-conversion set.
- **Explanation:** The destructive affordances render as text buttons in KMP versus icon buttons in native. This is a visible UI divergence: the top-right action shows the word 'Clear all' instead of a trash-can-with-X glyph, and each row shows a 'Delete' text button instead of a delete icon, changing row layout/width and visual weight. The KMP KDoc explicitly defers the icon conversion to UP-2/UP-4.
- **Suggested fix:** Convert both actions to IconButtons using the materialIconsExtended DeleteForever (clear-all, error tint) and Outlined.Delete (per-row, onBackground tint) to match native, keeping the same content descriptions (clear history / delete).

**🟡 [Medium] History — top bar styling (title size/weight/container color) — Native top bar title is 24sp Bold on a background-colored bar; KMP uses default M3 TopAppBar (titleLarge ~22sp Normal, surface container)** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — uses custom TopAppBarCom (HistoryScreen.kt:52) which sets titleSize = 24.sp, fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold, containerColor = colorScheme.background, textColor = onBackground (TopAppBarCom.kt:22-31).
- **KMP:** No (defaults) — HistoryScreen.kt:189-199 uses bare Material3 TopAppBar with title = Text(stringResource(history)) and no titleTextStyle/colors override, so it renders the default titleLarge (~22sp, FontWeight.Normal/Medium) on the default surface/elevated container color.
- **Explanation:** The History header text is visually smaller and lighter in KMP (default titleLarge ~22sp regular) versus native (24sp Bold), and the bar background differs (native explicitly background color, KMP default M3 TopAppBar surface color which differs once elevated/scrolled). This is a noticeable header divergence consistent across the rework screens but still a deviation from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply a titleTextStyle (24sp, FontWeight.Bold) and TopAppBarColors(containerColor = background) to the KMP TopAppBar (or introduce a shared Yami top-bar matching TopAppBarCom) to match native's 24sp Bold/background styling.

**⚪ [Low] History — empty state — KMP renders a centered icon + 'No reading history yet' empty state; native renders nothing (empty LazyColumn)** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — HistoryScreen.kt has no empty branch; when historyItems is empty the LazyColumn (:67-100) simply renders no items (blank content area under the top bar).
- **KMP:** Yes — HistoryScreen.kt:210 `state.isEmpty -> YamiEmptyState(title = stringResource(no_reading_history))` renders a 64dp onSurfaceVariant icon (YamiIcons.Empty) + titleMedium centered text (YamiStateViews.kt:76-119).
- **Explanation:** KMP adds an empty-state placeholder that the source-of-truth native app does not have. While arguably an improvement, it is a divergence from native parity: native shows a blank list area, KMP shows an illustrated empty state. The clear-all action is also correctly disabled in KMP's empty state (enabled = state.items.isNotEmpty(), :194), which native does not do (native's clear-all is always enabled).
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm with design whether the added empty state should remain. If strict native parity is required, remove the empty-state branch (or gate behind a flag). Otherwise document it as an intentional enhancement.

**⚪ [Low] History — loading state — KMP shows a centered loading spinner during initial load; native shows no spinner** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — native HistoryUiState has isLoading (HistoryUiState.kt:7) and the VM sets it (HistoryViewModel.kt:52,63), but HistoryScreen.kt never reads isLoading and renders no spinner — the list is simply empty until the first emission.
- **KMP:** Yes — HistoryScreen.kt:209 `state.isLoading -> YamiLoadingState()` renders a centered CircularProgressIndicator (YamiStateViews.kt:55-63); HistoryState.isLoading defaults to true (HistoryState.kt:76) until the first snapshot.
- **Explanation:** KMP displays a full-area centered progress spinner before the first history emission arrives; native never surfaces its isLoading flag in the UI, so native shows a blank area instead of a spinner during the brief load window. Minor visual divergence on first entry to the screen.
- **Suggested fix:** Either remove the loading branch to match native's blank-during-load behavior, or accept it as an enhancement and document it. If kept, ensure the spinner doesn't flicker for the typical instant Room emission.

**⚪ [Low] History — top bar title localization (Arabic) — Arabic title differs: native 'التاريخ' vs KMP 'السجل'** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — values-ar/strings.xml:5 `title_history = التاريخ`.
- **KMP:** Yes (different value) — ui/.../values-ar/strings.xml:263 `history = السجل`. The KMP screen uses Res.string.history (HistoryScreen.kt:190).
- **Explanation:** The Arabic word shown in the History top bar is different between the apps: native uses التاريخ ("the history/date") while KMP uses السجل ("the log/record"). Both are plausible translations but they are not identical, so Arabic users see different header text than the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the Arabic translation of the History title with native (التاريخ) for parity, or have localization sign off on السجل as the intended value.

**⚪ [Low] History — clear-all content description / accessibility — Native clear-all icon has contentDescription 'Clear history'; KMP TextButton has no contentDescription (label text only)** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes — HistoryScreen.kt:58 contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.content_description_clear_history) ("Clear history"); per-row delete icon contentDescription = content_description_delete (HistoryItem.kt:117).
- **KMP:** No dedicated CD — HistoryScreen.kt:196 the clear-all is a TextButton with visible text 'Clear all' (Res.string.clear_all) and no semantics/contentDescription; per-row delete is a TextButton with text 'Delete' (:324). Because they are text buttons the label serves as the accessible name, but the wording differs ('Clear all' vs 'Clear history').
- **Explanation:** Native exposes 'Clear history' / 'Delete' as icon content descriptions for TalkBack. KMP exposes the visible button labels 'Clear all' / 'Delete'. The delete label matches; the clear-all accessible name diverges in wording ('Clear all' vs native 'Clear history'). If/when KMP converts these to icon buttons, contentDescriptions must be added to avoid an accessibility regression.
- **Suggested fix:** If keeping TextButtons, optionally align wording; when converting to IconButtons, add contentDescription = stringResource for clear-history and delete to preserve native's accessibility labels.

**⚪ [Low] History — absolute-date group header under Arabic locale — Native formats >6-day group header via locale-aware DateTimeFormatter; KMP renders English month abbreviations because Arabic month_abbrev_* were never shipped** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — HistoryScreen.kt:126 `date.format(DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MMM d, yyyy"))` which is locale-aware on Android and renders localized (Arabic) month names under an Arabic locale.
- **KMP:** Partial — HistoryScreen.kt:354 builds `${monthAbbrev(date.monthNumber)} ${date.dayOfMonth}, ${date.year}` from month_abbrev_* string resources, but those keys exist only in values/strings_np_p2_hist_upd_stats.xml (Jan..Dec, :17-28) and are absent from values-ar (grep returns zero). The KDoc (:12-14) claims 'ar is appended in the trusted-Arabic pass' but it never was.
- **Explanation:** For history entries older than 6 days, the sticky group header on KMP under Arabic locale falls back to the English month abbreviation (e.g. 'Apr 15, 2025') because the Arabic month_abbrev_* resources are missing, whereas native renders a localized Arabic month name. Also the fixed 'MMM d, yyyy' ordering (month-day-year) is not RTL/locale reordered in KMP. Edge case (only entries >6 days old).
- **Suggested fix:** Add month_abbrev_jan..dec to values-ar (and other locales), or replace the manual concatenation with a locale-aware date formatter so the absolute-date header localizes like native.

**⚪ [Low] History — row text overflow / ellipsize — KMP sets TextOverflow.Ellipsis on title and chapter; native sets only maxLines with default clipping** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Partial — HistoryItem.kt:92-104: title maxLines = 2, chapter maxLines = 1, with NO explicit overflow (Compose default is TextOverflow.Clip).
- **KMP:** Yes — HistoryScreen.kt:304-312: title maxLines = 2 + overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis; chapter maxLines = 1 + overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis.
- **Explanation:** When manga/chapter titles exceed the line limit, native clips the text (default TextOverflow.Clip) while KMP shows an ellipsis (…). This produces a subtly different truncation appearance on long titles. KMP's behavior is arguably better UX but diverges from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** To match native exactly, drop the overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis (or set TextOverflow.Clip). Alternatively accept ellipsis as an intentional polish and document it.

**⚪ [Low] History — row inner layout (column spacing & delete tap target) — Native uses explicit Spacer(4.dp) between texts and an IconButton (48dp min touch target); KMP uses Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.xs) and a TextButton** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — HistoryItem.kt: Column uses Spacer(height(4.dp)) between title/chapter/date (:98,:106); cover Column padding start = 12.dp (:90); delete is an IconButton (:114) giving the standard 48dp touch target.
- **KMP:** Yes (different primitives) — HistoryScreen.kt:298 Column verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.xs); cover-to-column gap is a Spacer(width(spacing.md)) (:294) rather than Column padding start=12.dp; delete is a TextButton (:323) whose width/height is governed by its text + button padding, not a fixed 48dp icon target.
- **Explanation:** Functionally equivalent but the spacing is token-driven (LocalSpacing.xs/md) rather than the hard-coded 4.dp/12.dp native literals — so unless spacing.xs == 4.dp and spacing.md == 12.dp the inter-text gaps and cover gap differ by a few dp. The delete affordance also differs in hit-area shape (text button vs 48dp icon button). Needs verification that LocalSpacing tokens equal the native literals.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify LocalSpacing.xs == 4.dp and LocalSpacing.md == 12.dp (the native literals). If not, override with explicit 4.dp/12.dp to match native exactly; ensure the delete control retains a >=48dp touch target.

**⚪ [Low] History — list group header width modifier — Native sticky header uses Modifier.fillMaxSize() (likely a bug); KMP uses fillMaxWidth()** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — HistoryScreen.kt:82-83 stickyHeader Text uses Modifier.fillMaxSize() inside a LazyColumn item.
- **KMP:** No (corrected) — HistoryScreen.kt:238-241 header Text uses Modifier.fillMaxWidth() (plus background + padding 16h/8v).
- **Explanation:** Native applies fillMaxSize() to the sticky header Text, which in a LazyColumn item resolves to fill width (height is wrap by the item) — effectively the same as fillMaxWidth here, so it is a latent native quirk rather than a visible bug. KMP uses the semantically-correct fillMaxWidth(). This is a deliberate (and correct) deviation; no user-visible difference expected but noted for completeness.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed; KMP's fillMaxWidth() is the correct form. Optionally note that the divergence is intentional cleanup of a native quirk.

**⚪ [Low] History — clear-all confirmation — Neither app shows a confirmation dialog before clearing all history** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** No confirmation — HistoryScreen.kt:55 IconButton onClick directly calls viewModel.deleteAllHistory(); no AlertDialog.
- **KMP:** No confirmation — HistoryScreen.kt:193 onClick directly dispatches HistoryIntent.OnDeleteAll; DeleteAllHistoryUseCase.kt KDoc (:50-56) explicitly confirms no pre-flight gate.
- **Explanation:** This is a parity match (both clear immediately with no confirm dialog), recorded to document that the destructive clear-all behaves identically and the KMP did not regress or add a dialog. No divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix required for parity. (Optionally both could add a confirmation dialog as a future UX improvement, but that would itself be a divergence.)

**⚪ [Low] History — row gestures (swipe/long-press) — Neither app supports swipe-to-delete or long-press; delete is button-only on both** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** No swipe/long-press — HistoryItem.kt only wires clickable(onChapterClick) on the card (:56), clickable(onMangaClick) on the cover (:71), and an IconButton for delete (:114).
- **KMP:** No swipe/long-press — HistoryScreen.kt:271 card clickable(onChapterClick), :291 cover clickable(onMangaClick), :323 TextButton delete. No detectTapGestures/long-press/swipe-to-dismiss on either side.
- **Explanation:** Parity match on interactions: tap card = open reader, tap cover = open details, tap delete button = remove entry; no swipe-to-dismiss or long-press selection on either app. Recorded to confirm no interaction regression in the migration.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix required for parity.

**⚪ [Low] History — error state handling — Native has an error field in UiState (set on load/delete failure) but never renders it; KMP dropped the error field entirely** _(State)_

- **Native:** Partial — HistoryUiState.kt:8 has `error: String?`; HistoryViewModel.kt sets it on failures (:55-59,:73-76,:91-93,:124-126,:148-151,:160-163) and exposes clearError() (:187), but HistoryScreen.kt never reads/renders error (no error UI).
- **KMP:** No error field — HistoryState.kt:75-82 has only isLoading + items (KDoc :38-43 justifies dropping error since the Room flow doesn't throw); HistoryEffect.kt has no ShowError variant.
- **Explanation:** Neither app shows errors to the user on the History screen, so there is no observable behavioral difference. Native carries (but never surfaces) an error string; KMP omits it by design. Documented as a structural difference with no user-visible impact today, but if a future fallible upstream is added KMP has no error surface wired.
- **Suggested fix:** No user-facing fix needed. If desired for forward-safety, add the planned HistoryEffect.ShowError + a .catch on observeHistory as the KMP KDocs anticipate.

### Statistics  `statistics`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 18 (🔴0 🟠1 🟡5 ⚪12)

> Both apps render the same Statistics surface: a 3-cell overview Card on top, then an "Entries" section (In library / Started / Completed) and a "Chapters" section (Total / Read / Downloaded / Bookmarked), all backed by the same 7 Room COUNT(*) DAO queries plus a DataStore read-minutes counter formatted as "Xh Ym". The KMP data/computation path (StatisticsDeo + legacy :shared StatisticsRepository -> ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl combine -> ObserveReadingStatisticsUseCase -> MVI StatisticsViewModel) faithfully reproduces the native MVVM Hilt path, so the numbers agree. The headline divergences are UI/visual: KMP intentionally drops ALL row icons (8 outlined Material icons), replaces the native ArrowBack IconButton with a labelled "Back" TextButton, changes the overview middle label from the native "Read duration" (label_read_duration) to a new "Read Time" (read_time) string, uses a 12dp group-card corner instead of native 16dp, drops the native TopAppBar's 24sp-Bold title styling, and changes section-title/group padding. KMP also strips localization down to en+ar (native ships 11 locales for these keys, including the read_time replacement which exists only en+ar) and adds a loading state native does not have. No charts/time-range features exist on either side, so nothing chart-related is missing.
