StatsItem.kt (.../presentation/common/componants/list_items/StatsItem.kt) signature line 32-38 has `icon: ImageVector? = null`, and lines 51-59 render `Icon(imageVector=icon, tint=onBackground, Modifier.size(24.dp))` followed by `Spacer(Modifier.width(16.dp))` when icon != null — exactly the 24dp icon + 16dp spacer described. KMP drops all 7. /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt: the private StatsItem at line 321 has signature `(title: String, value: Int)` — no icon param. Its body (lines 323-342) renders only a title Text (weight 1f) + a value Text; no Icon composable, no leading-glyph Spacer. The 7 call sites (lines 208,210,212,219,221,223,225) pass only title+value. grep confirms no alternate icon-bearing StatsItem exists in :ui/:presentation/:composeApp. KDoc lines 69-75 explicitly state icons are 'intentionally omitted'. The left-shift claim also holds: removing the 24dp icon + 16dp spacer means the title column now starts at the row's leading edge (KMP StatsItem padding starts horizontal=spacing.lg with title weight(1f) immediately), vs native where the icon occupies the leading 40dp before the title column. Minor inaccuracies in the claim (not affecting the verdict): (1) one cited native line is off-by-one — chaptersTotal's icon is at line 101, not 100 (line 100 is the `title=` arg). (2) The KMP KDoc rationale that `compose.materialIconsExtended` is omitted from :ui is now stale — ui/build.gradle.kts:63 actually includes `implementation(compose.materialIconsExtended)`. The dep is present, yet the icons are still not rendered, so the visible divergence stands regardless.

**🟡 [Medium] Statistics - TopAppBar back affordance — Back control is a text 'Back' button in KMP vs an ArrowBack icon button in native** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes - StatisticsScreen.kt:53-55 renders an IconButton with Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack, tint onBackground, contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.desc_back).
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:166-174 renders navigationIcon as a TextButton showing the localized word 'Back' (Res.string.back) instead of an arrow icon.
- **Explanation:** The navigation slot affordance differs in form (text label vs directional arrow). The native arrow is RTL-mirrored via AutoMirrored and carries a localized contentDescription for accessibility; the KMP text button shows a translated word. Note the StatisticsScreenRoute.kt KDoc (lines 42-45) inaccurately claims the rework screen 'has no navigationIcon' and relies on system back, but the actual :ui code does render a navigationIcon TextButton - a stale-doc/behaviour mismatch worth flagging.
- **Suggested fix:** Replace the TextButton with an IconButton + a back-arrow vector (AutoMirrored arrow equivalent) tinted onSurface, with a localized contentDescription matching native desc_back, to restore the icon affordance and proper RTL mirroring.

**🟡 [Medium] Statistics - overview middle cell label — Overview middle label uses a different string key with far less localization coverage** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - StatsOverview.kt:48 uses R.string.label_read_duration ('Read duration'), localized in 11 locales (en/ar/de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr) per res strings.xml.
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:259 uses Res.string.read_time ('Read Time'), a NEW key present only in values/strings.xml:112 and values-ar/strings.xml:344. The pre-existing label_read_duration key is not reused.
- **Explanation:** Two divergences in one: (a) English copy changed from 'Read duration' to 'Read Time'; (b) the chosen key only has en + ar translations, whereas native covers 11 languages. On any of the 9 other native-supported locales the KMP cell will fall back to English 'Read Time'. The KDoc on the screen even calls read_time 'a new en-only key (ar-TODO)' which is now stale since ar was added, but the other 9 locales remain missing.
- **Suggested fix:** Reuse the existing localized label_read_duration concept (port its 11-locale translations into composeResources) or add the missing 9 locale translations for read_time, and align the English copy with native ('Read duration') unless the rename is an intentional product change.

**🟡 [Medium] Statistics - TopAppBar title typography — Title styling differs: native forces 24sp Bold; KMP uses default M3 TopAppBar title style** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes - TopAppBarCom.kt:22-40 sets titleSize = 24.sp and fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold on a titleLarge-based style, textColor = onBackground, containerColor = colorScheme.background.
- **KMP:** No - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:164-165 uses a plain Material3 TopAppBar with title = Text(...) and no fontSize/weight overrides, so it renders the default M3 titleLarge (~22sp, Medium) with default M3 topAppBar container/title colors.
- **Explanation:** Native's custom top bar uses a larger 24sp Bold title on a background-colored bar; KMP uses the stock M3 app-bar look (smaller, non-bold title, default surface container color). This is a noticeable header-weight and color divergence on a screen the user reaches from Settings.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply a titleLarge.copy(fontSize = 24.sp, fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold) style and set TopAppBar colors (container = background, title = onBackground) to match the native TopAppBarCom.

**🟡 [Medium] Statistics - localization coverage of section/label strings — KMP ships only en + ar for the statistics strings vs 11 locales in native** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - title_statistics, section_entries, section_chapters, label_in_library/started/completed/total/read/downloaded/bookmarked, value_count, h_m, desc_back are all translated across values, values-ar, values-de, values-es, values-fr, values-in, values-it, values-ja, values-pt, values-ru, values-tr.
- **KMP:** Partial - ui composeResources only has values/ (en) and values-ar/ for statistics/back/section/label keys (strings.xml lines 40-56,112 and values-ar 32-48,344). No de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr translations exist in the :ui module.
- **Explanation:** Native supports 11 languages on the Statistics screen; KMP supports only English and Arabic. Users on the 9 other native-supported locales will see English text in KMP. This is a broad localization regression spanning the whole screen (title, both section headers, all labels).
- **Suggested fix:** Port the missing 9 locale translations for the statistics-related keys into the :ui composeResources values-* directories to restore native localization coverage.

**🟡 [Medium] Statistics - duration formatting localization (h_m) — Read-duration 'Xh Ym' is hardcoded English literal in KMP; native uses a localized h_m resource** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - StatisticsRepository.kt:44-48 formats via context.getString(R.string.h_m, h, m); h_m is localized per-locale (e.g. ar '%1$dس %2$dد', ja '%1$d時 %2$d分', ru '%1$dч %2$dм').
- **KMP:** No - shared StatisticsRepository.kt:75-80 hardcodes "${h}h ${m}m" with an inline 'TODO Phase 10: stringResource(R.string.h_m, h, m)'. ReadingStatistics.readDuration carries this literal verbatim; the :ui screen never re-formats it.
- **Explanation:** The read-duration value is always rendered in English unit abbreviations ('h'/'m') regardless of app language. On Arabic the rest of the screen is translated but the duration shows Latin 'h/m', and the digits are not localized either (native h_m at least allows locale-specific unit suffixes). This is an acknowledged-but-unresolved migration TODO.
- **Suggested fix:** Move the h_m formatting to a localized Compose resource (or format in the :ui layer using stringResource(Res.string.h_m, h, m)) and add the per-locale unit strings, so the duration matches native localized output.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - overview completed cell label — Overview 3rd cell reuses label_completed instead of native label_completed_entries** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - StatsOverview.kt:53 uses R.string.label_completed_entries ('Completed entries'), distinct from the section row's label_completed ('Completed').
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:264 uses Res.string.label_completed ('Completed') for the overview cell, so the big-number overview cell and the Entries-section row both read 'Completed'. label_completed_entries was not ported to composeResources.
- **Explanation:** Native distinguishes the overview aggregate label ('Completed entries') from the per-section row ('Completed'). KMP collapses both to 'Completed', losing the distinction and the localized label_completed_entries copy (which native localizes in all 11 locales).
- **Suggested fix:** Add a label_completed_entries string (with locale translations) and use it for the overview cell at StatisticsScreen.kt:264 to match native wording.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - section group card corner radius — Group/card rounded-corner radius is 12dp in KMP vs 16dp in native** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes - ItemsGroup.kt:23 uses RoundedCornerShape(16.dp) for the Entries/Chapters group card.
- **KMP:** No - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:310 StatsItemsGroup uses RoundedCornerShape(12.dp).
- **Explanation:** The section group cards are visibly less rounded in KMP (12dp) than native (16dp). The overview card matches at 12dp on both sides, but native deliberately uses a larger 16dp radius for the grouped lists.
- **Suggested fix:** Change StatsItemsGroup's shape to RoundedCornerShape(16.dp) to match native ItemsGroup.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - section group inner padding — Group container padding differs (native pads the group; KMP pads each item)** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes - ItemsGroup.kt:25 applies padding(horizontal = 16.dp, vertical = 8.dp) on the group Column; individual StatsItem rows then add padding(vertical = 12.dp) (StatsItem.kt:47).
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:316 StatsItemsGroup wraps a bare Column with no padding; each StatsItem applies padding(horizontal = spacing.lg=16.dp, vertical = spacing.md=12.dp) (lines 324-326).
- **Explanation:** Horizontal padding ends up ~16dp on both, but vertical rhythm differs: native adds an 8dp group-level vertical pad PLUS 12dp per row (so ~20dp above the first row / below the last), while KMP only has 12dp per row with no group-level vertical pad. The dividers also sit at different insets because native dividers are inside the 16dp-padded group whereas KMP dividers are full-width inside the card. Net effect: top/bottom whitespace inside the group cards is tighter in KMP.
- **Suggested fix:** Add vertical = 8.dp padding to the StatsItemsGroup Column (and consider matching divider insets) so the grouped-list internal spacing matches native ItemsGroup.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - SectionTitle padding — Section title uses symmetric vertical padding in KMP vs bottom-only in native** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes - SectionTitle.kt:20 uses Modifier.padding(bottom = 8.dp) only.
- **KMP:** No - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:303 SectionTitle uses Modifier.padding(vertical = spacing.sm = 8.dp), i.e. 8dp top AND 8dp bottom.
- **Explanation:** KMP adds an extra 8dp above each section title that native does not have. Since the screen already inserts a Spacer(16.dp) before each section, the KMP title is pushed down a further 8dp relative to native, increasing the gap between the overview card and the first section header and between sections.
- **Suggested fix:** Change SectionTitle padding to bottom = 8.dp only (drop the top component) to match native SectionTitle.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - stat row value typography color — Row value/title color tokens differ slightly between implementations** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes - StatsItem.kt: title color = onBackground (line 65), value Text (lines 76-81) has NO explicit color so it inherits the default LocalContentColor (effectively onSurface/onBackground depending on container). Title fontSize fixed at 14.sp.
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt: title uses style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium with color = onSurface (lines 331-332); value uses fontSize 12.sp Bold color = onSurface (lines 336-341).
- **Explanation:** KMP pins both title and value to onSurface, while native uses onBackground for the title and an inherited content color for the value. On themes where onBackground != onSurface this produces a subtle color difference. Also native title is a fixed 14.sp whereas KMP uses bodyMedium (typically 14sp Normal) - close but token-driven rather than a hard 14.sp literal, which can drift if the type scale is retuned.
- **Suggested fix:** Use onBackground for the row title to match native, and set the value to the inherited content color (or onBackground); pin the title to 14.sp if exact parity with the literal is desired.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - loading state — KMP shows a loading spinner before first emission; native shows zeros immediately** _(State)_

- **Native:** No - StatisticsViewModel.kt:17-43 seeds every StateFlow with an immediate default (0 / '0h 0m') via stateIn(Eagerly), and StatisticsScreen renders the column unconditionally with no isLoading branch.
- **KMP:** Yes - StatisticsState.kt:65 isLoading defaults true; ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:178-189 renders YamiLoadingState (centered CircularProgressIndicator) until the first ReadingStatistics emission sets isLoading=false (StatisticsViewModel.kt:101).
- **Explanation:** Behavioural divergence on cold start: native immediately shows the populated (or zeroed) layout, KMP briefly shows a full-screen spinner. The KDoc concedes the gap is 'sub-frame in practice' since Room emits immediately, so the spinner is rarely visible, but it is still an added state that native does not have and could flash on slow first composition.
- **Suggested fix:** Either accept the spinner as an enhancement, or seed StatisticsState with isLoading=false (showing zeros like native) for exact behavioural parity; if kept, ensure it never produces a visible flash.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - read-duration default value before data — Default read-duration string before first emission differs** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes - StatisticsViewModel.kt:20-21 seeds readDuration StateFlow with literal '0h 0m'.
- **KMP:** Partial - StatisticsState.kt:67 seeds readDuration = "" (empty string); the real value arrives with the first emission.
- **Explanation:** If the KMP loading branch were ever bypassed or removed, the overview 'Read Time' cell would show an empty string instead of native's '0h 0m'. With the current isLoading gate the empty default is hidden, so this is latent rather than user-visible today, but it is a divergent initial value.
- **Suggested fix:** Default StatisticsState.readDuration to '0h 0m' (matching native) so any pre-emission render shows a sensible value.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - row interaction (clickable rows) — Native StatsItem supports an optional onClick/description; KMP row has neither** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Partial - StatsItem.kt:37,44-46 declare an optional onClick and a description param (rows become clickable when onClick != null). On the Statistics screen specifically, native does NOT pass onClick/description (StatisticsScreen.kt:77-121), so rows are non-interactive there too.
- **KMP:** No - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:321 StatsItem(title, value) has no onClick/description support at all.
- **Explanation:** Functionally there is no behavioural regression on this screen because native does not wire onClick for statistics rows. But the KMP reimplementation drops the capability entirely, so if a future drill-down is added the native component already supports it whereas KMP would need a rewrite. Documenting as a capability divergence, not a live-flow break.
- **Suggested fix:** Optional: add an onClick and description parameter to the KMP StatsItem to match the native component's surface area, even if unused on this screen, for forward parity.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - thousands grouping of counts (value_count) — KMP reimplements '%,d' grouping with a hand-rolled formatter using a hardcoded comma separator** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - native renders every count via R.string.value_count = '%,d' (StatsItem.kt:77 and StatsOverview formatStatValue:86-89), which is the JVM/ICU locale-aware grouping format (separator and grouping follow the device locale).
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:351-362 formatCount() manually inserts a literal ',' every 3 digits because String.format('%,d') is JVM-only on KMP. It always uses a comma regardless of locale.
- **Explanation:** Functionally the grouping count is reproduced, but the separator is hardcoded to ',' whereas native '%,d' uses the locale's grouping separator (e.g. space or '.' in many EU locales, and Arabic-Indic context). Under non-US/Arabic locales the displayed grouping character can differ from native. Magnitude grouping (every 3 digits) matches; only the separator glyph and locale-awareness differ.
- **Suggested fix:** Use a multiplatform locale-aware number formatter (e.g. expect/actual around NumberFormat / ICU, or a Compose-resources plural/number API) so the grouping separator follows the active locale like native '%,d'.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - divider component — Native uses Material 2 Divider; KMP uses Material 3 HorizontalDivider** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - StatisticsScreen.kt:82,88,104,110,116 use androidx.compose.material.Divider with color = colorScheme.background.copy(alpha = 0.8f).
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:365-368 StatsDivider uses Material3 HorizontalDivider with the same color = background.copy(alpha = 0.8f).
- **Explanation:** Color/alpha match (background @ 0.8 alpha on both). The component type differs (M2 Divider vs M3 HorizontalDivider) which can yield a marginally different default thickness/inset, but visually near-identical. Combined with the group-padding difference above, dividers span slightly different widths (native dividers sit inside the 16dp-padded group, KMP dividers are full card width).
- **Suggested fix:** No functional change needed for the component swap; if exact divider inset parity is desired, indent the KMP dividers to match the native group's 16dp horizontal padding or align thickness explicitly.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - charts / time-range selectors — Neither implementation has charts or time-range filtering** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** No - the native Statistics screen is a static overview card + two count-list sections; no charts, graphs, or time-range (day/week/month) selectors exist anywhere in the statistics feature.
- **KMP:** No - the KMP screen likewise has no charts or time ranges. StatisticsIntent/StatisticsEffect are empty sealed interfaces (no OnExport/drill-down/time-range intents).
- **Explanation:** Confirming absence on BOTH sides so it is not mistaken for a KMP regression: the audit task mentions 'charts/cards, computations, time ranges' but the source of truth has no charts and no time ranges - only the overview card and two count lists. So there is no chart/time-range parity gap to fix.
- **Suggested fix:** No action - parity holds on the absence of charts/time-ranges. (Empty MVI intent/effect surfaces in KMP are documented future-extension hooks, not regressions.)

**⚪ [Low] Statistics - underlying counts & computations — Counts and completed/started computations are faithfully reproduced** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - StatisticsDeo.kt defines COUNT(*) over saved_manga / saved_chapters with isDownloaded/isRead/isBookmarked filters; completed = manga with NO unread chapter (NOT EXISTS isRead=0), started = manga with at least one isRead=1; read-minutes from DataStore formatted to 'Xh Ym'.
- **KMP:** Yes - shared StatisticsDeo.kt has the identical 7 queries (same SQL, same NOT EXISTS/EXISTS subqueries); shared StatisticsRepository combines them; ReadingStatisticsRepositoryImpl.kt:130-150 combines the 7 Flow<Int> + readDurationFlow into ReadingStatistics, preserving index mapping.
- **Explanation:** The data/computation layer is a faithful port: identical DAO SQL, identical completed/started semantics, same DataStore read-minutes -> minutes/60 + minutes%60 formatting (TimeUnit.toMinutes replaced by /60000L, bit-identical). The 7 suspend *Once variants were pruned in KMP but they were unused dead code on both consumption paths, so no functional impact. No double-render risk per combine semantics.
- **Suggested fix:** No action - data-layer parity is intact. (Minor: KMP dropped the unused suspend *Once DAO variants, which is a harmless cleanup, not a regression.)

### Updates / Library Refresh  `updates-refresh`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 25 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡9 ⚪14)

> Native renders the Updates feed via NotificationScreen + NotificationItems (Hilt NotificationsViewModel, NotificationRepository over NotificationDao/LibraryDeo) and triggers library refresh through RefreshViewModel + the foreground LibraryRefreshWorker. KMP re-implements the feed as an MVI slice (UpdatesViewModel/State/Intent/Effect in :presentation, UpdatesScreen in :ui, UpdatesRepositoryImpl/UpdateMappers in :data over the same legacy Room DAOs) and ports the worker verbatim into app/.../work/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt with a platform BackgroundJobScheduler. The data/DB/worker layers are very high parity (same tables, same group-by-date algorithm, same batch sizes/timeouts/notification channels), but the UI and interaction layers diverge substantially: KMP wraps each row in a Card (native is a flat Row), shows the raw chapterNumber instead of the localized "Chapter %1$s" label, uses sticky headers vs plain item headers, uses an empty-state placeholder native lacks, omits the marks-read-on-row-tap behavior, omits the AdMob download-gate, and ships the four date-group headers and the chapter-number format without Arabic translations (English-only under RTL). The KMP swipe-right also cannot un-mark a read row whereas native toggles. Headline divergences are localization regressions (group headers + chapter label not translated), the lost mark-read-on-tap, the lost ad gate on per-row download, and several cosmetic/structural row differences.

**🟠 [High] Updates feed - date group headers — Today/Yesterday/Last Week/Older group headers have no Arabic translation in the :ui catalog** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - NotificationRepository.kt:63-70 maps to R.string.notifications_group_today/yesterday/last_week/older; values-ar/strings.xml:95-98 provides اليوم/أمس/الأسبوع الماضي/أقدم
- **KMP:** Partial - UpdatesScreen.kt:317-322 references Res.string.notifications_group_today/yesterday/last_week/older, but these keys exist only in ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/values/strings_np_hist_upd_stats.xml (English) with NO values-ar entries (grep of values-ar returned MISSING for all four)
- **Explanation:** Under an Arabic locale the native app shows اليوم/أمس/الأسبوع الماضي/أقدم, while the KMP app falls back to the English defaults Today/Yesterday/Last Week/Older because the four notifications_group_* keys are absent from the :ui Arabic catalog. This is a clear localization regression on a primary user-facing list that the native app fully translates.
- **Suggested fix:** Add notifications_group_today/yesterday/last_week/older to ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/values-ar/strings.xml (and all other shipped locales) with the same translations the native app uses.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/.../presentation/features/notifications/domain/NotificationRepository.kt:64-70 maps the four recency buckets to R.string.notifications_group_today/yesterday/last_week/older. native-app/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:93-96 = Today/Yesterday/Last Week/Older; native-app/app/src/main/res/values-ar/strings.xml:95-98 = اليوم/أمس/الأسبوع الماضي/أقدم. So under Arabic the native app shows the translated headers. (Native also translates these in de/es/fr/it/ja/pt/ru/tr/in.) KMP: ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/updates/UpdatesScreen.kt:84-87 imports the keys from me.manga.kira.ui.generated.resources (the :ui module Res), and lines 317-322 (RecencyBucket enum) + 339 (stringResource(bucket.headerKey)) render them. The ONLY definition of these four keys in the :ui catalog is the ENGLISH file ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/values/strings_np_hist_upd_stats.xml:16-19 (its own header comment at lines 12-13 states 'en-only pending trusted Arabic'). A find/grep across ALL of ui/.../composeResources confirms notifications_group_* appears ONLY in that values/ file — NO values-ar (nor any other locale) copy exists in :ui (the :ui values-ar dir contains strings.xml + 4 np_* files, none with these keys). RESOURCE ISOLATION (decisive): the keys ARE translated to Arabic, but in a DIFFERENT module/package. composeApp/src/commonMain/composeResources/values-ar/strings.xml:95-98 has اليوم/أمس/الأسبوع الماضي/أقدم, but composeApp/build.gradle.kts:140 sets packageOfResClass = me.manga.kira.composeapp.generated.resources while ui/build.gradle.kts:121 sets me.manga.kira.ui.generated.resources. UpdatesScreen.kt:76 imports the :ui Res. Compose Multiplatform resolves each module's Res against only that module's own composeResources bundle, so composeApp's Arabic values cannot back the :ui screen lookups. The active route confirms the :ui screen is what renders: composeApp/.../navigation/routes/UpdatesScreenRoute.kt:9,108 imports and calls me.manga.kira.ui.updates.UpdatesScreen (UpdatesReworkScreenRoute.kt:9,120 too). Result: Arabic locale -> KMP Updates headers fall back to English defaults. Minor citation note: claim's native file is under presentation/features/notifications/domain/NotificationRepository.kt (lines 64-70), not data/repository; values-ar lines 95-98 are exact.

**🟠 [High] Updates feed - mark read on row tap — Tapping a row no longer marks the chapter as read before navigating** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:217-220 onNotificationClick = { viewModel.markAsRead(it.chapterId); onNotificationClick(it) } — the row tap marks-read then opens the reader
- **KMP:** No - UpdatesScreen.kt:354 onChapterClick = { onIntent(UpdatesIntent.OnChapterClick(entry)) }; UpdatesViewModel.kt:177 OnChapterClick only emits NavigateToReader(entry) with no markAsRead call
- **Explanation:** In native, opening a chapter update from the feed automatically clears its unread state (the primary dot disappears, opacity dims). In KMP the unread indicator and full opacity persist after the user has opened and read the chapter from the feed, so the user must additionally swipe-right or use a separate action to clear it. This is a behavioral regression in the core read-tracking flow.
- **Suggested fix:** In UpdatesViewModel.handle, on OnChapterClick also launch markUpdateAsRead(entry) (only when !entry.isRead to avoid toggling it back to unread, since the underlying DAO uses isRead = NOT isRead) before/while emitting NavigateToReader.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/.../notifications/ui/screens/UpdateItem.kt:57 makes the entire row `.clickable { onNotificationClick(notification) }`. UpdatesScreen.kt:217-220 overrides that lambda for the feed row as `onNotificationClick = { viewModel.markAsRead(it.chapterId); onNotificationClick(it) }`, and NavGraphV2.kt:399-421 wires the outer `onNotificationClick` to navigate to the reader (Screen.ChapterImagesFragment). NotificationsViewModel.kt:56-57 `markAsRead(id) { repo.markAsRead(id) }` flips isRead; UpdateItem.kt:84,108 dim to alpha 0.4 and UpdateItem.kt:91 hide the unread dot when isRead. So a native row tap marks-read (dot disappears, row dims) AND opens the reader. KMP (regression): ui/.../updates/UpdatesScreen.kt:473 the row Card is `.clickable(onClick = onChapterClick)` and line 354 wires `onChapterClick = { onIntent(UpdatesIntent.OnChapterClick(entry)) }`. presentation/.../updates/UpdatesViewModel.kt:177 `is UpdatesIntent.OnChapterClick -> emit(UpdatesEffect.NavigateToReader(intent.entry))` — no markUpdateAsRead call. composeApp/.../routes/UpdatesReworkScreenRoute.kt:130-147 `onNavigateToReader` only calls safeNavigate(Screen.ChapterImagesFragment) — no mark-read. The unread dot (UpdatesScreen.kt:521 `if (!entry.isRead)`) and 0.4 dim (line 468 `if (entry.isRead) 0.4f else 1f`) are driven by entry.isRead, which the tap never mutates. A dedicated OnMarkAsRead intent exists (UpdatesIntent.kt:59, VM line 159) but in KMP it is reachable only via swipe-right (UpdatesScreen.kt:389) — there is no per-row mark-read button. Net: tapping a KMP feed row opens the reader without clearing unread state, exactly as claimed.

**🟡 [Medium] Updates feed - chapter label — Chapter number shown as raw string instead of localized "Chapter %1$s" format** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdateItem.kt:102-103 renders Text(stringResource(R.string.chapter_number, notification.chapterNumber)); strings.xml has chapter_number = "Chapter %1$s" (en) and "الفصل %1$s" (ar)
- **KMP:** No - UpdatesScreen.kt:530 renders Text(text = entry.chapterNumber) with no format wrapper; the :ui catalog has no chapter_number key at all (grep returned zero hits in ui/src/commonMain/composeResources)
- **Explanation:** Native displays e.g. "Chapter 72" (or "الفصل 72" in Arabic), prefixing the stored chapter number with a localized label. KMP shows only the bare stored value (e.g. "72" or "Chapter 72" depending on how the source stored it), with no localization and no consistent prefix. If sources store just a number, the KMP row loses the "Chapter" word entirely, and under Arabic locale it is never translated.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a chapter_number plural/format string to the :ui catalog (en + ar + other locales) and render the chapter label via stringResource(Res.string.chapter_number, entry.chapterNumber) in UpdatesRowContent.

**🟡 [Medium] Per-row download - AdMob gate — Per-row download no longer triggers the interstitial/ad flow** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - NotificationsRoute.kt:42-50 onNotificationDownloadClick calls downloadViewModel.downloadChapterNotification(...) AND adViewModel.onDownloadStarted(context, onProceed = {}) {}
- **KMP:** No - UpdatesScreen.kt:357 onDownloadClick = { onIntent(UpdatesIntent.OnDownloadClick(entry)) }; UpdatesViewModel.kt:178-188 only calls enqueueDownload(...).onFailure { ShowError }; no AdViewModel/ad-gate involvement anywhere in the updates path
- **Explanation:** Native wires the per-row download button through the AdMob onDownloadStarted gate (consistent with the rest of the app's monetization). The KMP updates download path bypasses any ad flow entirely. Beyond the missing ad, the side-effect ordering and any onProceed gating native applied is absent. This is a business-logic/monetization divergence introduced by the migration.
- **Suggested fix:** Route the OnDownloadClick handling through the same ad-gate the KMP app uses elsewhere for downloads (an effect like ShowDownloadAd or a shared ad use case), invoking the enqueue on proceed, to match native's onDownloadStarted gating.

**🟡 [Medium] Updates feed - row container styling — KMP wraps each row in an elevated rounded Card; native uses a flat Row** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdateItem.kt:54-60 is a plain Row (fillMaxWidth, clickable, padding(horizontal=16dp, vertical=8dp)) with no card/background/elevation
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:469-478 wraps the row in a Card(containerColor = surfaceVariant, shape = RoundedCornerShape(12dp), padding horizontal=16dp vertical=4dp)
- **Explanation:** Native renders updates as flat full-width list rows separated only by spacing; KMP renders each as a discrete surfaceVariant-tinted rounded card with margins. This is a noticeable visual divergence in list density, background color, corner radius, and per-item separation. Native vertical padding is 8dp per row vs KMP card outer vertical 4dp + inner spacing.md.
- **Suggested fix:** If strict parity is required, drop the Card wrapper and render a flat Row with horizontal=16dp/vertical=8dp padding and no surfaceVariant background, matching UpdateItem.kt; otherwise document the card styling as an intentional redesign.

**🟡 [Medium] Updates feed - error message rendering — Native renders an inline red error Text when the upstream flow throws; KMP has no error field/branch** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes - NotificationsViewModel.kt:40-49 catches upstream errors into errorMessage; UpdatesScreen.kt(native):98-106 renders Text(error, color = colorScheme.error, padding 16dp)
- **KMP:** No - UpdatesState.kt has no error field (documented as intentional, lines 49-55); UpdatesViewModel.kt:139-144 collector has no .catch {}; a thrown upstream would crash the collector rather than surface an inline message
- **Explanation:** Native defends against an upstream Room/flow exception by catching it and showing an inline error message (and clearing the list). KMP deliberately omits any error handling on the observeUpdates collector. While Room's observe site rarely throws, any future fallible upstream (or a mapping exception in toDomain) would propagate uncaught and the screen has no error UI, a robustness/UX regression vs native.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a .catch {} to the observeUpdates collector in UpdatesViewModel that updates state with an error and/or emits UpdatesEffect.ShowError, plus an inline error rendering in UpdatesScreenContent, matching native's errorMessage handling.

**🟡 [Medium] Updates feed - delete-with-undo persistence model — Native deletes the row from the DB immediately then restores on Undo; KMP keeps it in the DB and only soft-hides via UI state until the snackbar dismisses** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - NotificationsViewModel.kt:75-101 deleteWithUndo deletes from DB immediately (repo.delete), undoDelete re-inserts (repo.restore -> dao.insertNotification), confirmDelete just clears the pending ref
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesViewModel.kt:189-199 OnRequestDelete only stages id in pendingDeleteIds (no DB write) + emits snackbar; OnUndoDelete unstages (no DB write); OnConfirmDelete unstages then calls deleteUpdateEntry (DB delete happens only on dismiss)
- **Explanation:** The two implementations invert when the actual DB delete happens. Native removes the row immediately and re-inserts on undo (so a process death during the snackbar window leaves the row deleted; re-insert assigns a new autogenerated id via REPLACE). KMP defers the DB delete until snackbar dismissal (so a process death during the window leaves the row NOT deleted). User-visible result is similar in the happy path, but edge cases (process death, rapid navigation away, the new-row-id change on native restore) differ, and the KMP entry retains its original id on undo whereas native's restore reinserts. Behavioral divergence in delete semantics.
- **Suggested fix:** Document the chosen model; if strict parity matters, decide which semantics to standardize on. KMP's defer-delete is arguably safer, but verify navigating away mid-snackbar still finalizes the delete (the snackbar coroutine is tied to the screen scope and may be cancelled, potentially leaving the entry undeleted - native finalizes immediately and is immune to that).

**🟡 [Medium] Updates feed - delete-while-navigating-away edge case — KMP delete may never finalize if the user navigates away before the snackbar resolves** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Partial - native deletes immediately in deleteWithUndo, so leaving the screen leaves the row deleted regardless of the snackbar; only an explicit Undo restores it
- **KMP:** Yes (risk) - UpdatesScreen.kt:240-255 the snackbar is shown from scope = rememberCoroutineScope() inside the screen; OnConfirmDelete (the actual DB delete) only fires on SnackbarResult.Dismissed. If the screen leaves the composition, the coroutine is cancelled and neither OnUndoDelete nor OnConfirmDelete is dispatched, so the staged entry is never deleted (and pendingDeleteIds lives in the VM which may survive)
- **Explanation:** Because the KMP delete is deferred to snackbar dismissal and the snackbar lifecycle is bound to the composition scope, navigating away during the ~short snackbar window can drop both the confirm and undo branches: the row is not deleted (DB write never happens) but is also unstaged only if the VM is recreated. Native avoids this by deleting up-front. This is a potential correctness regression where a user-intended delete silently does not persist.
- **Suggested fix:** Move the snackbar result handling onto a scope that survives navigation (e.g., handle confirm/undo in the VM with a timeout, or use viewModelScope), or delete immediately and restore on undo like native, so a delete can never be silently lost.

**🟡 [Medium] Updates top bar - actions are icons vs text buttons — Native top-bar actions are IconButtons (DeleteSweep + DoneAll icons); KMP uses labelled TextButtons** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt(native):82-93 IconButton with Icons.Default.DeleteSweep (delete all) and Icons.Default.DoneAll (mark all read), each with contentDescription
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:273-286 TextButton "Mark all read" and TextButton "Clear all" (clear all tinted error color); no icons (the screen KDoc explicitly notes icon conversion was deferred)
- **Explanation:** Native exposes the two bulk actions as compact icon buttons (DoneAll, DeleteSweep) in the toolbar; KMP renders them as wide text buttons ("Mark all read", "Clear all"). This changes the toolbar's visual density and layout, the affordance shape, and removes the recognizable Material sweep/done-all iconography. Also note ordering: native shows Delete-all first then Mark-all-read; KMP shows Mark-all-read first then Clear-all (reversed order).
- **Suggested fix:** Convert the two KMP top-bar actions to IconButtons using DeleteSweep and DoneAll (materialIconsExtended is already available per the screen KDoc) and match native's order (delete-all then mark-all-read), or document the text-button toolbar as an intentional rework convention.

**🟡 [Medium] Library refresh notification - localization — Refresh foreground-notification strings are hardcoded English in KMP; native uses translated resources** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryRefreshWorker.kt(native):72-73,85-86,141,206-233 use R.string.notification_channel_library_refresh, notification_refreshing_library, notification_starting, notification_processing_batch, notification_finishing_up, notification_refresh_progress, notification_refresh_completed, notification_refresh_failed (all have ar translations in values-ar/strings.xml)
- **KMP:** No - app/.../work/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:88-101,124,130,146,172-191,268 hardcode "Library refresh updates", "Refreshing Library", "Starting…", "Processing batch N…", "Finishing up…", "Completed: X successful, Y failed", "Refresh failed: ...", "Library Refresh Failed" (KDoc lines 60-62 acknowledge this as localization debt / TODO)
- **Explanation:** The background library-refresh foreground notification (channel name, title, progress text, completion/failure text) is fully translated in native (Arabic and others) but hardcoded English in the KMP worker. An Arabic-locale user sees English refresh notifications. Same applies to the new-chapters notification text (see separate finding).
- **Suggested fix:** Reconcile the worker with a non-Compose string source (e.g., Android string resources duplicated into app/, or a localized provider injected into the worker) so the refresh notification strings localize, matching native's R.string.notification_* set.

**🟡 [Medium] New-chapter notification - localization & channel name — New-chapter notification text and channel name hardcoded English in KMP; native localizes them** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes - ChapterNotificationHelper.kt(native):53-58 channel name = R.string.new_chapters, desc = R.string.notifications_for_new_manga_chapters; line 156-160 content text = R.string.chapter_is_available with chapterNumber arg (all translated)
- **KMP:** No - app/.../core/util/notification/ChapterNotificationHelper.kt:62-65 hardcodes "New Chapters"/"Notifications for new manga chapters"; line 138 hardcodes "Chapter ${chapterNumber} is available" (KDoc lines 39-43 flag this as localization debt)
- **Explanation:** The high-importance new-chapter notification (channel name, description, and the "Chapter X is available" body) is localized in native but English-only in KMP. The notification channel name shown in Android system settings is also untranslated. Localization regression for the chapter-update notification flow.
- **Suggested fix:** Provide localized strings to the KMP ChapterNotificationHelper (Android string resources or an injected localizer) for the channel name/description and the chapter-available body, matching native's new_chapters / notifications_for_new_manga_chapters / chapter_is_available.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - title maxLines — Manga title maxLines differs (native 1, KMP 2)** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdateItem.kt:78-86 Text(maxLines = 1) for mangaTitle, fontSize = 16.sp explicitly set
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:507-514 Text(maxLines = 2, overflow = TextOverflow.Ellipsis), no explicit fontSize (uses titleMedium default)
- **Explanation:** Native truncates the manga title to a single line; KMP allows two lines before ellipsizing, changing row height for long titles. Native also pins fontSize to 16.sp on top of titleMedium, whereas KMP relies purely on titleMedium's default size, so font sizes may differ slightly depending on the theme's titleMedium definition.
- **Suggested fix:** Set maxLines = 1 on the KMP title Text and apply fontSize = 16.sp to match UpdateItem.kt, or confirm the two-line treatment is an intentional design change.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - chapter number text size — Chapter number explicit fontSize (native 12.sp) not applied in KMP** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdateItem.kt:102-110 chapter Text uses style = bodyMedium with explicit fontSize = 12.sp, maxLines = 1
- **KMP:** Partial - UpdatesScreen.kt:529-535 chapter Text uses style = bodyMedium but no explicit fontSize override; maxLines = 1, overflow Ellipsis
- **Explanation:** Native forces the chapter line to 12.sp on top of bodyMedium; KMP uses bodyMedium's default size. Depending on the theme's bodyMedium size (commonly 14.sp) the KMP chapter label may render larger than native's 12.sp.
- **Suggested fix:** Add fontSize = 12.sp to the KMP chapter-number Text to match native, or verify bodyMedium already resolves to 12.sp in the rework theme.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - read-state dimming — Read-state visual signal differs: native dims opacity only; KMP dims opacity AND changes font weight** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdateItem.kt:83-85 and 107-109 apply Modifier.alpha(if(isRead) 0.4f else 1f) to title and chapter; font weight is unchanged (titleMedium/bodyMedium as-is)
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:466-468 sets titleWeight = if(isRead) FontWeight.Normal else FontWeight.SemiBold AND contentAlpha = if(isRead) 0.4f else 1f applied via color alpha
- **Explanation:** Both dim read rows to 0.4 alpha (KMP applies it via onSurface.copy(alpha) on the text color rather than Modifier.alpha, a near-equivalent). However KMP additionally renders unread titles at SemiBold and read titles at Normal weight, a weight contrast native does not use (native keeps titleMedium weight for both states). Minor extra visual signal in KMP.
- **Suggested fix:** If exact parity is desired, drop the FontWeight switch in UpdatesRowContent so read-state is conveyed by opacity only, matching UpdateItem.kt; otherwise note the weight contrast as an intentional accessibility improvement.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - group header rendering — Group headers are sticky in KMP and plain scrolling items in native; header typography/padding differ** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:113-119 each group header is a plain item { Text(style = titleMedium, padding(16.dp)) } inside a non-sticky LazyColumn
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:337-347 uses stickyHeader with Text(style = titleMedium, fontWeight = SemiBold, background = colorScheme.background, padding(horizontal=16dp, vertical=8dp))
- **Explanation:** Native group headers scroll away with the list and use uniform 16dp padding with no weight override; KMP pins the headers to the top while scrolling (stickyHeader), gives them SemiBold weight and a background fill, and uses asymmetric 16dp/8dp padding. Different scroll behavior and header styling.
- **Suggested fix:** Switch the KMP group header from stickyHeader to a plain item, use padding(16.dp) uniformly, and drop the SemiBold/background to match native, unless sticky headers are an intentional enhancement.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - empty state — KMP shows a centered "No updates yet" empty-state placeholder; native shows nothing (blank list)** _(State)_

- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:299 state.isEmpty -> YamiEmptyState(title = stringResource(Res.string.no_updates)) with no_updates = "No updates yet" (en/ar present)

This is a divergence from the source of truth, though arguably a UX improvement. Flagged because the audit treats every divergence as potential regression.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - loading state — Loading indicator component differs (native LoadingScreen vs KMP YamiLoadingState)** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt(native):108-109 uses LoadingScreen() while uiState.isLoading
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:298 state.isLoading -> YamiLoadingState()
- **Explanation:** Both show a loading state during the initial pre-emission gap (native onStart emits isLoading=true; KMP UpdatesState defaults isLoading=true until first snapshot). The actual loading composables (LoadingScreen vs YamiLoadingState) are different implementations and may differ in spinner style/centering/size. Low impact but a visual divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm YamiLoadingState visually matches the native LoadingScreen (centered CircularProgressIndicator); align spinner color/size if they differ.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - swipe-right on already-read row — Native swipe-right toggles read state (can un-read a read row); KMP gates swipe-right to no-op on read rows** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt(native):128-130 StartToEnd always calls viewModel.markAsRead(notification.chapterId) which maps to markChapterAndNotificationRead = UPDATE ... SET isRead = NOT isRead (a toggle), so swiping a read row marks it unread
- **KMP:** Partial - UpdatesScreen.kt:389 StartToEnd -> if (!entry.isRead) onMarkReadClick(); the guard prevents calling the (toggle) use case on a read row, so a read row cannot be toggled back to unread via swipe
- **Explanation:** Native's swipe-right is an unconditional toggle (because the DAO uses NOT isRead), letting a user swipe a read row to mark it unread again. KMP guards the swipe so it only ever marks unread->read, never read->unread. Functional divergence in the swipe gesture's reversibility, though the KMP behavior is arguably more intuitive.
- **Suggested fix:** Either remove the !entry.isRead guard to restore native's toggle-on-swipe behavior, or document the gating as intentional. Note the underlying use case is still a toggle, so removing the guard restores parity exactly.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - swipe background styling — Swipe reveal background shape/padding/animation differ between native and KMP** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt(native):181-210 swipe background is a full-bleed Row with background(bgColor) + padding(horizontal=20dp), SpaceBetween arrangement, icons at both ends (24dp), animateColorAsState with TweenSpec(300ms, FastOutSlowInEasing)
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:421-455 SwipeBackground is a Box with padding(horizontal=16dp, vertical=4dp) + clip(RoundedCornerShape(12dp)) + background(color) + inner padding(horizontal=24dp), single icon aligned to one edge, animateColorAsState with default spec (no explicit 300ms tween)
- **Explanation:** Native's swipe background fills the row edge-to-edge with 20dp horizontal padding and a 300ms tween, showing a Done icon (start) or Delete icon (end). KMP rounds the background to 12dp corners (to match its card), insets it 16dp/4dp, uses 24dp inner padding, a single edge-aligned icon, and the default (spring) color animation. Different corner shape, insets, and animation timing.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the KMP swipe background to full-bleed (no rounded clip / 4dp inset) and an explicit TweenSpec(300ms, FastOutSlowInEasing) if matching native; otherwise these follow from the Card redesign and can be documented together with it.

**⚪ [Low] Updates top bar - title source — Top-bar title key differs (native title_notifications vs KMP updates)** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt(native):80 title = stringResource(R.string.title_notifications); ar = التحديثات
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:272 Text(stringResource(Res.string.updates)); en = "Updates", ar = التحديثات
- **Explanation:** Both resolve to the same Arabic string (التحديثات) and an English "Updates" equivalent, so user-visible parity holds. Flagged only because the underlying string key changed from title_notifications to updates during migration; if any locale defines title_notifications but not updates the KMP would fall back to English. Both keys are present in their respective catalogs here, so impact is minimal.
- **Suggested fix:** No action required for the shipped locales; ensure the updates key is translated in every locale that title_notifications covered to avoid future fallback gaps.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - cover thumbnail image loader / headers — Native passes an explicit per-source ImageLoader; KMP relies on the singleton loader** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdateItem.kt:61-71 AsyncImage(model = notification.mangaImageUrl, imageLoader = getImageLoader()) explicitly supplying the loader (which carries per-source headers)
- **KMP:** Partial - UpdatesScreen.kt:490-499 AsyncImage(model = entry.mangaImageUrl) with no explicit imageLoader; relies on the app-level setSingletonImageLoaderFactory (per KDoc) to attach the CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor
- **Explanation:** Functionally both should attach per-source request headers (native via getImageLoader(), KMP via the singleton interceptor). This is parity in intent, but the mechanism differs and the KMP correctness depends entirely on the singleton factory being installed with the header interceptor for the Updates host as well. If a cover URL needs a Referer/source header that the singleton interceptor host-matching misses, the native explicit loader could behave differently. Low risk but worth confirming.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify the singleton ImageLoader's CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor host-matches the same set of source hosts that native's getImageLoader() covers for cover thumbnails; add a test or confirm parity for the manga sources used in updates.

**⚪ [Low] Library refresh - empty-library guard message — Native shows a Toast when refresh is tapped with an empty library; KMP refresh has no such guard** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryRoute.kt:183-197 onRefreshLibrary checks items.isNullOrEmpty() and shows Toast "No manga in your library yet!" instead of enqueuing
- **KMP:** No - RefreshLibraryUseCase.kt:50 invoke() is an unconditional repository.refresh() pass-through (KDoc even notes "future" gating could live here but does not exist); the worker itself handles the empty case internally by posting a "No manga to refresh" notification rather than a UI Toast
- **Explanation:** Native short-circuits at the UI layer when the library is empty, giving immediate feedback ("No manga in your library yet!") and skipping the worker entirely. KMP always schedules the worker; the worker then walks zero manga and posts a background "No manga to refresh" notification. The user gets no immediate in-app feedback and an unnecessary foreground service spins up. Minor UX divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an empty-library check before invoking refresh in the KMP LibraryViewModel/refresh handler (or in RefreshLibraryUseCase) and surface a snackbar/toast equivalent to native's message instead of scheduling an empty refresh.

**⚪ [Low] Library refresh - notification channel name string — KMP refresh worker creates the channel with a hardcoded display name that doesn't match native's resource, but the channel ID matches** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryRefreshWorker.kt(native):72-77 channel name from R.string.notification_channel_library_refresh ("Library refresh"/"تحديث المكتبة"), CHANNEL_ID = "library_refresh"
- **KMP:** Partial - app/.../work/LibraryRefreshWorker.kt:86-91 channel name hardcoded "Library refresh updates", description "Shows progress of background library refresh", same CHANNEL_ID = "library_refresh"
- **Explanation:** The channel ID is identical (library_refresh) so behavior is consistent, but the user-facing channel name in system settings differs ("Library refresh updates" hardcoded English in KMP vs localized "Library refresh"/"تحديث المكتبة" in native). Because Android caches the channel by ID on first creation, the name/description also won't update on existing installs. Cosmetic + localization.
- **Suggested fix:** Localize the channel name/description to match native's R.string.notification_channel_library_refresh / _desc; covered by the broader refresh-notification localization fix.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - download affordance idle/done icon parity — Idle/done download affordances match icons but native uses a 48dp IconButton with tinted states; KMP IconButton defaults** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdateItem.kt:124-136 IconButton(size 48dp, enabled = !isDownloaded) with Icons.Default.DownloadDone (downloaded, tint primary) or Icons.Default.Download (tint onSurface @0.7 alpha)
- **KMP:** Partial - UpdatesScreen.kt:570-582 DONE -> disabled IconButton(DownloadDone, default tint), IDLE -> IconButton(Download, default tint); no explicit 48dp size, no primary/0.7-alpha tinting
- **Explanation:** Both use Download/DownloadDone icons with the running/queued spinner states correctly ported (RUNNING primary, QUEUED onPrimary, matching native UpdateItem.kt:118). However native tints the done icon primary and the idle icon onSurface@0.7, and sizes the button 48dp; KMP uses default IconButton tint (onSurface full) and default size. Subtle tint/size divergence on the trailing affordance.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply tint = primary to the DONE icon and onSurface.copy(alpha=0.7f) to the IDLE icon, and set the IconButton size to 48dp, matching UpdateItem.kt.

**⚪ [Low] Updates feed - cover thumbnail size parity — Thumbnail size matches (50dp/8dp corners) but row leading padding differs** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes - UpdateItem.kt:64-71 AsyncImage size 50dp, clip RoundedCornerShape(8dp), background surfaceVariant; Column padding(start = 16dp)
- **KMP:** Yes - UpdatesScreen.kt:489-501 AsyncImage size 50.dp, clip RoundedCornerShape(8dp), background surfaceVariant; then Spacer(width = spacing.md) before the Column
- **Explanation:** The cover thumbnail (50dp, 8dp corners, surfaceVariant fallback) is a faithful port (KMP KDoc GAP-UPD-02 confirms the intentional match). The gap between cover and text is native's fixed 16dp (Column padding start) vs KMP's spacing.md token (LocalSpacing) which may or may not equal 16dp. Verify spacing.md == 16dp; if it differs the horizontal rhythm changes slightly.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm LocalSpacing.md resolves to 16dp; if not, use a fixed 16dp gap to match native's Column start padding.

</details>

### Notifications Center  `notifications-center`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 24 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡5 ⚪16)

> The native "notifications" feature (MVVM NotificationsViewModel + NotificationRepository over the Room `notifications` table) is fully ported to the KMP "updates" MVI slice (UpdatesScreen + UpdatesViewModel + UpdateEntry + UpdatesRepositoryImpl), reachable via the same Screen.Updates bottom-nav tab. Core behaviors are present in both: list grouped into Today/Yesterday/Last Week/Older with within-bucket descending chapter-number sort, swipe-right mark-read, swipe-left delete-with-undo snackbar, per-row download affordance with queued/running spinners, mark-all-read and delete-all top-bar actions, unread dot + 0.4-alpha dimming, and identical reader/details navigation arg mapping. However several real divergences exist. The two highest-impact regressions: (1) KMP renders the raw chapterNumber with no localized "Chapter %1$s" prefix, and (2) tapping a row to open the chapter no longer marks the notification read (native did markAsRead-then-navigate). Localization regressed broadly — the :ui catalog ships only en+ar and even Arabic is missing the notifications_group_* date headers, where native localizes all strings across 11 languages. Cosmetic divergences include card-wrapped rows vs native flat rows, a stock Material3 top bar ("Updates", default style) vs native's 24sp-Bold "Notification" bar, text-button vs icon-button top actions, sticky vs inline headers, missing list animations, and an added empty-state native lacks. There is also a redundant double date-grouping (data layer + :ui) with a subtle 7-days-ago boundary / dual-"today" correctness smell. Bottom-nav badge count is absent in both (parity).

**🟠 [High] Notifications/Updates screen — chapter number rendering — Native prefixes chapter number with localized "Chapter %1$s" template; KMP renders the raw chapterNumber string with no prefix** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdateItem.kt:102-110 renders Text(text = stringResource(R.string.chapter_number, notification.chapterNumber)); R.string.chapter_number = "Chapter %1$s" (values/strings.xml:101) with 11 localized variants (e.g. Arabic "الفصل %1$s", Japanese "第%1$s話")
- **KMP:** No — UpdatesScreen.kt:529-535 renders Text(text = entry.chapterNumber) verbatim, no template, no "Chapter" prefix. The chapter_number format key does not exist in the :ui catalog (it only lives in composeApp/ for other screens, unused here)
- **Explanation:** The chapterNumber field stores only the raw number (ChapterNotificationHelper.kt:104 sets chapterNumber = chapter.number, e.g. "72" or "12.5"). Native therefore shows "Chapter 72" (localized per device language). KMP shows just "72" with no word "Chapter" and no localization. This is a visible content + i18n regression: the row's secondary line loses its descriptive label entirely in every language.
- **Suggested fix:** Render the chapter label via a localized template (add/reuse a chapter_number "Chapter %1$s" key in the :ui catalog with all locale variants) so the KMP row shows "Chapter <n>" matching native. Do not implement now — just restore the templated, localized label.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth): UpdateItem.kt:102-110 renders Text(text = stringResource(R.string.chapter_number, notification.chapterNumber)) — applies the "Chapter %1$s" template. values/strings.xml:101 = `<string name="chapter_number">Chapter %1$s</string>`; values-ar/strings.xml:103 = "الفصل %1$s"; values-ja/strings.xml:96 = "第%1$s話"; verified 11 res/values-* files contain name="chapter_number" (matches claimed 11 localized variants). ChapterNotificationHelper.kt:104 sets chapterNumber = chapter.number (raw number, e.g. "72"/"12.5"), so native displays a localized "Chapter <n>". KMP: ui/.../updates/UpdatesScreen.kt:529-535 renders Text(text = entry.chapterNumber) verbatim — no template, no "Chapter" prefix. The screen resolves strings from the :ui catalog (imports me.manga.kira.ui.generated.resources.Res, stringResource at lines 232/272/278/284/299/339/444/449/573/579). grep for "chapter_number" across the entire /ui module returns ZERO matches — the key is absent from ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/values/strings.xml; it only lives in composeApp/src/commonMain/composeResources/values/strings.xml:101 ("Chapter %1$s"), a different module not used here. DATA PARITY: KMP UpdateEntry.chapterNumber (domain/.../UpdateEntry.kt:122-123) is documented "Chapter number / display label as the source reported it" and is a passthrough (data/.../UpdateMappers.kt:43,60 chapterNumber = chapterNumber; shared/.../HandelDataClasses.kt chapterNumber = this.number), mirroring native's raw chapter.number. So both apps hold the same raw value; native adds the localized "Chapter" label, KMP does not. Claim is accurate in every cited detail.

**🟠 [High] Notifications/Updates screen — tap-to-read marks notification read — Native marks a notification as read when the user taps the row to open the chapter; KMP only navigates and does NOT mark as read** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:217-220 onNotificationClick = { viewModel.markAsRead(it.chapterId); onNotificationClick(it) } — the row body tap flips the read flag (and the cross-table saved_chapters flag) before navigating
- **KMP:** No — UpdatesViewModel.kt:177 OnChapterClick -> emit(UpdatesEffect.NavigateToReader(intent.entry)); the row-body tap only navigates. markUpdateAsRead is only invoked from OnMarkAsRead (the explicit per-row/swipe action), never on chapter open
- **Explanation:** In native, opening a chapter from the notification list automatically clears its unread state (the blue dot disappears, opacity dims, and the underlying saved_chapters.isRead toggles). In KMP, after opening and reading a chapter the notification stays unread forever unless the user separately swipes-right or taps a mark-read affordance. This breaks the core read-tracking expectation and leaves stale unread indicators after the user has clearly consumed the chapter.
- **Suggested fix:** In the KMP OnChapterClick handler, invoke markUpdateAsRead(entry) (fire-and-forget) before/alongside emitting NavigateToReader, mirroring native's markAsRead-then-navigate sequence.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — row-body tap marks the notification read before navigating. /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/notifications/ui/screens/UpdatesScreen.kt:215-220 wires the row content's `onNotificationClick = { viewModel.markAsRead(it.chapterId); onNotificationClick(it) }`. NotificationsViewModel.markAsRead (same path .../ui/viewmodel/NotificationsViewModel.kt:56-58) calls repo.markAsRead, and NotificationRepository.markAsRead (.../notifications/domain/NotificationRepository.kt:26-27) calls libraryDeo.markChapterAndNotificationRead(id). That native LibraryDeo @Transaction flips BOTH tables: `UPDATE saved_chapters SET isRead = NOT isRead WHERE id` + `UPDATE notifications SET isRead = NOT isRead WHERE chapterId` (NotificationDao.kt:140-149 mirrors it). So the cross-table claim is accurate. KMP — row-body tap only navigates. UI: /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/updates/UpdatesScreen.kt:469-473 the row Card uses `.clickable(onClick = onChapterClick)`, and UpdatesList wires `onChapterClick = { onIntent(UpdatesIntent.OnChapterClick(entry)) }` (line 354). The VM handles it as navigation-only: /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/updates/UpdatesViewModel.kt:177 `is UpdatesIntent.OnChapterClick -> emit(UpdatesEffect.NavigateToReader(intent.entry))`. The route (UpdatesReworkScreenRoute.kt:130-147) only navigates to the reader. markUpdateAsRead is invoked ONLY from OnMarkAsRead (UpdatesViewModel.kt:159-161), which the UI dispatches solely from the swipe-right gesture (UpdatesScreen.kt:389 `StartToEnd -> if (!entry.isRead) onMarkReadClick()` → line 356 OnMarkAsRead), plus the top-bar "Mark all read". Independent-state check confirms the user-visible regression is real: in BOTH apps `isRead` is a STORED column on the `notifications` table (native getAllNotifications `SELECT * FROM notifications`, NotificationDao.kt:33; KMP UpdateMappers.kt:46 maps entity.isRead straight to UpdateEntry.isRead; UpdatesRepositoryImpl.observeUpdates maps the same DAO flow, .../data/repository/UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:137-142). In KMP the ONLY writers of notifications.isRead are LibraryDeo.markNotificationReadInternal (UPDATE notifications SET isRead = NOT isRead, shared/.../LibraryDeo.kt:88-89, reached only via markAsRead) and NotificationDao.markAllAsRead (shared/.../NotificationDao.kt:88). Reading a chapter in the KMP reader runs ChapterDao.markChapterAsRead = `UPDATE saved_chapters SET isRead = 1 ... WHERE id` (shared/.../ChapterDao.kt:104-105) — it touches ONLY saved_chapters, never the notifications row, and there is no FK/join propagation. So after opening+reading a chapter from the Updates list, the KMP notification's stored isRead stays 0 (blue dot + full opacity persist) until the user separately swipes-right or hits Mark-all-read — exactly as claimed.

**🟠 [High] Notifications/Updates screen — date group header localization (Arabic + other locales) — Native ships notifications_group_today/yesterday/last_week/older in 11 locales; KMP :ui catalog ships these keys in en only (Arabic + 9 other locales fall back to English)** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — values/strings.xml:93-96 + values-ar/-fr/-de/-es/-in/-pt/-ja/-ru/-it/-tr all define notifications_group_today/yesterday/last_week/older (e.g. ar: اليوم/أمس/الأسبوع الماضي/أقدم)

- **Explanation:** The KMP :ui module ships only two locales (values, values-ar) and the date-group header keys are absent even from values-ar. So on Arabic devices the Updates screen shows English headers "Today/Yesterday/Last Week/Older" instead of the Arabic اليوم/أمس/الأسبوع الماضي/أقدم that native shows. The other 9 native locales (fr, de, es, in, pt, ja, ru, it, tr) are not present in the :ui catalog at all, so all of them regress to English on this screen. This is a broad localization regression versus the source of truth.
