Dependency is composeApp -> :ui (composeApp/build.gradle.kts:68 implementation(project(":ui"))); :ui does NOT depend on composeApp (ui/build.gradle.kts only api(project(":presentation"))). Compose Multiplatform generates per-module resource bundles that are NOT merged across modules, so the composeApp Arabic/other-locale translations are unreachable from the :ui UpdatesScreen's Res. The regression is real, but the claim's statement that the 9 other locales "are not present in the :ui catalog at all" overstates absence — they exist in the repo (composeApp) but are dead for this screen due to module resource isolation, not truly missing.

**🟡 [Medium] Notifications/Updates screen — top app bar title — Native top bar title uses R.string.title_notifications ("Notification") at 24sp Bold; KMP uses Res.string.updates ("Updates") with default Material titleLarge weight** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:79-80 TopAppBarCom(title = stringResource(R.string.title_notifications)); TopAppBarCom.kt:22-39 sets titleSize = 24.sp, fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold, style titleLarge.copy(fontSize=24.sp), textColor = onBackground, containerColor = background. title_notifications = "Notification" (values/strings.xml:6)
- **KMP:** Partial — UpdatesScreen.kt:271-272 TopAppBar(title = { Text(stringResource(Res.string.updates)) }); Res.string.updates = "Updates" (ui values/strings.xml:124). Uses stock Material3 TopAppBar default title style (titleLarge, ~22sp, Medium weight) and default surface container color, not the 24sp Bold background-colored bar
- **Explanation:** Two divergences: (1) the title text differs — native says "Notification" while KMP says "Updates" (note the bottom-nav label is title_notifications in BOTH apps, so KMP's screen title "Updates" is inconsistent with its own tab label); (2) typography differs — native forces 24sp Bold on a background-colored bar via TopAppBarCom, KMP uses the unstyled Material3 default (smaller, Medium weight, default surface tint). Visible header size/weight and copy mismatch.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native: use the screen's notifications title string and apply 24sp Bold title styling with background container color (port the TopAppBarCom styling). Reconcile the title vs bottom-tab label copy.

**🟡 [Medium] Notifications/Updates screen — Delete-all / Mark-all-read top bar actions — Native uses two IconButtons (DeleteSweep, DoneAll); KMP uses two text TextButtons ("Clear all", "Mark all read")** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:82-93: IconButton{Icon(Icons.Default.DeleteSweep, contentDescription=delete_all)} and IconButton{Icon(Icons.Default.DoneAll, contentDescription=mark_all_as_read)}. Order: DeleteSweep first, then DoneAll
- **KMP:** Partial — UpdatesScreen.kt:273-286: TextButton("Mark all read") then TextButton("Clear all", color = error). Labelled text buttons, no icons; order reversed (mark-all first, clear-all second)
- **Explanation:** Native presents compact glyph-only icon buttons (DeleteSweep, DoneAll) with localized content descriptions; KMP presents wide labelled text buttons with the error color applied only to "Clear all". The action order is also swapped (native: delete, then mark-read; KMP: mark-read, then clear). This is a noticeable toolbar layout/affordance divergence — text buttons consume more horizontal space and read differently. The KMP screen KDoc itself acknowledges the icon conversion was deferred (UP-2/UP-4).
- **Suggested fix:** Convert the two top-bar actions to IconButtons using DeleteSweep + DoneAll glyphs with localized content descriptions, and restore native ordering (delete-all first, mark-all-read second).

**🟡 [Medium] Notifications/Updates screen — row container styling (Card vs flat Row) — Native renders each notification as a flat clickable Row (no card, no surface); KMP wraps each row in an elevated-style Card with surfaceVariant background and 12dp rounded corners** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdateItem.kt:54-60 Row(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().clickable{...}.padding(horizontal=16dp, vertical=8dp)) — no Card, transparent background, full-bleed row
- **KMP:** No (divergent) — UpdatesScreen.kt:469-478 Card(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(horizontal=16dp, vertical=4dp).clickable, colors=cardColors(containerColor=surfaceVariant), shape=RoundedCornerShape(12dp)) wrapping an inner Row with padding(spacing.md)
- **Explanation:** Native rows are flat list items separated only by spacing on a plain background, edge-to-edge with 16dp horizontal / 8dp vertical padding. KMP rows are individually boxed Cards with a surfaceVariant fill, 12dp corners, and 16dp/4dp outer padding plus internal md padding. This produces a materially different list aesthetic (card list vs flat list), different background color behind each item, and different inter-item spacing.
- **Suggested fix:** Drop the Card wrapper and render a flat clickable Row with transparent background and horizontal=16dp/vertical=8dp padding to match native, or confirm the card treatment is an intended redesign.

**🟡 [Medium] Notifications/Updates screen — date-grouping LAST_WEEK boundary edge case — Native LAST_WEEK uses isAfter(today-7) AND isBefore(yesterday), excluding exactly 7-days-ago; KMP uses days in 2..6 (also excludes 7) but the OLDER boundary handling differs subtly at the today-7 day** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — NotificationRepository.kt:57-60 lastWeekList = filter { date.isAfter(lastWeek=today-7) && date.isBefore(yesterday) }; olderList = filter { date.isBefore(lastWeek=today-7) }. A date exactly == today-7 falls into NEITHER lastWeek (not after today-7) NOR older (not before today-7) — it is dropped from all buckets
- **KMP:** Partial — UpdatesScreen.kt:613-620 bucketFor: days<=0 TODAY, days==1 YESTERDAY, days in 2..6 LAST_WEEK, else OLDER. A date exactly 7 days ago (days==7) → OLDER (else branch). KMP also has a second groupByDate in UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:184-189 using date>lastWeek && date<yesterday / date<lastWeek which matches native's drop-at-7 behavior
- **Explanation:** There are TWO groupings in KMP and they disagree at the 7-days-ago boundary. UpdatesRepositoryImpl.groupByDate (data layer) faithfully ports native: a notification dated exactly 7 days ago is dropped (filtered out of every bucket) because it's neither >today-7 nor <today-7. But the :ui groupByRecency (UpdatesScreen.kt) re-buckets the flat list with days in 2..6 → LAST_WEEK / else → OLDER, so a 7-days-ago entry lands in OLDER. Since the data layer already flat-maps (and drops the 7-day entry), the :ui regroup operates on an already-filtered list — but if any entry survives at exactly the boundary the two layers compute different buckets. The double-grouping is redundant and the boundary semantics aren't guaranteed identical to native across both layers.
- **Suggested fix:** Consolidate to a single grouping. Verify the boundary (exactly today-7) is handled identically to native (native silently drops it). Prefer reusing the data-layer groupByDate result rather than re-bucketing in :ui to avoid divergent boundary logic.

**🟡 [Medium] Notifications/Updates screen — action label localization (Updates/Mark read/Clear all/Undo/etc.) — KMP-only strings (updates, mark_all_read, mark_read, clear_all, no_updates, update_deleted, undo, download, downloaded, delete) are localized only in en + ar; native equivalents are localized in 11 locales** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — the native screen's strings (title_notifications, contentDescription_delete_all, contentDescription_mark_all_as_read, chapter_number) are localized in all 11 locales
- **KMP:** Partial — ui values/strings.xml defines updates/mark_all_read/mark_read/clear_all/no_updates/update_deleted/undo (lines 122-136) and values-ar/strings.xml provides Arabic (lines 264-279); but the :ui catalog has only values + values-ar dirs — fr/de/es/in/pt/ja/ru/it/tr are missing entirely
- **Explanation:** All Updates-screen UI labels in KMP exist only in English and Arabic. On any of the 9 other languages native supports, the KMP Updates screen shows English action labels and snackbar copy. This compounds the date-header localization regression and means the entire screen is effectively bilingual (en/ar) where native is multilingual (11 languages).
- **Suggested fix:** Provide the full set of locale catalogs for the :ui module covering all 11 native languages for the Updates strings, or confirm the :ui localization scope is deliberately reduced.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — manga title maxLines & font size — Native title: titleMedium at fixed 16sp, maxLines = 1; KMP title: titleMedium (no fixed size), maxLines = 2 with ellipsis** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdateItem.kt:78-86 Text(notification.mangaTitle, style=titleMedium, fontSize=16.sp, maxLines=1)
- **KMP:** No (divergent) — UpdatesScreen.kt:507-514 Text(entry.mangaTitle, style=titleMedium, fontWeight=titleWeight, maxLines=2, overflow=Ellipsis); no explicit 16sp override (uses titleMedium default ~16sp but unpinned)
- **Explanation:** Native clamps the manga title to a single line at exactly 16sp. KMP allows two lines and does not pin 16sp. Long titles wrap to two lines in KMP but truncate to one in native, changing row height and vertical rhythm. Minor but a real layout divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Set maxLines = 1 on the KMP title and pin fontSize = 16.sp to match native single-line behavior, or confirm 2-line wrap is intended.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — read-state visual signal (title weight) — Native signals read state ONLY via 0.4 alpha on title + chapter text (title weight constant); KMP signals read state via BOTH 0.4 alpha AND font-weight change (SemiBold unread / Normal read)** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdateItem.kt:83-85 and 107-109 apply Modifier.alpha(if isRead 0.4f else 1f) to title and chapter texts; title weight is always titleMedium default (no weight toggle)
- **KMP:** Partial — UpdatesScreen.kt:466-468 titleWeight = if(isRead) Normal else SemiBold and contentAlpha = if(isRead) 0.4f else 1f; both weight and alpha vary
- **Explanation:** Both apps dim read rows to 0.4 alpha (parity on that). But KMP additionally bolds unread titles to SemiBold and de-bolds read titles to Normal, a weight signal native does not use (native keeps titleMedium's default weight regardless of read state). Subtle but a divergence in the read/unread visual treatment.
- **Suggested fix:** Remove the font-weight toggle (keep a constant titleMedium weight) so the only read-state signal is the 0.4 alpha + unread dot, matching native; or confirm the added weight emphasis is intentional.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — group header (sticky vs inline) — Native date-group headers are plain inline list items; KMP headers are stickyHeader items with a background and SemiBold weight, different padding** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:113-119 item { Text(stringResource(labelRes), style=titleMedium, Modifier.padding(16.dp)) } — non-sticky, 16dp padding all sides, default titleMedium weight, no background
- **KMP:** No (divergent) — UpdatesScreen.kt:337-347 stickyHeader { Text(..., style=titleMedium, fontWeight=SemiBold, color=onBackground, Modifier.fillMaxWidth().background(background).padding(horizontal=16dp, vertical=8dp)) }
- **Explanation:** Native headers scroll away with content and use a uniform 16dp padding with default weight. KMP headers stick to the top while scrolling, are SemiBold, fill width with an explicit background fill, and use 16dp horizontal / 8dp vertical padding. The sticky behavior and weight/padding differences are visible during scroll.
- **Suggested fix:** Use a non-sticky item header with 16dp uniform padding and default titleMedium weight (no background fill) to match native, or confirm sticky headers are an intended improvement.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — list animations — Native LazyColumn uses animateContentSize() and per-item animateItem()+animateContentSize(); KMP list has no content/item animations** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:111 LazyColumn(Modifier.animateContentSize()); 164-167 SwipeToDismissBox(Modifier.fillMaxWidth().animateItem().animateContentSize())
- **KMP:** No — UpdatesScreen.kt:332-334 LazyColumn(Modifier.fillMaxSize(), contentPadding=PaddingValues(bottom=8.dp)); UpdatesRow SwipeToDismissBox(Modifier.fillMaxWidth()) — no animateContentSize or animateItem modifiers
- **Explanation:** Native animates list-size changes and per-item placement/removal (e.g. when a row is deleted or marked read, the list smoothly resizes and items animate). KMP removes/adds rows without these animations, so deletions and re-groupings snap rather than animate. Subtle motion-design regression.
- **Suggested fix:** Add Modifier.animateContentSize() to the KMP LazyColumn and Modifier.animateItem() to each row item to restore native's animated insert/remove/resize behavior.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — swipe background layout & icon set — Native swipe background spans full width with both leading+trailing icon slots (SpaceBetween, Outlined Done/Delete, 20dp horiz padding, 24dp icons); KMP uses a clipped rounded background aligned to one edge with Filled Done/Delete and different padding** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:181-210 Row(fillMaxSize().background(bgColor).padding(horizontal=20.dp), SpaceBetween) showing Icons.Outlined.Done (StartToEnd, tint primary, size 24dp) at start and Icons.Outlined.Delete (EndToStart, tint error, 24dp) at end, with Spacer(24dp) placeholders; 300ms Tween FastOutSlowIn color animation
- **KMP:** Partial — UpdatesScreen.kt:421-455 SwipeBackground: Box(fillMaxSize().padding(horizontal=16dp, vertical=4dp).clip(RoundedCornerShape(12dp)).background(color).padding(horizontal=24dp)) aligned CenterStart/CenterEnd, Icons.Filled.Done / Icons.Filled.Delete; animateColorAsState default spec (not 300ms FastOutSlowIn)
- **Explanation:** Native paints the reveal edge-to-edge (full bleed) with 20dp horizontal padding, uses Outlined icon variants, and a deliberate 300ms FastOutSlowInEasing tween. KMP clips the reveal into a 12dp rounded rectangle inset by 16dp/4dp (to match its Card shape), uses Filled icon variants, 24dp inner padding, and the default color-animation spec. The reveal shape, icon style, padding, and animation timing all differ.
- **Suggested fix:** Use a full-bleed swipe background with 20dp horizontal padding, Outlined Done/Delete icons, and a 300ms FastOutSlowInEasing color tween to match native (this depends on also dropping the Card per the row-container finding).

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — error state rendering — Native renders an inline error message (red text at top of the list area) from uiState.errorMessage; KMP UpdatesScreen has no error state at all** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:98-106 uiState.errorMessage?.let { Text(error, color=colorScheme.error, Modifier.fillMaxWidth().padding(16.dp)) }; NotificationsViewModel.kt:40-49 .catch{} populates errorMessage from e.localizedMessage
- **KMP:** No — UpdatesState.kt has no error field (KDoc lines 49-55 explicitly justify omitting it); UpdatesScreen.kt:297-304 only branches on isLoading / isEmpty / list. The ShowError EFFECT exists but is only fired on download-enqueue failure, not on list-load failure, and renders as a transient snackbar not an inline message
- **Explanation:** Native has a dedicated inline error surface for the list flow (catch block + red error text). KMP intentionally drops it, reasoning the Room flow doesn't throw at the observe site. In practice the observe upstream is the same Room flow in both, so the divergence is low-risk, but it is a removed state surface relative to the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** If list-flow errors are truly impossible this is acceptable; otherwise add an error branch to UpdatesState + an inline error Text to fully mirror native. At minimum document the deliberate omission.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — empty state — Native has NO empty-state UI (empty list shows a blank area); KMP shows a centered YamiEmptyState with icon + "No updates yet"** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — UpdatesScreen.kt never renders an empty placeholder; when groupedNotifications is empty the LazyColumn simply renders nothing (blank), and the top-bar actions are disabled
- **KMP:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:299 state.isEmpty -> YamiEmptyState(title = stringResource(Res.string.no_updates)); YamiStateViews.kt:76-119 shows a 64dp muted icon + titleMedium title centered
- **Explanation:** KMP ADDS an empty-state placeholder (icon + "No updates yet") that native does not have. This is arguably an improvement, but it is a divergence from the source of truth: native shows a blank screen on empty, KMP shows an illustrated empty state. Worth noting for strict parity; the new no_updates string is also only localized in en + ar.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm the added empty state is an intended enhancement; if strict parity is required, either remove it or accept the divergence and ensure no_updates is fully localized across all native locales.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — loading indicator color/padding — Native LoadingScreen uses CircularProgressIndicator tinted colorScheme.inversePrimary inside a 16dp-padded centered Box; KMP YamiLoadingState uses a default-tinted spinner with no padding** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — LoadingScreen.kt:18-30 CircularProgressIndicator(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.inversePrimary) in Box(fillMaxSize().padding(16.dp), contentAlignment=Center)
- **KMP:** Partial — YamiStateViews.kt:55-63 YamiLoadingState: Column(fillMaxSize(), Center) { CircularProgressIndicator() } — default primary tint, no 16dp padding
- **Explanation:** Native's loading spinner is explicitly tinted inversePrimary and padded 16dp; KMP's shared loading state uses the default (primary) tint and no padding. The spinner color differs (inversePrimary vs primary) and the surrounding inset differs. Minor cosmetic divergence on the loading state.
- **Suggested fix:** Tint the KMP loading spinner with inversePrimary and add 16dp padding to match native, or accept the shared YamiLoadingState styling as the new standard.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — date-grouping uses different 'today' resolution between layers — KMP computes 'today' twice (data layer via Clock.System.todayIn; :ui via Clock.System.now().toLocalDateTime().date) which can disagree across a midnight boundary; native computes LocalDate.now() once** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — NotificationRepository.kt:48-50 today/yesterday/lastWeek all derived once from LocalDate.now() in the single grouping pass
- **KMP:** Partial — data layer UpdatesRepositoryImpl.kt:177 today = Clock.System.todayIn(...); ui layer UpdatesScreen.kt:600-601 today = Clock.System.now().toLocalDateTime(...).date. Two independent 'now' reads at different times/layers
- **Explanation:** Because KMP buckets the same data twice with two independently-sampled 'today' values (once in :data flatMap-ordering, once in :ui regroup), a notification observed exactly around midnight could be ordered by one 'today' but headered by another. Native samples once so its sort order and header always agree. Low likelihood but a correctness smell introduced by the redundant double-grouping.
- **Suggested fix:** Remove the redundant :ui regrouping and rely on the data-layer grouping (single 'today' sample), or pass a single 'today' through to both, matching native's single-sample semantics.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — effects collector keyed on Flow reference — KMP LaunchedEffect(effects) keys the collector on the effects Flow instance; native keys nothing (snackbar launched directly from confirmValueChange)** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:134-153 the undo snackbar is launched inside confirmValueChange via scope.launch{} directly; no LaunchedEffect keyed on a flow
- **KMP:** Partial — UpdatesScreen.kt:235-266 LaunchedEffect(effects) { effects.collect {...} }. Keying on the Flow reference is fragile: if viewModel.effects returns a new Flow instance per recomposition the collector restarts; conventionally these are keyed on Unit/true
- **Explanation:** Keying LaunchedEffect on the effects Flow is a code-smell relative to the usual key=Unit pattern. If MviViewModel.effects is a stable property it is harmless, but if it ever returns a fresh cold Flow per access the effect would re-launch on every recomposition (double-collecting) or miss emissions. Native sidesteps the issue by not using a flow-collector at all. Worth verifying effects is a stable SharedFlow.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm viewModel.effects is a stable hot flow (SharedFlow) reference; if so, key the LaunchedEffect on Unit/true for clarity, matching the sibling History/Library screens' convention.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — per-row download spinner QUEUED tint — Both tint a running download's spinner primary and a queued/other spinner onPrimary, but native's condition is structured differently and only ever shows onPrimary as a fallback; KMP has explicit QUEUED vs RUNNING states** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdateItem.kt:113-122 shows CircularProgressIndicator when chapterId is in downloadingChapters OR == runningChapter.chapterId, tint = if (runningChapter != null && chapterId == runningChapter.chapterId) primary else onPrimary, size 24dp strokeWidth 2dp
- **KMP:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:559-569 RUNNING -> spinner primary; QUEUED -> spinner onPrimary; both 24dp/2dp. State derived in UpdatesState.downloadStatusFor (RUNNING/COMPRESSING→RUNNING, QUEUED→QUEUED, SUCCESS→DONE, etc.)
- **Explanation:** Functionally close to parity (running=primary, queued=onPrimary, 24dp/2dp). The derivation differs: native keys off two raw lists (downloadingChapters + runningChapter) while KMP maps a unified DownloadedChapter.state enum including COMPRESSING→RUNNING and FAILED handling that native doesn't model on this row. Edge states (COMPRESSING, FAILED) render differently than native, which only knows queued/running. Minor.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify the COMPRESSING and FAILED mappings produce native-equivalent visuals (native would show onPrimary spinner for any non-running queued chapter and a download icon otherwise); align if needed.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — download-done icon tint — Native tints the DownloadDone icon primary and the Download icon onSurface@0.7 alpha; KMP uses default IconButton/Icon tint for both** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdateItem.kt:129-135 Icon(if isDownloaded DownloadDone else Download, tint = if isDownloaded primary else onSurface.copy(alpha=0.7f)); the IconButton is enabled only when !isDownloaded
- **KMP:** Partial — UpdatesScreen.kt:570-582 DONE -> IconButton(enabled=false){Icon(DownloadDone)} with NO explicit tint; IDLE -> IconButton{Icon(Download)} with NO explicit tint (both inherit default LocalContentColor / disabled alpha)
- **Explanation:** Native explicitly tints the done state primary (a clear 'downloaded' accent) and the idle download icon at 70% onSurface. KMP relies on default icon tint plus the disabled-state alpha for DONE, so the downloaded icon is greyed (disabled) rather than primary-accented, and the idle icon is full onSurface rather than 0.7 alpha. The download affordance reads differently (no primary accent on done).
- **Suggested fix:** Tint the DownloadDone icon with colorScheme.primary and the idle Download icon with onSurface at 0.7 alpha to match native's accent semantics.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — cover thumbnail ImageLoader/header handling — Native passes an explicit getImageLoader() to AsyncImage (per-source header interceptor); KMP relies on the singleton ImageLoader set globally** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdateItem.kt:61-71 AsyncImage(model=mangaImageUrl, imageLoader=getImageLoader(), size 50dp, clip RoundedCornerShape(8dp), background surfaceVariant, ContentScale.Crop)
- **KMP:** Partial — UpdatesScreen.kt:490-499 AsyncImage(model=mangaImageUrl, contentScale=Crop, 50dp, clip 8dp, background surfaceVariant) — no explicit imageLoader; depends on setSingletonImageLoaderFactory in App.kt carrying the CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor
- **Explanation:** Both render a 50dp ContentScale.Crop thumbnail with 8dp corners and surfaceVariant background (good parity on geometry). The header/anti-bot handling differs in mechanism: native injects a per-call image loader with source headers; KMP relies on a global singleton interceptor. If the global interceptor's host-matching doesn't cover a source the native per-source loader handles, cover images could fail to load on the Updates screen for some sources. Needs verification that the singleton interceptor reaches host parity.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify the singleton CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor attaches the same per-source headers native's getImageLoader() does for all sources; otherwise covers may 403/fail on the KMP Updates rows.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications center — unread badge count on bottom-nav tab — Neither native nor KMP shows an unread badge on the Updates/Notifications bottom-nav tab** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** No — BottomNavigationBar.kt (native) uses NavigationBarItem with icon Icons.Default.Notifications and contentDescription=null; no BadgedBox/Badge; NotificationDao.countAll() exists but is not wired to the tab
- **KMP:** No — composeApp BottomNavigationBar.kt:129-150 NavigationBarItem with Icons.Default.Notifications, no badge
- **Explanation:** The task brief lists badge counts as in-scope. Confirmed: neither implementation displays an unread-count badge on the Updates tab (native exposes NotificationDao.countAll() / getUnreadNotifications() but does not surface a badge in the bottom bar). So there is parity here (both absent) — documented to close the badge-count investigation. No regression.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix required for parity. If a badge is ever desired it would be a new feature in both apps, not a migration gap.

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — leftover debug log on undo path — Native leaves a stray Log.i with a garbage tag on the swipe-delete path; KMP does not (KMP is cleaner here)** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:146 Log.i("asfadfasdgasfgfdgdgdfgdfsgdf", result.toString()) inside the undo snackbar coroutine
- **KMP:** No — UpdatesScreen.kt effect collector (235-266) has no debug logging on the undo path
- **Explanation:** This is a case where the native source-of-truth contains a debug-grade defect (a stray Log.i with a nonsense tag) that the KMP rewrite correctly omitted. Not a KMP regression — noted for completeness so it isn't mistaken as missing behavior the KMP must replicate. The KMP behavior is preferable here.
- **Suggested fix:** No action for KMP. (Native could remove the stray log, but that is outside the KMP parity scope.)

**⚪ [Low] Notifications/Updates screen — Scaffold inner padding application — Native applies only the top padding of the scaffold inset (ignores others via SuppressLint) and no background; KMP applies full padding(padding) and a background fill** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — UpdatesScreen.kt:97 Box(Modifier.padding(top = paddingValues.calculateTopPadding())) — only top inset applied; @SuppressLint("UnusedMaterial3ScaffoldPaddingParameter"); no background on the content box
- **KMP:** No (divergent) — UpdatesScreen.kt:291-295 Box(Modifier.fillMaxSize().padding(padding).background(colorScheme.background)) — full scaffold padding plus background fill
- **Explanation:** Native deliberately consumes only the top inset (so the list can extend under bottom/side insets) and leaves the content box without a background. KMP applies the entire PaddingValues (top+bottom+sides) and fills the box with colorScheme.background. The bottom inset handling differs (native list can scroll under the bottom bar; KMP is fully inset), and KMP adds an explicit background. Subtle layout/inset divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide whether the list should extend under the bottom inset (native) or be fully inset (KMP) and align; if matching native, apply only calculateTopPadding() and drop the background fill.

### Settings  `settings`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 27 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡9 ⚪16)

> Native (source of truth) renders the Settings hub as a centered, icon-rich LazyColumn with NO top bar: a 250.dp launcher header image, then four `ItemsGroup` rounded cards (General toggles, CBZ/Download, Navigation rows, Other rows). Each row uses custom `SwitchItem`/`SettingsNavigationItem` composables that carry a leading 24.dp icon, a 14.sp title, a 12.sp description, and (for nav rows) a trailing KeyboardArrowRight chevron. KMP reimplements this as an MVI slice (`SettingsViewModel`/`SettingsState`/`SettingsIntent`) rendered by `ui/.../settings/SettingsScreen.kt` with a Material3 `TopAppBar`, visible section-title headers, text-only rows (no leading icons, no trailing chevron), and a generic loading spinner. The structural skeleton and toggle/nav set are largely present and the strings were carefully lifted, but there are many divergences: an added top bar + section headers, removed row icons + chevrons, the follow-system/dark/clear-cache/feedback row label & description mismatches, two KMP-extra nav rows (Theme, What's new), an extra auto-convert toggle surfaced in the main UI, a substantially degraded CBZ conversion progress dialog (no counts/current-item/Stop/cancel), a non-functional incognito default semantic, and hardcoded English snackbar strings in the VM. The CBZ "compress existing" engine is genuinely ported in :data (not a stub), but its progress/stop UX is lost.

| Sev | ✓ | Screen / Feature | Category | Difference | Native? | KMP? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Settings</summary>

**🟠 [High] Row leading icons (all rows) — Native every settings row has a 24.dp leading icon; KMP rows have NO leading icons** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — every SwitchItem and SettingsNavigationItem renders a 24.dp leading Icon with a 16.dp spacer. Examples: CloudOff (downloaded-only), incognito_svgrepo_com vector, switchthemes vector (follow system), ic_day_night (dark), Outlined.DarkMode (pure black), ic_complaint, ic_reader_setting, QueryStats, Language, Download, cache_cleaner, Message (feedback), Info (about), Help. SwitchItem.kt:44-52 / SettingsNavigationItem.kt:51-60.
- **KMP:** No — KMP ToggleRow/NavRow/ReadingModeRow/CacheRow render label/description + control only, no leading Icon. The KDoc at SettingsScreen.kt:181-184 explicitly states 'Rows are text-only (no leading icons)'.
- **Explanation:** This is the single largest visual regression in the screen: native settings rows are icon-led (a recognizable glyph per row), KMP strips all of them. Roughly 14 distinct icons (several custom vector drawables: incognito_svgrepo_com, switchthemes, ic_day_night, ic_complaint, ic_reader_setting, cache_cleaner, ic_plus_18) are absent. The screen reads completely differently.
- **Suggested fix:** Add leading icons to ToggleRow/NavRow/ReadingModeRow/CacheRow matching native (material-icons-extended is already on :ui per UP-2a); port the custom vector drawables (incognito, switchthemes, ic_day_night, ic_complaint, ic_reader_setting, cache_cleaner) into ui composeResources/drawable and wire per-row at 24.dp with a 16.dp gap.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — settings rows ARE icon-led. Native SettingsScreen.kt passes a 24.dp leading icon to 14 of 15 rows: - SwitchItem rows: CloudOff (:132), incognito_svgrepo_com (:141), switchthemes (:149), ic_day_night (:159, dark, gated on !followSystem), Outlined.DarkMode (:168, pure black), ic_plus_18 (:178, admin Testing Mode). - SettingsNavigationItem rows: ic_complaint (:249), ic_reader_setting (:260), Outlined.QueryStats (:267), Outlined.Language (:272), Outlined.Download (:276), cache_cleaner (:287), AutoMirrored.Outlined.Message (:296, feedback), Outlined.Info (:302, about), AutoMirrored.Outlined.Help (:309). The leading-icon rendering itself lives in the shared row composables: SwitchItem.kt:44-52 (`if (icon != null) { Icon(... Modifier.size(24.dp)); Spacer(width=16.dp) }`) and SettingsNavigationItem.kt:51-60 (identical 24.dp Icon + 16.dp Spacer). All 7 custom vector drawables cited (incognito_svgrepo_com, switchthemes, ic_day_night, ic_complaint, ic_reader_setting, cache_cleaner, ic_plus_18) confirmed present under native-app/app/src/main/res/drawable/*.xml. KMP — rows have NO leading icons, exactly as claimed. ui/.../settings/SettingsScreen.kt: - ToggleRow (:644-687), NavRow (:738-765), ReadingModeRow (:767-798), CacheRow (:800-837) each render only a Column(label + optional description) + the control (Switch / nothing / spinner). No leading Icon in any of them. - The only `Icon(...)` calls in the whole file are at :1221 (Check, inside ReadingModeDialog Apply button) and :1285 (Warning, inside CbzConversionDialog) — both in dialogs, not rows. material.icons imports are only Check + Warning (:25-26). - The only painterResource is the decorative header launcher image (:412), matching native's header Image (native :113-121), not a row icon. - The KDoc at :181-184 states verbatim: "**Rows are text-only (no leading icons)** — the hub renders each toggle / nav row as a label + control without a leading glyph." MINOR INACCURACY in claim wording: the claim says "every SwitchItem ... renders a 24.dp leading Icon", but the native use-Yami-compressor SwitchItem (SettingsScreen.kt:195-200) does NOT pass an icon (the only native row without one). So "every" overstates by one row; the real gap is 14 icon-led native rows vs 0 in KMP. This does not change the substance or severity.

**🟠 [High] CBZ conversion progress dialog (counts / current item / Stop) — KMP CbzConversionDialog is a stripped indeterminate dialog with no counts, no current manga/chapter, no Stop button, and no terminal success/error/stopped states** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — native CbzConversionDialog (CbzConversionDialog.kt) renders: a determinate LinearProgressIndicator (converted/total), 'Completed X / Y', 'Remaining Z', a Current section showing the current manga title + chapter number, a spinning indicator, AND a full-width Stop button. It also has dedicated Error and Success/Stopped states with their own icons/messages and a Close/Done button. Progress driven by CbzConversionViewModel.ConversionProgress.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP CbzConversionDialog (SettingsScreen.kt:1274-1328) shows only a Warning icon, 'Converting to CBZ' title, 'please don't close the app' caution, an INDETERMINATE LinearProgressIndicator + a CircularProgressIndicator, and confirmButton = {} (no Stop). No counts, no current-item, no Stop/cancel, no error/success/stopped terminal dialog states (terminal outcome is a generic snackbar instead).
- **Explanation:** Native gives the user live, granular feedback during a potentially long bulk conversion (X/Y converted, remaining count, which manga/chapter is converting now) plus the ability to STOP mid-run, plus distinct success/error/stopped result dialogs. KMP loses all of this: no progress numbers, no current item, no way to cancel, and the result collapses to a one-line snackbar. The :data CompressExistingDownloadsUseCase returns Result<Unit> with no progress Flow / cancel hook (CompressExistingDownloadsUseCase.kt; SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:216), so the affordances cannot be wired today. This is a real feature regression for a destructive, long-running operation.
- **Suggested fix:** Lift a Flow<ConversionProgress> (converted/total/current title+chapter) and a cancel/stop hook into the domain SettingsRepository.compressExistingDownloads (or a dedicated use case), then restore the determinate progress bar, counts, current-item section, and Stop button in CbzConversionDialog; add distinct success/error/stopped terminal dialog states with Close/Done.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — full-featured dialog + cancellable VM: - CbzConversionDialog.kt:24-271 takes `conversionProgress: ConversionProgress` and renders THREE states. Converting state (136-266): Warning icon, "Converting to CBZ" title, "please don't close" caution, a DETERMINATE LinearProgressIndicator (160-172: progress = convertedChapters/totalChapters), "Completed X / Y" row (181-191), "Remaining Z" row (200-210), a Current section with current manga title + "Chapter N" (214-243), a CircularProgressIndicator (249-252), and a full-width Stop button (257-265). Error state (63-91): Error icon + message + "Close" button. Success/Stopped state (94-133): CheckCircle/Warning icon, "Conversion complete"/"Conversion stopped" title, message, "Done" button. - CbzConversionViewModel.kt: ConversionProgress data class (22-31) carries isConverting/totalChapters/convertedChapters/currentMangaTitle/currentChapterNumber/error/successMessage/wasStopped, exposed as a StateFlow (43-44). startConversion() (103-208) updates it per-chapter (147-151) with index + manga title + chapter number; stopConversion() (74-98) sets a cancel flag, cancels the Job, and writes a "stopped" terminal state. - Wiring is live: native SettingsScreen.kt:83 collects conversionProgress; :408-413 passes it to the dialog and maps the dialog's onDismiss (the Stop button) to cbzViewModel.stopConversion() while converting. KMP — stripped indeterminate dialog, terminal outcome via snackbar: - ui SettingsScreen.kt:1274-1328 `CbzConversionDialog()` takes NO parameters. Renders ONLY a converting state: Warning icon (1284-1291), "Converting to CBZ" title (1292-1300), "please don't close" caution (1306-1311), an INDETERMINATE LinearProgressIndicator (1313-1318, no progress arg), a CircularProgressIndicator (1320-1323), and confirmButton = {} (1326). No counts, no current-item, no Stop, no Error/Success/Stopped terminal states. KDoc at 1263-1272 explicitly admits these are deferred. - Shown purely off a boolean: ui SettingsScreen.kt:380-381 `if (state.isCompressingDownloads) CbzConversionDialog()`. State flag: presentation SettingsState.kt:146 `val isCompressingDownloads: Boolean = false`. - Terminal outcome is a one-line snackbar: presentation SettingsViewModel.kt:205-220 handleCompressExistingDownloads() flips the boolean, awaits the use case, then emit(SettingsEffect.ShowSnackbar("Conversion complete" \| error message)). No progress collection. - No progress Flow / cancel hook exists: domain CompressExistingDownloadsUseCase.kt:25 `suspend operator fun invoke(): Result<Unit> = repository.compressExistingDownloads()`. data SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:216-235 `override suspend fun compressExistingDownloads(): Result<Unit>` — a runCatching batch loop over chapters; returns Result.success/failure only, emits nothing per-chapter, has no cancellation surface. Minor correction to the claim's incidentals (does not change the verdict): the use case's own KDoc (CompressExistingDownloadsUseCase.kt:11-15) and the claim's framing imply the engine "currently returns Result.failure / is not ported"; in fact SettingsRepositoryImpl.kt:216 IS implemented and returns Result.success on a completed walk. But the load-bearing assertion — Result<Unit> with no progress Flow and no cancel hook — is exactly correct.

**🟡 [Medium] Settings hub top bar — KMP adds a Settings TopAppBar that does not exist in native** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** No — native SettingsScreen.kt:101-104 uses a bare Scaffold with only a snackbarHost and backgroundColor; there is NO topBar. The screen scrolls from the top with the launcher image as the first item.
- **KMP:** Yes — SettingsScreen.kt:326-335 adds a Material3 TopAppBar titled stringResource(Res.string.settings) with FontWeight.SemiBold.
- **Explanation:** Native presents Settings as a chromeless, centered scrolling list (no app bar, content centered via horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally). KMP introduces a persistent top app bar with a 'Settings' title and the default TopAppBar height/insets, shifting the whole layout down and changing the visual identity. This is a structural addition with no native counterpart.
- **Suggested fix:** Remove the TopAppBar (or make it opt-in) to match native's chromeless Scaffold; if a title is desired, confirm with design since native deliberately omits it and centers content.

**🟡 [Medium] Section grouping headers — KMP shows visible section-title text headers above each card; native shows none** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** No — native groups rows into ItemsGroup rounded cards with NO title text. The only separators are a top Divider + Spacer before the first group (SettingsScreen.kt:125-126). There are no 'General'/'Navigation'/'Other' captions.
- **KMP:** Yes — SettingsScreen.kt:599-615 SectionCard renders a titleSmall, SemiBold, primary-colored header above each Card: section_general='General', downloads='Downloads', section_navigation='Navigation', section_other='Other'.
- **Explanation:** Native intentionally has unlabeled grouped cards. KMP adds four visible captions in MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary with titleSmall SemiBold. This is a clear visual divergence (added text, added vertical space, primary tint) that changes the screen's appearance versus the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Remove the SectionCard title text to match native's caption-less grouped cards, or confirm the added headers are an intentional rework UX decision (they are flagged GAP-SET-04 in code but still diverge from native).

**🟡 [Medium] Navigation rows trailing chevron — Native nav rows show a trailing KeyboardArrowRight chevron; KMP NavRow shows none** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — SettingsNavigationItem.kt:35 defaults endIcon = Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.KeyboardArrowRight and renders it tinted onBackground at the row's end (lines 80-86). All navigation rows (feedback, reading mode, statistics, language, downloads, clear cache, request feature/bug, about, help) display the chevron.
- **KMP:** No — KMP NavRow (SettingsScreen.kt:738-765) renders only a weighted Text label; there is no trailing chevron Icon. CacheRow/ReadingModeRow likewise omit it (CacheRow shows a spinner only when clearing).
- **Explanation:** The trailing right-chevron is a standard affordance signalling 'this row navigates'. Native shows it on every nav row (auto-mirrored for RTL). KMP removes it entirely, losing the navigational affordance and the RTL-aware mirroring.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a trailing Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.KeyboardArrowRight to NavRow (and ReadingModeRow) tinted onBackground/onSurface, matching native's default endIcon.

**🟡 [Medium] Dark mode row title & description — Native title = 'Custom Theme' (theme_title); KMP title = 'Dark Mode' (theme_dark)** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — native dark/light row title = theme_title ('Custom Theme'); description toggles between theme_dark ('Dark Mode') and theme_light ('Light Mode') based on themeMode (SettingsScreen.kt:156-162).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP DARK_MODE row title = theme_dark ('Dark Mode') (settingsToggleLabel line 854); description toggles theme_dark_desc ('Dark Mode') / theme_light_desc ('Light Mode') (lines 462-466).
- **Explanation:** Native row reads title 'Custom Theme' with a dynamic subtitle 'Dark Mode'/'Light Mode'. KMP row reads title 'Dark Mode' with subtitle also 'Dark Mode' (when on) — the title 'Custom Theme' is gone and the title/description become identical ('Dark Mode' over 'Dark Mode'), which is a confusing duplication and not parity. The native theme_title='Custom Theme' string is unused on the KMP side.
- **Suggested fix:** Set the dark-mode row title to 'Custom Theme' (theme_title) and keep the dynamic 'Dark Mode'/'Light Mode' subtitle, matching native exactly.

**🟡 [Medium] Request feature/bug row label & description (Other section) — Native row title 'Report Bug / Feature' + description 'Tap to send us your feedback'; KMP NavRow label 'Request feature / bug', no description** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — native uses request_feature_bug_title ('Report Bug / Feature') as title and request_feature_bug_desc ('Tap to send us your feedback') as description with a Message icon (SettingsScreen.kt:293-297).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP NavRow uses request_feature_bug ('Request feature / bug') as the label and shows NO description (SettingsScreen.kt:578-581).
- **Explanation:** Native row is title 'Report Bug / Feature' with subtitle 'Tap to send us your feedback' and a leading Message icon. KMP reduces it to a single line 'Request feature / bug' with no subtitle and no icon. Both still open the feedback dialog, but the label text, the descriptive subtitle, and the icon are all lost.
- **Suggested fix:** Use 'Report Bug / Feature' as the title and 'Tap to send us your feedback' as the description (add request_feature_bug_title / request_feature_bug_desc keys) plus a leading Message icon, matching native.

**🟡 [Medium] Auto-convert-to-CBZ toggle visibility — KMP surfaces an 'Auto-convert on Download' toggle in the main Settings UI; native does NOT show it on the Settings screen** _(Component)_

- **Native:** No — native CbzConversionViewModel exposes autoConvertToCbzFlow + setAutoConvertToCbz (CbzConversionViewModel.kt:51,65) but the native SettingsScreen ONLY renders the useCbz toggle + the Compress-Existing button (SettingsScreen.kt:195-237). There is no auto-convert SwitchItem on the native Settings screen.
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP renders an extra ToggleRow for AUTO_CONVERT_TO_CBZ ('Auto-convert on Download' / 'Automatically convert new downloads to CBZ') inside the CBZ section when useCbzFormat is on (SettingsScreen.kt:506-514).
- **Explanation:** KMP adds a user-facing toggle that native does not show on the Settings screen. While the underlying flow exists in native, exposing it as a settings row is a behavioral/UI addition (the user can now flip auto-convert from Settings, which they could not in native).
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm whether exposing auto-convert in Settings is intended. If strict parity is required, remove the AUTO_CONVERT_TO_CBZ ToggleRow from the Settings UI (keep the toggle wired where native exposes it, e.g. downloads flow).

**🟡 [Medium] CBZ conversion result snackbar copy — KMP success/failure conversion messages are hardcoded English strings in the VM ('Conversion complete'); native uses localized templated strings with counts** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — native builds rich localized messages: conversion_complete + chapters_converted_successfully(converted) + chapters_failed(failed); and on stop: conversion_stopped_by_user + chapters_converted + chapters_remaining (CbzConversionViewModel.kt:84-96,180-197).
- **KMP:** No (parity) — KMP SettingsViewModel.handleCompressExistingDownloads emits SettingsEffect.ShowSnackbar('Conversion complete') on success and the raw exception message on failure (SettingsViewModel.kt:211-219). Literal English, no counts, no localization, no stopped path.
- **Explanation:** The VM hardcodes 'Conversion complete' / 'Unknown error' rather than localized resources, and provides no converted/failed counts. This is both a localization regression (no Arabic) and an information regression (user no longer sees how many chapters converted/failed).
- **Suggested fix:** Route the conversion result through a typed effect (like FeedbackResult) so :ui resolves localized strings (and counts once the progress Flow exists); do not hardcode English in :presentation.

**🟡 [Medium] Reading-mode dialog surface/structure — Native dialog is a Dialog+Surface with chip selector; KMP is an AlertDialog with RadioButton list** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — native ReadingModeDialog (ReadingModeDialog.kt) uses Dialog{ Surface(surfaceContainerHigh, 8.dp tonal, 16.dp corners) } with a 'Reading mode' header (headlineSmall Bold, 24/16 dp padding), a scrollable ReadingModeChips selector, a Divider, and a Revert(OutlinedButton)/Apply(Button with Check icon) footer aligned End.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP ReadingModeDialog (SettingsScreen.kt:1165-1251) uses Material3 AlertDialog (surfaceContainerHigh, 8.dp tonal, 16.dp corners) with a RADIOBUTTON list (one Row per ReadingMode with a RadioButton) plus Revert/Apply buttons. The selection UI is radio rows, not native's chip selector (ReadingModeChips).
- **Explanation:** Native presents reading-mode options as chips (ReadingModeChips); KMP presents them as a vertical radio-button list. Both stage selection and commit on Apply (two-step semantics preserved), but the selection control type, layout, and likely per-mode icons (native chips may carry mode icons via iconRes) differ visually. Note the native Apply button has a known bug: contentColor=onBackground makes the 'Apply' text invisible (same color as container), though the Check icon + text are explicitly tinted background — KMP correctly sets contentColor=background, so KMP is actually more correct here.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the chip-based ReadingModeChips selector (with per-mode icons) to match native's dialog body, or confirm the radio-list rework is intentional. Verify mode labels/icons match native's titleRes/iconRes.

**🟡 [Medium] Feedback submit subject derivation — KMP sends subject = type.name (enum constant, e.g. 'TECHNICAL'); native sends the localized display name** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — native submits complaintViewModel.submit(it, it.getDisplayName(context), body, ...) (SettingsScreen.kt:320-323) — i.e. the localized display name as the subject.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP SettingsViewModel.handleSubmitFeedback calls submitFeedback(type, subject = type.name, body) (SettingsViewModel.kt:250) — the raw enum constant name (uppercase, unlocalized) as the subject.
- **Explanation:** Native uses the human-readable, localized category display name as the complaint subject; KMP sends the enum constant string ('TECHNICAL', 'SITES_ADD', etc.). On the server/admin side the subject text now reads as a code identifier rather than the user-facing category, a data-quality regression (acknowledged as a pre-Phase-10 stopgap in the intent KDoc).
- **Suggested fix:** Derive the submitted subject from the localized display name (resolve complaintTypeLabel at the :ui layer and pass it along with OnSubmitFeedback, or expose a display-name resolver) so the persisted subject matches native.

**⚪ [Low] Header launcher image alignment & layout — Native LazyColumn is center-aligned for the whole list; KMP only centers the header image via a Box** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — native LazyColumn (SettingsScreen.kt:105-112) sets horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally and pads horizontal=16.dp, vertical=8.dp; the 250.dp header image (lines 114-120) is centered by the column.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP centers only the header image by wrapping it in a Box(contentAlignment = Center) (SettingsScreen.kt:406-419); the list itself uses contentPadding = PaddingValues(vertical = spacing.md) with no horizontal padding on the LazyColumn (per-card horizontal padding comes from SectionCard spacing.md).
- **Explanation:** Native applies a uniform horizontal=16.dp/vertical=8.dp padding on the LazyColumn and centers every item. KMP applies vertical-only contentPadding on the list and pushes horizontal padding into each SectionCard (spacing.md). The exact horizontal inset depends on LocalSpacing.md vs native's hardcoded 16.dp; if spacing.md != 16.dp the card insets differ from native.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify LocalSpacing.md == 16.dp; otherwise align the card horizontal padding to native's 16.dp. Confirm vertical rhythm (native vertical=8.dp vs KMP spacing.md/spacing.sm gaps).

**⚪ [Low] Follow-system theme row label — Title differs: native 'System Theme' vs KMP 'Follow system theme'; description also differs** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — native row title = system_theme ('System Theme'), description = follow_system_theme ('Follow System Theme') (SettingsScreen.kt:146-152).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP uses follow_system_theme ('Follow system theme') as the TITLE (settingsToggleLabel, SettingsScreen.kt:853) and follow_system_theme_desc ('Follow System Theme') as the description (line 453). So the native TITLE 'System Theme' is missing; KMP title repurposes the native description string as its title.
- **Explanation:** Native shows title 'System Theme' / subtitle 'Follow System Theme'. KMP shows title 'Follow system theme' / subtitle 'Follow System Theme'. The native title string (system_theme = 'System Theme') is not used; the KMP title duplicates content close to its own description ('Follow system theme' over 'Follow System Theme'), which is redundant and not byte-parity with native.
- **Suggested fix:** Use 'System Theme' as the title (add/reuse a system_theme key) and 'Follow System Theme' as the description to match native's exact title/subtitle pairing.

**⚪ [Low] Clear-cache row title — Native title = 'Clear Chapter Cache'; KMP title = 'Clear cache'** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — native clear_cache string = 'Clear Chapter Cache' (strings.xml:133), used as the title (SettingsScreen.kt:285).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP clear_cache string = 'Clear cache' (strings_np_p2_settings_theme_lang.xml), used as the CacheRow title (SettingsScreen.kt:821).
- **Explanation:** Same key name but different value — native specifically labels it 'Clear Chapter Cache' (clarifying it clears chapter files >1MB), while KMP shortened it to 'Clear cache'. This is a copy regression.
- **Suggested fix:** Change the KMP clear_cache value to 'Clear Chapter Cache' to match native.

**⚪ [Low] Clear-cache row 'Used:' size prefix — Native description = 'Used: <size>'; KMP = 'Used: <size>' via cached_size — value parity OK but native concatenates raw string + space** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — native description = stringResource(cache_used) + ' ' + cacheSize where cache_used='Used: ' (strings.xml:134), so 'Used:  <size>' with the trailing space in the resource plus the concatenated space (SettingsScreen.kt:286).
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP uses cached_size='Used: %1$s' formatted with the size (SettingsScreen.kt:827). Rendered text matches 'Used: <size>'.
- **Explanation:** Functionally equivalent and arguably cleaner in KMP (proper format arg). Minor: native has a double space ('Used: ' + ' ' + size); KMP has a single space. Cosmetic only. Note also native's initial value is 'Calculating…' (R.string.calculating) shown until the IO walk completes; KMP shows an empty cacheSize ('') initially and hides the subtitle until the first emission (CacheRow line 825 guards cacheSize.isNotEmpty()), so the 'Calculating…' placeholder is absent in KMP.
- **Suggested fix:** Optionally show a 'Calculating…' placeholder before the first cache-size emission to match native's initial state; the value formatting itself can stay as-is.

**⚪ [Low] About row description — Native About row has a descriptive subtitle + Info icon; KMP NavRow is label-only** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — native About row title = about ('About'), description = app_information_and_updates_contact_us_on_social_media ('App information and updates. Contact us on social media'), icon = Outlined.Info (SettingsScreen.kt:299-303).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP NavRow uses about label only (settingsDestinationLabel line 879); no description, no icon (SettingsScreen.kt:583-586).
- **Explanation:** Native About row carries a two-line subtitle and an Info icon; KMP shows just 'About'. The descriptive subtitle and icon are dropped.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the About description ('App information and updates. Contact us on social media') and an Info leading icon to the About NavRow.

**⚪ [Low] Extra Theme + What's-new navigation rows — KMP Navigation section adds Theme and What's-new rows that have no counterpart in native Settings** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** No — native Settings Navigation group contains exactly: Feedbacks & complaints, Default Reading Mode, Statistics, App language, Downloads (SettingsScreen.kt:246-279). There is no Theme picker row and no What's-new row in native Settings.
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP appends NavRow THEME ('Theme') and NavRow WHATSNEW ("What's new") to the Navigation card (SettingsScreen.kt:556-565), routing to rework Theme/WhatsNew screens.
- **Explanation:** These are intentional rework additions (flagged KMP-EXTRA GAP-THM-11/GAP-SET-22 in code) because the rework introduced standalone Theme and What's-new screens. They are extra entries relative to the native source of truth. Documenting per the audit; severity low since they are additive, not removing native functionality.
- **Suggested fix:** No change required if these rework screens are intended; otherwise hide the Theme/What's-new rows to match native's 5-row Navigation group exactly.

**⚪ [Low] Reading-mode row placement & subtitle — Native 'Default Reading Mode' is a plain nav row with chevron + icon; KMP ReadingModeRow shows the current mode as a subtitle and has no icon/chevron** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — native uses SettingsNavigationItem(default_reading_mode='Default Reading Mode', icon=ic_reader_setting) with trailing chevron and NO subtitle; tapping opens the dialog (SettingsScreen.kt:258-263).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP ReadingModeRow shows title reading_mode ('Reading mode') + a subtitle = current mode label (e.g. 'Default'/'RTL') at alpha 0.8 (SettingsScreen.kt:786-795), no leading icon, no chevron.
- **Explanation:** Native row title is 'Default Reading Mode' with a reader icon and chevron, no current-value subtitle. KMP changes the title to 'Reading mode', adds a current-mode subtitle, and removes the icon + chevron. The added subtitle is a UX improvement but diverges from native; the title text and affordances differ.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native title 'Default Reading Mode', add the ic_reader_setting leading icon and trailing chevron. Decide whether to keep the current-mode subtitle (native shows none).

**⚪ [Low] Clear-cache result snackbar copy — KMP cache-clear snackbar uses hardcoded English ('Cache cleared' / 'Failed to clear cache: ...'); native shows no snackbar at all** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** No — native clearLargeCache() is fire-and-forget (SettingsViewModel.kt:63-69) and shows NO snackbar; it just recomputes the cache size which re-renders the 'Used:' subtitle.
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP emits SettingsEffect.ShowSnackbar with hardcoded English 'Cache cleared' or 'Failed to clear cache: <cause>' (SettingsViewModel.kt:229-237).
- **Explanation:** KMP adds a success/failure snackbar that native does not show, and the copy is hardcoded English (not localized). Minor behavioral addition + a localization gap.
- **Suggested fix:** Either drop the cache-clear snackbar to match native, or localize it via a typed effect resolved in :ui (no hardcoded English in the VM).

**⚪ [Low] Admin 'Testing Mode' switch tint — Native Testing Mode row uses a red icon tint AND ic_plus_18 icon; KMP colors the LABEL red and shows no icon** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — native admin-only Testing Mode SwitchItem uses tint = Color.Red.copy(0.5F) applied to the ic_plus_18 leading ICON; title 'Testing Mode' stays default onBackground color (SettingsScreen.kt:175-183).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP colors the TEXT label labelColor = Color.Red.copy(alpha = 0.5f) (SettingsScreen.kt:483-491) and has no icon (since rows are icon-less). The red is moved from the icon to the label.
- **Explanation:** Native tints the plus-18 icon red; the title text is normal color. KMP has no icon so it instead tints the title text red. The visual emphasis location differs and the ic_plus_18 glyph is gone. Admin-only, so low impact.
- **Suggested fix:** If row icons are restored, tint the ic_plus_18 icon red (0.5 alpha) and keep the label default color, matching native.

**⚪ [Low] Switch component colors — Native SwitchItem sets custom Switch colors; KMP ToggleRow uses default Material3 Switch colors** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — native SwitchItem.kt:61-71 uses material(2) Switch with SwitchDefaults.colors(checkedThumbColor=primary, uncheckedThumbColor=surfaceVariant, uncheckedTrackColor=onBackground, uncheckedTrackAlpha=0.4f).
- **KMP:** No (parity) — KMP ToggleRow uses Material3 Switch with NO custom colors (SettingsScreen.kt:682-685), inheriting default M3 SwitchColors (thumb/track defaults differ from native's M2 custom palette).
- **Explanation:** Native uses Compose Material 2 Switch with explicitly customized thumb/track colors and a 0.4 unchecked-track alpha. KMP uses an unstyled Material 3 Switch, so the checked/unchecked thumb and track colors will not match native's palette (e.g., M3 default uncheckedTrack differs from native's onBackground@0.4).
- **Suggested fix:** Apply SwitchDefaults.colors to the M3 Switch approximating native (checkedThumb = primary, unchecked track ~ onBackground/outline at low alpha) if exact switch coloring parity is desired.

**⚪ [Low] Switch row tap-to-toggle interaction — KMP makes the entire toggle row clickable to flip the switch; native only the Switch itself toggles** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** No — native SwitchItem Row has NO clickable modifier (SwitchItem.kt:38-43); only the Switch control responds to taps. Tapping the row text does nothing.
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP ToggleRow wraps the whole Row in .clickable { onCheckedChange(!checked) } (SettingsScreen.kt:658-659), so tapping anywhere on the row flips the toggle.
- **Explanation:** KMP adds a larger tap target (row-wide) that native lacks. This is arguably better UX but is a behavioral divergence from the source of truth (and adds row-wide ripple where native has none).
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm intended; if strict parity, restrict the toggle interaction to the Switch only (remove the row clickable) — though keeping it is a reasonable accessibility improvement.

**⚪ [Low] Feedback dialog dropdown trailing icon — Native feedback category field has an ArrowDropDown trailing icon; KMP omits it** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — native FeedbackDialog OutlinedTextField sets trailingIcon = Icons.Default.ArrowDropDown (FeedbackDialog.kt:98-103) and custom focused/unfocused border colors.
- **KMP:** No — KMP feedback dialog OutlinedTextField (SettingsScreen.kt:996-1006) has no trailingIcon and no custom border colors (relies on ExposedDropdownMenuBox default).
- **Explanation:** Native shows an explicit dropdown arrow on the category selector and tints the border with primary/outline@0.5. KMP relies on defaults (no explicit arrow, default border). Minor cosmetic divergence inside the feedback dialog.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a trailing ArrowDropDown icon and the focused/unfocused border colors to the KMP category OutlinedTextField for visual parity.

**⚪ [Low] Feedback social-media prompt-response copy — KMP uses a shorter prompt-response string than native** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — native uses you_ll_receive_a_prompt_response_our_developer_will_reach_out_to_you_shortly (FeedbackDialog.kt:194).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP uses you_ll_receive_a_prompt_response (SettingsScreen.kt:1082), a shorter key/value than native's full sentence.
- **Explanation:** The native footer copy is the longer 'You'll receive a prompt response, our developer will reach out to you shortly'; KMP uses a truncated variant. Copy regression in the feedback dialog footer.
- **Suggested fix:** Use the full native sentence value for the prompt-response line in the feedback dialog.

**⚪ [Low] downloadedOnly / incognito collection default — Native UI seeds downloadedOnly & incognito with collectAsStateWithLifecycle(true); KMP state defaults both to false** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — native SettingsScreen collects downloadedOnly = collectAsStateWithLifecycle(true) and incognito = collectAsStateWithLifecycle(true) (SettingsScreen.kt:87-88), i.e. the FIRST-FRAME default shown before DataStore emits is true (even though the DataStore default is false — DataStoreHelper.kt:43,46).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP SettingsState defaults downloadedOnly=false, incognito=false (SettingsState.kt:129-130), and isLoading=true shows a spinner until the first emission, so the initial 'true' flash never occurs.
- **Explanation:** Native's initial collect default (true) momentarily shows both switches ON before the real DataStore value (false) arrives — a brief inconsistent flash. KMP avoids this by gating on isLoading and defaulting to the real DataStore default (false). KMP is arguably more correct, but it diverges from native's (buggy) initial-render behavior. The eventual steady-state value is identical (false) on both. Documenting the divergence; KMP behavior is preferable.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed (KMP is more correct). Note for reviewers that the native 'true' initial default is a transient mislabel, not the actual default.

**⚪ [Low] Loading state rendering — KMP shows a centered CircularProgressIndicator while loading; native has no loading state** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — native renders the list immediately with collect defaults; there is no loading spinner for Settings.
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP shows CircularProgressIndicator centered while state.isLoading (SettingsScreen.kt:344-345) until the first combine emission.
- **Explanation:** KMP adds a brief loading spinner (sub-frame in practice) that native does not have. Minor additive state; unlikely to be perceptible but is a divergence from native's immediate render.
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable as-is; optionally render the list with defaults immediately (like native) to avoid any one-frame spinner, since the upstream emits near-instantly.

**⚪ [Low] CBZ section header label — KMP labels the CBZ card 'Downloads' (section header); native CBZ group is unlabeled** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** No — native CBZ ItemsGroup (SettingsScreen.kt:189-240) has no header text; it is just the use-Yami-compressor switch + Compress-Existing block in an unlabeled card.
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP SectionCard for CBZ uses title = downloads ('Downloads') (SettingsScreen.kt:497), so the compressor section is captioned 'Downloads' (which also collides conceptually with the separate Downloads nav row).
- **Explanation:** KMP not only adds a header (see section-headers finding) but labels the CBZ/compressor card 'Downloads' — the same word used for the navigation row that opens the Downloads screen, which is confusing. Native has no such caption.
- **Suggested fix:** Remove the CBZ section caption (matching native), or if headers are kept, use a distinct label like 'Storage' / 'Yami Compressor' to avoid colliding with the Downloads nav row.

</details>

### Sources / Repo Settings  `sources-repo-settings`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 15 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡4 ⚪9)

> The KMP rework consolidates the native app's TWO screens (in-settings `RepoSettingsScreen` and onboarding `SourcesScreen`) into a single parameterized `SourcesScreen` in :ui, driven by an MVI `SourcesViewModel`. Core behavior is largely preserved: language grouping, per-language master Switch with "any-enabled" semantics + bulk fan-out, per-source toggles, AnimatedVisibility reveal, the "Request adding source" row, "Upcoming Languages" info card, onboarding Finish button + default-language seed, and the request dialog. However there are numerous regressions vs the source of truth. The most important: (1) the in-settings entry LOST its top-bar back-arrow navigation icon entirely (native had an ArrowBack IconButton; KMP relies on system back only); (2) the per-source row DROPPED the source icon (native rendered `repo.ICON` with checked-state tint); (3) the per-language master row's description text changed from "Enable/disable all (XX) sources" to a computed "%d of %d enabled" count caption; (4) the complaint submission `subject` changed from the localized display name "Add Manga Site" to the raw enum name "SITES_ADD"; (5) the onboarding chain gained an extra duplicate Sources step (native: Sources→Library; KMP: Sources→RepoSettings(isFirstOpen)→Library); (6) the request dialog is a stripped-down version of the native FeedbackDialog (no category label, no "we'd love to hear from you" subtitle, no social-media row, no connect-with-us text); plus typography, color/tint, control-type (Checkbox vs Switch), AnimatedBackground fidelity, language-name localization, and string-text differences. None are crashers, but several are user-visible functional/visual regressions. NOTE: native source-of-truth files live under package me.manga.kira despite the me/manga/yami on-disk path.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Sources / Repo Settings</summary>

**🟠 [High] Sources Settings (in-settings entry) — Top app bar — The in-settings Sources screen lost its back-navigation icon.** _(Navigation / Toolbar)_

- **Native:** RepoSettingsScreen.kt:72-83 uses TopAppBarCom with navigationIcon = IconButton(onClick = onBackPress) { Icon(Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack, contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.desc_back), tint = onBackground) }; route passes onBackPress = { navController.safePopBackStack() } (RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:40).
- **KMP:** SourcesScreen.kt:352-354 renders a plain TopAppBar(title = { Text(topBarTitle) }) with NO navigationIcon. RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt KDoc (lines 55-63) explicitly states the rework screen does NOT accept an onBackPress parameter and the safePopBackStack defensive fallback is dropped, relying on system back.
- **Explanation:** On the in-settings entry, the user reaches Sources Settings from Home/Settings. Native provides a visible, tappable back arrow; KMP removes it, leaving only the OS/system back gesture. On devices/contexts without an obvious system-back affordance this is a visible navigation regression and an accessibility/discoverability loss (the desc_back content description is gone too).
- **Suggested fix:** Add a navigationIcon to the KMP TopAppBar (an AutoMirrored ArrowBack IconButton) wired to a new onBack callback threaded from RepoSettingsScreenRoute/SourcesReworkScreenRoute (navController.popBackStack). Restore the desc_back content description for accessibility.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). VERIFIED REAL. Both apps read directly. NATIVE (source of truth): - RepoSettingsScreen.kt:70-83 — Scaffold topBar uses TopAppBarCom(title = stringResource(R.string.title_sources_settings), navigationIcon = { IconButton(onClick = onBackPress) { Icon(Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack, contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.desc_back), tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground) } }). The IconButton/Icon block is lines 74-82 (claim cited 72-83; TopAppBarCom opens at 72 — essentially correct). - TopAppBarCom.kt:42 confirms `navigationIcon = navigationIcon` is wired into the Material3 TopAppBar, so the back arrow genuinely renders. - RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:40 — the trailing-lambda onBackPress passed to RepoSettingsScreen is `{ navController.safePopBackStack() }` (matches claim). - In-settings entry CONFIRMED: HomeRoute.kt:215 `navController.navigate(Screen.RepoSettings(false))` → NavGraphV2.kt:535 composable<Screen.RepoSettings> → RepoSettingsScreenRoute → RepoSettingsScreen. KMP: - SourcesScreen.kt:350-354 — Scaffold topBar = { TopAppBar(title = { Text(topBarTitle) }) } with NO navigationIcon parameter (TopAppBar is line 353; claim cited 352-354 — correct). Verified NO BackHandler anywhere in SourcesScreen.kt. - RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:124-148 — calls SourcesScreen(viewModel, onFinish = if (args.isFirstOpen) {...} else null) with no onBackPress. KDoc lines 55-63 explicitly state: legacy passed onBackPress = { navController.safePopBackStack() }; the rework SourcesScreen does NOT accept an onBackPress parameter, relies on system back, has no custom top-bar nav icon and no BackHandler, and the safePopBackStack defensive fallback is dropped. Matches claim verbatim. - In-settings entry CONFIRMED equivalent: HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:160 `safeNavigate(Screen.RepoSettings(false))` → App.kt:543 composable<Screen.RepoSettings> → RepoSettingsScreenRoute → SourcesScreen with onFinish = null (isFirstOpen = false). Same navigation chain shape as native; both originate from Home. NET: Native shows a tappable ArrowBack icon with desc_back content description on the in-settings Sources screen; KMP renders a plain title-only TopAppBar with no nav icon and no BackHandler, relying solely on the OS/system back gesture. The desc_back content description is also gone (accessibility loss). The difference is real and correctly characterized. Minor: trivial off-by-one in the cited line ranges (native IconButton block 74-82 not 72-83; KMP TopAppBar at 353 not 352-354) — not material.

**🟠 [High] Per-source row — source icon — Each per-source row no longer shows the source's brand/icon.** _(Icons / Components)_

- **Native:** LanguageToggleWithAnimation.kt:35-44 renders RepoToggleItem(..., icon = ImageVector.vectorResource(repo.ICON), ...); RepoToggleItem.kt:38-46 draws the Icon at size 24.dp with tint = if(checked) Color.Unspecified else onBackground (i.e. full-color when enabled, monochrome when disabled). repo.ICON comes from BaseMangaRepository.ICON (abstract val ICON: Int).
- **KMP:** SourceRow in SourcesScreen.kt:765-808 renders only a Column(api text + Enabled/Disabled caption) + Checkbox; no leading icon. The screen comment at lines 779-783 explicitly defers the icon: 'Source icon deferred — the rework Source domain model carries no icon field and RepoIconResolver is a null-returning stub'.
- **Explanation:** The per-source brand icon is a core visual identifier the user relies on to recognize sources at a glance, and its checked/unchecked tinting communicated enabled-state. This is fully absent in KMP, a clear visual regression. Root cause: the rework Source domain model (domain/model/sources/Source.kt) intentionally trimmed to 4 fields and dropped the icon resource, so the data is not even available to :ui.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an icon identifier to the Source domain model (e.g. an icon resource key or DrawableResource reference resolvable in :ui), map it in SourcesMappers from BaseMangaRepository.ICON, and render a leading 24.dp Icon in SourceRow with the native tint rule (Color.Unspecified when checked, onSurface/onBackground when unchecked).
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). VERIFIED REAL and correctly characterized on every cited point. NATIVE (source of truth) — renders the per-source brand icon: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/common/componants/sources/LanguageToggleWithAnimation.kt:33-44 — `repos.forEach { repo -> ... RepoToggleItem(title = repo.API, description = ..., icon = ImageVector.vectorResource(repo.ICON), checked = isEnabled, ...) }`. Line 40 is exactly `icon = ImageVector.vectorResource(repo.ICON)`. - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/repo_settings/ui/components/RepoToggleItem.kt:38-46 — `if (icon != null) { Icon(imageVector = icon, contentDescription = null, tint = if(checked) Color.Unspecified else MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground, modifier = Modifier.size(24.dp)) ; Spacer(width=16.dp) }`. Confirms 24.dp size, full-color when checked / onBackground tint when unchecked. KMP (new app) — no per-source icon: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/sources/SourcesScreen.kt:765-808 — `SourceRow` renders only `Row { Column(weight=1f){ Text(source.api); Text(enabled/disabled caption) } ; Checkbox(...) }`.
