**🟡 [Medium] Per-language master row — secondary text — The language header's secondary line changed from a localized 'Enable/disable all (XX) sources' description to a computed 'N of M enabled' count.** _(Typography / Business logic (computed text))_

- **Native:** RepoSettingsScreen.kt:156-159 passes description = stringResource(R.string.enable_disable_all_sources, language) → 'Enable/disable all %1$s sources'. LanguageToggle.kt:22-31 forwards it to SwitchItem which renders it at 12.sp, onBackground @ alpha 0.5.
- **KMP:** LanguageHeader in SourcesScreen.kt:748-756 renders stringResource(Res.string.sources_enabled_count, sources.count{it.isEnabled}, sources.size) → '%1$d of %2$d enabled' at bodySmall, onSurfaceVariant. The enable_disable_all_sources string is not used by the KMP screen.
- **Explanation:** Different information is conveyed: native describes the action ('Enable/disable all <Lang> sources'); KMP shows a live enabled/total count. While the count is arguably more informative, it is a behavioral/text divergence from the source of truth and changes the localized copy the user sees (and the native enable_disable_all_sources / sources_enabled_count strings differ).
- **Suggested fix:** Decide on intended parity. To match native, render stringResource(enable_disable_all_sources, language) as the header subtitle. If the count caption is a deliberate improvement, document it; otherwise revert to the native description string.

**🟡 [Medium] Request adding source — complaint submission subject — The complaint 'subject' sent to the backend changed from the localized display name to the raw enum name.** _(Business logic / API data)_

- **Native:** RepoSettingsScreen.kt:178-201 calls complaintViewModel.submit(it, it.getDisplayName(context), body, ...) — the second arg (subject) is ComplaintType.SITES_ADD.getDisplayName(context) = stringResource(add_manga_site) = 'Add Manga Site' (ComplaintType.kt:12, strings.xml:309).
- **KMP:** SourcesViewModel.kt:176-177 builds val type = ComplaintType.SITES_ADD; submitFeedback(type = type, subject = type.name, body = body) — subject is the enum constant name 'SITES_ADD'. FeedbackRepositoryImpl.kt:131-145 forwards subject verbatim into the Complaint written to Firestore.
- **Explanation:** Submitted complaints now carry subject='SITES_ADD' instead of the human-readable 'Add Manga Site'. This changes the data persisted to the backend (admin-visible subject line), a real data-behavior regression for whoever triages these requests. The KMP code comments (SourcesIntent.kt) acknowledge this as a pre-Phase-10 stopgap.
- **Suggested fix:** Resolve the localized display name for ComplaintType.SITES_ADD (the KMP equivalent of getDisplayName / add_manga_site) and pass it as the subject, matching native. If a context-free display-name lookup isn't available in :presentation, pass a localized string from :ui or add a displayName mapping to the domain ComplaintType.

**🟡 [Medium] Onboarding flow — Sources step navigation — KMP onboarding adds an extra duplicate Sources step before reaching Library.** _(Navigation & screen-flow)_

- **Native:** NavGraphV2.kt onboarding chain is Welcome → Theme → Sources (Screen.Sources, step 3). Native onboarding SourcesScreenRoute.kt onFinish navigates DIRECTLY to Screen.Library (popUpTo start, inclusive) and sets first_launch=false. RepoSettings is a separate in-settings destination, not part of the onboarding chain.
- **KMP:** SourcesScreenRoute.kt:167-169 onFinish does navController.safeNavigate(Screen.RepoSettings(isFirstOpen = true)) — i.e. it routes to a SECOND rendering of the same rework SourcesScreen (with another Finish button), and only THAT step's onFinish (RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:134-143) goes to Library. SourcesScreenRoute KDoc (lines 45-52) admits 'the step-3/step-4 redundancy (both render the rework Sources screen with a Finish button) is a pre-existing condition'.
- **Explanation:** During first-run onboarding the user now sees the Sources screen twice in a row, each with a Finish button. Native showed it once and went straight to Library. This is a screen-flow regression (extra, redundant step) introduced by the migration's route consolidation.
- **Suggested fix:** Make the onboarding SourcesScreenRoute.onFinish navigate directly to Screen.Library (set first_launch=false + popUpTo start inclusive) as native does, OR remove the separate RepoSettings(isFirstOpen=true) onboarding step so the chain is 3 steps. Keep RepoSettings(isFirstOpen=false) only for the in-settings entry.

**🟡 [Medium] Card / ItemsGroup grouping structure — The language sections are no longer wrapped in a rounded card (ItemsGroup) the way native groups them.** _(UI structure / Layout)_

- **Native:** RepoSettingsScreen.kt:148-172 wraps EACH language group (LanguageToggle + LanguageToggleWithAnimation) inside an ItemsGroup card (surfaceContainerHigh, RoundedCornerShape(16.dp), horizontal=16/vertical=8 padding) with 16.dp spacers between groups. The request row and info row are also each in their own ItemsGroup.
- **KMP:** Only the 'Request adding source' row and the 'Upcoming Languages' card are wrapped in an ItemsGroup-style Card (SourcesScreen.kt:489-509, 559-576). The per-LANGUAGE sections (LanguageHeader + source rows) are NOT wrapped in a card — they are plain rows with a HorizontalDivider after each source row (lines 516-547). So language groups render flat/edge-to-edge instead of as rounded cards.
- **Explanation:** Native presents every language group as a distinct rounded surface card with inter-group spacing; KMP renders the language groups as flat list rows with dividers (no card background, no rounded corners, no per-group spacing). This is a noticeable layout/grouping regression that changes the screen's visual structure.
- **Suggested fix:** Wrap each language section (LanguageHeader + its per-source rows) in the same ItemsGroup card used for the request/info rows, with 16.dp spacers between groups, to match native's grouped-card layout. Remove or reconcile the HorizontalDivider usage accordingly.

**⚪ [Low] Request source dialog — minimum body length validation mismatch — The dialog enables Submit at >=5 chars but the downstream repository rejects bodies shorter than 8 chars, so 5-7 char submissions fail.** _(Input validation)_

- **Native:** FeedbackDialog.kt:49-51 gates submit at feedbackBody.length >= 5 and the native send path validates body.length >= 8 (FeedbackRepositoryImpl.kt KDoc at line 49 documents the legacy 'body.length >= 8' require). Native has the same 5-vs-8 latent gap, but it routes failures through onError → request_failed snackbar.
- **KMP:** RequestSourceDialog (SourcesScreen.kt:870, 910) gates Submit at body.length >= 5; the KMP dialog KDoc (lines 845-850) explicitly notes 'Bodies in 5-7 char range will reach the SendComplaintUseCase require(body.length >= 8) block and surface a snackbar error — Phase 10 will reconcile the UI gate (5) with the use case gate (8)'.
- **Explanation:** A 5-7 character URL/description passes the UI gate, the dialog stays open, and the user gets a generic 'Failed to submit request' snackbar with no explanation of the real cause (too short). This is an inherited issue, but it remains unreconciled in the migration and is a confusing validation UX. (Severity Low because native shares the same latent gap.)
- **Suggested fix:** Align the UI gate with the repository gate (set both to >=8, or relax the repository to >=5), and surface a specific min-length message. Update Res.string.minimum_5_characters_required accordingly if the threshold changes.

**⚪ [Low] Request source dialog — content richness vs native FeedbackDialog — The KMP request dialog omits several content sections present in the native FeedbackDialog.** _(Components / Dialog)_

- **Native:** FeedbackDialog.kt renders: title header + 'we'd love to hear from you' subtitle (line 67-71); a 'Category' label (line 81-87) (with a pinned/preselected dropdown); 'Your feedback' label (line 142); a HorizontalDivider + 'Connect with us in social media' label (line 188-192) + 'you'll receive a prompt response...' text (line 193-197) + SocialMediaRow() (line 200); a char counter '${length}/500'.
- **KMP:** RequestSourceDialog (SourcesScreen.kt:860-966) renders only: title (request_adding_source) + we_will_add_it_as_soon_it_possible body text + OutlinedTextField + char counter (body.length/500) + min-5 error. No subtitle, no Category label, no 'Your feedback' label, no divider, no social-media row, no connect-with-us text.
- **Explanation:** For the SITES_ADD use the native dialog deliberately preselects the category, but it still showed the surrounding sections (subtitle, social row, support text). The KMP dialog is a leaner bespoke dialog. This is a visual/content reduction relative to the native FeedbackDialog the native Sources screen reused. Some omissions (category dropdown) are arguably correct for a pinned-type dialog; others (social row, subtitle, support text) are content losses.
- **Suggested fix:** If full parity is desired, reuse the shared feedback dialog component (or add the subtitle, social-media row, and support text) for the Request-Source dialog. If a leaner dialog is intentional, document the deviation.

**⚪ [Low] Per-source control — Checkbox styling/colors — The per-source Checkbox lost its custom color theming.** _(Colors / Components)_

- **Native:** RepoToggleItem.kt:63-71 uses an m2 Checkbox with CheckboxDefaults.colors(checkedColor = primary, uncheckedColor = onBackground, checkmarkColor = onPrimary).
- **KMP:** SourceRow (SourcesScreen.kt:803-806) uses an m3 Checkbox with default colors (no explicit colors argument).
- **Explanation:** The native checkbox explicitly themes checked color = primary, unchecked outline = onBackground, checkmark = onPrimary. The KMP checkbox uses Material 3 defaults, which can differ in unchecked outline color and checkmark color depending on the theme, a subtle visual divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply CheckboxDefaults.colors with checkedColor = primary, uncheckedColor = onSurface/onBackground, checkmarkColor = onPrimary to the KMP Checkbox to match native tints.

**⚪ [Low] Language header / row typography — Text sizes/styles changed from explicit sp values to Material 3 type tokens.** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** SwitchItem.kt:55-57 (language header) title at fontSize=14.sp onBackground, description at 12.sp onBackground@alpha 0.5. RepoToggleItem.kt:49-59 (per-source) title 14.sp onBackground, description 12.sp onBackground@alpha 0.8. SettingsNavigationItem.kt:63 title 14.sp.
- **KMP:** LanguageHeader: title = typography.titleMedium + FontWeight.SemiBold (~16sp), subtitle = typography.bodySmall onSurfaceVariant (SourcesScreen.kt:743-756). SourceRow: api = typography.bodyMedium (~14sp), caption = bodySmall onSurfaceVariant (SourcesScreen.kt:785-797). RequestSourceRow/UpcomingLanguagesCard titles = titleMedium SemiBold.
- **Explanation:** Native uses fixed 14.sp titles / 12.sp descriptions with specific alpha values; KMP uses Material 3 type scale (titleMedium ~16sp SemiBold, bodySmall ~12-14sp, onSurfaceVariant). The resulting font sizes, weights, and the description alpha (0.5/0.8 vs onSurfaceVariant) differ, producing a slightly different visual hierarchy.
- **Suggested fix:** If pixel parity matters, override the styles to 14.sp titles and 12.sp descriptions with the native alpha values; otherwise document the Material 3 token reconciliation as intentional.

**⚪ [Low] Onboarding animated background fidelity — Native Lottie AnimatedBackground replaced by a Compose gradient sweep.** _(Components / Animations)_

- **Native:** onboarding/SourcesScreen.kt:88 calls AnimatedBackground(modifier = fillMaxSize()) (a Lottie composition) behind a vertical gradient overlay (background@0.1f → @0.3f → solid, lines 91-103).
- **KMP:** AnimatedSourcesBackground (SourcesScreen.kt:417-453) is a KMP-friendly infinite-transition linear-gradient sweep (primaryContainer@0.18 / tertiaryContainer@0.12 → surface) plus the same vertical darkening overlay; rendered only when isOnboarding. The original Lottie asset is not used.
- **Explanation:** The onboarding decorative background is a different animation (gradient sweep vs Lottie). The KMP code documents this as an intentional KMP-friendly substitution with 'no semantic value', but it is still a visual divergence from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable if a faithful animated background is not required cross-platform. To match native more closely, port the Lottie composition (compottie or equivalent) or refine the gradient to better mimic the original motion. Otherwise document as accepted deviation.

**⚪ [Low] Onboarding language name localization — Localized language display name comes from a small hardcoded English-only map instead of the platform Locale API.** _(Localization / Business logic)_

- **Native:** onboarding/SourcesScreen.kt:243-254 getLanguageName uses java.util.Locale(code).getDisplayLanguage(inLocale) (full ICU localization, respects device locale; e.g. shows Arabic endonyms on an Arabic device), with a raw-code fallback.
- **KMP:** localizedLanguageName (SourcesScreen.kt:821-836) is a static when over 13 codes returning English-only names (e.g. 'en'->'English', 'ar'->'Arabic'), with raw-code fallback. Codes outside the 13 entries display the raw code.
- **Explanation:** Native localizes language names to the device locale and covers all ISO codes; KMP returns English-only names and only for 13 enumerated codes. On a non-English device, or for an uncovered code, KMP shows a less-localized/less-complete label during onboarding. (Only affects the onboarding entry; the in-settings entry shows the raw stripped code on both.)
- **Suggested fix:** Use a KMP-capable locale display-name API (or expand the map and localize per current app language) so onboarding language labels match native's getDisplayLanguage behavior, including non-Latin endonyms and full code coverage.

**⚪ [Low] Request adding source — row label string — The request-source row title text differs.** _(Localization / Text)_

- **Native:** strings.xml: request_adding_source = 'Request Adding Source/Site'.
- **KMP:** ui/.../values/strings.xml:61: request_adding_source = 'Request adding source' (also reused verbatim as the request dialog title at SourcesScreen.kt:883).
- **Explanation:** The user-visible label changed from 'Request Adding Source/Site' (mentions both Source and Site, title-case) to 'Request adding source' (drops '/Site', sentence-case). A copy regression vs the source of truth, also propagated to the dialog title.
- **Suggested fix:** Restore the native wording 'Request Adding Source/Site' in the KMP en string (and review the ar translation) if exact copy parity is required.

**⚪ [Low] Source list ordering — Per-source ordering within a language relies on raw DB insertion order rather than an explicit priority sort.** _(Business logic / Sorting)_

- **Native:** RepoSettingsViewModel.kt:35 repoList = sourcesRepository.repoTaps.sortedBy { it.PRIORITY }; groupedByLanguage() (line 114-115) groups this priority-sorted list, so within each language sources are ordered by PRIORITY. (Native also sorts by priority in allRepos/activeRepo paths.)
- **KMP:** SourcesState.groupedByLanguage (SourcesState.kt:99-100) = items.groupBy { it.language } over the raw observeSources() list, which is legacy.allSources mapped (SourcesRepositoryImpl.kt:143-144) = raw SELECT * FROM sources with no ORDER BY. The KMP KDoc itself notes the order is 'insertion-ordered ... stable-but-arbitrary' and not priority-sorted. Source.priority exists but is never used to sort.
- **Explanation:** Native displays sources ordered by PRIORITY within each language; KMP displays them in DB insertion order (which happens to be the seed/repoMap iteration order). The orders may coincide today but are not guaranteed to match native's explicit PRIORITY ordering, a latent ordering divergence given the priority field is carried but unused.
- **Suggested fix:** Sort each language bucket by Source.priority in SourcesState.groupedByLanguage (e.g. items.sortedBy { it.priority }.groupBy { it.language }) to match native's PRIORITY ordering.

**⚪ [Low] Empty / loading states — KMP adds explicit loading and empty states that native did not render.** _(States)_

- **Native:** RepoSettingsScreen.kt has no loading or empty branch — it always renders the LazyColumn with the request row, info card, and grouped languages (the source list is a static in-memory repoTaps list, so there is no empty/loading concept).
- **KMP:** SourcesScreen.kt:373-384 branches on state.isLoading -> YamiLoadingState (centered spinner) and state.isEmpty -> YamiEmptyState('No sources available'); only otherwise renders SourcesList. State starts isLoading=true (SourcesState.kt:75) until the first Room emission.
- **Explanation:** This is a behavioral addition, not strictly a regression. However, because the request-source row and Upcoming-Languages info card live INSIDE SourcesList, when state.isEmpty is true (no sources seeded yet) the user sees only a generic 'No sources available' empty screen with NO way to request a source and no info card, whereas native would still show those affordances. Edge case but a divergence worth noting.
- **Suggested fix:** If the empty state can occur in practice, render the request-source row and info card even when the source list is empty (e.g. keep them outside the isEmpty branch), so the request affordance is never lost. Otherwise confirm the seed always runs before this screen is reachable.

</details>

### Language  `language`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 13 (🔴0 🟠1 🟡2 ⚪10)

> The KMP Language picker reproduces the core flow of the native LanguageSelectionScreen (list of supported languages, tap-to-select, persist + applyApplicationLocale side-effect, a "request a language" entry, and submit/fail snackbars), and is actually cleaner/better-localized in some respects (8-char validation now matches the use case; full en+ar strings present). However there are several concrete regressions. The most important is a BEHAVIORAL one: on first run (no stored preference) native pre-selects the device's system language because DataStoreHelper.languageFlow defaults to Locale.getDefault().language, whereas the KMP DataStoreHelper.languageFlow defaults to "" — so the KMP picker shows NO selected row on first launch. The Request-a-Language dialog was substantially simplified: native's FeedbackDialog had a category dropdown, a "We'd love to hear from you" subtitle, a live 0/500 char counter, and a "Connect with us in social media" section with a SocialMediaRow; the KMP dialog has none of these, and the onOpenUrl social-media callback the KMP screen exposes is never wired by either route adapter (dead no-op). Additional smaller divergences: the bottom-row label uses a different string (request_add_language vs native request_language), the failure snackbar drops native's Retry action label and Long duration, the selected-row icon/tint differs (Icons.Filled.Check tinted primary vs native Icons.Default.Done tinted onBackground), per-row layout/typography differs (native StatsItem renders a trailing "0" count and uses 14sp/12sp; KMP uses bodyLarge/bodySmall and no count), divider styling and placement differ (native pads dividers 12dp and draws one after the request row too; KMP draws an unpadded HorizontalDivider after each language row only), horizontal content padding is 16dp vs native 24dp, and the top bar is a plain M3 TopAppBar vs native's bold 24sp TopAppBarCom. The supported-language list, order, and endonyms match exactly (11 languages, en/ar/de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr).

**🟠 [High] Language picker — first-run selected language default — On first launch with no stored preference, native pre-selects the device system language; KMP selects nothing.** _(Business logic / app-locale default)_

- **Native:** native-app/.../core/storage/DataStoreHelper.kt:56-57 — `val languageFlow: Flow<String> = dataStore.data.map { prefs -> prefs[StorageKeys.SELECTED_LANGUAGE] ?: Locale.getDefault().language }`. The screen also seeds collectAsState with `initial = Locale.getDefault().language` (LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:64-66).
- **KMP:** platform/.../storage/DataStoreHelper.kt:64-65 — `val languageFlow: Flow<String> = settings.getStringFlow(StorageKeys.SELECTED_LANGUAGE, defaultValue = "")`. LanguageState.kt:115 `selectedCode: String = ""`. LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:133 passes the flow through unchanged.
- **Explanation:** Native always shows a highlighted (Done-icon) row matching the device language on first run, so the user sees their current language reflected. In KMP the picker opens with no row marked selected until the user taps one — the screen does not reflect the actual locale the app is currently running under. This is a functional regression in how the selected state is computed, not just cosmetic.
- **Suggested fix:** Make the KMP selected-code resolution fall back to the platform/system language when the stored value is blank. Either change the platform DataStoreHelper.languageFlow default to the system language tag (mirroring native), or add a system-locale fallback in ObserveSelectedLanguageUseCase / LanguageRepositoryImpl that maps "" to the current platform locale's language code (the ObserveSelectedLanguageUseCase KDoc even anticipates this as a future composition).
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). VERIFIED REAL and correctly characterized. Read the actual code in both apps; every cited line and the behavioral characterization check out. NATIVE (source of truth): - native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/core/storage/DataStoreHelper.kt:56-57 — `val languageFlow: Flow<String> = dataStore.data.map { prefs -> prefs[StorageKeys.SELECTED_LANGUAGE] ?: Locale.getDefault().language }`. Confirmed verbatim. (On-disk path .../me/manga/yami but Kotlin package me.manga.kira.core.storage, line 1.) - .../presentation/features/language/ui/screens/LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:64-66 — `val selectedLanguage by viewModel.selectedLanguageFlow.collectAsState(initial = Locale.getDefault().language)`. Confirmed verbatim. The selected row is highlighted at line 107: `icon = if (lang.code == selectedLanguage) Icons.Default.Done else null`. So on first run BOTH the flow default AND the collectAsState seed resolve to the device language, and the matching row shows the Done icon. KMP (new app): - platform/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/platform/storage/DataStoreHelper.kt:64-65 — `val languageFlow: Flow<String> = settings.getStringFlow(StorageKeys.SELECTED_LANGUAGE, defaultValue = "")`. Confirmed verbatim. No Locale fallback. - data/.../repository/LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:133 — `override fun observeSelectedLanguageCode(): Flow<String> = legacy.languageFlow` (pure pass-through, no map). Confirmed. - The KMP upstream delegate chain confirmed end-to-end: LanguageRepositoryImpl -> legacy SettingsRepository (shared/.../settings/domain/SettingsRepository.kt:49 `val languageFlow = ds.languageFlow`, where line 7 imports the SAME `:platform` DataStoreHelper with defaultValue="") -> ObserveSelectedLanguageUseCase.kt:76 (`invoke(): Flow<String> = repository.observeSelectedLanguageCode()`, pass-through) -> LanguageViewModel.kt:160-166 init collector projects each emission into selectedCode. - presentation/.../language/LanguageState.kt:115 — `val selectedCode: String = ""`. Confirmed. - ui/.../language/LanguageScreen.kt:285 — `selected = language.code == selectedCode`, and LanguageRow only draws the trailing check Icon when `selected` is true (lines 343-349). With selectedCode == "" on first run and no supported Language having code "" (SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES at LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:153-165 are en/ar/de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr), NO row is marked selected. Grepped the entire KMP language path (ui, presentation, domain, data) for Locale.getDefault/systemLocale/defaultLocale — the only Locale references are for the WRITE-side `applyApplicationLocale(code)` side effect (LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:139), never for computing the initial selected value. So there is definitively no system-locale seeding in KMP. CONCLUSION: On first launch with no stored preference, native pre-selects (and highlights with the Done icon) the device system language via Locale.getDefault().language in both the flow default and the collectAsState initial; KMP defaults to empty string at every layer, so the picker opens with no row marked selected. The difference is real, the file:line citations are accurate, and the functional-regression framing is correct.

**🟡 [Medium] Request-a-Language dialog — subtitle, char counter, social-media section — Native dialog includes a 'We'd love to hear from you' subtitle, a live 'N/500' character counter, a HorizontalDivider, a 'Connect with us in social media' label, a descriptive line, and a SocialMediaRow. KMP dialog has none of these.** _(UI structure / typography / components)_

- **Native:** FeedbackDialog.kt:58-72 (header + we_d_love_to_hear_from_you subtitle), :173-177 (`"${feedbackBody.length}/500"` counter), :184-201 (connect_with_us_in_social_media + descriptive text + SocialMediaRow()).
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:420-447 — title=request_add_language, a single request_language_prompt line, and the OutlinedTextField; no counter, no social section, no divider.
- **Explanation:** The native request dialog is a richer feedback surface. The KMP version drops the 0/500 length affordance, the social-media contact row, and the supporting marketing copy. Users lose the social links and the visible character budget. The strings (we_d_love_to_hear_from_you, connect_with_us_in_social_media) exist in KMP resources but are unused by this screen.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the missing dialog sections to LanguageRequestDialog: a subtitle (we_d_love_to_hear_from_you), a character counter on the OutlinedTextField supportingText, and a social-media row. Wire SocialMediaRow via the already-declared but unused onOpenUrl callback (see separate finding) so the links actually open.

**🟡 [Medium] Request-failed snackbar — Retry action + duration — Native failure snackbar shows a Retry action label with SnackbarDuration.Long; native success uses SnackbarDuration.Short. KMP shows a plain snackbar with default duration and no action for both.** _(States / interactions)_

- **Native:** LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:142-149 — onError shows `showSnackbar(message=request_failed, actionLabel=retry, duration=SnackbarDuration.Long)`; onSuccess uses `duration=SnackbarDuration.Short` (lines 134-140).
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:202-210 — `snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(submittedMessage)` / `showSnackbar(failedMessage)` with no actionLabel and no explicit duration.
- **Explanation:** On failure the native user gets a longer-lived snackbar with a Retry affordance; the KMP user gets a short, action-less message. The KMP failure path does keep the dialog open with the typed text (so retry is still possible via the dialog), but the snackbar Retry affordance and the longer display duration are lost. The retry string exists in native; KMP would need it too.
- **Suggested fix:** In the KMP effect collector, pass actionLabel (a localized 'Retry' string) and SnackbarDuration.Long for RequestFailed, and SnackbarDuration.Short for RequestSubmitted; on Retry action result, re-dispatch LanguageIntent.OnSubmitRequest (or surface the dialog) to mirror native.

**⚪ [Low] Request-a-Language dialog — category dropdown — Native FeedbackDialog renders a Category dropdown (ExposedDropdownMenuBox) listing all ComplaintType entries, pre-set to LANGUAGES; KMP dialog has no dropdown at all.** _(Components / dialog)_

- **Native:** FeedbackDialog.kt:80-135 — `ExposedDropdownMenuBox` with OutlinedTextField (label `select_a_category`, ArrowDropDown trailing icon) and an ExposedDropdownMenu of `ComplaintType.entries`.
- **KMP:** ui/.../language/LanguageScreen.kt:408-470 (LanguageRequestDialog) — only a prompt Text + one OutlinedTextField + Send/Cancel; no category selector.
- **Explanation:** On the language screen the category was always pre-set to LANGUAGES, so omitting the dropdown for this single-purpose entry is a reasonable simplification and the KMP :data impl hardcodes subject="Languages". Documented intentionally. Logged as a UI-structure divergence for completeness; no functional loss for the language flow specifically.
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable as-is for the language-specific dialog. If strict visual parity is desired, add a read-only/disabled category field showing 'Languages'; otherwise leave omitted.

**⚪ [Low] Request-a-Language dialog — social-media onOpenUrl callback is dead — KMP LanguageScreen declares an onOpenUrl callback 'for the Request-Language dialog social-media row' but neither route adapter passes it, and the dialog never invokes it.** _(Navigation / wiring / dead code)_

- **Native:** FeedbackDialog.kt:200 SocialMediaRow() opens social links directly (self-contained component).
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:169-172 declares `onOpenUrl: (String) -> Unit = {}`; LanguageScreenRoute.kt:194-197 and LanguageReworkScreenRoute.kt:125-128 call LanguageScreen(viewModel=..., onBack=...) WITHOUT passing onOpenUrl, so it stays the no-op default and LanguageRequestDialog never calls it.
- **Explanation:** The parameter is documented as 'GAP-LANG-03' restoring social-media-row parity, but it is never wired and never invoked — there is no social media row in the KMP dialog at all. It is effectively dead surface area that gives a false impression of parity.
- **Suggested fix:** Either implement the social-media row in LanguageRequestDialog and forward onOpenUrl from the route adapters to a platform URL launcher, or remove the unused onOpenUrl parameter to avoid dead/misleading API.

**⚪ [Low] Request-a-Language — bottom row label string — The clickable bottom row that opens the dialog uses a different string than native.** _(Localization / string parity)_

- **Native:** LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:115 — row title = `stringResource(R.string.request_language)` ('Request Language'). The dialog header uses request_add_language separately (line 158).
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:382 (RequestLanguageRow) — text = `stringResource(Res.string.request_add_language)` ('Request a language'). The dialog title ALSO uses request_add_language (line 419). The native `request_language` string was not carried to KMP for this row.
- **Explanation:** Native distinguishes the trigger row label ('Request Language') from the dialog header ('Request Add Language'); KMP reuses request_add_language for both the row and the dialog title. Minor copy divergence on the entry-point row.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a request_language string (en + ar) to the KMP resources and use it for RequestLanguageRow's label to match native, keeping request_add_language for the dialog title.

**⚪ [Low] Language row — selected indicator icon and tint — Selected-row checkmark uses a different vector and tint.** _(Icons / colors)_

- **Native:** LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:107 passes `icon = if (lang.code == selectedLanguage) Icons.Default.Done else null`; StatsItem.kt:51-57 tints it `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onBackground`, size 24.dp, placed at the LEADING edge.
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:343-349 — `Icon(imageVector = YamiIcons.Check, tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primary)` (YamiIcons.kt:76 `Check = Icons.Filled.Check`), in a 24.dp box at the TRAILING edge.
- **Explanation:** Native uses Icons.Filled.Done (a plain checkmark) at the row's leading edge tinted onBackground; KMP uses Icons.Filled.Check tinted primary at the trailing edge. Both are checkmarks so the difference is subtle, but the glyph, the tint color, and the leading-vs-trailing position all diverge from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide on canonical placement/tint. To match native, use Icons.Filled.Done tinted onBackground (or onSurface) at the leading edge; or explicitly accept the trailing primary-tinted Check as the new design. At minimum align the tint to a deliberate token rather than diverging by accident.

**⚪ [Low] Language row — layout, trailing count, and typography — Native StatsItem rows render a trailing value count ('0') and use 14sp title / 12sp description; KMP rows render no count and use Material3 bodyLarge / bodySmall.** _(Typography / layout / components)_

- **Native:** StatsItem.kt:63-81 — title Text fontSize 14.sp color onBackground; description Text fontSize 12.sp color onBackground alpha 0.8; ALWAYS a trailing Text `stringResource(R.string.value_count, value)` (value defaults 0 → '0') fontSize 12.sp Bold. Each row is padded vertical 12.dp.
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:328-338 — displayName Text style bodyLarge; code Text style bodySmall color onSurfaceVariant; no trailing count; trailing slot only holds the selected check. Row padding horizontal=spacing.lg vertical=spacing.md.
- **Explanation:** Native's StatsItem reuse means every language row shows a meaningless trailing '0' (a reuse artifact). KMP correctly drops the count (an improvement) but also changes the type scale (explicit 14sp/12sp vs theme bodyLarge/bodySmall) and description color (onBackground 0.8 alpha vs onSurfaceVariant). Net visual divergence in row text sizing/coloring; the dropped '0' is arguably a fix rather than a regression.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm the intended type scale. If matching native pixel-for-pixel is required, set the name to 14sp and code to 12sp with onBackground alpha 0.8. The dropped trailing '0' should be kept dropped (native artifact).

**⚪ [Low] List dividers — style and placement — Native draws a padded Divider after every row INCLUDING the request row; KMP draws an unpadded HorizontalDivider after each language row but NONE after the request row.** _(Dividers / spacing)_

- **Native:** LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:110 (`Divider(modifier = Modifier.padding(vertical = 12.dp))` after each language) and :121 (another Divider after the request_language item).
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:290 `HorizontalDivider()` (no padding) inside the language items loop; the RequestLanguageRow item (LanguageScreen.kt:292-298) has NO trailing divider.
- **Explanation:** Native has 12.dp vertical padding around each divider and a final divider beneath the Request row; KMP uses default-spacing M3 HorizontalDivider and omits the divider after the Request row. The result is tighter divider spacing and a missing bottom divider in KMP.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native by adding vertical padding (12.dp) around dividers if that spacing is desired, and add a trailing divider after the RequestLanguageRow for visual parity (or deliberately standardize on M3 list dividers and document the change).

**⚪ [Low] Content horizontal padding — Native list horizontal padding is 24.dp; KMP is 16.dp.** _(Spacing / padding)_

- **Native:** LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:99-101 — LazyColumn `.padding(horizontal = 24.dp)`.
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:239 passes `paddingHorizontal = spacing.lg` and Spacing.kt:55 defines `lg = 16.dp`; applied per-row at LanguageScreen.kt:324/369.
- **Explanation:** The picker rows sit 24.dp from the screen edges in native but 16.dp in KMP, a visible horizontal-inset difference (note native applies padding to the LazyColumn container; KMP applies it per-row, which is equivalent in effect but uses a smaller value).
- **Suggested fix:** Change the horizontal padding to spacing.xl (24.dp) to match native, or document the intentional 16.dp standardization.

**⚪ [Low] Top app bar styling — Native uses a custom TopAppBarCom (24sp Bold title, background container color); KMP uses a plain Material3 TopAppBar with default styling.** _(Toolbars / typography / colors)_

- **Native:** LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:75-88 uses TopAppBarCom; TopAppBarCom.kt:18-44 — titleSize 24.sp, fontWeight Bold, containerColor = colorScheme.background, textColor = onBackground, title maxLines 1 + Ellipsis.
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:215-227 — plain `TopAppBar(title = { Text(select_language) }, navigationIcon = {...})` with no titleSize/weight/color overrides (defaults to titleLarge, default M3 surface/onSurface colors).
- **Explanation:** The native top bar title is explicitly 24sp Bold on a background-colored container; KMP relies on M3 TopAppBar defaults (smaller, non-bold title, default surface tint). The header weight/size/background therefore differ from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply matching titleLarge.copy(fontSize = 24.sp) + FontWeight.Bold and a background container color to the KMP TopAppBar, or route it through a shared top-bar component mirroring TopAppBarCom.

**⚪ [Low] Request dialog — submit/in-flight UX and re-entrancy — KMP adds a submitting state (CircularProgressIndicator in the Send button, disabled while in-flight) and a VM re-entrancy guard; native has neither.** _(States / interactions)_

- **Native:** ComplaintViewModel.submit (ComplaintViewModel.kt:47-74) is fire-and-forget with onSuccess/onError callbacks; the native FeedbackDialog Send button has no in-flight spinner or disable-on-submit; it closes the dialog immediately on tap (LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:128-153 sets showFeedbackDialog=false synchronously).
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:449-462 shows a CircularProgressIndicator when submitting and disables the button; LanguageViewModel.kt:188-208 guards on requestSubmitting and keeps the dialog open until the result returns.
- **Explanation:** This is a KMP improvement (prevents double-submission, shows progress, keeps dialog open on failure for edit-and-retry) rather than a regression. Native closes the dialog immediately and relies solely on the snackbar. Recorded as a behavioral divergence from the source of truth for completeness; no fix needed unless strict behavioral parity is required.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix required — the KMP behavior is safer. If exact native behavior is mandated, close the dialog on Send tap and drop the in-flight spinner, but this is not recommended.

**⚪ [Low] Loading state — KMP shows a centered CircularProgressIndicator while isLoading is true; native has no loading state on this screen.** _(States)_

- **Native:** LanguageSelectionScreen.kt has no loading branch — the list renders immediately from the resource array, and the selected code seeds from collectAsState initial value.
- **KMP:** LanguageScreen.kt:230-232 + LoadingBox (256-266); LanguageState.isLoading defaults true and clears on first languageFlow emission (LanguageViewModel.kt:160-166).
- **Explanation:** Because the KMP supported list is in state from frame 1 and the DataStore flow emits sub-millisecond, the spinner is essentially never visible; still, it is a structural state that does not exist in native. Negligible user impact.
- **Suggested fix:** Optional: render the list immediately (the languages are already available) and skip the spinner entirely to match native, since isLoading only gates the trailing-check visibility, not the rows.

</details>

### Theme Picker  `theme-picker`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 14 (🔴0 🟠0 🟡4 ⚪10)

> The native theme picker exists in two places: (1) the onboarding ThemeSelectionScreen + ThemeSelector (a 3-tab Light/Dark/System TabRow with icons, a notification-permission section, and a Continue button, wrapped in a Lottie AnimatedBackground + vertical gradient overlay), and (2) the running-app SettingsScreen, which exposes the live theme controls INLINE as three SwitchItem rows (Follow System / Dark-or-Light gated toggle / Pure Black). The KMP rework collapses the native two-boolean model (followSystem + darkMode) plus pureBlack into a single :ui ThemeScreen (themepicker package) backed by an MVI ThemeViewModel + domain AppTheme tri-state + ThemeRepositoryImpl strangler-fig over the legacy SettingsRepository. The persistence backbone, tri-state translation precedence, and PureBlack/dynamicColor color logic are faithfully preserved (YamiTheme mirrors YamiMangaTheme byte-for-byte; the same KEY_THEME_MODE/KEY_THEME_SYSTEM/KEY_PURE_BLACK prefs are read/written). The KMP Settings inline theme rows (FOLLOW_SYSTEM / DARK gated / PURE_BLACK) closely match native Settings, so the core controls reach parity. However, the KMP introduces a SEPARATE standalone Theme picker screen (Screen.ThemeRework) reached from a "Theme" nav row in Settings that has NO native counterpart, and that standalone screen contains several divergences from native: it adds a TopAppBar "Theme" title that native never shows, renders the picker as a TabRow rather than native Settings' switch rows, and shows the orthogonal PureBlack switch and a "Choose Your Theme" headline. In the onboarding entry, the KMP picker drops the native Lottie AnimatedBackground + gradient overlay, restyles the Continue button (M3 default vs custom 50dp/RoundedCornerShape(26.dp)), adds a PureBlack switch the native onboarding never had, and the title style loses the explicit 24.sp override. A latent first-run pureBlack-default divergence and a Continue-gating-logic difference were also found. Strings have full en+ar parity. No crash/regression in core theming, but multiple UX-structure and styling divergences in the picker surface.

**🟡 [Medium] Standalone Theme picker screen (Screen.ThemeRework) reached from Settings nav row — KMP adds an entire standalone full-screen Theme picker reachable from a 'Theme' navigation row in the Settings hub. Native has no such screen: native exposes its live theme controls only as inline SwitchItem rows directly in SettingsScreen, and the only dedicated theme screen in native is the onboarding ThemeSelectionScreen (not reachable from Settings).** _(Navigation & screen-flow / Missing-or-extra feature)_

- **Native:** /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/settings/ui/screens/SettingsScreen.kt:131-181 (inline Follow System / Dark / Pure Black SwitchItems; NO 'Theme' nav row anywhere in the Settings nav groups at lines 213-300)
- **KMP:** /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/SettingsRoute.kt:147 (SettingsDestination.THEME -> Screen.ThemeRework) + /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/ThemeReworkScreenRoute.kt:160-167 + /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:553-559
- **Explanation:** This is an extra surface, not a missing one — the KMP Settings hub already replicates the native inline theme toggles (GAP-SET-04), so the user does not lose functionality. But it is a structural divergence from the source of truth: native has one place to change theme inline in Settings, KMP has the inline toggles AND a second deep-linked screen showing the same prefs in a different layout (TabRow + Switch). The KMP code comment itself labels it a 'KMP-EXTRA' / 'intentional rework addition'. Two surfaces editing the same KEY_* prefs can confuse users and diverge visually.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide on a single source of truth for theme editing to match native. Either remove the 'Theme' nav row (SettingsRoute.kt:147 + SettingsScreen.kt:553-559) so theme is edited only via the inline Settings toggles like native, or, if the standalone picker is kept, remove the duplicate inline toggles. Document the deviation explicitly if the product intends to keep both.

**🟡 [Medium] Onboarding Theme step — animated background / gradient overlay — Native onboarding ThemeSelectionScreen renders a full-screen Lottie AnimatedBackground (R.raw.background, IterateForever, ContentScale.FillBounds) PLUS a Brush.verticalGradient overlay of background at alpha 0.1f -> 0.3f -> 1.0f. The KMP onboarding ThemeScreen drops both and uses a flat Scaffold with neutral Material 3 surfaces.** _(Colors / gradients / background decoration)_

- **Native:** /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/onboarding/theme_selection/ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:108-127 (AnimatedBackground + verticalGradient 0.1/0.3/1.0) + WelcomeScreen.kt:119-132 (AnimatedBackground Lottie)
- **KMP:** /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/themepicker/ThemeScreen.kt:230-249 (plain Scaffold/TopAppBar, no background brush) + ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt KDoc 'AnimatedBackground gradient overlay: NOT ported'
- **Explanation:** The onboarding theme step in native is a visually rich animated screen; the KMP version is a flat utility screen. This is a clear visual regression for the onboarding flow that the user sees on first launch. The migration explicitly chose not to port it, but per the strict-parity mandate the native is the source of truth so the divergence is documented as a regression.

Requires a Compose Multiplatform Lottie equivalent and the R.raw.background asset.

### About  `about`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 19 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡7 ⚪10)

> The KMP About screen is functionally complete and covers all of native's actionable rows plus the SocialMediaRow, app logo, version row and external-launch behavior — verdict ParityPartial rather than ParityHigh because of many concrete visual/structural regressions. The most material divergences: (1) every native row carries a leading icon (AppRegistration/Update/StarRate/ManageSearch/Code) AND a trailing KeyboardArrowRight chevron via the defaulted SettingsNavigationItem; the KMP AboutRow renders NEITHER leading icons NOR trailing chevrons, so the rows read as plain two-line text. (2) Native row ORDER is Version, Check for update, Rate our app, What's new, Source code, Privacy policy; KMP reorders to Version, Check for update, Rate our app, Privacy policy, Source code, What's new. (3) Native group container is surfaceContainerHigh with a 16.dp radius and 16.dp/8.dp inner padding; KMP uses surfaceVariant with a 12.dp radius and 16.dp/12.dp padding. (4) Native uses a vertically scrollable LazyColumn; KMP uses a non-scrollable Column — a real overflow/clipping risk on short screens given the 250.dp logo + 6 rows + social row. (5) KMP adds a footer PackageLabel (reverse-DNS package id) that does not exist in native. (6) Native back affordance is an ArrowBack icon; KMP renders a text "Back" TextButton. (7) The Source-code row's labels (np_source_code / np_soon) are only defined in English in KMP — there is no values-ar entry, so Arabic users see English "Source code"/"Soon" where native localizes source_code/soon across all 12 locales. (8) Native uses Material-2 components (Scaffold/Divider/Icon); KMP uses Material-3 — minor token/ripple differences. (9) Native row title is fixed 14.sp and subtitle auto-sizes (BasicText StepBased 6-12sp, ellipsize, maxLines=1); KMP uses bodyLarge title + bodySmall description with no auto-size/ellipsize. (10) KMP includes a CircularProgressIndicator loading state that native does not have. Both sides share the SocialMediaRow 6-button adaptive layout, press-scale animation, and identical URLs; the Public/website glyph was intentionally substituted (different vector from native's earth_svgrepo_com). The rework About screen IS the live About surface (legacy Screen.AboutScreen route was swapped to render the rework AboutScreen).

**🟠 [High] About — scroll behavior / overflow — Native content is in a vertically scrollable LazyColumn; KMP content is in a non-scrollable Column.** _(Responsiveness / States)_

- **Native:** AboutScreen.kt:89-160 LazyColumn (scrollable) holds the 250.dp Image item plus the rows/social item.
- **KMP:** AboutScreen.kt:252-324 a plain Column (no verticalScroll / not Lazy) holds the 250.dp Image, 6 rows, social row, package label.
- **Explanation:** With a 250.dp logo + 24.dp vertical padding + 6 rows + spacers + social row + footer, content can exceed viewport height on small or landscape screens. Native scrolls; KMP will clip / overflow without scrolling, a real layout/crash-risk regression on short screens.
- **Suggested fix:** Wrap the KMP Column in Modifier.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState()) or convert to a LazyColumn to match native's scrollable behavior.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: High). VERIFIED REAL. Native (source of truth) /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/about/screen/AboutScreen.kt:89 uses `LazyColumn(...).fillMaxSize()` (inherently vertically scrollable). It holds the 250.dp Image as item{} at lines 99-107 (Modifier.size(250.dp).padding(vertical=24.dp)) and a second item{} at lines 108-157 containing the under-logo Divider (Color.Gray .3a), a 24.dp Spacer, an ItemsGroup with 6 SettingsNavigationItem rows + dividers, SocialMediaRow(), and trailing 24.dp Spacers. Column/LazyColumn closes at line 160. KMP /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/about/AboutScreen.kt:252 uses a plain `Column(...)` with .fillMaxSize().padding(padding).background(...).padding(spacing.lg) and verticalArrangement=Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.sm). It is NOT a LazyColumn and has NO verticalScroll/rememberScrollState — confirmed by grep returning zero hits for `verticalScroll\|rememberScrollState\|LazyColumn` in the file. It holds: 250.dp Image with 24.dp vertical padding (lines 261-268), HorizontalDivider (272), spacing.md Spacer (274), AboutItemsGroup with 6 AboutRow rows + dividers (276-315), spacing.lg Spacer (317), SocialMediaRow (319), and a PackageLabel footer (323). Column closes at line 324. The claim's file:line anchors are accurate (native 89-160; KMP 252-324) and the structural delta is confirmed: native scrolls, KMP does not. Content stack (250.dp image + 48.dp image padding + divider + spacers + 6 rows each with ~12.dp vertical row padding + social row 36-56.dp + footer) plausibly exceeds a short/landscape viewport, leaving the bottom rows (What's new, social row, package label) unreachable in KMP. ONE INACCURACY: the claim says KMP will 'clip / overflow ... a real layout/CRASH-RISK regression.' A Compose `Column` that overflows simply clips its overflowing children — it does NOT crash or throw. So this is a genuine responsiveness/clipping regression, not a crash risk. Hence PartiallyCorrect: the difference and most of the characterization are correct; only the 'crash-risk' framing is wrong. Minor: the file-level KDoc in the KMP file (lines 83-195) cites a 'legacy composeApp/.../features/about/screen/AboutScreen.kt' which no longer exists; the only on-disk native AboutScreen is the native-app path above, used as the comparison source of truth here.

**🟡 [Medium] About — row trailing chevron — Native shows a trailing KeyboardArrowRight chevron on EVERY row (it is the defaulted endIcon); KMP shows no trailing chevron on any row.** _(Icons)_

- **Suggested fix:** Switch AboutItemsGroup to surfaceContainerHigh with a 16.dp radius and match native's flat background (Column with .background instead of an elevated Card, or Card with 0 elevation). Align inner padding to 16.dp/8.dp.

**🟡 [Medium] About — external link launch strategy (app-first deep links) — Native attempts native-app deep-link URIs first (twitter://, fb://, instagram://, whatsapp://) then falls back to web/Custom Tabs; KMP always passes the plain web URL.** _(Business logic / API behavior)_

- **Native:** openLink.kt:70-104 openTwitter/openFacebook/openInstagram try app:// scheme, then web Intent chooser, then CustomTabsIntent; sendWhatsAppMessage (113-171) tries com.whatsapp / com.whatsapp.w4b packages first.
- **KMP:** AboutScreen.kt:420-436 constants are web URLs only (twitter.com, facebook.com, instagram.com, api.whatsapp.com); AboutIntent.OnOpenUrl -> AboutEffect.OpenUrl -> IntentLauncher.openUrl(url) with no app-scheme attempt (AboutReworkScreenRoute.kt:149).
- **Explanation:** Native opens the installed Twitter/Facebook/Instagram/WhatsApp app directly when present (better UX); KMP always opens the browser/web URL. This is a behavioral regression in deep-link handling, plus the native Custom Tabs in-app fallback is lost.
- **Suggested fix:** Extend IntentLauncher (or the effect) to try platform app-scheme deep links first with web fallback, mirroring openLink.kt; at minimum document that KMP intentionally uses web-only links. WhatsApp normalization (Egypt 0->20 prefix) is preserved in the literal but the app-package-first attempt is not.

**⚪ [Low] About — SocialMediaRow press-scale animation spec — Press-scale animation stiffness/reset mechanism differs slightly.** _(Interactions / animations)_

- **Native:** SocialMediaRow.kt:120-127 animateFloatAsState spring(DampingRatioMediumBouncy, stiffness=StiffnessHigh) plus a manual 150ms LaunchedEffect reset of isPressed.
- **KMP:** AboutScreen.kt:546-550 animateFloatAsState spring(DampingRatioMediumBouncy) with default stiffness, driven by interactionSource.collectIsPressedAsState (no explicit StiffnessHigh, no manual delay reset).

- **Suggested fix:** Add stiffness = Spring.StiffnessHigh to the KMP spring to match native's snappier feedback. Behaviorally close; low priority.

- **Suggested fix:** Apply only top inset (and horizontal 16.dp) like native, or reconcile the extra uniform 16.dp so vertical rhythm matches the source.

### What's New  `whatsnew`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 21 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡7 ⚪12)

> Native implements What's New as a full-screen MVVM/Hilt feature: a HorizontalPager of FeatureCards (media at top via AutoSubtitleText auto-sizing title/description), a transparent header with bold title + circular Close button, animated page-indicator pills, Previous/Next/Get-Started navigation buttons, an inline Android VideoView player with fullscreen, image carousels (drawable-res AND URL), and a fullscreen media overlay. It is triggered on app launch from LibraryRoute when versionCode (Int) > last-shown, and reachable from About via WhatsNewScreen(false). The KMP rework ports most of this into a strict-MVI slice (:domain model/usecases, :presentation VM/state/intent/effect, :ui WhatsNewScreen) and actually does render a pager, nav buttons, indicators, Coil single-image + URL carousel, a tappable video poster, a fullscreen image Dialog, and a NEW chip — despite many KDocs that incorrectly claim these are "deferred"/"not ported" (the KDocs are stale; the code is more complete than they say). The headline divergences are: (1) the trigger gate moved from versionCode-Int comparison to versionName-String inequality (different semantics, downgrade-shows bug); (2) inline video playback replaced by an external-open poster (DEVIATION); (3) the :data mapper hard-codes imageUrlList = emptyList(), so multi-URL carousels from the remote JSON never render; (4) AutoSubtitleText auto-sizing typography replaced by fixed Material titleMedium/bodyMedium; (5) the de-facto reachable surface is the empty state because getDefaultFeatures() returns emptyList() and the remote success path drives content; (6) missing Arabic translations for nav buttons + fullscreen caption; (7) several layout/spacing/string-casing deltas. Loading/Error/Empty states are present but use shared Yami* components rather than native's inline versions.
