**🟠 [High] What's New — inline video playback — Native plays feature videos inline with a real player; KMP shows a static poster that opens the URL externally** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — FeatureCard.kt:166-181 renders SafeVideoPlayer (Android VideoView) with play/pause tap, looping, lifecycle pause/resume, 10s load-timeout, error+retry placeholder, and an in-card Fullscreen button (VideoComponents.kt:34-274).
- **KMP:** No (substitute) — WhatsNewScreen.kt:772-796 VideoPoster is a tappable card with a play glyph that emits WhatsNewIntent.OnOpenVideo → WhatsNewEffect.OpenVideo → IntentLauncher.openUrl (WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt:223). No inline playback, no loop, no in-place fullscreen, no error/retry.
- **Explanation:** A VIDEO feature in native plays a looping muted preview directly inside the card and can be expanded fullscreen in-app. In KMP, tapping the poster leaves the app to an external browser/video handler. This is a documented DEVIATION(platform) but is a real user-facing capability loss for any VIDEO-type What's New entry (native's commented default features include `home_scroll.mp4`).
- **Suggested fix:** Introduce a cross-platform inline video player SPI (the deferred :platform MediaPlayer) and render it in FeatureMedia for MediaType.VIDEO, restoring inline play/pause + fullscreen; until then keep the poster but clearly label it as 'opens externally'.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth) — inline player confirmed exactly as claimed: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/whatsnew/ui/components/FeatureCard.kt:166-181 — MediaType.VIDEO branch renders SafeVideoPlayer(videoUrl=feature.videoUrl, isActive, onFullscreenClick={ onMediaClick(MediaType.VIDEO,...,feature.videoUrl) }) at height mediaSize*0.75f when feature.videoUrl != null && showSmallVideo (else VideoPlaceholder). - VideoComponents.kt:34-274 SafeVideoPlayer: real Android VideoView via AndroidView (122-173); tap toggles play/pause (clickable box 200-221, play glyph 224-246); mediaPlayer.isLooping=true (135); lifecycle ON_PAUSE pause / ON_RESUME resume / ON_DESTROY release (69-108); 10s load timeout -> hasError (60-67); VideoErrorPlaceholder with Retry (113-120, 276-303); in-card Fullscreen IconButton bottom-end firing onFullscreenClick (248-267). The on-disk folder is me/manga/yami but the package is me.manga.kira (per task note); line numbers match the claim. KMP — static poster + external open confirmed exactly as claimed: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/whatsnew/WhatsNewScreen.kt:643-647 FeatureMedia VIDEO branch calls VideoPoster(onClick={ onOpenVideo(url) }); VideoPoster at 772-796 is a non-playing Box (MEDIA_SIZE x 0.75f) with a centered Play glyph, no VideoView/loop/fullscreen/error-retry. - Wiring: onOpenVideo -> WhatsNewIntent.OnOpenVideo (presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewIntent.kt:116) -> VM emits WhatsNewEffect.OpenVideo (WhatsNewEffect.kt:95) -> route /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/.../navigation/routes/WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt:223 `is WhatsNewEffect.OpenVideo -> launcher.openUrl(effect.url)` (same in WhatsNewReworkScreenRoute.kt:87). Confirms external-open substitute. Nuances (do not refute the claim): 1. A real PlatformVideoPlayer SPI with an Android VideoView actual DOES exist at composeApp/src/androidMain/.../core/platform/VideoPlayerSlot.android.kt (and expect at commonMain/.../VideoPlayerSlot.kt:79), ported from the Help Video dialog. But it is NOT wired into What's New — grep for actual `PlatformVideoPlayer(` call sites returns zero; the only WhatsNew references are KDoc text (WhatsNewScreen.kt:768, WhatsNewEffect.kt). So an inline player exists in the project yet is unused by What's New, which genuinely uses openUrl. Claim stands. 2. Reachability: native getDefaultFeatures.kt:8-45 returns an empty list — the home_scroll.mp4 VIDEO entry (lines 67-68) is commented out, as are all defaults. VIDEO entries are only reachable via remote data today. The claim itself notes the defaults are commented, so this is acknowledged.

**🟠 [High] What's New — multi-image URL carousel data — :data mapper hard-codes imageUrlList = emptyList(), so remote multi-image carousels never render** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewViewModel.kt:120-130 maps `imageUrlList = localized.imageList`; FeatureCard.kt:132-140 renders ImageUrlsCarousel when imageUrlList is non-empty.
- **KMP:** No — WhatsNewRepositoryImpl.kt:129 sets `imageUrlList = emptyList()` on the remote-success path (while `imageResName/imageResNameList` get localized.imageRes/imageList). The :ui ImageUrlCarousel (WhatsNewScreen.kt:710) reads imageUrlList, which is always empty from remote, so the carousel branch never triggers and falls through to a single image or placeholder.
- **Explanation:** On the remote-success path the KMP mapper discards the carousel list into imageResNameList (drawable names, which :ui never resolves because bundled drawables aren't packaged in :ui) and forces imageUrlList empty. Net result: a What's New feature that the server delivers as a multi-image gallery renders as at most a single image (imageUrl) or a placeholder in KMP, whereas native shows the full swipeable thumbnail carousel. Note the legacy getLocalizedFeature maps imageList from imageResList (resource names), so neither path yields URL carousels in KMP.
- **Suggested fix:** Map imageUrlList from the remote feature's URL list field (and have getLocalizedFeature expose the URL list) instead of forcing emptyList(); ensure the :ui ImageUrlCarousel receives the same data native feeds ImageUrlsCarousel.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). The mapping divergence is REAL and correctly characterized. NATIVE (source of truth) — wire `imageResList` becomes a URL carousel: - native-app/.../whatsnew/data/RemoteData.kt:11 — `val imageResList: List<String> = emptyList()` (a list of strings on the wire). - native-app/.../whatsnew/data/WhatsNewRemoteDataSource.kt:96-106 — getLocalizedFeature sets `imageList = feature.imageResList` and `imageRes = feature.imageRes`. - native-app/.../whatsnew/viewmodel/WhatsNewViewModel.kt:120-130 — maps `imageUrlList = localized.imageList` (so the wire `imageResList` strings are treated as URLs) and `imageRes = parseImageResource(localized.imageRes)`. - native-app/.../whatsnew/ui/components/FeatureCard.kt:120-164 — FeatureMedia for MediaType.IMAGE checks `imageResList` (Android @DrawableRes ints, empty for remote), then `imageUrlList.isNotEmpty()` -> ImageUrlsCarousel (lines 132-140), then single imageRes, then single imageUrl, else placeholder. - native-app/.../whatsnew/ui/components/ImageComponents.kt:99-218 — ImageUrlsCarousel loads each URL via Coil SubcomposeAsyncImage (lines 115-119, 189-193). So native renders a full swipeable URL thumbnail carousel from the wire `imageResList`. KMP — same wire field, but mapper discards it: - shared/.../whatsnew/data/RemoteData.kt:11 and LocalizedFeature.kt:8 and WhatsNewRemoteDataSource.kt:97-98 are IDENTICAL to native: `imageList = feature.imageResList`. - data/.../repository/WhatsNewRepositoryImpl.kt:122-133 (remote-success path) maps `imageResName = localized.imageRes`, `imageResNameList = localized.imageList`, `imageUrl = localized.imageUrl`, and HARD-CODES `imageUrlList = emptyList()` (line 129). So the wire carousel list is routed into imageResNameList and imageUrlList is forced empty — exactly as claimed. - domain/.../usecase/whatsnew/GetWhatsNewFeaturesUseCase.kt:77 is a pure pass-through (`repository.getFeatures()`); presentation/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewViewModel.kt:163-167 stores the list into state.features unchanged. No re-mapping downstream. - ui/.../whatsnew/WhatsNewScreen.kt FeatureMedia (lines 642-670): MediaType.LIST renders ImageUrlCarousel only if `imageUrlList.isNotEmpty()` (line 650); MediaType.IMAGE/URL renders ImageUrlCarousel if `imageUrlList.isNotEmpty()` (line 659) else single imageUrl else Unit. There is NO branch reading imageResNameList/imageResName; the KDoc at lines 627-629 explicitly states bundled drawable names are not packaged in :ui. ImageUrlCarousel (lines 710-763) is a fully working Coil URL carousel mirroring native, but it is never fed data from remote because imageUrlList is always empty. Both KMP routes that reach this screen (App.kt:605-611 legacy `WhatsNewScreenRoute`, reachable from LibraryScreenRoute.kt:176 `Screen.WhatsNewScreen(true)`, and App.kt:790 `WhatsNewReworkScreenRoute`) render the SAME :ui WhatsNewScreen via the SAME repository, so the defect affects the user-reachable screen, not just a dev route. CAVEAT (affects severity): The live production endpoint https://yamimanga.me/whatsnew/35/whatsnew.json currently returns only 2 features, both mediaType=IMAGE with a single `imageUrl` (full http URLs) and NO `imageResList`. With the current payload there is no observable difference (neither app shows a carousel today). The bug is a genuine latent mapping defect that manifests only when the server delivers an `imageResList` multi-image feature — at which point native shows the carousel and KMP shows at most a single image or nothing. The claim's mechanism is exactly right; its 'currently renders as single image/placeholder' framing assumes server data that is not present in the live feed right now.

**🟡 [Medium] What's New — per-version trigger/gating — Version-bump comparison changed from versionCode (Int, greater-than) to versionName (String, inequality)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewViewModel.kt:66-82 + getCurrentVersionCode():229-248 compute `shouldShow = currentVersion > lastVersion` on the integer versionCode; key `whats_new_last_shown_version` (Int) at line 36-40.
- **KMP:** Partial — shared WhatsNewViewModel.kt:171-186 computes `shouldShow = currentVersion.isNotBlank() && currentVersion != lastVersion` on `appVersionProvider.versionName` (String); key `whats_new_last_shown_version_name` (String) at line 230.
- **Explanation:** Native uses a monotonically-increasing integer versionCode with a strict greater-than, so a DOWNGRADE (installing an older build) does NOT re-show What's New. KMP compares versionName strings for inequality, so any change in versionName — including a downgrade or even a marketing-string change that doesn't bump the build — re-shows What's New. The semantics differ: native = 'show only when newer', KMP = 'show whenever the version string differs'. Also versionName equality can collide across distinct builds that share a versionName, suppressing What's New that native would show.
- **Suggested fix:** If a portable integer versionCode is available via AppVersionProvider, restore the greater-than comparison; otherwise document/accept the versionName-inequality behavior and at minimum guard against downgrades (store-and-compare an ordered build identifier) to match native's 'only on newer version' contract.

**🟡 [Medium] What's New — bundled drawable image rendering — Native renders bundled @DrawableRes images (single + carousel); KMP cannot resolve drawable names and falls through to placeholder** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — FeatureCard.kt:121-164 supports imageResList (ImageCarousel), imageRes (SingleImage via painterResource), in addition to URL variants; ImageComponents.kt:32-96/220-236.
- **KMP:** No — WhatsNewScreen.kt:636-671 FeatureMedia only handles imageUrlList (URL carousel) and imageUrl (single Coil image); the comment at lines 626-633 states bundled imageResName(List) drawables are 'not packaged in :ui composeResources' so the resource-name branches 'fall through to the placeholder'. WhatsNewFeature carries imageResName/imageResNameList but :ui never reads them.
- **Explanation:** If the remote JSON (or restored default features) reference bundled drawable names rather than URLs, native shows the actual artwork while KMP shows nothing rendered for that branch (no placeholder is even emitted in FeatureMedia — the IMAGE branch returns Unit when only resource names are present). This silently drops imagery for resource-name-based features.
- **Suggested fix:** Either package the relevant drawables into :ui composeResources and resolve imageResName via Res.drawable lookup, or guarantee the data layer always provides URLs; at minimum emit the ImagePlaceholder (title initials) when only resource names are present so the card is not blank.

**🟡 [Medium] What's New — title/description typography (AutoSubtitleText) — Native auto-sizes title/description with explicit min/max sp and tablet scaling; KMP uses fixed Material titleMedium/bodyMedium** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — FeatureCard.kt:86-105 uses AutoSubtitleText: title FontWeight.Bold, fontSize 26sp phone / 32sp tablet, maxSize 32/36sp, minSize 20sp, maxLines 2; description fontSize 15/18sp, maxSize 18/20sp, minSize 12sp, maxLines 15, both TextAlign.Center.
- **KMP:** No — WhatsNewScreen.kt:598-615 title is MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium + FontWeight.SemiBold, left/weighted (start-aligned in a Row), no auto-size, default maxLines; description is bodyMedium, start-aligned, no maxLines cap and no auto-size.
- **Explanation:** Native centers both title and description and auto-shrinks/grows the text to fit (StepBased autosize) with tablet-specific larger sizes and a 2-line title cap. KMP renders a fixed-size titleMedium (~16sp) SemiBold title left-aligned beside the NEW chip and a fixed bodyMedium description left-aligned. The visual weight, alignment (center vs start), font sizes, weight (Bold vs SemiBold), and tablet scaling all differ, and long titles won't be clamped to 2 lines.
- **Suggested fix:** Render title centered + Bold with larger size (and tablet scaling), description centered, and apply auto-sizing (BasicText autoSize) or at least the native min/max sp + maxLines (2 / 15) to match the native FeatureCard typography.

**🟡 [Medium] What's New — header layout & Close button styling — Native uses a custom Row header with a circular tinted Close button; KMP uses a Material3 TopAppBar with a plain IconButton action** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewComponents.kt:21-63: Surface(tonalElevation 2.dp, transparent) with a Row(padding horizontal=horizontalPadding, vertical=12.dp, SpaceBetween) holding a bold headlineSmall title and a 40.dp IconButton with surfaceVariant@0.5 circular background containing Icons.Default.Close.
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:263-284: a Material3 TopAppBar(transparent container) with bold title text and an actions IconButton (YamiIcons.Close) that has no circular background/tint. The Close also dispatches OnMarkSeen + onGetStarted (native header Close does NOT mark seen).
- **Explanation:** Native's header is a transparent custom row over the gradient with a distinct circular surfaceVariant-backed close affordance and headlineSmall bold title. KMP renders a standard TopAppBar (different default height/insets/title style ~titleLarge) with a bare close icon (no circular chip). Functionally the KMP header Close also marks the version seen and pops, whereas native's header Close only dismisses (mark-seen happens in the route's onDismiss only when isFirstOpen).
- **Suggested fix:** Replace the TopAppBar with a transparent Row header matching native padding (h=horizontalPadding, v=12.dp), use a 40.dp circular surfaceVariant@0.5 IconButton, and a headlineSmall Bold title; reconcile mark-seen semantics so the header Close matches native (dismiss-only) behavior.

**🟡 [Medium] What's New — fullscreen media viewer (zoom, video, instructions chip) — Native fullscreen viewer supports image AND video and a styled instruction chip; KMP fullscreen is image-only with a plain caption, no zoom** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — FullscreenMediaViewer.kt:26-140 handles MediaType.IMAGE (res or URL via SubcomposeAsyncImage with loading/error) AND MediaType.VIDEO (SafeVideoPlayer fullscreen); close IconButton 48.dp on surface@0.9 circular bg; 'tap_outside_to_close' Text in a rounded surface@0.9 chip at bottom.
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:481-528 FullscreenMediaViewer is a Dialog showing a single Coil AsyncImage only (no video), close IconButton has no circular background, and the caption is a plain white@0.7 bodySmall Text (no rounded surface chip). No pinch-zoom on either side, but native at least supports video fullscreen.
- **Explanation:** Native can open BOTH images and the video in fullscreen and styles the close button and 'tap outside to close' hint as surface-backed chips. KMP only opens images fullscreen (video never reaches fullscreen because it opens externally), the close button is unstyled, and the instruction text is a bare label. The fullscreen affordance for video is entirely absent.
- **Suggested fix:** When inline video lands, route the video poster's fullscreen to the same viewer; style the close button with a circular surface@0.9 background and wrap the caption in a rounded surface@0.9 chip to match FullscreenMediaViewer.kt:108-139.

**🟡 [Medium] What's New — Arabic localization for navigation buttons & fullscreen caption — np_previous / np_next / np_get_started / np_whats_new_close / np_close / np_tap_outside_to_close have no Arabic translations in KMP** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — native uses previous/next/get_started/close/tap_outside_to_close keys; native ships full per-language strings (RemoteData supports en,ar,de,es,fr,in,it,ja,pt,ru,tr) and the static labels are localized via res/values-ar.
- **KMP:** No — the rework screen uses np_previous/np_next/np_get_started/np_whats_new_close/np_close/np_tap_outside_to_close (ui/.../values/strings_np_complaint_etc.xml:35-41 and strings_np_p2_complaint_etc.xml:29). A search of ui/.../values-ar/ returns NO entries for any of these np_ keys, so Arabic users see English 'Previous/Next/Get Started/Close/Tap outside to close'.
- **Explanation:** The shared/new What's New labels (what_s_new, new_badge, whats_new_empty) have Arabic translations, but the navigation buttons and fullscreen caption (np_* keys) are only present in the default English file. In an Arabic locale these controls render in English, breaking localization parity with native which localizes Previous/Next/Get Started/Close.
- **Suggested fix:** Add Arabic (and the other supported languages) translations for np_previous, np_next, np_get_started, np_close, np_whats_new_close, and np_tap_outside_to_close in ui/.../values-ar/strings*.xml.

**🟡 [Medium] What's New — remote fetch language & i18n of content — Rework :data hard-codes language 'en' for the feature fetch, dropping per-user localized content; native/legacy use the user's selected language** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewViewModel.kt:103/173-181 uses the device/user language code (getUserLanguageCode) and getLocalizedFeature picks the localized title/description; legacy KMP shared VM uses DataStoreHelper.languageFlow.first().
- **KMP:** No — WhatsNewRepositoryImpl.kt:110/120/168 passes LANGUAGE_CODE_DEFAULT = "en" to fetchWhatsNewFeatures and getLocalizedFeature, so the rework display screen always requests/binds English copy regardless of the user's chosen language.
- **Explanation:** The remote JSON delivers per-language title/description maps (en,ar,de,es,fr,in,it,ja,pt,ru,tr). Native and the legacy gating VM resolve the user's language; the rework :data impl that backs the displayed screen hard-codes 'en'. An Arabic (or other non-English) user who reaches the rework What's New content would see English feature copy, unlike native. (Documented as deferred Phase 7.x.whatsnew.i18n.)
- **Suggested fix:** Thread the user's selected language (DataStoreHelper.languageFlow) into getFeatures() and getLocalizedFeature instead of the hard-coded 'en', matching native/legacy localization.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — responsive padding & sizing (tablet/landscape) — Native adapts horizontalPadding, cardPadding, mediaSize and card max-height to tablet/landscape; KMP uses fixed LocalSpacing and a fixed 220.dp media size** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewScreen.kt:36-51 derives isLandscape/isTablet and sets horizontalPadding 32/16.dp, cardPadding 32/16/24.dp; FeatureCard.kt:38-45 mediaSize 300/280/180/220.dp and maxCardHeight 0.85/0.75; card fillMaxHeight(maxCardHeight).
- **KMP:** No — WhatsNewScreen.kt:621 MEDIA_SIZE is a fixed 220.dp; FeatureCard uses spacing.lg padding; pager contentPadding = spacing.lg; the Card has no fillMaxHeight fraction. No isTablet/isLandscape branching anywhere in the rework screen.
- **Explanation:** On tablets and landscape, native enlarges media (up to 300.dp), increases padding (32.dp), and constrains the card to 75–85% of height. KMP keeps a constant 220.dp media and constant spacing on all form factors, so on large screens the card/media looks small and the layout doesn't adapt. Compose Multiplatform also runs on desktop/iOS where this matters more.
- **Suggested fix:** Add window-size-class (or BoxWithConstraints) branching to scale horizontalPadding, cardPadding, media size, and a card max-height fraction to mirror native's tablet/landscape values.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — card slide-in animation direction & shape — Native FeatureCard animates horizontal slide+fade keyed to active page; KMP animates a vertical slide+fade keyed to page composition** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — FeatureCard.kt:50-60 AnimatedVisibility(visible=isActive) with slideInHorizontally(initialOffsetX={it}) + fadeIn (tween 250) and slideOutHorizontally(targetOffsetX={-it}) + fadeOut.
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:393-399 AnimatedVisibility with fadeIn(250) + slideInVertically(250){ it/8 } only (no exit transition; key on page composition, not isActive).
- **Explanation:** Native slides each card in from the right and out to the left (horizontal, tied to the active page), reinforcing the pager direction. KMP does a small upward vertical slide + fade on first composition of each page and has no exit animation. The motion direction and feel differ, though both are minor cosmetic effects layered on top of the pager's own horizontal scroll.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native by using slideInHorizontally/slideOutHorizontally + fade keyed to the active page (or drop the per-card animation entirely and rely on the pager) for consistent horizontal motion.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — page indicator unselected color token — Native unselected indicator uses outline@0.3; KMP uses onSurfaceVariant@0.3** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewComponents.kt:88-92: selected = colorScheme.primary, unselected = colorScheme.outline.copy(alpha=0.3f); horizontal padding 3.dp; selected pill 24x8, unselected 8x8, RoundedCornerShape(4.dp).
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:547-557: selected = primary, unselected = onSurfaceVariant.copy(alpha=0.3f); padding spacing.xxs (value depends on token, native is 3.dp); same 24x8 / 8x8 / r4 geometry.
- **Explanation:** Geometry matches, but the unselected dot color token differs (outline vs onSurfaceVariant), which produces a slightly different unselected dot shade, and the horizontal spacing uses LocalSpacing.xxs instead of a literal 3.dp so it may not match exactly.
- **Suggested fix:** Use colorScheme.outline.copy(alpha=0.3f) for unselected indicators and 3.dp horizontal padding to match native PageIndicators exactly.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — navigation buttons (first-page spacer width, button paddings) — Native reserves an 80.dp spacer on the first page and uses explicit contentPadding (h=20,v=10) on all buttons; KMP uses a 1.dp spacer and default button paddings** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewComponents.kt:114-139: first page → Spacer(width=80.dp); Previous=OutlinedButton, Next=Button, last page=Get-Started Button, each with contentPadding(horizontal=20.dp, vertical=10.dp).
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:457-472: first page → Spacer(Modifier.width(1.dp)); OutlinedButton/Button use default Material content padding; row padding from LocalSpacing rather than horizontalPadding=16/32.dp.
- **Explanation:** Native keeps the Next/Get-Started button right-aligned with a fixed 80.dp left spacer and gives all buttons consistent enlarged content padding (20x10). KMP uses a 1.dp spacer (Next still right-aligns via SpaceBetween, so behavior is OK) but loses the explicit button content padding, making the buttons slightly smaller, and uses spacing-token row padding instead of the responsive horizontalPadding.
- **Suggested fix:** Apply contentPadding(horizontal=20.dp, vertical=10.dp) to the three buttons and use the responsive horizontalPadding for the row to match native button sizing/margins.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — Loading state copy & layout — Native loading state shows a 48.dp spinner (strokeWidth 4) + 'Loading What's New...' label; KMP shows the shared YamiLoadingState with no label** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewRoute.kt:60-81 LoadingState: centered Column with CircularProgressIndicator(48.dp, stroke 4.dp) and Text 'Loading What's New...' bodyLarge.
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:314-317 LoadingState delegates to YamiLoadingState (shared component) with only Scaffold padding; no descriptive label.
- **Explanation:** The loading affordance is present in both, but native shows a contextual 'Loading What's New...' label and a specific 48.dp/4.dp spinner; KMP uses the generic shared loading component without the label. Minor visual/text divergence on a transient state.
- **Suggested fix:** Optionally pass a 'Loading What's New…' message to YamiLoadingState (or render a labeled spinner) to match native; low priority since it's transient.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — Empty state layout (card vs centered text) & Close action — Native empty state is a centered elevated Card with title, body and a Close button; KMP empty state is a shared YamiEmptyState title-only with no action** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewRoute.kt:131-167 EmptyState: Card(elevation 4) with 'No Updates Available' headlineSmall, 'There are no new features to show at this time.' bodyMedium, and a Close Button that pops back.
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:330-335 EmptyState delegates to YamiEmptyState(title = whats_new_empty 'No new features in this version') with no body text and no Close button (relies on system back).
- **Explanation:** This empty state is the de-facto reachable surface in KMP (because getDefaultFeatures() returns emptyList() and content depends on the remote success path). Native presents a styled card with explicit title/body and an in-screen Close button; KMP shows a single-line empty state with no Close affordance and different copy. On desktop (no system back gesture), the missing Close is more impactful.
- **Suggested fix:** Match native by adding a body line and an explicit Close/Get-Started button in the empty state (especially for desktop), or confirm system-back is always available on the target platforms.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — Error state Close affordance — Native error state offers both Close and Retry; KMP error state offers only Retry** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewRoute.kt:83-129 ErrorState: Card with 'Failed to Load' headlineSmall (error color), the error message, and a Row with OutlinedButton 'Close' + Button 'Retry'.
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:319-327 ErrorState delegates to YamiErrorState(message, retryLabel, onRetry) — Retry only, no Close. Note both error paths are largely dormant because the :data impl swallows failures and returns the empty default list (WhatsNewRepositoryImpl.kt:138).
- **Explanation:** Native lets the user dismiss the error without retrying via a Close button; KMP only offers Retry and relies on system back. Both are mostly unreachable today because WhatsNewRepositoryImpl falls back to an empty list on remote failure rather than surfacing an error, but the affordance and the error-surfacing path diverge from native (which keeps loadError and renders the error card).
- **Suggested fix:** Add a Close button to the error state (parity with native) and decide whether remote failures should surface as the error state (native keeps loadError) rather than silently collapsing to empty.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — gradient/scrim parity — Background gradient matches native, but KMP applies it on the Scaffold while native applies it on a full-size Box behind a Column** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewScreen.kt:53-64 Box.fillMaxSize background Brush.verticalGradient(primaryContainer@0.3 → surface).
- **KMP:** Yes — WhatsNewScreen.kt:247-257 Scaffold modifier .fillMaxSize().background(same verticalGradient) with transparent containerColor and transparent TopAppBar.
- **Explanation:** The gradient colors and alpha match exactly (primaryContainer@0.3 → surface). The only structural difference is the container (Scaffold vs Box+Column) and the TopAppBar insets; visually near-identical. Recorded for completeness as a structural divergence rather than a defect.
- **Suggested fix:** No change needed for the gradient itself; ensure the TopAppBar insets/height don't shift content relative to native (covered by the header finding).

**⚪ [Low] What's New — card container color & NEW chip placement — Native card uses default Card surface with centered content and no inline NEW chip on the card; KMP card uses surfaceVariant container with a left-aligned title Row + inline NEW chip** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — FeatureCard.kt:62-106 Card(RoundedCornerShape 20, elevation 4) default container color; content centered; no per-card NEW chip rendered (isNew exists on the model but native FeatureCard does not draw a NEW badge).
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:578-617 Card(shape r20, elevation 4) but containerColor = surfaceVariant; title in a start-aligned Row with a NewChip (WhatsNewScreen.kt:803-818) when feature.isNew.
- **Explanation:** KMP adds a 'NEW' chip beside the title (a small enhancement) and tints the card surfaceVariant, whereas native uses the default Card surface and does not draw a NEW badge in FeatureCard. The chip addition and the start-aligned title (vs native centered) change the card's visual composition. The chip itself is not a regression, but the container color and title alignment diverge from native.
- **Suggested fix:** Center the title (matching native) or keep the chip but align with native's centered layout; reconsider surfaceVariant vs the default Card container to match native's appearance.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — title string casing — Header title text differs in casing: native 'What\'s New' vs KMP 'What\'s new'** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — res/values/strings.xml:454 whats_new_title = "What's New".
- **KMP:** Partial — ui/.../values/strings.xml:24 what_s_new = "What's new" (lowercase 'new').
- **Explanation:** The header uses a different key with different casing. Native renders 'What's New'; KMP renders 'What's new'. Minor cosmetic/text inconsistency in the screen title.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the casing (use 'What\'s New') if exact parity with native is desired, or accept the rework's house style consistently.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — About-screen entry point & mark-seen behavior — Native About row calls ensureFeaturesLoaded() then navigates with isFirstOpen=false; KMP About row navigates to a separate WhatsNewRework route (no isFirstOpen, separate VM instance)** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — AboutScreen.kt:134-139 'What's New' SettingsNavigationItem calls whatsNewViewModel.ensureFeaturesLoaded() then navController.navigate(Screen.WhatsNewScreen(false)); both auto-popup and About paths share one Hilt VM.
- **KMP:** Partial — About row dispatches AboutIntent.OnOpenWhatsNew → AboutEffect.NavigateToWhatsNew → navController.navigate(Screen.WhatsNewRework) (AboutReworkScreenRoute.kt:150); Settings hub also routes WHATSNEW → Screen.WhatsNewRework (SettingsRoute.kt:153). The auto-popup path uses Screen.WhatsNewScreen(true) via the legacy shared VM (LibraryScreenRoute.kt:176). The two routes use different NavBackStackEntry-scoped rework VM instances.
- **Explanation:** Both apps reach What's New from About without marking it seen (native isFirstOpen=false; KMP WhatsNewRework has no mark-seen). Behaviorally equivalent for gating. Divergences: native pre-warms features via ensureFeaturesLoaded() before navigating (avoids a loading flash), while KMP loads in the VM init on mount; and KMP splits the entry into two route types (WhatsNewScreen for first-open, WhatsNewRework for About/Settings) backed by independent VM instances, whereas native shares a single VM. Functionally close but structurally different.
- **Suggested fix:** Optionally consolidate the two KMP routes onto one entry to avoid duplicate VM instances and pre-load features when navigating from About; verify no double-fetch occurs across the two routes.

**⚪ [Low] What's New — KDoc/implementation drift (audit hazard) — Multiple KMP KDocs claim pager/images/video/fullscreen/nav-buttons are 'not ported / deferred' while the code actually implements them** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes (reference behavior present in native).
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt KDoc lines 116-209 state 'flat LazyColumn', 'No image rendering', 'No video rendering', 'No FullscreenMediaViewer', 'NavigationButtons NOT ported'; WhatsNewState/Intent/Effect/Repository KDocs repeat 'empty effect', 'foundation renders title+description only', etc. The actual code (WhatsNewScreen.kt:383-433/498/646/772, WhatsNewEffect.OpenVideo) implements pager, images, video poster, fullscreen image, and nav buttons.
- **Explanation:** The extensive 'audit-trail' KDocs are stale and internally contradictory with the shipped code (e.g., they claim WhatsNewEffect is an empty sealed interface and that nav buttons aren't ported, yet OpenVideo exists and NavigationButtons is implemented). This is not a runtime defect but a significant maintenance/audit hazard: future readers may believe features are missing when they are present, or vice-versa, and may 'restore' or 'remove' code incorrectly.
- **Suggested fix:** Update (or trim) the What's New KDocs to reflect the actual implemented surface (pager + images + video poster + fullscreen image + nav buttons + OpenVideo effect); do not implement code changes from this finding — it is documentation accuracy only.

### Complaint (User)  `complaint-user`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 24 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡8 ⚪13)

> The native user complaint flow has two halves: (1) a submit FeedbackDialog (invoked from Settings/Language/Sources) that picks a ComplaintType, validates body length, attaches device metadata, and writes to Firestore; and (2) a Feedback Manager screen (ComplaintScreen) listing the user's own complaints with search, status filter chips, status chips, per-card device-info + closure-reason, and a row-tap action dialog (Reply/Edit/Delete). KMP faithfully reproduces the overall structure via MVI (ComplaintViewModel/State/Intent/Effect in :presentation, ComplaintScreen/ComplaintActionDialog in :ui, use cases in :domain, strangler-fig repos in :data) and ports the status chip, closure-reason card, pinned FAQ entries, search/filter, and timestamp formatting. However parity is partial: the per-card device-metadata row (Android version + manufacturer) is entirely dropped because ComplaintSummary discarded the metadata map; edit nulls out metadata and reply drops parent metadata (data-loss regressions); the stored subject is the raw enum name (TECHNICAL) instead of the localized display name; the submit dropdown uses a divergent label set inconsistent with the list card; the empty/no-results/loading/error states are simplified (loss of the 403 Help affordance, error-code differentiation, secondary messages); and several strings (id format, search hint, count, dialog title, body label) and dialog icons diverge. KMP also intentionally changed the min-body-length floor from 8 to 5 and added a long-press-copy gesture.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Complaint (User)</summary>

**🟠 [High] Submit form — stored subject value — The complaint subject persisted on submit differs: native stores the human-readable type name, KMP stores the raw enum name** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — SettingsScreen.kt:320-322 calls complaintViewModel.submit(it, it.getDisplayName(context), body, ...), so subject = the localized display name e.g. "Error In The App".
- **KMP:** Yes (different) — SettingsViewModel.kt:250 calls submitFeedback(type = type, subject = type.name, body = body), so subject = the raw enum identifier e.g. "TECHNICAL". SubmitFeedbackUseCase.kt:127-128 KDoc confirms "the Settings hub passes type.name pre-Phase 10".
- **Explanation:** The subject field is stored in Firestore and rendered as the secondary line on the complaint card (ComplaintCard.kt:57 / ComplaintScreen.kt:446-451) and is searchable (applyFilter matches subject). Native produces a friendly subject ("Error In The App"); KMP produces an all-caps developer token ("TECHNICAL"), degrading both the displayed card and admin-side readability, and changing search-match behavior. This is a data-content regression introduced by the migration.
- **Suggested fix:** Pass the localized type display-name as the subject when submitting (resolve ComplaintType.displayName() at the :ui call site and forward it), matching native; do not store type.name.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). CLAIM IS REAL AND CORRECTLY CHARACTERIZED. NATIVE (source of truth) stores the localized display name as subject: - SettingsScreen.kt:320-322: complaintViewModel.submit(it, it.getDisplayName(context), body, ...) — 2nd arg is the subject. - ComplaintViewModel.kt:47-65 (native, viewmodes/): submit(type, subject, body) builds Complaint(..., subject = subject, ...). - ComplaintType.kt:8-17 (native model/): getDisplayName(context) returns localized strings; TECHNICAL -> R.string.error_in_the_app. - res/values/strings.xml:307: <string name="error_in_the_app">Error In The App</string>. => native subject = "Error In The App". KMP (new app) stores the raw enum identifier as subject: - presentation/settings/SettingsViewModel.kt:250: submitFeedback(type = type, subject = type.name, body = body) (import L7: domain.model.complaint.ComplaintType). - domain ComplaintType is declared inline in domain/model/complaint/ComplaintSummary.kt:167-173 with variants TECHNICAL, LANGUAGES, SITES_ADD, SITE_ERROR, FEATURES, CUSTOM => type.name == "TECHNICAL". - domain/usecase/feedback/SubmitFeedbackUseCase.kt:127-128 KDoc: "the Settings hub passes type.name pre-Phase 10"; L133-134 invoke is a pure pass-through to feedbackRepository.submit(type, subject, body). - data/repository/FeedbackRepositoryImpl.kt:131-139: stores subject = subject verbatim (only type is remapped via LegacyComplaintType.valueOf(type.name)); no display-name conversion. => KMP subject = "TECHNICAL". RENDERING + SEARCH claims verified on BOTH sides: - Native render ComplaintCard.kt:58 text = complaint.subject; native search ComplaintScreen.kt:116-119 matches complaint.subject.contains(searchQuery, true). - KMP render ui/complaint/ComplaintScreen.kt:446-451 renders complaint.subject as secondary line; KMP search presentation/complaint/ComplaintViewModel.kt:285-289 applyFilter matches complaint.subject.contains(query, ignoreCase=true). Note (broader than claimed, not contradicting): SubmitFeedbackUseCase.kt KDoc L62-66 documents a 2nd consumer, SourcesViewModel, which also passes type.name (pinned SITES_ADD) — so the same token-vs-displayname behavior exists beyond Settings.

**🟠 [High] Complaint list card — device metadata row (Android version / manufacturer) — The per-card device info row (Android version icon + manufacturer icon) is entirely absent in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — ComplaintCard.kt:69-96 renders an InfoItem row: Icons.Default.Android + apiLevelToAndroidVersion(osVersion) (e.g. "Android 14") and Icons.Default.PhoneAndroid + manufacturer, read from complaint.metadata["osVersion"]/["manufacturer"].
- **KMP:** No — ComplaintScreen.kt ComplaintRow (lines 421-509) renders type → subject → body → closure → footer with NO device-info row. ComplaintSummary.kt:124-151 has no metadata map (only appVersion/reason/replyToId carve-outs), so osVersion/manufacturer are never surfaced. apiLevelToAndroidVersion has no KMP counterpart.
- **Explanation:** Native shows the device (Android version) and manufacturer on every complaint card so users/admins can see the reporting environment. KMP dropped the entire metadata map from the domain model, so this diagnostic row cannot render. This is a feature loss in the user-facing list.
- **Suggested fix:** Carve out osVersion and manufacturer as typed String? fields on ComplaintSummary (like appVersion/reason), populate them in ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.toSummary(), and add the InfoItem row (Android + PhoneAndroid icons) to ComplaintRow, porting apiLevelToAndroidVersion for the os-version label.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): - ComplaintCard.kt:69-96 renders the device-info Row: complaint.metadata?.get("osVersion")?.toString()?.toIntOrNull()?.let { InfoItem(icon = Icons.Default.Android, text = apiLevelToAndroidVersion(it)) } (L74-83) and complaint.metadata?.get("manufacturer")...?.let { InfoItem(icon = Icons.Default.PhoneAndroid, text = manufacturer) } (L86-95). Exactly as claimed. - InfoItem composable defined in ComplaintComponents.kt:127. apiLevelToAndroidVersion is a real @Composable in .../complaint/utils/apiLevelToAndroidVersion.kt:8 mapping API level -> "Android 14" etc. - This card is rendered in the USER-facing list: ComplaintScreen.kt:32 imports ComplaintCard and L210 renders it inside items(filtered){...} of the LazyColumn (not admin-only). - Native Complaint model carries `metadata: Map<String, Any>?` (Complaint.kt:14). Metadata is populated on every real submission: ComplaintViewModel.kt:56,64 sets metadata = deviceInfoProvider.getDeviceMetadata(), and AndroidDeviceInfoProvider.kt:19-21 puts "manufacturer" to Build.MANUFACTURER and "osVersion" to Build.VERSION.SDK_INT. So the row renders for real complaints, not just samples. KMP (new app): - domain/.../complaint/ComplaintSummary.kt:124-151 has NO metadata map; only typed carve-outs id/userId/type/subject/body/createdAt/status/appVersion/reason/replyToId. KDoc L37-43 explicitly states "No metadata: Map<String,Any>? field" and only appVersion has been carved out. osVersion/manufacturer are absent. - data/.../ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt:135-146 toSummary() maps only metadata["appVersion"], metadata["reason"], metadata["replyto"] — never reads "osVersion" or "manufacturer", so they are dropped at the :data boundary. - ui/.../complaint/ComplaintScreen.kt ComplaintRow (L401-511) renders type (L434) -> subject (L446) -> body (L455) -> ClosureReasonCard (L477) -> footer timestamp+id (L485-508). There is NO device-info row. grep across ui/presentation/domain/data complaint code finds zero references to osVersion/manufacturer/Icons.Default.Android/PhoneAndroid/InfoItem (only an unrelated KDoc mention in FeedbackRepositoryImpl.kt:36). - apiLevelToAndroidVersion has no KMP counterpart (grep across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/composeApp: NONE FOUND). Minor inaccuracies in the claim's cited line numbers only: KMP ComplaintRow is L401-511 (claim said 421-509) and ComplaintSummary spans L124-151 — substance is correct.

**🟠 [High] Edit complaint — metadata preservation — KMP edit nulls out the complaint's metadata; native edit preserves it** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — native edit saves complaint.copy(body = body) (ComplaintScreenRoute.kt), which keeps the original metadata map intact (osVersion, manufacturer, reason, replyto, appVersion).
- **KMP:** No (regression) — ComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt:103-112 reconstructs the LegacyComplaint with metadata = null on edit (KDoc at lines 49-50 confirms "metadata field is set to null (not preserved across edits)"). ComplaintSummary has no metadata map to carry it back.
- **Explanation:** Editing a complaint in KMP destroys its device metadata and any closure reason stored in metadata, because the domain model carved out only appVersion/reason/replyToId and the action repo writes metadata=null. After an edit the card loses its Android-version/manufacturer info and (if CLOSED/PINNED) its ClosureReasonCard. Native keeps all of it via copy(). This is a data-loss regression.
- **Suggested fix:** Reconstruct the full metadata map on edit (carry the original osVersion/manufacturer/reason/replyto fields through ComplaintSummary or re-read the legacy record) instead of writing metadata = null, matching native's copy() preservation.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). REGRESSION IS REAL. Both ends verified by reading source. NATIVE (source of truth) PRESERVES metadata on edit: - Model carries it: native Complaint has `metadata: Map<String, Any>?` — /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/complaint/model/Complaint.kt:14. - Read populates it: ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.getComplaintsByUser reads the map (`doc.get("metadata") ?: doc.get("g")`) and sets it on the loaded Complaint — ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.kt:73 and :84 (also getAllComplaints :112,:121). - Edit keeps it: ComplaintScreenRoute.kt:53 calls `complaintViewModel.updateComplaint(complaint.copy(body = body))` — `copy` leaves `metadata` unchanged. - Write keeps it: ComplaintViewModel.updateComplaint -> UpdateComplaintUseCase -> ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.updateComplaint does `.set(dto)` where ComplaintDto.fromDomain sets `metadata = domain.metadata` — ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.kt:135-144 and DTO at :291-310 (esp. :307). So the full metadata map (osVersion, manufacturer, reason, replyto, appVersion) survives the edit in the shared `complaints_v2` doc. KMP NULLS metadata on edit (regression): - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/ComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt:103-112 reconstructs LegacyComplaint with `metadata = null` (line 111); KDoc lines 49-50 explicitly state "The legacy's `metadata` field is set to `null` (not preserved across edits)". - The underlying legacy update is a full-document `.set(dto)` overwrite (same ComplaintFirestoreDataSource semantics in :shared), so writing metadata=null DESTROYS the stored map in Firestore. - Domain model cannot carry it back: ComplaintSummary.kt:124-151 has NO `metadata: Map<String,Any>?` — only carve-outs appVersion(:132)/reason(:143)/replyToId(:150); KDoc lines 38-43 confirm "No `metadata: Map<String, Any>?` field." None of the carve-outs is re-written on edit (editComplaint ignores original.appVersion/reason/replyToId entirely). - Edit chain: ComplaintViewModel.kt:215 `editComplaint(original, subject, body)` -> EditComplaintUseCase.kt:95-103 pass-through -> repo writes metadata=null. - Confirmed downstream effect on the user card: ComplaintScreen.kt:473-478 renders ClosureReasonCard only from `complaint.reason`; after an edit of a CLOSED/PINNED complaint, the next reload (ComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt:144 `reason = metadata?.get("reason")`) yields null, so the ClosureReasonCard vanishes. Reply correlation (replyto) and admin appVersion diagnostics are likewise destroyed. MINOR INACCURACY in the claim's framing (does not change the verdict): the claim says the KMP card "loses its Android-version/manufacturer info." The native card DOES render osVersion/manufacturer InfoItems (ComplaintCard.kt:69-96), but the KMP user-side ComplaintRow never renders that device row at all (separate display gap) — so there is no visible KMP-card loss of that specific row. The data loss in Firestore is nonetheless real and affects the admin dashboard (appVersion filter/sort/stats) and closure-reason/reply-threading. The KDoc citations (lines 49-50) and file:line references in the claim are accurate.

**🟡 [Medium] Submit form — category dropdown labels — Submit-form category labels differ from the list-card labels for the same ComplaintType, and differ from native** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — native FeedbackDialog.kt:94,122 calls ComplaintType.getDisplayName(context) which maps TECHNICAL→error_in_the_app ("Error In The App"), LANGUAGES→add_languages ("Add Languages"), SITES_ADD→add_manga_site ("Add Manga Site"), SITE_ERROR→error_in_manga_site, FEATURES→ask_to_add_features, CUSTOM→custom_feedback ("Custom Feedback"). The list card (ComplaintCard.kt:51) uses the SAME getDisplayName, so submit and list agree.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP submit dialog (SettingsScreen.kt:896-902 complaintTypeLabel) maps TECHNICAL→complaint_technical ("Technical issue"), LANGUAGES→complaint_languages ("Languages"), SITES_ADD→complaint_sites_add ("Add a site"), SITE_ERROR→complaint_site_error ("Site error"), FEATURES→complaint_features ("Feature request"), CUSTOM→complaint_other ("Other"). But the list card (ComplaintTypeDisplay.kt:63-70) uses error_in_the_app/add_languages/... So within KMP the dropdown and the card show DIFFERENT labels for the same category.
- **Explanation:** Native uses one canonical label set for both the picker and the list. KMP introduced a second, divergent label set (complaint_technical etc.) only for the Settings feedback dropdown while the complaint list/card keeps the native labels. A user picks "Technical issue" but the resulting complaint card shows "Error In The App" — an internal inconsistency absent in native, plus the picker text itself differs from native wording.
- **Suggested fix:** Make the KMP FeedbackDialog dropdown use the same ComplaintType.displayName() helper (ComplaintTypeDisplay.kt) that the list card uses, so picker and card agree and match native's getDisplayName strings; delete the divergent complaint_technical/complaint_languages/... label set or repoint it to the native keys.

**🟡 [Medium] Complaint list — empty state — Empty state is reduced to a single title line; native shows icon + title + secondary message** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — EmptyState.kt:26-64 shows Icons.Default.Inbox (80.dp, onSurfaceVariant α0.6), title no_feedback_found ("No Feedback Yet", titleLarge/Medium), and message no_feedback_message ("When feedback is submitted, it will appear here.", bodyMedium), centered with 32.dp padding.
- **KMP:** Partial — ComplaintScreen.kt:247-248 calls YamiEmptyState(title = complaint_no_feedback) with only a title ("No feedback submitted yet"); no secondary message string is passed and the title wording differs.
- **Explanation:** The native empty state has a richer two-line layout (title + supporting sentence) and different copy. KMP routes through the shared YamiEmptyState with only a title. The supporting "When feedback is submitted, it will appear here." line and the exact title wording are lost.
- **Suggested fix:** Pass a body/message argument to YamiEmptyState equal to native no_feedback_message and align the title to "No Feedback Yet"; verify the icon matches native's Inbox.

**🟡 [Medium] Complaint list — no-results (search/filter) empty state — No-results state is a small inline icon+text vs native's full EmptyState with title + message** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — ComplaintScreen.kt:196-206 shows EmptyState(title=no_results_found "No results found", message=try_different_search "Try a different search term or filter", icon=Icons.Default.SearchOff) filling parent size with 32.dp top padding — same large icon+title+message layout as the empty state.
- **KMP:** Partial — ComplaintScreen.kt:295-313 shows a small Column with ComplaintSearchOff icon (default 24.dp, no size set) + a single bodyMedium text complaint_no_matches ("No matches"); no title, no "Try a different search term" message.
- **Explanation:** Native presents a prominent no-results state (large 80.dp SearchOff icon, titleLarge title, bodyMedium guidance). KMP shows a compact one-line "No matches" with a small default-size icon and drops the "Try a different search term or filter" guidance and the title. Noticeable UX downgrade.
- **Suggested fix:** Render the no-matches state with the same icon size + title (no_results_found) + secondary guidance (try_different_search) as native, ideally via the shared YamiEmptyState with the SearchOff icon.

**🟡 [Medium] Complaint list — error state & 403 Help affordance — Native error state is code-aware (icon per HTTP code, error-code text, optional Help button for 403); KMP shows a generic message + Retry only** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — ErrorState.kt:33-118 picks an icon by code (0→WifiOff, 4xx→Lock, 5xx→CloudOff, else Error), shows error_occurred title, error_code_format ("Error code: %d", Monospace), and a Retry button. ComplaintScreen.kt:166 passes onHelp only when code==403, enabling a help affordance for permission-denied.
- **KMP:** Partial — ComplaintScreen.kt:240-246 shows YamiErrorState(message=state.error, retryLabel=retry, onRetry=OnRetry). No per-code icon, no error-code line, and NO Help/403 path. ComplaintReworkScreenRoute.kt KDoc explicitly states the onHelp 403 help-URL launcher "remains genuinely deferred (Phase 10.x)".
- **Explanation:** Native differentiates network vs client vs server errors with distinct icons and surfaces an error code, and offers a Help action specifically on 403 (Forbidden) so users can resolve permission problems. KMP collapses everything to one generic error + Retry and drops the 403 Help entry point entirely — a lost recovery affordance for the common Firestore PERMISSION_DENIED case.
- **Suggested fix:** Carry an error code/type through ComplaintState (not just a String), render a code-appropriate icon + error-code line, and re-add the Help affordance on the 403/permission-denied branch (wire IntentLauncher.openUrl).

**🟡 [Medium] Edit complaint — subject edit persistence — Native discards the edited subject and saves only the body; KMP saves both subject and body** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — ComplaintActionDialog EditContent edits subject + body, but the route only forwards body: ComplaintScreenRoute.kt onEditComplaint = { complaint, body -> updateComplaint(complaint.copy(body = body)) }. The edited subject is thrown away (the dialog's onEdit signature is (Complaint, String)->body only).
- **KMP:** Yes (different) — ComplaintActionDialog.kt:567 dispatches OnSubmitEdit(trimmedSubject, trimmedBody); EditComplaintUseCase.kt:98-102 + ComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt:103-113 write BOTH the new subject and body.
- **Explanation:** This is actually a KMP improvement/divergence: native's edit UI lets the user change the subject but silently discards it on save (only body persists). KMP persists the edited subject too. Behavior differs from the source of truth, so it must be flagged — it could surprise admins comparing data, though it is arguably more correct.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm the intended behavior. If strict parity is required, either persist only the body (drop the subject from OnSubmitEdit) or fix native; document the deliberate divergence if KMP's behavior is preferred.

**🟡 [Medium] Reply to complaint — metadata preservation — Native reply preserves the parent's metadata and adds replyto; KMP reply keeps only replyto** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — ComplaintActionDialog.kt:312 builds the reply with metadata = (complaint.metadata ?: emptyMap()) + mapOf("replyto" to complaint.id), preserving osVersion/manufacturer/appVersion plus the link.
- **KMP:** No (different) — ComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt:84-93 builds the reply with metadata = mapOf("replyto" to parent.id) only, dropping the parent's device metadata.
- **Explanation:** A reply in native carries forward the parent's device metadata (so the reply record also shows Android version/manufacturer) and adds the replyto link. KMP only sets replyto, so the reply record has no device info. Because the user list also doesn't render the device row in KMP, the visible impact is smaller, but the persisted data diverges from native and would differ in the admin view.
- **Suggested fix:** When constructing the reply, merge the parent's metadata (or the carved-out osVersion/manufacturer/appVersion fields) with the replyto entry, matching native's metadata merge.

**🟡 [Medium] Action dialog — icon affordances on buttons & headers — Native action-dialog buttons and info/warning cards carry icons; KMP dialog is icon-free** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — ComplaintActionDialog.kt: Reply button has Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.Reply, Edit has Icons.Default.Edit, Delete has Icons.Default.Delete; Close uses Icons.Default.Close; back uses ArrowBack; Edit info-card has Icons.Default.Info; Delete warning-card has Icons.Default.Warning; ClosureReason chip uses CheckCircle/Update/PushPin/Info.
- **KMP:** Partial — ComplaintActionDialog.kt: Reply/Edit/Delete are plain text buttons (no leading icons); Close/Back are labelled TextButtons (no icons); the Edit info-card (lines 494-510) and Delete warning-card (621-641) have NO leading Info/Warning icon (text only). The screen-level back/search/clear/no-matches icons ARE restored (ComplaintIcons.kt), and the ClosureReasonCard icons ARE present (ClosureReason.kt:120-125).
- **Explanation:** The KMP dialog deliberately drops the per-button and per-card glyphs (documented as an intentional icon-free posture to avoid the materialIconsExtended dep). Native shows Reply/Edit/Delete/Info/Warning icons inside the action dialog. The closure-reason and screen-level icons were restored, but the action-dialog affordance icons remain absent — a visible divergence from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Add inline ImageVector glyphs (as already done in ComplaintIcons) for Reply/Edit/Delete buttons and Info/Warning on the edit/delete cards, or accept the documented icon-free posture as an intentional design choice.

**🟡 [Medium] Action dialog — status badge color in preview card — Native preview card uses the vivid getColorWithContrast palette; KMP preview reuses the M3 container ComplaintStatusChip** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — ComplaintActionDialog.kt:630-642 ComplaintPreviewCard uses complaint.status.getColorWithContrast() (e.g. OPEN→0xFF00BCD4 cyan/white, IN_PROGRESS→0xFF2196F3 blue/white, RESOLVED→0xFF4CAF50 green/white) with RoundedCornerShape(8.dp).
- **KMP:** Yes (different) — ComplaintActionDialog.kt:714 ComplaintPreviewCard reuses ComplaintStatusChip (chipColors → M3 primaryContainer/tertiaryContainer/etc., RoundedCornerShape(16.dp)).

KMP collapses both to the single ComplaintStatusChip, so the dialog preview badge color and corner radius no longer match native's vivid badge. The list-card chip itself matches native's StatusChip, but the dialog preview badge diverges.

This is a behavior change vs the source of truth and is flagged for completeness, though it is a corrective improvement.

The effective gap depends on spacing.sm's value (likely 8.dp), so inter-card spacing may be larger than native's 8.dp combined (4+4). Subtle layout difference; also horizontal padding is a token (spacing.md) vs native's literal 16.dp — equal only if the token is 16.dp.

### Complaint (Admin)  `complaint-admin`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 23 (🔴0 🟠4 🟡5 ⚪14)

> Native implements the admin moderation dashboard as a single LazyColumn (scrolling CenterAlignedTopAppBar + statistics card + search/2-filter+version-filter+sort + cards). Each card is rich: a tappable status pill with an edit pencil, an inline ClosureReasonCard for CLOSED/PINNED, a truncated complaint-ID footer, and three dedicated action IconButtons (closure/edit/delete) plus body long-press copy. Mutations open AlertDialogs (status radio list, edit with TYPE dropdown + subject/body, closure with type dropdown + pre-fill, delete with warning icon + details). KMP reimplements this as MVI (:presentation VM/state/intent/effect + :ui Scaffold screen + a single AdminComplaintActionDialog with MENU→STATUS_CHANGE/EDIT/CLOSURE_REASON/DELETE_CONFIRM sub-modes). Core data behavior has high parity: search across subject/body/id/userId, 3-axis filter, 7 sort modes, semver-aware chip ordering, metadata-preserving closure (reasonAddedBy/reasonAddedAt, auto-CLOSE), and the Admin.isAdmin Settings gate are all faithfully ported, and KMP actually adds real snackbars (native silently printlns). The headline divergences are all on the card surface and edit flow: KMP's row has NO per-card action buttons, NO clickable status pill, NO inline closure-reason card, and NO complaint-ID line — everything is funneled behind a 2-tap row→MENU dialog; and the KMP edit dialog cannot change the complaint TYPE. Secondary divergences are cosmetic (top bar alignment/title/scroll, statistics card chip vs text, empty/no-results state copy+icons, results-count wording) and localization (hardcoded English mutation snackbar strings in the VM).
