<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Complaint (Admin)</summary>

**🟠 [High] Admin complaint card — per-card action buttons — Native renders 3 dedicated action IconButtons (closure-reason, edit, delete) in each card footer; KMP renders no action buttons on the row** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes
- **KMP:** No — ui/complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt AdminComplaintRow (lines 686-807) has no action buttons; all actions are reached only by tapping the whole row to open an action MENU dialog
- **Explanation:** Native exposes each admin action as a one-tap affordance directly on the card (closure/edit/delete icons always visible, plus the status pill is itself tappable to change status). KMP collapses everything behind a single full-row tap that opens a MENU dialog (AdminComplaintActionDialog ActionSelectionContent, lines 232-302), requiring 2 taps to reach any action and changing the discoverability/ergonomics entirely. The action set also reorders: native footer order is closure, edit, delete; KMP MENU order is Change status, Edit, Add closure reason, Delete.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a footer action Row to AdminComplaintRow with the three IconButtons (closure/edit/delete) matching native tints (secondary/tertiary/error containers) and make the status chip tappable to launch STATUS_CHANGE, dispatching OnSelectAction-style intents directly instead of routing through MENU. Alternatively keep the dialog but document the intentional ergonomic change as a deviation.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt): AdminComplaintCard footer renders an "Action buttons" Row (lines 849-894) with 3 dedicated IconButtons in order closure-reason → edit → delete: closure-reason IconButton (lines 854-865, Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.Note, secondaryContainer), edit IconButton (lines 868-879, Icons.Default.Edit, tertiaryContainer), delete IconButton (lines 882-893, Icons.Default.Delete, errorContainer). The status pill is ALSO a one-tap affordance: Surface(modifier = Modifier.clickable { onStatusClick() }, line 774) wrapping the StatusChip. So every admin action is reachable in one tap directly on the card. KMP (ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt): AdminComplaintRow (lines 686-807) renders NO action IconButtons; the entire Card is .clickable(onClick = onClick) (line 701) dispatching AdminComplaintIntent.OnRowClick(complaint) (line 397). The status chip (line 726 ComplaintStatusChip) is NOT clickable in the row (no clickable modifier), unlike native's tappable pill. The body has only a long-press copy (lines 751-757). All admin actions are funneled into the MENU dialog: AdminComplaintScreenContent mounts AdminComplaintActionDialog when actionDialogMode != NONE (lines 298-305), which for MENU mode renders ActionSelectionContent (AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt lines 232-302) with 4 buttons in order Change status (266-272) → Edit (274-280) → Add closure reason (282-288) → Delete (290-299). Thus KMP requires 2 taps (row tap to open dialog + menu-item tap) to reach any action, and the order differs from native's closure/edit/delete footer order. Claim's file:line citations (KMP row 686-807, dialog 232-302) and ordering description are all accurate.

**🟠 [High] Admin complaint card — tappable status pill with edit affordance — Native makes the status chip a clickable Surface (primaryContainer) with a trailing Edit pencil icon to open status-change; KMP status chip is non-interactive** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:770-793: a Surface(clickable{onStatusClick()}, primaryContainer, r8) wrapping StatusChip + Icons.Default.Edit (16.dp, onPrimaryContainer tint, start padding 4dp)
- **KMP:** No — AdminComplaintRow line 726 renders a bare ComplaintStatusChip with no clickable wrapper and no edit icon
- **Explanation:** In native, tapping the status pill directly opens StatusChangeDialog. The visual cue (pill on primaryContainer with a pencil) communicates that status is editable inline. KMP loses the dedicated status-change tap target and the visual edit affordance; status change is only reachable via the row→MENU→Change status path.
- **Suggested fix:** Wrap ComplaintStatusChip in a clickable Surface (primaryContainer, RoundedCornerShape(8.dp)) with a trailing 16.dp Edit icon tinted onPrimaryContainer, dispatching the status-change action on click, mirroring AdminComplaintScreen.kt:770-793.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth) native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:773-792 — status pill is `Surface(modifier = Modifier.clickable { onStatusClick() }, shape = RoundedCornerShape(8.dp), color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.primaryContainer)` wrapping a Row(padding 8.dp) of `StatusChip(status = complaint.status)` + `Icon(Icons.Default.Edit, contentDescription = "Change Status", modifier = Modifier.size(16.dp).padding(start = 4.dp), tint = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onPrimaryContainer)`. Every claimed detail (primaryContainer, r8, Edit pencil 16.dp, onPrimaryContainer tint, start padding 4.dp) matches exactly. AdminComplaintScreen.kt:276-279 wires onStatusClick to set selectedComplaint + showStatusDialog=true, which renders StatusChangeDialog (lines 298-312) directly. Native card has NO row-level click/menu at all; its affordances are the tappable status pill plus three separate footer IconButtons (closure-reason :854, edit :868, delete :882). KMP ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt:726 — AdminComplaintRow renders a bare `ComplaintStatusChip(status = complaint.status)` with no clickable wrapper and no Edit icon (only a Spacer(Modifier.height(0.dp)) precedes it in the header Row). The sole tap target is the whole-card `.clickable(onClick = onClick)` at :701 dispatching OnRowClick. presentation/.../AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:164-172 handleRowClick opens AdminActionDialogMode.MENU (not STATUS_CHANGE). ui/.../AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt:266-272 — from MENU the user must tap the "Change status" ElevatedButton (OnSelectAction(STATUS_CHANGE)) to reach StatusChangeContent. So KMP status change is reachable only via card->MENU->Change status, with no dedicated status-pill tap target and no pencil/primaryContainer edit affordance — exactly as claimed.

**🟠 [High] Admin complaint card — inline closure-reason display — Native shows a ClosureReasonCard inside the card for CLOSED/PINNED complaints with a stored reason; KMP admin row never renders the closure reason** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:818-825: when status==CLOSED\|\|PINNED and metadata["reason"] is non-blank, renders ClosureReasonCard(closureReason) (ComplaintComponents.kt:53-124 — colored card, icon by type, label, optional type chip, reason text maxLines 10)
- **KMP:** No — AdminComplaintRow (686-807) does not render the closure reason at all. The ported ClosureReasonCard composable exists (ui/complaint/ClosureReason.kt:117) and ComplaintSummary.reason is populated, but the admin screen never calls it (only the user-side ComplaintScreen.kt:477 does)
- **Explanation:** Admins cannot see the closure reason they/others added directly on the list card. The data is present (ComplaintSummary.reason) and a matching ClosureReasonCard composable already exists in :ui, but the admin row omits the CLOSED/PINNED reason block that native renders. This is a visible regression for the moderation workflow.
- **Suggested fix:** In AdminComplaintRow, after the body Text, add: if (complaint.status == CLOSED \|\| complaint.status == PINNED) and complaint.reason is non-blank, render ClosureReasonCard(reason = complaint.reason) with an 8.dp spacer above, matching AdminComplaintScreen.kt:818-825.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/admin/complaint/AdminComplaintScreen.kt — the list-row composable AdminComplaintCard (declared line 691, rendered at line 274 inside `items(filteredComplaints) { AdminComplaintCard(...) }`) renders the closure reason at lines 818-825: `if (complaint.status == ComplaintStatus.CLOSED \|\| complaint.status == ComplaintStatus.PINNED) { val closureReason = complaint.metadata?.get("reason")?.toString(); if (!closureReason.isNullOrBlank()) { Spacer(8.dp); ClosureReasonCard(closureReason = closureReason) } }`. The ClosureReasonCard composable is defined in ComplaintComponents.kt:53-124 (colored Card r8, leading icon by ClosureReasonType — CheckCircle/Update/PushPin/Info, closure_reason_label heading, optional non-OTHER type chip, reason text maxLines 10) — matching the claim exactly. KMP: /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/complaint/admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt — the admin list-row AdminComplaintRow (lines 686-807) renders type display name + ComplaintStatusChip (711-727), subject (728-734), replyToId (738-744), body (745-758), user-id + app-version chip row (763-790), and createdAt timestamp (798-804). It contains NO `status == CLOSED \|\| PINNED` check and NO ClosureReasonCard call — the closure-reason block native shows is entirely absent. Data IS present for the admin row: ComplaintSummary.reason exists (/Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/domain/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/domain/model/complaint/ComplaintSummary.kt:143) and is populated by the admin mapper at /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/data/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/repository/AdminComplaintListRepositoryImpl.kt:102 (`reason = metadata?.get("reason")?.toString()`). The ported ClosureReasonCard composable exists in :ui at /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/complaint/ClosureReason.kt:117 (matching layout: Card r8, icon-by-type, label, optional non-OTHER chip, reason text maxLines 10). It is invoked ONLY on the user side — ComplaintScreen.kt:469-477 (`if (reason != null && (status == CLOSED \|\| status == PINNED)) ClosureReasonCard(reason = reason)`) and the dialog preview (ComplaintActionDialog.kt:723) — and never from the admin screen. A grep for ClosureReasonCard usage across :ui confirms no call site inside admin/AdminComplaintScreen.kt. Note: the claim cited the user-side call at ComplaintScreen.kt:477 (correct, the actual ClosureReasonCard line) and the KMP card definition at ClosureReason.kt:117 (correct). All cited file:line anchors verified accurate.

**🟠 [High] Admin edit dialog — complaint type selector — Native EditComplaintDialog lets the admin change the complaint Type via a dropdown; KMP EditContent only edits subject + body** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — StatusChangeDialog.kt (EditComplaintDialog) lines 156-205: a readOnly OutlinedTextField + DropdownMenu over ComplaintType.entries with a check leadingIcon; on save the updated complaint copies type=selectedType (line 271)
- **KMP:** No — AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt EditContent (552-680) edits only editedSubject and editedBody; OnSubmitEdit(subject, body) carries no type, and AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.editComplaint (162-173) copies only subject+body, leaving type unchanged
- **Explanation:** Native admins can re-categorize a complaint's type during edit; KMP cannot. This is a lost moderation capability — the type field is immutable in the KMP edit flow.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a ComplaintType dropdown to EditContent (mirroring StatusChangeDialog.kt:156-205), extend OnSubmitEdit to carry the selected type, and update AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.editComplaint to copy(type = newType.toLegacyType()).
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth) — native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/admin/complaint/StatusChangeDialog.kt: EditComplaintDialog at line 113; `var selectedType by remember { mutableStateOf(complaint.type) }` (119), `showTypeDropdown` (122), hasChanges includes `selectedType != complaint.type` (124-126). Type selector is a readOnly OutlinedTextField over `selectedType.getDisplayName(context)` (168-181) with a DropdownMenu over `ComplaintType.entries` (183-205), each item carrying a Check leadingIcon when selected (197-201). On Save: `complaint.copy(type = selectedType, subject = subject.trim(), body = body.trim())` (270-274) → onComplaintUpdated → AdminComplaintScreen.kt:316-323 onUpdateComplaint → AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:101-111 `updateComplaintUseCase(complaint)` persists the full object INCLUDING type. So native admins can re-categorize the type. (Verified the native file is genuine source-of-truth: it lives under native-app/.../me/manga/yami/ even though its Kotlin package is me.manga.kira, matching the prompt's note.) KMP — ui/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt EditContent (552-680) declares ONLY `editedSubject` (559) and `editedBody` (560); no type state, no type dropdown — just two OutlinedTextFields for subject (605) and body (615). Submit dispatches `AdminComplaintIntent.OnSubmitEdit(trimmedSubject, trimmedBody)` (660). The intent itself carries no type: presentation/.../complaint/admin/AdminComplaintIntent.kt:237 `data class OnSubmitEdit(val subject: String, val body: String)`. Handler AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:224-233 calls `adminEditComplaint(target, subject, body)`. data/.../AdminComplaintActionRepositoryImpl.kt editComplaint (162-173) copies only `subject` + `body` onto the fetched legacy complaint (`legacy.copy(subject = subject, body = body)`), leaving `type` unchanged. The KMP edit flow has no path to mutate type. Every line citation in the claim is accurate. The difference is REAL and correctly characterized: native edit can change complaint type; KMP edit cannot.

**🟡 [Medium] Admin complaint card — feedback ID footer line — Native footer shows a truncated complaint ID line ('ID: <8 chars>…' monospace); KMP row omits the ID entirely** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:841-846: Text(stringResource(feedback_id_format, complaint.id.take(8)), bodySmall, onSurfaceVariant, FontFamily.Monospace). feedback_id_format = 'ID: %s…' (strings.xml:63)
- **KMP:** No — AdminComplaintRow renders userId, appVersion and createdAt but never the complaint id
- **Explanation:** The complaint document ID is a key piece of moderation metadata in native (shown truncated in monospace in every card footer). KMP drops it from the row, so admins can no longer see/identify the complaint id on the list. The id is shown only inside dialogs (preview/edit), not on the card.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a footer Text in AdminComplaintRow showing the truncated id (id.take(8)) in Monospace bodySmall onSurfaceVariant, alongside the timestamp, mirroring native's footer Column at AdminComplaintScreen.kt:835-847. Add a matching string resource ('ID: %s…').

**🟡 [Medium] Admin edit dialog — input fields and keyboard options — Native edit subject/body use sentence capitalization + IME actions and a 120.dp fixed-height body (maxLines 5) with no char cap; KMP uses a 1000-char cap, char counter, minLines 4/maxLines 8, and no capitalization/IME options** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** Yes — StatusChangeDialog.kt:216-252: subject OutlinedTextField (KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences, ImeAction.Next, singleLine), body OutlinedTextField (height 120.dp, maxLines 5, Sentences capitalization). No max-length validation; Save enabled when hasChanges && subject/body non-empty (line 278)
- **KMP:** Partial — EditContent (605-667): subject singleLine, body minLines 4/maxLines 8 with a 1000-char cap + '%d/1000' counter (lines 617,633), isError when over cap. No KeyboardCapitalization/ImeAction set. Save enabled when subject+body non-blank && body<=1000 (664-667)
- **Explanation:** Behavioral divergence in the edit form: native has no length cap and uses sentence-case auto-capitalization + Next IME action; KMP adds a 1000-char body cap with a counter and drops the capitalization/IME hints. Native also gates Save on 'hasChanges' (the edited value must differ from the original) which KMP does not — KMP allows submitting an unchanged complaint.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the edit form: either drop the 1000-char cap to match native or document it as an intentional improvement; add KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences + ImeAction.Next to subject; and add a hasChanges guard (disable Save when subject==original.subject && body==original.body) to match native's line 124-126/278.

**🟡 [Medium] Admin top app bar — type, color, scroll behavior, title text — Native uses a CenterAlignedTopAppBar (bold title 'Admin Complaint Management', container=background) placed INSIDE the scrolling LazyColumn; KMP uses a fixed Scaffold TopAppBar (SemiBold title 'Admin Complaints', default container)** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:162-188: CenterAlignedTopAppBar as the first LazyColumn item (scrolls away), title FontWeight.Bold, centerAlignedTopAppBarColors(containerColor=background), title = admin_complaint_management ('Admin Complaint Management')
- **KMP:** Partial — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:223-261: a start-aligned TopAppBar pinned in Scaffold.topBar (does not scroll), title FontWeight.SemiBold, default colors, title = admincomplaint_title ('Admin Complaints')
- **Explanation:** Three divergences: (1) title alignment center vs start; (2) title weight Bold vs SemiBold and text differs ('Admin Complaint Management' vs 'Admin Complaints'); (3) the bar scrolls with content in native (it is a LazyColumn item) but is pinned in KMP (Scaffold topBar). The container color also differs (background vs M3 default surface).
- **Suggested fix:** Use CenterAlignedTopAppBar with FontWeight.Bold and a containerColor of MaterialTheme.colorScheme.background; reconcile the title string to 'Admin Complaint Management'. If the pinned-bar behavior is intentional, document it; otherwise the scroll-away behavior could be preserved, though pinned is usually acceptable.

**🟡 [Medium] Admin statistics card — By app version top-5 layout vs By status header text — Minor parity gaps in the statistics card: KMP title is SemiBold 'Statistics' vs native Bold primary-colored 'Complaints Statistics'; total label text differs; native shows StatusChip pills in the by-status breakdown, KMP shows plain status text** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:600-685: title 'Complaints Statistics' (titleMedium, Bold, color=primary); a 'Total Complaints' SpaceBetween row (label + bold count); 'By Status' rows each rendering a StatusChip pill + count; 'By app version' top-5 rows
- **KMP:** Partial — StatisticsCard (594-684): title 'Statistics' (titleMedium, SemiBold, onSurface); 'Total complaints: %d' single line (not a SpaceBetween label+value row); by-status rows render plain status.displayName() text (not the colored StatusChip pill) + count; by-app-version top-5 matches
- **Explanation:** The statistics card diverges on several cosmetic/structural points: native uses the colored StatusChip in the by-status breakdown (visually consistent with the cards) while KMP uses plain text; native total is a right-aligned label/value SpaceBetween row while KMP is a single inline 'Total complaints: N' string; title text and weight/color differ ('Complaints Statistics' Bold primary vs 'Statistics' SemiBold onSurface).
- **Suggested fix:** Render ComplaintStatusChip in the by-status rows instead of plain text; change the total into a SpaceBetween label+value row; set the title to Bold primary and reconcile the string to 'Complaints Statistics' / 'Total Complaints'.

**🟡 [Medium] Admin list — empty / no-results / loading / error states — Native uses bespoke EmptyState/ErrorState/LoadingState composables with specific titles+messages+icons; KMP uses generic Yami* state views with single titles and loses the no-results FilterAlt icon + 'Try adjusting your search or filters' message** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt: Loading→LoadingState(message=loading_complaints 'Loading complaints…'); Error→ErrorState(error,onRetry); empty→EmptyState(title=no_complaints_found 'No Complaints Found', message=no_complaints_message 'No complaints have been submitted yet.'); no-results→EmptyState(title=no_results_found 'No results found', message=try_different_filters 'Try adjusting your search or filters', icon=Icons.Default.FilterAlt) (lines 192-270)
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP uses YamiLoadingState() (no message), YamiErrorState(message,retry), YamiEmptyState(title=admincomplaint_no_complaints 'No complaints submitted'); no-results is a small centered Column with ComplaintSearchOff icon + 'No matches' (admincomplaint_no_matches) (lines 275-392)
- **Explanation:** Empty/no-results states lose detail: native empty state has a title AND a descriptive message; KMP empty state has only a title. Native no-results uses a FilterAlt icon with 'No results found' + 'Try adjusting your search or filters'; KMP uses a SearchOff icon with a terse 'No matches' and no secondary guidance. Loading state native shows 'Loading complaints…'; KMP shows a bare spinner with no message.
- **Suggested fix:** Pass a loading message to YamiLoadingState; add the secondary message to YamiEmptyState; expand the no-matches state to include both 'No results found' title and 'Try adjusting your search or filters' body, matching native strings, and consider a filter-style icon to match native's FilterAlt.

**⚪ [Low] Admin success/error messaging on mutations — Native admin actions show NO real user-facing confirmation (the route's onShowMessage is a println); KMP shows real Snackbars for every action** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Partial — AdminComplaintScreenRoute.kt:37-41 defines showMessage as `{ println("Admin Message: $message") }`; the screen calls onShowMessage('Status updated…','Complaint deleted successfully', etc.) but nothing is shown to the user (only logcat). Body long-press copy DOES show a Toast (title_copied 'Title copied!')
- **KMP:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:193-200 collects effects into a real SnackbarHostState; completeAction emits ShowSuccessMessage/ShowErrorMessage ('Status updated','Closure reason added','Complaint deleted','Complaint updated','Copied to clipboard')
- **Explanation:** This is one place KMP is arguably BETTER than the source of truth: native's success/error messages are silently printed to logcat (the route never wires a snackbar/toast), so admins get no confirmation except for the body-copy Toast. KMP renders proper snackbars. Flagged as a divergence per strict-parity instructions, though it is an improvement. Note the copy confirmation text differs: native Toast 'Title copied!' vs KMP snackbar 'Copied to clipboard'.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed for the snackbar improvement; if strict parity to the silent native behavior were desired it would be a regression to remove it. Optionally reconcile the copy-confirmation wording to native's 'Title copied!'. Note all KMP snackbar messages are hardcoded English literals in the VM (not localized) — see separate localization finding.

**⚪ [Low] Admin mutation snackbar/message strings — localization — KMP admin mutation result messages are hardcoded English string literals in the ViewModel, not resource-backed** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Partial — native success messages are also literals passed from the screen ('Status updated to X','Complaint deleted successfully' at AdminComplaintScreen.kt:307,358 etc.) but they are not displayed; the only displayed message (Toast) uses a resource (R.string.title_copied)
- **KMP:** No (not localized) — AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:198,209,220,231,236 emit hardcoded 'Status updated','Closure reason added','Complaint deleted','Complaint updated','Copied to clipboard'; error fallback 'Unknown error' (252-253) also literal
- **Explanation:** The KMP admin VM, which now actually surfaces these messages via snackbar, hardcodes English literals in :presentation rather than using compose-resources, so they cannot be localized (the rest of the admin :ui uses stringResource). This is a localization regression for the now-visible messages.
- **Suggested fix:** Move the admin mutation result strings into compose-resources and resolve them at the :ui layer (e.g., map effect variants to string keys in the snackbar collector), keeping :presentation free of UI literals — consistent with the rest of the admin screen's stringResource usage.

**⚪ [Low] Admin list — active filters summary line — Native shows an 'Active filters: …' summary line under the results count; KMP omits it** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:560-575: builds a list of active filters (Status/Type/Version/Search) and renders 'Active filters: <joined>' in bodySmall, color=primary, when any filter is active
- **KMP:** No — SearchAndFilterSection (405-547) renders only the results-count Text (535-543); there is no active-filters summary line
- **Explanation:** Native surfaces a human-readable summary of which filters are currently applied (e.g., 'Active filters: Status: Open, Search: "foo"'). KMP drops this affordance, so the only feedback that filters are active is the chip selection state and the result count.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an 'Active filters: …' Text below the results count in SearchAndFilterSection, built from selectedStatus/selectedType/selectedAppVersion/searchQuery, color=primary bodySmall, mirroring AdminComplaintScreen.kt:560-575. Requires a new string resource.

**⚪ [Low] Admin list — results count string / pluralization — Native uses a single format '%d complaints found'; KMP uses two strings (singular '%d result' / plural '%d results') with different wording** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes — complaints_found_count = '%d complaints found' (strings.xml:484), rendered at AdminComplaintScreen.kt:554-558
- **KMP:** Partial — admincomplaint_result_singular '%1$d result' / admincomplaint_results_plural '%1$d results' chosen by resultsCount==1 (AdminComplaintScreen.kt:535-540)
- **Explanation:** Wording diverges ('N complaints found' vs 'N result(s)') and KMP introduces a manual singular/plural branch rather than native's single fixed string. Cosmetic/localization divergence in the count label.
- **Suggested fix:** Reconcile to native wording 'N complaints found' (or keep the pluralized form but use a proper plurals resource). Confirm the desired copy with product.

**⚪ [Low] Admin card — reply-to reference line rendering — Native renders the raw replyToId string with no label in the header (onSurfaceVariant); KMP renders 'Reply to Complaint ID: <id>' with a label in primary color** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:730-736: if replyToId != null, Text(replyToId.toString(), bodyMedium, onSurfaceVariant) — no label prefix, sits under the subject in the header column
- **KMP:** Partial — AdminComplaintRow:738-744: Text(stringResource(np_reply_to_complaint_id, replyToId), bodySmall, color=primary) — adds a 'Reply to Complaint ID: ' label and uses primary color + bodySmall
- **Explanation:** Both show the reply-to reference, but native shows the bare id string in onSurfaceVariant bodyMedium with no label, while KMP adds a descriptive label, uses the primary color, and a smaller text style. The KMP version is arguably clearer but diverges in style, color and copy from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** If strict parity is desired, render the raw replyToId in onSurfaceVariant without the label and at bodyMedium; otherwise document the labeled version as an intentional clarity improvement.

**⚪ [Low] Admin card — body long-press copy confirmation — Native shows an Android Toast 'Title copied!' on body long-press; KMP shows a Snackbar 'Copied to clipboard'** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes
- **KMP:** Partial — AdminComplaintRow:751-757 copies to clipboard via LocalClipboardManager and fires OnCopyBody → VM emits ShowSuccessMessage('Copied to clipboard') shown as a Snackbar
- **Explanation:** Both copy the body on long-press, but the confirmation mechanism (Toast vs Snackbar) and wording ('Title copied!' vs 'Copied to clipboard') differ. The KMP wording also mislabels — native's string id is title_copied even though it copies the body.
- **Suggested fix:** Reconcile the confirmation wording; Snackbar vs Toast is an acceptable cross-platform difference, but the message text should match (or both be corrected to 'Copied').

**⚪ [Low] Admin list — top-level layout container padding/spacing — Native LazyColumn uses contentPadding vertical=16.dp with cards padded horizontal=16/vertical=4; KMP uses contentPadding vertical=spacing.md with verticalArrangement spacedBy(spacing.sm) and cards padded horizontal=spacing.md** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:159 contentPadding vertical=16.dp; AdminComplaintCard padding horizontal=16.dp vertical=4.dp (line 705); card inner padding 16.dp (710)
- **KMP:** Partial — AdminComplaintList LazyColumn contentPadding vertical=spacing.md, verticalArrangement Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.sm) (lines 340-341); card padding horizontal=spacing.md (700), inner padding spacing.md (706)
- **Explanation:** Native spaces cards via per-card vertical=4.dp padding and no list-level item spacing; KMP uses verticalArrangement.spacedBy(spacing.sm) at the list level and drops the per-card vertical padding. The exact dp values depend on LocalSpacing tokens (md/sm) which may not equal native's 16/4dp, producing subtly different inter-card gaps and outer margins. The internal row spacing also uses spacing.xs vs native explicit Spacer(8/12.dp).
- **Suggested fix:** Verify LocalSpacing.md == 16.dp and sm == ~8.dp; if not, align the list contentPadding and card padding to native's literal 16.dp/4.dp values, or document the design-token mapping as the intended spacing system.

**⚪ [Low] Admin card header — type as primary line and subject styling — Native renders subject in bodyMedium onSurfaceVariant; KMP renders subject in bodySmall onSurfaceVariant and adds maxLines=2 + ellipsis to the type title (native type title has no maxLines)** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintScreen.kt:719-728: type titleMedium SemiBold (no maxLines), subject bodyMedium onSurfaceVariant
- **KMP:** Partial — AdminComplaintRow:716-733: type titleMedium SemiBold with maxLines=2 + TextOverflow.Ellipsis + weight(1f); subject rendered in bodySmall (not bodyMedium) onSurfaceVariant, only when non-empty
- **Explanation:** The subject line typography differs (bodyMedium vs bodySmall), making the KMP subject smaller. KMP also truncates the type title to 2 lines with ellipsis (native does not truncate) and only renders the subject when non-empty (native always renders it). Minor but visible typographic divergence in the card header.
- **Suggested fix:** Render the subject in bodyMedium to match native; decide whether to keep the type maxLines=2 truncation (native is unbounded). Keep the non-empty guard only if subjects are reliably non-empty.

**⚪ [Low] Admin sort — app-version sort labels and semantics — Native APP_VERSION/APP_VERSION_DESC labels say 'App Version (Newest)'/'(Oldest)'; KMP says 'App version (asc)'/'(desc)'. Both sort lexicographically by string (no semver), matching** _(Business Logic)_

- **Native:** Yes — SortOption labels sort_app_version='App Version (Newest)', sort_app_version_desc='App Version (Oldest)' (strings.xml:493-494); sortedBy/ sortedByDescending on metadata appVersion string (AdminComplaintScreen.kt:145-150)
- **KMP:** Partial — admincomplaint_sort_app_version_asc='App version (asc)', admincomplaint_sort_app_version_desc='App version (desc)' (strings.xml:212-213); sortedBy/sortedByDescending on appVersion (AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:324-325)
- **Explanation:** Sort logic matches (lexicographic string compare, ascending/descending; nulls sort first/last per Kotlin convention). Only the dropdown labels diverge in wording ('Newest/Oldest' vs 'asc/desc'). Native's 'Newest/Oldest' wording is misleading for lexicographic sort but is the source-of-truth copy.
- **Suggested fix:** Reconcile the sort-mode labels to native's 'App Version (Newest)'/'(Oldest)' for strict parity, or keep asc/desc if deemed clearer (it is more accurate). Note native's available-version chip list sort uses a semver-aware comparator (numeric part compare) while the SortOption.APP_VERSION list sort is plain string — KMP matches both (chip comparator at AdminComplaintScreen.kt:318-336 is semver-aware, list sort is lexicographic).

**⚪ [Low] Admin — bulk update/delete & statistics helpers (native VM) — Native VM exposes bulkUpdateStatus / bulkDeleteComplaints / getComplaintsStatistics(recentCount, avgResponseTime) methods; KMP has no bulk paths and a reduced statistics shape** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdminComplaintViewModel.kt:227-352: bulkUpdateStatus, bulkDeleteComplaints, getComplaintsStatistics (returns ComplaintsStatistics with total, byStatus, byType, recentCount=last-24h, avgResponseTime)
- **KMP:** Partial — AdminComplaintViewModel computeStatistics (291-297) produces only total + byStatus + byAppVersion; no byType, recentCount, or avgResponseTime; no bulk intents/methods exist
- **Explanation:** Native VM carries bulk-mutation methods and a richer ComplaintsStatistics (recentCount, avgResponseTime, byType). However, the native bulk methods and the extended statistics fields are NOT wired to any native UI (the bulk methods have no UI callers and AdminStatisticsCard only uses statusCounts/appVersionCounts). So this is dead code in native; KMP correctly omitted the unused bulk paths (documented as GAP-CMP-20). Flagged for completeness; no user-facing impact.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed — the native bulk methods and recentCount/avgResponseTime are unused dead code. Confirm product does not intend to surface bulk moderation; if they do, it must be built on both sides.

**⚪ [Low] Admin auth gate — entry point routing — Both gate admin access via Admin.isAdmin in the Settings hub, navigating to the admin screen for admins and the user complaint screen otherwise — parity is HIGH here** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — SettingsScreen.kt:251-256: feedbacks_and_complaints item navigates to Screen.ComplaintAdmin if Admin.isAdmin else Screen.Complaint; Admin.isAdmin defaults true (admin/Admin.kt:10)
- **KMP:** Yes — SettingsReworkScreenRoute.kt:127: navigates to Screen.ComplaintAdminRework if Admin.isAdmin else Screen.ComplaintRework; shared/admin/Admin.kt isAdmin defaults true. The route adapter AdminComplaintReworkScreenRoute renders the rework AdminComplaintScreen and does not re-check admin status (same posture as native)
- **Explanation:** The admin auth gate is preserved with high fidelity: same Admin.isAdmin flag (default true), same Settings entry point, same admin-vs-user branch, same no-re-check-at-route posture. One nuance: KMP has two admin routes (Screen.ComplaintAdmin→AdminComplaintScreenRoute and Screen.ComplaintAdminRework→AdminComplaintReworkScreenRoute) but the live Settings gate uses ComplaintAdminRework, and per kdoc both now converge on the rework screen. No functional divergence in the gate itself.
- **Suggested fix:** None required. Optionally remove the now-redundant duplicate admin route (Screen.ComplaintAdmin vs ComplaintAdminRework) to avoid confusion, since both render the same rework screen.

**⚪ [Low] Admin closure-reason dialog — current status display & pre-fill — Parity is largely HIGH; minor: native closure dialog shows a 'Current status:' StatusChip row, KMP shows a 'Current: <name>' text label; KMP adds a 500-char counter native lacks** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — StatusChangeDialog.kt (ClosureReasonDialog) 336-345: 'Current status:' label + StatusChip(complaint.status); reason field maxLines 5, no char counter; pre-fills existing reason + type via LaunchedEffect (299-305); builds 'key: reason' for non-OTHER (440-444)
- **KMP:** Partial — ClosureReasonContent (387-532): preview card + reason-type dropdown + reason field (minLines 3/maxLines 6) + a '%d/500' counter; pre-fills + strips the 'key: ' prefix (400-402); rebuilds 'key: reason' for non-OTHER (515-519). No 'current status' StatusChip row (status is shown only in STATUS_CHANGE, not here)
- **Explanation:** The closure-reason flow is well-ported (type dropdown, pre-fill, key-prefix logic, auto-CLOSE in data layer all match). Divergences: native shows the current status as a StatusChip inside the closure dialog (KMP does not); KMP adds a 500-char cap+counter (native has no cap); KMP strips the stored 'key:' prefix for editing (an intentional fix to native's double-prefix bug, per its own kdoc). Reason field line counts differ (5 vs 3-6).
- **Suggested fix:** Optionally add the 'Current status:' StatusChip row to ClosureReasonContent for parity; the 500-char cap and prefix-strip are reasonable improvements but should be confirmed as intended deviations from native.

**⚪ [Low] Admin status-change dialog — header ID line vs preview card — Native StatusChangeDialog is a compact AlertDialog showing 'Complaint ID: <12 chars>' + radio list; KMP STATUS_CHANGE is a custom Card showing a full preview card (user/subject/body) + 'Current: <status>' + radio list** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — StatusChangeDialog.kt:45-110: AlertDialog with title 'Change Status', body shows complaint_id_format(id.take(12)) text, 'Select new status' label, RadioButton+StatusChip per status, Update button enabled only when selection != current
- **KMP:** Partial — StatusChangeContent (304-385): custom Card (not AlertDialog) with a header Row (title + Back), an AdminComplaintPreviewCard (userId.take(12)+subject+body), 'Current: <status>' line, RadioButton+StatusChip per status, Confirm enabled when selection != current
- **Explanation:** Functionally equivalent (radio list excluding no-op, confirm gated on change). Structural divergence: native is a native AlertDialog showing just the truncated complaint ID; KMP is a custom Card-in-Dialog with a richer preview (user/subject/body) and a Back button (because KMP funnels through a MENU). The dialog chrome (AlertDialog vs custom Card r16 elev8) and the ID-vs-preview content differ.
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable functional parity; if visual parity matters, consider matching native's AlertDialog chrome and the simple 'Complaint ID:' line. Otherwise document the richer preview as an intentional design-system change.

**⚪ [Low] Admin delete confirmation dialog — warning icon and details card — Native DeleteConfirmationDialog has a Warning icon, a details Card (id+subject+status chip), and an error-colored Delete button; KMP DeleteConfirmationContent shows a preview card + warning text + Delete forever button, no warning icon** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — StatusChangeDialog.kt (DeleteConfirmationDialog) 458-548: AlertDialog with Icons.Default.Warning (error tint), title 'Delete complaint', message, a details Card (errorContainer alpha 0.3) showing complaint id (monospace), subject, and 'Status:' + StatusChip; confirm Button error-colored 'Delete'
- **KMP:** Partial — DeleteConfirmationContent (682-739): header Row (title error-colored + Back), AdminComplaintPreviewCard (user/subject/body), warning Text (admincomplaint_delete_warning), error-colored 'Delete forever' button. No Warning icon; no status chip in the details; uses the generic preview card (surfaceVariant) instead of native's errorContainer-tinted details card
- **Explanation:** Both confirm deletion with an error-colored button. Divergences: native shows a leading Warning icon (KMP none); native's detail card is errorContainer-tinted and includes the complaint ID (monospace) + a StatusChip; KMP reuses the neutral surfaceVariant preview card (user/subject/body, no status chip, no error tint). Button label 'Delete' vs 'Delete forever'.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a leading Warning icon and an error-tinted details card with the complaint id + StatusChip to DeleteConfirmationContent for closer parity; reconcile the button label.

### Onboarding ↔ Welcome  `onboarding-welcome`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 13 (🔴0 🟠1 🟡4 ⚪8)

> The native app implements a 3-step first-run onboarding wizard (Welcome → ThemeSelection → Sources) driven by a `first_launch` SharedPreferences boolean read in NavGraphV2 (rootStart = Welcome if firstLaunch else Library). Welcome shows a Lottie animated background + gradient overlay + title/subtitle + Get-Started; ThemeSelection shows a theme TabRow with notification-permission auto-request and a Continue button gated on the permission; Sources shows a source-seed list (default-language auto-enable based on locale) + Request-Source dialog + Upcoming-Languages card + Finish button that flips first_launch=false and clears the back stack to Library. The KMP app ports this faithfully into :ui/:presentation/:domain/:composeApp and wires it in App.kt with the SAME `first_launch` key and start-destination logic — but with several real divergences: (1) the KMP chain has FOUR steps (Welcome → Theme → Sources → RepoSettings → Library) where the Sources screen is rendered TWICE (step 3 and step 4 are the same SourcesScreen), and the flag flip moved from the Sources Finish button to the RepoSettings step; (2) the KMP Welcome and Sources backgrounds replace the native Lottie animation with a Compose gradient-sweep substitute (lottie-compose not on the :ui classpath) — different motion and visuals; (3) the KMP Theme step adds a TopAppBar titled "Theme" (native has no top bar) and adds a PureBlack/OLED Switch that native onboarding does not expose; (4) several minor control/typography deltas. The core flow works and reaches Library, so this is ParityPartial rather than Missing.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Onboarding ↔ Welcome</summary>

**🟠 [High] Onboarding chain structure / step count — Native onboarding is 3 steps (Welcome→Theme→Sources); KMP is 4 steps (Welcome→Theme→Sources→RepoSettings) with the Sources screen rendered twice** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — NavGraphV2.kt:160-187 + WelcomeScreenRoute.kt:17-19 (Welcome→Theme), ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:59 (Theme→Sources), SourcesScreenRoute.kt:27-36 (Sources Finish→Library, flips first_launch). 3 distinct screens, 3 steps.
- **KMP:** Partial — App.kt:409-431 wires Welcome/Theme/Sources, but SourcesScreenRoute.kt:167-169 navigates Sources→Screen.RepoSettings(isFirstOpen=true), and RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:132-147 renders the SAME ui/.../sources/SourcesScreen again with a Finish button. So the user sees the Sources screen twice in a row.
- **Explanation:** The native Sources step's Finish button directly flips first_launch=false and navigates to Library (SourcesScreenRoute.kt:28-31). In KMP the Sources step (step 3) Finish navigates to RepoSettings (step 4), which is literally the same SourcesScreen composable again (RepoSettingsScreenRoute renders SourcesScreen with isFirstOpen gating). The KMP SourcesScreenRoute KDoc explicitly admits this: 'The step-3 / step-4 redundancy (both render the rework Sources screen with a Finish button) is a pre-existing condition... a future Phase 9.x.onboarding.cleanup slice can collapse if desired.' A first-run user therefore taps Finish on a Sources list, then is shown an identical Sources list and must tap Finish again — a confusing duplicated step that does not exist in the native flow.
- **Suggested fix:** Collapse the KMP onboarding back to 3 steps: have SourcesScreenRoute.onFinish flip first_launch=false and navigate to Library directly (matching native SourcesScreenRoute.kt:28-31), and drop the extra RepoSettings(isFirstOpen=true) hop from the onboarding chain. Keep Screen.RepoSettings only for the in-settings entry.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — onboarding is exactly 3 distinct steps, each a different composable, ending at Library: - WelcomeScreenRoute.kt:17-19 → navigate(Screen.Theme). - ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:59 → navigate(Screen.Sources). - SourcesScreenRoute.kt:27-36 → SourcesScreen renders, Finish callback sets firstLaunch=false (line 28) and navigate(Screen.Library) with popUpTo(startDestinationId, inclusive=true) (lines 29-35). Goes DIRECTLY to Library. - Native Screen.Sources renders presentation/features/onboarding/sources/SourcesScreen.kt (its own composable, fun SourcesScreen at line 61). Native Screen.RepoSettings renders a DIFFERENT composable, repo_settings/ui/screens/RepoSettingsScreen.kt (RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:12,30). RepoSettings is NOT in the onboarding chain — grep shows it is reached only from HomeRoute.kt:215 (navigate(Screen.RepoSettings(false)), an in-settings entry with isFirstOpen=false). NavGraphV2.kt:160 startDestination = Welcome when firstLaunch; composables for Welcome/Theme/Sources at lines 168-187. KMP — onboarding is 4 steps, and steps 3 & 4 render the SAME ui/.../sources/SourcesScreen with a Finish button: - App.kt:402 startDestination Welcome; App.kt:409-431 wire Welcome/Theme/Sources; App.kt:543-549 wire Screen.RepoSettings → RepoSettingsScreenRoute. - WelcomeScreenRoute.kt:133-137 → navigate(Screen.Theme). - ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:170 → navigate(Screen.Sources). - SourcesScreenRoute.kt:164-170 renders me.manga.kira.ui.sources.SourcesScreen (import line 12) and onFinish (lines 167-169) → safeNavigate(Screen.RepoSettings(isFirstOpen=true)). Does NOT go to Library; advances to a 4th step. - RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:132-147 renders the SAME me.manga.kira.ui.sources.SourcesScreen (import line 10) with onFinish (when isFirstOpen=true) flipping first_launch=false (line 136) and navigate(Screen.Library) with back-stack clear (lines 137-142). - Shared screen ui/sources/SourcesScreen.kt:361 renders FinishButton iff onFinish != null; both routes pass a non-null onFinish, so the user sees the Sources screen with a Finish button TWICE in a row. The KMP SourcesScreenRoute.kt KDoc (lines 48-52) explicitly admits this: "The 4-step structure is preserved deliberately... The step-3 / step-4 redundancy (both render the rework Sources screen with a Finish button) is a pre-existing condition... a future Phase 9.x.onboarding.cleanup slice can collapse if desired." All cited line numbers in the claim match the current code.

**🟡 [Medium] first_launch flag flip location — Native flips first_launch=false in the Sources Finish handler; KMP flips it in the RepoSettings step (and not in Sources)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — SourcesScreenRoute.kt:21-28: PrefsDelegate(key='first_launch') and `firstLaunch = false` set inside SourcesScreen{...} onFinish before navigating to Library.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP SourcesScreenRoute.kt:167-169 does NOT touch first_launch; the flip happens later in RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:134-143 (`prefs.putBoolean("first_launch", false)`), gated on args.isFirstOpen.
- **Explanation:** Because the flag flip moved one step downstream, if a first-run user backs out or kills the app while on the duplicated step-3 Sources screen (after the first Finish but before reaching/finishing RepoSettings), first_launch remains true and they re-enter the entire onboarding wizard on next launch. In native, completing the single Sources step already persists first_launch=false. The key string ('first_launch') and pop-up-to-startDestination + launchSingleTop behavior are otherwise faithfully preserved.
- **Suggested fix:** Move the first_launch=false write into the first reachable Finish (Sources step) as native does, so completing the source-selection step is the canonical onboarding-complete gate. If the 4-step structure is kept, at minimum also flip the flag at the Sources step to avoid a re-entry window.

**🟡 [Medium] Welcome screen animated background — Native uses a Lottie raw animation (R.raw.background) full-screen; KMP replaces it with a Compose linear-gradient infinite sweep** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — WelcomeScreen.kt:33-37,119-132: rememberLottieComposition(LottieCompositionSpec.RawRes(R.raw.background)) + LottieAnimation(iterations=IterateForever, speed=1.0f, contentScale=FillBounds). Asset present at native-app/.../res/raw/background.lottie.
- **KMP:** Partial — ui/.../welcome/WelcomeScreen.kt:124-154: a rememberInfiniteTransition driving Brush.linearGradient(primary@0.35f, secondary@0.25f, base) with panning start/end Offsets over a 9000ms LinearEasing Reverse loop. The actual Lottie asset IS shipped (composeApp/.../composeResources/files/background.lottie) but is NOT rendered (lottie-compose not on :ui classpath, per the in-file comment).
- **Explanation:** The native Welcome shows a rich Lottie illustration/motion behind the content; KMP shows only a subtle two-color gradient sweep. This is a visible first-impression divergence on the very first screen the user sees. The vertical darkening overlay (background.copy(alpha 0.1f→0.3f→opaque)) is preserved verbatim on both sides, but the decorative animation is absent in KMP.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a Lottie-compose (or compottie KMP) dependency to :ui and render the already-shipped background.lottie via LottieAnimation with IterateForever/FillBounds to match native, or accept the gradient substitute as an intentional cross-platform compromise and document it as a known visual delta.

**🟡 [Medium] Theme selection step — TopAppBar — KMP Theme step adds a Material3 TopAppBar titled 'Theme'; native Theme step has no top bar at all** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** No — theme_selection/ThemeSelectionScreen.kt uses Surface + AnimatedBackground + a plain Column; there is no Scaffold/TopAppBar (grep confirms none). The step name is conveyed only by the in-body headline 'Choose Your Theme' (24sp) at line 123-130. No 'theme_screen_title' string exists in native strings.xml.

Visually the KMP step now has both a TopAppBar 'Theme' AND the in-body 'Choose Your Theme' headline (the headline is preserved per ThemeScreen.kt:360-364), producing a redundant double-title not present in native. The route KDoc acknowledges this as an intentional rework delta.

**🟡 [Medium] Theme selection step — PureBlack/OLED toggle — KMP Theme step exposes a PureBlack/OLED Switch row that the native onboarding Theme step does not have** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** No — ThemeSelectionScreen.kt / ThemeSelector.kt expose ONLY the Light/Dark/System TabRow plus the notification-permission section. There is no pure-black/OLED toggle anywhere in the native onboarding (OnboardingViewModel.kt only exposes darkMode + followSystem).

This is an added affordance/visual element on the onboarding Theme step. It is harmless functionally (default false) but is a real divergence from the source-of-truth onboarding surface and changes the step's layout/height.

**⚪ [Low] Sources (onboarding) animated background — Native Sources step uses the same full-screen Lottie background; KMP uses a Compose gradient drawBehind sweep** _(Component)_

The KMP code does correctly scope the decorative background to the onboarding entry only (non-onboarding/settings entry renders flat), matching native intent, but the motion/visual is a gradient approximation, not the native Lottie animation.

**⚪ [Low] Theme selection step — Continue button initial disabled state — Native disables Continue until notification permission resolves; KMP gates only when the permission callback is wired, with the same effect — but the default-permission semantics differ subtly** _(State)_

In the onboarding route (ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:171-172) onRequestNotificationPermission is non-null, so gating applies; hasPermission comes from rememberNotificationPermissionRequester().hasPermission (Android actual seeds from checkSelfPermission, RememberNotificationPermissionRequester.android.kt:113).

- **Suggested fix:** No fix required for Android parity; document the iOS/Desktop always-granted gate behavior. Verify the auto-request LaunchedEffect timing matches native (fires once on first composition) which it does.

- **KMP:** Partial — ui/.../sources/SourcesScreen.kt:758-761 LanguageHeader uses a Switch (master), and SourceRow:803-806 uses a Checkbox per source — the in-file GAP-SRC-08 comment states it reconciles the native m2 Checkbox to an m3 Checkbox.
- **Explanation:** This appears to be intentionally reconciled to match native (master Switch + per-source Checkbox), and the AnimatedVisibility reveal (fadeIn+expandVertically) mirrors the native LanguageToggleWithAnimation. Flagged only as a control-type note to verify against the exact native RepoToggleItem rendering; the per-source enabled/disabled caption (source_enabled/source_disabled) is added in KMP and reflects the native enabled/disabled desc.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify against the native RepoToggleItem/SwitchItem split that the master-vs-per-source control types match exactly; no change needed if native also uses Switch(master)+Checkbox(source).

**⚪ [Low] Sources step — default-language seeding policy — Native seeds with the raw device locale tag (no blank-coercion in the call site) and an English fallback; KMP coerces blank→'en' before seeding** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — sources/SourcesScreen.kt:77-79: LaunchedEffect(Unit) { setLanguageEnabledDefault("(${languageCode.uppercase(Locale.ROOT)})", true) } where languageCode = configuration.locales[0].language; RepoSettingsViewModel.kt:97-111 applies the English ('(EN)') fallback when no sources match.
- **KMP:** Yes — SourcesScreenRoute.kt:160-166 collects DataStoreHelper.languageFlow (initial='') and passes it as onboardingLanguageTag; ui SourcesScreen.kt:344-348 fires OnSeedDefaultLanguage; EnableDefaultLanguageSourcesUseCase.kt:124-130 does languageTag.ifBlank{'en'}.uppercase() then setLanguageEnabledWithFallback(primary='($tag)', fallback='(EN)').
- **Explanation:** The fallback-to-English behavior matches. The seed SOURCE differs: native reads the live Android device locale (configuration.locales[0].language) at the Sources step, whereas KMP reads the app's persisted user-selected language pref (DataStoreHelper.languageFlow, default ''). On a fresh first-run install the KMP pref is typically empty → coerced to 'en', so a non-English-locale device that has never set the in-app language would seed English sources in KMP but seed the device-locale sources in native. The keying (LaunchedEffect on tag) and idempotency are otherwise faithfully ported.
- **Suggested fix:** On the onboarding Sources entry, seed from the device/platform locale (a KMP locale provider) rather than the persisted app-language pref, so a fresh install on e.g. an Arabic device auto-enables Arabic sources as native does, falling back to English only when no locale sources exist.

**⚪ [Low] Sources step — Request-Source dialog body length validation — KMP adds an explicit minimum-5-character client-side gate on the request-source dialog; native FeedbackDialog has no such UI gate (relies on the use-case's require(length>=8))** _(Validation)_

- **KMP:** Yes — ui/.../sources/SourcesScreen.kt:870,910-919,937: submitEnabled = body.length>=5, isError when 0<length<5, 'minimum 5 characters required' supporting text, and a 500-char cap on input.

The KMP code itself notes the mismatch between its UI gate (5) and the legacy use-case gate (8), meaning a 5-7 char body passes the KMP UI gate but is rejected downstream with a snackbar error — a small validation inconsistency. Native shows no client-side length error at all.
- **Suggested fix:** Align the KMP client-side minimum with the downstream use-case requirement (8 chars) to avoid the 5-7 char accept-then-reject window, or remove the client gate to match native and let the server validate.

- **Explanation:** The pill dimensions (50dp height, 26dp corner radius, full width) and primary coloring match native. The structural difference is that KMP anchors the Finish button in a Scaffold bottomBar (always pinned at the bottom) whereas native lets it sit at the end of the scrollable/SpaceBetween content Column. Minor layout-anchoring delta; visually close.
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable as-is; if exact parity is needed, render the Finish button as the trailing content item rather than a pinned bottomBar to match the native Column placement.

**⚪ [Low] Welcome screen typography & button — Welcome title/subtitle/button styling is ported verbatim between native and KMP** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — WelcomeScreen.kt:74-112: title headlineLarge 36sp ExtraBold primary (bottom padding 12dp); subtitle bodyMedium 18sp onBackground@0.9f (horizontal 16dp/vertical 8dp); 24dp Spacer; Button fillMaxWidth height 52dp clip RoundedCornerShape(26dp) primary container, label labelLarge 18sp onPrimary; Column padding 24dp, Arrangement.Bottom, CenterHorizontally, animateContentSize tween(600).
- **KMP:** Yes — ui/.../welcome/WelcomeScreen.kt:170-218: identical values — title 36sp ExtraBold primary 12dp; subtitle 18sp onBackground@0.9f 16dp/8dp; 24dp Spacer; Button 52dp/26dp primary, label 18sp onPrimary; Column 24dp padding, Arrangement.Bottom, CenterHorizontally, animateContentSize tween(600). Strings welcome_title/welcome_suptitle/get_started match verbatim in both string catalogs.

Recorded as a positive-parity finding.

### WebView (Cloudflare solver)  `webview-screen`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 13 (🔴1 🟠2 🟡5 ⚪5)

> Native has TWO WebView surfaces: (1) a full-screen Cloudflare/anti-bot solver route (`WebViewComposeScreen` + `WebViewViewModel`, NavGraphV2.kt L527) embedding `android.webkit.WebView` directly with a custom `WebViewClient`/`WebChromeClient`, a 50-entry in-app history stack, Back/Forward/Reload/Save toolbar, page-title display, 0-100% determinate progress, render-process-gone crash recovery, lifecycle pause/resume, and same-host URL gating; and (2) an INLINE `WebViewDialog` (rounded 24dp dialog at 95%w x 90%h with a localized "Please solve the bot check" header) launched automatically by `Handle403Error` whenever the Reader/Details/Home flows hit a 403/Cloudflare error. The KMP rewrite keeps only the full-screen route, delegating the whole web stack to a cross-platform `WebViewHost` expect/actual (Android `WebView`, iOS `WKWebView`, Desktop KCEF). KMP did re-add Back/Forward/Reload via a `WebViewController` (the screen's own KDoc is stale and wrongly says these were dropped). The headline divergences: the entire inline 403 `WebViewDialog` interstitial is MISSING in KMP (replaced by navigating to the full screen or an error button); captured headers are narrowed from the full `request.requestHeaders` map to just `{Cookie, User-Agent}`; the page title is no longer shown; the Android crash-recovery / lifecycle / cache / focus / network / zoom-stability settings are dropped; the desktop actual ignores the UA override and is entirely unavailable on macOS. Header persistence (`saveHeaders → getRepoByName(api).refreshHeaders → saveHeadersForApi`) is otherwise faithfully ported.
