<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for WebView (Cloudflare solver)</summary>

**🔴 [Critical] Inline 403 / Cloudflare WebViewDialog interstitial — The auto-launching inline bot-check dialog (WebViewDialog) is entirely absent in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — work/webViewDialog.kt L23-75 defines `WebViewDialog` (a Compose `Dialog` with `DialogProperties(usePlatformDefaultWidth=false)`, a rounded `RoundedCornerShape(24.dp)` `Surface` at `fillMaxWidth(0.95f)`/`fillMaxSize(0.9f)`, `tonalElevation=6.dp`, a centered `titleMedium`/`SemiBold` 'Please solve the bot check' header, then the embedded `WebViewScreen`). It is shown automatically by core/util/Handle403Error.kt L38-48 when a screen's `State.Error.code == 403` (and by ReaderScreen.kt L649-656 on a 403 page error).
- **KMP:** No — grep across composeApp/ui/presentation/shared finds no `WebViewDialog` composable and no `Handle403Error` composable. KMP only exposes the full-screen `Screen.WebView` route (App.kt L535). Details/Home instead navigate to the full screen or show an Open-in-WebView OutlinedButton (DetailsScreen.kt L534-538 explicitly notes the inline WebViewDialog interstitial was deferred on the §253 list).
- **Explanation:** In native, a 403/Cloudflare block is resolved in-place: the user stays on the Reader/Details/Home screen, an overlay dialog opens the solver, and on dismiss the original load is retried automatically (Handle403Error onDismiss → retry). In KMP this seamless inline recovery is gone — the user must be navigated away to a full-screen WebView (losing reading position context) or manually tap an error button. The automatic 403 detection→dialog→retry loop (with `maxDismissals`/`dismissCount` guarding against infinite loops) has no KMP counterpart, so the core anti-bot recovery UX is materially degraded.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a cross-platform `WebViewDialog`/`Handle403Error` equivalent in :ui (or :composeApp) that renders `WebViewHost` inside a Compose `Dialog` (24dp rounded Surface, 95%x90%, tonalElevation 6dp, centered 'please_solve_the_bot_check' header) and auto-shows it when a screen state reports a 403, mirroring the native dismiss→retry + maxDismissals loop.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: Low). NATIVE (source of truth) — confirmed exactly as claimed: native-app/.../work/webViewDialog.kt L23-75 defines WebViewDialog (Compose Dialog, DialogProperties(usePlatformDefaultWidth=false), RoundedCornerShape(24.dp) Surface at fillMaxWidth(0.95f)/fillMaxSize(0.9f), tonalElevation=6.dp, centered titleMedium/SemiBold bot-check header, embeds WebViewScreen). native-app/.../core/util/Handle403Error.kt L22-49 auto-shows it on State.Error && code==403 with maxDismissals/dismissCount guard and runs onDismiss()=retry. Wired auto-detect+retry at HomeRoute.kt L136-146, MangaDetailsRoute.kt L57-67, ReadingScreenRoute.kt L88-104, ReaderScreen.kt L649-668. KMP — claim's core assertion ("entirely absent", "no KMP counterpart", "seamless inline recovery is gone", user "must ... manually tap an error button") is REFUTED. The automatic 403-detection -> solver -> auto-retry loop IS present, just rendered as a full-screen route instead of an inline dialog: presentation/.../details/DetailsViewModel.kt L404-417 auto-emits DetailsEffect.SolveCloudflareChallenge when AppError.Network.Http.statusCode in CHALLENGE_STATUSES (no user tap); presentation/.../reader/ReaderViewModel.kt L539-549 does the same for page-fetch 403-family errors; ui/.../details/DetailsScreen.kt L317 and ui/.../reader/ReaderScreen.kt L440-441 auto-invoke onSolveCloudflareChallenge from the effect collector; composeApp/.../routes/MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute.kt L250-279 (rememberCloudflareChallengeSolver) and ChapterImagesReworkScreenRoute.kt L182-211 (rememberReaderCloudflareChallengeSolver) navigate to Screen.WebView, arm a one-shot pendingRetry latch on currentBackStackEntryFlow, and auto-fire onRetry() on return — explicitly documented L235-245 as "the rework equivalent of the legacy Handle403Error + auto-retry-on-dismiss flow (bug #2)". KMP even WIDENED detection to {403,429,503,520-524} (CHALLENGE_STATUSES, DetailsViewModel.kt L160, ReaderViewModel.kt L629) vs native's 403-only. WHAT IS GENUINELY DIFFERENT (the real, narrower delta): (1) the inline WebViewDialog Compose component itself is absent in KMP — grep finds no WebViewDialog/Handle403Error composable, only Screen.WebView full-screen route; (2) recovery navigates the user away to a full-screen WebView rather than overlaying an in-place dialog, so reading/details context is visually left (valid UX point). ui/.../details/DetailsScreen.kt L533-540 documents this: the OutlinedButton "Open in WebView" is the rework's substitute for the inline WebViewDialog interstitial ("slice §253 deferral list") — but it is an ADDITIONAL manual affordance, NOT the primary recovery; the claim mischaracterizes it as the only fallback.

**🟠 [High] WebView header capture scope — Native persists the full intercepted request-headers map; KMP persists only Cookie + User-Agent** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L228-234 builds `savedHeaders` from the entire `request.requestHeaders.toMutableMap()` (every outbound header the WebView sent: Accept, Accept-Language, Referer, sec-* etc.) plus the injected `Cookie`, captured in `shouldInterceptRequest`. The full map is handed to `refreshHeaders`/`saveHeadersForApi`.
- **KMP:** Partial — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L181-189 builds `savedHeaders` as a `buildMap` containing only `Cookie` and (optionally) `User-Agent`. WebViewHost.android.kt L88-97 only surfaces `CookieManager.getCookie(resolved)` and `view.settings.userAgentString`; no other request headers are captured.
- **Explanation:** Sources that gate on headers beyond Cookie/UA (e.g. Referer, Accept-Language, X-Requested-With, sec-fetch-*) will no longer receive those captured values on subsequent repo fetches, because the WebView no longer captures or replays them. The KMP screen's own KDoc (L62-63) acknowledges this is 'still narrower than upstream Android'. This is a behavioral regression for any source whose anti-bot check inspects more than the cookie+UA pair.
- **Suggested fix:** Expand the `WebViewHost` contract with an `onRequestHeadersAvailable(Map<String,String>)` callback (Android can read them in `shouldInterceptRequest`; iOS/desktop best-effort) and merge them into `savedHeaders`, or document the deliberate narrowing as accepted per-source. At minimum capture Referer/Accept-Language which several sources check.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/webview/ui/screens/WebViewComposeScreen.kt: - L214-245 `shouldInterceptRequest`: gated on the initialUrl host (L219-221), then L226-234 builds `val headers = request.requestHeaders.toMutableMap().apply { put("Cookie", cookie) }` and assigns it to `savedHeaders` (L233). This captures the ENTIRE outbound request-header map (Accept, Accept-Language, Referer, X-Requested-With, sec-fetch-*, etc.) plus the injected Cookie. Confirmed this is the only `savedHeaders` write of header content (grep shows L228/233 are the sole capture site; L289 nulls it on crash). No separate per-header allowlist. - L466 Save button: `onSaveHeaders(savedHeaders, api)` hands the full map downstream; the per-source `refreshHeaders` impls call `dataStore.saveHeadersForApi(API, newHeaders)` (e.g. KomikuRepository.kt:278) which persists the map verbatim. So the full header map is what gets saved/replayed. KMP — /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/features/webview/ui/screens/WebViewComposeScreen.kt: - L181-189 `savedHeaders` is a derived `buildMap { put("Cookie", cookie); capturedUserAgent?...?.let { put("User-Agent", it) } }` — strictly Cookie + optional User-Agent. No other headers. - Capture channels are only `onCookiesAvailable` (L288-292) and `onUserAgentResolved` (L293-297). - KDoc L61-62 explicitly admits: "Source's full `request.requestHeaders` capture is still narrower than upstream Android, but the UA covers the bulk of the regression." KMP actual — /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/core/webview/WebViewHost.android.kt: - L83-98 `onPageFinished` is the ONLY capture path: L88-90 `CookieManager.getInstance().getCookie(resolved)` → `onCookiesAvailable`, and L95-97 `view?.settings?.userAgentString` → `onUserAgentResolved`. There is NO `shouldInterceptRequest` override and NO access to `request.requestHeaders`; the WebViewClient only overrides `shouldOverrideUrlLoading`, `onPageStarted`, `onPageFinished`. Confirmed no other request headers are captured. Both apps' save chains (`saveHeadersForApi`) persist whatever map is passed verbatim, so the divergence is entirely at the capture point: native = full request-headers map + Cookie; KMP = Cookie + UA only. One precision note on the claim text: Android's `WebResourceRequest.requestHeaders` map generally does NOT include the User-Agent header, so native captures "all outbound headers EXCEPT UA" while KMP captures "Cookie + UA". They are not strict subsets — KMP actually adds UA that native omits, while dropping Accept/Accept-Language/Referer/sec-* that native keeps. This does not refute the claim's core thrust (native = broad full-map capture; KMP = narrow allowlist), and the cited line numbers (native L228-234, KMP L181-189, host L88-97) are all accurate.

**🟠 [High] Android WebView render-process-gone crash recovery — Native recovers from a crashed WebView render process by recreating it; KMP has no recovery** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L277-293 overrides `onRenderProcessGone` to clean up, set `webViewError=true`, bump `recreationKey`, clear history/headers, and the `LaunchedEffect(webViewError, recreationKey)` (L102) rebuilds the WebView; a crashed-state placeholder Text ('WebView crashed. Recreating...') is shown meanwhile (L515-521).
- **KMP:** No — WebViewHost.android.kt declares no `onRenderProcessGone` override. If the render process dies, on Android 8+ the whole app process is killed (the framework default when `onRenderProcessGone` returns false / is absent).
- **Explanation:** The native solver was specifically hardened against WebView render-process crashes (a common occurrence on memory-pressured devices loading heavy Cloudflare challenge pages). Without an `onRenderProcessGone` override returning true, a render crash takes down the entire Compose-Multiplatform app instead of recreating the WebView — a crash regression directly in the anti-bot flow.
- **Suggested fix:** In WebViewHost.android.kt add `onRenderProcessGone(view, detail): Boolean` returning `true`, detach/destroy the dead WebView, and trigger recomposition to rebuild it (mirror native's recreationKey loop). Optionally surface a transient 'recreating' state through the controller.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/webview/ui/screens/WebViewComposeScreen.kt: the active (non-commented) implementation has crash-recovery exactly as claimed. L82-83 declare `var webViewError` / `var recreationKey`. L102 `LaunchedEffect(webViewError, recreationKey)` rebuilds the WebView. L277-293 override `onRenderProcessGone(view, detail)`: calls cleanupWebView(view), sets webViewError=true, recreationKey++, clears history, resets historyIndex/savedHeaders, nulls webViewInstance, and **returns true** (L292) so the framework does NOT kill the app process. L515-521 render a placeholder `Text(text = if (webViewError) "WebView crashed. Recreating..." else "Loading WebView...")` while recreating. (The duplicate copy at L538-1043 is fully commented out; the active code is real.) All cited line numbers (277-293, 102, 515-521) verified accurate. KMP — /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/core/webview/WebViewHost.android.kt: the WebViewClient at L64-99 overrides ONLY shouldOverrideUrlLoading (L65), onPageStarted (L78), onPageFinished (L83) — there is NO onRenderProcessGone override. DisposableEffect(webView, url) at L117-123 does a one-time loadUrl + destroy with no recreation-on-crash loop. The AndroidWebViewController (L131-185) has no recovery logic either. The commonMain screen /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/features/webview/ui/screens/WebViewComposeScreen.kt L50 KDoc explicitly admits upstream had 'render-process-gone recovery' that the rewrite delegated to WebViewHost — but the Android actual never implemented it. Exhaustive grep across the entire KMP tree (excluding native-app) for onRenderProcessGone\|RenderProcessGone\|recreationKey\|webViewError\|render-process returns exactly ONE hit: the KDoc prose at WebViewComposeScreen.kt:50. Zero actual override in any KMP actual (Android/iOS/Desktop).  Impact: with onRenderProcessGone absent (framework default = return false), Android API 26+ kills the process hosting a foreground WebView when its renderer dies — crashing the whole Compose-Multiplatform app. This sits in the Cloudflare cf_clearance anti-bot header-capture flow (rationale documented in both WebViewHost.kt L11-14 and the screen KDoc), where heavy challenge pages are prone to renderer kills under memory pressure.

**🟡 [Medium] WebView top-bar title — Native shows the HTML page title as the primary title line; KMP shows the URL (or 'Loading...') and never reads the page title** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — `pageTitle` is updated in `WebChromeClient.onReceivedTitle` (WebViewComposeScreen.kt L154-156) and rendered as the primary `Text` (L398-402: `pageTitle.ifEmpty { "Loading..." }`), with `currentUrl` as the secondary `bodySmall` line (L403-408).
- **KMP:** No — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L205-209 renders the primary `Text` as `if (isLoading) loading else currentUrl`, i.e. the URL, never the page title. There is no `onReceivedTitle` hook in `WebViewHost`; the Android actual's `WebChromeClient` only overrides `onProgressChanged` (WebViewHost.android.kt L101-106).
- **Explanation:** The top bar now shows the URL twice (primary line is the URL when loaded, secondary `bodySmall` line is also the URL) instead of native's page-title-over-URL pairing. Users lose the human-readable page title in the toolbar; both lines being identical also looks like a layout bug.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an `onTitleReceived(String)` callback to `WebViewHost` (Android `onReceivedTitle`, iOS `WKWebView.title` KVO/poll, desktop `CefDisplayHandler.onTitleChange`), store it as `pageTitle`, and render it as the primary title line with the URL as the secondary line, matching native L397-409.

**🟡 [Medium] Android WebView lifecycle pause/resume + timers — Native pauses/resumes the WebView and its timers on lifecycle changes; KMP does not** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L326-361 registers a `LifecycleEventObserver` calling `webView.onResume()/resumeTimers()` on ON_RESUME and `webView.onPause()/pauseTimers()` on ON_PAUSE, and `cleanupWebView` on ON_DESTROY.
- **KMP:** No — WebViewHost.android.kt only has a `DisposableEffect` that `loadUrl` on attach and `stopLoading()/destroy()` on dispose (L117-123). No `onPause/onResume/pauseTimers/resumeTimers` lifecycle handling.
- **Explanation:** When the app is backgrounded the embedded WebView keeps running JS timers/animations (battery/CPU drain) and is not properly paused, diverging from native's explicit lifecycle management. This can also affect Cloudflare JS challenges that expect the page to be foregrounded.
- **Suggested fix:** In WebViewHost.android.kt observe the Compose `LocalLifecycleOwner` (as native does) and call `onPause()/pauseTimers()` / `onResume()/resumeTimers()` accordingly.

**🟡 [Medium] Android WebView settings parity (cache/focus/network/zoom-stability) — Several WebView settings native sets are omitted in the KMP Android actual** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L111-151 sets: `isFocusable=false`/`isFocusableInTouchMode=false` (L113-114), `cacheMode=LOAD_CACHE_ELSE_NETWORK` (L122), `setRenderPriority(HIGH)` (L131), `setNetworkAvailable(true)` (L144), `textZoom=100` (L147), `defaultTextEncodingName="utf-8"` (L148), `layoutAlgorithm=NORMAL` (L149), and `setLayerType(LAYER_TYPE_HARDWARE)` (L150).
- **KMP:** Partial — WebViewHost.android.kt L37-62 sets javaScript/domStorage/database, loadWithOverviewMode, useWideViewPort, the security flags (allowFileAccess etc.), mixedContentMode, mediaPlayback, geolocation, multiple-windows, and zoom (support/builtin/displayZoomControls). It does NOT set cacheMode, renderPriority, networkAvailable, textZoom, defaultTextEncodingName, layoutAlgorithm, layerType, or the focus flags.
- **Explanation:** The native author added these as explicit 'ANR FIX' / stability tweaks (comments at L121, L143). Their omission means the KMP WebView uses framework defaults: default cache mode, default (lower) render priority, no forced hardware layer, default text encoding/zoom, and is focusable. While most are minor, the missing `cacheMode`/`renderPriority`/hardware-layer and focus settings were deliberately tuned to avoid ANRs and focus-steal during the challenge flow; dropping them risks the exact jank/ANR the native code worked around.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the remaining stability settings into the WebViewHost.android.kt `remember` settings block: cacheMode, renderPriority HIGH, setNetworkAvailable(true), textZoom=100, defaultTextEncodingName utf-8, layoutAlgorithm NORMAL, hardware layer, and isFocusable/isFocusableInTouchMode=false — matching native verbatim unless intentionally changed.

**🟡 [Medium] Desktop WebView availability (macOS) — Embedded WebView is unavailable on macOS desktop and renders a placeholder** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** N/A — native targets Android only.
- **KMP:** Partial — Main.kt L124 skips `KCEF.init` on macOS ('current KCEF bundle layout is incompatible'), so WebViewHost.desktop.kt L87-95 hits the null-client branch and renders the static text 'Embedded WebView unavailable on this Desktop runtime.' with no cookie/UA capture.
- **Explanation:** On macOS desktop the entire Cloudflare-solver flow is non-functional: no challenge page, no cookie capture, no header save. Any source requiring the WebView bypass cannot be unlocked on macOS. This is a platform-specific gap introduced by the migration's choice of KCEF, with no fallback (e.g. system browser).
- **Suggested fix:** Provide a macOS fallback (open the URL in the system browser and prompt the user to copy back, or bundle a layout-correct CEF), or clearly surface to the user that this source can't be unlocked on macOS rather than a generic 'unavailable' string.

**🟡 [Medium] In-app history stack (50-entry) and back navigation semantics — Native maintains its own 50-entry URL history list with custom back/forward; KMP delegates to the platform WebView's native history** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L79-80,L253-274 maintains a `mutableStateListOf` history capped at 50 entries with `historyIndex`, dedups consecutive same-URL entries, truncates forward history on new navigation, and Back/Forward `loadUrl` the stored URL (L412-449). The Android `BackHandler` (L364-383) walks this list and only closes when at index 0.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP uses the controller's `goBack()/goForward()/reload()` which call the platform WebView's native `goBack()/goForward()` (WebViewHost.android.kt L174-184). There is no app-level history list, no 50-entry cap, no dedup, and no explicit `BackHandler` — system back closes the screen rather than navigating WebView history.
- **Explanation:** Behavioral divergence: native's hardware-back first walks the in-page history and only pops the screen at the start; KMP's hardware/system back will pop the whole screen immediately (no BackHandler intercept in the common screen), so users can't use the system back button to step back through pages they navigated. The 50-entry cap/dedup logic is also gone (now whatever the platform WebView keeps). Toolbar Back/Forward do work via the controller, but the back-button UX regressed.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a platform back-press interceptor in the WebView screen that calls `controller.goBack()` when `nav.canGoBack` before popping (Android `BackHandler`, iOS swipe/back, desktop window), restoring native's 'back navigates page history first' behavior.

**⚪ [Low] Sub-frame anti-exfiltration gate (javascript:/file:) — Native blocks javascript:/file: schemes on sub-frame loads even when no sandbox is supplied; KMP only gates when a predicate is passed and the predicate's sub-frame rule differs subtly** _(Permissions)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L188-211 always runs `shouldOverrideUrlLoading`: for sub-frames it blocks `javascript`/`file` schemes unconditionally (L204-210). The gating is always active because it is baked into the screen's own WebViewClient.
- **KMP:** Partial — WebViewHost.android.kt L73 `val gate = allowNavigation ?: return false` means if no `allowNavigation` predicate is supplied, NOTHING is gated. The full-screen route always passes a `WebViewUrlSandbox` predicate (WebViewComposeScreen.kt L299), so the rule applies there, but any other `WebViewHost` caller without a predicate (e.g. a future inline dialog) gets zero sub-frame scheme blocking. The sandbox sub-frame rule itself (WebViewUrlSandbox.kt L54-57) faithfully blocks javascript:/file:.
- **Explanation:** For the full-screen route the behavior matches (sandbox always supplied). The latent regression is that the gate is opt-in in KMP rather than always-on as in native, so any `WebViewHost` usage that forgets the predicate silently loses the anti-exfiltration sub-frame block. The native design made the rule intrinsic to the component.
- **Suggested fix:** Make the same-host sandbox the default in WebViewHost (derive a `WebViewUrlSandbox(url)` internally when `allowNavigation` is null) so the javascript:/file: sub-frame block is always enforced, matching native's always-on WebViewClient.

**⚪ [Low] Desktop WebView User-Agent override — Desktop actual ignores the `userAgent` override parameter entirely** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** N/A — native is Android-only; it does not set a custom outbound UA either (relies on WebView default), but it captures and replays whatever UA it used.
- **KMP:** Partial — WebViewHost.desktop.kt L216-217 explicitly discards the `userAgent` param (`@Suppress("UNUSED_VALUE") val ignoredUserAgent = userAgent`), per the KDoc L46-54. It still reads the UA back via the JS bridge for capture.
- **Explanation:** On desktop, if a caller wants to force a specific UA before loading (to match a cookie earned elsewhere), it has no effect — Chromium's default UA is always used. Today no caller passes a non-null userAgent so impact is latent, but the contract is silently not honored on this platform, unlike Android/iOS which apply `settings.userAgentString` / `customUserAgent`.
- **Suggested fix:** Either wire the UA override through CefSettings at KCEF.init or a per-request handler, or change the `WebViewHost` KDoc/signature to make the desktop limitation explicit so callers don't rely on it.

**⚪ [Low] Determinate load progress 0-100% — Native always shows a determinate 0-100% progress bar; KMP shows indeterminate where the platform can't report percentage** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L158-161 tracks `progress` via `onProgressChanged` and renders `LinearProgressIndicator(progress = progress/100f)` (L482-487) — always determinate.
- **KMP:** Partial — Android does report determinate progress (WebViewHost.android.kt L102-104 → controller `progress = newProgress/100f`), and the screen renders determinate when `nav.progress != null` else indeterminate (WebViewComposeScreen.kt L264-279). But desktop (KCEF, L163-165) and iOS-at-finish set `progress = null`, falling back to an indeterminate bar.
- **Explanation:** On Android parity is effectively preserved. On desktop there is no determinate progress channel (indeterminate bar) and iOS uses polled `estimatedProgress` while loading. This is an acceptable platform limitation but is a minor visual divergence from native's always-determinate bar.
- **Suggested fix:** Document as accepted platform limitation; optionally drive desktop progress from `CefDisplayHandler`/load events if a percentage becomes available.

**⚪ [Low] Stale/incorrect KDoc on KMP WebViewComposeScreen — The KMP screen's KDoc asserts Back/Forward/Reload were NOT ported and `WebViewController` does not exist, contradicting the actual code** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** N/A — documentation issue specific to the KMP file.
- **KMP:** Yes — WebViewComposeScreen.kt L63-67 (Delta #3) and L114-123 claim forward/back/reload are 'NOT exposed here' and that `WebViewController` 'matches ZERO live references', yet the same file imports `rememberWebViewController` (L42), uses `controller.goBack()/goForward()/reload()` (L220-245), and `WebViewController.kt` defines the interface. The KDoc is self-contradictory and stale.
- **Explanation:** Not a runtime regression, but the load-bearing port-deltas manifest is factually wrong about a core feature (nav controls), which will mislead future maintainers auditing parity and could cause someone to 're-add' already-present functionality or wrongly conclude a regression exists.
- **Suggested fix:** Update the KDoc Delta #3 / audit-trail postscript to reflect that Back/Forward/Reload ARE implemented via `WebViewController`/`rememberWebViewController`, and remove the 'WebViewController matches ZERO references' claim.

**⚪ [Low] Save Headers button enable condition — Save button enablement uses screen-local `isLoading` (set only at first page finish) rather than the live controller loading state** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — Save `IconButton` enabled = `savedHeaders != null && !isLoading` where `isLoading` reflects ongoing WebChromeClient progress (WebViewComposeScreen.kt L465-468, L160).
- **KMP:** Partial — Save `IconButton` enabled = `savedHeaders != null && !isLoading` (WebViewComposeScreen.kt L246-248) but here `isLoading` is the screen-local flag that is set `false` once on the FIRST `onPageFinished` (L168, L286) and never set back to `true` on subsequent navigations, whereas Back/Forward/Reload use `nav.isLoading` from the controller. So after the first load, Save stays enabled even while a later navigation is in flight.
- **Explanation:** Inconsistency: the screen mixes two loading signals — the toolbar nav buttons use the live `nav.isLoading`, but the title text and Save button use the one-shot `isLoading`. After the initial page, Save can be tapped mid-navigation (capturing potentially partial cookies) where native would have it disabled. Minor, but a behavioral divergence in the save-gating.
- **Suggested fix:** Drive the Save button (and the title's loading text) off `nav.isLoading` from the controller for consistency, or reset the local `isLoading=true` on each new navigation, matching native's per-load progress gating.

### Design System / Theme  `design-system-theme`

**Parity verdict:** ParityHigh  ·  **Findings:** 12 (🔴0 🟠0 🟡3 ⚪9)

> The native app is the source of truth and carries TWO parallel design-system surfaces: (1) a Jetpack-Compose theme `YamiMangaTheme` in package `me.manga.kira.theme` (Color.kt/Theme.kt/Type.kt) and (2) an Android XML theme stack (`Theme.YamiManga` + splash `Theme.App.Starting`, colors.xml/values-night/colors.xml, dimens.xml, themes.xml). The KMP app re-implements the Compose theme in `:ui` (`YamiColors`/`YamiTypography`/`YamiShapes`/`YamiTheme` + new `Spacing`) plus a thin legacy alias in `:composeApp`. The Compose color schemes (dark/light M3 tokens), shapes (4/8/12/16/0 dp), and the 3-slot Gellix typography override (bodyLarge 16sp Bold, titleMedium 14sp Medium, titleSmall 12sp Normal) are token-for-token IDENTICAL between native and KMP — high parity on the core token sets. The headline divergences are: native's `dynamicColor` (Material You on Android 12+) is fully dropped to a no-op in KMP; the native XML `Theme.YamiManga` uses a DIFFERENT palette than the Compose theme (green tertiary, distinct surfaceVariant + an explicit surfaceContainer ladder) and the KMP composeApp ships no Android XML theme/manifest/splash at all; and KMP introduces a new `LocalSpacing` 8-pt scale that has no native counterpart. Elevation is M3-default on both sides (no custom elevation tokens either side).

**🟡 [Medium] App theme / Material You dynamic color — Dynamic color (Material You) is functional on native but a hard no-op in KMP** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — Theme.kt:106-114 picks dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)/dynamicLightColorScheme(context) when `dynamicColor && Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= S` (Android 12+), reading LocalContext.current.
- **KMP:** Partial — YamiTheme.kt:92 declares `@Suppress("UNUSED_PARAMETER") dynamicColor: Boolean = false` and the body (YamiTheme.kt:95) never branches on it; composeApp/theme/Theme.kt:26,33 forwards it but it is ignored. Always falls back to the static YamiDark/Light schemes.
- **Explanation:** Native supports OS wallpaper-derived Material You palettes on Android 12+ when `dynamicColor=true`. The KMP port silently drops this: the parameter is kept on the signature for source compatibility but does nothing. In practice the native default is `dynamicColor=false` (MainActivity.kt:339-341 never passes it true and the call site omits it), so the user-visible behavior may be unchanged today; however the capability present in the source-of-truth theme engine is gone, and any caller relying on it gets static colors. The KMP KDoc itself classifies this as FORECAST-NOT-YET-FULFILLED (Phase 10 expect/actual SPI not built).
- **Suggested fix:** Introduce a `:platform` expect/actual `DynamicColorProvider` (isDynamicColorAvailable + dynamic dark/light ColorScheme on Android via dynamicDarkColorScheme/dynamicLightColorScheme + LocalContext) and wire YamiTheme to consume it when dynamicColor is true; no-op on iOS/desktop. Until then, document the gap explicitly as a known reduced-capability rather than a transparent no-op.

**🟡 [Medium] Android window chrome / system bars / fullscreen — Native ships windowFullscreen, transparent translucent navigation bar, windowBackground, windowNoTitle via XML theme; KMP composeApp has no Android XML theme/manifest declaring these** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — themes.xml `Theme.YamiManga` lines 115-120: android:windowNoTitle=true, windowContentOverlay=@null, windowFullscreen=true, navigationBarColor=@android:color/transparent, windowTranslucentNavigation=true; line 102 windowBackground=@color/black (values-night line 102 windowBackground=@color/white). Applied as postSplashScreenTheme (themes.xml:135).
- **KMP:** No — composeApp/src/androidMain contains only kotlin platform helpers; no themes.xml, no colors.xml, no AndroidManifest.xml present under src/androidMain. System-bar handling exists only as a runtime helper HideNavigationBarSideEffect.android.kt (WindowCompat insets), not as a window theme.
- **Explanation:** Native establishes immersive/fullscreen window behavior, a transparent translucent navigation bar, and an explicit pre-Compose window background through the XML Activity theme — this governs how the window paints before/around Compose (edge-to-edge, nav bar scrim, the flash color during startup). The KMP composeApp module has no Android theme XML or manifest in this snapshot, so these window-level design-system attributes are not reproduced in-tree; the KMP Android window will use platform/AGP defaults unless declared elsewhere. This is a design-system divergence at the window-chrome layer (not the Compose token layer).
- **Suggested fix:** Add a KMP androidMain `Theme.YamiManga` style (or equivalent) mirroring windowFullscreen, navigationBarColor=transparent, windowTranslucentNavigation, windowNoTitle, and an appropriate windowBackground, and reference it from the KMP Android manifest, to reproduce native window chrome. Verify the KMP manifest's activity theme matches native's immersive behavior.

**🟡 [Medium] Splash screen — Native has an animated SplashScreen (Theme.App.Starting + installSplashScreen) with branded icon/background; KMP composeApp has none** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — themes.xml:133-137 `Theme.App.Starting` parent Theme.SplashScreen with windowSplashScreenBackground=?attr/android:colorBackground, postSplashScreenTheme=@style/Theme.YamiManga, windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon=@drawable/ic_launcher_foreground; MainActivity.kt:36,200 import + call installSplashScreen(); manifest applies Theme.App.Starting to the launcher activity.
- **KMP:** No — grep for installSplashScreen / SplashScreen / windowSplashScreen across composeApp returns no matches; no splash theme XML exists.
- **Explanation:** The native app presents a branded animated splash (launcher icon foreground on the theme background) via the AndroidX SplashScreen API and a dedicated starting theme that transitions into Theme.YamiManga. This is a visible part of the app's design-system/launch experience. The KMP composeApp does not install a splash screen nor declare a splash theme in-tree, so the migration loses the branded launch transition (or defers it to default platform behavior).
- **Suggested fix:** Port the splash: add a Theme.App.Starting style (parent Theme.SplashScreen) with the Yami launcher icon + colorBackground, set it as the launcher activity theme, set postSplashScreenTheme to the ported YamiManga theme, and call installSplashScreen() in the KMP Android entry Activity before setContent.

**⚪ [Low] Android Activity theme (XML Theme.YamiManga) — tertiary palette — Native XML Activity theme uses a GREEN tertiary palette that diverges from the Compose theme's blue/grey tertiary; KMP has no XML theme at all** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — values/colors.xml:75-78 light tertiary #006E1B / onTertiary #FFFFFF / tertiaryContainer #95F990 / onTertiaryContainer #002203; values-night/colors.xml:25-28 dark tertiary #7ADC77 / tertiaryContainer #005312 / onTertiaryContainer #95F990; mapped in themes.xml `Theme.YamiManga` (lines 97-100). Note this DIFFERS from the Compose DarkColorScheme/LightColorScheme tertiary (Theme.kt:28-31 / 64-67: tertiary #B8D0FF/#0061A3, tertiaryContainer #2C2C2F).
- **KMP:** No — KMP composeApp/src/androidMain has only kotlin (no res/, no themes.xml, no colors.xml). The only KMP tertiary tokens are the Compose ones in YamiColors.kt:65-68 / 99-102 (tertiaryContainer #2C2C2F), which match the native Compose theme but NOT the native XML theme's green tertiary.
- **Explanation:** Native ships two palettes: the Compose theme (used for all Compose content) and the XML `Theme.YamiManga` (the actual Activity/window theme, applied as postSplashScreenTheme). The XML theme's green tertiary + green tertiaryContainer affect any View-system / XML-attr-driven chrome (e.g. `?attr/colorTertiary` in XML, MDC widgets, the BottomNavigation active indicator referencing `?attr/colorPrimaryContainer`). Because KMP is pure Compose with no XML theme, these XML-only tokens have no equivalent. Low severity if the KMP app renders 100% in Compose (the green tertiary is never surfaced in Compose), but it is a real design-system divergence in the source of truth that should be confirmed as dead in the KMP rendering path.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm no Compose surface in the KMP app reads `tertiary`/`tertiaryContainer` expecting the green XML values (they would get the grey/blue Compose values instead). If green tertiary is intended brand color, reconcile the Compose YamiColors tertiary tokens with the XML palette; otherwise document the XML green tertiary as legacy View-system-only and intentionally not ported.

**⚪ [Low] Android Activity theme — surfaceVariant & surfaceContainer ladder — Native XML theme defines an explicit surfaceContainer ladder and a different surfaceVariant than the Compose theme; KMP carries neither (relies on M3 auto-derivation)** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — values/colors.xml:83-98 and values-night/colors.xml:33-48 define surfaceVariant (light #F3EDF7, dark #211F26) plus surfaceContainerLowest/Low/Container/High/Highest (e.g. dark #1A181D/#1E1C22/#211F26/#292730/#302E38), wired in themes.xml:107-114. Native Compose theme uses surfaceVariant #E3E2EC light / #44464F dark (Theme.kt:39,73) and does NOT set surfaceContainer* (M3 derives them from surface).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP YamiColors.kt sets surfaceVariant #E3E2EC light / #44464F dark (matches native Compose, not native XML) and does NOT declare surfaceContainer* tokens; M3 derives them from surface (#FEFBFF / #15202B). No XML ladder exists.
- **Explanation:** Same two-palette situation as the tertiary finding. The native XML theme's surfaceContainer ladder (#1A181D…#302E38 dark) and surfaceVariant (#211F26 dark, #F3EDF7 light) only affect View-system chrome. The Compose theme (native and KMP, identical) uses different surfaceVariant values and lets M3 auto-derive surfaceContainer* from the Twitter-blue surface #15202B, so Compose surfaceContainer surfaces will look different from the XML ladder. Low severity for a Compose-only KMP app, but worth confirming the KMP Compose surfaceContainer auto-derivation visually matches the native Compose app (it should, since the Compose schemes are identical).
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed for token parity (Compose schemes are identical native↔KMP). Optionally document that native's explicit XML surfaceContainer ladder is View-system-only and the Compose path intentionally relies on M3 auto-derivation on both sides.

**⚪ [Low] Spacing scale (8-pt grid) — KMP introduces a formal LocalSpacing token scale (xxs..xxl) that does not exist in the native theme** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** No — native has no Spacing data class / LocalSpacing; grep for `object Spacing`/`LocalSpacing`/`data class Spacing` in native-app returns nothing. Native uses inline literal dp values and a 2-entry dimens.xml (activity_horizontal_margin/vertical_margin = 16dp each).
- **KMP:** Yes — Spacing.kt:50-64 defines `data class Spacing(xxs=2, xs=4, sm=8, md=12, lg=16, xl=24, xxl=32 dp)` exposed via `LocalSpacing = compositionLocalOf { Spacing() }`, installed by YamiTheme.kt:110.
- **Explanation:** This is an ADDITIVE design-system abstraction in KMP with no native counterpart. It is not a regression of native behavior (native never had a spacing token system). The risk is indirect: if KMP screens consume LocalSpacing tokens whose values do not match the exact inline dp literals the native screens used at corresponding call sites, per-screen spacing can drift. The token set (2/4/8/12/16/24/32) is chosen to match the native app's most common padding literals, but native also used values outside this set in places; those screens must round to a token, which can change spacing by a few dp. The token scale itself is fine; verify per-screen consumption in the other section audits.
- **Suggested fix:** No change to the scale. During per-screen parity audits, verify each LocalSpacing usage maps to the exact native literal at that call site; where native used a non-grid value (e.g. 6dp, 10dp, 20dp), confirm the chosen token does not visibly shift the layout.

**⚪ [Low] Typography — non-overridden M3 slots / Gellix scope — Only 3 of the M3 type slots use Gellix on both sides; all other slots fall back to the platform default font — same on both, but worth confirming font fallback parity across platforms** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes — Type.kt:18-36 overrides only bodyLarge (16sp Bold), titleMedium (14sp Medium), titleSmall (12sp Normal) with GellixFontFamily; all other slots use M3 defaults (Roboto on Android).
- **KMP:** Yes — YamiTypography.kt:43-47 overrides the identical 3 slots with identical sizes/weights; all other slots inherit M3 defaults. Same 3-weight Gellix family (regular→Normal, semibold→Medium, bold→Bold).
- **Explanation:** Token parity is exact for the 3 overridden slots (family + size + weight match byte-for-byte). The subtlety is the NON-overridden slots: native (Android) falls back to Roboto for, e.g., titleLarge/headlineX/labelX, whereas KMP on non-Android platforms (iOS/desktop) will fall back to the respective platform default (San Francisco / system serif-sans). On Android the KMP fallback should also be Roboto, so Android↔Android parity holds. This is only a cross-platform concern, and is intentional (Gellix is Latin-only; default fallback preserves Arabic glyphs). Flagged so it is not mistaken for missing typography. No native regression on Android.
- **Suggested fix:** No action for Android parity. If pixel-identical typography is required on iOS/desktop, consider explicitly setting a fallback FontFamily for the non-Gellix slots; otherwise document the intentional platform-default fallback.

**⚪ [Low] Type scale — letter spacing / line height / additional slots — Neither side sets explicit letterSpacing or lineHeight on the 3 Gellix slots (both rely on M3 TextStyle defaults), and the legacy Type.kt comment hints other slots were intended but omitted — parity preserved** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Partial — Type.kt:19-33 sets only fontFamily/fontWeight/fontSize on the 3 slots; no letterSpacing, no lineHeight; trailing comment '…and so on (or omit and just rely on all the built-in defaults)' (Type.kt:35).
- **KMP:** Partial — YamiTypography.kt:44-46 sets only fontFamily/fontWeight/fontSize on the same 3 slots; no letterSpacing, no lineHeight.
- **Explanation:** Both implementations leave letterSpacing and lineHeight to the Material 3 TextStyle defaults for the overridden slots, so computed line height and tracking are identical on the same Compose/M3 version. There is no divergence here; recording it explicitly so the absence of explicit lineHeight/letterSpacing is documented as intentional parity rather than an oversight. One caveat: because line height is M3-default-derived, a future Compose-M3 version bump on the KMP side (if it differs from the native app's pinned M3 version) could change derived metrics — verify M3 versions align.
- **Suggested fix:** No change. Optionally pin/verify the Compose Material3 version used by KMP matches the native app's so default-derived lineHeight/letterSpacing stay identical.

**⚪ [Low] Shapes / corner radii — Shape tokens identical (extraSmall 4 / small 8 / medium 12 / large 16 / extraLarge 0 dp) on both sides** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — Theme.kt:89-95 Shapes(extraSmall=4dp, small=8dp, medium=12dp, large=16dp, extraLarge=0dp).
- **KMP:** Yes — YamiShapes.kt:36-42 Shapes(extraSmall=4dp, small=8dp, medium=12dp, large=16dp, extraLarge=0dp). Byte-for-byte match including the deliberate extraLarge=0dp (full-bleed reader surfaces).
- **Explanation:** Full parity. extraLarge=0.dp is intentional on both sides for full-bleed surfaces (reader). No divergence. Recorded as a verified parity point.
- **Suggested fix:** None — parity confirmed.

**⚪ [Low] Pure-black (AMOLED) override — pureBlack override logic and default identical on both sides** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — Theme.kt:117-125 when `darkTheme && pureBlack` copies background=Color.Black, surfaceContainer=Color.Black; default pureBlack=true (SettingsRepository.kt isPureBlack defaultValue=true).
- **KMP:** Yes — YamiTheme.kt:96-103 identical copy(background=Color.Black, surfaceContainer=Color.Black); ThemeState.kt:83 default pureBlack=true; shared SettingsRepository default true. KMP App.kt:341 passes pureBlack through.
- **Explanation:** Full parity: same override targets (background + surfaceContainer to pure black), same gating (darkTheme && pureBlack), same first-run default (true). One subtle note: the override sets surfaceContainer to black but not surfaceContainerLow/High/Highest, so derived container shades remain non-black on both sides — identical behavior, not a regression. Recorded as verified parity.
- **Suggested fix:** None — parity confirmed. (If a future polish wants fully-black containers, it must change both sides identically.)

**⚪ [Low] Theme mode model (system/dark/light tri-state) — Native uses two booleans (followSystem + darkMode); KMP presentation layer introduces an AppTheme tri-state enum, but persistence and effective-dark computation are equivalent** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.kt:319-341 reads followSystem + darkMode + pureBlack booleans; effective dark = `if (system) isSystemInDarkTheme() else dark`. Backed by SharedPreferences KEY_THEME_SYSTEM / KEY_THEME_MODE / KEY_PURE_BLACK.
- **KMP:** Partial — domain AppTheme.kt enum {Light, Dark, System} + ThemeState.kt; but App.kt:330-334 still reads followSystem/darkMode/pureBlack and computes `effectiveDark = if (followSystem) systemDark else darkMode`, identical to native. The enum is used by the rework theme picker, translated back to the same two booleans by ThemeRepositoryImpl.
- **Explanation:** The effective theme computation and persistence keys are equivalent (KMP App.kt:334 mirrors native MainActivity.kt:340). KMP additionally models the tri-state as a domain enum for the picker, but it round-trips to the same legacy boolean storage, so no behavior regression in how dark/light/system resolves at the theme layer. Recorded for completeness; defaults (followSystem=true, pureBlack=true) match on both sides.
- **Suggested fix:** None for the theme layer. (Picker-screen parity is covered by the settings/theme-picker section audit.)

**⚪ [Low] Wizard residue palette (Purple/Pink) and Type.kt resource Font — Default Android Studio wizard colors carried over verbatim into KMP (dead on both); native uses non-composable Font, KMP uses composable Font factory** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — native theme/Color.kt:5-11 declares Purple80/PurpleGrey80/Pink80/Purple40/PurpleGrey40/Pink40, unused by YamiMangaTheme; Type.kt uses non-composable `Font(R.font.gellix_*)` top-level val.
- **KMP:** Yes — composeApp/theme/Color.kt:5-11 carries the identical 6 unused wizard colors (dead code); YamiTypography.kt uses compose-resources `@Composable Font(Res.font.gellix_*)` via a composable `yamiTypography()` factory instead of a top-level val.
- **Explanation:** The wizard residue palette is dead on both sides (parity, harmless). The meaningful structural difference is that KMP must build the Gellix family inside a @Composable (compose-resources Font is composable), so typography is produced by `yamiTypography()` called at the MaterialTheme call-site rather than a top-level `val Typography`. This is a correct platform adaptation, not a regression — output type scale is identical. Recorded so the val→composable change is documented and not mistaken for a behavioral change.
- **Suggested fix:** None functionally. Optional cleanup: delete the unused wizard Purple/Pink colors on both sides in a dedicated polish pass (out of scope for parity).

### Reusable Components  `reusable-components`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 14 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡4 ⚪8)

> The native app has no single "design-system" component file; reusable behaviour lives in scattered files (LoadingScreen, ErrorScreen, LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar with BOTH a list and a grid variant, SocialMediaRow, plus per-card cover/badge code inline in MangaCard/MangaSearchItems/IconWithCount and the SimpleStatusScreen in SiteMaintenanceScreen). The KMP rework consolidates these into :ui/components (YamiCoverImage, YamiStateViews, YamiCountBadge, YamiIconButton, YamiSocialMediaRow, VerticalFastScroller, YamiIcons) plus a vendored SocialMediaIcons. The fast-scroller, social row, and site-status view are faithful 1:1 list-variant ports, but several concrete regressions exist: the LazyGrid fast-scroller (VerticalGridFastScroller, used by the native Library grid) was dropped entirely, so the Library grid has no quick-jump thumb; the social-row press-scale spring animation was dropped; systemGestureExclusion was dropped from the scroller; the error state was restructured from a 3-action horizontal IconAboveTextButton row to stacked vertical Buttons; the count badge changed from native's adaptive BoxWithConstraints sizing to fixed 14dp; the website globe icon was swapped from the detailed earth drawable to a simpler Material glyph; and the cover image's loading/error treatment (Coil ColorPainter placeholder/error) was replaced with a tinted box + broken-image glyph with no loading placeholder distinct from the tint.

**🟠 [High] Fast scroller (Library grid) — VerticalGridFastScroller (LazyGridState overload) dropped entirely in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar.kt:229 `fun VerticalGridFastScroller(state: LazyGridState, columns, arrangement, contentPadding, ...)`; used by the Library grid at LibraryItems.kt:188 `VerticalGridFastScroller(...)`.
- **KMP:** No — ui/components/VerticalFastScroller.kt contains ONLY the LazyListState overload; grep for VerticalGridFastScroller across :ui returns nothing. LibraryScreen.kt has no scroller/scrollbar reference at all (the grid uses a bare LazyVerticalGrid).
- **Explanation:** The native Library is a grid with a draggable quick-jump thumb (VerticalGridFastScroller wrapping the LazyVerticalGrid). The KMP rework ported only the list-variant VerticalFastScroller and wired it solely into the Details chapter list; the Library grid has no fast-scroller. On large libraries the user loses the draggable scrollbar entirely — a usable interaction present in native is absent in KMP.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the VerticalGridFastScroller (LazyGridState overload, including rememberColumnWidthSums and the grid computeScrollOffset/computeScrollRange) from LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar.kt into :ui/components, and wrap the Library LazyVerticalGrid with it.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/common/componants/scroll/LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar.kt:229 defines `fun VerticalGridFastScroller(state: LazyGridState, columns: GridCells, arrangement: Arrangement.Horizontal, contentPadding: PaddingValues, ...)` — a SubcomposeLayout fast-scroller with a draggable thumb (drag-handling LaunchedEffect L281-310; thumbColor param) plus grid-specific computeScrollOffset/computeScrollRange helpers at L389/L404. It is used by the Library grid at native-app/.../library/ui/screens/LibraryItems.kt:188 `VerticalGridFastScroller(state = gridState, columns = ..., arrangement = ..., contentPadding = ..., modifier = ..., thumbColor = ...)` wrapping `LazyVerticalGrid(... state = gridState ...)` at L198. Import at LibraryItems.kt:51. The native scroll file holds BOTH overloads (VerticalFastScroller L61 + VerticalGridFastScroller L229). KMP: ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/components/VerticalFastScroller.kt has ONLY the LazyListState overload — `fun VerticalFastScroller(listState: LazyListState, ...)` at L79; no LazyGridState/GridCells anywhere in the file. Its sole caller is ui/.../details/DetailsScreen.kt:573 `VerticalFastScroller(listState = listState, ...)` wrapping a `LazyColumn` (chapter list, L577) — exactly the claim that the list variant is wired solely into Details. The KMP Library grid at ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt:834-863 (`LibraryGrid`) uses a bare `LazyVerticalGrid(columns = GridCells.Adaptive(...), ...)` at L844 with NO rememberLazyGridState, NO scroller wrapper, and NO scroll/scrollbar import in the file. Grep for `VerticalGridFastScroller` across :ui/:presentation/:domain/:data/:shared returns ZERO live definitions or callers (only KDoc prose). A stray duplicate composeApp/.../scroll/LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar.kt exists, but its own KDoc (L70-71, L109-120) states the grid overload "was retired ... zero callers across the tree," and it too defines only the LazyListState VerticalFastScroller (L137) — no grid fun, no LazyGridState/GridCells. KMP message (lines 207-213): style=MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, color=MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface (theme default, NOT error red), no maxLines/overflow set (unbounded, no ellipsize). Call site HomeScreen.kt:326-334 passes all three label/onClick pairs, so all three stacked buttons actually render. Every claimed detail (horizontal row -> vertical stack; icons present -> absent; filled+outlined mix vs transparent equal-weight; 14.sp Bold error maxLines=2 ellipsized -> titleMedium onSurface unbounded) is verified correct. Minor imprecision only: the file also contains a sibling single-action YamiErrorState at 130-167, but it does not affect the verdict.

**🟡 [Medium] Social media row — Press-scale spring animation on each social button dropped in KMP** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — SocialMediaRow.kt:118-163 each SocialMediaButton tracks `isPressed`, drives `animateFloatAsState` targetValue 0.85f when pressed via spring(DampingRatioMediumBouncy, StiffnessHigh), applies Modifier.scale(scale), and resets isPressed after a 150ms delay (LaunchedEffect).
- **KMP:** No — YamiSocialMediaRow.kt:114-145 SocialMediaButton is a plain IconButton with no scale animation, no isPressed state, no spring, no LaunchedEffect delay.
- **Explanation:** Native gives each social icon a tactile bounce (shrinks to 85% and springs back) on tap. KMP buttons are static. The layout math (6 buttons, 8.dp spacing, sizes coerced 36..56dp / icons 18..28dp), container colors (primaryContainer 0.3 / 0.2 alpha), and tint (primary) are otherwise byte-identical, so this is the one behavioural divergence in the row.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the animateFloatAsState press-scale (spring DampingRatioMediumBouncy / StiffnessHigh, 0.85f target) + Modifier.scale + 150ms isPressed-reset LaunchedEffect to YamiSocialMediaRow.SocialMediaButton to match the native press feedback.

**🟡 [Medium] Fast scroller — Modifier.systemGestureExclusion() on the thumb omitted in KMP** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar.kt:168-175 applies Modifier.systemGestureExclusion() to the thumb when `isThumbVisible && !isThumbDragged && !isScrollInProgress` so an edge swipe starting on the thumb is treated as a drag, not an OS back gesture.
- **KMP:** No — VerticalFastScroller.kt:170-197 omits the systemGestureExclusion .then() block; KDoc lines 60-67 acknowledge it was deliberately dropped because the helper lives in :composeApp and :ui cannot depend on it.
- **Explanation:** On Android, without systemGestureExclusion a predictive-back / edge swipe that begins exactly on the fast-scroller thumb (which sits on the layout-end edge) can be consumed by the system back gesture instead of dragging the thumb. Native excludes the thumb region; KMP does not, so the drag may be intercepted on Android. The thumb position (placed at contentWidth - scrollerWidth, end edge), ThumbLength 48.dp, ThumbThickness 12.dp, 8.dp horizontal padding are otherwise identical.
- **Suggested fix:** Introduce a no-arg gesture-exclusion modifier in :ui via an expect/actual (Android actual = Modifier.systemGestureExclusion(), other platforms = no-op) and apply it on the thumb under the same isThumbVisible && !isThumbDragged && !isScrollInProgress condition as native.

**🟡 [Medium] Count badge (card chapter/read/download/bookmark counts) — Native IconWithCount is adaptive (BoxWithConstraints, width-proportional sizing, white tint, AutoSubtitleText); KMP YamiCountBadge is fixed-size with theme content color** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — IconWithCount.kt:23-71: BoxWithConstraints computes iconDp = (width*0.4f).coerceIn(1.dp,24.dp), fontSp = (width*0.3f).coerceIn(1,12).sp, padding (width*0.1f).coerceIn(0.2.dp,4.dp); Icon tint hardcoded Color.White; count via AutoSubtitleText (auto-shrinking BasicText). Used 4x in MangaCard.kt:313-328.
- **KMP:** Partial — YamiCountBadge.kt:30-54: Row with FIXED iconSize default 14.dp, count Text style labelSmall, tint defaults LocalContentColor.current, fixed 2.dp spacing. No width-adaptive scaling, no auto-sizing text, no white default.
- **Explanation:** Native badge scales its icon (1-24dp), font (1-12sp) and padding proportionally to the available cell width and forces white tint (it sits over the card cover gradient). KMP uses a fixed 14dp icon + labelSmall text + ambient content color, so on narrow grid cells the native shrink behaviour is lost and the default tint is theme-content (not white) — readability over the cover scrim depends on the caller passing the correct tint. The native icon set was also Outlined (List/RemoveRedEye/Download/BookmarkAdd) whereas YamiIcons exposes Filled variants.
- **Suggested fix:** Either make YamiCountBadge width-adaptive (BoxWithConstraints proportional icon/font/padding matching IconWithCount's 0.4/0.3/0.1 fractions and clamps) or document that callers must pass tint=Color.White and an appropriate iconSize; ensure each card call site forwards a white tint over the cover.

**🟡 [Medium] Cover image (grid/list cards) — Cover loading/error treatment changed: native uses Coil ColorPainter placeholder+error; KMP uses a tinted box + broken-image glyph and no distinct loading placeholder** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaCard.kt:87-93,146-158: AsyncImage gets placeholder=ColorPainter(onSurface alpha 0.12) and error=ColorPainter(error alpha 0.24); during load a 12% onSurface fill shows, on error a 24% error-tinted fill shows. MangaSearchItems SearchItems.kt:101-107 uses a plain AsyncImage with no placeholder/error.
- **KMP:** Partial — YamiCoverImage.kt:69-96: tinted box background = placeholderTint(outline) at 0.15 alpha for both loading and blank URL; on terminal error it overlays a 28.dp BrokenImage glyph at placeholderTint 0.6 alpha. No loading-vs-blank distinction (both just show the 0.15 tint); error shows a glyph rather than native's flat error-tinted fill.
- **Explanation:** Native's failure state is a 24%-alpha error-colored solid fill (no glyph); KMP's failure state is a broken-image glyph over a 15% outline-tinted box. Native's loading placeholder is a 12%-alpha onSurface fill; KMP's loading state is the same 15% outline tint as a blank URL. The placeholder tint token differs (native onSurface 0.12 vs KMP outline 0.15) and the error visual differs (flat error fill vs glyph). These are visible differences in the empty/loading/error cell rendering across Home/Search/Library grids.
- **Suggested fix:** Align YamiCoverImage's placeholder tint to onSurface@0.12 and decide on the error treatment: either render a flat error-container-tinted fill to match native, or keep the broken-image glyph but document the intentional change. Optionally surface a distinct loading state if native parity is required.

**⚪ [Low] Cover image scrim — Bottom gradient scrim differs from native card overlay (start/stop and end alpha)** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaCard.kt:286-294 bottom info column draws Brush.verticalGradient(Transparent → Black alpha 0.8) over the lower area; MangaSearchItems SearchItems.kt:119-124 uses a flat Black alpha 0.3 band 50.dp tall behind the title.
- **KMP:** Partial — YamiCoverImage.kt:97-108 scrim (opt-in, default OFF) = Brush.verticalGradient(0.55f→Transparent, 1f→Black alpha 0.45). Different stop (0.55) and weaker end alpha (0.45 vs native 0.8).
- **Explanation:** The KMP shared scrim tops out at Black 0.45 alpha starting at 55% height, whereas the native card title gradient reaches Black 0.8 alpha. The native search cell uses a flat 0.3 band, not a gradient. Because YamiCoverImage's scrim defaults to false, parity depends on each card re-implementing its own gradient anyway; the shared scrim, when used, is lighter than native.
- **Suggested fix:** If callers rely on YamiCoverImage's built-in scrim for the title backdrop, raise the end alpha toward 0.8 to match the native MangaCard gradient; otherwise confirm each card site overlays its own native-matching gradient.

At 18-28dp button size the difference is subtle but present, and the native fill attribute (colorOnSecondary) differs from KMP's primary tint. The other five glyphs (X, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Discord) are path-faithful ports.

**⚪ [Low] Facebook social icon — Native uses Material Icons-Extended Icons.Default.Facebook; KMP vendors an equivalent path** _(Icon)_

The Instagram and WhatsApp glyphs are likewise ported from the native ic_instagram.xml/ic_whatsapp.xml drawables at 32x32 viewport. **⚪ [Low] Loading state — Native LoadingScreen wraps the spinner in a 16.dp-padded fillMaxSize Box; KMP YamiLoadingState has no padding** _(Spacing)_

The KMP HomeScreen separately corrects the color to inversePrimary at its own call site (HomeScreen.kt:317-318 comment), but the shared YamiLoadingState itself does not, so any other caller gets primary instead of native's inversePrimary.

It changes the visual of empty screens versus native's ad-hoc grey text, but since native had no single source-of-truth empty component there is nothing to diverge from pixel-for-pixel. Flagged so the divergence in empty-screen appearance vs native's plain text is on record.

HomeScreen.kt:281-311 passes the same icon+color triples (Build/primary/primaryContainer, Error/error/errorContainer, Error/tertiary/tertiaryContainer).

No user-visible regression.

**⚪ [Low] Fast scroller fade duration — Native derives scrollbar fade duration from ViewConfiguration; KMP hardcodes 250ms** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — LazyVerticalScrollerWithScrollBar.kt:448-454 FadeOutAnimationSpec/ImmediateFadeOutAnimationSpec use durationMillis = ViewConfiguration.getScrollBarFadeDuration() (the platform/OEM-configured value).
- **KMP:** Partial — VerticalFastScroller.kt:251,256-262 hardcodes SCROLLBAR_FADE_DURATION_MS = 250 (the historical Android default), with a KDoc note (lines 71-73) that ViewConfiguration is unavailable in common code.

The 2000ms pre-fade delay is identical on both sides. Minor and only observable on devices whose ViewConfiguration differs from 250ms.

Note the native ErrorScreen back button uses Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack with contentDescription R.string.desc_back; the KMP equivalent YamiIcons.Back is also auto-mirrored, so RTL behaviour matches.

### Navigation & Screen Flow  `navigation-flow`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 11 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡5 ⚪4)

> Both apps use a single androidx.navigation type-safe NavHost driven by a sealed `Screen` route class, hosted in a Material 3 Scaffold with a 5-tab bottom NavigationBar (Library/Updates/Home/History/Settings) plus a top HorizontalDivider, with bottom-bar visibility toggled per-route via `onBottomBarVisibleChange`/`SideEffect`. The start destination is chosen identically from the `first_launch` SharedPrefs flag (Welcome on first run, else Library). The bottom bar items, order, icons, indicator color and Home-tab-reselect onClick branch are byte-for-byte ported. However there are real divergences: (1) the Home-tab double-tap "scroll to top" feature is dead in KMP — nothing ever registers `NavigationHandlerHolder.homeReselectHandler`; (2) the native `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails` route (the offline/library-manga details screen) and its whole identity-based navigation flow from Home/Library/History/Updates were removed in KMP — these now route to the URL-based `Screen.MangaDetails` losing the "is this saved in library?" branch and the "manga deleted from library" Toast guards; (3) the KMP Settings hub navigates to the *rework* sibling routes (StatisticsRework/LanguageRework/AboutRework/ComplaintRework/DownloadsRework/ThemeRework) instead of the native's legacy user-facing routes, so the legacy route keys are orphaned and users land on reduced-feature screens; (4) the native MangaDetails download-click `popUpTo(graph.id)`→Library-tab back-stack behaviour is replaced by a navigate to `DownloadsRework`; (5) the KMP App.kt drops the native Home/Library `BackHandler` blocks; (6) the admin `ApiTestScreen` testing-mode top-level branch in MainActivity is absent. Deep links are not a concern — native uses MAIN/LAUNCHER only with no URI intent-filters and notifications carry no navigation PendingIntent.

**🟠 [High] Library/History/Updates/Home → manga details routing (LibraryMangaDetails) — The native identity-based `Screen.LibraryMangaDetails(mangaId)` route and the entire offline/library-details flow are removed in KMP; all paths now go to URL-based `Screen.MangaDetails(url, api)`** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — Screen.LibraryMangaDetails(mangaId: Long) declared in NavGraphV2.kt:101-104 and hosted at NavGraphV2.kt:469-497 via LibraryMangaRoute. Home (NavGraphV2.kt:220-238) branches on isSaved: looks up id via sharedChaptersVm.getIdByApiTitle and navigates to LibraryMangaDetails(id) if saved, else MangaDetails(url, api). Library (291-308) and History (323-326) and Updates (424) all navigate to LibraryMangaDetails(mangaId).
- **KMP:** No — Screen.kt has no LibraryMangaDetails route at all (App.kt:106-109 documents it was retired as a 'cascade orphan'). HistoryScreenRoute.kt:175-181 and UpdatesScreenRoute.kt:110-116 unconditionally navigate to Screen.MangaDetails(url, api). LibraryScreenRoute.kt:201-211 navigates to Screen.MangaDetailsRework(full tuple).
- **Explanation:** Native distinguishes 'open the manga I already saved (by DB id, works offline / from cached chapters)' from 'open a network manga (by url+api)'. KMP collapses everything to URL/api-based details. For saved/offline manga this is a behavioural regression: the library-manga details screen (LibraryMangaRoute) which read from the local DB is gone, and saved-manga navigation from Home/Library/History/Updates now always hits the network-details path, losing offline access and the saved-state fast path.
- **Suggested fix:** Re-introduce an identity-based details path (e.g. a route arg carrying mangaId, or have the rework DetailsViewModel resolve library membership and prefer the local DB when a saved id exists) so saved manga open from their cached/local record exactly as native's LibraryMangaDetails did, including offline.
