**🟠 [High] Settings hub → secondary screens (Statistics/Language/About/Complaint/Downloads/Theme/WhatsNew) — KMP Settings navigates to the *Rework* sibling routes; native navigates to the legacy user-facing routes, leaving the native-parity route keys orphaned in KMP** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — SettingsScreen.kt navigates to the canonical routes: Screen.Statistics (line 269), Screen.LanguageScreen (273), Screen.DownloadsScreen (277), Screen.AboutScreen (303), Screen.Complaint / Screen.ComplaintAdmin (252-254 admin-gated).
- **KMP:** Partial — SettingsRoute.kt:146-156 maps every destination to a Rework route: STATISTICS→StatisticsRework, LANGUAGE→LanguageRework, ABOUT→AboutRework, COMPLAINT→ComplaintAdminRework/ComplaintRework, WHATSNEW→WhatsNewRework, DOWNLOADS→DownloadsRework, THEME→ThemeRework. The legacy keys Screen.Statistics/LanguageScreen/AboutScreen/Complaint/ComplaintAdmin/DownloadsScreen/WhatsNewScreen are still declared and bound in App.kt but are now unreachable from any user entry point.
- **Explanation:** The KMP Screen.kt KDocs themselves document that the Rework screens are deliberately *reduced-surface* ports (e.g. AboutRework omits the Whats-new row, Source-code row, app-icon and SocialMediaRow per Screen.kt:623-629; LanguageRework omits the 'Request a new language' FeedbackDialog per Screen.kt:757-763; ComplaintRework is read-only with no reply/edit/delete per Screen.kt:808-816; Updates/Statistics noted as reduced). Because Settings now routes to these reduced screens, the user actually lands on feature-reduced versions of About/Language/Complaint/etc., a user-visible feature regression versus native — even though the full-parity legacy route keys still technically exist in the graph (dead).
- **Suggested fix:** Either (a) finish porting the missing affordances into the Rework screens so they reach parity before they are the user-facing target, or (b) point the Settings nav rows at the legacy parity routes until the rework screens reach parity. Also remove or document the now-orphaned legacy route keys to avoid confusion.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: Low). NATIVE (source of truth) — confirmed exactly as claimed. native-app/.../settings/ui/screens/SettingsScreen.kt navigates to canonical routes: Complaint/ComplaintAdmin admin-gated at lines 251-255, Screen.Statistics at 269, Screen.LanguageScreen at 273, Screen.DownloadsScreen at 277, Screen.AboutScreen at 303. These are real, bound routes in native NavGraphV2.kt (composable<Screen.Statistics> L520, LanguageScreen L543, DownloadsScreen L550, AboutScreen L557, Complaint L567, ComplaintAdmin L584), each hosting the full native feature screen. KMP Settings routing — confirmed verbatim. composeApp/.../navigation/routes/SettingsRoute.kt:146-156 maps every destination to a Rework route (THEME→ThemeRework, STATISTICS→StatisticsRework, LANGUAGE→LanguageRework, ABOUT→AboutRework, COMPLAINT→ComplaintAdminRework/ComplaintRework, WHATSNEW→WhatsNewRework, DOWNLOADS→DownloadsRework). KMP legacy keys still declared + bound + user-unreachable — confirmed. Screen.kt declares both legacy keys (Statistics L33, LanguageScreen L46, DownloadsScreen L49, AboutScreen L52, Complaint L83, ComplaintAdmin L86, WhatsNewScreen L36) and Rework keys (L268,601,679,729,783,835,913,1058). App.kt binds the legacy keys (composable<Screen.Statistics> L527, LanguageScreen L551, DownloadsScreen L559, AboutScreen L589, Complaint L597, WhatsNewScreen L605, ComplaintAdmin L613). A tree-wide grep found ZERO live navigate(Screen.Statistics\|LanguageScreen\|DownloadsScreen\|AboutScreen\|Complaint\|ComplaintAdmin\|WhatsNewScreen) calls (only KDoc-comment mentions), so the legacy keys are indeed orphaned/dead. The CLAIM'S CENTRAL ERROR — the orphaned legacy keys are NOT full-parity screens. Each legacy route HOST was swapped to render the SAME rework :ui screen as its Rework sibling: AboutScreenRoute.kt:11,203 imports/renders ui.about.AboutScreen (identical to AboutReworkScreenRoute.kt:11,144); StatisticsScreenRoute.kt:8,130 renders ui.statistics.StatisticsScreen (= StatisticsReworkScreenRoute:8,111); likewise LanguageScreenRoute→ui.language.LanguageScreen, DownloadsScreenRoute→ui.downloads.DownloadsScreen, ComplaintScreenRoute→ui.complaint.ComplaintScreen, WhatsNewScreenRoute→ui.whatsnew.WhatsNewScreen, AdminComplaintScreenRoute→ui.complaint.admin.AdminComplaintScreen — all backed by the same rework :presentation ViewModels. There is exactly ONE composable per feature in :ui (e.g. only one fun AboutScreen at ui/.../about/AboutScreen.kt:197) and NO legacy full-parity composables remain in composeApp (find for features/about, features/language, features/whatsnew returned nothing). The DI/repo KDocs corroborate: StatisticsReworkModule/ComplaintReworkModule/DownloadsReworkModule etc. state the legacy keys were 're-pointed' so 'both now converge on' the rework screen. Therefore the claimed 'user-visible feature regression versus native — because Settings routes to reduced screens while full-parity legacy keys exist (dead)' is false: navigating to either the legacy key or the Rework key lands the user on the IDENTICAL reduced rework screen. The reduced-surface-vs-NATIVE regression (Screen.kt KDocs at 623-629 About, 757-763 Language, 808-816 Complaint) is real but exists regardless of KMP route choice and is not caused by Settings picking Rework routes; the legacy keys preserve no extra parity. Accurate parts: Settings→Rework mapping, legacy keys orphaned/dead. Wrong parts: 'full-parity legacy keys' and the impact framing.

**🟡 [Medium] Bottom nav — Home tab double-tap (scroll-to-top) — Home-tab reselect handler is never registered in KMP, so double-tapping Home does nothing** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — NavGraphV2.kt:202-211 builds a HomeTabReselectedHandler that scrolls listState/gridState to item 0 and assigns it to NavigationHandlerHolder.homeReselectHandler; also re-registered in HomeRoute.kt:131-134 via LaunchedEffect. BottomNavigationBar.kt:61-63 invokes it when Home is reselected.
- **KMP:** No — BottomNavigationBar.kt:134-136 still calls NavigationHandlerHolder.homeReselectHandler?.onHomeTabReselected(), but nothing in the KMP tree ever assigns homeReselectHandler. App.kt Home block (440-446) and HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt never set it (App.kt:119 explicitly defers the HomeTabReselectedHandler plumbing). The `?.` makes the call a silent no-op.
- **Explanation:** In native, tapping the already-selected Home tab scrolls the home feed (both the LazyList and LazyGrid) back to the top — a standard, discoverable manga-app affordance. In KMP the holder remains null forever, so the gesture is inert. The interface, holder singleton, and the BottomNavigationBar invocation were ported, but the registration site (the only place that gives the feature meaning) was dropped during the Home rework swap.
- **Suggested fix:** In HomeReworkScreenRoute (or the App.kt Screen.Home composable), register a HomeTabReselectedHandler into NavigationHandlerHolder.homeReselectHandler that dispatches a HomeIntent (e.g. OnScrollToTop) so the rework HomeScreen's LazyGridState/LazyListState animates/scrolls to index 0, mirroring NavGraphV2.kt:202-211. Clear it on dispose to avoid a stale handler.

**🟡 [Medium] History/Updates → manga 'deleted from library' guard — Native guards cover/row taps with an existence check + Toast; KMP navigates unconditionally** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — History onHistoryImgClick (NavGraphV2.kt:322-349) and onHistoryItemClick (353-387), plus the Updates path, call sharedChaptersVm.isMangaExists(mangaId); if the manga no longer exists in the library they show Toast 'THis Manga Is Deleted from the Libarary' and abort navigation, otherwise navigate to LibraryMangaDetails / ChapterImagesFragment.
- **KMP:** No — HistoryScreenRoute.kt:175-200 and UpdatesScreenRoute.kt:110-135 navigate directly to Screen.MangaDetails / Screen.ChapterImagesFragment with no existence check and no Toast.
- **Explanation:** In native, tapping a history/updates entry whose manga was deleted from the library is blocked with an explanatory Toast (for entries that had a mangaId != 0). KMP removes this guard entirely, so the user is navigated into a details/reader screen for a manga record that may no longer exist locally, potentially surfacing an empty/error state instead of the clear 'deleted from library' message.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the isMangaExists(mangaId)/Toast guard into the rework History/Updates flow (in the VM or route adapter): when a row has a non-zero mangaId and the manga is no longer in the library, surface the equivalent localized 'manga deleted from library' message (Res.string) instead of navigating.

**🟡 [Medium] MangaDetails → Download click back-stack behaviour — Native pops to the nav-graph root and lands on the Library tab; KMP navigates forward to the rework Downloads screen** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — NavGraphV2.kt:459-464 onDownloadClick navigates to Screen.Library.route with popUpTo(navController.graph.id){inclusive=false} + launchSingleTop=true, i.e. it clears the details stack and returns to the Library tab.
- **KMP:** No (changed) — MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute.kt:131 onNavigateToDownloads = navController.safeNavigate(Screen.DownloadsRework); it pushes the rework Downloads screen onto the stack instead of popping back to Library. The KDoc (App.kt:494, MangaDetailsReworkScreenRoute §253/ADR-3) calls this an 'intentional UX change'.
- **Explanation:** In native, after enqueuing a download from the details screen the user is taken back to the Library tab (stack cleared to root), reflecting that downloads surface there. In KMP, tapping the download action opens a dedicated Downloads screen pushed on top of details — a different destination and a different back-stack shape (back returns to details rather than to Library). This is a deliberate divergence per the KMP docs but is still a navigation-flow parity difference to record.
- **Suggested fix:** If parity with native is desired, route the details download action to the Library tab via popUpTo(graph root){inclusive=false}+launchSingleTop, or confirm the DownloadsRework destination is the intended new UX and update product expectations accordingly.

**🟡 [Medium] Home/Library system-back handling (BackHandler) — Native installs explicit BackHandler blocks on Home and Library; KMP drops them** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — NavGraphV2.kt Home block (190-193) installs BackHandler(enabled = previousBackStackEntry != null){ safePopBackStack() }; Library block (276-278) installs BackHandler(enabled = false){} to prevent popping past the start destination. SearchScreen also uses BackHandler in HomeRoute.kt:289-293 to close search on back.
- **KMP:** No — App.kt:112-114 explicitly states the BackHandler calls are 'intentionally dropped' because there is no commonMain BackHandler shim, relying on default Compose Navigation pop behaviour. HomeReworkScreenRoute.kt:28-30 notes the 'system-back-while-searching intercept is deferred'.
- **Explanation:** On native, back from the Home search overlay closes the search (it does not pop the Home destination), and Home routes its back through safePopBackStack (focus-clearing + library fallback). In KMP commonMain there is no BackHandler, so (a) Android system back while the Search overlay is open will pop the Home destination / exit instead of merely closing search, and (b) Home back no longer goes through the safe focus-clearing pop. This is a real interaction regression specifically on Android.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a commonMain BackHandler expect/actual (Android delegates to androidx.activity.compose.BackHandler) and wire it in HomeReworkScreenRoute so back closes the search overlay when isSearching, mirroring native HomeRoute.kt:289-293; optionally route Home back through safePopBackStack.

**🟡 [Medium] safePopBackStack / safeNavigate — focus clearing on Android — KMP commonMain safePopBackStack/safeNavigate drop the Android focus-clearing that native used to prevent FocusFinder crashes** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — safePopBackStack.kt:24-35 and safeNavigate (138-149) accept clearFocus=true and call clearAllFocus(context) (decorView.clearFocus()) before popping/navigating, explicitly to prevent NullPointerException in FocusFinder when a TextField has focus during navigation (documented at safePopBackStack.kt:11-16).
- **KMP:** Partial — composeApp safePopBackStack.kt has the same try/catch fallback-to-Library structure but no clearFocus parameter and no clearAllFocus call (it cannot — Activity/decorView are Android-only and the file is commonMain). safeNavigate (65-81) likewise has no focus clearing.
- **Explanation:** Native deliberately clears view focus before navigation to avoid a known FocusFinder NPE crash class when navigating away from a screen with a focused TextField (e.g. the search field). KMP's commonMain port omits this entirely, so on Android the crash class native guarded against can reappear during rapid navigation away from focused text inputs. The exception-swallowing fallback remains, but the proactive focus clear does not.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a platform hook (expect/actual) invoked by safeNavigate/safePopBackStack that on Android clears window/decorView focus before navigating, restoring the native FocusFinder-crash guard; no-op on iOS/Desktop.

**⚪ [Low] MainActivity testing-mode (ApiTestScreen) branch — Native swaps the entire UI to ApiTestScreen when Admin.testingMode is on; KMP MainScreen has no such branch** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.kt:344-420: inside YamiMangaTheme, if (Admin.testingMode) it renders ApiTestScreen(api, context, scope) instead of MainScreen(); else MainScreen(). This entirely replaces the nav graph with an admin API-test surface.
- **KMP:** No — App.kt MainScreen()/AppNavHost have no Admin.testingMode branch; the NavHost is always shown. (Admin.isAdmin is still consulted in SettingsRoute.kt:152 for the complaint admin gate, but the testing-mode UI swap is absent.)
- **Explanation:** This is an admin/debug-only top-level UI swap, not a normal user flow, so user-facing impact is minimal, but it is a navigation-entry divergence: the native app can short-circuit the whole nav graph to an API-test screen for admins, and KMP cannot. Worth recording for completeness of the navigation entry surface.
- **Suggested fix:** If admin API testing is still needed on KMP, add an equivalent top-level branch in App.MainScreen gated on Admin.testingMode that renders the (ported) ApiTestScreen; otherwise explicitly confirm the feature was intentionally dropped.

**⚪ [Low] Onboarding chain / RepoSettings start branch — Native start-destination onboarding goes Welcome→Theme→Sources→...; native does NOT include RepoSettings as a separate start branch but KMP doc claims a RepoSettings step — minor flow-doc divergence, and both share the same first_launch flip responsibility** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — NavGraphV2.kt:160 rootStart = if (firstLaunch) Screen.Welcome else Screen.Library; onboarding hosts Welcome/Theme/Sources/RepoSettings are all wired (168-187, 535-542). The first_launch flag is read via PrefsDelegate(key='first_launch').
- **KMP:** Yes — App.kt:401-402 firstLaunch = prefs.getBoolean('first_launch', true); rootStart = if (firstLaunch) Screen.Welcome else Screen.Library — identical key and identical branch. Welcome/Theme/Sources/RepoSettings composables are all present (App.kt:409-431, 543-549).
- **Explanation:** The start-destination logic and the first_launch SharedPrefs key are byte-for-byte identical, so this dimension is at parity. The only nuance is documentation: App.kt's KDoc describes the chain as Welcome→Theme→Sources→RepoSettings→Library and notes the flag is flipped in RepoSettingsScreenRoute.onFinish, which matches native's wiring. No functional divergence found here; recorded as Low to document that the start/onboarding entry was verified at parity.
- **Suggested fix:** No change required for the start-destination logic. Optionally verify RepoSettingsScreenRoute.onFinish actually flips first_launch in KMP (the App.kt KDoc asserts it) so the onboarding chain terminates correctly.

**⚪ [Low] Deep links / notification & FCM navigation — Neither app defines URI deep links; native notifications carry no navigation PendingIntent — so this dimension is at parity (nothing to port)** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** No deep links — AndroidManifest.xml MainActivity (33-43) declares only MAIN/LAUNCHER, no <data scheme>/custom intent-filter; notification helpers (ChapterNotificationHelper.kt, NotificationHelper.kt) and MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt contain no PendingIntent/Intent-into-route wiring (grep returned no matches). In-app, notification taps are handled inside the Updates screen via onNotificationClick callbacks (NavGraphV2.kt:399-427), not via system deep links.
- **KMP:** N/A — KMP has no NavHost deepLinks either (none in App.kt), consistent with native. Updates row taps are handled in-app by UpdatesScreenRoute callbacks (UpdatesScreenRoute.kt:110-135).
- **Explanation:** Confirmed via manifest + notification-helper inspection that the native app does not use system-level deep links and notifications do not navigate into specific routes from outside the app. Therefore the absence of deep-link handling in KMP is not a regression — it matches native. Recorded explicitly so the audit shows the deep-link dimension was investigated and found at parity.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed. If future requirements add notification-tap-to-chapter deep linking, both apps would need it added equally.

**⚪ [Low] Route set — rework debug routes present only in KMP — KMP graph contains ~13 extra *Rework debug routes not present in native** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** No — native NavGraphV2.kt has exactly the canonical route set (Welcome, Theme, Sources, Home, Library, History, Updates, Setting, Statistics, WhatsNewScreen, RepoSettings, LanguageScreen, DownloadsScreen, AboutScreen, MangaDetails, LibraryMangaDetails, ChapterImagesFragment, WebView, Complaint, ComplaintAdmin).
- **KMP:** Yes (additional) — Screen.kt/App.kt add MangaDetailsRework, ChapterImagesRework, StatisticsRework, HistoryRework, UpdatesRework, SourcesRework, ThemeRework, AboutRework, WhatsNewRework, LanguageRework, ComplaintRework, ComplaintAdminRework, DownloadsRework, SettingsRework (App.kt:581-889). Several are described in KDoc as 'debug-reachable, not surfaced in any user-facing entry'.
- **Explanation:** These extra routes are migration scaffolding and most are not user-reachable, so they do not directly change the user-facing flow. They are noted because (a) some ARE now the actual Settings targets (see the Settings-hub finding) and (b) the duplicated route surface plus the orphaned legacy keys increases the risk of a wrong-route binding regression and bloats the graph relative to native.
- **Suggested fix:** Once each rework screen reaches parity and becomes the user-facing target, retire the corresponding legacy route key (as already done for LibraryMangaDetails) so the KMP route set converges back toward the native canonical set and dead routes are removed.

### Localization & RTL  `localization-rtl`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 11 (🔴1 🟠4 🟡1 ⚪5)

> Native ships a fully-translated app across 11 locales (en, ar, de, es, fr, in, it, ja, pt, ru, tr) with 514 strings + 7 plurals each, locale-aware date formatting (DateTimeFormatter MMM d, yyyy), runtime locale switching via AppCompatDelegate, AutoMirrored RTL icons, and a localized Arabic app_name. The KMP migration produced TWO separate compose-resource packages: :composeApp holds a byte-for-byte perfect mirror of native (all 11 locales, 0 missing keys, 0 value diffs, +3 new webview keys), but it is largely dead code; and :ui holds the catalog the 19 live screens actually consume (verified via composeApp navigation routes importing ui.* screens). The critical regression is that :ui ships ONLY values/ and values-ar/ — the 9 locales de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr are entirely absent from the active package, so every non-English/non-Arabic user sees the whole app in English despite the translations existing (unreachably) in :composeApp. Plurals are a second structural regression: :ui has zero <plurals>, and the live relative-time and item-count formatters were re-implemented with singular-only strings (days_ago=\"%1$d days ago\", library_items_count=\"%1$d items\"), losing English n=1 correctness and all of Arabic's six plural forms; the correctly-pluralized composeApp Date.kt is orphaned. Additional gaps: 80 net-new :ui keys lack Arabic, month names are hardcoded English abbreviations (no localization), app_name is not localized to Arabic, and 11 Arabic values in :ui diverge from the native source of truth. Faithfully preserved: the Android locale-switch mechanism, the 11-language picker list, and RTL auto-mirrored icons with supportsRtl enabled.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Localization & RTL</summary>

**🔴 [Critical] All localized screens (19 live ui-module screens: Home/Library/Details/Reader/Settings/History/Updates/Statistics/Downloads/Sources/Language/About/Complaint/Theme/Welcome/WhatsNew/Search/etc.) — 9 of 11 locales (de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr) are completely missing from the active :ui resource catalog** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - full translations for all 11 locales in native-app/app/src/main/res/values{,-ar,-de,-es,-fr,-in,-it,-ja,-pt,-ru,-tr}/strings.xml, each 514 strings + 7 plurals
- **KMP:** Partial - the live screens import me.manga.kira.ui.generated.resources.Res (26 files; 427 distinct keys), but ui/src/commonMain/composeResources only contains values/ and values-ar/ (verified: `ls` shows only those two dirs). No values-de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr exist in :ui.
- **Explanation:** The 19 user-facing screens are all wired in composeApp navigation routes importing ui.* screens (e.g. StatisticsReworkScreenRoute imports me.manga.kira.ui.statistics.StatisticsScreen). Those screens render strings via the :ui generated Res package. Compose Multiplatform resolves a string against the resource package that owns the Res symbol, and :ui ships ONLY English (values) + Arabic (values-ar). The full 11-locale catalog DOES exist but only in a SEPARATE package, :composeApp (composeApp/src/commonMain/composeResources/values-de etc., a byte-perfect mirror of native - verified 0 missing keys / 0 value diffs across all 10 non-default locales), which the :ui screens never import. Net effect: a German/Spanish/French/Indonesian/Italian/Japanese/Portuguese/Russian/Turkish user sees the entire app in English. 157 keys actually rendered by :ui have German translations sitting unreachable in :composeApp's values-de. This is the single largest localization regression: native ships a fully-translated app in 11 languages; KMP effectively ships 2 (en + partial ar).
- **Suggested fix:** Move/duplicate the per-locale catalogs (values-de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr) into ui/src/commonMain/composeResources so the :ui Res package that the live screens consume resolves them, OR consolidate all string resources into a single shared compose-resources package that every screen imports. Do not rely on the :composeApp catalog - it is not reachable from the :ui render path.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). CONFIRMED via per-module Compose-Resources package isolation. NATIVE (source of truth): 11 locale dirs exist at native-app/app/src/main/res/values{,-ar,-de,-es,-fr,-in,-it,-ja,-pt,-ru,-tr}/strings.xml; values/strings.xml = 514 strings + 7 plurals; values-de = 514 strings with REAL German (e.g. <string name="statistics">Statistiken</string>, "Suchen"); values-ja real Japanese ("検索"). KMP :ui catalog ships ONLY two locales: ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/ contains exactly values/ and values-ar/ (values-de = "No such file or directory" confirmed); no de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr. The 17 live navigated screens live in :ui and render via stringResource(Res.string.X) bound to Res = me.manga.kira.ui.generated.resources.Res (ui/build.gradle.kts:121 packageOfResClass="me.manga.kira.ui.generated.resources"); e.g. StatisticsScreen.kt:34 imports that Res and :165 calls stringResource(Res.string.statistics). composeApp/App.kt imports the live ui.* screens (AboutScreen..WhatsNewScreen, 17 distinct) into navigation routes. The full 11-locale catalog exists but ONLY in a SEPARATE module/package: composeApp/src/commonMain/composeResources/values-de etc. under packageOfResClass="me.manga.kira.composeapp.generated.resources" (composeApp/build.gradle.kts:140). The two Res classes are isolated — 0 files in :composeApp import ui.generated.resources and 0 in :ui import composeapp.generated.resources; each module has its own compose.resources{} block, and CMP resolves a string against the Res class that owns the symbol, so :ui can only resolve en+ar. Locale switching IS wired (platform/.../AndroidLocaleSwitcher.kt -> AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales), so a German user can select German but :ui falls back to English (values/). Intersection math reproduced: :ui references 427 distinct generated.resources keys (425 Res.string.* call sites); 157 of those keys have German translations sitting unreachable in composeApp/values-de; 140 of those are defined in :ui's own English catalog (render English-only). Net effect (de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr users see all :ui screens in English) is real. Minor wording nit: the "427 distinct keys" is the count of keys REFERENCED/imported by :ui code, not the size of :ui's catalog (:ui values/strings.xml defines 328 strings) — does not affect the conclusion.

**🟠 [High] Library card item count / chapter counts — Native items_count plural replaced by a singular-only string library_items_count = "%1$d items"** _(Localization/RTL)_

Native had no equivalent (these are new), but since they are user-facing in the shipped Arabic build, they constitute an Arabic-localization gap relative to the app's bilingual baseline.

CORE FINDING CONFIRMED: Extracting all string keys, ui/values (English) defines 446 keys; ui/values-ar defines 357; 89 EN keys have no ui-ar value. Of those, exactly 80 are ALSO absent from composeApp/values-ar -> matching the claimed "80 keys missing ar in both" exactly. The other 9 DO have Arabic in composeApp/values-ar. MECHANISM CONFIRMED (why missing ui-ar matters): the live screens import the :ui module's own generated Res, e.g. ui/.../home/HomeScreen.kt:67 `import me.manga.kira.ui.generated.resources.Res`; same in whatsnew/WhatsNewScreen.kt:81, library/LibraryScreen.kt:69, settings/SettingsScreen.kt:75, history/HistoryScreen.kt:55, details/DetailsScreen.kt:93. Compose Multiplatform generates a per-module Res; Arabic for a :ui string resolves ONLY from ui/values-ar, so composeApp/values-ar cannot supply a fallback. Thus the 80 ui-ar-missing keys render English for Arabic users. KEYS ARE LIVE AND RENDERED (sample, all via Res.string.X): - WhatsNewScreen.kt:466/470/514 -> np_get_started, np_next, np_close (onboarding nav buttons); screen is wired in composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt + navigation/routes/WhatsNewScreenRoute.kt + App.kt. - HomeScreen.kt:285/287/307 -> home_status_maintenance_title/body, home_status_adult_title (status banners). - LibraryScreen.kt:426 -> library_single_delete_title. - DetailsScreen.kt:1115 -> details_mark_read. - SettingsScreen.kt:293/453 -> feedback_submitted, follow_system_theme_desc. - HistoryScreen.kt:380 -> month_abbrev_jan. Your feedback was submitted.", np_next="Next"). MISCHARACTERIZATION 1 -- "none exist in native" is overstated. **🟠 [High] Plurals support in the live resource module — The active :ui resource catalog contains zero <plurals>** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - 7 plurals in every native locale (items_count, time_minutes/hours/days/weeks/months/years_ago), with full Arabic six-form coverage (zero/one/two/few/many/other)
- **KMP:** No plurals in :ui (0 in values and values-ar). 7 plurals exist only in :composeApp (mirroring native), but :composeApp's pluralStringResource consumer toRelativeString is dead code; live :ui screens use singular strings instead.
- **Explanation:** Because the live screens render from :ui, and :ui has no plurals at all, the app has effectively lost runtime plural resolution. Every count-bearing string (item counts, all relative-time strings) now uses a single fixed form, which is grammatically wrong in English for n=1 in some paths and broadly wrong in Arabic where plural category depends on the number. This is the structural root cause behind the items_count and time-ago findings.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the 7 <plurals> to ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/values and values-ar (plus all locales) and switch the count/time formatters in :ui to pluralStringResource. Remove or rewire the orphaned composeApp Date.kt.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). STRUCTURAL CLAIM CONFIRMED. Native has 7 <plurals> in all 11 locales: native-app/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:46 (items_count), :713,718,723,728,733,738 (time_minutes/hours/days/weeks/months/years_ago); grep -c shows exactly 7 in every values*/strings.xml. Arabic six-form coverage is full: native values-ar/strings.xml shows items_count (lines ~34-41) and each time_*_ago (713-770) with zero/one/two/few/many/other items, e.g. time_minutes_ago has قبل 0 دقيقة / قبل دقيقة واحدة / قبل دقيقتين / قبل %d دقائق / قبل %d دقيقة / قبل %d دقيقة. :composeApp mirrors all 7 plurals in all locales with the same six Arabic forms (composeApp/.../values-ar/strings.xml:34-41, 717-770). :ui has ZERO plurals: of 21 XML files under ui/src/commonMain/composeResources, grep -rl "<plurals" returns 0 files (both values and values-ar). DEAD-CODE CLAIM CONFIRMED. The sole pluralStringResource consumer in the KMP tree is composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/core/util/date/Date.kt — timeAgo() (lines 65-99) calls pluralStringResource(Res.plurals.time_minutes_ago,…) etc. (lines 75,79,84,88,92,96). It is never invoked: grep for "timeAgo()" and ".toRelativeString(" outside Date.kt itself returns zero hits across :ui, :presentation, :domain, :data, :shared, and :composeApp. :ui/:presentation reference zero "composeapp.generated" resource IDs, so the helper is unreachable from live screens. LIVE-SCREENS-USE-SINGULAR CLAIM CONFIRMED. Live relative-time rendering is an inline helper in ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt:798-818 (formatRelativeTime) using singular stringResource(Res.string.minutes_ago/hours_ago/days_ago/weeks_ago/months_ago/years_ago, n) — lines 810-816. Its own KDoc (LibraryScreen.kt:751-758) states it deliberately does NOT route through the :composeApp timeAgo() plural helper ("pulling it into :ui would be a cross-layer leak"). DetailsScreen.kt:817 and HistoryScreen.kt:350,366 likewise use singular days_ago. The :ui singular strings carry no plural categories: ui values/strings.xml:310 minutes_ago=%1$d minutes ago, :89 days_ago=%1$d days ago; Arabic ui values-ar/strings.xml:387 منذ %1$d دقائق, :82 منذ %1$d أيام (hardcoded to one plural form for all n). Item count: native uses pluralStringResource(R.plurals.items_count,…) at LibraryItems.kt:156-159; :ui uses singular stringResource(Res.string.library_items_count, count) at LibraryScreen.kt:550 (LibraryItemCountCaption), where library_items_count=%1$d items (ui values/strings_np_p2_library.xml:14) and is ABSENT from values-ar entirely (grep returns nothing), so Arabic falls back to English — even worse than claimed. Native time-ago consumer for parity: native Date.kt:32-53 uses getQuantityString(R.plurals.time_*_ago,…).

**🟡 [Medium] Date display (MMM d, yyyy) in Details/History/Updates/Statistics — Native locale-aware month names replaced by hardcoded English month abbreviations** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - native core/util/date/Date.kt:17 formats via DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern("MMM d, yyyy"), which yields locale-localized month names (Arabic month names under ar, German under de, etc.)
- **KMP:** Partial - 12 hardcoded strings month_abbrev_jan..dec (ui/values/strings_np_p2_hist_upd_stats.xml:17+, e.g. "Jan"), imported in DetailsScreen/HistoryScreen/UpdatesScreen. They have NO Arabic translation (0 in any values-ar) and exist in NO other locale.
- **Explanation:** Native rendered month names localized per active locale via java.time. KMP hardcoded English 3-letter abbreviations as string resources that exist only in English. Result: dates display "Jan/Feb/..." in English for every locale including Arabic, instead of localized month names. This is a date-localization regression affecting all non-English users.
- **Suggested fix:** Either provide month_abbrev_* translations for all 11 locales (ar/de/es/fr/in/it/ja/pt/ru/tr), or use a locale-aware date formatter (kotlinx-datetime + locale month names) instead of hardcoded English abbreviation strings.

- **KMP:** No - app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml has only app_name="Yami Manga"; there is no app/src/main/res/values-ar (verified: app res dirs are values + mipmaps only). The file's own comment calls itself a stub: 'Phase 10 will reconcile resources.'

Only Arabic localized the name in native (other locales kept English), so the gap is Arabic-specific.

**⚪ [Low] Language picker display names (endonyms) — Native derives endonyms at runtime via Locale.getDisplayLanguage; KMP hardcodes a curated table** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - LanguageScreenRoute.kt:30 builds LanguageOption(tag, Locale.forLanguageTag(tag).getDisplayLanguage(locale)) from R.array.supported_languages (en,ar,de,es,fr,in,it,ja,pt,ru,tr)
- **KMP:** Partial - data/repository/LanguageRepositoryImpl.kt:153-164 hardcodes SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES with displayName endonyms (English, العربية, Deutsch, Español, Français, Bahasa Indonesia, Italiano, 日本語, Português, Русский, Türkçe). Same 11 codes (composeApp/values/arrays.xml supported_languages matches native).
- **Explanation:** The code list and order match exactly (11 languages). The endonyms are equivalent, but native's java.util.Locale.getDisplayLanguage can produce platform/ICU-specific spellings that may differ subtly per device/Android version (e.g. for tag 'in' Java maps to Indonesian and may yield 'Indonesia' rather than the hardcoded 'Bahasa Indonesia'; 'ja' may render '日本語' identically). Since KMP common code cannot use java.util.Locale, the curated table is a reasonable port, but it is a static divergence from native's runtime-resolved names and could drift from device locale data.
- **Suggested fix:** Accept the curated table (necessary in commonMain) but verify each endonym matches what native's getDisplayLanguage produces on a reference device, especially for 'in' (Indonesian) where Java's display name may differ from 'Bahasa Indonesia'.

**⚪ [Low] Per-app locale switching mechanism — None functionally on Android; iOS/Desktop are intentional no-ops** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - LanguageViewModel.updateLocale uses AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales(LocaleListCompat.forLanguageTags(code)) after settingsRepo.setLanguage(code)
- **KMP:** Yes (Android) - platform/androidMain AndroidLocaleSwitcher.applyApplicationLocale uses the same AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales(LocaleListCompat.forLanguageTags(...)); persisted via DataStoreHelper. iOS (IosLocaleSwitcher) and Desktop (DesktopLocaleSwitcher) are documented no-ops (locale applied on next launch).
- **Explanation:** The runtime locale-switch is faithfully ported on Android (the only platform native targeted). iOS/Desktop no-ops are reasonable (those platforms require process restart for locale changes) and documented, but they mean a mid-session language change on iOS/Desktop will not take effect until relaunch - a behavioral difference from Android's immediate activity recreation. This is a platform constraint, not a defect, but worth noting for cross-platform UX parity.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed for Android. For iOS/Desktop, consider surfacing a 'restart required' hint to the user after selecting a language, since the switch is deferred to next launch unlike Android.

- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed - RTL icon mirroring matches native. (Optional: verify Compose Multiplatform on Android propagates the per-app Arabic locale to LayoutDirection.Rtl in composition the same way native did, since both rely on framework default rather than an explicit provider.)

### Responsiveness / Screen Sizes  `responsiveness-screensizes`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 9 (🔴0 🟠1 🟡4 ⚪4)

> The native Android app is phone-first and handles responsiveness entirely at runtime in Compose (no layout-*/values-sw*/values-land resource variants exist — verified the only res/layout files are three native-ad XMLs). Its responsive surfaces are: a user-selectable Library "items per row" Slider (0=auto Adaptive, 1-8 Fixed columns), a WhatsNew screen that branches on isTablet (screenWidthDp>=600) and isLandscape to scale media size, typography, padding and card-height fraction, an adaptive SocialMediaRow (BoxWithConstraints), per-card BoxWithConstraints button scaling in MangaCard, and reader page sizing driven by LocalConfiguration.screenWidthDp/screenHeightDp. The KMP app reaches high parity on the Home/Search grids (both Adaptive(minSize=160.dp)) and the SocialMediaRow (byte-identical 36..56dp / 18..28dp math), but diverges materially on the Library grid (replaced the column-count Slider with a 3-value GridDensity enum mapping to 96/120/160dp — no fixed-column option, different auto cell size) and the WhatsNew screen (fixed 220.dp media and fixed typography with NO tablet/landscape adaptation). KMP additionally ships Desktop (1280x800 resizable window) and iOS/iPad hosts the native app never targeted, yet the shared App root applies no max-content-width cap and there is zero WindowSizeClass / isTablet / orientation logic anywhere in :ui or :composeApp commonMain — so wide windows stretch single-column screens edge-to-edge. The reader page sizing was reworked to container-relative (BoxWithConstraints.maxHeight + fillMaxWidth) which is arguably more correct than native's device-screen-relative math in multi-window/large-window contexts.

**🟠 [High] Library grid — user-controlled column count — Native exposes a 0-8 'items per row' Slider (0=auto Adaptive, 1-8 Fixed columns); KMP replaced it with a 3-value density enum** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryViewModel.kt:65 `itemsPerRow: Int = 2`, persisted via KEY_ITEMS_PER_ROW (LibraryViewModel.kt:123,159,358-363); DisplayOptionsSection.kt:41-46 Slider valueRange 0f..8f, steps 7 (positions 0..8); LibraryItems.kt:184-205 `columns = if (itemsPerRow > 0) GridCells.Fixed(itemsPerRow) else GridCells.Adaptive(minSizeDp)` with `minSizeDp = if (itemsPerRow>0) (screenWidthDp/itemsPerRow).dp else 140.dp`.
- **KMP:** Partial — LibraryScreen.kt:844-845 `columns = GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = gridDensity.minSize())`; GridDensity.minSize() (LibraryScreen.kt:655-659) maps COMPACT=96.dp / COMFORTABLE=120.dp / SPACIOUS=160.dp. LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:154-167 offers only the 3 density radio options. LibraryState.kt:111 `gridDensity: GridDensity = GridDensity.COMFORTABLE`. No fixed-column / slider path exists.
- **Explanation:** Native lets the user pick an EXACT column count (1-8) via a slider, with 0 meaning auto (Adaptive at 140.dp). This is a responsiveness/personalization feature: a tablet/landscape user could force 6-8 columns, a phone user could force 1-2. KMP collapses this to three coarse buckets that only ever use GridCells.Adaptive — the user can no longer pin a fixed column count, and the auto cell size differs (native auto fallback = 140.dp; KMP default COMFORTABLE = 120.dp, so the same width yields more columns by default than native's auto). On large/desktop windows the loss of an explicit column control is most visible.
- **Suggested fix:** Restore a column-count control: add an Int `itemsPerRow` (0=auto) to LibraryState persisted via a use case mirroring the native KEY_ITEMS_PER_ROW, render a Slider (0..8) in LibraryOptionsSheet's Display tab, and in LibraryGrid switch to `if (itemsPerRow>0) GridCells.Fixed(itemsPerRow) else GridCells.Adaptive(140.dp)` to match native semantics and the 140.dp auto cell. Keep GridDensity only if intentionally additive.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — the 0-8 itemsPerRow slider is LIVE-wired end-to-end: - LibraryViewModel.kt:65 `val itemsPerRow: Int = 2` (data-class field default). Persistence: KEY_ITEMS_PER_ROW = "library_items_per_row" (LibraryViewModel.kt:123); loaded at init via `itemsPerRow = prefs.getInt(KEY_ITEMS_PER_ROW, 0)` (LibraryViewModel.kt:159); written via `onItemsPerRowChange(count)` -> `prefs.putInt(KEY_ITEMS_PER_ROW, count)` (LibraryViewModel.kt:358-363). - DisplayOptionsSection.kt:41-46 renders `Slider(value=count.toFloat(), onValueChange={onCountChange(it.toInt())}, valueRange = 0f..8f, steps = 7)` -> 9 discrete positions 0..8; count==0 shows "auto" label (lines 47-57). - LibraryScreen.kt (native):227-318 the LIVE `CustomFilterBottomSheet(... pageContents=...)` passes `DisplayOptionsSection(count = itemsPerRow, onCountChange = viewModel::onItemsPerRowChange, ...)` at lines 266-269; `itemsPerRow` is destructured from `uiState` (line 86) and also fed to the grid at line 206 (`itemsPerRow = uiState.itemsPerRow`). - LibraryItems.kt:184-205 consumes it: `minSizeDp = if (itemsPerRow > 0) (screenWidthDp / itemsPerRow).dp else 140.dp`; `columns = if (itemsPerRow > 0) GridCells.Fixed(itemsPerRow) else GridCells.Adaptive(minSizeDp)` (in BOTH the VerticalGridFastScroller and inner LazyVerticalGrid). So 1-8 = exact Fixed columns, 0 = Adaptive(140.dp). KMP (rework) — replaced by a 3-value density enum; NO fixed-column path exists anywhere: - domain GridDensity.kt:73-77 `enum class GridDensity { COMPACT, COMFORTABLE, SPACIOUS }` (exactly 3 values). - presentation/LibraryState.kt:111 `val gridDensity: GridDensity = GridDensity.COMFORTABLE`. - ui/LibraryScreen.kt:655-659 `GridDensity.minSize()` maps COMPACT->96.dp / COMFORTABLE->120.dp / SPACIOUS->160.dp. - ui/LibraryScreen.kt:844-845 `LibraryGrid` does `columns = GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = gridDensity.minSize())` — Adaptive only, never Fixed. - ui/LibraryOptionsSheet.kt:154-167 (Display tab) offers ONLY the 3 density radio OptionRows via `GridDensity.entries.forEach`; no Slider import/usage; the only Slider import in the codebase is native DisplayOptionsSection.kt. - Codebase-wide grep over :ui/:presentation/:domain/:shared/:data: ZERO occurrences of `GridCells.Fixed`, `itemsPerRow`, `items_per_row`, or `ITEMS_PER_ROW`. Every grid (Library, Home, Search) uses `GridCells.Adaptive`. Cell-size delta confirmed: native auto fallback = 140.dp (LibraryItems.kt:185) vs KMP default COMFORTABLE = 120.dp (LibraryScreen.kt:657) — same content width yields ~one extra column by default in KMP. Two minor citation imprecisions in the claim (do NOT change the verdict): (1) The claim's "itemsPerRow default = 2" is the data-class field default; the actual loaded default for a fresh user is 0/auto (prefs.getInt(..., 0) at LibraryViewModel.kt:159), so native starts in Adaptive(140.dp), not 2-Fixed. (2) The slider's own inline comment (DisplayOptionsSection.kt:45) stale-claims "5 positions 0..4", but the executable `valueRange 0f..8f, steps=7` gives 9 positions 0..8 — the claim's 0-8 description is correct.

**🟡 [Medium] Library grid — auto/default cell minSize — Native auto (itemsPerRow=0) uses Adaptive minSize 140.dp; KMP default (COMFORTABLE) uses 120.dp** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — LibraryItems.kt:185 `else 140.dp` feeds GridCells.Adaptive when itemsPerRow==0 (the default-ish auto path).
- **KMP:** Yes — LibraryScreen.kt:657 `GridDensity.COMFORTABLE -> 120.dp` is the default (LibraryState.kt:111).
- **Explanation:** Even ignoring the slider, the default adaptive cell width differs: native 140.dp vs KMP 120.dp. On a ~360.dp content phone width native auto yields ~2 columns (360/140≈2.5→2) while KMP COMFORTABLE yields ~3 (360/120=3). The library renders denser by default in KMP than in native, a visible layout-density regression across all screen sizes.
- **Suggested fix:** Set the default adaptive cell minSize to 140.dp (or set COMFORTABLE=140.dp) to match native's auto fallback so the default column count is identical on the same width.

**🟡 [Medium] What's New screen — tablet/landscape responsiveness — Native scales WhatsNew media size, typography, padding and card height by isTablet/isLandscape; KMP uses fixed values with no orientation/size adaptation** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — WhatsNewScreen.kt:37-51 computes `isLandscape = screenWidthDp>screenHeightDp`, `isTablet = screenWidthDp>=600`, `horizontalPadding = if(isTablet) 32.dp else 16.dp`, `cardPadding = isTablet→32 / isLandscape→16 / else 24`. FeatureCard.kt:38-45 `mediaSize = isTablet&&isLandscape→300 / isTablet→280 / isLandscape→180 / else 220`, `maxCardHeight = if(isLandscape) 0.85f else 0.75f`; FeatureCard.kt:89-104 title fontSize 32sp(tablet)/26sp, body 18sp(tablet)/15sp.
- **KMP:** Partial — WhatsNewScreen.kt:621 `MEDIA_SIZE = 220.dp` (fixed); VideoPoster height = MEDIA_SIZE*0.75f (fixed); FeatureCard uses titleMedium / bodyMedium (fixed typography, WhatsNewScreen.kt:598-614); FeaturePager pads with spacing.lg (16.dp) regardless of size. No isTablet/isLandscape/screenWidthDp logic anywhere in the file.
- **Explanation:** On a tablet or landscape phone the native WhatsNew media grows to 280-300.dp and text to 32/18sp with 32.dp padding, giving a proportionate large-screen presentation. KMP renders the same fixed 220.dp media and Material titleMedium/bodyMedium at every size — on a wide desktop/iPad window the card content looks small and the surrounding gradient dominates. This is a direct regression of native's adaptive WhatsNew layout, now also visible on the new Desktop/iOS targets KMP added.
- **Suggested fix:** Introduce a size-class helper (e.g. via BoxWithConstraints maxWidth or material3 WindowSizeClass) in WhatsNewScreen and thread isTablet/isLandscape into FeatureCard to scale MEDIA_SIZE (220/180/280/300), typography (26/32sp title, 15/18sp body) and card padding/height fraction (0.75/0.85), matching native FeatureCard.kt.

**🟡 [Medium] Global — no WindowSizeClass / tablet / orientation layout system — Native has runtime isTablet/isLandscape/screenWidthDp branches; KMP commonMain has ZERO WindowSizeClass, isTablet, isLandscape, or orientation-aware layout** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — LocalConfiguration.screenWidthDp/screenHeightDp used in WhatsNewScreen.kt:36-38, ReaderScreen.kt:127-129; isTablet/isLandscape branches in WhatsNew/FeatureCard.
- **KMP:** No — grep across /ui/src/commonMain and /composeApp/src/commonMain found no WindowSizeClass, calculateWindowSizeClass, currentWindowAdaptiveInfo, isTablet, isLandscape, screenWidthDp, or screenHeightDp. The only `Orientation` usages (VerticalFastScroller.kt:6,178; composeApp scroll component) are fast-scroller gesture axes, not responsive layout.
- **Explanation:** The migration dropped every device-size/orientation branch the native app used and introduced no replacement size-class abstraction. Combined with the new Desktop (1280x800) and iOS/iPad targets, screens that should reflow or cap width on large viewports simply scale their Adaptive grids while all single-column content (Settings, Details, History, About, dialogs, top bars) stretches full width. The native parity bar (WhatsNew tablet/landscape) is unmet and the new platforms have no large-window story.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a small commonMain size-class utility (BoxWithConstraints-based or material3-adaptive `currentWindowAdaptiveInfo`) and adopt it where native branched (WhatsNew) plus the new wide-window screens; document the intended phone/tablet/desktop breakpoints.

**🟡 [Medium] Desktop/large-window — content max-width cap — KMP root applies no max-content-width; on the 1280-wide desktop window and iPad, single-column screens stretch edge-to-edge** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** N/A — native is phone-only Android (no desktop/tablet-optimized layout); not a parity baseline, but the native UX is implicitly narrow-width.
- **KMP:** No cap — App.kt has no widthIn/sizeIn/BoxWithConstraints content container (only one fillMaxWidth at App.kt:366). Desktop Main.kt:131-138 opens a resizable 1280x800 Window with no min/max and no content-width constraint; iOS MainViewController.kt:19 hosts App() directly.
- **Explanation:** Because KMP now runs on Desktop (default 1280.dp wide, freely resizable wider) and iPad, and the App root never wraps content in a max-width container, list rows, detail panes, settings rows, top bars and dialogs span the full window width. Lines of text and form rows become uncomfortably long, and there is no two-pane / master-detail adaptation. This is a divergence introduced purely by the migration's new targets with no responsive accommodation.
- **Suggested fix:** Wrap the NavHost/content in a centered `Modifier.widthIn(max = ~840.dp)` container (or a WindowSizeClass-driven layout) so wide desktop/tablet windows show centered, readably-bounded content; consider a two-pane Library/Details layout on EXPANDED width.

**⚪ [Low] Reader — page/viewport sizing source — Native sizes reading-mode pages from device screenWidthDp/screenHeightDp; KMP uses container-relative BoxWithConstraints.maxHeight + fillMaxWidth** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReaderScreen.kt:127-129 `screenWidthPx = configuration.screenWidthDp...`, `screenHeightDb = configuration.screenHeightDp.dp`; reading modes compute `expectedHeight = screenWidthDp * aspectRatio` (WebToonReadingMode.kt:315-316, ContinuousVerticalReadingMode.kt:324-325, PagerImageItem.kt:163-165).
- **KMP:** Yes (reworked) — ReaderScreen.kt:505-518 `BoxWithConstraints { val screenHeightDb: Dp = maxHeight }`; pages use fillMaxWidth (ReaderScreen.kt:812,822,1354 etc.), i.e. the actual reader container size, not the device screen.
- **Explanation:** The KMP reader derives its height reservation and width from the container (maxHeight / fillMaxWidth) rather than the device screen. In fullscreen this is equivalent to native, but in split-screen / multi-window / resized-desktop contexts the KMP approach is actually MORE correct (it reflects the real viewport), whereas native's device-screen math would over-reserve height. Flagged as a benign divergence rather than a regression; verify webtoon images do not become excessively wide on very wide desktop windows where fillMaxWidth has no cap.
- **Suggested fix:** No change required for parity; optionally cap webtoon page width on very wide windows (e.g. `widthIn(max = 700.dp)` centered) so single-page-width manga doesn't stretch across a 1280+dp desktop window.

**⚪ [Low] Home & Search grids — adaptive columns — Both Home and Search grids use GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = 160.dp) on both sides** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:309 `GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = 160.dp)`; MangaSearchItems.kt:55 `GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = 160.dp)`.
- **KMP:** Yes — HomeScreen.kt:366 `GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = 160.dp)`; SearchScreen.kt:373 `GridCells.Adaptive(minSize = 160.dp)`.
- **Explanation:** Confirmed parity: both grids adapt column count to width identically (160.dp cells). Documented as a positive parity point — the migration preserved the Home/Search responsive grid behavior exactly, including matching code comments referencing the legacy 160.dp value. No action needed.
- **Suggested fix:** None — parity confirmed. Keep the 160.dp value aligned if either side is tuned later.

**⚪ [Low] About/WhatsNew social row — adaptive icon sizing — Native and KMP SocialMediaRow use byte-identical BoxWithConstraints adaptive math (button 36..56dp, icon 0.5f coerced 18..28dp)** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — SocialMediaRow.kt:45-51 `buttonSize = (availableWidth/6).coerceIn(36.dp,56.dp)`, `iconSize = (buttonSize*0.5f).coerceIn(18.dp,28.dp)`, 8.dp spacing, 6 buttons.
- **KMP:** Yes — YamiSocialMediaRow.kt:55-61 identical math (buttonCount=6, spacing=8.dp, buttonSize coerceIn 36..56.dp, iconSize buttonSize*0.5f coerceIn 18..28.dp).
- **Explanation:** Confirmed parity: the adaptive social-media button/icon sizing was ported byte-for-byte (KMP KDoc at YamiSocialMediaRow.kt:46-48 even documents 'byte-identical to the legacy math'). One subtle behavioral delta: native SocialMediaButton adds a press-scale spring animation (scale 0.85f, SocialMediaRow.kt:120-127) that the KMP SocialMediaButton omits — but that is an interaction/animation difference, not a responsiveness one.
- **Suggested fix:** None for responsiveness — parity confirmed. (The missing press-scale animation belongs to the interaction-audit section, not this one.)

**⚪ [Low] Library MangaCard — per-card adaptive button/icon scaling — Native MangaCard scales its overlay action buttons/icons to the card's resolved width via BoxWithConstraints; KMP LibraryCard uses fixed-size controls** _(Responsiveness)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaCard.kt:128-144 `BoxWithConstraints { buttonSize = (maxWidth*0.22f).coerceIn(4.dp,40.dp); iconSize = buttonSize*0.55f; spacerSize = (maxWidth*0.01f).coerceIn(1.dp,3.dp) }`; card itself `aspectRatio(1f/1.5f).widthIn(120.dp)` (MangaCard.kt:122-123).
- **KMP:** Partial — LibraryScreen.kt:915-916 LibraryCard uses BoxWithConstraints to read `cardWidth = maxWidth` for the cover, but the per-card action IconButtons are described as 'sized adaptively by the caller via BoxWithConstraints' (LibraryScreen.kt:1270) — needs confirmation the 0.22f/0.55f scaling factors and the 120.dp widthIn / 1:1.5 aspect ratio match native. The grid card otherwise relies on Adaptive cell width without an explicit widthIn(120.dp) floor.
- **Explanation:** Native cards enforce a 120.dp minimum width and a 1:1.5 aspect ratio, and scale the overlay watch/like/delete buttons to 22% of card width (icon 55% of button). If KMP's LibraryCard does not reproduce the 120.dp widthIn floor and the 0.22f/0.55f button-scaling ratios, the overlay controls will not shrink/grow with column count the way native's do — most visible at high column counts (small cards) where native shrinks buttons to the 4.dp floor. Given the Library grid already diverges (density enum), the exact card-internal scaling is a secondary cosmetic concern.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm and, if missing, port the native MangaCard sizing: `widthIn(min=120.dp)` + `aspectRatio(1f/1.5f)` on the card, and BoxWithConstraints-driven button/icon sizing (buttonSize=cardWidth*0.22f coerceIn 4..40dp, iconSize=buttonSize*0.55f) so overlay controls scale with column count as in native.

### Accessibility  `accessibility`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 12 (🔴0 🟠0 🟡1 ⚪11)

> Both apps implement accessibility identically at the strategy level: the ONLY accessibility mechanism in either codebase is the `contentDescription` parameter on `Icon`/`Image`/`AsyncImage`. I verified that NEITHER app uses `Modifier.semantics{}`, `Role`, `heading()`, `stateDescription`, `liveRegion`, `mergeDescendants`, or `testTag`-as-label (grep returned 0 on both sides; the 20 "semantics" hits in KMP are all KDoc prose, not code). Touch targets on both sides rely on Material defaults (IconButton ~48dp); neither uses `minimumInteractiveComponentSize`, and the library-card action buttons are capped at 40dp on BOTH sides (parity, both sub-48dp). The headline difference is that native hardcodes English content descriptions while KMP routes most of them through `stringResource` (en + Arabic) — a net localization/TalkBack improvement, with a handful of wording divergences and a few content-description strings that lack Arabic translations. Concrete regressions in KMP: the library card cover content description is `null` (native uses "Cover of {title}"), the About-screen logo content description is `null` (native uses "Header Icon"), and the Statistics/About back affordance is rendered as a text "Back" button instead of native's labeled ArrowBack IconButton (still labeled, but a touch-target/structure change). The home-feed save toggle changed icon (heart→bookmark) and label wording. Overall accessibility parity is partial: TalkBack label coverage is broadly equivalent or better in KMP, with a few specific cover/image labels lost.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Accessibility</summary>

**🟡 [Medium] Library / MangaCard cover image — Library cover image has no TalkBack content description in KMP** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes — native MangaCard.kt:148-150 sets the cover AsyncImage `contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.manga_cover_description, item.title)` which resolves to "Cover of {title}" (en) / "غلاف {title}" (ar).
- **KMP:** No — ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt:1161-1164 `LibraryCardCover` passes `contentDescription = null` to YamiCoverImage, so the library-card cover is treated as decorative and TalkBack announces nothing for it.
- **Explanation:** The native library grid announces each cover as "Cover of {manga title}" (localized, including Arabic). In KMP the same cover is explicitly null, so a TalkBack user swiping the library grid gets no per-item cover label. Native is the source of truth and intentionally describes this image with a formatted, localized string. The KMP card does render the title as visible text elsewhere on the card, but the cover image itself loses its description.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a localized formatted string (e.g. reuse/port `manga_cover_description` = "Cover of %1$s") and pass it as the `contentDescription` to `LibraryCardCover`'s YamiCoverImage instead of null.

**⚪ [Low] About screen header logo — About-screen app logo content description is null in KMP but labeled in native** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes — native about/screen/AboutScreen.kt:101-102 renders the `ic_launcher_foreground` Image with `contentDescription = "Header Icon"`.
- **KMP:** No — ui/about/AboutScreen.kt:261-263 renders the same `ic_launcher_foreground` painter with `contentDescription = null`.
- **Explanation:** Native describes the About header logo as "Header Icon"; KMP marks it decorative (null). This is also internally inconsistent in KMP: the identical `ic_launcher_foreground` logo on the Settings screen IS labeled (ui/settings/SettingsScreen.kt:413 uses `settings_header_icon` = "Header Icon") while the About one is null. Native labels both. Marking a logo decorative is defensible, but it diverges from the source of truth and from KMP's own Settings screen.
- **Suggested fix:** For consistency with native and with KMP's own Settings header, either label the About logo with a (localized) "Header Icon"/app-name string, or make BOTH the Settings and About logos null. Pick one policy and apply it to both.

**⚪ [Low] Statistics screen / About screen — back navigation affordance — Back is a text "Back" TextButton in KMP vs a labeled ArrowBack IconButton in native** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes (IconButton) — native StatisticsScreen.kt:54 uses `Icon(Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack, contentDescription = stringResource(R.string.desc_back))`; native about/screen/AboutScreen.kt:75-80 uses an ArrowBack IconButton with `contentDescription = "Back"`. Both are ~48dp touch targets.
- **KMP:** Partial (TextButton) — ui/statistics/StatisticsScreen.kt:171-173 and ui/about/AboutScreen.kt (navigationIcon, see KDoc L146-149) render a `TextButton(onClick = onBack) { Text(stringResource(Res.string.back)) }` instead of an icon button.
- **Explanation:** Both are accessible (TalkBack reads "Back, button" either way), so label parity is preserved. The divergence is structural: the touch target changes from a fixed ~48dp square IconButton to a text-shaped button whose height/width depend on text metrics, and the visual affordance (chevron vs word) differs from the source of truth. This affects focus-target size/shape consistency across the app's back affordances (other KMP screens like Language/Details/Complaint keep the ArrowBack IconButton).
- **Suggested fix:** Use the same `Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.ArrowBack` IconButton + localized `back` content description in the Statistics and About navigationIcon slots that the rest of the KMP app already uses, to keep back affordances uniform and the touch target a consistent 48dp.

**⚪ [Low] Home feed list card — save/bookmark toggle — Save toggle icon changed from heart to bookmark, and TalkBack label wording changed** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — native MangaHomeCard.kt:279-281 uses `Icons.Filled.Favorite`/`Icons.Filled.FavoriteBorder` (a HEART) tinted Color.Red, with `contentDescription = if (isSaved) "Saved" else "Save"`.
- **KMP:** Partial — ui/home/components/HomeFeedRow.kt:143-144 uses `YamiIcons.Bookmark`/`YamiIcons.BookmarkOutline` (a BOOKMARK) and content descriptions `home_saved` ("Saved") / `home_save` ("Save to library") passed from HomeScreen.kt:433-434.
- **Explanation:** On the home feed, native shows a red heart for the save toggle; KMP shows a bookmark glyph. The KMP code comment claims it matches "legacy ic_bookmark semantics", but the actual native source at MangaHomeCard.kt:279 uses Icons.Filled.Favorite (a heart), so the icon truly differs. The TalkBack label also changes: native announces "Save"/"Saved"; KMP announces "Save to library"/"Saved". The label is still meaningful (and localized in KMP), but it diverges from the source of truth's wording, and the icon-to-meaning mapping a TalkBack user might infer from the visual differs.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide whether the home-feed save action should visually be a heart (native) or a bookmark (KMP); align the icon to native if strict parity is required. Align the content-description wording to native's "Save"/"Saved" or confirm "Save to library" is the intended copy and update native accordingly.

**⚪ [Low] Home top bar — open-in-webview action — TalkBack label for the web action differs: "Options" (native) vs "Open in browser" (KMP)** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes — native HomeScreen.kt:244-245 `Icon(Icons.Default.Web, contentDescription = "Options")`.
- **KMP:** Yes (different text) — ui/home/HomeScreen.kt:211-213 uses `contentDescription = stringResource(Res.string.home_open_in_webview)` where `home_open_in_webview` = "Open in browser".
- **Explanation:** The same toolbar action (open the source site in a webview) is announced as "Options" by native TalkBack and as "Open in browser" by KMP. KMP's label is arguably clearer and is localized, but it diverges from the source-of-truth wording. Worth flagging because the native string "Options" is vague and could be intentional product copy.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm the intended TalkBack label for the home web action. If native's "Options" is authoritative, change `home_open_in_webview`; otherwise treat KMP's "Open in browser" as the corrected copy and update native.

**⚪ [Low] Content descriptions — Arabic/localization coverage of a11y strings — Several KMP content-description strings have no Arabic translation, so TalkBack reads English in ar locale** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** N/A — native hardcodes ALL content descriptions in English (e.g. "Settings", "Share", "+18 Icon", "Header Icon"), so native never localizes them at all.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP localizes most content descriptions, but `settings_header_icon`, `np_details_adult_icon_cd`, and `np_reader_share` exist only in values/ (en) with NO entry in any values-ar/ file (verified by grep across ui/src/commonMain/composeResources/values-ar/). Many other a11y strings (back, downloads, reader_*, library_*, home_*) DO have Arabic.
- **Explanation:** This is a partial-localization gap, not a regression vs native (native is English-only for these). When the device is Arabic, KMP TalkBack will announce these three labels in English while sibling labels announce in Arabic — an inconsistency within the KMP Arabic experience. Because native never localized them, KMP is still equal-or-better, hence Low severity.
- **Suggested fix:** Add values-ar/ translations for `settings_header_icon`, `np_details_adult_icon_cd`, and `np_reader_share` (and audit the full a11y-string set for any other en-only content descriptions) so the Arabic TalkBack experience is consistent.

**⚪ [Low] Updates screen — swipe-to-dismiss action icons — Swipe background icon label wording differs: "Mark as read" (native) vs "Mark read" (KMP)** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes — native notifications/UpdatesScreen.kt:192 swipe-reveal icon `Icons.Outlined.Done` has `contentDescription = "Mark as read"`; delete side `contentDescription = "Delete"`.
- **KMP:** Yes (different text) — ui/updates/UpdatesScreen.kt:444 uses `contentDescription = stringResource(Res.string.mark_read)` where `mark_read` = "Mark read"; delete uses `delete` = "Delete".
- **Explanation:** Minor wording divergence on the swipe-to-dismiss reveal icons ("Mark as read" → "Mark read"). The delete label matches. These icons sit in the swipe background and are largely decorative since the gesture, not the icon, performs the action, so TalkBack impact is small. KMP's version is localized (en + ar). Flagged for exact-wording parity completeness.
- **Suggested fix:** If exact-wording parity with native is required, change the `mark_read` string to "Mark as read". Otherwise document "Mark read" as the intended copy.

**⚪ [Low] Details — per-chapter download button label — Native per-chapter download IconButton has NO content description (clickable-without-label); KMP adds labels** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Partial/unlabeled — native details/ui/screens/ChapterItem.kt:87-93 wraps the download glyph in an `IconButton(onClick=...)` whose Icon has `contentDescription = null`, so the clickable per-chapter download/done control is announced by TalkBack only as an unlabeled "button".
- **KMP:** Yes — ui/details/DetailsScreen.kt:1129/1138/1147 label the chapter download states with `details_cancel_chapter_download` / `downloaded` / `details_download_chapter`, and DetailsScreen.kt:1112 adds a labeled read/unread toggle (`details_mark_read`/`details_mark_unread`).
- **Explanation:** This is a divergence where KMP IMPROVES on the source of truth: native's chapter download button is a clickable IconButton with a null contentDescription (a genuine TalkBack 'unlabeled clickable' defect), whereas KMP gives it a stateful localized label and additionally surfaces a labeled read/unread toggle. Documented as a divergence because native is the declared source of truth, but it is in the accessibility-positive direction.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed in KMP. Optionally back-port the labels to native to remove the unlabeled-clickable defect there. Keep KMP's labeled states.

**⚪ [Low] Dialog header icons (CBZ conversion, adult/18+ warnings, error/empty states) — Native labels several dialog/state header icons; KMP sets the equivalents to null** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes — native labels decorative dialog header icons: CbzConversionDialog.kt:66/139 ("Error"/"Warning"), MConfirmationDialog.kt:52 ("18+ Warning"), AdultConfirmationDialog.kt:55 ("+18 Icon").
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP sets such header icons to null (e.g. SettingsScreen.kt:1287 Warning icon `contentDescription = null`; YamiStateViews.kt:93/147/203/288 empty/error icons null), though it DOES label the details adult icon via `np_details_adult_icon_cd` = "Adult content warning" (DetailsScreen.kt:1312).
- **Explanation:** Native announces dialog header/state icons ("Warning", "Error", "18+ Warning", "+18 Icon"); KMP generally treats them as decorative (null) because an accompanying visible title already conveys the meaning. Marking these decorative is the more correct a11y practice (avoids redundant TalkBack announcements), but it diverges from the source of truth and is applied inconsistently in KMP (the details adult icon IS labeled while the settings/state ones are not).
- **Suggested fix:** Adopt one consistent policy for header/state icons that are already described by adjacent title text (recommend null/decorative everywhere), and apply it uniformly — including the details adult icon — rather than mixing labeled and null. If strict native parity is required instead, add the corresponding (localized) labels.

**⚪ [Low] Reader — page step buttons (SeekBar) icon/label mapping — KMP fixes native's swapped Next/Previous icon-and-label and makes them RTL-aware; native has them inverted** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes (inverted) — native SeekBarContainer.kt:50-62 places the FIRST button bound to `hasNext`/`onNext` but draws the `ic_previous` drawable with `contentDescription = "Next"`; the SECOND button is bound to `hasPrevious`/`onPrevious` drawing `ic_next` with `contentDescription = "Previous"`. Drawables are not AutoMirrored.
- **KMP:** Yes (corrected) — ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt:970-993 uses `Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.NavigateBefore` with `np_reader_previous_page` on the left (decrements index) and `Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.NavigateNext` with `np_reader_next_page` on the right (increments index). Code comment at L957-961 explicitly states it carries the intent not the swapped labels.
- **Explanation:** Native's reader page-step buttons have a label/icon inversion (a button that advances pages draws a 'previous' glyph and is described "Next"). KMP intentionally corrects this so the left button is previous-page (NavigateBefore, localized "Previous page") and the right is next-page, using AutoMirrored icons that flip in RTL/Arabic. This is an accessibility and RTL improvement over the source of truth, documented as a behavioral divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed in KMP. The corrected, RTL-aware mapping is preferable; optionally back-port the fix to native.

**⚪ [Low] Touch target size — library card action buttons — Library card Watch/Like/Delete action buttons can be smaller than the 48dp minimum on BOTH sides** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes (sub-48dp) — native MangaCard.kt:133-140 computes `buttonSize = (cardWidth * 0.22f).coerceIn(4.dp, 40.dp)` and renders each action as a `Box(.size(buttonSize)).clickable{}` (max 40dp, no minimum-interactive-size enforcement).
- **KMP:** Yes (sub-48dp) — ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt:917 computes the same `buttonSize = (cardWidth * 0.22f).coerceIn(4.dp, 40.dp)` and passes it as `Modifier.size(buttonSize)` to YamiIconButton (LibraryScreen.kt:1309/1320/1327); the explicit size override shrinks IconButton's default 48dp target to <=40dp.
- **Explanation:** Both implementations cap the library-card action touch targets at 40dp (and as low as 4dp on a tiny card), below the WCAG/Material 48dp recommendation. This is a PARITY item — the KMP migration faithfully reproduced the native sizing, including the sub-48dp ceiling — so it is not a regression, but it is a shared accessibility weakness. Neither side uses `minimumInteractiveComponentSize`.
- **Suggested fix:** On both sides, raise the coerce ceiling to >=48dp or wrap the action in a `minimumInteractiveComponentSize`/`sizeIn(minWidth=48.dp,minHeight=48.dp)` while keeping the visual icon at the current size, so the hit target meets the 48dp guideline.

**⚪ [Low] Details — top-bar actions vs native labeled ActionButtons; missing visible labels — Native details actions are icon+visible-text ActionButtons; KMP collapses them to icon-only top-bar buttons** _(Accessibility)_

- **Native:** Yes — native details/ui/components/HeaderSection.kt:110-142 renders bookmark/schedule/download/language as `ActionButton`s, each with both `Icon(contentDescription = text)` AND a visible `AutoSubtitleText` label below it (ActionButton.kt:60-72).
- **KMP:** Partial — ui/details/DetailsScreen.kt:472-510 moves bookmark/download/open-in-webview/refresh into icon-only `YamiIconButton`s in the TopAppBar `actions` slot (each has a content description but NO visible text label).
- **Explanation:** For non-TalkBack users with cognitive/low-vision needs, native's visible per-action text labels ("Like", "Download", etc. under each icon) aid recognition; KMP's icon-only top-bar relies entirely on the icon glyph plus the TalkBack content description. TalkBack parity is preserved (both have content descriptions), so the impact is limited to the loss of always-visible text affordance labels. Also note native includes a "Schedule"/Watch-Later ActionButton (HeaderSection.kt:127 with `onClick = {}` — a dead no-op) that KMP omits.
- **Suggested fix:** This is primarily a UI-structure decision (covered more fully by the details/layout audit). For accessibility, ensure the icon-only top-bar actions keep their content descriptions (they do). If the visible-label affordance is valued, consider tooltips or retaining labeled actions. Separately, native's no-op Schedule ActionButton should be reviewed.

</details>

### Validation & Forms  `validation-forms`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 14 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡5 ⚪7)

> Native funnels every "feedback-like" form (Settings feedback, Request-Language, Request-Add-Source) through ONE shared composable `FeedbackDialog.kt` (category dropdown + min-5-char body + /500 counter + "minimum 5 characters required" error + social-media footer; submit gated on `selectedType != null && body.length >= 5`). The user-side ComplaintActionDialog adds Reply (<=500) and Edit (non-blank subject+body, <=1000), and the admin StatusChangeDialog.kt provides admin Edit (type dropdown + hasChanges gate, no length cap), ClosureReason (non-blank, no cap), StatusChange (differs-from-current), Delete. KMP splits these into per-feature dialogs in :ui (SettingsScreen.FeedbackDialog, SourcesScreen.RequestSourceDialog, LanguageScreen.LanguageRequestDialog, ComplaintActionDialog, admin AdminComplaintActionDialog) and the gating values diverge: the KMP Language request gates at 8 chars (vs native 5) with a different error string and no category dropdown / counter / social row; the Sources dialog drops the category dropdown and social row; admin Edit drops the complaint-type field and the hasChanges gate while adding length caps native never had; and the shared SendComplaintUseCase floor was changed from 8 to 5. Headline divergences: inconsistent min-length (8 vs 5) on language requests, missing form controls (type dropdown, social row, counters) on the language/sources dialogs, and admin-edit functional/validation regressions.

**🟠 [High] Request-Language form — Language request minimum body length is 8 chars in KMP but 5 chars in native** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** Yes - LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:125-160 reuses the shared FeedbackDialog; FeedbackDialog.kt:49-51 gates submit on `selectedTypeState != null && feedbackBody.length >= 5` (min 5).
- **KMP:** Yes - LanguageScreen.kt:416 `submitEnabled = !submitting && text.length >= MIN_REQUEST_LENGTH` with `MIN_REQUEST_LENGTH = 8` (LanguageScreen.kt:472).
- **Explanation:** Native allows a language request of 5-7 characters (e.g. 'Hindi', 'Hausa', 'Tamil', 'Khmer'); KMP blocks any request under 8 characters, so a user typing 'Hindi' (5) or 'French' (6) cannot submit. The KMP file's own KDoc (LanguageScreen.kt:92,397-398) justifies 8 as matching the legacy `require(body.length >= 8)` in SendComplaintUseCase, but (a) the native UI gate was 5 not 8, and (b) the KMP shared SendComplaintUseCase floor was itself lowered to 5 (MIN_BODY_LENGTH=5), so the 8-char UI gate is now stricter than both native and the current backend. This is also inconsistent with the sibling KMP Settings/Sources dialogs which gate at 5.
- **Suggested fix:** Change MIN_REQUEST_LENGTH to 5 (LanguageScreen.kt:472) to match native FeedbackDialog and the other two KMP feedback dialogs, and update the error string accordingly.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). FULLY VERIFIED by reading both apps end-to-end. NATIVE (source of truth): - FeedbackDialog.kt:49-51 — `val submitEnabled = remember(...) { selectedTypeState != null && feedbackBody.length >= 5 }` (UI gate = 5). Corroborated by FeedbackDialog.kt:158 `isError = ... feedbackBody.length < 5`, :164 `if (feedbackBody.length < 5)`, and the resource id `minimum_5_characters_required` (:166). - LanguageSelectionScreen.kt:125-160 — calls `FeedbackDialog(visible=..., selectedType = ComplaintType.LANGUAGES, headerText = request_add_language, textFieldText = enter_your_language)`. So the Request-Language form is exactly the shared FeedbackDialog gating at 5. Confirms `existsInNative` claim. - (Native backend nuance) native SendComplaintUseCase.kt:14 `require(complaint.body.length >= 8)`. The native USE CASE floor was 8, but the native UI gate the user hits is 5; the claim correctly characterizes the native gate as 5. KMP: - LanguageScreen.kt:416 — `val submitEnabled = !submitting && text.length >= MIN_REQUEST_LENGTH`. - LanguageScreen.kt:472 — `private const val MIN_REQUEST_LENGTH = 8`. Corroborated by :437 `isError = text.isNotEmpty() && text.length < MIN_REQUEST_LENGTH` and :439-441 helper "at_least_n_characters, 8". Confirms `existsInKmp` claim (min 8). - KMP KDoc rationale at LanguageScreen.kt:92-93 and :397-398 explicitly cites "threshold (8 chars) matches the legacy `require(body.length >= 8)` in SendComplaintUseCase" — confirming the claim that the file justifies 8 by the legacy require. - BUT the current KMP shared SendComplaintUseCase.kt:14,20 is now `require(complaint.body.length >= MIN_BODY_LENGTH)` with `const val MIN_BODY_LENGTH = 5` (comment :11-13 says "OLD native FeedbackDialog gated the body at >= 5... prior >= 8 floor silently rejected 5-7 char bodies — a parity break"). So the KMP UI gate of 8 is now STRICTER than the current KMP backend (5). The KDoc rationale at LanguageScreen.kt:92/397 is itself stale. - Submission path verified live: LanguageScreen -> LanguageIntent.OnSubmitRequest -> domain SendLanguageRequestUseCase.kt:120-121 (pass-through) -> FeedbackRepository.kt:157-158 default impl pins `subject = "Languages"` (LANGUAGE_REQUEST_SUBJECT, :166) -> FeedbackRepositoryImpl.kt:131-146 -> legacy shared SendComplaintUseCase (floor 5). So a 5-7 char request WOULD pass the current backend; only the KMP UI gate blocks it. SIBLING INCONSISTENCY (confirmed): - SettingsScreen.kt:951 — `val submitEnabled = selectedType != null && body.length >= 5 && !isSubmitting`. - SourcesScreen.kt:870 — `val submitEnabled = body.length >= 5 && !isSubmitting`. Both sibling KMP feedback dialogs gate at 5; LanguageScreen alone gates at 8. NET: A user typing "Hindi"(5)/"French"(6)/"Tamil"(5)/"Hausa"(5) can submit in native (UI gate 5) and would pass the current KMP backend (floor 5), but is blocked by the KMP LanguageScreen UI gate (8). Every sub-claim — values, file:line citations, the stale-KDoc rationale, the lowered shared floor, and the sibling-dialog inconsistency — checks out.

**🟠 [High] Admin Edit-Complaint form — Admin edit dialog cannot change the complaint TYPE in KMP; native admin edit has a ComplaintType dropdown** _(MissingFeature)_

The complaint type is silently preserved from the original, so the admin loses a field-level edit affordance present in the source of truth.
