KDoc (L11-14) explicitly states it "preserves the parent's userId, `type`, createdAt, status, AND metadata", confirming type is silently carried over from the original, not editable. - The type field DOES exist in KMP: ComplaintSummary.type: ComplaintType (ComplaintSummary.kt:127) and the ComplaintType enum (ComplaintSummary.kt:167-174, same 6 variants TECHNICAL/LANGUAGES/SITES_ADD/SITE_ERROR/FEATURES/CUSTOM as native). So the data model supports it; only the admin edit affordance is missing. All claimed line references verified accurate.

**🟡 [Medium] Request-Language form — Language request dialog drops the category dropdown, the /500 character counter, and the social-media footer present in native** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - native routes Request-Language through FeedbackDialog.kt which shows: a category ExposedDropdownMenuBox pre-set to LANGUAGES (FeedbackDialog.kt:89-135, user can re-pick), a '${length}/500' counter (FeedbackDialog.kt:173-177), and a SocialMediaRow footer with divider + copy (FeedbackDialog.kt:184-201).
- **KMP:** No - LanguageRequestDialog (LanguageScreen.kt:408-470) is a bespoke AlertDialog with only a prompt Text + single OutlinedTextField; no dropdown, no /500 counter, no social-media row.
- **Explanation:** The native Request-Language dialog is the full feedback form (category selectable, char counter, social links). KMP's custom dialog is a stripped multiline text box. Although the category is fixed to LANGUAGES semantically, the native UI still rendered the dropdown and the social/counter chrome; KMP users lose the running character count, the social-contact affordance, and the visual consistency with the other feedback entry points.
- **Suggested fix:** Either reuse the shared KMP FeedbackDialog composable for the language path (pre-selecting LANGUAGES) or add the /500 counter and YamiSocialMediaRow footer to LanguageRequestDialog to match native.

**🟡 [Medium] Request-Language form — Language-request error text differs: native 'Minimum 5 characters required' vs KMP 'At least 8 characters'** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - error shown is `minimum_5_characters_required` = 'Minimum 5 characters required' (strings.xml:306, FeedbackDialog.kt:164-169).
- **KMP:** Yes - error shown is `at_least_n_characters` = 'At least %1$d characters' formatted with 8 (LanguageScreen.kt:439-444; strings.xml:138).
- **Explanation:** Different wording AND different threshold communicated to the user. Native: 'Minimum 5 characters required'. KMP: 'At least 8 characters'. This both confuses parity testers and exposes the threshold bug to end users.
- **Suggested fix:** Use the `minimum_5_characters_required` string (or a 5-based message) for the language dialog once the threshold is corrected to 5.

**🟡 [Medium] Request-Add-Source form — Sources request dialog drops the category dropdown and social-media footer present in native** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - SourcesScreen.kt:184-219 and RepoSettingsScreen.kt:175-210 reuse FeedbackDialog with `selectedType = ComplaintType.SITES_ADD`; the dialog renders the category dropdown (FeedbackDialog.kt:89-135) and the SocialMediaRow footer (FeedbackDialog.kt:184-201).
- **KMP:** No - RequestSourceDialog (SourcesScreen.kt:861-960) renders only a prompt Text + single OutlinedTextField with /500 counter; no category dropdown, no social-media row.
- **Explanation:** Native's add-source flow is the full FeedbackDialog (with the category pre-selected to SITES_ADD but still shown and changeable, plus the social footer). KMP's RequestSourceDialog removes the dropdown and the social row. KMP did keep the /500 counter and min-5 gate here, so validation gating matches, but the form structure/chrome diverges from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the YamiSocialMediaRow footer (and optionally a read-only/fixed category indicator) to RequestSourceDialog, or reuse the shared FeedbackDialog with SITES_ADD pre-selected, to match native.

**🟡 [Medium] Admin Edit-Complaint form — Admin edit Save button gating: native requires the content to have CHANGED (hasChanges); KMP enables Save even when nothing changed** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** Yes - native EditComplaintDialog Save is `enabled = hasChanges && subject.trim().isNotEmpty() && body.trim().isNotEmpty()` (StatusChangeDialog.kt:278), where hasChanges = type/subject/body differs from the original (lines 124-126).
- **KMP:** No - KMP admin EditContent Save is `enabled = !isSubmitting && editedSubject.isNotBlank() && editedBody.isNotBlank() && editedBody.length <= maxChars` (AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt:664-667); there is no equality-to-original check.
- **Explanation:** Native disables Save until the admin actually changes something, preventing no-op writes. KMP allows submitting an unchanged complaint, which fires a redundant Firestore write. Same gap exists on the user-side EditContent (ComplaintActionDialog.kt:571-574) which also omits a hasChanges guard.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a hasChanges derived boolean (subject/body [and type] differ from complaint) and AND it into the enabled condition for both the admin and user-side EditContent Save buttons.

**🟡 [Medium] Settings feedback form / shared backend — Shared SendComplaintUseCase minimum body length changed from 8 (native) to 5 (KMP)** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** Yes - native SendComplaintUseCase.kt:14 enforces `require(complaint.body.length >= 8) { "Body too short" }`.
- **KMP:** Yes - KMP shared SendComplaintUseCase.kt:14,20 enforces `require(complaint.body.length >= MIN_BODY_LENGTH)` with `MIN_BODY_LENGTH = 5`.
- **Explanation:** The native backend invariant rejects bodies under 8 chars; KMP lowered it to 5. This was a deliberate reconciliation (the KMP comment notes the native FeedbackDialog UI only gated at 5, so 5-7 char bodies were silently rejected server-side in native). Documenting it as a divergence from the literal source-of-truth value: KMP now accepts 5-7 char complaint bodies that native's use case would have thrown on. Net effect is more permissive submission than native; correct for the Settings/Sources paths (UI gate 5) but it also means the KMP language path's 8-char UI gate is now stricter than its own backend.
- **Suggested fix:** Keep MIN_BODY_LENGTH=5 if the intent is to match the native UI gate, but align ALL KMP UI gates (especially the language dialog at 8) to the same 5 so UI and backend agree app-wide.

**⚪ [Low] Admin Edit-Complaint form — KMP admin edit imposes a 1000-char body cap + counter that native admin edit does not have** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** No - native EditComplaintDialog body field has no maxChars guard and no counter; `onValueChange = { body = it }` (StatusChangeDialog.kt:241), maxLines=5 only.
- **KMP:** Yes - KMP admin EditContent caps body at 1000 chars (`if (it.length <= maxChars) editedBody = it`), shows `${editedBody.length}/$maxChars`, sets isError above cap (AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt:558,617,624,633).
- **Explanation:** KMP added a hard 1000-char cap and a character counter to the admin edit body that the native admin dialog never enforced. While reasonable, it is a behavioral divergence from the source of truth (native admin could type unlimited body length). The KMP KDoc cites the user-side dialog's 1000 cap, but the native ADMIN dialog had no such cap.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm with product whether the 1000-char cap is intended for admin edits; if strict parity is required, remove the cap/counter from the admin EditContent body field, otherwise document the intentional tightening.

**⚪ [Low] Admin Closure-Reason form — KMP closure-reason field imposes a 500-char cap + counter; native ClosureReasonDialog has no length cap** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** No - native ClosureReasonDialog reason field is `onValueChange = { reasonText = it }` with no length guard and no counter (StatusChangeDialog.kt:409-422); Add enabled only on `reasonText.trim().isNotEmpty()` (line 448).
- **KMP:** Yes - KMP ClosureReasonContent caps at `maxChars = 500` (`if (it.length <= maxChars) reasonText = it`) and shows `${reasonText.length}/$maxChars` (AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt:394,491,501). Submit gated on `reasonText.isNotBlank()` (line 507).
- **Explanation:** KMP enforces a 500-char hard limit and a counter on the closure-reason text that native never had. The KMP source comment/KDoc (AdminComplaintActionDialog.kt:141-142,163,172) asserts 'matches legacy maxLength = 500', but the native ClosureReasonDialog in StatusChangeDialog.kt has NO maxLength on its reason field — so the claimed parity precedent is inaccurate and the cap is a net-new constraint.
- **Suggested fix:** Either remove the 500-char cap to match native, or verify the cap is intentional and correct the KDoc that falsely claims native parity for maxLength=500.

**⚪ [Low] Settings feedback form — Feedback body field label text differs: native 'Enter your feedback' vs KMP 'Describe the issue or feature'** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - native Settings passes `textFieldText = enter_your_feedback` ('Enter your feedback', strings.xml:263) into FeedbackDialog, used as the body OutlinedTextField label (FeedbackDialog.kt:148-151).
- **KMP:** Yes - KMP FeedbackDialog hardcodes the body label to `describe_issue_or_feature` ('Describe the issue or feature', strings.xml:170) (SettingsScreen.kt:1039); the parameterizable textFieldText concept was dropped.
- **Explanation:** Native FeedbackDialog took headerText/textFieldText parameters so each call site (Settings='Enter your feedback', Language='Enter your language', Sources='Enter the site url') showed tailored copy. KMP hardcodes the Settings body label to a new string 'Describe the issue or feature' that does not exist in native. Title matches (request_feature_bug) but the field label diverges.
- **Suggested fix:** Use the `enter_your_feedback` string for the Settings feedback body label to match native, or confirm the new copy is an intentional product change.

**⚪ [Low] Feedback form error string — The min-5 error string text was shortened: native 'Minimum 5 characters required' vs KMP 'Minimum 5 characters'** _(Localization/RTL)_

- **Native:** Yes - `minimum_5_characters_required` = 'Minimum 5 characters required' (strings.xml:306).
- **KMP:** Yes - same key `minimum_5_characters_required` = 'Minimum 5 characters' (strings.xml:68) — the word 'required' was dropped.
- **Explanation:** Same resource key, different value. Used in both the KMP Settings FeedbackDialog (SettingsScreen.kt:1054) and Sources RequestSourceDialog (SourcesScreen.kt:918). The user-facing text lost the word 'required', a small copy regression from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Restore the value to 'Minimum 5 characters required' to match native, including the Arabic translation.

**⚪ [Low] Search input — KMP short-circuits a blank search query to an empty result; native fires the search regardless** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** No blank guard - native SearchScreen submits `localQuery` on IME action with no emptiness check (SearchScreen.kt:95-103) and HomeViewModel.fetchAllSearchResults(query)/single-search fire the network call even for blank/whitespace queries (HomeViewModel.kt:55-79).
- **KMP:** Yes - SearchViewModel.runSearch returns early on `query.isBlank()` setting `single = Success(emptyList()), multi = emptyMap()` (SearchViewModel.kt:91-94).
- **Explanation:** KMP added input validation to the search path (blank => empty result, no network call), which native never had. This is arguably an improvement but is a behavioral divergence from the source of truth: native would actually issue a (likely empty/unfiltered) search request for a blank query. Difference is visible if a user clears the field and submits.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm the blank-query short-circuit is the desired behavior; if strict native parity is required, allow the blank query through, otherwise document the intentional guard.

**⚪ [Low] Complaint Reply form — KMP trims reply/edit text before submit and gates on raw isNotBlank; native submits raw untrimmed text** _(Validation)_

- **Native:** Native ReplyContent sends raw `replyText` in the Complaint (FeedbackDialog/ComplaintActionDialog.kt:303-314) and EditContent sends raw `editedText` (ComplaintActionDialog.kt:451-456); enabled gates on `replyText.isNotBlank()` / `editedText.isNotBlank() && editedSubject.isNotBlank()`.
- **KMP:** KMP trims before dispatch: `val trimmed = replyText.trim(); if (trimmed.isNotBlank() ...) OnSubmitReply(trimmed)` (ComplaintActionDialog.kt:435-437) and `OnSubmitEdit(trimmedSubject, trimmedBody)` (ComplaintActionDialog.kt:561-567); enabled still gates on the raw (untrimmed) `replyText.isNotBlank()`.
- **Explanation:** Behavioral divergence: native persists leading/trailing whitespace exactly as typed; KMP strips it. Also a subtle inconsistency in KMP itself - the enabled flag uses the untrimmed value (`replyText.isNotBlank()`) while the onClick guard uses the trimmed value, so a whitespace-only entry can leave the button enabled yet the onClick no-ops (button looks tappable but does nothing). Native had the same enabled-uses-raw pattern but no trim, so the button always submitted.
- **Suggested fix:** Make the enabled condition use the trimmed value (e.g. `replyText.trim().isNotBlank()`) so the button state matches the submit guard; decide whether trimming on submit is the intended parity behavior.

**⚪ [Low] Complaint Reply form — Reply/Edit character counter uses a hardcoded string in KMP vs a localized formatted resource in native** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes - native uses `stringResource(R.string.character_count, length, maxChars)` where character_count = '%1$d/%2$d' (ComplaintActionDialog.kt:281,430; strings.xml:437).
- **KMP:** Yes - KMP hardcodes `"${replyText.length}/$maxChars"` and `"${editedBody.length}/$maxChars"` (ComplaintActionDialog.kt:414,540).
- **Explanation:** Output is visually equivalent ('12/500'), but KMP bypasses the localizable `character_count` resource. For locales that need locale-specific digit shaping or layout (e.g. Arabic-Indic digits), the hardcoded interpolation will not localize whereas the native formatted resource could. Minor and cosmetic in most locales.
- **Suggested fix:** Route the counter through a formatted string resource (equivalent of character_count) so digit/format localization is preserved.

</details>

### Global States & Error Handling  `global-states-errors`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 13 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡4 ⚪6)

> Native centralizes state in core/states/State.kt (sealed Success/Loading/Error with an HTTP-status-code + Throwable-to-message mapper) and renders states with three shared composables: LoadingScreen (CircularProgressIndicator defaulting to inversePrimary), ErrorScreen (a 3-action layout of icon-above-text buttons: Retry / Open in WebView / Help, error message bold-red 14sp maxLines=2), and SimpleStatusScreen variants (Maintenance / Stopped / Adult-blocked). Offline handling is explicit: NetworkConnectivityObserver drives a per-screen ConnectivityObserver.Status that gates downloads in LibraryMangaRoute and shows a "No internet connection..." snackbar before enqueue; 403 errors auto-pop a WebViewDialog via Handle403Error on Home/Details/Reader/Library routes. KMP replaces State<T> with a typed AppError hierarchy mapped per-screen to a small fixed set of generic strings, and renders state via YamiLoadingState / YamiEmptyState / YamiErrorState (and YamiSiteStatusView faithfully porting SimpleStatusScreen). The headline divergences: KMP collapses all of native's granular network/HTTP/timeout error messages into a single "Network error" / "Failed to load" string (no HTTP code, no host/timeout distinction); KMP's Search error state drops the Open-in-WebView and Help actions native shows; KMP never gates download enqueue on connectivity nor shows the "No internet" snackbar; the shared loading spinners default to primary instead of native's inversePrimary; and the Library empty state regresses from a rich centered icon+bold-title placeholder to a bare unparameterized Text. The connectivity observer itself was ported faithfully but is no longer consumed by any UI offline affordance.

**🟠 [High] Global error message mapping (Network / HTTP status codes) — KMP collapses all network + HTTP-status errors into a single generic 'Network error' string; native maps each HTTP code to a distinct human message** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - core/states/State.kt:32-50 httpStatusMessage(code) maps 400 'Bad Request', 401 'Unauthorized', 403 'Forbidden Click On Help To Solve The Problem', 404 'Not Found', 408 'Request Timeout', 500 'Internal Server Error', 502 'Bad Gateway', 503 'Service Unavailable', 504 'Gateway Timeout', with generic 'Client Error N'/'Server Error N' fallbacks. These messages flow into ErrorScreen via State.Error.message.
- **KMP:** Partial - AppError.kt:90 keeps the numeric Http(statusCode) but every UI mapper (HomeScreen.kt:505, DetailsScreen.kt:1268, LibraryScreen.kt:1352, ReaderScreen.kt:1629, SearchScreen rememberSearchErrorMessages) does `is AppError.Network -> stringResource(Res.string.error_network)` => always 'Network error' (strings.xml:263). The statusCode is discarded for messaging.
- **Explanation:** A native user seeing a 500 reads 'Internal Server Error', a 404 reads 'Not Found', a 403 reads guidance to tap Help. Every KMP user instead reads the identical 'Network error' regardless of whether the server returned 404, 500, 503, etc. The diagnostic granularity native provided is gone; the statusCode is carried in AppError.Network.Http but never surfaced. This degrades the user's ability to understand and act on failures.
- **Suggested fix:** In the per-screen AppError->String mappers, branch on AppError.Network subtypes and on Http(statusCode) to reproduce native's httpStatusMessage table (distinct strings for 401/403/404/408/500/502/503/504 plus generic client/server fallbacks), instead of one error_network string for the whole Network branch.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: Medium). State.Error.fromCode (L17-18) is called with real HTTP codes: HomeViewModel.kt:111 fromCode(response.code), LibraryDetailsViewModel.kt:224, BaseManga.kt:240. The message reaches the UI: ErrorScreen.kt:68 renders text=message; MangaDetailsScreen.kt:51-56 ErrorScreen(message=state.message); HomeScreen.kt:299/372, SearchScreen.kt:150, ReaderViewModel.kt:239/435, LibraryItems.kt:172 surface state.message. So native users do see code-specific text. KMP: core/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/core/error/AppError.kt:90 keeps Network.Http(statusCode:Int). Data layer builds it with the real code: MangaDetailsRepositoryImpl.kt:138/148/171, ChapterPagesRepositoryImpl.kt:112, HomeMappers.kt:158. Every UI error mapper collapses the whole Network parent to one string `is AppError.Network -> network`: HomeScreen.kt:505, DetailsScreen.kt:1268, LibraryScreen.kt:1352, ReaderScreen.kt:1629 & 1653, SearchScreen.kt:546 (rememberSearchErrorMessages). Strings error_network=strings.xml:263, details_error_network=251, reader_error_network=316 all equal "Network error". statusCode is never used to choose a message. This preserves/improves native's 403 "tap Help" behavior as functional routing, but does NOT restore per-code message text. No openInWebViewLabel/onOpenInWebView and no helpLabel/onHelp — exactly as claimed. - ui/.../ui/components/YamiStateViews.kt: TWO overloads exist — simple (lines 131-167: message/retryLabel/onRetry only) and multi-action (lines 183-239: also openInWebViewLabel/onOpenInWebView (OutlinedButton) + helpLabel/onHelp (OutlinedButton); KDoc lines 169-180 explicitly calls it "the design-system equivalent of the legacy 3-action ErrorScreen (Retry + Open-in-WebView + Help)"). Search uses the simple one. - The recovery capability is ENTIRELY ABSENT from the KMP Search slice, not merely unused at the UI layer: presentation/.../search/SearchIntent.kt has only OnLoadFilters/OnQueryChange/OnModeTabChange/OnApplyFilters/OnMangaClick/OnClose (no OnOpenWebView/OnHelp); SearchEffect.kt has only NavigateToDetails/Close/ShowError; grep for webview\|browser\|help\|403 in the search presentation package returns nothing. CORROBORATION the gap is a real omission, not a platform limitation: the KMP HomeScreen DOES use the 3-action overload — ui/.../ui/home/HomeScreen.kt:326-333 calls YamiErrorState(..., openInWebViewLabel=stringResource(Res.string.home_error_open_in_webview), onOpenInWebView={onIntent(HomeIntent.OnOpenWebView)}, helpLabel=stringResource(Res.string.home_help), onHelp={onIntent(HomeIntent.OnHelp)}). So the Open-in-WebView/Help recovery pattern is fully implemented and proven in KMP (Home, Details, Reader all reference onOpenInWebView), and Search diverges by offering Retry only — matching the native source of truth's behavior and confirming the High severity (on a 403/Cloudflare search failure the KMP user's only action re-hits the same failure with no WebView/Help escape path).

**🟠 [High] Download enqueue offline gating + 'No internet' snackbar — Native blocks download enqueue when offline and shows a 'No internet connection...' snackbar; KMP enqueues downloads unconditionally with no offline check** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes - LibraryMangaRoute.kt:128-140 (single chapter), 169-181 (download all), 206-214 (custom download): each checks `if (internetStatus != ConnectivityObserver.Status.Available)` and calls snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(R.string.no_internet_connection_please_try_again_when_you_re_online) then returns without enqueueing. internetStatus comes from downloadViewModel.networkAvailable (NetworkConnectivityObserver).
- **KMP:** No - grep of presentation/downloads and presentation/details for connectivity/NoConnectivity/networkAvailable/no_internet returns nothing; DownloadsActionRepositoryImpl has no networkStatus(); download intents enqueue without consulting ConnectivityObserver. The 'no internet connection...' string and pre-enqueue guard have no KMP counterpart.
- **Explanation:** A KMP user tapping download while offline gets no immediate feedback — the work is silently enqueued (or fails later inside the worker), whereas native immediately tells them to come back online. This is a user-facing interaction regression in a core flow. The ConnectivityObserver is ported (platform/connectivity/*) but is no longer consumed by any download UI path.
- **Suggested fix:** Expose ConnectivityObserver.observe() to the downloads/details presentation layer, gate the download/download-all/custom-download intents on Status.Available, and emit a ShowError/snackbar effect with the 'No internet connection. Please try again when you're online.' message before enqueue when offline.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (gate EXISTS): native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/navigation/routes/LibraryMangaRoute.kt L75-77 binds internetStatus = downloadViewModel.networkAvailable (ConnectivityObserver, default Unavailable). L128-140 (onChapterDownloadClick, single), L169-181 (downloadAllManga), L206-214 (onCustomDownload) each do `if (internetStatus != ConnectivityObserver.Status.Available) { snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(getString(R.string.no_internet_connection_please_try_again_when_you_re_online)); return }` BEFORE calling downloadViewModel.downloadChapter/downloadChapters. networkAvailable = repository.networkStatus() at presentation/features/download/ui/test2/DownloadViewModelv2.kt:68. String at app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:352 ("No internet connection. Please try again when you're online."). KMP (gate ABSENT, enqueues unconditionally): presentation/src/commonMain/.../details/DetailsViewModel.kt onDownloadChapter (L536-544), onDownloadAllClick (L446-452), onDownloadSelected (L581-594) gate ONLY on state.isInLibrary + null guards; no connectivity check before enqueueChapterDownload/enqueueAllChaptersDownload. domain/.../usecase/downloads/EnqueueChapterDownloadUseCase.kt resolves id + enqueues, no check; EnqueueDownloadUseCase.kt is a thin pass-through to repository.enqueueDownload, KDoc explicitly says the only gate is a UI rule on isDownloaded, not connectivity. ConnectivityObserver IS ported at platform/src/{common,android,ios,desktop}Main/.../connectivity/ConnectivityObserver.kt but consumed by NO download path. shared/src/commonMain/.../download/domain/clean/DownloadRepository.kt L56-59 explicitly documents networkStatus() and its reach chain (VM networkAvailable -> LibraryMangaScreenRoute) were RETIRED; DownloadRepositoryImpl.kt L44-48 dropped the connectivityObserver ctor param. ConnectivityObserver is observed only by ReaderViewModel (page-progress context), not download gating. No no_internet string counterpart and no pre-enqueue guard anywhere in :presentation/:domain/:data/:ui download paths.

**🟡 [Medium] Global error message mapping (connectivity / timeout / connect-exception) — Native distinguishes no-connectivity, timeout, and connect failures with three different messages; KMP shows the same 'Network error' for all three** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes - core/states/State.kt:19-31 fromException maps UnknownHostException -> 'Cannot reach server—please check your internet connection.', SocketTimeoutException -> 'The request timed out—please try again later.', ConnectException -> 'Unable to connect to the server.', else -> 'An unexpected error occurred: <localizedMessage>'.
- **KMP:** Partial - AppError.kt:88-91 declares Network.NoConnectivity, Network.Timeout, Network.Http, Network.Serialization as distinct subclasses, but all UI mappers fold the whole `is AppError.Network` branch to one 'Network error' string, so NoConnectivity and Timeout render identically.
- **Explanation:** Native told the user specifically 'please check your internet connection' vs 'the request timed out—try again later' vs 'unable to connect'. KMP has the typed subclasses available (NoConnectivity, Timeout) but renders all of them as 'Network error', losing the actionable wording. The 'offline' case in particular no longer reads as an offline/connectivity hint anywhere in the typed-error UI path.
- **Suggested fix:** Extend the AppError->String mappers to match the inner Network subtypes: NoConnectivity -> a 'check your internet connection' string, Timeout -> a 'request timed out, try again' string, Serialization/Http -> their own strings, matching native's fromException wording.

**🟡 [Medium] Home feed error state message — Native shows 'Failed to load : <specific error>' interpolating the underlying message; KMP shows just 'Failed to load' with no detail** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes - HomeScreen.kt:297-300 & 370-373 `message = stringResource(R.string.failed_to_load, mangaItemsState.message)`; strings.xml:222 `failed_to_load = 'Failed to load : %1$s'` so the user sees e.g. 'Failed to load : Internal Server Error'.
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/home/HomeScreen.kt:326-327 `state.feedError != null && state.feed.isEmpty() -> YamiErrorState(message = stringResource(Res.string.home_failed_to_load), ...)`; strings.xml:366 `home_failed_to_load = 'Failed to load'` (no %1$s placeholder, no detail appended).
- **Explanation:** Native's home error always carries the concrete reason after the colon; KMP drops the placeholder entirely so the home error never tells the user what failed. Additionally KMP only shows the error when feed.isEmpty(); native shows the error block whenever mangaItemsState is State.Error regardless of any cached items (KMP keeps stale feed and hides the error).
- **Suggested fix:** Reintroduce a parameterized 'Failed to load : %1$s' string and pass the resolved AppError message into YamiErrorState; reconsider the `&& state.feed.isEmpty()` guard so a refresh failure surfaces even when stale items remain (or confirm intended).

**🟡 [Medium] 403 / Cloudflare auto-recovery (Handle403Error) — Native auto-pops an inline WebViewDialog on a 403 (no user tap needed) on Home/Details/Reader/Library; KMP requires the user to manually tap an action or routes to a full WebView screen** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes - Handle403Error.kt:32-49 watches State for code==403 and auto-shows WebViewDialog; wired in HomeRoute.kt:119-136, MangaDetailsRoute, ReadingScreenRoute.kt:88-93, and LibraryMangaRoute.kt:86-97 (showWebViewDalog=true on requestState 403). Recovery is automatic and inline (dialog overlay), then onDismiss retries.
- **KMP:** Partial - Details (DetailsViewModel.kt:160 CHALLENGE_STATUSES, DetailsEffect.SolveCloudflareChallenge) and Reader (ReaderViewModel.kt:629) do auto-detect 403-family and emit an effect, but the :composeApp adapter navigates to a full Screen.WebView rather than an inline dialog; Home/Search/Library expose only a manual 'Open in WebView' button (HomeScreen.kt:326-331) with NO automatic 403 trigger.
- **Explanation:** Native silently surfaces the challenge solver the moment a 403 occurs and returns the user to the same screen on dismiss (inline dialog). KMP Home/Library require the user to notice the failure and manually tap 'Open in WebView'; Details/Reader auto-route but to a separate full-screen WebView (different navigation/back behavior than an overlay dialog). The Library 403 auto-recovery present in native LibraryMangaRoute has no KMP equivalent.
- **Suggested fix:** For Home/Library KMP paths, auto-detect 403-family AppError.Network.Http and trigger the WebView recovery without a manual tap (matching Handle403Error); consider an inline dialog presentation to match native's overlay-and-return UX rather than a full screen navigation.

**🟡 [Medium] Library empty state — Native shows a rich centered placeholder (Inbox icon 72dp @0.7 alpha + titleLarge Bold, library-name-parameterized text); KMP shows a bare single Text with no icon, not bold, generic non-parameterized label** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes - EmptyLibraryPlaceholder.kt:26-50: fillMaxSize Column centered, Icons.Outlined.Inbox at 72.dp tint onBackground@0.7, 16dp spacer, Text style titleLarge FontWeight.Bold centered, message `empty_library_message = 'Your %1$s is empty'` (parameterized with library name).
- **KMP:** Partial - ui/library/LibraryScreen.kt:821-832 EmptyLibraryMessage is just a single Text(style=bodyLarge, color=onSurfaceVariant) with `library_empty = 'Library is empty'` (not parameterized) or no_results_found when searching; no icon, no Bold, not explicitly centered (relies on passed modifier). The shared YamiEmptyState (which has icon+title) is not used here.
- **Explanation:** The native empty library is a designed illustration (large inbox icon + bold title naming the specific library, e.g. 'Your Favorites is empty'); KMP regresses to a plain muted body line that doesn't name the library and has no icon, a clear visual and informational downgrade. KMP also doesn't reuse its own YamiEmptyState here, so it's even less rich than KMP's other empty states.
- **Suggested fix:** Replace EmptyLibraryMessage with YamiEmptyState (Inbox icon, titleMedium/Large, library-name-parameterized title) to match native's EmptyLibraryPlaceholder icon size 72dp, alpha 0.7, bold title and parameterized 'Your %1$s is empty' string.

**⚪ [Low] Error screen action buttons styling (icon-above-text) — Native error actions are transparent icon-above-text buttons (Retry/Refresh, WebAsset, HelpOutline icons); KMP error actions are plain text Button/OutlinedButton with no icons** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes - ErrorScreen.kt:85-102 uses IconAboveTextButton with Icons.Default.Refresh, Icons.Default.WebAsset, Icons.AutoMirrored.Filled.HelpOutline; IconAboveTextButton.kt:31-52 renders a transparent Button (backgroundColor=Transparent, elevation 0, contentColor=primary) with a 24dp icon above auto-sized centered text, laid out in a fillMaxWidth Row with 12dp spacing, each weight(1f).
- **KMP:** No - YamiStateViews.kt:158-237 YamiErrorState renders a filled Button for Retry and OutlinedButton(s) for Open-in-WebView/Help, text-only, stacked vertically (padding top sm/lg) — no icons, different button styles, vertical not horizontal layout.
- **Explanation:** The recovery affordances look materially different: native presents three equal-weight transparent icon+label buttons in a horizontal row; KMP presents a filled primary Retry plus stacked outlined text buttons. Different visual hierarchy, no icons, different arrangement axis.
- **Suggested fix:** If pixel parity is desired, give YamiErrorState's actions icons (Refresh/WebAsset/HelpOutline) and a horizontal equal-weight transparent-button row matching IconAboveTextButton, or document the design-system divergence as intentional.

**⚪ [Low] Error message typography (full-area error) — Native error message is 14sp Bold error-color, maxLines=2, ellipsized; KMP error message is titleMedium (or bodyLarge), not bold, no maxLines cap** _(Typography)_

- **Native:** Yes - ErrorScreen.kt:67-75 Text(message, fontSize=14.sp, color=colorScheme.error, fontWeight=FontWeight.Bold, maxLines=2, overflow=TextOverflow.Ellipsis, textAlign=Center).
- **KMP:** Partial - YamiStateViews.kt:151-157 YamiErrorState Text uses MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium, color=onSurface (NOT error), no fontWeight Bold, no maxLines/overflow. DetailsScreen.kt:528-532 error text uses bodyLarge with colorScheme.error and no maxLines.
- **Explanation:** Native error text is small bold red capped at 2 lines with ellipsis; KMP uses a larger non-bold onSurface-colored title with unbounded lines (so the YamiErrorState icon is colored error but the message text is onSurface, unlike native's red text). A long error message in KMP will wrap to many lines rather than truncating at 2 with ellipsis.
- **Suggested fix:** Align YamiErrorState message styling with native: 14sp/Bold, color=colorScheme.error, maxLines=2 + TextOverflow.Ellipsis (or define an intentional design-system value).

**⚪ [Low] Loading spinner color — Native LoadingScreen defaults the spinner to inversePrimary everywhere; KMP shared YamiLoadingState and search CenteredSpinner use the default primary color** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes - LoadingScreen.kt:18-29 `color: Color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.inversePrimary` and CircularProgressIndicator(color=color); used at 14 sites with the default, so spinners are inversePrimary.
- **KMP:** Partial - HomeScreen.kt:320 & 452 explicitly set inversePrimary (GAP-HOME-15), but YamiStateViews.kt:61 YamiLoadingState calls `CircularProgressIndicator()` (default = primary) and SearchScreen.kt:531 CenteredSpinner calls `CircularProgressIndicator()` (default = primary). Reader (ReaderScreen.kt:1497-area) and others use default too.
- **Explanation:** Only the Home feed spinner matches native's inversePrimary; all other KMP loading spinners (search, the shared YamiLoadingState consumed by downloads/history/etc.) render in primary, a visibly different hue than native's inversePrimary (e.g. inversePrimary 0xFFB0C6FF in dark vs primary). Inconsistent within KMP and divergent from native.
- **Suggested fix:** Give YamiLoadingState a `color: Color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.inversePrimary` parameter (matching native LoadingScreen default) and use it for CenteredSpinner and other spinner sites for app-wide parity.

**⚪ [Low] Connectivity Losing/Lost granularity on iOS & Desktop — Native Android emits 4 states (Available/Unavailable/Losing/Lost); KMP iOS/Desktop poll-based observers collapse to only Available/Unavailable** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - NetworkConnectivityObserver.kt:27-54 emits Status.Available/Losing/Lost/Unavailable via NetworkCallback onAvailable/onLosing/onLost/onUnavailable.
- **KMP:** Partial - AndroidConnectivityObserver.kt:32-52 preserves all 4; but IosConnectivityObserver.kt:58-63 and DesktopConnectivityObserver.kt:46-62 only ever emit Available/Unavailable (HEAD-probe polling), with Losing/Lost documented as collapsed (ConnectivityObserver.kt:73-77).
- **Explanation:** On the new non-Android targets the observer cannot distinguish a network that is in the process of going away (Losing) or just lost (Lost) — both become Unavailable, and the 5s poll interval means up to ~5s latency detecting a transition vs Android's push callback. The native app is Android-only so this is a new-platform limitation rather than a strict Android regression, and Android parity is preserved; flagged because any cross-platform offline UX would behave differently on iOS/Desktop.
- **Suggested fix:** Document the iOS/Desktop coarse-grained-and-polled connectivity as an accepted platform limitation, or replace with native SCNetworkReachability (iOS, already TODO'd in IosConnectivityObserver) / a push-style JVM mechanism for parity; ensure any offline-banner UI tolerates the ~5s detection latency.

**⚪ [Low] Custom in-app ToastHost component — Native has a custom slide-up rounded snackbar ToastHost; in practice it is dead code, and KMP has no equivalent custom toast (uses platform ToastShower + Material SnackbarHost)** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Partial - ToastHostState.kt:29-88 defines a ToastHostState + ToastHost composable (slide-in/fade animated, rounded 8dp, onPrimaryContainer bg, 4dp shadow, 2s auto-dismiss), but its only call site (LibraryMangaRoute.kt:61,131-133,268-274) is fully commented out; runtime feedback uses Material SnackbarHostState and Android Toast.makeText elsewhere.
- **KMP:** No - KMP uses a ToastShower platform SPI (Android Toast, DesktopToastShower.kt logs only, iOS) plus Material3 SnackbarHost driven by MVI effects (DownloadsEffect.ShowError etc.). No port of the animated rounded ToastHost composable.
- **Explanation:** The custom ToastHost is effectively unused in native (commented out), so its absence in KMP is not a functional regression. Worth noting that the toast feedback model changed: native = Android Toast + Material Snackbar; KMP = ToastShower SPI (which on Desktop only writes a log line, i.e. no visible toast on Desktop) + Material Snackbar. Desktop has no visible toast surface.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed for parity with native's dead ToastHost; if Desktop visible toasts are desired, back DesktopToastShower with a SnackbarHost-based surface (already noted as a future phase in DesktopToastShower KDoc).

**⚪ [Low] ImagesState (per-image load state) — Native exposes a dedicated ImagesState (Loading/Success/Error) sealed type for cover/image loading; KMP has no direct counterpart sealed type** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes - core/states/ImagesState.kt:3-7 sealed ImagesState { Loading, Success(url), Error(url, throwable) }, used to drive per-image error/loading affordances (e.g. requestState/imageStatus in routes).
- **KMP:** Partial - per-image state is handled inline via Coil/painter state in YamiCoverImage and ReaderScreen (painter.restart() at ReaderScreen.kt:1497), and a 'failed_to_load_image' string (strings.xml) with a Retry+Open-in-WebView row, rather than a shared ImagesState sealed type. No single ImagesState equivalent located after grep.
- **Explanation:** The image-load state machine is implemented differently (Coil AsyncImagePainter state inline vs native's explicit ImagesState carried through ViewModels). The user-facing reader image error retry exists in KMP; the divergence is structural (no shared type), with the cover-image error affordance handled by the image component. Low risk but a notable architectural difference for image error/loading consistency.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm every native ImagesState consumer (cover blur/placeholder, details header image error) has an equivalent inline Coil-state handling in KMP; if image error UX must be consistent across screens, introduce a shared helper rather than per-call-site painter handling.

### Permissions  `permissions`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 11 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡3 ⚪6)

> Declared Android manifest permissions are at full parity: native (AndroidManifest.xml:4-17) and KMP (app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:9-22) declare the identical 7 uses-permission entries with identical attributes (INTERNET, ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_DATA_SYNC, AD_ID, POST_NOTIFICATIONS required=false, WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE maxSdkVersion=28). There is exactly one runtime permission flow on both sides, POST_NOTIFICATIONS requested from the Theme onboarding step, and KMP ports the core (expect/actual rememberNotificationPermissionRequester, TIRAMISU gating via checkSelfPermission, auto-request-once LaunchedEffect guarded on not-hasPermission, denial toast, permission-gated Continue, Grant Permission row). Headline regression: native's permanent-denial recovery (detect Don't-ask-again via shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale then deep-link to App Settings, ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:76-84) is NOT wired in KMP; the Android openAppSettings actual exists but is dead code, trapping a permanently-denied user on the Continue-gated onboarding step. Secondary divergences: native always shows the grant row vs KMP only when denied; the denial toast fires from a state-keyed LaunchedEffect (can over-fire) instead of the result callback; iOS authorization is a stub relying on a launch-time request absent from iosApp; plus minor grant-row typography/button styling deltas. No storage or other runtime permissions are requested at runtime on either side.

**🟠 [High] Notification permission - permanent-denial redirect to App Settings — Native deep-links to system App Settings when POST_NOTIFICATIONS is permanently denied; KMP never does** _(Permissions)_

- **Native:** Yes - ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:76-84: in the result callback, if not-granted and SDK>=TIRAMISU and not shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale, it calls context.openAppSettings() (lines 209-213, Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS)
- **KMP:** No - ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:155-166 only shows a toast on denial; it never checks shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale and never calls openAppSettings(). The Android actual openAppSettings() (RememberNotificationPermissionRequester.android.kt:134-140) is implemented but dead code with zero call sites repo-wide
- **Explanation:** After Don't-ask-again the system dialog never re-appears. Native detects this and deep-links into OS App Settings so the user can manually enable notifications. Since onboarding gates Continue on the permission, this is the only recovery path. In KMP, after permanent denial both the Grant button and the auto-request become silent no-ops, leaving the user stuck on the Theme step with a disabled Continue button and no way forward. Functional dead-end regression in a core onboarding flow.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale probe to the requester (or expose it from the Android actual) and call openAppSettings() on permanent denial, matching native. Document only.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/onboarding/theme_selection/ThemeSelectionScreen.kt: - Lines 76-84: in the RequestPermission result callback, `if (!granted && Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= TIRAMISU && !ActivityCompat.shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale(context as Activity, POST_NOTIFICATIONS)) { context.openAppSettings() }` — exact permanent-denial detection + redirect. - Lines 209-213: `private fun Context.openAppSettings()` launches `Intent(Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS)` with package Uri + NEW_TASK flag. - Line 151: Continue `Button(enabled = hasNotificationPermission.value)` — onboarding gates Continue on the permission. Auto-request (88-96) and the ThemeSelector Grant button (138-146) both route through the same `launcher`, whose callback (66-85) holds the redirect. ThemeSelector.kt:116-117 Grant button onClick = onRequestNotificationPermission → launcher.launch. Native call-site count for openAppSettings = 2 (one decl L209, one invocation L83). KMP — sole live owner is the route adapter, which never redirects: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/navigation/routes/ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:155-159: denial handling is ONLY `LaunchedEffect(hasPermission, autoRequested.value){ if(autoRequested.value && !hasPermission) toastShower.showLong(deniedMessage) }` — a toast, nothing more. Line 172: Grant button callback = `{ permissionRequester.request() }` only. No rationale check, no openAppSettings call. (Minor: claim cites "155-166" for the toast; 161-166 is actually the auto-request LaunchedEffect — the toast-only branch is 155-159. Immaterial.) - shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale: ZERO occurrences anywhere in the KMP codebase (grep across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/composeApp returned nothing). - openAppSettings(): declared on the interface (shared/.../core/platform/NotificationPermissionRequester.kt:37) and implemented in the Android actual (composeApp/src/androidMain/.../RememberNotificationPermissionRequester.android.kt:134-140, ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS deep-link), with iOS/desktop println stubs — but `grep '\.openAppSettings('` repo-wide (excluding native-app) returns ZERO real invocations; all matches are `override fun` declarations or KDoc prose. Confirmed dead code. - ThemeScreen.kt:402: Continue `Button(enabled = onRequestNotificationPermission == null \|\| hasNotificationPermission)`; route passes a non-null onRequestNotificationPermission (line 172), so Continue is disabled while permission is denied. Grant row only shows while denied (ThemeScreen.kt:396). - Only live consumer of rememberNotificationPermissionRequester() is ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:150 (the KDoc claim of a HomeScreenRoute consumer is itself stale — no such call site exists). Net: Native deep-links to OS App Settings on permanent denial; KMP only toasts and re-calls request() (a silent no-op once permanently denied), leaving a disabled-Continue dead-end with the implemented openAppSettings() never invoked. Difference is REAL and correctly characterized.

**🟠 [High] Notification permission - Continue button hard-gating dead-end — Both gate Continue on permission, but KMP lacks native's settings-redirect escape hatch, worsening the dead-end** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes (gated, with escape) - ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:151 Button enabled = hasNotificationPermission.value; recovery via openAppSettings() on permanent deny (line 83)
- **KMP:** Partial - ThemeScreen.kt:402 enabled = onRequestNotificationPermission == null \|\| hasNotificationPermission; same gating, no openAppSettings recovery
- **Explanation:** Continue is permission-gated identically. In native this is survivable because permanent denial triggers the App Settings redirect. In KMP the same gating plus the missing redirect means a user who picks Don't-ask-again can never enable Continue and cannot complete onboarding. The gating is at parity; the consequence diverges due to the missing recovery path.
- **Suggested fix:** Restore the openAppSettings recovery path, or reconsider hard-gating Continue on a permission declared required=false. No implementation now.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — composeApp app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/onboarding/theme_selection/ThemeSelectionScreen.kt: Continue gated at line 151 `enabled = hasNotificationPermission.value`. Auto-launches POST_NOTIFICATIONS on first composition (LaunchedEffect lines 88-96). ESCAPE HATCH: the RequestPermission result callback (lines 66-85) detects permanent denial — `if (!granted && SDK>=TIRAMISU && !ActivityCompat.shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale(...))` (lines 76-82) — and calls `context.openAppSettings()` (line 83), defined at lines 209-213 launching Settings.ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS. So a Don't-ask-again user is redirected to App Settings to manually enable, then can return and grant. KMP — onboarding step 2 (Screen.Theme) routes to ThemeSelectionScreenRoute (composeApp/.../App.kt:417-419), NOT the ungated ThemeReworkScreenRoute. ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt passes non-null callback (line 172 `onRequestNotificationPermission = { permissionRequester.request() }`) and `hasNotificationPermission = hasPermission` (line 171), plus auto-launch (lines 161-166). ui/.../themepicker/ThemeScreen.kt:402 gates Continue `enabled = onRequestNotificationPermission == null \|\| hasNotificationPermission`; because the callback is non-null here, this collapses to `hasNotificationPermission` — IDENTICAL gating to native line 151. MISSING RECOVERY (key divergence): The Android requester actual composeApp/src/androidMain/.../core/platform/RememberNotificationPermissionRequester.android.kt result callback (lines 117-119) only does `hasPermission.value = granted` — NO shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale check, NO permanent-deny detection. The `openAppSettings()` method EXISTS on the interface (shared/.../core/platform/NotificationPermissionRequester.kt:37) and IS implemented in the Android actual (lines 134-140, ACTION_APPLICATION_DETAILS_SETTINGS), but grep across the entire non-native KMP tree shows ZERO call sites of openAppSettings() — it is wired-in dead code. Neither ThemeSelectionScreenRoute nor ThemeScreen ever invokes it. Net user-facing effect: a Don't-ask-again denial leaves Continue permanently disabled with no in-app path to re-enable, dead-ending onboarding.

**🟡 [Medium] Notification permission grant row - visibility — Native always renders the grant row; KMP renders it only while permission is denied** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes (always) - ThemeSelector.kt:86-130 unconditionally renders the Enable Notifications title + description + Grant button regardless of permission state
- **KMP:** Partial (conditional) - ThemeScreen.kt:396-398 renders NotificationPermissionRow only when onRequestNotificationPermission != null and not hasNotificationPermission
- **Explanation:** Native shows the explanation + Grant button at all times on the Theme step, even after granting (button no-ops on re-tap). KMP hides the row once permission is granted, causing a layout reflow/jump. Noticeable behavioral/layout divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Render the row unconditionally to match native (only gate Continue), or accept and document the divergence. Do not implement now.

**🟡 [Medium] iOS notification permission - authorization never requested — KMP iOS models permission as implicitly granted and relies on a launch-time request absent from iosApp** _(Permissions)_

- **Native:** N/A - native is Android-only, no iOS counterpart (KMP-introduced surface)
- **KMP:** Partial/stub - RememberNotificationPermissionRequester.ios.kt:21-32 returns hasPermission = MutableStateFlow(true), request()/openAppSettings() are no-ops. KDoc (lines 12-16) and the shared interface KDoc (NotificationPermissionRequester.kt:9-11) claim the iOS app shell requests UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorizationWithOptions at launch, but a grep across /iosApp finds zero occurrences - the launch-time request is never wired
- **Explanation:** On iOS the requester always reports granted and never prompts, assuming a launch-time authorization request that does not exist anywhere in iosApp. iOS notifications would silently never gain authorization. Incomplete/stubbed migration surface scoped to the not-yet-shipping iOS target.
- **Suggested fix:** Wire a real UNUserNotificationCenter.requestAuthorizationWithOptions (in the iosApp shell at launch or in the iOS actual request()) and back hasPermission with the real status. Do not implement now.

**🟡 [Medium] Notification permission - denial toast trigger semantics — Native fires the denial toast in the result callback; KMP fires it via a LaunchedEffect keyed on (hasPermission, autoRequested)** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes - ThemeSelectionScreen.kt:70-72: Toast.makeText(..., you_need_to_enable_notifications, LENGTH_LONG) fired only inside the RequestPermission result lambda when not-granted
- **KMP:** Partial - ThemeSelectionScreenRoute.kt:155-159: LaunchedEffect(hasPermission, autoRequested.value){ if(autoRequested.value and not-hasPermission) toastShower.showLong(deniedMessage) }
- **Explanation:** Same string and long duration, but the trigger model differs. Native fires once per actual denial event. KMP fires from a LaunchedEffect re-running on key change; since autoRequested flips true on first composition while hasPermission is already false, it can fire on entering the screen and re-fire on recomposition/config-change re-entry, surfacing the toast when native would not.
- **Suggested fix:** Drive the toast from the permission-result callback (expose a one-shot denied event from the requester) so it fires once per denial like native. Do not implement now.

### Notifications & Background Work  `notifications-background`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 13 (🔴1 🟠3 🟡3 ⚪6)

> Native uses Hilt-injected helpers (NotificationHelper singleton + ChapterNotificationHelper), WorkManager workers (LibraryRefreshWorker foreground worker, CbzMigrationWorker, the active DownloadWorkerV2 + DownloadCancelReceiver, plus a commented-out MangaDownloadWorker and a debug NotificationWorker), and an FCM service (MyFirebaseMessagingService) that actually displays notifications and stubs token registration. KMP splits this across a :platform NotificationPresenter/PushTokenProvider/BackgroundJobScheduler SPI (Android/iOS/Desktop actuals), Koin-bound workers in :app (LibraryRefreshWorker, CbzMigrationWorker, ChapterNotificationHelper) and :shared/androidMain (DownloadWorkerV2), with scheduling driven by LibraryRefreshRepositoryImpl through the platform BackgroundJobScheduler. The library-refresh and chapter-download foreground worker paths are faithfully ported (same channels, IDs, batching, foreground types). However several behaviors regressed: the KMP MyFirebaseMessagingService is a completely empty stub (no onMessageReceived display, no onNewToken token bridge), the KMP DownloadCancelReceiver is an empty no-op so notification Cancel actions do nothing, the native NotificationHelper's generic message channel / FCM display path is replaced by a NotificationPresenter SPI with a placeholder icon and no real consumers, and the NotificationPresenter Android actual posts to a generic "default" channel without creating it. Periodic background refresh is commented out in both (parity) and only a manual one-off refresh path exists.

**🔴 [Critical] FCM push messaging - incoming message display — KMP FCM service does not display received push notifications** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes - MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:20-28 overrides onMessageReceived, extracts title/body from remote.notification or remote.data (defaults 'Hello' / 'You've got a message'), and calls helper.showNotification(this, title, body) which posts to the firebase_messages IMPORTANCE_HIGH channel with ic_message icon.
- **KMP:** No - app/.../firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:9 is an empty stub: `class MyFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService()` with no onMessageReceived override. Its own postscript (lines 13-26) admits it is a behavioral no-op. The manifest (app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:90-96) still routes com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT to it, so data-only/foreground FCM pushes are silently dropped.
- **Explanation:** Any FCM data message or foreground notification message that the app is expected to render itself is silently discarded in KMP. Native renders it via NotificationHelper.showNotification. This breaks the entire app-messaging / announcement push feature when the app is in the foreground or when data-only messages are sent. There is no consumer anywhere in KMP that displays an FCM payload (NotificationPresenter.show has zero non-DI callers).
- **Suggested fix:** Port onMessageReceived into the KMP MyFirebaseMessagingService: resolve a notification presenter (e.g. the :platform NotificationPresenter via GlobalContext.get, mirroring DownloadWorkerV2's GlobalContext pattern), ensure an IMPORTANCE_HIGH 'firebase_messages'/'App Messages' channel exists, and post title/body with the ic_message icon and the same fallback strings as native.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:20-28 overrides onMessageReceived(remote: RemoteMessage), extracts title = remote.notification?.title ?: remote.data["title"] ?: "Hello" and body = remote.notification?.body ?: remote.data["body"] ?: "You've got a message" (lines 23-24), then calls helper.showNotification(this, title, body) (line 27). The injected helper is NotificationHelper (line 13). native-app/.../core/util/notification/NotificationHelper.kt:128-143 showNotification builds on CHANNEL_ID_MESSAGES = "firebase_messages" (line 19), a channel created with NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_HIGH (lines 41-45) using ic_message small icon (line 131). Helper initialized in native MyApp.kt:51 (NotificationHelper.init(this)). Native manifest (native-app/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:85-94) routes com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT to the service. KMP: app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:9 is exactly `class MyFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService()` with NO onMessageReceived and NO onNewToken override (verified: the only onMessageReceived/RemoteMessage occurrences anywhere in KMP are inside this same file's comment block, lines 18/20/29/36). The KDoc (lines 5-9) and §253 postscript (lines 11-41) explicitly classify it as a "LIVE-HOST stub ... behavioral no-op" with payload handling deferred. KMP manifest app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:90-96 still routes com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT to this stub (default_notification_icon meta-data at lines 98-100), so data-only/foreground FCM pushes are silently dropped. NO FCM CONSUMER: NotificationPresenter.show is declared at platform/src/commonMain/.../notification/NotificationPresenter.kt:59 with three actuals (AndroidNotificationPresenter.kt:31, IosNotificationPresenter, DesktopNotificationPresenter) and is DI-registered in shared/.../PlatformModule.{android,ios,desktop}.kt (e.g. android line 126). It has ZERO functional callers: grep for presenter.show / get<NotificationPresenter>().show / .show(id returned nothing. The only MyApp.kt reference (line 120) merely eagerly primes the Koin singleton; it never renders an FCM payload. Minor note: AndroidNotificationPresenter.show uses placeholder icon android.R.drawable.ic_dialog_info (line 38) not ic_message — moot since nothing invokes it. Line-number nuance: claim cites KMP stub at line 9 (correct), manifest 90-96 (correct), native 20-28 (correct). All key references check out.

**🟠 [High] FCM push messaging - token registration (onNewToken) — KMP FCM service never forwards new tokens; PushTokenBroadcaster is never fed** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Partial - MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:15-18 overrides onNewToken(token) (body is a commented-out 'ApiClient.registerFcmToken(token)' placeholder, but the override exists as the integration seam).
- **KMP:** No - the empty stub service does not override onNewToken at all. AndroidPushTokenProvider.observeTokens (platform/.../push/AndroidPushTokenProvider.kt:42-56) explicitly expects MyFirebaseMessagingService.onNewToken to call PushTokenBroadcaster.publish(token) (documented at PushTokenProvider.kt:11-13 and AndroidPushTokenProvider.kt:19-21), but nothing ever calls publish(). Token rotations after the initial getToken() emit are never observed.
- **Explanation:** The KMP push-token plumbing is wired on the provider side (observeTokens forwards PushTokenBroadcaster.tokens) but the producer side is missing: onNewToken is never overridden, so PushTokenBroadcaster.publish is never invoked. Subscribers to observeTokens() get only the one-shot initial token and never see FCM token rotations (app reinstall, GCM re-registration). This is a designed-but-unconnected seam.
- **Suggested fix:** Override onNewToken(token) in the KMP MyFirebaseMessagingService and call me.manga.kira.platform.push.PushTokenBroadcaster.publish(token), as the provider/KDoc contract requires.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:15-18 — onNewToken(token) IS overridden but its body is only `super.onNewToken(token)` + a commented placeholder `// e.g., ApiClient.registerFcmToken(token)`. KMP: app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:9 declares `class MyFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService()` with an EMPTY body — no onNewToken (and no onMessageReceived) override (the only `onNewToken` strings in the file are in its own KDoc, lines 18/21/31). Manifest still registers it: app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:91,94 (service name + MESSAGING_EVENT intent-filter). Provider side: platform/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/platform/push/AndroidPushTokenProvider.kt:42-56 — observeTokens() trySend(initial) at line 49 (one-shot getToken) then collects PushTokenBroadcaster.tokens at line 53; PushTokenBroadcaster.publish(token) is defined at line 76. Tree-wide grep for `PushTokenBroadcaster.publish`/`onNewToken` (excluding native-app) returns ONLY KDoc/comment matches (AndroidPushTokenProvider.kt:21 & 129; PushTokenProvider.kt:13/33) — publish() is never invoked from executable code anywhere in :app/:platform/:shared/:ui/:presentation/:domain/:data. The documented contract (PushTokenProvider.kt:11-13; AndroidPushTokenProvider.kt:19-21,64-69) says MyFirebaseMessagingService.onNewToken should call PushTokenBroadcaster.publish(token), but no override does. MyApp.kt:119-123 only eagerly constructs it, but AndroidNotificationPresenter has no channel-creation side effect on construction.

Ensure whatever channel is used is actually created and uses a branded icon.

**🟡 [Medium] NotificationPresenter (Android) - channel creation & icon — KMP Android NotificationPresenter posts to an uncreated channel and uses a placeholder system icon** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes - native always posts to channels it created (NotificationHelper.init creates manga_downloads + firebase_messages; ChapterNotificationHelper/LibraryRefreshWorker create their own) and uses branded icons (R.drawable.ic_launcher_foreground, R.drawable.ic_message).

**🟡 [Medium] ChapterNotificationHelper - localized strings & channel name — New-chapter notification text and channel name/description are hardcoded English in KMP** _(Localization/RTL)_

**⚪ [Low] DownloadWorkerV2 - dependency injection mechanism — KMP DownloadWorkerV2 resolves dependencies via GlobalContext.get() lazily instead of constructor injection** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes - native DownloadWorkerV2 is @HiltWorker @AssistedInject with constructor params (downloadRepo, chapterDownloadDao, chapterDao, chapterDownloadService) provided by Hilt's worker factory at construction time.
- **KMP:** Partial - shared/.../test2/DownloadWorkerV2.kt:78-90 has only (Context, WorkerParameters) ctor and resolves chapterDownloadDao/chapterDao/mangaDao/chapterDownloadService/sourcesRepository lazily via `koin.get()` from GlobalContext (lines 84-90). It is NOT registered via workerOf(::DownloadWorkerV2) (KDoc lines 46-57 acknowledge this), relying on the default WorkManager factory fallback.
- **Explanation:** Behaviorally equivalent at runtime (same dependency graph), but the worker now depends on GlobalContext being initialized when WorkManager reflectively instantiates it. If WorkManager ever auto-initializes the worker before Koin starts (e.g. process restart for pending work before MyApp.onCreate completes Koin), the lazy koin.get() could throw. Native's Hilt factory guaranteed deps at construction. Minor robustness/architecture divergence.
- **Suggested fix:** Register the worker with workerOf(::DownloadWorkerV2) in a Koin module and convert the lazy GlobalContext.get() fields to constructor parameters, matching the LibraryRefreshWorker/CbzMigrationWorker pattern already used in appKoinModule.

- **Suggested fix:** Collapse the duplicate catch into a single block (or differentiate the exception types) in the KMP DownloadWorkerV2; harmless but dead code.

**⚪ [Low] Library refresh worker - last-updated timestamp source — KMP persists library_last_updated using kotlinx-datetime LocalDateTime instead of java.time.LocalDateTime** _(API/Data)_

### Ads / Monetization  `ads-monetization`

**Parity verdict:** MissingInKmp  ·  **Findings:** 13 (🔴4 🟠3 🟡4 ⚪2)

> The native app (source of truth) ships a complete AdMob monetization system: an AdConfig with 3 production ad unit IDs (rewarded/native/banner) plus Google test IDs and retry/backoff/interval constants; an AdCoordinator that initializes MobileAds and preloads ads; a RewardedAdManager with preload, exponential-backoff retry and show-timeout safety; a NativeAdQueue with a pooled (5/max 10) serial-loading queue and SDK-based impression tracking with no-fill/rate-limit backoff; Compose BannerAdView/AdaptiveBannerAdView placed in the Details header, Reader last page, Library header, Search, and MultiRepo results; a NativeAdListItem rendered via an XML layout with shimmer; interleaveAds/interleaveAdsCustom that weave native ads into Home (interval 5) and Search lists; an AdViewModel that gates downloads behind a rewarded ad every 6 chapters and shows a rewarded ad on bulk download; a full UMP/GDPR consent flow run in MainActivity.onCreate that gates ad initialization; and AdMob mediation adapters (inMobi, ironSource, Vungle, Facebook). The KMP app implements almost none of this at runtime. It has only a relocation-scaffold AdProvider facade (interstitial/rewarded/banner) and a ConsentFlowClient, both bound in Koin but with activityProvider = { null } so every fullscreen show returns Failed and the consent flow no-ops; neither is referenced by any presentation/domain/ui/data code, the BuildConfig ad unit IDs are defined but never read, and there is no banner placement, no native ad, no list interleaving, no download-count ad gating, and no consent invocation anywhere. The KMP App.kt KDoc itself documents AdViewModel plumbing as deferred/stubbed. Net effect: the entire ad-monetization surface present in native is absent from the KMP UI — a complete revenue/feature regression on the migrated app.

**🔴 [Critical] Rewarded ad on download (gating) — Download-count rewarded-ad gating is entirely absent in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — AdViewModel.onDownloadStarted (AdViewModel.kt:96-163) increments a persisted download counter and, when newCount % AdConfig.DOWNLOAD_AD_INTERVAL == 0 (interval = 6, AdConfig.kt:61), shows a rewarded ad before proceeding; called from LibraryMangaRoute.kt:146 and NotificationsRoute.kt:45.
- **KMP:** No — grep for onDownloadStarted / shouldShowAd / DOWNLOAD_AD_INTERVAL / downloaded_chapters_count across domain/data/presentation/ui/composeApp/shared/app returns zero matches. composeApp/App.kt:119,129 explicitly state AdViewModel plumbing is 'deferred / stubbed pending ad-network expect/actual'. KMP DownloadsScreenRoute/download flow proceeds with no ad.
- **Explanation:** This is a core monetization flow on the source-of-truth app: every 6th chapter download forces a rewarded interstitial whose reward unlocks the download. In KMP the download simply proceeds with no ad, so the rewarded-ad revenue stream and the gating UX are completely gone. The AdProvider facade exists but no caller invokes loadRewarded/showRewarded for downloads.
- **Suggested fix:** Port AdViewModel's counter+threshold logic (persist count via DataStore/SecureStorage, threshold % 6) into a presentation-layer use case that calls AdProvider.loadRewarded(BANNER/REWARDED unit id)/showRewarded() and gates the download on AdResult.EarnedReward, wiring it into the KMP download initiation path.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). NATIVE (source of truth) — claim verified exactly as stated: - AdViewModel.onDownloadStarted at native-app/.../ad_mob/AdViewModel.kt:96-163 launches an IO coroutine, reads getDownloadedChaptersCount() (L136), computes newCount = currentCount + 1 (L137), and if shouldShowAd(newCount) (L140) calls showRewardedAdForDownload(context, newCount, onProceed, onBlocked). - shouldShowAd (AdViewModel.kt:285-286): `downloadedCount > 0 && downloadedCount % AdConfig.DOWNLOAD_AD_INTERVAL == 0`. - AdConfig.DOWNLOAD_AD_INTERVAL = 6 at native-app/.../ad_mob/AdConfig.kt:61. - Persisted counter via DataStore key "downloaded_chapters_count" (AdViewModel.kt:340), read/written by getDownloadedChaptersCount()/saveDownloadedChaptersCount() (L288-305). - showRewardedAdForDownload (AdViewModel.kt:180-240) calls rewardedAdManager.show(context); only RewardEarned (L214-223), Failed (L228-237), or ad-not-ready (L193-204) call onProceed(); Dismissed (L224-227) calls onBlocked?.invoke() — i.e. the reward gates the download. - Call sites confirmed: native-app/.../navigation/routes/LibraryMangaRoute.kt:146 and NotificationsRoute.kt:45 both call adViewModel.onDownloadStarted(context, onProceed = {}). KMP — claim verified: - grep for onDownloadStarted / shouldShowAd / DOWNLOAD_AD_INTERVAL / downloaded_chapters_count / getDownloadsUntilNextAd / resetDownloadCounter across ui, presentation, domain, data, shared, platform, composeApp, app returns ZERO matches. - composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/App.kt:119-121,129 state AdViewModel plumbing is deferred / 'stubbed pending ad-network expect/actual'. - KMP download flow has no ad gate: DetailsViewModel.kt:536-544 onDownloadChapter() calls enqueueChapterDownload(...) directly; EnqueueChapterDownloadUseCase.kt:28 and EnqueueDownloadUseCase.kt:110 are pure pass-throughs to DownloadsActionRepository.enqueueDownload (no counter, no ad logic — grep for ad/reward/interstitial/count in those files matched only KDoc/substrings). - Nuance (also as claimed): an AdProvider facade DOES exist (platform/src/commonMain/.../ads/AdProvider.kt:22-23 declares loadRewarded/showRewarded) and AndroidAdProvider.kt:116,142 implements them, but it is only bound in DI (single<AdProvider> in PlatformModule.android/ios/desktop.kt) and never invoked by any download caller — no loadRewarded/showRewarded call exists outside the platform impls themselves.

### Play Update / Review / Consent  `play-update-review-consent`

**Parity verdict:** ParityLow  ·  **Findings:** 15 (🔴4 🟠7 🟡1 ⚪3)

> Native implements three Play Core flows that all fire at app launch: AppUpdateHelper (flexible in-app update checked in MainActivity.onCreate, with InstallStateUpdatedListener for download progress, resumeUpdate in onResume, onActivityResult for request code 100, and an immediate-update branch); ReviewManagerHelper (in-app review gated behind a persisted first-open timestamp and a ~20-day elapsed threshold before requestReviewFlow/launchReviewFlow); and a UMP consent flow in MainActivity (requestConsentInfoUpdate → loadConsentForm → form.show when REQUIRED, then MobileAds.initialize gated on canRequestAds()). The KMP app relocated all three into :platform SPIs (AppUpdateClient, InAppReviewClient, ConsentFlowClient) with full Android actuals bound in shared/PlatformModule.android.kt, but the actual user-facing behavior is almost entirely missing: a repo-wide grep shows ZERO live call sites of checkForUpdate/startFlexibleUpdate/completeUpdate/requestReview/requestConsentInfoUpdate/loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired/canRequestAds anywhere outside native-app and the implementations themselves. MyApp only constructs AppUpdateClient (Play Core handshake) and never triggers a check; the thin MainActivity has no onResume/onActivityResult/onDestroy; the review eligibility/timing logic is entirely absent; consent is never invoked and MobileAds is initialized unconditionally without consent gating. Compounding this, all three Android facades are bound with the default ForegroundActivityProvider { null }, so even if invoked they would short-circuit to false/UNKNOWN because no foreground Activity is ever supplied (the rework graph explicitly defers Activity wiring to 'Phase 11'). The audit-trail KDocs claiming these clients are 'not yet bound in any rework Koin module' are themselves stale/incorrect — they are bound in shared/PlatformModule.android.kt:149-151 — but bound-yet-never-called and never given an Activity. Net effect: the in-app update, in-app review, and UMP consent features are functionally regressed to non-operational on Android.
