<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Play Update / Review / Consent</summary>

**🔴 [Critical] In-app update (Play Core) — flow invocation / wiring — KMP never triggers the in-app update flow; the update check that native runs on every launch is absent** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../MainActivity.kt:278-288 calls AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate(activity=this, immediate=updateType) inside onCreate on every launch; AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate (google_play_cores/app_update/AppUpdateHelper.kt:40-71) queries appUpdateInfo and, on UPDATE_AVAILABLE, auto-starts the flexible update flow via startUpdate→startUpdateFlowForResult.
- **KMP:** No (effectively) — AppUpdateClient.checkForUpdate()/startFlexibleUpdate() are implemented in AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:36-73 and bound in shared/.../PlatformModule.android.kt:149, but a repo-wide grep shows ZERO call sites of checkForUpdate()/startFlexibleUpdate() outside native-app and the impl itself. app/.../MyApp.kt:115 only does get<AppUpdateClient>() to construct the Play Core manager; it never calls checkForUpdate. App.kt (composeApp) has no update references.
- **Explanation:** On native, opening the app automatically checks Play for an available update and launches the flexible update consent dialog when one exists. In KMP, the AppUpdateClient singleton is constructed at startup (Play Core handshake only) but no method that actually checks for or starts an update is ever invoked anywhere in the live graph (commonMain App, presentation, domain, data, or the Android host). The entire user-facing in-app update experience is therefore gone in the migration even though the SPI plumbing exists.
- **Suggested fix:** In the Android host (MyApp/MainActivity or an App-level LaunchedEffect), inject AppUpdateClient and call checkForUpdate() then startFlexibleUpdate()/handle immediate on launch, replicating native MainActivity.onCreate lines 278-313. Ensure it runs once per launch with a foreground Activity available.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). NATIVE (source of truth) triggers the in-app update flow on every launch: - native-app/.../me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:278-288 — inside onCreate(), AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate(activity=this, immediate=updateType=false, onUpdateNotAvailable, onError). updateType is declared at MainActivity.kt:197 (flexible by default). - native-app/.../google_play_cores/app_update/AppUpdateHelper.kt:40-71 — checkForUpdate awaits manager.appUpdateInfo and on success calls handleUpdateInfo (lines 73-107), which on UpdateAvailability.UPDATE_AVAILABLE auto-invokes startUpdate (lines 109-133) → appUpdateManager.startUpdateFlowForResult(info, FLEXIBLE, activity, REQUEST_CODE=100). Native also wires the full lifecycle: registerListener (MainActivity.kt:304), resumeUpdate in onResume (MainActivity.kt:889), completeUpdate, onActivityResult (899), unregisterListener (929), and AppUpdateHelper.init(this) in native MyApp.kt:27. KMP: the SPI exists and is bound, but is NEVER invoked in the live graph: - platform/.../platform/update/AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:36-73 implements checkForUpdate()/startFlexibleUpdate() (real Play Core delegation). - shared/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:149 binds single<AppUpdateClient> { AndroidAppUpdateClient(androidContext()) }. Note: it passes the DEFAULT activityProvider = { null } (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:30; PlatformModule.android.kt:146-147 comment "activityProvider stays { null } until Phase 11"), so startFlexibleUpdate would early-return false (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:54-57) even if called. - app/.../MyApp.kt:114-118 only does get<AppUpdateClient>() (eager construction = Play Core manager handshake only); it never calls checkForUpdate/startFlexibleUpdate. The KDoc at MyApp.kt:38-42 explicitly states this replaces only AppUpdateHelper.init(this), not the launch-time check. - Repo-wide grep (excluding native-app): ZERO method-invocation call sites of .checkForUpdate() or .startFlexibleUpdate() — every match outside native-app is the interface decl (AppUpdateClient.kt:24,27), the 3 platform impls (Android/iOS/Desktop), or KDoc prose. No AppUpdateClient reference in :presentation, :domain, :data, or :ui. composeApp/.../App.kt has no Play Core update references (its "Updates" routes are the manga new-chapters feature, unrelated). Minor framing nit (does not change verdict): the legacy :shared me.manga.kira.core.update.AppUpdateClient twin referenced in the source files' audit-trail postscripts (and the claim's mention of PlatformModule.android.kt:123) no longer exists — find for */core/update/* returns nothing; the only live AppUpdateClient is the :platform one bound at line 149. This strengthens rather than weakens the finding.

**🔴 [Critical] In-app update — foreground Activity wiring (ForegroundActivityProvider) — AndroidAppUpdateClient is bound with no ForegroundActivityProvider, so startFlexibleUpdate() can never obtain an Activity and always returns false** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — native passes the concrete Activity (this) directly into AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate/startUpdateFlowForResult (MainActivity.kt:278, AppUpdateHelper.kt:119-124), so the Play Store update dialog can actually be shown.
- **KMP:** No — shared/.../PlatformModule.android.kt:149 binds single<AppUpdateClient> { AndroidAppUpdateClient(androidContext()) } with only context; the activityProvider parameter defaults to { null } (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:30). startFlexibleUpdate() at lines 54-57 short-circuits to false when activityProvider() is null. Grep confirms ForegroundActivityProvider is never bound to a real Activity anywhere (only default { null } usages and KDoc).
- **Explanation:** Even if a caller were added, the update flow could never launch because no foreground Activity is supplied. HideNavigationBarSideEffect.kt:33 explicitly documents that the Koin-backed ForegroundActivityProvider is 'unavailable to the rework graph until Phase 11'. This makes the entire Activity-bound Play Core surface (update, review, consent) non-functional on Android.
- **Suggested fix:** Implement an ActivityHolder (WeakReference to current Activity, registered via ActivityLifecycleCallbacks in MyApp) and bind the four Phase-5.z facades with that provider, e.g. AndroidAppUpdateClient(androidContext()) { ActivityHolder.current }, as the KDoc's '{ MainActivity.current?.get() }' pattern intends.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). NATIVE (source of truth): MainActivity.kt:95 `class MainActivity : AppCompatActivity()` is a real Activity; MainActivity.kt:278-280 `AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate(activity = this, immediate = updateType, ...)` passes the concrete Activity; AppUpdateHelper.kt:40-41 `checkForUpdate(activity: Activity, ...)` and AppUpdateHelper.kt:119-124 `appUpdateManager.startUpdateFlowForResult(info, type, activity, REQUEST_CODE)` actually launch the Play Store dialog. Native claim verified correct. KMP: AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:30 `private val activityProvider: ForegroundActivityProvider = { null }`; AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:53-57 `startFlexibleUpdate()` does `val activity = activityProvider() ?: run { log.w { "startFlexibleUpdate: no foreground Activity available" }; return false }`; PlatformModule.android.kt:149 `single<AppUpdateClient> { AndroidAppUpdateClient(androidContext()) }` passes only context, so activityProvider stays the default `{ null }`. ForegroundActivityProvider.kt:30 is just `typealias = () -> Activity?`. Repo-wide grep (excluding native-app) finds AndroidAppUpdateClient constructed ONLY at PlatformModule.android.kt:149 (context-only) — it is never given a real Activity; HideNavigationBarSideEffect.kt:33 documents the Koin ForegroundActivityProvider is unavailable until Phase 11. So startFlexibleUpdate() can only ever short-circuit to false. Claim verified. Two framing corrections (do not refute the claim): (1) The rework client IS constructed/eager-init'd — MyApp.kt:12 imports `me.manga.kira.platform.update.AppUpdateClient` and MyApp.kt:115 `get<AppUpdateClient>()` resolves the PlatformModule.android.kt:149 binding (Play Core manager inits). The audit-trail postscript at AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:105-112 claiming a separate LIVE legacy `:shared` `core.update.AppUpdateClient` twin and "zero composeApp hits / binding pending" is itself stale: `find` shows no `shared/.../core/update/AppUpdateClient.kt` exists, and MyApp.kt binds the platform interface directly. (2) Beyond the missing Activity, there is NO caller of startFlexibleUpdate() or checkForUpdate() anywhere in presentation/domain/ui — MyApp.kt:115 only primes the singleton via get(), never invoking the flow. So the in-app-update feature is wholly non-functional/absent in the rework on Android, while fully working in native. Net regression confirmed.

**🔴 [Critical] In-app review — flow invocation — KMP never launches the in-app review flow that native runs on launch** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onCreate launches reviewScope.launch { launchInAppReviewSafely() } (MainActivity.kt:299-301), which calls reviewHelper.launchInAppReview(this) (MainActivity.kt:534-544). ReviewManagerHelper.launchInAppReview (ReviewManagerHelper.kt:76-90) gates on shouldShowReview() then runs requestReviewFlow()+launchReviewFlow().
- **KMP:** No (effectively) — InAppReviewClient.requestReview() is implemented (AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:32-45) and bound (PlatformModule.android.kt:150), but grep shows ZERO live call sites of requestReview() anywhere outside native-app and the impl. App.kt and MyApp.kt never invoke it; there is no domain/presentation wrapper.
- **Explanation:** The native app proactively shows the Google in-app review dialog after a usage threshold. In KMP the review client is bound in Koin but nothing ever calls requestReview(), so users are never prompted to review. The whole in-app review feature is absent from the live flow.
- **Suggested fix:** Inject InAppReviewClient and call requestReview() at an appropriate launch point after the review-eligibility gate (see next finding) is reintroduced; also wire ForegroundActivityProvider so the review surface can actually show.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). NATIVE (source of truth) — in-app review IS wired into the live launch flow: native-app/.../me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:98 injects `lateinit var reviewHelper: ReviewManagerHelper` (Hilt); :108 defines `reviewScope`; onCreate at :299-301 runs `reviewScope.launch { launchInAppReviewSafely() }`; :534-544 `launchInAppReviewSafely()` calls `reviewHelper.launchInAppReview(this@MainActivity)`; ReviewManagerHelper.kt:76-90 `launchInAppReview` gates on `shouldShowReview()` then runs `manager.requestReviewFlow().await()` + `manager.launchReviewFlow(activity, reviewInfo).await()`. (Note: threshold is `TimeUnit.DAYS.toMillis(20)` = 20 days, ReviewManagerHelper.kt:31, despite the SEVEN_DAYS name — does not affect verdict.) KMP — client exists and is bound but NEVER invoked: platform/.../review/InAppReviewClient.kt:57-64 declares `suspend fun requestReview(): Boolean`; platform/.../androidMain/.../review/AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:32-45 fully implements it via Play Core; shared/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:150 binds `single<InAppReviewClient> { AndroidInAppReviewClient(androidContext()) }` (imports at :49-50). Repo-wide `grep requestReview` excluding native-app returns ONLY the interface decl, the 3 platform impls (android/ios/desktop), and doc/audit comments — zero call sites. `grep -rn "Review"` across :domain :presentation :ui :data :composeApp :app returns 0 matches. App.kt, MyApp.kt, and KMP MainActivity.kt (app/.../MainActivity.kt, 58 lines) contain no review reference; KMP MainActivity.onCreate (:19-22) only installs splash + renders App(). There is no domain/presentation wrapper around requestReview(). (Aside: the audit-trail comment in AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:64-75 claiming a still-bound legacy :shared expect-class shadow SPI is itself stale — no legacy :shared review code exists; the :platform facade is the only thing bound. Also the Android binding uses default activityProvider={null}, so even if called today it would return false early — but the operative fact is it is never called.)

**🔴 [Critical] UMP consent flow — invocation — KMP never runs the UMP consent flow that native runs on launch before ads** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onCreate launches requestConsent(this) on Dispatchers.IO (MainActivity.kt:289-298). requestConsent (lines 428-472) builds ConsentRequestParameters (setTagForUnderAgeOfConsent(false)), calls consentInformation.requestConsentInfoUpdate(...), and on success either loadAndShowForm() (when a form is available) or initializeAds(); loadAndShowForm (lines 496-522) shows the form only when consentStatus==REQUIRED.
- **KMP:** No (effectively) — ConsentFlowClient (requestConsentInfoUpdate/loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired/canRequestAds) is implemented (AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:42-87) and bound (PlatformModule.android.kt:151), but grep shows ZERO live call sites of any of these methods outside native-app and the impl. App.kt/MyApp.kt never invoke the consent flow.
- **Explanation:** The native app runs the GDPR/UMP consent flow at startup and only initializes ads afterward. In KMP the consent client is bound but never invoked anywhere in the live graph, so the EEA consent form is never requested or shown. This is both a feature regression and a potential compliance problem.
- **Suggested fix:** At Android startup (before/around MobileAds init), inject ConsentFlowClient, call requestConsentInfoUpdate() then loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired(), and gate ad init on canRequestAds(), replicating native requestConsent/loadAndShowForm/initializeAds. Wire ForegroundActivityProvider so the form can render.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). NATIVE (source of truth) /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt: onCreate launches requestConsent(this@MainActivity) on Dispatchers.IO (line 291, inside the CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO).launch block at 289-298). requestConsent (lines 428-472) builds ConsentRequestParameters with setTagForUnderAgeOfConsent(false) (line 444) and calls consentInformation.requestConsentInfoUpdate(...) (line 454); on success it calls loadAndShowForm(activity) when isConsentFormAvailable (line 461) else initializeAds(activity) (line 464). loadAndShowForm (lines 496-522) shows the form only when consentStatus==REQUIRED (lines 503-510). initializeAds (line 524) gates MobileAds.initialize behind consentInformation.canRequestAds() (lines 526-527). So native runs the full UMP/GDPR flow at launch and only inits ads afterward. KMP: The consent client IS implemented at /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/platform/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/platform/consent/AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:42-87 (requestConsentInfoUpdate, loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired, canRequestAds) and IS bound at /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/shared/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/PlatformModule.android.kt:151 (single<ConsentFlowClient> { AndroidConsentFlowClient(androidContext()) }). But it is NEVER invoked: an exhaustive grep for .requestConsentInfoUpdate( / .loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired( / .canRequestAds( across the whole repo (excluding native-app) returns matches ONLY inside AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt itself (lines 49, 69, 80 — the impl delegating to the UMP SDK). No file in :presentation, :domain, :ui, :data, :composeApp, or :app injects or references ConsentFlowClient (grep returned zero). KMP MainActivity (/Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MainActivity.kt) is a thin host that only calls App(). composeApp App.kt has no consent/ads references. Critically, MyApp.onCreate (/Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MyApp.kt:133) calls MobileAds.initialize(this) DIRECTLY with no consent gating whatsoever. Also AndroidConsentFlowClient activityProvider defaults to { null } (line 35), so even if called it would short-circuit to UNKNOWN/false. The KMP file's own postscript (AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:99-114) corroborates the binding is staged awaiting a Phase 11 cutover. Only minor citation nit: native launch call is at line 291 (claim said 289-298, which is the enclosing block — immaterial). Net effect is slightly worse than claimed: ads are initialized unconditionally while the EEA consent form is never requested/shown — feature regression plus GDPR/UMP compliance gap.

**🟠 [High] In-app update — resumeUpdate on onResume — Native resumes/completes a downloaded flexible update on every onResume; KMP has no onResume handling** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onResume() (MainActivity.kt:883-897) calls AppUpdateHelper.resumeUpdate(this) which checks installStatus()==DOWNLOADED and calls completeUpdate() to install. resumeUpdate is defined at AppUpdateHelper.kt:149-185.
- **KMP:** No — app/.../MainActivity.kt is a thin shell with only onCreate { setContent { App() } } (lines 18-27); there is no onResume override. AppUpdateClient exposes completeUpdate() (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:75-83) but it is never called in the live graph, and there is no equivalent of resumeUpdate (querying installStatus on resume).
- **Explanation:** A flexible update that finishes downloading while the app is backgrounded is installed in native when the user returns (onResume → resumeUpdate → completeUpdate). KMP drops this entirely: there is no resume-side install completion and no completeUpdate caller, so even a hypothetically-downloaded update would never be installed.
- **Suggested fix:** Add an onResume hook (in MainActivity or a lifecycle-aware effect) that queries the update status and calls AppUpdateClient.completeUpdate() when a flexible download is ready, mirroring native resumeUpdate. Note the SPI lacks a 'query install status' method, so add one or expose resume semantics.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:883-897 overrides onResume() and calls AppUpdateHelper.resumeUpdate(this) { AppUpdateHelper.completeUpdate() }. AppUpdateHelper.resumeUpdate is defined at native-app/.../app_update/AppUpdateHelper.kt:149-185: it awaits appUpdateInfo and, on info.installStatus()==InstallStatus.DOWNLOADED (line 164), invokes onDownloaded() which calls completeUpdate() (defined at lines 255-267 -> appUpdateManager.completeUpdate()). Native also registers an InstallStateUpdatedListener (MainActivity.kt:304-313) that calls completeUpdate() on DOWNLOADED. So a flexible update that finished downloading while backgrounded is installed on return to foreground. KMP: app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MainActivity.kt:18-27 is a thin ComponentActivity with ONLY onCreate { installSplashScreen(); enableEdgeToEdge(); setContent { App() } } — no onResume override at all. completeUpdate()/startFlexibleUpdate()/checkForUpdate() exist only as the AppUpdateClient interface (platform/.../update/AppUpdateClient.kt:22-31) and its actuals (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:75-83 plus iOS/Desktop no-ops at IosAppUpdateClient.kt:28-31, DesktopAppUpdateClient.kt:28-31). A repo-wide grep excluding native-app finds ZERO callers of completeUpdate/startFlexibleUpdate/checkForUpdate in :presentation, :domain, :data, :ui, :composeApp, or :app. The Android client is bound (shared/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:149 single<AppUpdateClient> { AndroidAppUpdateClient(androidContext()) }) and only constructed eagerly at app/.../MyApp.kt:115 get<AppUpdateClient>() — never invoked. No installStatus query on resume, no InstallStateUpdatedListener/registerListener, no onActivityResult plumbing anywhere in KMP. Note: the audit comments citing a legacy :shared/core/update twin are stale — that directory no longer exists (ls confirms absent); the live binding is the :platform actual. Claim's file:line references all verified accurate.

**🟠 [High] In-app update — InstallStateUpdatedListener / download progress — Native registers a Play Core install-state listener (progress + auto-complete on DOWNLOADED); KMP has no listener at all** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.kt:304-313 calls AppUpdateHelper.registerListener(onProgress, onDownloaded={completeUpdate()}); listener impl handles DOWNLOADING (bytesDownloaded/totalBytesToDownload), DOWNLOADED (auto completeUpdate), FAILED (installErrorCode), CANCELED (AppUpdateHelper.kt:190-231). unregisterListener() is called in onDestroy (MainActivity.kt:929).
- **KMP:** No — AppUpdateClient SPI (AppUpdateClient.kt:22-31) exposes only checkForUpdate/startFlexibleUpdate/completeUpdate. There is no registerListener/InstallStateUpdatedListener concept; the commonMain KDoc (AppUpdateClient.kt:16-20) explicitly states the InstallStateUpdatedListener was 'intentionally simplified' away. No progress callback or auto-complete-on-download exists.
- **Explanation:** Native monitors flexible-update download progress and automatically calls completeUpdate() the moment the download finishes (so the install can proceed without waiting for the next onResume). KMP removed the listener API entirely, so there is no download progress feedback and no eager install trigger — the simplified SPI cannot reproduce native behavior even if wired.
- **Suggested fix:** Expand the AppUpdateClient SPI with an install-state flow/listener (e.g. Flow<UpdateInstallState> with DOWNLOADING progress + DOWNLOADED) and register it in the Android actual, then have the host complete the update on DOWNLOADED and unregister on destroy — restoring native registerListener/unregisterListener.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): AppUpdateHelper.kt has a full Play Core install-state listener. registerListener(onProgress, onDownloaded, onFailed) at lines 190-231 builds an InstallStateUpdatedListener (imported line 10) and registers it (line 225), handling DOWNLOADING with state.bytesDownloaded()/state.totalBytesToDownload() -> onProgress (lines 203-208), DOWNLOADED -> onDownloaded (lines 209-212), FAILED with state.installErrorCode() -> onFailed (lines 213-216), and CANCELED (lines 217-219). completeUpdate() at lines 255-267. MainActivity.kt:304-313 calls AppUpdateHelper.registerListener(onProgress = {percent calc}, onDownloaded = { AppUpdateHelper.completeUpdate() }) i.e. auto-completes the install on download finish. MainActivity.kt:929 (inside onDestroy, lines 924-933) calls AppUpdateHelper.unregisterListener() (impl AppUpdateHelper.kt:236-250). Every detail of the native claim verified. KMP: The sole AppUpdateClient is the simplified commonMain SPI at platform/.../update/AppUpdateClient.kt:22-31, exposing only checkForUpdate() (line 24), startFlexibleUpdate() (line 27), completeUpdate() (line 30) — no registerListener, no listener concept. Its KDoc at lines 17-20 explicitly states "The full upstream flow (Activity-bound startUpdateFlowForResult, InstallStateUpdatedListener) is intentionally simplified". The Android actual AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:28-89 implements exactly those three methods via Play Core; it never imports or uses InstallStateUpdatedListener, registerListener, bytesDownloaded, totalBytesToDownload, or installErrorCode, and has no auto-complete-on-download. iOS/Desktop actuals are no-ops. The single interface + 3 actuals are bound via Koin (PlatformModule.android.kt:149, .ios.kt:131, .desktop.kt:131) and consumed at app/.../MyApp.kt:115. Repo-wide grep (excluding native-app) for registerListener/InstallStateUpdatedListener/bytesDownloaded/totalBytesToDownload/installErrorCode found zero functional usages — only the SPI KDoc mentioning what was removed; unrelated onProgress hits are CBZ/download/webview. (Note: the AppUpdateClient.kt audit-trail postscript and AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt §253 block reference a legacy ':shared/core/update/AppUpdateClient' twin, but no such file exists — that prose is stale and does not affect the verdict.) So no progress callback and no eager install trigger exist in KMP, exactly as claimed.

**🟠 [High] In-app update — onActivityResult (request code 100) — Native handles the update flow result (RESULT_OK/CANCELED/failure, finishAffinity for immediate); KMP has no result handling** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onActivityResult (MainActivity.kt:899-922) handles requestCode 100: logs OK, logs CANCELED, and on failure for immediate updates calls finishAffinity() (lines 914-917). REQUEST_CODE=100 in AppUpdateHelper.kt:20.
- **KMP:** No — KMP MainActivity has no onActivityResult override. The commonMain KDoc (AppUpdateClient.kt:18-20, 60-63) says request-code-100/onActivityResult plumbing 'stays in the Android host's Activity callback wiring' — but the Android host (app/.../MainActivity.kt) contains no such wiring. AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:87 defines REQUEST_CODE=100 for startUpdateFlowForResult, but nothing consumes the result.
- **Explanation:** Native observes the outcome of the update consent dialog and, for an immediate update that the user dismisses, terminates the app (finishAffinity). KMP never receives or acts on the update flow result, so cancellation/failure handling (including the immediate-update force-exit) is absent. The KDoc claims the host owns this wiring, but it does not exist.
- **Suggested fix:** Add onActivityResult (or a Registered ActivityResult callback) for request code 100 in the Android host to log/handle OK, CANCELED, and failure, including the immediate-update finishAffinity path, matching native MainActivity.onActivityResult.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: Low). REAL structural difference confirmed. NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/.../me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:899-922 overrides onActivityResult; for requestCode==100 it logs RESULT_OK (905), logs RESULT_CANCELED (908), and in the failure else-branch (911-919) calls finishAffinity() (917) gated on `if (updateType)` (915). updateType is a hardcoded `false` constant (MainActivity.kt:197) passed as immediate=updateType to checkForUpdate (280), so the finishAffinity force-exit is DEAD in practice — only the Log.d/Log.w branches ever run. REQUEST_CODE=100 in AppUpdateHelper.kt:20, used at startUpdateFlowForResult(...,REQUEST_CODE) (119-124). Native MainActivity is AppCompatActivity (line 95). KMP: app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MainActivity.kt is a ComponentActivity with ONLY onCreate (lines 18-27) — NO onActivityResult override (its own audit comment line 51 confirms "only onCreate is overridden"). The only other Activity, CrashActivity.kt (finishAffinity at line 76), is crash-recovery, unrelated to updates. The commonMain KDoc (platform/.../update/AppUpdateClient.kt:17-20, 59-63) and Android impl KDoc (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:24-25, 128-129) both claim the request-code-100/onActivityResult plumbing "stays in the Android host's Activity callback wiring" — FALSE: grep across app/composeApp/ui/presentation/platform/shared finds no such wiring. AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:62-67 calls startUpdateFlowForResult(...,REQUEST_CODE=100 at line 87) so a result CAN be produced but is never consumed. The client IS wired (PlatformModule.android.kt:149 binds AppUpdateClient; MyApp.kt:115 get<AppUpdateClient>() eager-inits Play Core). HOWEVER startFlexibleUpdate() has ZERO callers anywhere in the KMP graph (grep shows only the interface decl + the 3 platform impls, no invocations), so the update consent flow is never even started in KMP — there is no result to handle. The claim's facts are accurate but its High severity overstates impact: native's missing logic is debug logging plus a never-true (updateType=false) force-exit, and KMP's path is unreachable, so there is no observable runtime divergence.

**🟠 [High] In-app review — eligibility timing (first-open + 20-day threshold) — Native gates the review prompt behind a persisted first-open timestamp and an elapsed-time threshold; KMP has no eligibility logic at all** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — ReviewManagerHelper (app_review/ReviewManagerHelper.kt:28-70) persists KEY_FIRST_OPEN_TIME via dataStoreLong; on first read it records System.currentTimeMillis() and returns false; thereafter shouldShowReviewFlow emits true only when (now - firstOpen) >= SEVEN_DAYS_MILLIS, where SEVEN_DAYS_MILLIS = TimeUnit.DAYS.toMillis(20) (line 31 — actually 20 days). launchInAppReview only proceeds when shouldShowReview() is true.
- **KMP:** No — grep for first_open / firstOpenTime / shouldShowReview / has_reviewed / SEVEN_DAYS finds matches ONLY in native-app. The KMP InAppReviewClient.requestReview() (AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:32-45) immediately runs requestReviewFlow/launchReviewFlow with no timing/eligibility gate. No DataStore key for first-open exists in the KMP graph.
- **Explanation:** Native only asks for a review once the user has had the app for ~20 days (the constant is named SEVEN_DAYS but actually uses 20 days), tracking first-open time in DataStore. KMP has no equivalent persistence or threshold; the SPI is a bare 'show it now' call. So the carefully-timed prompt cadence (a deliberate business rule) is completely lost in the migration.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the first-open-timestamp DataStore persistence and the elapsed-time gate (preserving the native 20-day value, or fix to the intended 7 days if that was a bug) into a domain use case that decides eligibility before calling InAppReviewClient.requestReview().
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — eligibility logic EXISTS and is LIVE: - native-app/.../google_play_cores/app_review/ReviewManagerHelper.kt:30-31 — KEY_FIRST_OPEN_TIME = "first_open_time"; SEVEN_DAYS_MILLIS = TimeUnit.DAYS.toMillis(20) (constant named SEVEN_DAYS but actually 20 days, exactly as claimed). - ReviewManagerHelper.kt:43-47 — firstOpenTimePref = context.dataStoreLong(KEY_FIRST_OPEN_TIME, default = 0L) → persisted to DataStore (dataStoreLong confirmed real at core/storage/DataStoreDelegate.kt:64-65 using longPreferencesKey). - ReviewManagerHelper.kt:50-63 — shouldShowReviewFlow: if firstOpen == 0L it records System.currentTimeMillis() and returns false on first read; otherwise emits (now - firstOpen) >= SEVEN_DAYS_MILLIS. - ReviewManagerHelper.kt:76-90 — launchInAppReview() only calls requestReviewFlow()/launchReviewFlow() when shouldShowReview() is true (the gate). - MainActivity.kt:299-300 + 534-538 — gate is wired live: launchInAppReviewSafely() → reviewHelper.launchInAppReview(this) on startup. KMP — NO eligibility logic: - platform/src/androidMain/.../review/AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:32-45 — requestReview() immediately runs manager.requestReviewFlow().await() + manager.launchReviewFlow(activity, reviewInfo).await(); no first-open/threshold/timing gate at all (only an early-false when no foreground Activity). - platform/src/commonMain/.../review/InAppReviewClient.kt:57-64 — SPI is a bare suspend fun requestReview(): Boolean; no eligibility concept exists in the contract. - Repo-wide grep across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/platform/composeApp/app: ZERO matches for shouldShowReview, has_reviewed, SEVEN_DAYS. Matches for first_open/firstOpen are ALL unrelated onboarding navigation (isFirstOpen for WhatsNewScreen/RepoSettings, e.g. composeApp/.../navigation/Screen.kt:37 and RepoSettingsScreenRoute.kt:134) — none relate to review timing, and no DataStore key for review first-open exists. - iOS/Desktop actuals (IosInAppReviewClient.kt:18-21, DesktopInAppReviewClient.kt:18-21) are no-ops returning false. ADDITIONAL FINDING (strengthens, not refutes): KMP requestReview() has ZERO call sites in ui/presentation/domain/data/composeApp/app (grep returned none). It is bound in DI (shared/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:150 single<InAppReviewClient>{AndroidInAppReviewClient(androidContext())}) but never invoked — so the KMP app currently neither gates nor even triggers the review prompt.

**🟠 [High] In-app review — foreground Activity wiring — AndroidInAppReviewClient bound without an Activity provider, so requestReview() can never show the dialog** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — native passes the concrete Activity (this@MainActivity) into launchInAppReview/launchReviewFlow (MainActivity.kt:538, ReviewManagerHelper.kt:86).
- **KMP:** No — PlatformModule.android.kt:150 binds AndroidInAppReviewClient(androidContext()) with activityProvider defaulting to { null } (AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:26). requestReview() returns false early when activityProvider() is null (lines 33-36). No real provider is ever bound.
- **Explanation:** Same root cause as the update-flow Activity gap: the review dialog requires a foreground Activity, but the bound client always gets null, so requestReview() always returns false even if it were called. The feature is doubly broken (never called AND unable to show).
- **Suggested fix:** Bind AndroidInAppReviewClient with a real ForegroundActivityProvider via an ActivityHolder, same fix as the update-flow Activity wiring.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — in-app review is real and wired with a concrete Activity end-to-end: MainActivity.kt:299-301 launches `reviewScope.launch { launchInAppReviewSafely() }`; MainActivity.kt:534-544 `launchInAppReviewSafely()` calls `reviewHelper.launchInAppReview(this@MainActivity)` (line 538, passing the concrete Activity); ReviewManagerHelper.kt:76-90 `launchInAppReview(activity: Activity)` gates on `shouldShowReview()` then `manager.requestReviewFlow().await()` + `manager.launchReviewFlow(activity, reviewInfo).await()` (line 86 uses the passed Activity). KMP — confirmed bound without an Activity provider: AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:24-27 ctor `AndroidInAppReviewClient(context: Context, private val activityProvider: ForegroundActivityProvider = { null })`; AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:32-36 `requestReview()` does `val activity = activityProvider() ?: run { log.w{...}; return false }` (early-false when provider is null); PlatformModule.android.kt:150 `single<InAppReviewClient> { AndroidInAppReviewClient(androidContext()) }` supplies only the context, leaving activityProvider at its `{ null }` default. Repo-wide grep confirms NO `ActivityHolder` class exists anywhere; no real provider is bound to this facade (the same null default also applies to AndroidAdProvider/AndroidAppUpdateClient/AndroidConsentFlowClient). The module's own KDoc (PlatformModule.android.kt:92-95, 146) and audit postscript (lines 261-285) explicitly label this an unfulfilled "Phase 11" forecast. KMP — also confirmed never called: `requestReview`/`InAppReviewClient` has ZERO call sites in :ui, :presentation, :domain, :data, legacy :shared, or :composeApp — it appears only in the three PlatformModule.* DI bindings and the :platform definition/actual files. So requestReview() would return false even if invoked, and it is never invoked. The claim's specific line refs (AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:26 default, :33-36 early-return, PlatformModule.android.kt:150 binding, MainActivity.kt:538 + ReviewManagerHelper.kt:86 native) are all accurate.

**🟠 [High] UMP consent flow — AdMob initialized without consent gating — KMP initializes MobileAds unconditionally at startup; native only initializes ads after consent and only when canRequestAds() is true** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — native gates ad init: initializeAds() (MainActivity.kt:524-532) calls MobileAds.initialize only inside if (consentInformation.canRequestAds()), and initializeAds is only reached after the consent flow resolves. (Note native MyApp.kt:52 also eagerly calls MobileAds.initialize, but the MainActivity path is consent-gated.)
- **KMP:** No — app/.../MyApp.kt:132-136 calls MobileAds.initialize(this) unconditionally in onCreate, with no consent check and no prior UMP flow. canRequestAds() (AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:80) is never consulted before ad init anywhere in the KMP graph.
- **Explanation:** Native ties AdMob initialization to the UMP consent outcome (canRequestAds()). KMP initializes the Mobile Ads SDK at app start regardless of consent state and never invokes the UMP flow, diverging from native's privacy-gated behavior and risking serving personalized ads without the required consent in EEA regions.
- **Suggested fix:** Move MobileAds.initialize out of unconditional onCreate; first run the ConsentFlowClient flow, then only initialize ads when canRequestAds() returns true, matching native initializeAds gating.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: Medium). KMP (NEW): app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MyApp.kt:132-136 calls MobileAds.initialize(this) in onCreate, wrapped only in try/catch — no consent check, no UMP flow. platform/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/platform/consent/AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:80 defines canRequestAds() but it is NEVER called: ConsentFlowClient is only registered in DI (shared/src/androidMain/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:151 `single<ConsentFlowClient> { AndroidConsentFlowClient(androidContext()) }`) with ZERO consumers anywhere in ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/platform/composeApp/app — no ViewModel, use case, or MyApp bootstrap injects it (verified by grep: only DI single<> + class defs, no injection sites). AndroidAdProvider.kt has no consent gating either. The file's own postscript admits the actual is "NOT yet bound in any rework Koin module... staged, awaiting the Phase 8-12 rework-DI cutover." NATIVE (SOURCE OF TRUTH): native-app/.../MainActivity.kt:524-532 — initializeAds() calls MobileAds.initialize ONLY inside `if (consentInformation.canRequestAds())`. It is reached only via the UMP flow: requestConsent() (line 428, launched at 289-298 in onCreate) → requestConsentInfoUpdate → loadAndShowForm (461) showing the form then initializeAds (508/513), or initializeAds (464) when not required; failure paths (469, 519) also route through the canRequestAds-gated initializeAds. IMPORTANT NUANCE the claim itself flags: native-app/.../MyApp.kt:52 ALSO calls MobileAds.initialize(this) UNCONDITIONALLY in Application.onCreate — IDENTICAL to KMP's MyApp:133. So native does NOT exclusively gate ad init on consent; its Application-level init is unconditional too. The claim's framing ("native only initializes ads after consent") overstates this. The genuine, confirmed divergence is that KMP is missing native's ADDITIONAL consent-gated MainActivity path and never invokes the UMP consent flow at all (no requestConsentInfoUpdate, no loadAndShowConsentForm, no canRequestAds consult anywhere).

**🟠 [High] UMP consent flow — foreground Activity wiring — AndroidConsentFlowClient bound without an Activity provider; both async methods would return UNKNOWN/false** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes — native passes the Activity into requestConsentInfoUpdate(activity, ...) and form.show(activity) (MainActivity.kt:454, 506).
- **KMP:** No — PlatformModule.android.kt:151 binds AndroidConsentFlowClient(androidContext()) with activityProvider defaulting to { null } (AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:35). requestConsentInfoUpdate returns ConsentStatus.UNKNOWN and loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired returns false when activityProvider() is null (lines 43-46, 64-67).
- **Explanation:** As with update/review, the consent flow needs a foreground Activity but the bound client always receives null. So even if the flow were invoked, requestConsentInfoUpdate would resolve to UNKNOWN and the form would never display. The consent surface is non-functional.
- **Suggested fix:** Bind AndroidConsentFlowClient with a real ForegroundActivityProvider via the ActivityHolder, same fix as update/review.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — consent flow fully wired with a real Activity: MainActivity.kt:291 invokes requestConsent(this@MainActivity) in onCreate; requestConsent(activity) calls consentInformation.requestConsentInfoUpdate(activity, params, onSuccess, onFailure) at MainActivity.kt:454-456 (claim's line 454 is exact); on REQUIRED it calls form.show(activity) at MainActivity.kt:506 (claim's line 506 is exact). The native consent surface is functional. KMP — bound without an Activity provider, both async methods short-circuit to UNKNOWN/false: AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:35 declares `private val activityProvider: ForegroundActivityProvider = { null }` (typealias `() -> Activity?` confirmed at platform/.../activity/ForegroundActivityProvider.kt:30). requestConsentInfoUpdate() returns ConsentStatus.UNKNOWN when activityProvider() is null (AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:43-46). loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired() returns false when activityProvider() is null (AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:64-67). The Koin binding at shared/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:151 is `single<ConsentFlowClient> { AndroidConsentFlowClient(androidContext()) }` — only context is passed, so activityProvider falls back to the `{ null }` default. The module KDoc/comment (PlatformModule.android.kt:91-95, 146-147) explicitly states activityProvider stays `{ null }` until a Phase-11 ActivityHolder is wired. Corroborating: grep across platform/shared/composeApp/app finds NO ActivityHolder class (only forecast prose); the in-file postscript at PlatformModule.android.kt:271 itself states "Grep-verified no ActivityHolder class exists anywhere in the workspace." Additionally, no consumer injects ConsentFlowClient anywhere — grep for get<ConsentFlowClient>/inject/constructor params across :presentation, :domain, :ui, :data, :composeApp returns zero hits, and there are no call sites for requestConsentInfoUpdate()/loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired() outside the actuals themselves. The claim's mechanics are exactly correct; if anything it understates the regression (the flow is not merely Activity-less, it is never invoked at all on Android).

**🟡 [Medium] In-app update — immediate vs flexible dispatch & developer-triggered-in-progress — Native supports an immediate-update branch and resumes a DEVELOPER_TRIGGERED_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS; KMP Android actual only ever starts FLEXIBLE** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — AppUpdateHelper.handleUpdateInfo (AppUpdateHelper.kt:79-107) chooses IMMEDIATE when immediate flag set and allowed, else FLEXIBLE; and on DEVELOPER_TRIGGERED_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS re-starts immediate (lines 96-101). The immediate flag is wired via updateType (MainActivity.kt:197, currently false).
- **KMP:** Partial — AndroidAppUpdateClient.checkForUpdate (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:40-46) computes isImmediate only as (FLEXIBLE not allowed AND IMMEDIATE allowed) and exposes it on AppUpdateInfo, but startFlexibleUpdate() (lines 53-73) hard-returns false if FLEXIBLE is not allowed (line 61) — it never starts an IMMEDIATE flow. It also does not handle DEVELOPER_TRIGGERED_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS (only checks UPDATE_AVAILABLE).
- **Explanation:** Native can run a Play Core IMMEDIATE update (and resume one already in progress), even though it currently launches with immediate=false. KMP's Android actual has no method to start an immediate update at all (startFlexibleUpdate bails when flexible isn't allowed) and ignores the DEVELOPER_TRIGGERED_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS availability state, so a release that only permits immediate updates would silently do nothing.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a startImmediateUpdate() to the SPI/Android actual using AppUpdateType.IMMEDIATE, handle DEVELOPER_TRIGGERED_UPDATE_IN_PROGRESS in checkForUpdate, and let the host pick the flow based on AppUpdateInfo.isImmediate, mirroring native handleUpdateInfo.

**⚪ [Low] UMP consent flow — form-show API divergence (manual loadConsentForm + REQUIRED gate vs loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired) — Native manually loads the form and shows it only when consentStatus==REQUIRED; KMP uses the convenience loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired and reports 'shown' even when no form was required** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — native uses UserMessagingPlatform.loadConsentForm(...) and explicitly branches: only when consentInformation.consentStatus == ConsentInformation.ConsentStatus.REQUIRED does it call form.show(activity){...} (MainActivity.kt:497-515); otherwise it skips straight to initializeAds.
- **KMP:** Partial — AndroidConsentFlowClient.loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired (AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:63-78) delegates to UserMessagingPlatform.loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired(activity){error->...} and returns true whenever no error occurs — i.e. it returns true even when no form needed to be shown, conflating 'shown' and 'not required'. The SPI KDoc (ConsentFlowClient.kt:23-26) documents this ('Returns true if a form was shown (or if no form was required)').
- **Explanation:** Functionally both approaches show the EEA form when required, but the KMP boolean cannot distinguish 'form was actually shown' from 'no form required', whereas native's explicit REQUIRED branch makes that distinction. This is a behavioral/semantics divergence in the consent API surface that matters if a caller needs to know whether a form rendered. (Lower severity than the missing-invocation issues because the convenience API is broadly equivalent for the show-when-required goal.)
- **Suggested fix:** If callers need to distinguish shown vs not-required, expose the consentStatus/REQUIRED branch (as native does) or return a richer result type instead of a single boolean; otherwise document the conflation explicitly at the call site.

**⚪ [Low] Play Core flows — eager init parity — Native eagerly inits the update manager in Application.onCreate; KMP eagerly constructs AppUpdateClient but NOT the review/consent clients** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — native MyApp.onCreate calls AppUpdateHelper.init(this) (native MyApp.kt:27). Review/consent are created on demand in MainActivity.
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP MyApp.onCreate calls get<AppUpdateClient>() (app/.../MyApp.kt:115) to construct the Play Core manager eagerly, but does not eagerly construct InAppReviewClient or ConsentFlowClient (only NotificationPresenter besides update). All three are Koin singletons created lazily on first get(), which never happens for review/consent.
- **Explanation:** The update manager handshake happens at startup in both apps (parity on construction). However, because no code ever resolves InAppReviewClient or ConsentFlowClient, their constructors (which create the Play Core ReviewManager / UMP ConsentInformation) never run in the KMP app at all. This is a minor divergence on top of the larger 'never invoked' findings.
- **Suggested fix:** This is subsumed by reintroducing the actual flow invocations; once review/consent are called, their singletons will construct. No separate fix needed beyond wiring the flows.

**⚪ [Low] Play Core flows — cross-platform (iOS/Desktop) behavior — iOS/Desktop are intentional no-ops for update/review/consent (returning null/false/NOT_REQUIRED/canRequestAds=true)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** N/A — native is Android-only; no cross-platform expectation exists.
- **KMP:** Yes — IosAppUpdateClient/DesktopAppUpdateClient return null/false (IosAppUpdateClient.kt:18-31); Ios/DesktopInAppReviewClient return false; Ios/DesktopConsentFlowClient return NOT_REQUIRED + true + canRequestAds()=true (IosConsentFlowClient.kt:18-28, DesktopConsentFlowClient.kt:17-27).
- **Explanation:** This is expected behavior for non-Android platforms (App Store handles updates, no AdMob/ads on iOS/Desktop), not a regression against the Android source of truth. Noted for completeness: the consent stubs return canRequestAds()=true so ads (if any) would be allowed on those platforms without a form, which is consistent with 'no ads served there' but worth flagging if ad logic ever runs cross-platform.
- **Suggested fix:** No action required; document that ads must remain disabled on iOS/Desktop given canRequestAds() unconditionally returns true there.

</details>

### Crash / Analytics / Firebase  `crash-analytics-firebase`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 12 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡2 ⚪7)

> Native uses Firebase directly: FirebaseAnalytics logs an APP_OPEN event in MainActivity.onCreate and a custom "manga_open" event (params manga_api/manga_title/source_screen) from both MangaDetailsScreen and LibraryMangaScreen; FirebaseCrashlytics.recordException + sendUnsentReports runs inside CrashActivity/CrashScreen (the global uncaught handler is commented out); MyFirebaseMessagingService displays notifications on onMessageReceived; ComplaintFirestoreDataSource talks to the complaints_v2 collection. KMP abstracts these behind :platform facades (AnalyticsClient, CrashReporter, RemoteDocStore, PushTokenProvider) bound per-platform in PlatformModule.*.kt, with Android backed by the real Firebase SDK and iOS/Desktop as Kermit-logging no-ops. The Firestore/complaint port is faithful and the crash-report recording is actually MORE complete than native (KMP wires a real global uncaught handler in MyApp). However two real telemetry regressions exist: (1) ALL analytics is dead — AnalyticsClient is bound but has zero call sites, so neither app_open nor manga_open is ever logged on any platform; (2) the KMP MyFirebaseMessagingService is an empty stub with no onMessageReceived (data/notification FCM messages are silently dropped) and no onNewToken (the PushTokenBroadcaster it is documented to feed is never invoked). The crash UI was also redesigned (hardcoded English strings, different layout) rather than ported verbatim. iOS/Desktop have no crash reporting, analytics, or Firestore at all (deferred).

**🟠 [High] Analytics — APP_OPEN event — Native logs Firebase APP_OPEN on app launch; KMP never logs it** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.kt:274 `firebaseAnalytics.logEvent(FirebaseAnalytics.Event.APP_OPEN, Bundle())` in onCreate, with FirebaseAnalytics injected via Hilt (MainActivity.kt:99-100, FirebaseModule.kt:34-41).
- **KMP:** No — KMP MainActivity.kt is a 58-line thin host (onCreate only calls installSplashScreen/enableEdgeToEdge/setContent{App()}); no analytics call. MyApp.kt onCreate also never logs app_open. grep for `.logEvent(`/`APP_OPEN` across all non-native modules returns only the AndroidAnalyticsClient facade internals.
- **Explanation:** The standard Firebase `app_open` engagement signal is completely lost in KMP. Although `AnalyticsClient` is bound in Koin (PlatformModule.android.kt:140 `single<AnalyticsClient> { AndroidAnalyticsClient(androidContext()) }`), it has ZERO call sites anywhere in the codebase — so no app-open telemetry reaches Firebase. This breaks DAU/retention dashboards that depend on app_open.
- **Suggested fix:** Inject the Koin-bound AnalyticsClient into MainActivity/MyApp (or an App-level LaunchedEffect) and call `analyticsClient.logEvent("app_open")` (Firebase auto-collects screen_view/session, but the source app explicitly logged APP_OPEN) once on launch, mirroring native MainActivity.kt:274.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — APP_OPEN IS logged on launch: - native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:199 `override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?)`; inside it at MainActivity.kt:274 `firebaseAnalytics.logEvent(FirebaseAnalytics.Event.APP_OPEN, Bundle())` (runs before setContent at line 317). - firebaseAnalytics injected via Hilt at MainActivity.kt:99-100 (`@Inject lateinit var firebaseAnalytics: FirebaseAnalytics`). - Provided by di/firebase/FirebaseModule.kt:34-41 (`@Provides @Singleton fun provideFirebaseAnalytics(...) = FirebaseAnalytics.getInstance(context)`). KMP — APP_OPEN is NEVER logged: - app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MainActivity.kt:18-27 is a thin host; onCreate only calls installSplashScreen(), enableEdgeToEdge(), super.onCreate(), setContent { App() }. No analytics call. - app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MyApp.kt:127 calls FirebaseApp.initializeApp(this) but never logs app_open anywhere in onCreate. - The facade AnalyticsClient is bound in Koin: shared/src/androidMain/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:140 `single<AnalyticsClient> { AndroidAnalyticsClient(androidContext()) }`. - platform/.../analytics/AndroidAnalyticsClient.kt:23-48 wraps FirebaseAnalytics and its logEvent (line 28) is fully capable of emitting APP_OPEN — but it is never invoked. - Exhaustive grep across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/platform/composeApp/app for `logEvent`/`APP_OPEN`/`app_open`/`AnalyticsClient`: every hit is either the interface definition (platform/.../analytics/AnalyticsClient.kt:20-21), one of the 3 platform actuals' class declarations (Android line 23, iOS IosAnalyticsClient.kt:15, Desktop DesktopAnalyticsClient.kt:13), the 3 Koin binding lines (android:140, ios:124, desktop:124), or prose/comments. There is NO constructor-injected `AnalyticsClient`, no `get<AnalyticsClient>()`, no `by inject`/`koinInject` — i.e. ZERO call sites. So no app_open (and in fact no analytics event at all) reaches Firebase from KMP. Native's other analytics (manga_open at MangaDetailsScreen.kt:72 / LibraryMangaScreen.kt:112) are also unported, but the specific APP_OPEN claim is exactly correct. Minor note: a stale code comment in AndroidAnalyticsClient.kt:75 and PlatformModule.android.kt prose say binding is at 'android.kt:114', but the live binding line is 140 as the claim states.

**🟠 [High] Analytics — manga_open event (Details + Library) — Native logs a custom `manga_open` event with manga_api/manga_title/source_screen params; KMP logs nothing** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — two call sites: MangaDetailsScreen.kt:65-72 logs `manga_open` with params manga_api, manga_title, source_screen="home" inside a LaunchedEffect(state.data.title) after success; LibraryMangaScreen.kt:102-113 logs `manga_open` with manga_api, manga_title, source_screen="library" inside LaunchedEffect(manga.id) (guarded by `if (manga.id == 0L) return`). Both obtain analytics via rememberFirebaseAnalytics() (firebase_cores/common/rememberFirebaseAnalytics.kt).
- **KMP:** No — grep for `manga_open`/`rememberFirebaseAnalytics`/`logEvent`/`AnalyticsClient` across :ui, :presentation, :composeApp returns no matches; rememberFirebaseAnalytics has no KMP counterpart (only referenced in migration/*.md docs). The custom event and all three params are never emitted.
- **Explanation:** The app's only custom analytics event — content engagement per manga, broken down by source screen (home vs library) — is entirely missing in KMP. Product analytics on which manga are opened and from where are lost. The facade exists but is dead code with no consumers.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a `manga_open` logEvent in the KMP details and library-details screens/ViewModels using the injected AnalyticsClient, passing manga_api, manga_title, and source_screen, replicating the exact event name and param keys and the source_screen values ("home" / "library") and the manga.id==0 guard from native.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (confirmed exactly as claimed): native-app/.../details/ui/screens/MangaDetailsScreen.kt:65 calls rememberFirebaseAnalytics(); lines 66-73 = LaunchedEffect(state.data.title) building a Bundle with manga_api (l68), manga_title (l69), source_screen="home" (l70) then firebaseAnalytics.logEvent("manga_open", params) at l72. native-app/.../library_details/ui/screens/LibraryMangaScreen.kt:102 calls rememberFirebaseAnalytics(); lines 104-113 = LaunchedEffect(manga.id) guarded by `if (manga.id == 0L) return@LaunchedEffect` (l106), building manga_api (l108), manga_title (l109), source_screen="library" (l110), then logEvent("manga_open", params) at l112. Facade at firebase_cores/common/rememberFirebaseAnalytics.kt:9-13 returns FirebaseAnalytics.getInstance(context). KMP (event genuinely absent — core claim TRUE): repo-wide grep for the literal "manga_open" across all .kt files (excluding native-app) = ZERO matches. presentation/.../details/DetailsViewModel.kt and presentation/.../library/LibraryViewModel.kt have zero analytics references. ui/.../details/DetailsScreen.kt and ui/.../library/LibraryScreen.kt have zero analytics references. The only .logEvent( calls in all of KMP are inside the facade implementation itself: platform/src/androidMain/.../analytics/AndroidAnalyticsClient.kt:30 and :47 (Firebase wrapper, not a consumer). CLAIM INACCURACY: The claim's existsInKmp sub-statement that grep for "rememberFirebaseAnalytics/logEvent/AnalyticsClient returns no matches" is FALSE for :platform and :shared. A full cross-platform AnalyticsClient facade DOES exist: platform/src/commonMain/.../analytics/AnalyticsClient.kt:20 (interface, logEvent at l21), with actuals AndroidAnalyticsClient.kt:23 (real Firebase backend), IosAnalyticsClient.kt:15 (no-op) and DesktopAnalyticsClient.kt:13 (no-op), and it IS bound in Koin: PlatformModule.android.kt:140 `single<AnalyticsClient> { AndroidAnalyticsClient(androidContext()) }`, PlatformModule.ios.kt:124, PlatformModule.desktop.kt:124. However the claim's own explanation ("the facade exists but is dead code with no consumers") is accurate: nothing in :ui/:presentation/:domain/:data ever calls logEvent, so the manga_open event and its three params (manga_api, manga_title, source_screen) are never emitted on any platform.

**🟠 [High] FCM — onMessageReceived (push notification display) — Native shows a notification for every received FCM message; KMP drops all messages silently** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes — MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:20-28 overrides onMessageReceived, extracts title/body from remote.notification or data map (defaults "Hello"/"You've got a message") and calls `helper.showNotification(this, title, body)` (NotificationHelper @Inject).
- **KMP:** No — app/.../firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt is `class MyFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService()` with an empty body (KDoc admits "real FCM payload handling migrated in Phase 4/11" but it never was). No onMessageReceived override.
- **Explanation:** The service is still registered in AndroidManifest.xml:90-96 with the MESSAGING_EVENT intent filter, so Firebase delivers messages to it, but with no onMessageReceived the app silently swallows every data-payload push (and notification-payload messages only show via the system tray when the app is backgrounded — foreground delivery and all data messages produce nothing). Any server-driven push (new chapter alerts, announcements) is broken on KMP. This is a behavioral regression hidden behind a present-but-empty class.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the native onMessageReceived: read title/body from remote.notification / remote.data with the same defaults and route through the KMP NotificationPresenter (the :platform facade that replaced NotificationHelper), so foreground/data pushes display a notification as before.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:20-28 overrides onMessageReceived(remote: RemoteMessage): line 23 `val title = remote.notification?.title ?: remote.data["title"] ?: "Hello"`, line 24 `val body = remote.notification?.body ?: remote.data["body"] ?: "You've got a message"`, line 27 `helper.showNotification(this, title, body)`. The class is @AndroidEntryPoint (line 10). showNotification exists in native-app/.../core/util/notification/NotificationHelper.kt:128-143 (builds a NotificationCompat on the "firebase_messages"/"App Messages" IMPORTANCE_HIGH channel and notifies). Native manifest native-app/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:85-91 registers the service exported=true with the com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT intent-filter (line 89). [Minor: claim said NotificationHelper is @Inject'd, but native NotificationHelper is an `object` singleton at line 15 — the @Inject on line 13 is effectively a no-op since the object is referenced directly; behavior is unaffected. Claim's native line range 20-28 is exact; manifest range is 85-91 not 90-96.] KMP (new app) — app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:9 is `class MyFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService()` with an EMPTY body — no onMessageReceived, no onNewToken. Its own KDoc/audit comment (lines 5-8, 20-22) admits "real FCM payload handling migrated in Phase 4/11 from the source project" and "no onMessageReceived, no onNewToken override." The service is still registered in KMP manifest app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:90-101 with the com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT intent-filter (line 94) and default_notification_icon meta-data, so Firebase delivers messages to a no-op handler. A repo-wide grep for `onMessageReceived` outside native-app finds ONLY documentation/comment hits (no real override anywhere in :ui/:presentation/:domain/:data/:shared/:platform/:app). `showNotification` does not exist anywhere in the KMP tree outside native-app. The :platform facades NotificationPresenter.show() (AndroidNotificationPresenter.kt:31) and PushTokenProvider exist but are NOT wired to the FCM receive path — nothing in the empty service calls them. The app-module ChapterNotificationHelper.kt only handles internal new-chapter/download notifications, not server pushes. Conclusion: REAL regression. Native displays a notification (own app-message channel) for every received FCM message including data payloads; KMP's registered-but-empty service silently swallows all data-payload pushes and foreground notification-payload messages.

**🟡 [Medium] Crash — CrashScreen UI redesign — KMP crash screen is a different layout with hardcoded English strings; native uses the localized InfoScreen scaffold** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — CrashScreen.kt uses InfoScreen (CrashInfoScreen.kt) with: Icons.Outlined.BugReport tinted colorScheme.primary at 48.dp; headline=stringResource(R.string.crash_screen_title) with typography.headlineLarge; subtitle=stringResource(crash_screen_description, app_name) titleSmall; a bottomBar with a Button (acceptText=pref_dump_crash_logs) + OutlinedButton (rejectText=crash_screen_restart_application), 48.dp top padding, 8.dp horizontal padding, hairline outline divider, status-bar scrim; trace shown in a surfaceVariant Box clipped to shapes.small with 8.dp padding.
- **KMP:** Yes but redesigned — composeApp/.../crash/CrashScreen.kt: a centered Column (24.dp padding), BugReport icon tinted colorScheme.error at 72.dp height, headlineSmall "Oops! Something went wrong", bodyMedium "Yami Manga has crashed...", trace in a weight(1f) surfaceVariant Box (12.dp padding), and two full-width buttons at the bottom of the same column ("Send Crash Report" Button + "Restart App" OutlinedButton). All strings are hardcoded English (KDoc lines 57-67 explicitly note R.string.* not wired; TODO Phase 12.x.future).
- **Explanation:** Multiple concrete divergences: (1) icon tint primary->error and size 48.dp->72.dp; (2) text styles headlineLarge/titleSmall -> headlineSmall/bodyMedium; (3) layout: native uses a Scaffold bottomBar with windowInsets handling, status-bar scrim, and an outline divider line, while KMP stacks everything in one centered Column with no scrim/divider; (4) buttons live in a fixed bottomBar (native) vs inline at column bottom (KMP); (5) button labels differ — native accept=pref_dump_crash_logs / reject=crash_screen_restart_application (both call onRestartClick), KMP="Send Crash Report"/"Restart App"; (6) ALL native strings are localized resources (Arabic etc.), KMP hardcodes English, breaking localization/RTL on the crash screen.
- **Suggested fix:** Re-skin the KMP CrashScreen to match native's InfoScreen layout (bottomBar buttons, status-bar scrim, outline divider, icon tint=primary at 48.dp, headlineLarge title + titleSmall subtitle) and wire the crash strings to compose-resources (Res.string.crash_screen_title, crash_screen_description, pref_dump_crash_logs, crash_screen_restart_application) so the crash UI is localized like native.

**🟡 [Medium] iOS/Desktop — crash reporting, analytics, Firestore — On non-Android KMP targets, all crash/analytics/Firestore telemetry is a no-op** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** N/A — native is Android-only (source of truth has no iOS/Desktop).
- **KMP:** Partial/No — IosCrashReporter.kt and DesktopCrashReporter.kt only Kermit-log (no Crashlytics); IosAnalyticsClient.kt:19-28 / DesktopAnalyticsClient log-and-return (no real analytics); IosRemoteDocStore / DesktopRemoteDocStore return null/empty/no-op (no Firestore). All documented as deferred to Phase 12/13.
- **Explanation:** Because KMP is multiplatform, the iOS and Desktop builds ship with zero crash reporting, zero analytics, and zero Firestore connectivity — meaning the complaint/feedback feature (which depends on ComplaintRepository->Firestore) uses the REST-based ComplaintFirestoreRestDataSource on iOS/Desktop (real) but crash/analytics telemetry is entirely absent there. If iOS/Desktop are shipped, crashes and engagement on those platforms are invisible. This is a parity gap relative to the Android source-of-truth only if those targets ship.
- **Suggested fix:** If iOS/Desktop are user-facing, wire Firebase Crashlytics iOS (via CocoaPods/cinterop) and Firebase/GA4 analytics (or Measurement Protocol over Ktor) per the documented Phase 12/13 plan; until then, document that these platforms have no crash/analytics telemetry.

**⚪ [Low] FCM — onNewToken / push-token registration — KMP documents a PushTokenBroadcaster fed from onNewToken, but the FCM service never overrides onNewToken so the broadcaster is never fed** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Partial — MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:15-18 overrides onNewToken but its body is only a commented-out `// e.g., ApiClient.registerFcmToken(token)`; native does not actually register the token either.
- **KMP:** Partial/No — AndroidPushTokenProvider.kt:71-81 defines `object PushTokenBroadcaster` whose KDoc (lines 63-70, and audit note lines 126-133) states the FCM service "calls PushTokenBroadcaster.publish(token) from its onNewToken callback", but the KMP MyFirebaseMessagingService has no onNewToken override, so publish() is never invoked. observeTokens()/getToken() also have zero consumers across :domain/:data/:presentation/:shared.
- **Explanation:** Functionally both apps end up NOT registering the FCM token with a backend, so end-user behavior is unchanged. However the KMP code is internally inconsistent: AndroidPushTokenProvider's contract assumes onNewToken feeds PushTokenBroadcaster, but the wiring is absent, leaving observeTokens() permanently stuck on only its initial getToken() value with no rotation events. This is a latent bug for anyone who later relies on token rotation.
- **Suggested fix:** If/when push-token sync is implemented, override onNewToken in the KMP MyFirebaseMessagingService to call PushTokenBroadcaster.publish(token). For strict parity with native today, leaving it unwired is acceptable, but document that observeTokens never sees rotations until then.

**⚪ [Low] Crash — global uncaught exception handler — KMP installs a real Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler; native has it commented out** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** No (commented) — MyApp.kt:33-50 the entire `Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler { ... recordException ... CrashActivity.start ... }` block is commented out; native only reports crashes that route through CrashActivity (which is itself only launched if something else starts it — effectively the handler is dormant).
- **KMP:** Yes — MyApp.kt:84-108 installs a global handler that calls `get<CrashReporter>().recordException(throwable, mapOf("thread" to thread.name, "phase" to "uncaught"))`, then posts `CrashActivity.start(this, stack)` on the main looper, then delegates to the previous handler.
- **Explanation:** This is an IMPROVEMENT over native, not a regression: KMP actually wires the crash bridge native left as dead commented code (native MyApp.kt:33-50). KMP additionally attaches custom keys `thread` and `phase=uncaught` via CrashReporter.recordException's context map (AndroidCrashReporter.kt:27-32 fans them into setCustomKey before recordException). Worth flagging only because it is a behavioral divergence from the source of truth — KMP will surface CrashActivity and Crashlytics reports on uncaught exceptions where native would not.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix needed for parity correctness; if exact source-of-truth fidelity is required (native does NOT auto-handle uncaught crashes), confirm with product whether the always-on crash screen is intended. Otherwise keep — it is strictly better telemetry.

**⚪ [Low] Crash — CrashActivity Crashlytics handshake timing — KMP records the exception in CrashActivity.onCreate (outside Compose); native records it inside CrashScreen's LaunchedEffect** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — recording is inside CrashScreen.kt:29-36 `LaunchedEffect(Unit){ FirebaseCrashlytics.getInstance().apply { recordException(it); sendUnsentReports() } }`, i.e. it fires when the composable enters composition.
- **KMP:** Yes but relocated — CrashActivity.kt:52-59 calls FirebaseCrashlytics.getInstance().recordException(RuntimeException(trace)) + sendUnsentReports() directly in onCreate (wrapped in try/catch), because CrashScreen now lives in composeApp/commonMain and cannot reference Firebase.
- **Explanation:** Behavior is preserved (record + flush still happen once when the crash surface appears). The divergence is structural: native records the original Throwable handed to CrashScreen; KMP records a fresh RuntimeException(trace) built from the stack-trace string (because the Throwable cannot cross the Intent boundary). Both ultimately log a RuntimeException wrapping the trace string, so the Crashlytics report fidelity is equivalent. Low impact; noted for completeness.
- **Suggested fix:** No change needed; optionally pass richer structured data (exception class name, message) as additional intent extras and set them as Crashlytics custom keys before recordException to slightly improve report grouping vs the single concatenated trace string.

**⚪ [Low] Crashlytics custom keys / log / setUserId surface — KMP exposes a richer CrashReporter API (log, setUserId, setCustomKey) that native never had; only recordException context-keys are actually used** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Partial — native only ever calls FirebaseCrashlytics.recordException + sendUnsentReports (CrashScreen.kt:32-34). It never calls setCustomKey, log, or setUserId anywhere.
- **KMP:** Yes — CrashReporter interface (platform/.../crash/CrashReporter.kt:19-24) defines recordException(throwable, context), log(message), setUserId(id), setCustomKey(key,value); AndroidCrashReporter.kt:27-45 implements all via Crashlytics. Only recordException with context {thread, phase} is actually called (MyApp.kt:87-93); log/setUserId/setCustomKey have no callers.
- **Explanation:** KMP adds capability beyond native (custom keys on uncaught crashes, plus unused log/setUserId/setCustomKey hooks). This is not a regression — it is a superset. Flagged because three of the four methods are dead (no consumers), and the added 'thread'/'phase' custom keys are telemetry native never produced, so Crashlytics dashboards will differ between the two builds.
- **Suggested fix:** Keep the richer API. Optionally remove or wire up the unused log/setUserId/setCustomKey methods to avoid dead surface, and document the new thread/phase custom keys so they are expected in Crashlytics.

**⚪ [Low] Analytics — setUserProperty / setUserId — KMP AnalyticsClient exposes setUserProperty/setUserId; both apps never call them** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** No — native FirebaseAnalytics is used only for logEvent (APP_OPEN, manga_open). No setUserProperty/setUserId calls exist.
- **KMP:** Partial — AnalyticsClient.kt:22-23 declares setUserProperty/setUserId, AndroidAnalyticsClient.kt:50-56 implements them, but there are no callers anywhere.
- **Explanation:** Neither side sets analytics user properties/ids, so behavior is at parity (both no-op in practice). The KMP interface merely exposes unused capability. Noted for completeness; no user-property telemetry is sent on either platform.
- **Suggested fix:** No action required for parity. If user segmentation is later desired, these hooks are ready; otherwise they are harmless dead API surface.

**⚪ [Low] Firestore — complaints_v2 data source — Faithful port; Android uses Firebase SDK identically, iOS/Desktop use a REST equivalent** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.kt (native) uses FirebaseFirestore.collection("complaints_v2") with add/get/where(Filter.or(equalTo a/userId))/document.set/delete, multi-key legacy parsing (a..g), @ServerTimestamp DTO, and a multi-format extractCreatedAt fallback.
- **KMP:** Yes — shared/androidMain/.../ComplaintFirestoreDataSource.kt is a near-verbatim port (same collection name, same Filter.or, same legacy-key cascade, same extractCreatedAt branches), with android.util.Log->Kermit and createdAt Date<->kotlin.time.Instant boundary conversions. Bound in PlatformModule.android.kt:229-230 (FirebaseFirestore.getInstance() + ComplaintFirestoreDataSource(get())). iOS/Desktop bind a Ktor REST ComplaintFirestoreRestDataSource against the same collection.
- **Explanation:** Firestore parity is high. One subtle divergence: native extractCreatedAt returns java.util.Date (nullable in declared signature but always defaults to Date()); KMP returns non-nullable kotlin.time.Instant via the same Date() fallback, and Instant->Date on write truncates sub-millisecond nanos (lossless in practice for Firestore millis resolution). Logging moved from Logcat tags to Kermit tags. No functional regression in the document read/write/parse logic.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix required. Optionally verify the Firestore composite index on (a, userId) referenced by Filter.or exists in the production project so getComplaintsByUser does not fail at runtime, and confirm google-services.json is supplied at build time (not present in the repo for either app) so FirebaseFirestore.getInstance() initializes.

**⚪ [Low] Build — kermit-crashlytics dependency unused — KMP declares kermit-crashlytics but never installs a CrashlyticsLogWriter** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** No — native does not use Kermit at all.
- **KMP:** Partial — app/build.gradle.kts:150 `implementation(libs.kermit.crashlytics)` is declared, but a repo-wide grep for CrashlyticsLogWriter / Logger.addLogWriter(CrashlyticsLogWriter) returns no matches; no Kermit log writer is wired to Crashlytics.
- **Explanation:** The kermit-crashlytics artifact (which would forward Kermit log/error calls into Crashlytics breadcrumbs) is a dependency with no setup code, so Kermit logs across the app (e.g. the many log.w/log.e in AndroidRemoteDocStore, ComplaintFirestoreDataSource, AndroidPushTokenProvider) are NOT attached to Crashlytics reports. This is dead dependency weight and a missed telemetry opportunity, not a native regression (native had no equivalent).
- **Suggested fix:** Either remove the unused kermit.crashlytics dependency, or in MyApp.onCreate install it via `Logger.setLogWriters(platformLogWriter(), CrashlyticsLogWriter())` so Kermit breadcrumbs enrich Crashlytics crash reports.

### Image Loading & Caching  `image-loading`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 13 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡3 ⚪7)

> Both apps build on Coil 3 with a singleton ImageLoader, an Android AVIF decoder (org.aomedia.avif.android), per-source auth headers (Cookie/User-Agent/Referer), and per-page RGB_565+allowHardware(false) decoder hints on Android. The KMP port faithfully reproduces the AVIF decoder, adds a high-quality Skia decoder for iOS/Desktop, and reproduces the reader's RGB_565 hints via applyReaderDecoderHints. However several native behaviors are dropped or diverge: (1) the KMP Android Coil OkHttpClient is a bare client with only a progress interceptor — it loses the native CoilModule client's 200MB disk cache, 30s/60s/60s timeouts, retryOnConnectionFailure, 15s ping, the manhastro force-cache/offline-cache interceptors, and the *.s3.wasabisys.com hostname verifier. (2) KMP rework covers (Library/Details/History/Home/Search) render via bare AsyncImage(model = url) and rely on a host-matching CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor that silently fails on CDN subdomains, instead of native's explicit per-source buildImageRequest/buildItemsImageRequest with attached headers + crossfade + RGB_565. (3) crossfade(true), present on every native cover and reader page, is missing on KMP rework covers and reader pages. (4) the native reader's large-image (>99MB) compression pipeline is entirely absent in KMP. (5) the native reader error pane's "Open in WebView" action is deferred in KMP. The Base64 image-recovery converter and DominantColorExtractor exist as orphaned, unwired SPIs in KMP (the native Base64 downloader is itself dead code; neither app actually tints covers). Coil version differs (native 3.1.0 vs KMP 3.4.0), which the KMP code works around with maxBitmapSize overrides.
