<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Image Loading & Caching</summary>

**🟠 [High] Coil OkHttp client config (Android image fetcher) — KMP Android image OkHttpClient drops the native CoilModule client's cache/timeouts/retry/ping/interceptors/hostname-verifier** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — CoilModule.provideCoilOkHttpClient (CoilModule.kt:32-49) starts from the MainOkHttpClient (AppModule.kt:42-70: 200MB disk Cache, connectTimeout 30s, readTimeout 60s, writeTimeout 60s, retryOnConnectionFailure(true), pingInterval(15s), forceCacheForDados network interceptor, offlineCacheInterceptor), then adds ProgressInterceptor + a *.s3.wasabisys.com hostnameVerifier, and feeds it to OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory (CoilModule.kt:60-63).
- **KMP:** No — PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt:45-48 builds a brand-new vanilla OkHttpClient.Builder().addInterceptor(OkHttpProgressInterceptor(...)).build(). No cache, no timeouts, no retryOnConnectionFailure, no pingInterval, no forceCacheForDados/offlineCacheInterceptor, no wasabisys hostname verifier. The KDoc at lines 28-32 explicitly asserts Coil's default is 'observationally equivalent' and that none of the native config is load-bearing — which is incorrect versus the source of truth.
- **Explanation:** On Android the image pipeline now has no HTTP disk cache (native: 200MB), so every cover/page re-downloads across cold starts and cache eviction; no read/connect/write timeouts (native 30/60/60s) so slow CDNs can hang the loader thread indefinitely instead of erroring; no retryOnConnectionFailure / pingInterval(15s) which native added specifically to survive HTTP/2 stream stalls on flaky mobile networks; loss of the manhastro force-cache + offline-cache interceptors means the api2.manhastro.net/dados endpoint no longer serves cached/stale data offline; and loss of the *.s3.wasabisys.com hostname verifier means images served from Wasabi S3 buckets whose cert host mismatches will fail TLS verification (native explicitly bypassed this).
- **Suggested fix:** In PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt resolve the app's MainOkHttpClient (the same one used for API calls) and newBuilder() it to add the ProgressInterceptor + wasabisys hostnameVerifier, mirroring CoilModule. At minimum add a 200MB okhttp Cache, the 30/60/60s timeouts, retryOnConnectionFailure(true), pingInterval(15s), the forceCacheForDados/offlineCacheInterceptor, and the wasabisys hostname verifier before passing the client to OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). REAL difference, confirmed by reading both apps. NATIVE (source of truth): - AppModule.kt:42-70 (/Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/di/app/AppModule.kt) builds @MainOkHttpClient with: Cache(200MB) at line 46-48/56, connectTimeout(30s) L57, readTimeout(60s) L58, writeTimeout(60s) L59, retryOnConnectionFailure(true) L60, pingInterval(15s) L61, addNetworkInterceptor(forceCacheForDados()) L67, addInterceptor(offlineCacheInterceptor(context)) L68. - CoilModule.kt:32-49 (.../di/coli/CoilModule.kt) takes that baseClient and does baseClient.newBuilder().addNetworkInterceptor(ProgressInterceptor()) L36 + .hostnameVerifier{...} L37-47 that returns true for any host ending ".s3.wasabisys.com" else delegates to the default verifier. Feeds it to OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory(callFactory = { callFactory }) at L60-63. So the image client inherits all of the 200MB cache / timeouts / retry / ping / both cache interceptors plus the wasabisys verifier. - forceCacheForDados.kt:10-44 (.../core/network_cache/) confirms both interceptors target only "https://api2.manhastro.net/dados" (a JSON API endpoint), forcing public max-age=86400 on responses and onlyIfCached/maxStale(7d) when offline. KMP (new app): - PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt:45-48 (/Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/common/componants/images/PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt) builds a brand-new OkHttpClient.Builder().addInterceptor(OkHttpProgressInterceptor(reporter = repository::report)).build() — NO .cache, NO connect/read/writeTimeout, NO retryOnConnectionFailure, NO pingInterval, NO forceCacheForDados/offlineCacheInterceptor, NO wasabisys hostnameVerifier. Returns OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory(callFactory = { client }) L48. - App.kt:308-326 (/Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/composeApp/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/App.kt) wires this factory into setSingletonImageLoaderFactory; the ImageLoader.Builder sets only .maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL) — no .diskCache(...). - Grep across all non-native KMP modules for pingInterval/retryOnConnectionFailure/wasabisys/okhttp_cache/"200L * 1024" matches ONLY the Ktor HttpClientFactory (the general API client), never the image OkHttpClient. forceCacheForDados is ported to shared/.../core/network_cache/forceCacheForDados.kt as a Ktor plugin for the API path, but its own KDoc states offlineCacheInterceptor was NOT ported, and neither is wired into the image fetcher. - The KDoc at PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt:27-32 explicitly asserts Coil's default is "observationally equivalent" and the native config is not load-bearing — contradicted by the source of truth above (200MB cache, timeouts, retry, ping, wasabisys verifier are all real config that is dropped). NUANCE / correction to the claim's severity narrative: (1) Coil 3's ImageLoader.Builder installs its OWN default Android DiskCache even with no .diskCache() call, so the "every cover/page re-downloads across cold starts" assertion is overstated — Coil's image disk cache persists across cold starts independently of OkHttp's HTTP cache. The truly lost piece is OkHttp's HTTP-layer cache (revalidation/Cache-Control honoring) and the 200MB sizing. (2) forceCacheForDados/offlineCacheInterceptor only ever applied to the api2.manhastro.net/dados JSON endpoint, NOT to image URLs, so their loss on the IMAGE client has minimal image-pipeline impact (they matter for the API path, which is handled separately by the Ktor stack). The genuinely image-relevant losses are: connect/read/write timeouts, retryOnConnectionFailure, pingInterval(15s) for HTTP/2 stall survival, and the *.s3.wasabisys.com hostname verifier (TLS host-mismatch bypass) — all real and absent.

**🟠 [High] Per-source auth headers on covers (Library / Home / Search / Details / History) — KMP rework covers omit explicit per-source headers and rely on a host-match interceptor with a documented silent-fail mode; native attaches headers per request** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — every cover call site builds the request via the source repo's buildImageRequest/buildItemsImageRequest, which attaches defaultHeaders (Cookie/User-Agent/Referer) as Coil httpHeaders for the exact request: MangaCard.kt:96-106 + 146-158, MangaHomeCard.kt:86-92 + 141-152, MangaSearchItems.kt:101-105, HeaderSection.kt:70-73 (details cover), all via BaseManga.buildImageRequest (BaseManga.kt:107-126) / buildItemsImageRequest (BaseManga.kt:194-208).
- **KMP:** Partial — rework covers use bare AsyncImage(model = coverUrl) / SubcomposeAsyncImage(model = coverUrl): YamiCoverImage.kt:81-87 (Library/Home/Search), DetailsScreen.kt:772-779 (header backdrop) + 906-929 (details cover), HistoryScreen.kt:283-292. These carry no headers and depend entirely on App.kt's CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor (App.kt:269-294) which matches the image URL host to a repo via findRepoByHost and injects defaultHeaders. SourceImageRequest.kt:24-29 explicitly documents this interceptor's silent-fail mode when the image CDN host is on a different subdomain than the source's stored base URL (e.g. tempsolo.lek-manga.net vs lekmanga.net) — 'Bug 4 layer 4'. The header-aware rememberSourceImageRequest helper exists but is NOT used by the rework cover composables (only the reader/home use it).
- **Explanation:** Cloudflare-protected sources require Cookie+User-Agent+Referer on cover requests. Native guarantees them per request. KMP's interceptor only injects headers when the image host resolves to a known repo AND that repo's defaultHeaders are already hydrated AND the host matches by apex/subdomain; for sources whose cover CDN is on a different subdomain than the stored base URL, or sources not yet hit this session, covers will 403/fail to load where native succeeds. This is a real regression on protected sources for the most-used cover surfaces (Library/History/Details/Home/Search).
- **Suggested fix:** Route the rework cover composables through the existing header-aware rememberSourceImageRequest(url, api, ...) helper (which also does ensureSiteInitialized hydration) instead of bare AsyncImage(model = url). Pass the source api/name down to YamiCoverImage, the Details cover, and HistoryItem so each cover request gets explicit defaultHeaders attached, matching native buildItemsImageRequest.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) attaches per-source auth headers per cover request: - BaseManga.buildImageRequest builds Coil NetworkHeaders from defaultHeaders and attaches via .httpHeaders(coilHeaders) per request: native-app/.../sources_repositry/common/BaseManga.kt:101-188 (buildImageRequest) and :189-209 (buildItemsImageRequest). (Claim cited 107-126/194-208; actual ranges are 101-188/189-209 — minor line drift, substance correct.) - Cover call sites route through repo-provided builders: MangaCard.kt:96-106 (produceState builds imageRequest via buildImageRequest) + :146-158 (AsyncImage model=imageRequest); MangaHomeCard.kt:86-92 + :141-152; MangaSearchItems.kt:101-105 (model = buildImageRequest(...)); HeaderSection.kt:70-78 (details cover, model = buildImageRequest(...)); History uses it too (HistoryItem.kt:75, HistoryViewModel.kt:184-185). ViewModels resolve sourcesRepository.getRepoByName(api).buildImageRequest(...) (LibraryViewModel.kt:442-443, MangaViewModel.kt:285-286, MangaDerailsViewModel.kt:71-72, HistoryViewModel.kt:184-185). Per-source overrides confirmed (e.g. ProMangaRepository.kt:112-134 attaches httpHeaders from defaultHeaders). KMP (rework) covers carry NO per-request headers and depend on the interceptor: - YamiCoverImage.kt:81-87 = bare AsyncImage(model = coverUrl); its own KDoc (line 45) says it relies on the singleton loader's "source-header interceptor". Used by Library (LibraryScreen.kt:1162), Home (HomeFeedGridCard.kt:62, HomeFeedRow.kt:92, FeaturedCarousel.kt:104), Search (SearchScreen.kt:499). No KMP MangaCard composable exists. - DetailsScreen.kt:772-779 (header backdrop AsyncImage(model=coverUrl)) and :906-929 (details cover SubcomposeAsyncImage(model=coverUrl)) — both bare. - HistoryScreen.kt:283-292 — bare AsyncImage(model = entry.mangaImageUrl). - The only header path is CoilSourceHeaderInterceptor (App.kt:269-294): matches URL host via SourcesRepository.findRepoByHost; if no repo matches OR match.defaultHeaders.isEmpty() it returns chain.proceed() with NO headers (App.kt:281-287) — the documented silent-fail. findRepoByHost (SourcesRepository.kt:191-211) matches by baseUrl/BASE_URL/imgBaseUrl host with apex/subdomain hostsMatch (:218-221) plus a DataStore fallback. defaultHeaders is empty until initSite()/ensureSiteInitialized() runs (BaseManga.kt:120-148: "_cachedHeaders null ... defaultHeaders returned empty/static-only maps — saved auth cookies were silently dropped"), so a source not yet fetched this session loses cover auth. - SourceImageRequest.kt:24-29 explicitly documents the interceptor's silent-fail / "Bug 4 layer 4" (tempsolo.lek-manga.net vs lekmanga.net). The header-aware rememberSourceImageRequest helper exists (SourceImageRequest.kt:34-120) but grep shows it is consumed ONLY by BlurredImageCoil.kt:99 and the reader — NOT by any cover surface. ReaderDecoderHints.kt:53-55 independently corroborates: "the rework's covers don't yet use a builder-level helper (they use AsyncImage(model = url) directly through the singleton loader)". (Note: SourceImageRequest.kt:174-175 KDoc postscript wrongly lists MangaCard/Details/Library as consumers — stale/false per actual usage grep.) Minor correction to the explanation: the subdomain-mismatch failure the claim emphasizes is partly mitigated — findRepoByHost's hostsMatch handles apex+subdomain (tempsolo.lek-manga.net DOES match lek-manga.net) and a DataStore fallback handles user-edited mirrors. The dominant, definitely-real failure modes are (a) repo's defaultHeaders empty because the source wasn't hit this session, and (b) image CDN host sharing no apex with any of the repo's three stored URLs. Both yield headerless cover requests where native succeeds.

**🟠 [High] Reader large-image (>99MB) compression pipeline — Native reader compresses decoded images larger than ~99MB before display; KMP reader has no such pipeline** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — PagerImageItem.kt:99-133 checks decoded img.size against maxBytes = 99L*1024*1024; under threshold renders directly, over threshold routes to PagerCompressedImageHandler (PagerImageItem.kt:143-198) which shows a 'Compressing image...' placeholder, triggers onStartImageCompression, and renders item.compressedPainter when isCompressed (PagerImageItem.kt:50-64). CompressionState / onRetryCompression are part of the reader state.
- **KMP:** No — grep for CompressionState / isCompressed / onStartImageCompression / compressedPainter across ui/presentation/domain/data/composeApp/shared returns zero matches. ReaderScreen.kt renders pages via SubcomposeAsyncImage with loading/error/success states only (ReaderScreen.kt:1417-1480); no oversized-bitmap branch, no compression, no 'Compressing image...' state.
- **Explanation:** Native guards against extremely large decoded bitmaps (huge webtoon pages) by compressing them before draw, with a dedicated compressing placeholder and retry. KMP will attempt to render the full decoded bitmap directly; on memory-constrained devices this risks OOM / draw failures on pages native handled gracefully, and the user loses the 'Compressing image...' state + its retry affordance.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the oversized-image branch: in the reader page composable, inspect the decoded image size on success and, above a threshold, route to a compression handler that emits a compressing placeholder, performs platform downscale/compression, and renders the compressed result with a retry path — mirroring PagerImageItem/PagerCompressedImageHandler.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) HAS the >99MB compression pipeline. /Users/.../native-app/.../reader/ui/reading_modes/PagerImageItem.kt: line 50-64 renders `item.compressedPainter` when `item.isCompressed` is true; lines 99-133 (the AsyncImagePainter.State.Success arm) read `img.size`, compare to `maxBytes = 99L*1024*1024` (line 101), and below threshold render directly via SubcomposeAsyncImage (107-118) while above threshold route to PagerCompressedImageHandler (121-132); the handler (143-198) fires `onStartImageCompression(...)` from a LaunchedEffect (169-173), shows PagerCompressionLoadingPlaceholder while `compressionState.isCompressing` (176-180), and on error offers `onRetryCompression(imageUrl)` (182-189); the literal "Compressing image..." text is at line 214. CompressionState.kt:3-7 defines `data class CompressionState(isCompressing, error, isCompleted)`. ReaderViewModel.kt:78-79 hold the `compressionStates` StateFlow; startImageCompression (580-643) launches a job that calls compressImageToSizeOptimized (669-698) — which down-scales the bitmap (bitmap.scale(finalWidth,finalHeight), line 697) so its allocationByteCount fits maxSizeBytes — wraps it in a BitmapPainter (605-607), and copies it into the item as isCompressed=true/compressedPainter (612-615); retryCompression at 645-649. All native line numbers in the claim verify exactly. KMP DOES NOT have any such pipeline. /Users/.../yami-kmp/ui/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/ui/reader/ReaderScreen.kt:1417-1494 renders each page with SubcomposeAsyncImage exposing only `loading` (1422-1447, spinner) and `error` (1448-1494, failed_to_load_image + per-page painter.restart() retry + Open-in-WebView) slots; the success path simply draws the full decoded bitmap with no size check, no maxBytes threshold, no compression branch, and no "Compressing image..." placeholder. Notably ReaderScreen.kt:1381 calls `.maxBitmapSize(Size(Dimension.Undefined, Dimension.Undefined))`, deliberately removing Coil's default 4096x4096 cap to decode webtoon strips at full resolution — the exact oversized-bitmap case native guards against. A repo-wide grep for CompressionState / isCompressed / onStartImageCompression / compressedPainter / onRetryCompression across :ui, :presentation, :domain, :data, :platform, :app, :composeApp, :shared returns ZERO reader-related matches; the only compression hits are the unrelated Settings "compress existing downloads" feature (SettingsState.kt:146 isCompressingDownloads; SettingsScreen.kt:380) and CBZ download notification/chunking code (CbzManager.kt:189 maxBytes=50_000_000). The absence is intentional and documented: /Users/.../yami-kmp/presentation/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/presentation/reader/ReaderState.kt:58-61 lists under "Deferred state fields": "Per-page bitmap compression (was the legacy `compressionStates` shim, now componentpruned in Phase 9.x.readervm.componentprune) — needs a cross-platform bitmap-compression pipeline." No legacy ReaderViewModel or compressionStates code remains in :shared (grep returns nothing), so the KDoc's "legacy already nopped this" claim could not be confirmed against the native source-of-truth, which clearly does NOT no-op compression.

**🟡 [Medium] Crossfade animation on covers and reader pages — crossfade(true) present on every native cover and reader page is missing on KMP rework covers and reader pages** _(Interaction)_

- **Native:** Yes — BaseManga.buildImageRequest sets .crossfade(true) (BaseManga.kt:186) and buildItemsImageRequest sets .crossfade(true) (BaseManga.kt:207); the reader builds pages via buildImageRequest (ReaderViewModel.kt:200,362) so reader pages also crossfade. Per-source overrides (e.g. SenkuroRepository, ProMangaRepository, ComickRepository, etc.) all also chain .crossfade(true).
- **KMP:** No — rework cover composables (YamiCoverImage.kt:81, DetailsScreen.kt:772/906, HistoryScreen.kt:283) use bare AsyncImage/SubcomposeAsyncImage with no .crossfade. The reader builds its ImageRequest inline (ReaderScreen.kt:1370-1406) and never calls .crossfade(true). The dead legacy BaseMangaRepository.buildImageRequest in :shared does set crossfade (BaseMangaRepository.kt:88,100) but it is not consumed by the rework UI.
- **Explanation:** Native fades every image in over the placeholder/previous content; KMP pops images in instantly. This is a visible, app-wide motion-polish regression across all cover surfaces and the reader. The image-quality memory and reader KDoc carefully preserve sizing/decoder hints but the crossfade was dropped silently.
- **Suggested fix:** Add .crossfade(true) to the reader page ImageRequest in ReaderScreen.kt and to the cover request paths (either inside rememberSourceImageRequest when adopted for covers, or directly on the AsyncImage builders) to match native's buildImageRequest/buildItemsImageRequest.

**🟡 [Medium] Reader per-page error pane — Open in WebView action — Native reader image-load error pane offers Retry + Open-in-WebView; KMP defers the Open-in-WebView half** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — ImageLoadError.kt:20-58 renders the failure message plus two BorderedPrimaryButtons: Retry (onRetry) and 'Open in browser' (action_open_in_browser → onOpenInWebView). Wired from PagerImageItem.kt:87-97.
- **KMP:** Partial — ReaderScreen.kt:1448-1480 error slot provides only the per-page Retry (painter.restart()). The KDoc at ReaderScreen.kt:1458-1461 states the 'Open in WebView' half is deferred pending a new ReaderEffect (OpenChapterInWebView) + route adapter + platform IntentLauncher (tracked in ARCHITECTURE.md §71).
- **Explanation:** When a page fails to load (commonly Cloudflare/anti-bot), native lets the user open that page/chapter in the in-app WebView to solve the challenge, then retry. KMP only offers retry, which will keep failing for challenge-gated pages — a functional dead-end native avoided.
- **Suggested fix:** Add the deferred OpenChapterInWebView ReaderEffect + route-adapter handler and surface a second 'Open in browser' button in the reader error slot alongside Retry, matching ImageLoadError.

**🟡 [Medium] Cover placeholder / error painters — Native covers pass explicit placeholder + error ColorPainters; KMP covers vary (tinted box, no error glyph on some; broken-image glyph on YamiCoverImage)** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MangaCard.kt:87-93 + 156-157 pass placeholder = ColorPainter(onSurface 12%) and error = ColorPainter(error 24%) to AsyncImage; MangaHomeCard.kt:78-84 + 150-151 same pattern; both use deterministic colored placeholder + colored error fill.
- **KMP:** Partial — YamiCoverImage.kt:69-96 shows a tinted placeholder box (outline 15%) and, on terminal error only, a centered BrokenImage glyph (28dp, tint outline 60%) — deliberately no loading spinner. Details cover uses a CircularProgressIndicator loading state (DetailsScreen.kt:911-918) and a surfaceVariant box; History cover (HistoryScreen.kt:283-292) shows neither placeholder painter nor error indicator (bare AsyncImage with only a clip/background from the Card).
- **Explanation:** Native uses a uniform colored placeholder + colored error fill across grid/list/home covers. KMP diverges per surface: YamiCoverImage adds a broken-image glyph native lacks; Details adds a spinner native lacks; History shows no error/placeholder treatment at all, so a failed history cover renders as an empty/transparent cell rather than native's error-tinted fill. These are noticeable visual-state divergences from the source of truth.
- **Suggested fix:** Standardize cover placeholder/error rendering to match native: a colored placeholder fill while loading and a colored error fill on failure across Library/Home/Search/Details/History. At minimum give the History cover an explicit error/placeholder treatment so failed thumbnails are not blank.

**⚪ [Low] Reader byte-progress vs native ProgressManager — Both show per-page progress but via completely different plumbing; native covers covers+pages uniformly via a global ProgressManager, KMP via per-platform fetcher observers + MVI repository** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — ProgressInterceptor (ProgressInterceptor.kt) is a network interceptor on the Coil OkHttp client that reports to a global ProgressManager singleton; the reader reads ProgressManager.getProgressFlow(url) (WebToonReadingMode.kt:223) to drive a determinate ring.
- **KMP:** Partial — Android uses OkHttpProgressInterceptor wrapping every response body (OkHttpProgressInterceptor.android.kt) feeding a PageProgressRepository (MVI), throttled to 50ms/1%; iOS/Desktop use a ktor3 HttpResponsePipeline observer (KtorPageProgressObserver.kt). Start/Complete/Failed come from a Coil per-request listener (ReaderScreen.kt:1400-1405). Functionally equivalent for the reader ring.
- **Explanation:** The user-visible reader progress ring is preserved with comparable throttling. The divergence is architectural (global mutable singleton vs MVI repository) and the KMP path additionally instruments cover requests it never displays progress for, but there is no clear user-facing regression.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix required for parity; optionally scope progress wrapping to reader requests to avoid the documented residual map entries for cover URLs.

**⚪ [Low] Loader-level maxBitmapSize / Coil version handling — KMP sets loader-level maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL) plus per-request maxBitmapSize overrides to defeat Coil 3.3+ downsampling; native (Coil 3.1.0) needs none of this** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Partial — native uses Coil 3.1.0 (app/build.gradle.kts:199-200) which did not aggressively apply the 4096x4096 cap to tall pages, so CoilModule sets no maxBitmapSize and per-source buildImageRequest only sets size(Pixels(screenWidthPx), Undefined) when screenWidthPx != 0 (BaseManga.kt:127-132).
- **KMP:** Yes — KMP uses Coil 3.4.0 (libs.versions.toml:26) and compensates: App.kt:325 sets loader-level maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL); rememberSourceImageRequest and the reader request additionally set per-request maxBitmapSize(Undefined, Undefined) (SourceImageRequest.kt:55/111, ReaderScreen.kt:1381) because the loader-level override does not always propagate.
- **Explanation:** This is a deliberate, well-documented compensation for the Coil version bump rather than a regression; the intended end-state (full-resolution tall webtoon decode) matches native. Risk is only that cover requests that do NOT go through rememberSourceImageRequest rely solely on the loader-level Size.ORIGINAL, which the code itself notes 'doesn't always propagate' — so some bare-AsyncImage covers could still be capped.
- **Suggested fix:** When routing covers through rememberSourceImageRequest (per the headers finding), the per-request maxBitmapSize override is inherited; verify bare-AsyncImage cover sites either adopt the helper or set the per-request override so the documented non-propagation of the loader-level cap cannot blur covers.

**⚪ [Low] AVIF decoder (Android) — Faithful port; aspect-ratio guard, RGB_565/ARGB_8888 selection, mutex, magic-byte detection all preserved** _(Component)_

- **Native:** Yes — HeifDecoder.kt:17-157 (class AvifDecoderCoil) registered in CoilModule.kt:64 via AvifDecoderCoil.Factory(). 10:1 aspect-ratio reject, RGB_565 for opaque / ARGB_8888 for alpha, decoderMutex, ftyp+avif/avis magic bytes, defensive recycle.
- **KMP:** Yes — platform/androidMain/.../AvifDecoderCoil.kt:35-163 is a verbatim port (named constants instead of magic numbers, Kermit logging instead of android.util.Log), registered via AndroidImageDecoderRegistry.kt:17-19, installed in App.kt:307+316. Behavior is byte-equivalent.
- **Explanation:** This load-bearing AVIF fix is preserved with full behavioral parity; the only differences are a Kermit-vs-Log logging swap and constant extraction, neither user-visible.
- **Suggested fix:** None — parity is high. (Note: the native AvifDecoderCoil was on Coil 3.1.0 and the port on 3.4.0; confirm the 3.4.0 Decoder.Factory.create SPI signature still matches, which the code already targets.)

**⚪ [Low] iOS / Desktop high-quality Skia decoder — KMP adds a CATMULL_ROM Skia decoder for iOS/Desktop that native (Android-only app) never needed** _(Component)_

- **Native:** No — native is Android-only and uses BitmapFactory's bilinear path; there is no iOS/Desktop target and no Skia decoder.
- **KMP:** Yes — HighQualitySkiaImageDecoder.kt registered via IosImageDecoderRegistry.kt:16-18 and DesktopImageDecoderRegistry.kt:16-18; replaces Coil's stock nearest-neighbor SkiaImageDecoder with Catmull-Rom cubic resampling, N32 pixel format (not RGB_565, to avoid screentone banding).
- **Explanation:** This is additive multiplatform work with no native counterpart to diverge from; it is the correct approach to match Android's decode sharpness on Skia targets. Documented as a load-bearing quality fix.
- **Suggested fix:** None — additive parity-restoring fix for non-Android platforms.

**⚪ [Low] Base64 / ZIP image-recovery converter — Native's downloadAndConvertImageBytes is dead code; KMP's Base64ImageConverter SPI is an orphaned, unwired interface (iOS ZIP extraction is a no-op stub)** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Partial — Base64ImageConverter.kt defines downloadAndConvertImageBytes (isValidImage / isZip / extractFirstImageFromZip / tryFindAndDecodeBase64) but grep shows zero callers in native — it is dead code (no orchestrator uses it).
- **KMP:** Partial — split into a :platform SPI interface Base64ImageConverter (Base64ImageConverter.kt:63-78) with Android (BitmapFactory+ZipInputStream), Desktop (ImageIO+ZipInputStream), and iOS (UIImage sniff; extractFirstImageFromZipBytes returns null — Phase 11 stub) actuals. The KDoc + the cluster269 postscript confirm NO Koin module binds it and the Phase 11 :data orchestrator (downloadAndConvertImageBytes) is not wired — it is consumer-orphaned.
- **Explanation:** Neither app actually exercises this recovery path today (native caller is dead, KMP orchestrator unwired), so there is no live behavioral regression. The latent divergence is that the KMP iOS actual cannot extract images from ZIP/CBZ-wrapped responses (returns null) whereas the native helper could on Android — relevant only if/when a Phase 11 orchestrator is wired.
- **Suggested fix:** Either remove the orphaned SPI/dead native helper, or, when wiring the Phase 11 :data orchestrator, implement the iOS ZIP extraction (Foundation/zlib) so the recovery path has parity across platforms. No action needed for current parity.

**⚪ [Low] DominantColorExtractor — KMP ships a bound-but-unused DominantColorExtractor whose KDoc claims library cover tinting; native has no dominant-color extraction at all** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** No — grep for Palette/Dominant/extractColor/vibrant/averageColor across native returns nothing; native does not extract or tint by dominant color.
- **KMP:** Partial — DominantColorExtractor.kt defines the SPI; Android (Palette.getDominantColor), iOS (1x1 CoreGraphics average), Desktop (SCALE_AREA_AVERAGING) actuals exist and are bound in Koin (PlatformModule.android/ios/desktop.kt:156/138/138). But grep for real .extract( consumers in ui/presentation/data/domain/composeApp returns zero — the KDoc's 'cover-art tinting in the library UI' consumer does NOT exist; it is an orphaned binding.
- **Explanation:** This is extra KMP scaffolding with no native counterpart and no live consumer, so it neither matches nor regresses native behavior. The risk is only the misleading KDoc claiming a live consumer that does not exist (audit hazard, not a user-facing bug).
- **Suggested fix:** Remove or correct the DominantColorExtractor KDoc claim of a live library-tinting consumer, and either wire the intended tinting feature or drop the unused SPI + Koin bindings to avoid dead code.

**⚪ [Low] Header backdrop blur behind Details header — Native blurs via a Coil RenderScript BlurTransformation (radius 25f, sample 8x); KMP blurs via Modifier.blur(24dp/8dp) and drops the transformation** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — native ImageWithGradientOverlay / InfoCompose build a Coil ImageRequest with transformations(BlurTransformation(context, radius=25f, sampling=8f)) (an Android RenderScript transform via RSToolkit), plus crossfade(true) (InfoCompose.kt:40).
- **KMP:** Partial — BlurredImageCoil.kt substitutes Modifier.blur(8.dp) for the Coil BlurTransformation (RenderScript dropped as non-multiplatform / API-31-deprecated); DetailsScreen header backdrop uses AsyncImage(...).blur(24dp) (DetailsScreen.kt:772-779) with a vertical surface-fade scrim. No crossfade.
- **Explanation:** The visual intent (blurred cover backdrop with gradient scrim) is preserved, but the blur is implemented differently (Compose Modifier.blur vs RenderScript transform) and radii differ (native 25f/8x sample vs KMP 8dp in BlurredImageCoil, 24dp in DetailsScreen backdrop). The two KMP blur radii are themselves inconsistent. Result is a subtly different blur strength and the loss of the crossfade fade-in on the backdrop.
- **Suggested fix:** Pick a single blur radius consistent with native's perceived strength and apply it uniformly; consider adding crossfade to the backdrop image. Acceptable as a documented multiplatform substitution otherwise.

### App Chrome / Splash  `app-chrome-splash`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 13 (🔴0 🟠2 🟡4 ⚪7)

> Native (source of truth) hosts the app in an AppCompatActivity that calls installSplashScreen() before super.onCreate(), then WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window,false) for edge-to-edge, and applies YamiMangaTheme (Material3) with a Scaffold that pads ONLY the bottom system inset to keep the top status bar edge-to-edge. All system-bar coloring/transparency/fullscreen is driven declaratively by the XML themes Theme.App.Starting -> Theme.YamiManga (transparent nav bar, translucent nav, windowFullscreen, windowNoTitle, full M3 token set, theme-adaptive splash background via ?attr/android:colorBackground + windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon). The KMP app reproduces the runtime structure faithfully (App.kt -> YamiTheme -> MainScreen Scaffold with contentWindowInsets bottom-only + BottomNavigationBar divider), and the Compose color/typography/shape tokens are byte-for-byte ports. The headline divergences are all in the Android resource/host layer: the KMP app/ module's Theme.App.Starting hardcodes a white splash background (white flash in dark mode) and drops the animated splash icon; the post-splash Theme.YamiManga is a bare AppCompat stub with NO status/nav-bar transparency, fullscreen, or window attributes (the native theme's transparent navigation bar, windowTranslucentNavigation, windowFullscreen, windowBackground are all absent); there is no values-night theme; the host uses enableEdgeToEdge() (which injects its own auto-contrast scrim/icon behavior) instead of native's plain setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) + theme-driven transparency; and the Admin testing-mode (ApiTestScreen) root branch present in native is dropped. On non-Android platforms (iOS/Desktop) the splash, edge-to-edge, and system-bar concerns have no native counterpart and are reasonable no-ops.

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for App Chrome / Splash</summary>

**🟠 [High] Splash screen background color — Splash window background is hardcoded white in KMP vs theme-adaptive in native** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../res/values/themes.xml:133-137 Theme.App.Starting sets <item name="windowSplashScreenBackground">?attr/android:colorBackground</item>, which resolves through postSplashScreenTheme=Theme.YamiManga to @color/yami_manga_background (#FEFBFF light, values-night/colors.xml:29 #1B1B1F dark). Splash background follows day/night.
- **KMP:** Partial — app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml:5-8 Theme.App.Starting sets <item name="windowSplashScreenBackground">@android:color/white</item>, a fixed opaque white regardless of dark/light mode.
- **Explanation:** On a device in dark mode, the KMP app shows a bright white splash flash on every cold start before the dark Compose UI mounts, whereas native shows a dark (#1B1B1F) splash that matches the post-splash dark theme. This is a visible, jarring launch regression for the app's primary dark-mode users and breaks the seamless splash->content handoff the SplashScreen API is designed for.
- **Suggested fix:** In app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml change windowSplashScreenBackground to ?attr/android:colorBackground (or @color/yami_manga_background) and add a values-night themes.xml mirroring native so the splash background tracks day/night.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: High). CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED. NATIVE (source of truth): /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml:133-137 defines Theme.App.Starting (parent Theme.SplashScreen) with windowSplashScreenBackground = ?attr/android:colorBackground and postSplashScreenTheme = @style/Theme.YamiManga. Theme.App.Starting exists ONLY in values/ (grep found no values-night/values-v26 override), and uses androidx.core:core-splashscreen 1.0.1 (native-app/app/build.gradle.kts:211). It is the launch theme (AndroidManifest.xml:30,37) and installSplashScreen() is called (native-app/.../me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:200). The yami_manga_background color is day/night: values/colors.xml:79 = #FEFBFF, values-night/colors.xml:29 = #1B1B1F. Net result: native splash background IS day/night-adaptive. KMP: /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml:5-8 defines Theme.App.Starting (parent Theme.SplashScreen) with windowSplashScreenBackground = @android:color/white (fixed opaque white) and postSplashScreenTheme = @style/Theme.YamiManga. The :app module has ONLY a values/ resource dir (no values-night), so white applies in all UI modes. It is the launch theme (app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:35,43) and installSplashScreen() is invoked (app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MainActivity.kt:7,20). composeApp has no themes.xml of its own. Both apps use core-splashscreen 1.0.1 (libs.versions.toml:48). So on a dark-mode cold start the KMP app shows a fixed white splash while native shows a dark/adaptive splash. This regression is REAL. INACCURACY IN CLAIM'S MECHANISM: The claim says ?attr/android:colorBackground 'resolves through postSplashScreenTheme=Theme.YamiManga to @color/yami_manga_background'. That is not how ?attr resolution works — the windowSplashScreenBackground attribute is resolved against the SPLASH theme in effect (Theme.App.Starting / its Theme.SplashScreen DayNight base), NOT the postSplashScreenTheme (which only applies after installSplashScreen swaps it post-splash). The native dark splash color is therefore the system DayNight android:colorBackground, not provably exactly #1B1B1F. The day/night-adaptive-vs-fixed-white conclusion and severity are nonetheless accurate.

**🟠 [High] Post-splash app theme (system bar / fullscreen attributes) — KMP post-splash Theme.YamiManga is a bare AppCompat stub missing all of native's window/system-bar attributes** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../res/values/themes.xml:88-124 Theme.YamiManga parent Theme.Material3.DayNight.NoActionBar declares android:navigationBarColor=@android:color/transparent, android:windowTranslucentNavigation=true, android:windowFullscreen=true, android:windowNoTitle=true, android:windowContentOverlay=@null, android:windowBackground=@color/black (values-night windowBackground=@color/white), plus the full M3 color token set (colorPrimary..colorSurfaceContainer*).
- **KMP:** Partial — app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml:10 declares <style name="Theme.YamiManga" parent="Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar" /> with an EMPTY body: no navigationBarColor, no windowTranslucentNavigation, no windowFullscreen, no windowNoTitle, no windowBackground, no M3 color tokens. Parent is AppCompat (not Material3).
- **Explanation:** The Android-host window theme governs the navigation/status bar transparency and the pre-Compose window background. Native makes the navigation bar transparent and translucent and the window fullscreen at the theme level; the KMP stub leaves these at the AppCompat defaults, so the system navigation bar will not be transparent the same way, the window background flashes a different color during config-change/recreate, and the theme parent change (Material3->AppCompat) can alter system-controlled chrome (e.g., default statusBar/navBar handling). The KDoc in app/res/themes.xml admits 'Phase 10/11 will reconcile the full theme from the source project' — this is an unfinished migration stub.
- **Suggested fix:** Port the native Theme.YamiManga verbatim into the KMP app/ module (Material3 parent + navigationBarColor transparent + windowTranslucentNavigation + windowFullscreen + windowNoTitle + windowBackground + full M3 token set) and add a values-night variant, so the Android window chrome matches native before Compose mounts.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml:88-124 defines `<style name="Theme.YamiManga" parent="Theme.Material3.DayNight.NoActionBar">` with: windowBackground=@color/black (L102), windowNoTitle=true (L115), windowActionBar=true (L116), windowContentOverlay=@null (L117), windowFullscreen=true (L118), navigationBarColor=@android:color/transparent (L119), windowTranslucentNavigation=true (L120), plus full M3 token set colorPrimary..colorSurfaceContainer* (L89-114). values-night/themes.xml:88-122 carries the same window attrs on Theme.YamiManga.Dark with windowBackground=@color/white (L102). Theme.App.Starting (values/themes.xml:133-137) sets postSplashScreenTheme=@style/Theme.YamiManga. KMP: app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml:10 is `<style name="Theme.YamiManga" parent="Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar" />` — empty self-closing element. NO navigationBarColor, NO windowTranslucentNavigation, NO windowFullscreen, NO windowNoTitle, NO windowContentOverlay, NO windowBackground, NO M3 color tokens. Parent is AppCompat (not Material3). KDoc L3-4 states 'Phase 10/11 will reconcile the full theme from the source project.' No values-night/ or values-v26/ variants exist in the KMP app module (find returned none); colors.xml has 0 'yami_manga' tokens (grep -c = 0). Both AndroidManifests apply Theme.App.Starting whose postSplashScreenTheme=Theme.YamiManga (KMP app/.../AndroidManifest.xml:35,43; native native-app/app/.../AndroidManifest.xml:30,37), so this window theme is the active post-splash theme at runtime in both apps — the divergence is load-bearing. Every specific attribute, the claimed parent change, the claimed line numbers (native 88-124, KMP 10), and the values-night windowBackground=@color/white detail all match exactly.

**🟡 [Medium] Splash animated icon — KMP splash omits the windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon shown by native** _(Icon)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../res/values/themes.xml:136 <item name="windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon">@drawable/ic_launcher_foreground</item> renders the app icon centered on the splash screen.
- **KMP:** No — app/src/main/res/values/themes.xml:5-8 Theme.App.Starting declares only windowSplashScreenBackground + postSplashScreenTheme; no windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon item (the ic_launcher_foreground.xml drawable does exist in app/res/drawable, so it is just unreferenced).
- **Explanation:** Native shows the branded launcher-foreground icon during the splash; KMP shows a blank/system-default splash with no icon. This is a branding/visual regression at every cold start, and inconsistent with the system splash on devices that would otherwise pull the default launcher icon.
- **Suggested fix:** Add <item name="windowSplashScreenAnimatedIcon">@drawable/ic_launcher_foreground</item> to the KMP Theme.App.Starting to match native.

**🟡 [Medium] Dark/night resource theme — KMP app/ module has no values-night themes/colors; native does** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../res/values-night/themes.xml and values-night/colors.xml provide the night Theme.YamiManga.Dark window background (@color/white inverted), dark M3 tokens, and dark splash colorBackground (#1B1B1F).
- **KMP:** No — only app/src/main/res/values exists (verified: find returns a single values dir, no values-night, no values-v26). The Compose layer handles dark mode at runtime via YamiTheme(darkTheme=...), but the Android window/splash resource layer has no night variant.
- **Explanation:** Because there is no values-night resource theme, the pre-Compose window background and the splash background cannot adapt to dark mode at the Android resource level. Combined with the white-splash finding, dark-mode users get a non-adaptive launch window. The Compose UI itself still goes dark once mounted, so this is scoped to the launch/window-decoration window of time rather than in-app content.
- **Suggested fix:** Add app/src/main/res/values-night/themes.xml (and colors.xml if referencing color resources) mirroring native's night theme so the window/splash decoration adapts to dark mode.

**🟡 [Medium] Edge-to-edge enablement mechanism — KMP uses enableEdgeToEdge() (auto scrim/contrast); native uses WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) + theme-driven transparency** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../MainActivity.kt:203 calls WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false) after super.onCreate(); system-bar transparency comes from the XML theme (navigationBarColor transparent, windowTranslucentNavigation). No enableEdgeToEdge().
- **KMP:** Partial — app/.../MainActivity.kt:21 calls androidx.activity.enableEdgeToEdge() before super.onCreate(). enableEdgeToEdge() not only sets decorFitsSystemWindows(false) but also forces transparent system bars with an automatic light/dark scrim and auto-adjusts status/nav icon appearance based on the underlying content luminance.
- **Explanation:** enableEdgeToEdge() applies the Android-13+ default behavior: it overrides whatever navigation/status bar color the theme set and applies a translucent scrim + automatic icon-contrast switching. Native instead leaves the bars transparent/translucent purely via theme attributes with no auto-scrim. The practical divergence is the system-bar scrim and the auto light/dark icon switching: native's status/nav bar icons follow the theme (and the bars are translucent), while KMP's icons flip automatically based on content brightness and the bars get the framework's default edge-to-edge scrim. This can produce a subtly different status/nav bar appearance (different scrim tint, different icon polarity) than native.
- **Suggested fix:** To match native exactly, replace enableEdgeToEdge() with WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false) and let the (ported) Theme.YamiManga drive bar transparency; or pass an explicit SystemBarStyle to enableEdgeToEdge() that reproduces native's transparent-nav / translucent-status posture. Verify status/nav icon polarity matches native in both light and dark mode.

**🟡 [Medium] Status/navigation bar icon appearance (light/dark) — Neither side sets isAppearanceLightStatusBars/NavigationBars explicitly; appearance source differs** _(State)_

- **Native:** Partial — native sets only WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) and theme transparency; no explicit isAppearanceLightStatusBars call (verified by grep). Icon contrast falls back to the framework/theme default for the translucent bars. A private setupTransparentNavigationBar() exists (MainActivity.kt:582) but is NOT called from onCreate (grep shows only its declaration).
- **KMP:** Partial — KMP relies on enableEdgeToEdge()'s automatic light/dark icon switching (driven by SystemBarStyle.auto defaults); no explicit isAppearanceLightStatusBars call in composeApp/ui (verified by grep).
- **Explanation:** Because native never explicitly controls bar-icon polarity and uses theme-translucent bars, while KMP's enableEdgeToEdge() actively auto-toggles icon polarity per content luminance, the status/navigation bar icon color can differ between the two apps on the same screen (e.g., dark icons on KMP where native shows light icons, or vice versa) depending on what content sits under the bar. This is a concrete, observable system-bar appearance divergence stemming from the different edge-to-edge mechanism.
- **Suggested fix:** Pick the intended polarity explicitly (WindowInsetsControllerCompat.isAppearanceLightStatusBars/NavigationBars) to match native's observed behavior, or configure enableEdgeToEdge() SystemBarStyle to lock the polarity rather than relying on auto-contrast, then compare against native on representative screens.

**⚪ [Low] Scaffold inset consumption for bottom bar — Native pads only calculated bottom padding; KMP consumes the whole padding via Modifier.padding(paddingValues) after restricting contentWindowInsets** _(Spacing)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../MainActivity.kt:567-577 the content Box uses Modifier.padding(bottom = paddingValues.calculateBottomPadding()) only, explicitly leaving the top edge-to-edge ('apply only bottom padding so top is still edge-to-edge').
- **KMP:** Partial — App.kt:359 sets contentWindowInsets = WindowInsets.systemBars.only(WindowInsetsSides.Bottom), then App.kt:373 wraps content in Box(Modifier.padding(paddingValues)) applying ALL four edges of the (now bottom-only) padding values.
- **Explanation:** The end result is equivalent for the top edge (both keep the status bar edge-to-edge because the Scaffold's contentWindowInsets is restricted to the bottom), but the mechanism differs: native hard-restricts to calculateBottomPadding(), while KMP relies on contentWindowInsets already being bottom-only so the full padding it then applies is effectively just bottom. Behaviorally near-identical, but the KMP version also picks up the bottomBar height padding the same way; functionally a wash. Documented as a low-severity structural divergence for completeness.
- **Suggested fix:** No functional change required; optionally align the comment/mechanism with native (apply only calculateBottomPadding) for clarity, but current behavior matches the edge-to-edge intent.

**⚪ [Low] Root Surface wrapper — KMP wraps MainScreen in a Surface(fillMaxSize); native applies the Scaffold directly under the theme** _(Component)_

- **Native:** No — native-app/.../MainActivity.kt:339-421 applies YamiMangaTheme { ... MainScreen() } and MainScreen() (line 553) is a bare Scaffold with no enclosing Surface.
- **KMP:** Yes — App.kt:341-345 wraps content as YamiTheme { Surface(modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()) { MainScreen() } }, adding a full-screen Material Surface (default color = colorScheme.surface) behind the Scaffold.
- **Explanation:** The added Surface paints the theme surface color behind everything. With the matching color schemes this is visually near-identical to native (the Scaffold itself also paints its background), but it introduces an extra elevation-0 surface layer not present in native and can subtly affect the window background color seen behind transparent system bars (surface color vs Scaffold/window background). Low impact given identical surface tokens.
- **Suggested fix:** Optional: drop the extra Surface or confirm its color equals the window/Scaffold background so the area behind translucent system bars matches native exactly.

**⚪ [Low] Activity base class — Native MainActivity extends AppCompatActivity; KMP extends ComponentActivity** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../MainActivity.kt:95 class MainActivity : AppCompatActivity() (with @AndroidEntryPoint Hilt).
- **KMP:** Partial — app/.../MainActivity.kt:18 class MainActivity : ComponentActivity().
- **Explanation:** AppCompatActivity vs ComponentActivity differ in AppCompat theming/vector-drawable compat and night-mode delegate (AppCompatDelegate). Native's window theme is Material3.DayNight under AppCompat; the KMP stub theme is Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar but the activity is ComponentActivity, so the AppCompat night-mode delegate is not engaged. Since dark mode is driven by Compose (YamiTheme), this rarely matters in practice, but it is a real host-level divergence that affects any AppCompat-dependent resource resolution and the day/night attribute application on the window theme.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide intentionally: if relying on the AppCompat DayNight theme attributes for the window, extend AppCompatActivity to engage the delegate; otherwise switch the stub theme parent off AppCompat. Align with native by using AppCompatActivity to reduce window-theming surprises.

**⚪ [Low] Admin testing-mode root branch — Native root composable branches to ApiTestScreen when Admin.testingMode; KMP App() has no such branch** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../MainActivity.kt:344-420 inside YamiMangaTheme: if (Admin.testingMode) { ApiTestScreen(api, context, coroutineScope) } else { MainScreen() }.
- **KMP:** No — App.kt:341-345 unconditionally renders MainScreen() inside YamiTheme; no Admin.testingMode gate, no ApiTestScreen entry at the root.
- **Explanation:** This is a developer/QA-only screen (API testing harness) gated behind Admin.testingMode, not a user-facing flow, so user-impact is minimal. It is nonetheless a divergence at the app-chrome/root composition level: the native root can swap the entire UI to the API test screen, the KMP root cannot. Flagged as Low because it is dev-only.
- **Suggested fix:** If the API test harness is still wanted on KMP, add an Admin.testingMode branch at the App() root (or a debug-only nav entry). Otherwise document the intentional removal.

**⚪ [Low] System back / predictive back — Both enable OnBackInvokedCallback at manifest level; KMP intentionally drops upstream BackHandler usage at NavGraph** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — native-app/.../AndroidManifest.xml:26 android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true"; native NavGraphV2/Home/Library used BackHandler blocks (per KMP App.kt KDoc item 4, the upstream had BackHandler(enabled=false) on Library and Home BackHandler).
- **KMP:** Partial — app/.../AndroidManifest.xml:31 also sets android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="true" (parity). However App.kt:108-114 KDoc documents that the upstream BackHandler calls are intentionally dropped (no commonMain BackHandler shim), relying on default Compose Navigation back-stack pop.
- **Explanation:** Manifest-level predictive-back is at parity. The behavioral note: native's Library BackHandler(enabled=false) was a documented no-op (it only prevented popping past start, which is already Compose Navigation's default), so dropping it does not change observable back behavior. No other back-flow chrome divergence found at the app-chrome level (per-screen BackHandlers are out of this section's scope).
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed for app-chrome parity; if any screen relied on a non-no-op BackHandler, address it in that screen's audit (a commonMain BackHandler expect/actual is the documented TODO).

**⚪ [Low] Screen-on / secure-window flags — Neither native nor KMP sets FLAG_SECURE or FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON — parity confirmed** _(State)_

- **Native:** No — grep across native-app for FLAG_SECURE / FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON / keepScreenOn finds no window-flag usage (only Intent flags). The reader hides only the navigation bar (ReaderScreen.kt:768-786 HideSystemBars), no keep-screen-on.
- **KMP:** No — grep across composeApp/ui/app for FLAG_SECURE / keepScreenOn finds none; the reader port (HideNavigationBarSideEffect.android.kt:34-49) hides only the navigation bar, matching native exactly.
- **Explanation:** Confirmed parity: there is no secure-window or keep-screen-on behavior in either implementation, so there is no regression here. The reader's hide-navigation-bar behavior is a faithful verbatim port (BEHAVIOR_DEFAULT, status bar untouched, nav bar restored on dispose).
- **Suggested fix:** No action required.

**⚪ [Low] Theme color/typography/shape tokens — Compose theme tokens are byte-for-byte equivalent across native and KMP** _(Color)_

- **Native:** Yes — native YamiMangaTheme (theme/Theme.kt) DarkColorScheme/LightColorScheme + Type.kt (Gellix on bodyLarge/titleMedium/titleSmall) + Shapes (4/8/12/16/0 dp). pureBlack overrides background+surfaceContainer to Color.Black in dark.
- **KMP:** Yes — ui/.../YamiColors.kt YamiDark/LightColorScheme match every hex verbatim (dark background #15202B, etc.); YamiTypography.kt yamiTypography() applies Gellix to the same 3 slots with same sizes/weights; YamiTheme.kt applies the same pureBlack background+surfaceContainer Color.Black override. YamiShapes assumed matching (not shown here).
- **Explanation:** This is a positive parity confirmation, recorded so the audit is explicit: the runtime Compose theme (the part that actually colors the app chrome and content once mounted) is a faithful port. The only chrome divergences are in the Android window/splash XML resource layer and the host edge-to-edge mechanism, not in the Compose color/type/shape tokens.
- **Suggested fix:** No action required for tokens; ensure YamiShapes also matches native Shapes (extraLarge=0.dp) if not already verified in the typography/shape audit.

### Data — Room Schema & Migrations  `data-room-schema`

**Parity verdict:** ParityHigh  ·  **Findings:** 9 (🔴0 🟠0 🟡3 ⚪6)

> The Room database SCHEMA (entities, columns, column types, indices, primary keys, foreign keys, DB version, the 7 migrations, and the 5 type converters) is a faithful, near-byte-identical port from native v8 to KMP v8. All 6 entities (SavedMangaEntity, SavedChapterEntity, HistoryItemD, ChapterNotification, ChapterDownloadEntity, SourcesEntity) preserve identical table names, columns, defaults, indices, and PK/FK declarations; both DBs are version 8 with the same DATABASE_NAME = "manga_database"; all 7 migration objects (MIGRATION_1_2 .. MIGRATION_7_8) carry verbatim-identical SQL; the DownloadingState and SourceState enums match constant-for-constant so the enum-name converters round-trip identically; date/string converters preserve the exact on-disk wire formats. The headline DIVERGENCES are not in the schema but in the DAO surface and DB-builder wiring: (1) the Library metrics query was rewritten from native's single LEFT JOIN ... GROUP BY m.id (SavedMangaWithMetrics) to a saved_chapters-only GROUP BY mangaId (MangaChapterMetrics) with the join now done in Kotlin — a deliberate fix for a BundledSQLiteDriver Flow-invalidation bug, but it changes zero-chapter-manga semantics; (2) the two PagingSource download DAO methods were dropped (Room paging is Android-only); (3) every DAO had large numbers of methods pruned as documented dead code; (4) KMP relies on BundledSQLiteDriver, whose foreign-key enforcement defaults OFF (vs Android Room ON) and is never re-enabled, so the saved_chapters onDelete=CASCADE will not fire automatically. exportSchema was flipped false→true (additive, harmless).

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Data — Room Schema & Migrations</summary>

**🟡 [Medium] Database builder / foreign-key enforcement — saved_chapters onDelete=CASCADE foreign key will not auto-cascade on KMP because foreign keys are not enabled on BundledSQLiteDriver** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - native Room on Android enables PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON by default; SavedChapterEntity declares ForeignKey(parentColumns=[id], childColumns=[mangaId], onDelete=CASCADE) at native SavedChapterEntity.kt:13-20, so deleting a saved_manga row cascades its chapters. DatabaseModule.kt:30-48 builds the DB with no explicit FK toggle (default ON).
- **KMP:** Partial - identical ForeignKey/CASCADE declared at shared SavedChapterEntity.kt:22-29, but KMP uses BundledSQLiteDriver (MangaDatabaseFactory.kt:35 .setDriver(BundledSQLiteDriver())) whose SQLite default is foreign_keys=OFF, and no callback/PRAGMA re-enables it (grep for foreign_keys/PRAGMA/addCallback in shared/src returned nothing). So a raw DELETE on saved_manga will NOT cascade-delete saved_chapters.
- **Explanation:** Room on Android turns FK enforcement on automatically; with the bundled SQLite driver used across all KMP targets, FK enforcement must be enabled explicitly (e.g. an onOpen callback executing 'PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON'). Neither MangaDatabaseFactory nor any platform builder does so. In practice the LIVE deletion path (LibraryDeo.removeMangaWithChapters, shared LibraryDeo.kt:62-68) deletes saved_chapters, notifications, and history explicitly before deleting the manga, so the cascade rarely fires; but any code path that deletes a manga row directly (or future code relying on the declared cascade) will silently orphan saved_chapters rows on KMP where native would cascade. This is a behavioral divergence from the source of truth and a latent data-integrity risk.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a RoomDatabase callback (or setQueryCallback/onOpen hook) in MangaDatabaseFactory.buildMangaDatabase() that runs 'PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON' on every connection open, matching Android Room's default-on behavior, so the declared onDelete=CASCADE on saved_chapters is actually enforced on all KMP targets.

**🟡 [Medium] Library metrics query (MangaDao) — Native computes per-manga metrics with a single LEFT JOIN ... GROUP BY m.id returning the embedded manga row; KMP rewrote it to a saved_chapters-only GROUP BY mangaId and joins in Kotlin** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - MangaDao.getSavedMangaWithMetricsFlow() runs `SELECT m.*, COUNT(c.id) AS totalChapters, SUM(...) ..., MAX(c.lastReadDate) AS lastReadTs FROM saved_manga AS m LEFT JOIN saved_chapters AS c ON c.mangaId = m.id GROUP BY m.id` returning Flow<List<SavedMangaWithMetrics>> with @Embedded manga (native MangaDao.kt:16-31; SavedMangaWithMetrics.kt:7-14). LEFT JOIN guarantees every manga (incl. those with zero chapters) yields a row with totalChapters=0.
- **KMP:** Partial - the JOIN query is gone; replaced by MangaDao.getAllChapterMetricsFlow() running `SELECT mangaId, COUNT(*) AS totalChapters, SUM(...) ..., MAX(lastReadDate) AS lastReadTs FROM saved_chapters GROUP BY mangaId` returning Flow<List<MangaChapterMetrics>> (no manga columns) at shared MangaDao.kt:64-77; MangaChapterMetrics.kt:18-30. The manga<->metrics join is done in Kotlin in LibraryRepositoryImpl.observeLibrary() per the KMP MangaDao/MangaDatabaseFactory KDoc.
- **Explanation:** This is a deliberate, documented workaround (KMP MangaDatabaseFactory.kt:16-23 and MangaChapterMetrics.kt:5-17 explain that on Desktop with BundledSQLiteDriver a LEFT JOIN ... GROUP BY aggregate Flow did not re-emit after writes). Functionally the metrics are the same, but there is a subtle semantic change: native's LEFT JOIN emits a metrics row for EVERY manga including chapter-less ones (totalChapters=0); KMP's GROUP BY saved_chapters only emits rows for manga that HAVE at least one chapter, so a manga with zero saved chapters has no MangaChapterMetrics row and the repository must default its counts to 0. If the Kotlin-side combine in LibraryRepositoryImpl does not explicitly synthesize zeros for chapter-less manga, those manga could be dropped or show wrong counts. The query is correct as a chapter aggregate but is no longer a self-contained library projection.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify LibraryRepositoryImpl.observeLibrary() defaults missing MangaChapterMetrics (manga with no chapters) to totalChapters=0/readCount=0/etc rather than excluding them, so library list parity with native's LEFT JOIN is preserved. Keep the split-query approach (it fixes the real Desktop invalidation bug) but document/test the zero-chapter case.

**🟡 [Medium] Downloads list (ChapterDownloadDao paging) — Native PagingSource-backed download queries are absent in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes - ChapterDownloadDao exposes `observeAllDownloadsPaged(): PagingSource<Int, ChapterDownloadEntity>` and `observeDownloadsByStatePaged(states): PagingSource<Int, ChapterDownloadEntity>` plus `getCountByState(state): Flow<Int>` (native ChapterDownloadDao.kt:120-133) for paged, memory-safe download list rendering (the non-paged variant is @Deprecated 'to avoid CursorWindow overflow', native ChapterDownloadDao.kt:96-98).
- **KMP:** No - both PagingSource methods and getCountByState are removed; only the non-paginated `observeAllDownloads(): Flow<List<ChapterDownloadEntity>>` remains (shared ChapterDownloadDao.kt:168-169). The KDoc (shared ChapterDownloadDao.kt:162-167) states Room's LimitOffsetPagingSource is Android-only and defers per-platform Pager to a future Phase 10.
- **Explanation:** Room KMP cannot generate PagingSource (LimitOffsetPagingSource is Android-only), so the migration legitimately had to drop the paged queries. However this is a real behavior regression vs the source of truth: native intentionally used pagination to avoid CursorWindow overflow on large download lists, and the non-paginated query it kept is explicitly @Deprecated for that exact reason. On KMP the entire downloads table is loaded into a single List<ChapterDownloadEntity> in memory, which can OOM / overflow with large download histories. The deprecation marker was also dropped.
- **Suggested fix:** Reinstate paged download lists on a per-platform basis (e.g. expect/actual Pager backed by Room paging on Android and a manual LIMIT/OFFSET query Flow on iOS/Desktop), or at minimum bound observeAllDownloads with a LIMIT to avoid loading an unbounded result set into memory. Re-add a count Flow if the UI needs queued/failed badges.

**⚪ [Low] StringListConverter (List<String> column persistence) — Null/empty/invalid JSON tolerance differs: native Gson returns null gracefully, KMP kotlinx.serialization throws** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** Yes - native StringListConverter.fromString(value: String) uses Gson.fromJson, which returns null for the JSON literal 'null' or empty input rather than throwing (native StringListConverter.kt:11-14).
- **KMP:** Partial - shared StringListConverter.fromString(value: String) uses Json.decodeFromString(ListSerializer(String.serializer()), value) (shared StringListConverter.kt:15-17), which throws SerializationException on empty string, the literal 'null', or malformed JSON.
- **Explanation:** For well-formed JSON arrays the wire format is identical (a bare JSON array of strings), so normal rows round-trip identically and existing DB data deserializes fine (correctly noted in the KMP migration note). The divergence is only at the edge: a NULL or empty/garbage value in a localImagePaths/genres column would make native return null (and the non-null Kotlin field would then NPE only when dereferenced) whereas KMP throws a SerializationException at read time inside Room's cursor mapping, potentially crashing the query. Both are buggy, but the failure mode and crash surface differ. Low likelihood because these columns are always written by the same converter as JSON arrays.
- **Suggested fix:** Make KMP StringListConverter.fromString defensive: return emptyList() (or null-equivalent) when value is blank or equals 'null', and wrap decodeFromString in a try/catch returning emptyList() on SerializationException, matching native's lenient Gson behavior and avoiding read-time crashes on legacy/garbage rows.

**⚪ [Low] Entities parcelability (SavedChapterEntity, ChapterNotification) — @Parcelize / Parcelable implementation dropped in KMP** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - SavedChapterEntity is `@Parcelize ... : Parcelable` (native SavedChapterEntity.kt:25-41) and ChapterNotification is `@Parcelize data class ... : Parcelable` (native ChapterNotification.kt:10-27), allowing them to be passed via Android Bundle/SavedStateHandle/nav args.
- **KMP:** No - both are plain data classes; @Parcelize and the Parcelable supertype are removed (shared SavedChapterEntity.kt:34, shared ChapterNotification.kt:17). The KMP migration notes explicitly state Parcelable was dropped as Android-only, with kotlinx.serialization @Serializable planned for a later phase 'if needed'.
- **Explanation:** This does not affect the on-disk schema at all (Parcelable is purely an in-memory/IPC concern). It is a correct KMP port decision since Parcelable is Android-only. It is recorded only because it is a concrete divergence from the source of truth: any native code path that relied on putting these entities directly into a Bundle / nav argument / SavedStateHandle would need a different serialization mechanism on KMP. No evidence the schema layer depends on it.
- **Suggested fix:** No schema action needed. If KMP navigation/state-restoration needs to pass these entities, add @Serializable (kotlinx.serialization) to the entities (it is already a dependency for StringListConverter) rather than reintroducing Parcelable.

**⚪ [Low] MangaDatabase exportSchema — exportSchema flipped from false (native) to true (KMP) with schema JSON now generated to shared/schemas** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - @Database(... exportSchema = false) (native MangaDatabase.kt:36).
- **KMP:** Partial - @Database(... exportSchema = true) (shared MangaDatabase.kt:45) with room { schemaDirectory("$projectDir/schemas") } configured (shared/build.gradle.kts:226-227) and a generated me.manga.kira.data.local.MangaDatabase schema folder present.
- **Explanation:** This is an additive, intentional change (documented at shared MangaDatabase.kt:28-31). exportSchema=true only affects build-time schema JSON emission and auto-migration validation; it has zero effect on the runtime DB shape, version, or data. It actually improves the KMP build by enabling Room to validate schema/migration consistency. Recorded for completeness as a divergence from the source-of-truth annotation value.
- **Suggested fix:** No fix required. Keep exportSchema=true and ensure the generated schema JSON is committed so Room can validate future migrations; optionally add the same schema export to the native build for symmetry (not necessary).

**⚪ [Low] Per-platform database file location (iOS/Desktop) — KMP places the DB file in platform-specific user directories; only Android matches native's getDatabasePath location** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - native is Android-only and stores manga_database under the app's standard /data/data/<pkg>/databases/ path (Room.databaseBuilder with context+name, DatabaseModule.kt:30-34).
- **KMP:** Partial - Android actual uses appContext.getDatabasePath(DATABASE_NAME) (DatabaseBuilder.android.kt:23-27) matching native; iOS uses NSDocumentDirectory/manga_database (DatabaseBuilder.ios.kt:12-21); Desktop uses ~/.yami-manga/manga_database (DatabaseBuilder.desktop.kt:8-12).
- **Explanation:** The Android KMP path matches native exactly, so existing native users' databases will be found and migrated normally. The iOS and Desktop locations are new platforms with no native counterpart, so there is no parity regression there — it is simply new platform behavior. Recorded as informational: the schema and migrations are identical across all targets; only the on-disk file path differs per platform, which is expected and correct for a multiplatform app.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed. The Android path matches the source of truth. For iOS, consider excluding the DB from iCloud backup (NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey) if the DB is regenerable cache, but that is a platform polish item, not a parity defect.

**⚪ [Low] DAO method surface (dead-code pruning across all DAOs) — KMP DAOs dropped a large number of native DAO methods, documented as unreached dead code** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - native DAOs expose many extra members, e.g. ChapterDao (toggleChapterRead, deleteChaptersByIds, removeAllChaptersForManga, getBookmarkedChapters, insertChapter, getChaptersByIds, isChapterDownloadedFlow, updateChapterLastReadDate, updateChapterLocalPathsByUrl, getChaptersByMangaIdR, update), MangaDao (getSavedMangaWithMetricsFlow, saveManga, saveChapters, isMangaSaved/Flow, getIdByUrl, getMangaByApi, getMangaIdsByApi, removeMangaById, searchMangaByTitle, getApiByLocalId, update), NotificationDao (~21 methods), SourcesDao (update/delete/getSourcesByEnabled/getSourceNamesByState/updateBaseUrlAndVersionByName/updateImageBaseUrlAndVersionByName/updateSiteStateByName/deleteByName + transactions), StatisticsDeo (7 *Once suspend variants), HistoryDao (getHistoryByManga/getHistoryByChapter/deleteHistoryByManga/getHistoryByApi/update), LibraryDeo (getSavedMangaTitlesFlow/deleteChaptersByMangaId/deleteMangaByUrl/deleteMangaByTitle/deleteMangaWithChapters/removeManga).
- **KMP:** Partial - each KMP DAO retains only the methods with live reachers; the removals are exhaustively documented in per-file Phase 9.x componentprune KDoc headers (e.g. shared ChapterDao.kt:11-70, MangaDao.kt:11-60, NotificationDao.kt:13-72, SourcesDao.kt:11-59, StatisticsDeo.kt:7-48, HistoryDao.kt:14-39, ChapterDownloadDao.kt:12-102). All SQL of the surviving methods is byte-identical to native.
- **Explanation:** These removals do not change the schema (no table/column/index/PK/type changes) and each is documented as a method with zero live callers in the reworked architecture. Since the audit's source of truth is the native app's behavior, removing genuinely-unreached DAO methods is not a user-facing regression. Two of the removals do carry standalone findings above because they DO change behavior (the metrics JOIN rewrite and the paging removal). The remainder are pure dead-code elimination. Flagged at Low so the breadth of the API-surface delta is on record; if any of these methods are in fact reached by code paths outside the audited DAO files, that would escalate — but the per-method reacher audits in the KDocs assert zero reachers.
- **Suggested fix:** No schema action. Optionally spot-verify a few of the higher-risk removals against the reworked :data/:domain repositories (especially SourcesDao.updateBaseUrlAndVersionByName / updateImageBaseUrlAndVersionByName, which back native's per-source auto base/image URL update feature) to confirm the equivalent functionality exists in the KMP repository layer and was not silently lost with the UpdateSourcesRepository retire.

**⚪ [Low] Time-source for entity default timestamps — System.currentTimeMillis()/LocalDate.now()/LocalDateTime.now() defaults replaced with kotlin.time.Clock / kotlinx-datetime equivalents** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes - SavedMangaEntity.savedTimestamp/lastOpenTimestamp default to System.currentTimeMillis() (native SavedMangaEntity.kt:27-28); SavedChapterEntity.date defaults to java.time.LocalDate.now() (native SavedChapterEntity.kt:33); HistoryItemD.lastReadDate defaults to java.time.LocalDateTime.now() (native HistoryItemD.kt:21); ChapterDao.markChapterAsRead default currentTime = System.currentTimeMillis() (native ChapterDao.kt:69-70).
- **KMP:** Partial - same defaults via Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds() (shared SavedMangaEntity.kt:31-32), Clock.System.todayIn(TimeZone.currentSystemDefault()) (shared SavedChapterEntity.kt:41, ChapterNotification.kt:29), Clock.System.now().toLocalDateTime(TimeZone.currentSystemDefault()) (shared HistoryItemD.kt:30), and kotlin.time.Clock.System.now().toEpochMilliseconds() on markChapterAsRead (shared ChapterDao.kt:105).
- **Explanation:** The persisted wire types are unchanged (Long epoch-millis, Long epoch-day, Long epoch-millis), so the schema and stored data are identical. The values produced are equivalent. One subtle note: native LocalDateTimeConverter persists at ZoneOffset.UTC and HistoryItemD default uses LocalDateTime.now() (system default zone) — the KMP HistoryItemD default uses TimeZone.currentSystemDefault() then the converter persists at TimeZone.UTC, exactly mirroring native's behavior. No divergence in stored representation; recorded only to document that the time source was intentionally swapped for KMP portability.
- **Suggested fix:** No action needed; the migration is correct and storage-format-preserving. If absolute cross-device timestamp determinism matters, consider standardizing entity date defaults on UTC, but this matches native behavior and is out of scope for parity.

</details>

### Networking / HTTP / Cloudflare  `networking-http`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 11 (🔴0 🟠3 🟡3 ⚪5)

> Native (source of truth) builds a single Hilt-provided OkHttpClient (AppModule.provideOkHttpClient) with a 200 MB disk Cache, connect 30s / read 60s / write 60s, retryOnConnectionFailure(true), pingInterval(15s), BODY-level HttpLoggingInterceptor only in DEBUG, a forceCacheForDados network interceptor (1-day cache stamping for api2.manhastro.net/dados) and an offlineCacheInterceptor (only-if-cached + 7-day maxStale when offline for the same host). This same client is reused by Retrofit (IMangaDataApiServices, raw String / ScalarsConverterFactory) and, in CoilModule, derived for image loading with a ProgressInterceptor and a custom *.s3.wasabisys.com hostname verifier. KMP replaces this with per-platform Ktor createHttpClient() actuals (OkHttp/Darwin/CIO) wired through Koin, plus an ApiClient wrapper. The headline divergences: KMP has NO disk HTTP cache (200 MB cache dropped on all platforms); KMP adds a whole-request requestTimeoutMillis=60s that native never had (native has no callTimeout, only socket-level read/write); KMP logging is ALWAYS on at HEADERS level (native logs BODY only in DEBUG); the Ktor HttpCache plugin is never installed so the ported attachForceCacheForDados extension is dead code and never attached; the offlineCacheInterceptor is not ported at all; retry/keepalive is Android-only (iOS/Desktop lack it); installBrowserHeaders is dead code; and the KMP Android image fetcher uses a bare OkHttpClient with no cache, timeouts, ping/retry, or wasabisys hostname verifier. The per-request endpoint surface (raw-String body, status via status.value, header maps) was ported faithfully and the Chrome-114 UA / referer values are preserved verbatim where used.
