**🟠 [High] HTTP client / disk cache — 200 MB OkHttp disk cache dropped entirely in KMP** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - AppModule.kt:46-48,56 creates a 200 MB okhttp_cache directory (cacheSize = 200L*1024*1024) under context.cacheDir and installs it via .cache(cache) on the main OkHttpClient used by both API and Coil.
- **KMP:** No - createHttpClient() actuals (HttpClientFactory.android.kt:12-26, ios:11-19, desktop:11-19) install only ContentNegotiation, Logging and HttpTimeout. No disk cache is configured on any platform and the Ktor HttpCache plugin is never installed.
- **Explanation:** Native persists up to 200 MB of HTTP responses to disk, which materially reduces network traffic and speeds repeat loads (and is what the offline/manhastro caching relies on). KMP keeps no disk cache at all, so every request hits the network. This is a behavioral regression affecting data usage, latency and offline behavior across every source.
- **Suggested fix:** On Android install a Ktor HttpCache plugin backed by an OkHttp Cache(File(cacheDir, "okhttp_cache"), 200L*1024*1024) on the OkHttp engine, or configure the engine's preconfigured OkHttpClient with the same .cache(...). For iOS/Desktop add an equivalent HttpCache (Darwin URLCache / CIO file cache) sized to ~200 MB to restore parity.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/di/app/AppModule.kt:46-48 creates a 200 MB OkHttp cache (`val cacheSize = 200L * 1024 * 1024`; `val cacheDir = File(context.cacheDir, "okhttp_cache")`; `val cache = Cache(cacheDir, cacheSize)`), installed at line 56 via `.cache(cache)` on the @MainOkHttpClient singleton. That client is used for the API (NetworkModule.kt:23-30 injects @MainOkHttpClient into Retrofit) AND for Coil images (CoilModule.kt:33 `@MainOkHttpClient baseClient`, `.newBuilder()...build()` at lines 35-48, fed to OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory at 53-66). The manhastro/offline caching genuinely relies on this disk cache: core/network_cache/forceCacheForDados.kt:10-44 sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400` on api2.manhastro.net/dados and `offlineCacheInterceptor` uses `onlyIfCached()` + `maxStale(7, TimeUnit.DAYS)` when offline — both wired at AppModule.kt:67-68. KMP: All three createHttpClient() actuals install ONLY ContentNegotiation, Logging(HEADERS), HttpTimeout — no HttpCache, no disk cache. /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/shared/src/androidMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/data/remote/ktor/HttpClientFactory.android.kt:12-26 (plugins lines 13-15; engine block adds only retryOnConnectionFailure/pingInterval, no cache); HttpClientFactory.ios.kt:11-19; HttpClientFactory.desktop.kt:11-19. This client is the live API client: shared/.../di/SharedModule.kt:118 `single { createHttpClient() }` feeds ApiClient. The Ktor HttpCache plugin and the ported `attachForceCacheForDados()` are referenced ONLY inside shared/.../core/network_cache/forceCacheForDados.kt (definition + KDoc usage example at lines 26/29/35) — grep across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/composeApp finds zero `install(HttpCache)` and zero call sites for `attachForceCacheForDados()`, so the port is dead code; its KDoc also states the offline interceptor was "intentionally NOT ported". The KMP image pipeline likewise has no disk cache: composeApp/.../App.kt:309-326 builds the singleton ImageLoader with components + maxBitmapSize + build() and no `.diskCache(...)`; the Android PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt builds a plain `OkHttpClient.Builder().addInterceptor(...).build()` (no `.cache()`), and its own KDoc notes Coil 3.4.0's default is "a vanilla OkHttpClient() with no cache". Minor: the claimed actual line ranges are off by 1-2 lines but fall within the cited ranges; substantively accurate.

**🟠 [High] HTTP client / Cloudflare-style edge caching (forceCacheForDados) — forceCacheForDados ported but never wired; HttpCache plugin never installed, so it is dead code** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - forceCacheForDados() is a network interceptor added via .addNetworkInterceptor(forceCacheForDados()) in AppModule.kt:67; it rewrites responses for https://api2.manhastro.net/dados to Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 and removes Pragma (forceCacheForDados.kt:10-26).
- **KMP:** Partial - HttpClient.attachForceCacheForDados() exists in commonMain forceCacheForDados.kt:35-44 but a repo-wide grep shows it is NEVER called, and no createHttpClient() actual installs HttpCache or HttpSend. Even its own KDoc usage block requires install(HttpCache)+install(HttpSend), neither of which is present, so the 1-day caching for the manhastro dados endpoint does not happen.
- **Explanation:** The manhastro source relies on the 1-day Cache-Control stamping (and the disk cache) to avoid re-fetching expensive /dados payloads. In KMP this optimization is entirely inert: the extension is never attached and the HttpCache plugin it depends on is never installed, so requests are not cached or rate-limited the way native intended.
- **Suggested fix:** Install HttpCache and HttpSend in each createHttpClient() actual and call client.attachForceCacheForDados() right after constructing the client (e.g. in the Koin single{} after createHttpClient()), so the dados Cache-Control rewrite actually takes effect on top of a real disk cache.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth, caching is LIVE): - /native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/core/network_cache/forceCacheForDados.kt:10-26 — forceCacheForDados() Interceptor rewrites RESPONSES whose URL startsWith "https://api2.manhastro.net/dados" to header Cache-Control: "public, max-age=86400" (1 day) and removeHeader("Pragma"); other requests pass through. - /native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/di/app/AppModule.kt:67 — .addNetworkInterceptor(forceCacheForDados()) actually wires it into the @Singleton OkHttpClient. AppModule.kt:46-48 backs it with a 200MB disk Cache(okhttp_cache); AppModule.kt:68 adds the companion offlineCacheInterceptor(context) for offline only-if-cached. So native caching genuinely happens. KMP (extension exists but is dead code): - /shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/core/network_cache/forceCacheForDados.kt:35-44 — fun HttpClient.attachForceCacheForDados() exists, implemented via plugin(HttpSend).intercept { ... } matching DADOS_URL_PREFIX (line 32) and rewriting CacheControl/Pragma. Its own KDoc (lines 24-30) states usage requires install(HttpCache)+install(HttpSend)+client.attachForceCacheForDados(). - Repo-wide grep (excluding /native-app): the ONLY occurrences of attachForceCacheForDados, HttpCache, and HttpSend outside native are inside forceCacheForDados.kt itself (its definition + KDoc example + audit-trail comment). ZERO external callers; ZERO install(HttpCache)/install(HttpSend) anywhere. - All three createHttpClient() actuals install only ContentNegotiation + Logging + HttpTimeout, never HttpCache/HttpSend, never the extension: /shared/src/androidMain/.../HttpClientFactory.android.kt:12-26 (OkHttp), /shared/src/iosMain/.../HttpClientFactory.ios.kt:11-19 (Darwin), /shared/src/desktopMain/.../HttpClientFactory.desktop.kt:11-19 (CIO). - /shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/di/SharedModule.kt:118-119 — Koin binds single { createHttpClient() } then single { ApiClient(get()) }; the raw client is injected into ApiClient (/shared/.../data/remote/api/ApiClient.kt:28) with no .attachForceCacheForDados() call at the binding or any actual. No Ktor CacheStorage / disk-cache equivalent of native's 200MB OkHttp cache exists. Result: 1-day caching for /dados does not happen in KMP. (Minor port mismatch not affecting verdict: native rewrites the RESPONSE Cache-Control, the KMP port rewrites the outgoing REQUEST headers — but it is never wired so this is moot.)

**🟠 [High] Image loading HTTP client (Coil) — KMP Android image OkHttpClient is bare: no shared cache, timeouts, ping/retry, or wasabisys hostname verifier** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - CoilModule.kt:32-49 derives the image client from the fully-configured @MainOkHttpClient via baseClient.newBuilder(), so it inherits the 200 MB cache, 30/60/60 timeouts, retry and pingInterval, then adds ProgressInterceptor AND a custom hostnameVerifier that trusts any *.s3.wasabisys.com host (CoilModule.kt:37-47).
- **KMP:** Partial/No - PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt:45-48 builds a brand-new OkHttpClient.Builder().addInterceptor(OkHttpProgressInterceptor(...)).build() with NO cache, NO timeouts, NO retry/ping, and crucially NO *.s3.wasabisys.com hostname verifier. iOS/Desktop fall through to the ktor3 fetcher (PlatformNetworkFetcher.kt expect returns null on those).
- **Explanation:** Two regressions: (1) image fetches no longer share the 200 MB cache or native timeouts/keepalive, so image caching/perf differs; (2) the missing *.s3.wasabisys.com hostname verifier means images hosted on Wasabi S3 buckets that native explicitly allowed (bypassing default hostname verification) can fail TLS hostname verification in KMP and not load. The KDoc even warns 'If Coil's defaults ever grow load-bearing behavior, this wire-up must mirror them' - the verifier and cache are exactly that load-bearing config.
- **Suggested fix:** Build the Android Coil OkHttpClient from the same configured base client (cache, timeouts, retry, pingInterval) used by the Ktor OkHttp engine, and re-add the hostnameVerifier that returns true for hosts ending in .s3.wasabisys.com (falling back to the default verifier otherwise), matching CoilModule.provideCoilOkHttpClient.
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): native-app/.../di/app/AppModule.kt:39-70 — @MainOkHttpClient builds the fully-configured client: 200 MB Cache (lines 46-48 + .cache(cache) line 56), connectTimeout(30s) line 57, readTimeout(60s) line 58, writeTimeout(60s) line 59, retryOnConnectionFailure(true) line 60, pingInterval(15, SECONDS) line 61 (note: 15s, not 60s as the claim loosely implies), plus forceCacheForDados() network interceptor (67) and offlineCacheInterceptor (68). native-app/.../di/coli/CoilModule.kt:32-49 — image client = baseClient.newBuilder() (line 35) inheriting ALL of the above, then .addNetworkInterceptor(ProgressInterceptor()) (36) and a custom .hostnameVerifier{} (37-47) that returns true for any host ending in ".s3.wasabisys.com" (41-42) and falls back to the default verifier otherwise (44-45). Wired into ImageLoader via OkHttpNetworkFetcherFactory at CoilModule.kt:51-67. The native half of the claim is confirmed exactly. KMP: composeApp/src/androidMain/.../images/PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt:45-48 — builds OkHttpClient.Builder().addInterceptor(OkHttpProgressInterceptor(reporter=repository::report)).build(): NO .cache(), NO timeouts, NO retryOnConnectionFailure, NO pingInterval, and NO *.s3.wasabisys.com hostnameVerifier. A codebase-wide grep for "wasabisys" / "HostnameVerifier" across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/composeApp returned ZERO matches — the verifier is entirely absent on every platform. composeApp/.../App.kt:308-326 wires this fetcher into the singleton ImageLoader and only adds maxBitmapSize(Size.ORIGINAL) + component-level interceptors; nothing restores the OkHttp client config. The KDoc at PlatformNetworkFetcher.android.kt:27-32 explicitly states the explicit client is "observationally equivalent" to Coil's default and warns "If Coil's defaults ever grow load-bearing behavior, this wire-up must mirror them" — confirming the verifier/cache are exactly the un-mirrored config. CLAIM ERROR: The claim states "iOS/Desktop fall through to the ktor3 fetcher (PlatformNetworkFetcher.kt expect returns null on those)." This is outdated/false. PlatformNetworkFetcher.ios.kt:56-62 and PlatformNetworkFetcher.desktop.kt:30-36 now explicitly construct vanilla ktor3 HttpClient{} instances and return KtorNetworkFetcherFactory(httpClient={client}) — they do NOT return null. The commonMain expect KDoc (PlatformNetworkFetcher.kt:19) still says "Returns null on Desktop and iOS" but the actuals contradict it. This does not change the core regression (those ktor clients are equally bare and also lack the wasabisys verifier) but the stated mechanism is wrong.

**🟡 [Medium] HTTP client / offline cache — offlineCacheInterceptor (offline only-if-cached + 7-day maxStale) not ported at all** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - offlineCacheInterceptor(context) added via .addInterceptor(...) in AppModule.kt:68; when the device is offline and the URL starts with https://api2.manhastro.net/dados it rewrites the request with CacheControl.onlyIfCached().maxStale(7, DAYS) so stale cached dados can be served offline (forceCacheForDados.kt:27-44).
- **KMP:** No - there is no KMP equivalent. The commonMain forceCacheForDados.kt KDoc explicitly states offlineCacheInterceptor is intentionally NOT ported (depends on android Context/ConnectivityManager) and should live behind a connectivity expect/actual that has not been authored.
- **Explanation:** Native can serve the manhastro dados endpoint from a stale (up to 7 days) cache while offline, enabling a degree of offline browsing for that source. KMP has no such path, so offline access to that source is lost, and combined with the missing disk cache there is nothing to fall back to.
- **Suggested fix:** Add a ConnectivityObserver-based expect/actual and a Ktor HttpSend interceptor that, when offline and URL starts with the dados prefix, sets request cache headers equivalent to onlyIfCached + maxStale 7 days against the (newly added) HttpCache store.

**🟡 [Medium] HTTP client / timeouts — KMP adds a 60s whole-request timeout that native never had; native's read/write semantics differ from Ktor's socket timeout** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - AppModule.kt:57-59 sets connectTimeout(30s), readTimeout(60s), writeTimeout(60s) only. There is NO callTimeout / whole-request timeout (grep for callTimeout returns nothing), so a long multi-read response (e.g. large chapter HTML/JSON over a slow link) can run well beyond 60s as long as each individual read/write stays under 60s.
- **KMP:** Partial - all three actuals set connectTimeoutMillis=30_000, requestTimeoutMillis=60_000, socketTimeoutMillis=60_000 (HttpClientFactory.android.kt:15-19 and siblings). requestTimeoutMillis is a hard ceiling on the ENTIRE request/response, which native does not impose; there is no separate writeTimeout.
- **Explanation:** Because KMP imposes a 60s whole-request cap that native lacks, slow but progressing downloads that native would allow to complete will be aborted with HttpRequestTimeoutException in KMP. This can cause spurious failures on large pages/slow connections that work fine on native. socketTimeoutMillis approximates native read but native's writeTimeout has no distinct counterpart.
- **Suggested fix:** Remove requestTimeoutMillis (or raise it substantially) to match native's lack of a whole-request timeout, keeping connectTimeoutMillis=30_000 and socketTimeoutMillis=60_000 to mirror native's connect/read; document that Ktor has no separate write timeout.

**🟡 [Medium] HTTP client / logging — KMP logs HTTP on every build at HEADERS level; native logs only in DEBUG at BODY level** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - AppModule.kt:49-53,64 builds an HttpLoggingInterceptor at Level.BODY and adds it only when BuildConfig.DEBUG is true (if (BuildConfig.DEBUG) addInterceptor(logging)). Release builds do no HTTP logging.
- **KMP:** Yes (always-on) - every actual unconditionally installs install(Logging){ level = LogLevel.HEADERS } (HttpClientFactory.android.kt:14, ios:13, desktop:13). There is no DEBUG guard, so release builds also log request/response headers.
- **Explanation:** Two divergences: (1) logging level differs (native BODY vs KMP HEADERS) so KMP debug logs omit request/response bodies the native devs relied on; (2) more importantly KMP logs in release builds, which native deliberately avoided. Always-on header logging in release adds overhead and can leak header data (cookies, referers, UA) into device logs.
- **Suggested fix:** Gate the Logging install behind a debug/build flag (an expect val isDebug or BuildKonfig) and, when enabled, use LogLevel.BODY to match native's Level.BODY; disable logging entirely in release as native does.

**⚪ [Low] HTTP client / connection keepalive & retry (non-Android) — retryOnConnectionFailure + 15s pingInterval applied only on Android; iOS/Desktop omit them** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - AppModule.kt:60-61 sets retryOnConnectionFailure(true) and pingInterval(15, SECONDS) on the single OkHttpClient (Android is the only native target).
- **KMP:** Partial - only the Android actual replicates this in an engine{ config{ retryOnConnectionFailure(true); pingInterval(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS) } } block (HttpClientFactory.android.kt:20-25). The iOS (Darwin) and Desktop (CIO) actuals have no engine{} block and no equivalent retry/keepalive tuning (HttpClientFactory.ios.kt / .desktop.kt).
- **Explanation:** Android parity is preserved, but iOS/Desktop rely on NSURLSession/CIO defaults for retry and HTTP/2 keepalive. While defensible (engine defaults differ), it is still a behavioral divergence from the single source-of-truth config; HTTP/2 stream timeouts the 15s ping was meant to prevent are not explicitly guarded on those platforms.
- **Suggested fix:** Document the per-platform default behavior, and if HTTP/2 stream resets are observed on iOS/Desktop, add Darwin/CIO equivalents (e.g. CIO endpoint keepAliveTime/maxConnectionsPerRoute, Darwin NSURLSessionConfiguration tuning) to mirror native's retry+keepalive intent.

**⚪ [Low] HTTP client / JSON configuration — KMP installs kotlinx ContentNegotiation JSON with lenient settings; native Retrofit uses ScalarsConverterFactory (raw String only)** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - NetworkModule.kt:28 registers only ScalarsConverterFactory.create() and every IMangaDataApiServices method returns Response<String>. There is no JSON converter at the HTTP layer; JSON parsing is done manually downstream per-source.
- **KMP:** Yes (additional) - every actual installs ContentNegotiation with json(DefaultJson) where DefaultJson = Json{ ignoreUnknownKeys=true; isLenient=true; coerceInputValues=true } (HttpClientFactory.kt:16-20). ApiClient still returns raw HttpResponse/bodyAsText, so the body path matches, but ContentNegotiation can now auto-decode/encode JSON for any typed body call.
- **Explanation:** Functionally the raw-String path is preserved (callers use bodyAsText()), so this is mostly additive. However it is a config divergence from the source of truth: native never had a content-negotiation/JSON layer, and the lenient DefaultJson behavior (coerceInputValues, isLenient) could change how any typed JSON body is parsed compared to whatever per-source manual parser native used.
- **Suggested fix:** Acceptable as additive, but verify no repo accidentally relies on ContentNegotiation auto-decoding where native did manual parsing; if strict parity is desired, confirm all source repos still parse the raw bodyAsText() string exactly as native did rather than relying on the new typed JSON path.

**⚪ [Low] HTTP client / default browser headers (installBrowserHeaders) — installBrowserHeaders extension is dead code in KMP (never called); this matches native where BrowserHeadersInterceptor is also unused** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Partial - BrowserHeadersInterceptor.kt defines an OkHttp interceptor that sets Referer + Chrome-114 User-Agent on every request, but a repo-wide grep shows it is NEVER added to any OkHttpClient (the main client in AppModule does not install it). It is effectively dead code in native too; per-source repos set UA/Referer per-request instead.
- **KMP:** Partial - installBrowserHeaders(referer) (BrowserHeadersInterceptor.kt:20-29) is a faithful Ktor/DefaultRequest port preserving the same Chrome-114 UA verbatim, but a repo-wide grep confirms it is never called anywhere either. So both sides leave it unused.
- **Explanation:** This is parity at the 'both unused' level rather than a regression: neither app installs a global UA/Referer interceptor on its main client; both rely on per-source header maps. Worth recording because the KMP KDoc claims it is 'consumed by per-source repo HttpClient configurations', which is inaccurate (no caller exists). No user-visible behavior change.
- **Suggested fix:** Either delete the unused installBrowserHeaders extension (and the dead native BrowserHeadersInterceptor) to avoid the misleading KDoc, or, if a global UA/Referer default is actually desired, install it in createHttpClient() — but only if native intends the same, to preserve parity.

**⚪ [Low] HTTP client / engine fan-out (Retrofit vs Ktor) — Retrofit+single OkHttpClient replaced by 3 Ktor engines (OkHttp/Darwin/CIO) with no shared config extraction** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - one OkHttpClient (AppModule) feeding a single Retrofit instance with baseUrl https://placeholder.com/ (NetworkModule.kt:27) and @Url-driven absolute URLs; Android-only.
- **KMP:** Yes - createHttpClient() is an expect fun with OkHttp (android), Darwin (ios), CIO (desktop) actuals; the ContentNegotiation/Logging/HttpTimeout triad is hand-replicated in each actual rather than factored out, so config drift between platforms is possible (and already exists: only Android has retry/ping, see separate finding).
- **Explanation:** The migration is structurally sound and the per-request shape is preserved, but because there is no shared config helper the three actuals must be kept manually in sync; the audit found the engine-config block, logging, cache and timeouts are not uniform across them, which is the root cause of several findings above.
- **Suggested fix:** Introduce a shared configuration function (e.g. an inline HttpClientConfig<*>.applyCommonConfig() applied by all three actuals) that installs cache, timeouts, logging (debug-gated), retry/keepalive and forceCacheForDados consistently, so the source-of-truth config lives in one place across platforms.

**⚪ [Low] HTTP client / endpoint surface (ApiClient vs IMangaDataApiServices) — ApiClient exposes 9 methods vs native's 17 Retrofit methods; the convenience FormUrlEncoded helpers (searchManga/searchMangaWithOrder/loadMore/normalPost) are collapsed into generic postForm/postJson** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes - IMangaDataApiServices.kt declares ~17 methods including typed FormUrlEncoded endpoints (searchManga, searchManga3, searchMangaWithOrder with vars[...] fields, loadMore, normalPost with RequestBody) - though grep shows many (loadMore, getDataPost, searchManga3, searchMangaWithOrder, getHomeData, getMangaData, getChapterData) have 0 call sites and normalPost only 1.
- **KMP:** Partial - ApiClient.kt:30-90 provides 9 generic methods (get, get+headers, get+referer, getJson, postEmpty, postForm(fields map), postJson, postUrlencoded, getString). The typed Field/vars[...] search endpoints are gone; callers must build the field map themselves. The KDoc admits 8 endpoints were dropped as orphaned.
- **Explanation:** Because the dropped native endpoints were largely uncalled (verified 0 call sites for most), collapsing them into generic postForm/postJson is reasonable and likely behavior-preserving. The risk is subtle: native's @FormUrlEncoded with named @Field('vars[s]') etc. guarantees exact field encoding; a hand-built map in KMP must replicate those exact field names/order or a source's search/loadMore could break. This is per-source territory but flagged here as the HTTP-surface contraction.
- **Suggested fix:** Confirm each source repo that previously used the typed search/loadMore endpoints now passes the identical field keys (e.g. 'vars[s]', 'vars[orderby]', 'action', 'page', 'template') through postForm; add a small typed helper or tests for the WordPress-madara style search payloads to guard against field-name drift.

</details>

<details><summary>Full detail (explanation, evidence, suggested fix) for Source Repositories Parity</summary>

**🟠 [High] Source registry - Italian MangaPark (Mangapark-It) — Italian MangaPark source active in native, completely missing (unported stub) in KMP** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes - real class MangaParkRepositoryIt at native it/mangapark/MangaParkRepositoryIt.kt:1; bound ACTIVE via bindMangaParkIt in RepositoryModule.kt:108
- **KMP:** No - KMP it/mangapark/MangaParkRepositoryIt.kt has NO live class (body is a block comment); not bound in SharedModule.kt; absent from the active set (SharedModule.kt:227-282)
- **Explanation:** Native active set 44 repos, KMP 43; exact diff is MangaParkRepositoryIt. saveSources() seeds DB rows only from the injected set (SharedModule.kt:273-290), so the Mangapark-It row is never created and cannot be enabled. MANGAPARK_IT enum entry still exists (MangaSource.kt:75), orphaned. The stub comment claims EN MangaParkRepository is unported, but it IS ported and active (SharedModule.kt:140,245).

### DI / Startup / Lifecycle  `di-startup-lifecycle`

**Parity verdict:** ParityPartial  ·  **Findings:** 17 (🔴1 🟠4 🟡5 ⚪7)

> Native (Hilt/MVVM) splits startup across two objects: MyApp.onCreate does AppUpdateHelper.init → FirebaseApp.initializeApp → NotificationHelper.init → MobileAds.initialize, and MainActivity.onCreate does a large amount of user-facing startup work — FirebaseAnalytics APP_OPEN logging, updateSources.initializeSources() (remote source-list seeding), AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate + registerListener, UMP consent (requestConsent → loadAndShowForm → consent-gated MobileAds.initialize), and an in-app review launch — plus onResume (resumeUpdate), onActivityResult (update result), and onDestroy (cleanup). KMP migrated DI from Hilt to Koin (initKoin(allReworkModules()){…} in MyApp) and reduced MainActivity to a thin ComponentActivity that only installs splash, enables edge-to-edge, and mounts the shared App() composable. The Koin graph is broad and the per-platform facades (AppUpdateClient, InAppReviewClient, ConsentFlowClient, AnalyticsClient, PushTokenProvider) exist, but almost none of native's startup orchestration is actually invoked: there are zero callers of the consent flow, in-app review, update check/listener/resume, APP_OPEN analytics, or remote source-list seeding anywhere in the KMP tree. The headline divergences are: missing UMP consent before ads (compliance risk), unconditional vs consent-gated MobileAds init, missing in-app update check/resume/listener, missing in-app review prompt, missing remote source seeding, an empty FCM service (no notification display), and a crash handler that KMP newly ENABLES vs native leaving it commented out. DI/Koin coverage of singletons (SharedPrefsHelper, ApplicationScope, HttpClient, WorkManager factory) is otherwise solid.

**🔴 [Critical] Startup — Remote source-list seeding (initializeSources) — Native fetches and seeds/updates the manga source list from a remote endpoint at startup; KMP has no equivalent and the responsible class was retired** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onCreate calls updateSources.initializeSources() (MainActivity.kt:386), which (UpdateSourcesRepository.kt:39-) calls updateUrls() → api.get(if(Admin.isAdmin) "https://yamimanga.me/dev/source" else "https://yamimanga.me/source/35"), parses the response, and updates SourcesDao with versioned source/image URLs.
- **KMP:** No — repo-wide grep for yamimanga.me/source, /source/35, updateUrls, updateSourcesFromApi, initializeSources returns zero hits in KMP. shared/.../admin/Admin.kt KDoc explicitly states UpdateSourcesRepository was retired (Task #387) as an 'orphan Koin single with zero reachers'. No replacement startup source-refresh exists.
- **Explanation:** Native keeps source base URLs / parsing configs current by pulling the live source list on every launch (handling domain changes for sources). With this removed and no replacement, KMP relies solely on whatever source URLs are baked in / persisted, so when a source's domain or config changes server-side, KMP cannot update and those sources will silently break — a core functional regression for a scraping-based manga app.
- **Suggested fix:** Reintroduce a startup source-list refresh: add a domain use case (e.g. RefreshSourcesUseCase) that GETs https://yamimanga.me/source/35 (or /dev/source when Admin.isAdmin) and upserts SourcesDao with version comparison, and invoke it from a startup side-effect (App() LaunchedEffect on the application scope) as native's initializeSources did.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Critical). NATIVE (source of truth) — the remote source-seeding pipeline exists and runs at startup: - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:106 declares `lateinit var updateSources: UpdateSourcesRepository`; line 276 in `onCreate` calls `updateSources.initializeSources()` (NOTE: the claim cited line 386, which is wrong — line 386 is commented-out unrelated code; the real call is at line 276, but the call unambiguously exists). - /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/presentation/features/repo_settings/domain/UpdateSourcesRepository.kt:39 `initializeSources()` → `updateUrls()` (line 51) → `api.get(if (Admin.isAdmin) "https://yamimanga.me/dev/source" else "https://yamimanga.me/source/35")` (line 60), then `parseApiResponse` (JSON list of Source), `getCurrentSourceVersions`/`getCurrentImageSourceVersions`, and `updateSourcesFromApi` (line 75). That last method compares `apiSource.baseVersion`/`imageUrlVersion` against persisted versions, calls `sourcesDao.updateBaseUrlAndVersionByName` / `updateImageBaseUrlAndVersionByName` / `deleteSourceByName`, and propagates URL changes across manga/chapter/history/notification rows (propagateUrlChanges / propagateImageUrlChanges, lines 235+). The DAO methods exist at native-app/.../data/local/dao/SourcesDao.kt:46,49,78. KMP (new app) — no equivalent; class retired, endpoints/methods absent: - Repo-wide grep across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/platform/composeApp/app (excluding native-app) for `yamimanga.me/source`, `/source/35`, `/dev/source`, `updateUrls`, `updateSourcesFromApi`, `initializeSources`, `UpdateSourcesRepository` returns ZERO implementation hits — only KDoc/comment lineage documenting the retirement. - shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/me/manga/yamiapk/admin/Admin.kt:13-16 KDoc states verbatim: "Phase 9.x.updatesourcesrepository.retire (Task #387): ... `UpdateSourcesRepository` is itself now retired (orphan Koin `single` with zero `get<UpdateSourcesRepository>()` reachers in the source tree)." - KMP startup entry points carry no source-refresh: app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MainActivity.kt is a thin `setContent { App() }` shell; app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MyApp.kt `onCreate` bootstraps only Context/Koin/crash-bridge/AppUpdateClient/NotificationPresenter/Firebase/AdMob — no source-list fetch. - The surviving KMP sources surface only seeds LOCALLY from the compiled-in repo set, never remotely: shared/.../repo_settings/domain/SourcesRepository.kt `init { applicationScope.launch { saveSources() } }` and `saveSources()` (≈line 264) inserts SourcesEntity rows from the in-memory `repoMap` (repo.API/BASE_URL/URL_VERSION/imgBaseUrl/imgUrlVersion) — baked-in values, no network. The domain interface domain/.../repository/SourcesRepository.kt and data/.../SourcesRepositoryImpl.kt expose only observeSources/setSourceEnabled/setLanguageEnabled/setLanguageEnabledWithFallback (toggles + read), plus the legacy facade's routing surface (findRepoByHost/activeRepoFlow/getEnabledRepos). No remote version-comparison or URL update exists. - KMP SourcesDao.kt (shared) retains only getAllSources/insert/setEnabledByName/getBaseUrlFor/getSiteStateByName(Sync); the version-update methods native's updateSourcesFromApi relied on (updateBaseUrlAndVersionByName / updateImageBaseUrlAndVersionByName / deleteSourceByName) were pruned (Task #388), so even the DAO surface to apply a remote source-list update is gone. Conclusion: Native pulls the live source list (dev/prod URL gated by Admin.isAdmin) on every launch and version-updates base/image URLs + propagates them to existing rows; KMP has no remote source-refresh at all and relies solely on the locally baked-in source URLs seeded once via saveSources(). The difference is real and correctly characterized (only the cited native line number 386 is inaccurate — it's actually MainActivity.kt:276).

**🟠 [High] Startup — UMP consent gathering before ads — Native runs the full Google UMP consent flow at startup before initializing ads; KMP never invokes consent** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onCreate launches requestConsent(this@MainActivity) on Dispatchers.IO (MainActivity.kt:399-408), which calls UserMessagingPlatform.getConsentInformation, requestConsentInfoUpdate, then loadAndShowForm/form.show, and only calls initializeAds() (consent-gated MobileAds.initialize) when consentInformation.canRequestAds() is true (MainActivity.kt:538-642).
- **KMP:** Partial/No — ConsentFlowClient facade is defined and bound (platform/src/androidMain/.../consent/AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:42-80, registered shared/.../PlatformModule.android.kt:151) but a repo-wide grep for requestConsentInfoUpdate / loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired returns ZERO callers outside the platform impls. No code path runs the consent flow at startup or anywhere else.
- **Explanation:** The UMP (User Messaging Platform) consent dialog is a Google Play / GDPR compliance requirement for EEA users before personalized ads. Native gathers consent and gates ad initialization on canRequestAds(); KMP skips consent entirely and initializes ads unconditionally (MyApp.kt:133). Beyond the missing dialog UX, this is a policy/compliance regression and means EEA users never see the consent form the native app shows.
- **Suggested fix:** Wire a startup-time consent flow: from the shared App() (or a launcher-side effect) resolve ConsentFlowClient, call requestConsentInfoUpdate() then loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired(), and only initialize ads (AdProvider/MobileAds) once canRequestAds() returns true — mirroring native MainActivity.requestConsent/loadAndShowForm/initializeAds.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth) — full UMP consent flow runs at startup and gates ads: - /native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:289-291: onCreate launches `CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO).launch { requestConsent(this@MainActivity) }`. - MainActivity.kt:428-472: requestConsent() calls UserMessagingPlatform.getConsentInformation (429), builds ConsentRequestParameters (443), calls consentInformation.requestConsentInfoUpdate (454); on success either loadAndShowForm() (461) or initializeAds() (464). - MainActivity.kt:496-522: loadAndShowForm() calls UserMessagingPlatform.loadConsentForm (497) and form.show(activity) when status==REQUIRED (506). - MainActivity.kt:524-532: initializeAds() is consent-gated — `if (consentInformation.canRequestAds()) { MobileAds.initialize(...) }`. (Note: the claim's native line refs 399-408/538-642 are off; the actual lines are 289-291 and 428-532, but the described behavior matches exactly.) KMP — consent flow exists as a facade but is NEVER invoked, and ads init unconditionally: - Facade is fully implemented: /platform/src/androidMain/.../consent/AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:42-80 wraps real UMP (requestConsentInfoUpdate at :49, loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired at :69, canRequestAds at :80). Interface at /platform/src/commonMain/.../consent/ConsentFlowClient.kt:15-29. - It IS DI-bound: /shared/src/androidMain/.../di/PlatformModule.android.kt:151 `single<ConsentFlowClient> { AndroidConsentFlowClient(androidContext()) }` (iOS/Desktop bind no-op stubs at PlatformModule.ios.kt:133 / PlatformModule.desktop.kt:133). - ZERO consumers: repo-wide grep across ui/presentation/domain/data/shared/composeApp/app shows every `ConsentFlowClient` / `requestConsentInfoUpdate` / `loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired` / `canRequestAds` hit is confined to the platform impl files, the interface, KDoc comments, or the `single<ConsentFlowClient>` DI bindings. No `get<ConsentFlowClient>()` / `by inject` / constructor injection anywhere. - KMP MainActivity (/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MainActivity.kt, 58 lines) has NO consent/ads/MobileAds references at all. - Ads init unconditionally: /app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MyApp.kt:132-136 calls `MobileAds.initialize(this) {...}` in onCreate step 5 with no consent gate and no ConsentFlowClient call. - Stronger than claimed: even the live DI binding uses the default `activityProvider = { null }` (AndroidConsentFlowClient.kt:35; PlatformModule.android.kt:146 comment: "activityProvider stays `{ null }` until Phase 11"), so requestConsentInfoUpdate/loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired would early-return UNKNOWN/false ("no foreground Activity") even if something did call them.

**🟠 [High] Startup — In-app review prompt — Native launches Play in-app review at startup; KMP never triggers it** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onCreate runs reviewScope.launch { launchInAppReviewSafely() } (MainActivity.kt:409-411, 644-654) which calls reviewHelper.launchInAppReview(this) on a Dispatchers.IO scope.
- **KMP:** No — InAppReviewClient interface + AndroidInAppReviewClient are defined and bound (platform/.../review/AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt; PlatformModule.android.kt:150), but a repo-wide grep for launchReviewFlow/requestReviewFlow/InAppReviewClient usage shows only DI registration — no caller invokes the review flow at startup or anywhere.
- **Explanation:** The Play Store in-app review prompt that native surfaces on app open is entirely absent in KMP; the facade exists but is dead. Users will never be prompted to rate the app, a deliberate native engagement feature.
- **Suggested fix:** Invoke InAppReviewClient.requestReviewFlow()/launchReviewFlow() from a startup side-effect (e.g. a LaunchedEffect in App() or in MainActivity) on an IO scope with try/catch, mirroring native MainActivity.launchInAppReviewSafely().
- **Verification:** PartiallyCorrect (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth) — in-app review IS triggered at startup: native-app/.../me/manga/yami/MainActivity.kt:98 injects `reviewHelper: ReviewManagerHelper`; line 108 defines `reviewScope = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO + Job())`; inside onCreate at MainActivity.kt:299-301 it runs `reviewScope.launch { launchInAppReviewSafely() }`; MainActivity.kt:534-544 `launchInAppReviewSafely()` calls `reviewHelper.launchInAppReview(this@MainActivity)`. ReviewManagerHelper.kt:76-90 gates on `shouldShowReview()` (20-day-since-first-open window, KEY_FIRST_OPEN_TIME, SEVEN_DAYS_MILLIS = TimeUnit.DAYS.toMillis(20)) then runs Play Core `manager.requestReviewFlow().await()` + `manager.launchReviewFlow(activity, reviewInfo).await()`. So native does NOT prompt unconditionally on every open — it is a delayed (≥20 day) one-time nudge. KMP — facade exists but has ZERO callers (dead): interface platform/src/commonMain/.../review/InAppReviewClient.kt:57-65 declares `suspend fun requestReview(): Boolean`; AndroidInAppReviewClient.kt:32-45 is a real Play Core impl (requestReviewFlow/launchReviewFlow via ForegroundActivityProvider); IosInAppReviewClient.kt:18-20 and DesktopInAppReviewClient.kt:18-20 are no-ops returning false. A grep for requestReview/launchReviewFlow/requestReviewFlow/InAppReviewClient across ui+presentation+domain+data+shared+platform+composeApp+app returned only the interface, the 3 actuals, the DI bindings, and KDoc/audit comments — NO invocation. KMP Android entrypoint app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MainActivity.kt:19-26 onCreate does only installSplashScreen/enableEdgeToEdge/super.onCreate/setContent{App()}; MyApp.onCreate starts Koin but never triggers review. The 3 presentation 'review' hits (ReaderIntent.kt:19 'reviewable', ComplaintState.kt 'preview', ThemeIntent.kt 'OnPreviewTheme') are false positives. No legacy `expect class InAppReviewClient` exists in :shared either. CLAIM ERRORS: (1) cited native lines 409-411 and 644-654 are WRONG — those are commented-out code; real call sites are 299-301 and 534-538. (2) Claim implies an unconditional open-time prompt; native actually gates behind a 20-day window. (3) Audit-comment-derived assertion about a separate 'legacy :shared expect-class SPI bound at PlatformModule.android.kt:124' is inaccurate — line 150 binds the new :platform AndroidInAppReviewClient; there is only one facade. The core conclusion (feature present in native, absent/dead in KMP) is correct.

**🟠 [High] Startup — In-app update check (Play Core) — Native checks for and starts a flexible in-app update at startup; KMP only constructs the update manager and never checks** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onCreate calls AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate(activity=this, immediate=updateType(false), …) (MainActivity.kt:388-398) which queries appUpdateInfo and starts a FLEXIBLE update flow via startUpdateFlowForResult (AppUpdateHelper.kt:checkForUpdate/handleUpdateInfo/startUpdate).
- **KMP:** No — MyApp.onCreate only eagerly resolves get<AppUpdateClient>() (app/.../MyApp.kt:115) which merely constructs AndroidAppUpdateClient (AppUpdateManagerFactory.create, AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:34). AppUpdateClient.checkForUpdate()/startFlexibleUpdate() (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:37,54) are defined but have ZERO callers in the repo.
- **Explanation:** Native prompts users to install app updates via the Play in-app update flow at launch. KMP creates the manager (matching AppUpdateHelper.init) but never calls checkForUpdate or startFlexibleUpdate, so the update prompt never appears — a missing core distribution feature.
- **Suggested fix:** After Koin start, call AppUpdateClient.checkForUpdate() and, if an update is available, AppUpdateClient.startFlexibleUpdate() from a foreground-activity-aware startup effect, replicating native MainActivity's AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate(immediate=false).
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: Medium). NATIVE (source of truth) actively checks + starts a FLEXIBLE in-app update at startup: native-app/.../MyApp.kt:27 `AppUpdateHelper.init(this)` constructs the manager; MainActivity.kt:199 onCreate calls (line 278) `AppUpdateHelper.checkForUpdate(activity=this, immediate=updateType, ...)` with updateType=false (MainActivity.kt:197 => FLEXIBLE). AppUpdateHelper.kt:58 queries appUpdateManager.appUpdateInfo, handleUpdateInfo (line 73) dispatches, startUpdate (line 109) calls startUpdateFlowForResult (the flexible flow). Full lifecycle wired: registerListener (MainActivity.kt:304), resumeUpdate/completeUpdate in onResume (lines 889-891), onActivityResult REQUEST_CODE 100 (line 899), unregisterListener onDestroy (line 929). KMP only constructs the manager and never checks/starts: app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/MyApp.kt:115 does only `get<AppUpdateClient>()` (eager construction), which runs AndroidAppUpdateClient's constructor `AppUpdateManagerFactory.create(...)` at platform/.../AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:34. MyApp's own KDoc (lines 38-42, 110-113) explicitly says this mirrors only AppUpdateHelper.init, not the check. AppUpdateClient.checkForUpdate() (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:36), startFlexibleUpdate() (line 53), completeUpdate() (line 75) are DEFINED but have ZERO callers across presentation/domain/data/ui/composeApp/app/shared — repo-wide grep returns only the interface decl (platform/.../update/AppUpdateClient.kt:24,27,30), the 3 actuals (Android real; iOS+Desktop no-ops), and KDoc/audit prose. Koin binding shared/.../PlatformModule.android.kt:149 `single<AppUpdateClient> { AndroidAppUpdateClient(androidContext()) }` uses the default ForegroundActivityProvider = { null }, so startFlexibleUpdate() would short-circuit to false anyway (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt:54-56). Net: the Play in-app update prompt that native shows at launch never appears in KMP. Claim inaccuracies (do not change verdict): native call site is MainActivity.kt:278 in onCreate, NOT 388-398 (those lines are commented-out experimental network code). The claim's referenced legacy :shared/.../core/update/AppUpdateClient twin does not exist; MyApp imports and resolves the :platform interface me.manga.kira.platform.update.AppUpdateClient (MyApp.kt:12).

**🟠 [High] Notifications — FCM message handling (MyFirebaseMessagingService) — Native's FCM service displays incoming push notifications and handles token refresh; KMP's service is an empty stub** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes — MyFirebaseMessagingService (@AndroidEntryPoint) overrides onMessageReceived to build title/body from remote.notification/remote.data and call helper.showNotification(this,title,body), and overrides onNewToken (native-app/.../firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:11-26).
- **KMP:** No — KMP MyFirebaseMessagingService is declared as `class MyFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService()` with an empty body and no overrides (app/.../firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt:9); its own KDoc admits it's a stub and 'real FCM payload handling migrated in Phase 4/11' (not done).
- **Explanation:** The manifest registers this service for com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT on both sides, but in KMP no push notification is ever displayed (no onMessageReceived) and no token is captured (no onNewToken). Server-pushed messages that native shows as notifications are silently dropped in KMP — a notification/background regression.
- **Suggested fix:** Implement onMessageReceived to extract title/body (remote.notification ?: remote.data) and display via NotificationPresenter/ChapterNotificationHelper using the firebase_messages channel, and implement onNewToken to feed PushTokenProvider, matching native helper.showNotification.
- **Verification:** Confirmed (corrected severity: High). NATIVE (source of truth): /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt — declared `package me.manga.kira.firebase_cores.messaging` (line 1; on-disk folder is me/manga/yami, matching the stated package/folder mismatch). Annotated `@AndroidEntryPoint` (line 10), `class MyFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService()` (line 11) with `@Inject lateinit var helper: NotificationHelper` (line 13). Overrides `onNewToken(token)` (lines 15-18) and `onMessageReceived(remote)` (lines 20-28): builds title = `remote.notification?.title ?: remote.data["title"] ?: "Hello"` (line 23) and body = `remote.notification?.body ?: remote.data["body"] ?: "You've got a message"` (line 24), then calls `helper.showNotification(this, title, body)` (line 27). The native NotificationHelper.showNotification exists at /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/native-app/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yami/core/util/notification/NotificationHelper.kt:128. Manifest registers the service with the FCM intent-filter: native-app/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:85-91 (service name .firebase_cores.messaging.MyFirebaseMessagingService, intent-filter com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT at line 89). KMP (new app): /Users/abdelrahman/Projects/yami-kmp-v2/yami-kmp/app/src/main/java/me/manga/yamiapk/firebase_cores/messaging/MyFirebaseMessagingService.kt — line 9 is the entire class body: `class MyFirebaseMessagingService : FirebaseMessagingService()`. No @AndroidEntryPoint, no @Inject, NO onMessageReceived, NO onNewToken. KDoc (lines 5-8) admits it is a stub: 'real FCM payload handling migrated in Phase 4/11 from the source project'. A grep across the whole repo (excluding native-app) for onMessageReceived/onNewToken found only comments — zero real overrides anywhere in KMP. Manifest still registers it for FCM: app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:90-96 (intent-filter com.google.firebase.MESSAGING_EVENT at line 94). The :platform PushTokenBroadcaster facade exists (platform/src/androidMain/.../push/AndroidPushTokenProvider.kt:64-67) and its KDoc claims MyFirebaseMessagingService.onNewToken calls PushTokenBroadcaster.publish(token), but since the KMP service has NO onNewToken override, nothing ever calls publish() — so token capture is also dead. Net: server-pushed FCM messages produce a notification in native but are silently dropped in KMP, and token-refresh is never observed in KMP.

**🟡 [Medium] Startup — MobileAds initialization (consent gating) — Native defers/gates ad init on consent; KMP initializes MobileAds unconditionally and eagerly** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — native calls MobileAds.initialize twice: once unconditionally in MyApp.onCreate (MyApp.kt:52) and again, consent-gated, in MainActivity.initializeAds() only when consentInformation.canRequestAds() (MainActivity.kt:634-642).
- **KMP:** Partial — MobileAds.initialize(this) is called once, unconditionally, in MyApp.onCreate inside a try/catch (app/.../MyApp.kt:133), with no consent gate and no second consent-gated init.
- **Explanation:** Native's design ensures the SDK is gated by consent before requesting ads (canRequestAds()). KMP always initializes ads at process start regardless of consent state, which both diverges from native behavior and can request personalized ads without consent on first run.
- **Suggested fix:** Keep the early MobileAds.initialize only if necessary for SDK bootstrap, but gate actual ad requests on ConsentFlowClient.canRequestAds() as native does; add a consent-gated re-init/ad-request path matching MainActivity.initializeAds().

**🟡 [Medium] Startup — In-app update progress listener — Native registers a flexible-update progress/downloaded listener at startup; KMP has no such listener** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onCreate calls AppUpdateHelper.registerListener(onProgress = …, onDownloaded = { AppUpdateHelper.completeUpdate() }) (MainActivity.kt:414-423; AppUpdateHelper.registerListener wires an InstallStateUpdatedListener for DOWNLOADING/DOWNLOADED/FAILED/CANCELED).
- **KMP:** No — AppUpdateClient (commonMain interface) exposes only checkForUpdate/startFlexibleUpdate/completeUpdate (AppUpdateClient.kt:24-30); there is no install-state/progress listener API and no registration call anywhere.
- **Explanation:** Native observes download progress and auto-completes the install when the flexible update finishes downloading. KMP cannot observe progress or auto-complete; even if checkForUpdate were wired, the completion handshake native performs (onDownloaded → completeUpdate) is absent.
- **Suggested fix:** Extend AppUpdateClient with an install-state listener (or expose a callback flow) and register it at startup with an onDownloaded → completeUpdate() callback, matching native AppUpdateHelper.registerListener.

**🟡 [Medium] Lifecycle — Activity.onResume update resume — Native resumes a pending flexible update in onResume; KMP MainActivity has no onResume** _(MissingFeature)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onResume calls AppUpdateHelper.resumeUpdate(this) { AppUpdateHelper.completeUpdate() } guarded by !isFinishing && !isDestroyed (MainActivity.kt:993-1007); resumeUpdate checks installStatus()==DOWNLOADED and re-prompts completion.
- **KMP:** No — KMP MainActivity overrides only onCreate (app/.../MainActivity.kt:17-26); no onResume override exists, and the file's own KDoc states 'only onCreate is overridden; no onResume/onPause logic'.
- **Explanation:** If a flexible update finished downloading while the app was backgrounded, native re-surfaces the install completion on resume. KMP never does this, so a downloaded update can stall with no completion prompt.
- **Suggested fix:** Either override onResume in MainActivity (or use a Compose lifecycle observer in App()) to call AppUpdateClient resume/complete logic equivalent to native AppUpdateHelper.resumeUpdate.

**🟡 [Medium] Startup — FirebaseAnalytics APP_OPEN event — Native logs an APP_OPEN analytics event on each launch; KMP logs nothing at startup** _(API/Data)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onCreate calls firebaseAnalytics.logEvent(FirebaseAnalytics.Event.APP_OPEN, Bundle()) (MainActivity.kt:384).
- **KMP:** No — AnalyticsClient/AndroidAnalyticsClient.logEvent exist (platform/.../analytics/AndroidAnalyticsClient.kt:28) but a repo-wide grep for APP_OPEN / app_open and AnalyticsClient.logEvent callers shows no startup logging; nothing in MyApp/App() logs APP_OPEN.
- **Explanation:** Native emits the standard Firebase APP_OPEN event for engagement analytics. KMP omits it, so APP_OPEN-based analytics/funnels diverge from the native baseline.
- **Suggested fix:** Resolve AnalyticsClient at startup and call logEvent("app_open") (FirebaseAnalytics.Event.APP_OPEN) from App() / MyApp, matching native MainActivity.

**🟡 [Medium] Startup — Uncaught exception / crash handler — KMP actively installs a global uncaught-exception handler that records to Crashlytics and launches CrashActivity; native leaves this code commented out (inactive)** _(Bug/Regression)_

- **Native:** No (inactive) — MyApp.onCreate has the Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler / FirebaseCrashlytics.recordException / CrashActivity.start logic entirely commented out (native-app/.../MyApp.kt:33-50). Native installs NO custom uncaught handler at runtime.
- **KMP:** Yes — MyApp.onCreate installs Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler that calls get<CrashReporter>().recordException(...) then posts CrashActivity.start(this, stack) on the main looper and delegates to the previous handler (app/.../MyApp.kt:84-108).
- **Explanation:** This is a behavioral divergence where KMP ADDS functionality native deliberately disabled. On a crash, KMP launches a custom CrashActivity and records to Crashlytics, whereas native lets the system default handler show the standard 'App keeps stopping' dialog. This changes crash UX and crash-reporting volume relative to the source of truth, and risks loops if CrashActivity itself can crash.
- **Suggested fix:** Decide intentionally: if matching native, gate the custom handler behind a flag/off by default; if keeping it, ensure CrashActivity launch is robust (it is wrapped in try/catch) and confirm Crashlytics recording is desired vs native's commented-out behavior.

**⚪ [Low] Lifecycle — Activity.onActivityResult (update flow result) — Native handles the in-app update flow result (RESULT_OK/CANCELED/failure) in onActivityResult; KMP has no handler** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onActivityResult handles requestCode==100 with RESULT_OK / RESULT_CANCELED / failure branches, optionally finishAffinity() for immediate updates (MainActivity.kt:1009-1032). AppUpdateHelper uses REQUEST_CODE=100 for startUpdateFlowForResult.
- **KMP:** No — KMP MainActivity has no onActivityResult override. AndroidAppUpdateClient still passes REQUEST_CODE=100 to startUpdateFlowForResult (AndroidAppUpdateClient.kt comment + impl), but no Activity callback consumes the result.
- **Explanation:** Without onActivityResult, the result of an update flow (user cancelled / failed) is not logged or acted upon. Since the flow itself is never started in KMP, impact is currently latent, but wiring the update flow without this handler would leave native's cancellation/failure handling unmatched.
- **Suggested fix:** When wiring the update flow, add an Activity Result handler for the Play Core update request code (100) replicating native's RESULT_OK/RESULT_CANCELED/failure branches.

**⚪ [Low] Lifecycle — Activity.onDestroy cleanup — Native cancels its review scope and unregisters the update listener in onDestroy; KMP has no onDestroy** _(State)_

- **Native:** Yes — MainActivity.onDestroy calls reviewScope.cancel() and AppUpdateHelper.unregisterListener() in try/catch (MainActivity.kt:1034-1043).
- **KMP:** No — KMP MainActivity overrides only onCreate; no onDestroy. (There is also no reviewScope nor registered update listener to clean up, since those features are absent.)
- **Explanation:** Native performs resource cleanup (coroutine scope cancellation, Play Core listener unregister) on activity destroy. KMP omits this, which is consistent with the missing review/update-listener features but is still a behavioral divergence if those features are later added without cleanup.
- **Suggested fix:** If/when review scope and update listeners are introduced, add an onDestroy (or DisposableEffect in App) to cancel scopes and unregister listeners, matching native MainActivity.onDestroy.

**⚪ [Low] Startup — testing-mode ApiTestScreen branch at app root — Native conditionally renders an admin ApiTestScreen at the app root when Admin.testingMode; KMP always renders MainScreen** _(Navigation)_

- **Native:** Yes — inside YamiMangaTheme, native does `if (Admin.testingMode) { ApiTestScreen(api,context,coroutineScope) } else { MainScreen() }` (MainActivity.kt:454-530).
- **KMP:** No — App() always renders MainScreen() inside YamiTheme (composeApp/.../App.kt:341-345); there is no Admin.testingMode branch at the root. Admin.testingMode exists (shared/.../admin/Admin.kt) but per KDoc is only consumed by the Settings hub, not the app root.
- **Explanation:** Native admins/testers can flip Admin.testingMode to swap the entire UI to an API test harness at launch. KMP cannot reach an ApiTestScreen from the root regardless of testingMode, so this developer/QA flow is unavailable.
- **Suggested fix:** If the test harness is needed, port ApiTestScreen and branch on Admin.testingMode at the App() root (gated to admin builds), mirroring native MainActivity.

**⚪ [Low] Startup — edge-to-edge / decor-fits-system-windows ordering — Native calls WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window,false) AFTER super.onCreate; KMP calls enableEdgeToEdge() BEFORE super.onCreate** _(UI/Layout)_

- **Native:** Yes — installSplashScreen() → super.onCreate() → WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false) (MainActivity.kt:310-313). Native also has a setupTransparentNavigationBar() helper (MainActivity.kt:692-715) though it is not called from onCreate.
- **KMP:** Yes (different API/order) — installSplashScreen() → enableEdgeToEdge() → super.onCreate() (app/.../MainActivity.kt:19-22). Uses AndroidX enableEdgeToEdge() rather than WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows.
- **Explanation:** Both achieve edge-to-edge, but the API and call ordering differ (enableEdgeToEdge before super vs setDecorFitsSystemWindows after super). enableEdgeToEdge applies default transparent/scrim system bar styling that can differ subtly from native's manual decorFitsSystemWindows=false (which left bar coloring to be handled by the shared UI). This can produce minor differences in status/nav bar scrim or icon contrast.
- **Suggested fix:** Verify system bar appearance parity on a device; if scrims/contrast differ, configure enableEdgeToEdge(SystemBarStyle...) to match native's transparent-bar intent, or switch to WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows to mirror native exactly.

**⚪ [Low] WorkManager — Configuration.Provider setup — Native sets the worker factory directly in the WorkManager Configuration; KMP sets only a logging level and relies on Koin's workManagerFactory()** _(Notification/Background)_

- **Native:** Yes — MyApp implements Configuration.Provider with workManagerConfiguration = Configuration.Builder().setWorkerFactory(workerFactory /* HiltWorkerFactory injected */).build() (native-app/.../MyApp.kt:101-104, @Inject workerFactory).
- **KMP:** Partial — MyApp implements Configuration.Provider but workManagerConfiguration only sets setMinimumLoggingLevel(Log.INFO) (app/.../MyApp.kt with no setWorkerFactory). The Koin worker factory is installed separately via workManagerFactory() inside initKoin (MyApp.kt:77) and workerOf(::CbzMigrationWorker)/workerOf(::LibraryRefreshWorker) in appKoinModule.
- **Explanation:** Functionally both supply a worker factory (Hilt vs Koin), so this is largely an implementation-detail divergence. The risk is ordering: KMP's factory is wired into Koin's GlobalContext in onCreate; if WorkManager initialized before that (the manifest removes androidx.startup InitializationProvider on both sides to defer init, which mitigates this). Worth noting native explicitly returns the factory in the config while KMP returns a config without a factory.
- **Suggested fix:** No change required if WorkManager init is correctly deferred (InitializationProvider removed) and workManagerFactory() runs before first WorkManager use; optionally document/verify the init-order invariant to avoid a factory-miss regression.

**⚪ [Low] Startup — onCreate initialization order (MyApp) — The sequence of startup initializers differs between native and KMP** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — native MyApp.onCreate order: AppUpdateHelper.init → FirebaseApp.initializeApp → NotificationHelper.init → MobileAds.initialize (native-app/.../MyApp.kt:23-54). DI is provided by Hilt (no explicit startKoin).
- **KMP:** Yes (reordered + expanded) — KMP MyApp.onCreate order: setAndroidAppContext → initKoin(allReworkModules()){…} → install crash handler → eager get<AppUpdateClient>() → eager get<NotificationPresenter>() → FirebaseApp.initializeApp → MobileAds.initialize (app/.../MyApp.kt:onCreate).
- **Explanation:** KMP must start Koin and register the Android Context before resolving singletons, so the ordering legitimately differs. The notable functional reorder: native initializes Firebase before notifications; KMP initializes notifications (NotificationPresenter eager) before Firebase. Both create the same side-effects (notification channels, update manager). This is acceptable for the DI migration but is a documented divergence; the eager get<> calls correctly mirror native's *Helper.init side-effects.
- **Suggested fix:** No functional fix required; the order is dictated by Koin bootstrap needs. Optionally initialize FirebaseApp before NotificationPresenter to match native ordering if any Firebase-dependent notification setup is later added.

**⚪ [Low] DI graph — Koin vs Hilt coverage of core singletons — Network stack and provider bindings were re-platformed from Hilt (OkHttp/Retrofit) to Koin (Ktor); coverage is otherwise comparable** _(BusinessLogic)_

- **Native:** Yes — Hilt provides MainOkHttpClient OkHttpClient with 200MB cache + offline/force-cache interceptors + BODY logging in DEBUG (AppModule.kt:provideOkHttpClient), Retrofit ScalarsConverterFactory + IMangaDataApiServices (NetworkModule.kt), SharedPrefsHelper, ApplicationScope (SupervisorJob+IO), Firebase (App/Firestore/Analytics/Messaging), WorkManager, NotificationHelper, DeviceInfo/UserId providers (AppBindings.kt).
- **KMP:** Partial — Koin SharedModule binds SharedPrefsHelper (SharedModule.kt:209), ApplicationScope CoroutineScope(SupervisorJob()+IODispatcher) (SharedModule.kt:207), Ktor HttpClient via createHttpClient() (SharedModule.kt:118) instead of OkHttp/Retrofit; PlatformModule.android binds AnalyticsClient/AppUpdateClient/InAppReviewClient/ConsentFlowClient/AdProvider. The 200MB OkHttp disk cache + offline/force-cache interceptor behavior from native AppModule is not an obvious 1:1 in the Ktor client (network-layer concern, flagged for the network audit).
- **Explanation:** DI coverage for app-scoped singletons is broadly preserved across the Hilt→Koin migration. The main re-platforming is the HTTP stack (OkHttp/Retrofit → Ktor); whether the native 200MB cache + offline/forceCacheForDados interceptors are reproduced in the Ktor client is out of this section's scope but should be confirmed by the network/data audit to avoid a caching regression.
- **Suggested fix:** Cross-check with the network/data section that the Ktor HttpClient reproduces native's 200MB disk cache, offlineCacheInterceptor, and forceCacheForDados network interceptor; no startup/DI-structure change needed otherwise.

### 4.3 Priority order for fixing

**P0 — Critical (do first):** core flows, crashes, data-integrity. Ads / Monetization: Rewarded ad on download (gating); Ads / Monetization: Native ads interleaved in lists (Home/Search); Ads / Monetization: Banner ads (Details / Reader / Library / Search / MultiRepo); Ads / Monetization: UMP / GDPR consent flow; DI / Startup / Lifecycle: Startup — Remote source-list seeding (initializeSources); Localization & RTL: All localized screens (19 live ui-module screens: Home/Library/Details/Reader/Settings/History/Updates/Statistics/Downloads/Sources/Language/About/Complaint/Theme/Welcome/WhatsNew/Search/etc.); Manga Details: Adult-content gate (multi-step MStep monetization-block dialogs); Notifications & Background Work: FCM push messaging - incoming message display; Play Update / Review / Consent: In-app update (Play Core) — flow invocation / wiring; Play Update / Review / Consent: In-app update — foreground Activity wiring (ForegroundActivityProvider); Play Update / Review / Consent: In-app review — flow invocation; Play Update / Review / Consent: UMP consent flow — invocation; WebView (Cloudflare solver): Inline 403 / Cloudflare WebViewDialog interstitial

**P1 — High:** missing features/states/interactions and clear behavioural regressions (97 items) — prioritise monetization (ads), resilience (Cloudflare/403, offline), data/schema & migration parity, background work & notifications, then per-screen feature gaps.

**P2 — Medium (202 items):** noticeable UI/behaviour divergences — spacing/typography/color/component differences, default-value flips, secondary interactions.

**P3 — Low (368 items):** subtle cosmetic and copy-level differences, accessibility label wording, and parity-positive divergences (where KMP improved on native).

- [ ] `Medium` **Onboarding Theme step — animated background / gradient overlay** — Native onboarding ThemeSelectionScreen renders a full-screen Lottie AnimatedBackground (R.raw.background, IterateForever, ContentScale.FillBounds) PLUS a Brush.verticalGradient overlay of background at alpha 0.1f -> 0.3f -> 1.0f. The KMP onboarding ThemeScreen drops both and uses a flat Scaffold with neutral Material 3 surfaces.
- [ ] `Medium` **Theme picker — selected-tab indicator color/styling** — Native ThemeSelector customizes the TabRow with a transparent container (surfaceVariant alpha 0f) and an explicit primary-colored TabRowDefaults.Indicator offset to the selected tab, wrapped in an ItemsGroup card (surfaceContainerHigh alpha 0.4f, RoundedCornerShape(16dp), padding 16dp). KMP uses a default TabRow with containerColor=Transparent and contentColor=primary, NO custom indicator, and NO surrounding ItemsGroup card.
- [ ] `Medium` **Notification-permission section layout in picker** — Native renders the notification section unconditionally inside the selector card: header (enable_notifications, bodyMedium/14sp/onBackground, bottom padding 4.dp), body (notification_permission, bodySmall/12sp/onBackground, maxLines=3, bottom padding 8.dp), and a right-aligned Grant Permission Button with contentPadding(h=16,v=8) using AutoSubtitleText. KMP renders the section only when onRequestNotificationPermission != null AND !hasNotificationPermission, with header bodyLarge, body bodySmall colored onSurfaceVariant, and a default Button.
- [ ] `Low` **Theme picker — TopAppBar title** — KMP ThemeScreen always renders a Material 3 TopAppBar with title text 'Theme' (theme_screen_title). Native onboarding ThemeSelectionScreen has NO top app bar at all; it shows only an in-body 'Choose Your Theme' headline. Native Settings inline theme controls likewise have no per-section top bar.
- [ ] `Low` **Onboarding Theme picker — tab labels in TabRow** — Native tab labels use AutoSubtitleText (an auto-sizing/auto-shrinking text component with maxLines=1 and a minSize floor) with bodyMedium/14sp/primary. KMP uses a plain Material3 Text with primary color and no auto-shrink, no explicit maxLines.
- [ ] `Low` **Onboarding Theme picker — 'Choose Your Theme' headline typography** — Native headline style is headlineMedium.copy(fontSize = 24.sp, color = primary) — i.e. an explicit 24sp override on top of headlineMedium. KMP uses plain MaterialTheme.typography.headlineMedium with color=primary and no explicit 24.sp override, so the rendered size is whatever the M3 headlineMedium token resolves to (typically 28sp in default M3 type scale).
- [ ] `Low` **Onboarding Theme step — Continue button styling** — Native Continue button is fillMaxWidth + height(50.dp) + clip(RoundedCornerShape(26.dp)) + shape=shapes.medium + ButtonDefaults.buttonColors(containerColor=primary), label labelLarge/16sp/onPrimary. KMP uses a default Material3 Button(fillMaxWidth) with the M3 default height/shape/colors and a default Text('Continue').
- [ ] `Low` **Onboarding Theme step — PureBlack switch present in onboarding** — KMP renders the PureBlack/OLED Switch row inside the theme picker, which means it appears in the ONBOARDING flow as well as the Settings-reached screen. Native onboarding ThemeSelector does NOT expose a PureBlack toggle at all — native exposes PureBlack only later in the Settings screen.
- [ ] `Low` **Theme picker — PureBlack toggle label text** — Both sides reuse pure_black_mode_title, BUT the native string value is 'Pure black dark mode' and the KMP value is also 'Pure black dark mode' (verified equal). However the KMP ThemeScreen KDoc and PureBlackRow comments repeatedly describe the label as 'Pure Black for dark mode' / 'Pure Black for dark mode', which does not match the actual rendered string. The rendered strings match; only the in-source documentation is inconsistent.
- [ ] `Low` **ThemeViewModel / ThemeState — first-run pureBlack default vs theme provider default** — Native: SettingsRepository.isPureBlack() defaults to true and pureBlackFlow uses default=isPureBlack() (true). The KMP ThemeState.pureBlack initial value is also true, and ThemeRepositoryImpl.observePureBlack() passes through legacy.pureBlackFlow (default true), so the picker state matches. BUT the KMP YamiTheme/legacy YamiMangaTheme composable's pureBlack PARAMETER default is false. Parity holds at runtime only because App.kt explicitly collects pureBlack from the flow (default true) and passes it in. The default-parameter mismatch (false) is a latent trap.
- [ ] `Low` **Theme picker — onboarding Continue enabled-gating logic** — Native Continue button is gated as enabled = hasNotificationPermission.value, where hasNotificationPermission starts as the real permission state and is also force-set to true on pre-Tiramisu devices and after grant. KMP gates as enabled = onRequestNotificationPermission == null \|\| hasNotificationPermission — i.e. enabled whenever no permission callback was supplied. In the onboarding route the callback IS supplied and hasPermission is the real value, so behaviour matches; but the gating is keyed on callback-nullness rather than the permission state directly.
- [ ] `Low` **Theme picker — spacing/padding of picker column** — Native onboarding screen uses an outer Column padding of 24.dp with verticalArrangement=SpaceBetween (title at top, button at bottom) and a 16.dp Spacer between title and selector, plus a 24.dp Spacer inside the selector before the notification section. KMP uses Column padding of spacing.lg horizontal + spacing.md vertical with verticalArrangement=Arrangement.spacedBy(spacing.md) (uniform gaps, top-aligned, no SpaceBetween).
- [ ] `Low` **Theme system — dynamic color (Material You) support** — Native YamiMangaTheme supports dynamicColor (Android 12+ dynamicDark/LightColorScheme) via a parameter, though it is never enabled by callers (always defaults false / not passed true). KMP YamiTheme declares dynamicColor as an @Suppress(UNUSED_PARAMETER) no-op with a TODO to restore via a future :platform DynamicColorProvider SPI.

#### About
- [ ] `High` **About — row leading icons** — Native renders a leading Material icon on each actionable row; KMP renders no leading icons on any row. ✅
- [ ] `High` **About — scroll behavior / overflow** — Native content is in a vertically scrollable LazyColumn; KMP content is in a non-scrollable Column. ➗
- [ ] `Medium` **About — row trailing chevron** — Native shows a trailing KeyboardArrowRight chevron on EVERY row (it is the defaulted endIcon); KMP shows no trailing chevron on any row.
- [ ] `Medium` **About — row order** — The actionable rows appear in a different order.
- [ ] `Medium` **About — Source code row localization** — The Source code row labels are English-only in KMP; native localizes them across all 12 locales.
- [ ] `Medium` **About — group container styling** — Group card background color, corner radius and inner padding differ.
- [ ] `Medium` **About — back navigation affordance** — Native back control is an ArrowBack icon button; KMP is a text 'Back' button.
- [ ] `Medium` **About — top app bar title typography** — Title font size and weight differ.
- [ ] `Medium` **About — external link launch strategy (app-first deep links)** — Native attempts native-app deep-link URIs first (twitter://, fb://, instagram://, whatsapp://) then falls back to web/Custom Tabs; KMP always passes the plain web URL.
- [ ] `Low` **About — footer package label** — KMP adds a centered footer showing the reverse-DNS package id; native has no such element.
- [ ] `Low` **About — row text typography & auto-size** — Row title/subtitle sizing and overflow handling differ.
- [ ] `Low` **About — row vertical padding** — Per-row vertical padding differs.
- [ ] `Low` **About — divider colors** — Inter-row divider color tokens differ slightly and Material version differs.
- [ ] `Low` **About — Material 2 vs Material 3 components** — Native screen is built on androidx.compose.material (M2) Scaffold/Icon/IconButton/Divider; KMP uses androidx.compose.material3 throughout.
- [ ] `Low` **About — loading state** — KMP shows a centered CircularProgressIndicator while metadata loads; native has no loading state.
- [ ] `Low` **About — website (Public) social icon glyph** — The website button uses a different vector glyph than native.
- [ ] `Low` **About — SocialMediaRow press-scale animation spec** — Press-scale animation stiffness/reset mechanism differs slightly.
- [ ] `Low` **About — version row value source** — Both show the app versionName; native reads it via PackageManager synchronously, KMP via GetAppMetadataUseCase/AppVersionProvider.
- [ ] `Low` **About — outer content padding** — Outer horizontal padding matches (16.dp) but top padding handling differs.

#### What's New
- [ ] `High` **What's New — inline video playback** — Native plays feature videos inline with a real player; KMP shows a static poster that opens the URL externally ✅
- [ ] `High` **What's New — multi-image URL carousel data** — :data mapper hard-codes imageUrlList = emptyList(), so remote multi-image carousels never render ✅
- [ ] `Medium` **What's New — per-version trigger/gating** — Version-bump comparison changed from versionCode (Int, greater-than) to versionName (String, inequality)
- [ ] `Medium` **What's New — bundled drawable image rendering** — Native renders bundled @DrawableRes images (single + carousel); KMP cannot resolve drawable names and falls through to placeholder
- [ ] `Medium` **What's New — title/description typography (AutoSubtitleText)** — Native auto-sizes title/description with explicit min/max sp and tablet scaling; KMP uses fixed Material titleMedium/bodyMedium
- [ ] `Medium` **What's New — header layout & Close button styling** — Native uses a custom Row header with a circular tinted Close button; KMP uses a Material3 TopAppBar with a plain IconButton action
- [ ] `Medium` **What's New — fullscreen media viewer (zoom, video, instructions chip)** — Native fullscreen viewer supports image AND video and a styled instruction chip; KMP fullscreen is image-only with a plain caption, no zoom
- [ ] `Medium` **What's New — Arabic localization for navigation buttons & fullscreen caption** — np_previous / np_next / np_get_started / np_whats_new_close / np_close / np_tap_outside_to_close have no Arabic translations in KMP
- [ ] `Medium` **What's New — remote fetch language & i18n of content** — Rework :data hard-codes language 'en' for the feature fetch, dropping per-user localized content; native/legacy use the user's selected language
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — responsive padding & sizing (tablet/landscape)** — Native adapts horizontalPadding, cardPadding, mediaSize and card max-height to tablet/landscape; KMP uses fixed LocalSpacing and a fixed 220.dp media size
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — card slide-in animation direction & shape** — Native FeatureCard animates horizontal slide+fade keyed to active page; KMP animates a vertical slide+fade keyed to page composition
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — page indicator unselected color token** — Native unselected indicator uses outline@0.3; KMP uses onSurfaceVariant@0.3
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — navigation buttons (first-page spacer width, button paddings)** — Native reserves an 80.dp spacer on the first page and uses explicit contentPadding (h=20,v=10) on all buttons; KMP uses a 1.dp spacer and default button paddings
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — Loading state copy & layout** — Native loading state shows a 48.dp spinner (strokeWidth 4) + 'Loading What's New...' label; KMP shows the shared YamiLoadingState with no label
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — Empty state layout (card vs centered text) & Close action** — Native empty state is a centered elevated Card with title, body and a Close button; KMP empty state is a shared YamiEmptyState title-only with no action
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — Error state Close affordance** — Native error state offers both Close and Retry; KMP error state offers only Retry
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — gradient/scrim parity** — Background gradient matches native, but KMP applies it on the Scaffold while native applies it on a full-size Box behind a Column
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — card container color & NEW chip placement** — Native card uses default Card surface with centered content and no inline NEW chip on the card; KMP card uses surfaceVariant container with a left-aligned title Row + inline NEW chip
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — title string casing** — Header title text differs in casing: native 'What\'s New' vs KMP 'What\'s new'
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — About-screen entry point & mark-seen behavior** — Native About row calls ensureFeaturesLoaded() then navigates with isFirstOpen=false; KMP About row navigates to a separate WhatsNewRework route (no isFirstOpen, separate VM instance)
- [ ] `Low` **What's New — KDoc/implementation drift (audit hazard)** — Multiple KMP KDocs claim pager/images/video/fullscreen/nav-buttons are 'not ported / deferred' while the code actually implements them
